As an overwhelming terror begins taking over her life, Rose must confront her troubling past in order to survive and escape her horrifying new reality.
tagline: Once you see it, it’s too late.
title: Smile
plot:
Smile is a 2022 American supernatural horror film directed by Parker Finn and produced by Paramount Pictures.

The movie follows Dr. Rose Cotter (played by Sosie Bacon), a psychologist who returns to her hometown after the death of her mother, only to find herself dealing with a mysterious and terrifying phenomenon that seems to be connected to an antique dental mirror in her family's old house.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the mirror has a dark history and is somehow linked to Rose's own traumatic past. The mirror appears to be exerting some kind of malevolent influence over those who come into contact with it, causing them to smile uncontrollably and eventually succumb to madness and terror.

Rose soon discovers that she is not immune to the mirror's effects and must navigate a series of surreal and terrifying events as she tries to uncover the truth behind the mirror's power. Along the way, she teams up with her skeptical brother Trevor (played by Jessie T. Usher) and a local antique dealer who may hold some clues about the mirror's origins.

As the story builds towards its climax, Rose must confront her own dark past and the evil force that is driving her to madness. The film's climax features a shocking twist that reveals the true nature of the mirror and the source of its power.

Throughout the movie, Finn uses a range of clever visual effects and camera tricks to create a sense of unease and tension, making it clear that Smile is not just a horror movie but also a deeply unsettling exploration of trauma, grief, and the supernatural. The film's score, composed by Michael Abels, adds to the overall sense of dread and unease.

Overall, Smile is a tense and unsettling horror movie that explores themes of trauma, grief, and the supernatural in a unique and thought-provoking way.

overview: After a divorce, Sophia moves to the south of Italy with her daughter, Helena. Their new home, an apartment within an austere building of the fascist age, is a chance for them to start a new life. But inside an old storage room hides a mysterious closet and a buried secret. After the loss of Helena’s first baby tooth, a chilling obsession begins and an apparition haunts her sleep...
tagline: She's coming for her.
title: The Haunting of Helena
plot:
The Haunting of Helena, released in some countries as Fairytale, is a 2012 Italian supernatural horror film written and directed by Christian Bisceglia and shot in Italy. Harriet MacMasters-Green and Sabrina Jolie Perez star. It was distributed as part of the Bloody Disgusting Selects line.

Sophia, a recently divorced university professor living in Italy with her young daughter, Helena, is involved in a car accident with her on the day Helena loses her first tooth. Soon afterward Helena begins describing strange visions. Researching their apartment, Sophia learns that during the Fascist era a man who lived there tortured his wife by pulling out her teeth and locked her in a closet to die. Helena starts talking to an unseen presence in the closet and buys teeth from classmates, saying they are for the tooth fairy. A teacher who looks into this behavior is killed by a swarm of mosquitoes. Ignoring a warning to leave from the elderly man who lives upstairs, mother and daughter are attacked by the toothless ghost of the dead woman, escaping when Sophia throws the teeth at her.

Eighteen months later, Helena has stopped speaking and is confined to an institution, and her father, now back in Italy, believes Sophia is unfit to care for her. Bloody teeth rain briefly from the ceiling of Helena's room, and the closet door begins appearing in other places; when her father opens it, mosquitoes swarm and kill him. Doctors grow suspicious of Sophia, especially after his bloody teeth turn up in Helena's locker. Drawn by visions of the murderer at a window of the institution's abandoned psychiatric wing, Sophia finds his file and works out where the dead woman's teeth are hidden. She throws them through the closet door when it reappears, and Helena begins speaking again, apparently freed. But a recorded interview with the murderer reveals that his wife was a serial killer who ate the faces of children and that he killed her to stop her. Sophia finds a patient with a mauled face, who tells her the ogre has her teeth again, and she enters Helena's room before backing out screaming. Later, Sophia herself is a patient at the institution, gazing up at the abandoned wing where Helena's ghost, half her face gone, stands beside the murderer.

Reviews were largely negative, criticizing the clichéd plot and the performances. Slant's Chuck Bowen said it borrowed so heavily from Guillermo del Toro that he could almost sue for plagiarism.

original_title: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Beginning
overview: Chrissie and her friends set out on a road trip for a final fling before one is shipped off to Vietnam. Along the way, bikers harass the foursome and cause an accident that throws Chrissie from the vehicle. The lawman who arrives on the scene kills one of the bikers and brings Chrissie's friends to the Hewitt homestead, where young Leatherface is learning the tools of terror.
tagline: What you know about fear... doesn't even come close.
title: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Beginning
plot:
The Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Beginning is an American slasher film of 2006 directed by Jonathan Liebesman; Sheldon Turner scripted it from a story he devised with David J. Schow. A prequel to the 2003 remake, it is the sixth film in the franchise. Jordana Brewster stars as Chrissie, with Taylor Handley as Dean, Matt Bomer as Eric, Diora Baird as Bailey, Andrew Bryniarski as Thomas Hewitt, the killer later known as Leatherface, and R. Lee Ermey as Charlie Hewitt, who takes the identity of Sheriff Hoyt.

In 1939 a woman dies giving birth on the floor of a Texas slaughterhouse, and the supervisor throws the baby into a dumpster. Young Luda Mae Hewitt finds him, takes him home, names him Thomas and raises him as her son. In 1969 Thomas works at the same plant under the same supervisor. When health inspectors close the plant, he refuses to leave, kills the supervisor with a hammer and takes a chainsaw. When the local sheriff, Winston Hoyt, tries to arrest him, Luda Mae's son Charlie kills him and assumes his identity.

Meanwhile two brothers, Eric and Dean, are on a cross-country road trip with Chrissie and Bailey, their girlfriends, bound for Vietnam. After a run-in with bikers at a diner, a woman biker forces their car off the road at gunpoint, and Chrissie is thrown into a field in the crash. The fake Hoyt arrives, kills the biker and takes the others to the Hewitt house, where Thomas butchers the body, while Chrissie, hiding in the towed jeep, escapes and returns with Holden, the biker's boyfriend. Hoyt tortures Dean for planning to dodge the draft. Eric frees himself and helps Dean, but Bailey is dragged back with a meat hook, Dean is caught in a bear trap and Eric is knocked out. Thomas kills Holden with his chainsaw, murders Eric and cuts off his face to wear as a mask. Chrissie, forced to sit at the family's dinner table with Bailey and the unconscious Dean, watches Leatherface cut Bailey's throat, then stabs him with a screwdriver and leaps from a window. Dean beats Hoyt savagely and follows her to the slaughterhouse, where Leatherface kills him. Chrissie escapes in the supervisor's car, but as she stops beside a state trooper, Leatherface rises from the back seat and kills her with the chainsaw; the car crashes, killing the trooper and a passer-by, and Leatherface walks home along the road.

Released in October 2006, the film opened at number two at the American box office with $18.5 million. Critics dismissed it, giving it 17% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Chuck Nolan, a top international manager for FedEx, and Kelly, a Ph.D. student, are in love and heading towards marriage. Then Chuck's plane to Malaysia crashes at sea during a terrible storm. He's the only survivor, and finds himself marooned on a desolate island. With no way to escape, Chuck must find ways to survive in his new home.
tagline: At the edge of the world, his journey begins.
title: Cast Away
plot:
Cast Away is a survival drama film directed by Robert Zemeckis, released in 2000 by DreamWorks Pictures.

The movie begins with Chuck Noland (played by Tom Hanks), an FedEx employee who works as a systems engineer. Chuck's life is mundane and unfulfilling, and he feels disconnected from his colleagues and loved ones. He travels the world for work, but never stays in one place long enough to form meaningful relationships.

On Christmas Eve, Chuck boards a plane that crashes on a deserted island in the Pacific Ocean. The only survivor of the crash, Chuck is left stranded with limited supplies and no way to communicate with the outside world. As he tries to survive on the island, Chuck's life becomes a solitary struggle for survival.

Initially, Chuck uses his skills as an engineer to build shelter, start a fire, and find food. He also creates a volleyball, which he names "Wilson," to keep himself company. Over time, Chuck forms a bond with Wilson, talking to him and even giving him a name. As the days turn into weeks, Chuck's mental state begins to deteriorate due to his isolation.

As the months pass, Chuck becomes more and more obsessed with finding a way off the island. He tries to signal for help using various methods, including building a fire on the highest point of the island and creating a makeshift flag. However, despite his efforts, no one comes to rescue him.

Meanwhile, back in the United States, Chuck's colleagues and loved ones are searching for him. They receive a distress call from Chuck's plane, but it is too late. The crew has given up hope, and they begin to move on with their lives.

As the years go by, Chuck becomes more and more despondent. He starts to question his own identity and purpose in life. However, he also begins to find ways to occupy himself on the island, including writing letters to his loved ones and creating a makeshift calendar.

In the end, Chuck's luck changes when a ship passes by the island, and he is rescued. As he steps off the boat, Chuck is greeted with tears of joy from his colleagues and loved ones. However, as he looks back at the island, he realizes that he has changed forever. He has found a new sense of purpose in life and has learned to appreciate the simple things.

The movie ends with Chuck returning home, where he is reunited with his girlfriend, Kelly (played by Helen Hunt). The two share a tender moment, and it seems that Chuck has finally found happiness. However, as the camera pans out, we see that Chuck's experiences on the island have left him changed forever. He is no longer the same person who set off on that fateful plane ride.

Overall, Cast Away is a powerful and emotional film that explores themes of survival, loneliness, and redemption. Tom Hanks' performance as Chuck Noland is outstanding, and his portrayal of a man struggling to survive on a deserted island is both heartbreaking and inspiring.

overview: A recently retired man embarks on a journey to his estranged daughter's wedding, only to discover more about himself and life than he ever expected.
tagline: Schmidt Happens.
title: About Schmidt
plot:
About Schmidt is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of life, identity, and human connection. The movie follows the story of Warren Schmidt, a middle-aged man who embarks on a journey of self-discovery after his wife leaves him for another man.

At its core, About Schmidt explores the theme of existential crisis, as Warren grapples with the meaninglessness of modern life and the search for purpose in a seemingly indifferent world. As he navigates through various experiences, including a disastrous trip to Nebraska, Warren begins to question the societal expectations placed upon him and the emptiness of his own life.

The film also touches on the theme of loneliness and isolation, as Warren struggles to form meaningful connections with others. His relationships with his children, particularly his son Mike, are strained, and he finds himself disconnected from those around him. This sense of disconnection serves as a catalyst for Warren's journey, as he seeks to re-evaluate his life and find a new sense of belonging.

Furthermore, About Schmidt critiques the societal pressures that shape our lives, particularly in terms of masculinity and middle-class expectations. Warren's struggles with his own identity and sense of purpose serve as a commentary on the constraints placed upon men by traditional masculine norms.

Ultimately, the film presents a nuanced exploration of human vulnerability, imperfection, and the search for authenticity in a world that often values superficiality over depth. Through Warren's journey, About Schmidt invites viewers to reflect on their own lives, relationships, and sense of purpose, offering a poignant reminder of the importance of embracing our complexities and imperfections.

overview: Set in a futuristic world where humans live in isolation and interact through surrogate robots, a cop is forced to leave his home for the first time in years in order to investigate the murders of others' surrogates.
tagline: How do you save humanity when the only thing that's real is you?
title: Surrogates
plot:
Surrogates is a 2009 science fiction action film directed by Jonathan Mostow and starring Bruce Willis, Radha Mitchell, and Rosamund Pike.

The main themes of Surrogates can be broken down into several key areas:

1. **Convenience vs. Humanity**: The movie explores the idea of a society where people use surrogates, or robotic duplicates, to control their lives. On one hand, this technology provides convenience, efficiency, and a sense of security. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that this reliance on surrogates comes at the cost of genuine human connections and emotions.

2. **Free Will vs. Control**: The film raises questions about the nature of free will and control in a world where people can manipulate their surrogates to do their bidding. As the protagonist, Detective Greer (Bruce Willis), delves deeper into the mystery, he begins to realize that his own life is not as under his control as he thought.

3. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: The movie explores the theme of identity and self-discovery through the character of Greer, who must confront the possibility that his surrogate may be a copycat killer. As he navigates this complex web of identities, Greer is forced to re-examine his own sense of self and purpose.

4. **The Dangers of Unchecked Technological Advancement**: Surrogates serves as a cautionary tale about the potential risks of unchecked technological advancement. The film highlights the dangers of relying too heavily on technology to solve our problems, rather than addressing the underlying issues that drive human behavior.

5. **Human Connection and Empathy**: Ultimately, the movie suggests that true human connection and empathy are essential for a fulfilling life. As Greer forms connections with those around him, including his wife (Radha Mitchell) and a young girl named Verity (Pike), he begins to realize that these relationships are what truly make us human.

Overall, Surrogates is a thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human nature in a world where technology is increasingly integrated into our lives.

overview: On their home planet of Cybertron, the Autobots and Decepticons are involved in an explosive battle over the coveted AllSpark. With the fate of the universe at stake, the Autobots send it far from the reaches of the ruthless Megatron, leader of the Decepticons. But there are even more surprises in store when it crash-lands on Earth.
tagline: See what happened before Optimus Prime and Megatron came to Earth.
title: Transformers: Beginnings
plot:
Transformers: Beginnings is a 2007 American animated short that serves as a prequel to Michael Bay's live-action film Transformers. Rather than full animation, it is presented as a motion comic: a shortened, voiced adaptation of the prequel comic book published by IDW Publishing ahead of the film, with artwork set in motion by the studio Sunny Boy Creative. Running about 19 minutes, it is narrated by the Autobot Bumblebee, voiced by Mark Ryan, who also performed the character's voice in the feature. Peter Cullen returns as Optimus Prime and Frank Welker, the voice of Megatron in the original 1980s cartoon, plays the Decepticon leader, with Patrick Hallahan as Starscream, Brian Stepanek as Blackout and Sector Seven agent Seymour Simmons, Kevin Dunn as Ron Witwicky and Patrick Viall as Captain Archibald Witwicky.

Bumblebee's account begins on Cybertron, where the AllSpark, the source of all Transformer life, once allowed the planet to flourish under the joint leadership of Optimus Prime and Megatron. Megatron, however, becomes corrupted and tries to seize the artifact for himself, igniting the war between the Autobots and the Decepticons. Bumblebee fights to protect it, and the Autobots finally launch the AllSpark into space to keep it from Megatron, who destroys Bumblebee's voice before setting off in pursuit. Megatron tracks the cube to prehistoric Earth but becomes trapped in Arctic ice. Some four million years later, an expedition led by Captain Archibald Witwicky stumbles upon the frozen robot; Witwicky ends his days in a mental institution after filling page after page with alien designs, which draw the attention of the secret government agency Sector Seven. The agency excavates Megatron, discovers the AllSpark in Colorado and, decades later, oversees the building of the Hoover Dam. The story then jumps to 2003, when Bumblebee's arrival on Earth is detected and Sector Seven, led by Simmons, begins hunting the robot disguised as a yellow Camaro, while Sam Witwicky learns of his great-great-grandfather's legacy.

The short was not sold on its own: it was included on a bonus disc available only with the Walmart edition of the Transformers DVD, released in North America on 16 October 2007. The Transformers DVD itself became the fastest-selling DVD of 2007 in North America, with 8.3 million copies sold in its first week.

overview: When famed photographer Christina Eames dies unexpectedly, she leaves her estranged daughter, Mae, hurt, angry and full of questions. When Mae finds a photograph tucked away in a safe-deposit box, she soon finds herself delving into her mother's early life -- an investigation that leads to an unexpected romance with a rising journalist.
title: The Photograph
plot:
The Photograph is an American romantic drama of 2020 written and directed by Stella Meghie. Issa Rae stars as Mae Morton, with LaKeith Stanfield as the reporter Michael Block, Chanté Adams as Mae's mother Christina Eames in her youth, Y'lan Noel and Rob Morgan as Isaac Jefferson at different ages, Courtney B. Vance as Louis Morton, and Lil Rel Howery and Chelsea Peretti in supporting roles.

In the present, Michael travels to Louisiana to interview Isaac about his life after Hurricane Katrina. A photograph of a young woman, Christina Eames, in Isaac's home intrigues him. Christina, now dead, has left her daughter Mae a safety deposit box containing the same picture and two letters, one for Mae and one to be delivered to her father. Back in New York, Michael seeks out Mae, an assistant curator, who shows him her mother's archives. Attracted to her, he engineers a chance encounter at a French film screening at her gallery, and a first date ends in a kiss. As the romance grows, Michael is offered a job in London and, unsure how to tell her so early in their relationship, begins avoiding her calls.

The story of Christina unfolds in parallel. As a young woman she shares a flirtatious friendship with Isaac and eventually moves in with him, but she longs to become a photographer and, without telling him, takes a bus to New York, where she lands a job as a photographer's assistant. At her mother's funeral, her friend Denise tells her that Isaac has married. Years later Christina returns with the young Mae; when Isaac invites them to dinner with his wife, Christina refuses and weeps after kissing his cheek, a moment Mae never forgets.

In the present, Mae visits Isaac and delivers her mother's letter, which reveals that he is her biological father; he admits he suspected as much but was too afraid to ask. Michael, arriving to finish his article, is surprised to find her there, and after a day together he tells her about London but she says a long-distance relationship is impractical. Preparing a retrospective of Christina's work, Mae finds a video in which her mother wishes she had been better at loving people. Later she invites Michael to a Kendrick Lamar concert, and when they meet in New York she declares her feelings and they resolve to make it work.

Released by Universal Pictures on Valentine's Day 2020, the film grossed $21 million and drew favourable reviews, with 75% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: It was an ingenious enough plan: rob the Riviera Casino's count room during an Elvis impersonator convention. But Thomas Murphy decided to keep all the money for himself and shot all his partners, including recently-freed ex-con Michael Zane. With $3.2 million at stake, the Marshals Service closing in, Michael must track down Murphy.
tagline: Crime Is King
title: 3000 Miles to Graceland
plot:
3000 Miles to Graceland is a 2001 American action crime film directed and co-produced by Demian Lichtenstein, who shares a writing credit with Richard Recco, the author of the original script. The cast includes Kurt Russell, Kevin Costner, Courteney Cox, David Arquette, Bokeem Woodbine, Christian Slater, Kevin Pollak and Daisy McCrackin. The title refers to Elvis Presley's home, Graceland.

Recently paroled Michael Zane stops at a run-down desert motel outside Las Vegas, where he catches a boy, Jesse, stealing from his car and follows him back to his mother, Cybil Waingrow, whom he seduces. The next day Michael is collected by Murphy, Hanson, Gus and Franklin, and the five men, dressed as Elvis, rob the Riviera casino during an Elvis convention. Franklin is killed in the shootout during their escape, and Murphy later shoots Hanson in a quarrel over Franklin's share. Michael hides the money in the attic, unaware that Jesse is watching. When the survivors drive into the desert to bury Hanson, Murphy shoots Gus and Michael, but on his way back he hits a coyote and is knocked out in the crash. Michael, saved by a bulletproof vest, returns to find the money gone, retrieves it from Cybil's room and reluctantly takes mother and son with him, since the marked cash must be laundered through a contact in Idaho. Cybil steals Michael's wallet and the password for the launderer, Peterson, and drives off, but Murphy, using the same password, reaches Peterson first, and Cybil walks into his trap; Michael later finds Peterson and his secretary dead. Michael has Murphy arrested by reporting his own car stolen, but is also jailed for driving a stolen vehicle; Jesse bails him out in exchange for becoming his partner, while Murphy secures his release through a contact and recruits a mercenary. After Murphy runs Cybil and Jesse off the road and takes the boy hostage, Michael tips off the authorities and meets Murphy at a warehouse to trade. The bag Michael hands over is full of cut-up newspaper and a hidden scorpion, which stings Murphy. Surrounded by a SWAT team, Murphy shoots Michael and is killed by police. Cybil and Jesse steal the ambulance carrying Michael, again saved by a vest, and the three escape aboard his boat, the Graceland.

Released on February 23, 2001, the film was panned, with a 15% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and earned only $18.7 million against a budget of $47.4 million. It received five Golden Raspberry Award nominations.

overview: When Scooby and the gang hear of a werewolf plaguing a traveling circus, they go undercover as circus performers to get to the bottom.
title: Big Top Scooby-Doo!
plot:
Big Top Scooby-Doo! is a 2012 animated mystery comedy film that pays homage to the classic Scooby-Doo franchise while also incorporating elements of circus culture and adventure. At its core, the movie revolves around the theme of teamwork and unity among friends as they work together to solve a mysterious plot threatening their beloved Big Top Circus.

The story delves into the idea of embracing one's individuality and finding strength in diversity, as each member of the gang brings their unique skills and personalities to the table. The film also explores the concept of loyalty and trust, highlighting the importance of standing by one another through thick and thin.

Furthermore, Big Top Scooby-Doo! touches on the theme of facing fears and overcoming anxieties, as the characters confront their personal demons and learn to rely on each other for support. This is particularly evident in Shaggy's struggles with his fear of clowns, which serves as a metaphor for the challenges we all face in life.

Ultimately, the movie presents a heartwarming tale of friendship, perseverance, and the power of believing in oneself and one's friends. With its lighthearted tone and engaging storyline, Big Top Scooby-Doo! is a delightful addition to the Scooby-Doo franchise that will leave audiences of all ages smiling and entertained.

overview: Held captive for 7 years in an enclosed space, a woman and her young son finally gain their freedom, allowing the boy to experience the outside world for the first time.
tagline: Love knows no boundaries
title: Room
plot:
Room is a 2015 psychological drama directed by Lenny Abrahamson and written by Emma Donoghue, adapting her own 2010 novel. Brie Larson stars as a young woman held captive for seven years and Jacob Tremblay as her five-year-old son, born in captivity, with Joan Allen, Sean Bridgers, Tom McCamus and William H. Macy. A co-production of Canada, Ireland, the United Kingdom and the United States, it was shot in Toronto on a set built at Pinewood Toronto Studios, with removable sections to give the crew access. Larson consulted a trauma expert and a nutritionist, dieted and avoided sunlight to prepare.

In Akron, Ohio, Joy Newsome and her son Jack live locked inside a squalid shed they call "Room", lit only by a skylight. Their captor, "Old Nick", abducted Joy seven years earlier and rapes her while Jack sleeps in the wardrobe. To protect Jack, Joy has told him that only Room is real and the rest of the world exists on television. When Old Nick reveals he has lost his job and cuts off their heat after a confrontation, Joy finally explains the outside world to Jack. A faked fever fails to get him to a hospital, so she rolls him in a rug and has him play dead. Old Nick drives off with the "body" in his pickup, and Jack, overwhelmed by his first sight of the world, leaps out and gets a stranger's attention. The police rescue him, find Joy and arrest Old Nick.

Joy returns to her childhood home to live with her mother, Nancy, and Nancy's new partner, Leo, while her father cannot accept Jack as his grandson. Jack struggles with the vast new world and longs for Room, and Joy, consumed by anger and depression, is shaken when a television interviewer questions her decision to keep her baby. After Jack finds her unconscious following a suicide attempt, she is hospitalized. Jack slowly grows close to his grandmother and Leo and makes a friend, and sends Joy a lock of his hair. When she comes home, they visit Room one last time, and Jack, finding it smaller than he remembered, says goodbye.

Larson plays Joy and Tremblay plays Jack, with Allen as Nancy and McCamus as Leo. Room won the People's Choice Award at the Toronto International Film Festival and was widely acclaimed, with 93% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. Larson won the Academy Award, Golden Globe, BAFTA and SAG Award for Best Actress, and the film received four Oscar nominations in all. It grossed $36.3 million worldwide on a $13 million budget.

overview: Raquel's longtime crush on her next-door neighbor turns into something more when he starts developing feelings for her, despite his family's objections.
tagline: It all started with the Wi-Fi password...
title: Through My Window
plot:
Through My Window (Spanish: A través de mi ventana) is a 2022 Spanish teen romantic drama directed by Marçal Forés from a screenplay by Eduard Sola, based on Ariana Godoy's novel of the same name. Clara Galle stars as Raquel Mendoza and Julio Peña as Ares Hidalgo, with Pilar Castro and Eric Masip.

Raquel, who writes stories but lacks the courage to share them, narrates how her life changed. Her modest family home sits beside the mansion of the wealthy Hidalgos, owners of Alpha 3, one of the country's most influential companies, headquartered in Barcelona. The three Hidalgo heirs are Artemis, Ares and Apolo. Raquel is obsessed with Ares, though she has never spoken to him. When Apolo thanks her for letting the brothers use her Wi-Fi, she realizes that Ares has hacked her computer for the password. She confronts him in the woods, admits that she likes him and vows to make him fall for her. Their flirtation intensifies when he climbs through her window to reconnect the Wi-Fi she has unplugged, and at a party she seduces him only to walk away. Ares later opens up to her about his grandfather's death, and they sleep together.

Ares then turns cold, pushing her away repeatedly, until he finds Raquel drunk in the street and takes her home. He confesses that she makes him feel things he cannot afford, because his father has already mapped out a future for him with no room for love, and asks for another chance. Things go well until he brings her to a family party to defy his father, where Raquel is humiliated to see her mother working as a waiter. Her mother tells her that her father was a gifted writer who never dared publish his novel and urges her to be honest with Ares. When Raquel goes to his home, his family turns her away as a distraction. Ares defies them and goes to the prom, where Raquel's friend Yoshi, angry at how he has hurt Raquel, fights him and pushes him into a partly drained pool. Raquel stays at his side in the hospital until he recovers, after which his family lets him choose his own path, and he decides to study medicine in Stockholm. At the airport Ares admits that he broke the family's Wi-Fi on purpose so he could talk to her. Four months later Raquel publishes her own book, Through My Window, and Ares climbs through her window again.

Netflix released the film on 4 February 2022. Critics were negative, with a 0% Rotten Tomatoes rating from six reviews, and Cinemanía faulted its toxic clichés. Two sequels followed in 2023 and 2024.

overview: At the NFL Draft, general manager Sonny Weaver has the opportunity to rebuild his team when he trades for the number one pick. He must decide what he's willing to sacrifice on a life-changing day for a few hundred young men with NFL dreams.
tagline: The greatest victories don't always happen on the field.
title: Draft Day
plot:
Draft Day is a sports drama film that revolves around the story of Sonny Weaver Jr., a general manager of an NFL team who must navigate the complexities of the draft day to secure the player he believes will lead his team to victory. The movie delves into themes of ambition, sacrifice, and the high stakes of professional sports.

At its core, Draft Day is a film about the human cost of success in a cutthroat industry where players are mere commodities. Sonny's relentless pursuit of the perfect draft pick puts him at odds with his own personal life, including his relationships with those closest to him. As he navigates the treacherous waters of the NFL draft, he must confront the moral implications of his decisions and weigh the importance of winning against the value of human connections.

The film also explores the theme of identity, as Sonny struggles to reconcile his own sense of self-worth with the expectations placed upon him by others. His character is defined by his role as a general manager, but as he faces challenges on draft day, he is forced to confront the emptiness that can come from prioritizing success above all else.

Ultimately, Draft Day is a movie about the complexities of human relationships and the difficult choices we must make in pursuit of our goals. It's a story about the high stakes of professional sports, but also about the personal costs of ambition and the importance of staying true to oneself.

overview: Oscar is a small fish whose big aspirations often get him into trouble. Meanwhile, Lenny is a great white shark with a surprising secret that no sea creature would guess: He's a vegetarian. When a lie turns Oscar into an improbable hero and Lenny becomes an outcast, the two form an unlikely friendship.
tagline: Behind every little fish is a great white lie.
title: Shark Tale
plot:
Shark Tale is a computer-animated comedy film released in 2004 by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie takes place in the underwater city of New York, where fish live and thrive.

The story begins with Oscar, a small fish who lives on the outskirts of the city. Oscar dreams of becoming a great hero like his idol, Lenny, a famous fish who saved the city from a shark attack years ago. However, Oscar's life is mundane and uneventful, working as a "fish food" taste-tester for a local restaurant.

One day, while swimming near the surface, Oscar meets Don Lino, a great white shark who rules the ocean with an iron fin. Don Lino is feared by all fish in the city, and his reputation is built on his brutal attacks on other sea creatures. However, Oscar soon discovers that Don Lino's life is not as glamorous as it seems.

As Oscar navigates his new friendship with Don Lino, he also meets Lenny, who has become a legend among the fish for saving the city from sharks. Oscar becomes obsessed with meeting Lenny and earning his respect, but things take a turn when Oscar accidentally kills Don Lino's son, Lenny Jr., in self-defense.

Panicked, Oscar flees the scene and hides behind a coral reef, where he meets Lenny himself. However, to Oscar's surprise, Lenny is not the hero he expected. Instead, Lenny is a cowardly fish who has been hiding from Don Lino for years.

Together, Oscar and Lenny concoct a plan to convince Don Lino that his son was killed by another shark, thereby avoiding a war between sharks and fish. Along the way, they meet a motley crew of fish, including Angie, a sassy fish who becomes Oscar's love interest, and Sykes, a wise-cracking fish who serves as their guide.

As the story unfolds, Oscar learns valuable lessons about bravery, loyalty, and being true to oneself. In the end, Don Lino is convinced that his son was killed by another shark, and he vows to protect the city from other sharks. However, in a surprising twist, it is revealed that Lenny Jr. was actually alive all along, and he has been hiding with Oscar.

The movie ends with Oscar being hailed as a hero for saving Don Lino's life, and he finally earns the respect of his idol, Lenny. The film concludes on a heartwarming note, with Oscar and Angie sharing a romantic moment, and the city of New York thriving in peace.

Overall, Shark Tale is a fun and entertaining animated film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has become a beloved classic among children and families.

overview: When world-famous air racer Dusty learns that his engine is damaged and he may never race again, he must shift gears and is launched into the world of aerial firefighting. Dusty joins forces with veteran fire and rescue helicopter Blade Ranger and his team, a bunch of all-terrain vehicles known as The Smokejumpers. Together, the fearless team battles a massive wildfire, and Dusty learns what it takes to become a true hero.
tagline: When others fly out, heroes fly in.
title: Planes: Fire & Rescue
plot:
Planes: Fire & Rescue is a 2014 animated adventure comedy film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios and directed by Bobs Gannaway. The movie takes place in the fictional town of Piston Peak, where planes live and work together to maintain order and safety.

The story begins with Dusty Crophopper (voiced by Dane Cook), a hotshot fire plane who has just returned from his first big rescue mission. However, he soon realizes that being a hero isn't all it's cracked up to be, as he struggles to live up to the expectations of his friends and family.

Meanwhile, a series of devastating wildfires is sweeping across Piston Peak, threatening the town and its inhabitants. The fire department, led by Captain Skipper (voiced by Ed Harris), is stretched thin trying to keep up with the blazes. Dusty sees this as an opportunity to prove himself and joins the fire department.

However, things take a turn when a new plane, Lil' Dipper (voiced by Curtis Armstrong), arrives in Piston Peak. Lil' Dipper is a rescue plane who specializes in water rescues, but he's also a bit of a show-off and a rival to Dusty. The two planes engage in a series of competitions and one-upmanship, which distracts them from the real issue at hand.

As the wildfires intensify, Dusty and Lil' Dipper are forced to put aside their differences and work together to save Piston Peak. Along the way, they meet a new character, Windlifter (voiced by Wes Studi), a veteran fire plane who becomes a mentor to Dusty.

The movie's climax features an epic rescue mission as Dusty and Lil' Dipper team up to save a group of planes trapped in a burning hangar. The film's ending is heartwarming, as Dusty learns the value of teamwork and humility, and Lil' Dipper finds redemption for his past mistakes.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of humorous moments, including cameos from other Disney characters, such as Felix (voiced by Brad Garrett) and Maru (voiced by Curtis Armstrong). The animation is colorful and vibrant, with a mix of realistic and fantastical elements that bring the world of Piston Peak to life.

Overall, Planes: Fire & Rescue is a fun and action-packed adventure that explores themes of teamwork, humility, and redemption. While it may not be as well-known as some other Disney movies, it has its own unique charm and is sure to delight fans of animation and adventure films.

overview: March 1965. In the heat of the Cold War, the USA and the USSR are competing for supremacy in space. What both superpowers aim for in this race, is to be the first to have a man walk in outer space. To accomplish that, no price is too high and no risk is too great. Now it’s up to the unlikely duo of a seasoned war veteran and a hot-headed test-pilot to fulfill this mission. Two men in a tiny spaceship, without proper testing, facing the complete unknown. They were supposed to do what no man has done before—and no man imagined what would happen next.
tagline: So far from home, so close to disaster
title: The Spacewalker
plot:
The Spacewalker (Russian: Время первых, Vremya Pervykh), also known as The Age of Pioneers or Spacewalk, is a 2017 Russian historical drama film about the cosmonaut Alexei Leonov, the first person to walk in space, who served as a consultant on the production. Directed by Dmitry Kiselyov and co-produced by Timur Bekmambetov and Yevgeny Mironov, it stars Mironov as Leonov and Konstantin Khabensky as the mission commander Pavel Belyayev, with Vladimir Ilyin as the chief designer Sergei Korolev and Alexandra Ursuliak as Leonov's wife Svetlana.

In the 1960s, at the height of the Space Race, the Soviet Union prepares to send a man out of his spacecraft and into open space. A technician dies during construction, engineers doubt the craft's safety, and the Kosmos 57 test vehicle, a stand-in for Voskhod 2, breaks up two weeks before launch for reasons no one can identify. The former wartime pilot Belyayev and the test pilot Leonov are chosen to fly, but when Pavel injures his leg in a parachute landing he is replaced by the young, inexperienced Yevgeny Khrunov, to Alexei's dismay. Pavel recovers through sheer determination and is reinstated. Voskhod 2 launches and Alexei completes his spacewalk to national celebration, but his suit swells so much that he cannot get back into the airlock while the ship is out of contact with ground control. Defying procedure, he enters head first, partly deflates the suit and twists round to close the jammed outer hatch, running out of oxygen and losing consciousness before Pavel pulls him inside and revives him. Ordered to orbit for 22 hours until an automatic landing sequence, the crew detach the airlock, setting the craft spinning, and then find the oxygen pressure rising to dangerous levels. Pavel collapses, and Alexei, hallucinating about his childhood, manages to disconnect the faulty system. When the automatic landing fails, the cosmonauts are allowed to steer manually, and Pavel brings the ship down in the Ural mountains, far off course. Their radio signals are picked up only by an amateur enthusiast on Sakhalin, and a rescue helicopter about to turn back for lack of fuel finally spots Alexei's flare. The two men are later cheered by huge crowds in Moscow.

Released in Russia in April 2017, the film was widely praised by Russian critics, who compared it to Apollo 13, but its gross of 561 million roubles against a 400 million rouble budget was considered a box-office failure.

overview: A teenager transitions from female to male, and his family must come to terms with that fact.
tagline: A Family In Transition
title: 3 Generations
plot:
"3 Generations" is a poignant and heart-wrenching drama that explores the complexities of family relationships, love, loss, and identity. The film delves into the intricate web of connections between three generations of women: Maggie, her mother, and her granddaughter.

At its core, "3 Generations" is a story about the power of female bonds and the ways in which they can both heal and harm us. Through the characters' struggles with addiction, mental health, and self-discovery, the film sheds light on the cyclical nature of trauma and the resilience of the human spirit.

The movie also grapples with themes of identity, particularly for women who have been marginalized or oppressed in their lives. Maggie's journey is a powerful exploration of finding one's own voice and autonomy, while her mother's struggles serve as a reminder of the long-lasting impact of past traumas on future generations.

Furthermore, "3 Generations" touches on the complexities of love and relationships, highlighting both the redemptive power of human connection and the ways in which our choices can both harm and heal us. The film's nuanced portrayal of these themes is both deeply moving and thought-provoking, inviting audiences to reflect on their own experiences with family, love, and identity.

Overall, "3 Generations" is a powerful exploration of the intricate web of relationships that shape our lives, and the ways in which we can both hurt and heal each other.

overview: The Mystery Inc. gang have gone their separate ways and have been apart for two years, until they each receive an invitation to Spooky Island. Not knowing that the others have also been invited, they show up and discover an amusement park that affects young visitors in very strange ways.
tagline: Be afraid. Be kind of afraid.
title: Scooby-Doo
plot:
Scooby-Doo is a 2002 American comedy-supernatural mystery film directed by Raja Gosnell and written by Daniel Waters. The movie is based on the popular Hanna-Barbera cartoon series of the same name.

The story begins with Fred Jones (Freddie Prinze Jr.), Daphne Blake (Sarah Michelle Gellar), Velma Dinkley (Linda Cardellini), Shaggy Rogers (Matthew Lillard), and Scooby-Doo (voiced by Neil Fanning) arriving at the Coolsville High School, where they plan to spend their summer vacation. However, upon arrival, they discover that the school is being haunted by a ghost.

The gang decides to solve the mystery of the haunting, which leads them to uncover a sinister plot involving a rival businessman, Emile Mondavarious (Tim Blake Nelson), who seeks to buy out the school's founder, Mr. Coolidge (John Mahoney). As they dig deeper, they discover that Mondavarious is using his wealth and influence to scare people away from the school, in order to drive down its value.

Throughout their investigation, the gang encounters various supernatural entities, including ghosts, monsters, and a mysterious curse. However, as they progress, it becomes clear that these events are being manipulated by Mondavarious's accomplices, who are using special effects and disguises to create the illusion of paranormal activity.

As the mystery unfolds, Shaggy and Scooby-Doo become increasingly entangled in the plot, often providing comedic relief with their antics. Meanwhile, Velma uses her intelligence and research skills to uncover the truth behind the haunting, while Daphne and Fred work together to gather evidence and expose Mondavarious's scheme.

In the end, the gang discovers that Mondavarious is using a combination of special effects, disguises, and manipulation to create the illusion of paranormal activity. They also learn that he has been trying to buy out the school in order to build a new shopping mall on its site.

With the truth revealed, the gang exposes Mondavarious's scheme, and he is brought to justice. The movie ends with the gang being hailed as heroes for solving the mystery, and they all share a laugh together as Scooby-Doo enjoys his favorite food, Scooby Snacks.

Overall, Scooby-Doo (2002) is a fun and lighthearted take on the classic cartoon series, with plenty of humor, action, and adventure. The movie stays true to the spirit of the original series while also introducing new characters and plot twists to keep things fresh.

overview: Werner Herzog gains exclusive access to film inside the Chauvet caves of Southern France, capturing the oldest known pictorial creations of humankind in their astonishing natural setting.
tagline: Humanity's Lost Masterpiece... in 3D
title: Cave of Forgotten Dreams
plot:
Cave of Forgotten Dreams is a 2010 3D documentary written, directed and narrated by Werner Herzog about the Chauvet Cave in the Ardèche region of southern France, whose walls hold some of the oldest human-made images yet discovered, created more than 30,000 years ago. Herzog's interest was sparked by Judith Thurman's 2008 New Yorker article "First Impressions", and Thurman became one of the film's co-producers. The project was sponsored by the French Ministry of Culture and partly financed by the History channel.

Discovered in 1994, the cave had been sealed for millennia by a rockfall at its entrance, preserving some 420 painted or engraved animal figures, as well as hand prints, animal bones and glittering mineral formations. The film moves slowly through the chambers, letting the camera dwell on the drawings while Herzog muses on what they reveal about the people who made them and about the origins of human imagination. Between these passages he interviews scientists and specialists connected with the site, among them Jean Clottes, Dominique Baffier and Jean-Michel Geneste, along with researchers such as Carole Fritz, Gilles Tosello, Julien Monney and Nicholas J. Conard. The film also visits the nearby Pont d'Arc natural bridge and the nuclear power station at Cruas, and ends with a dedication to Roger Ebert.

Access to Chauvet is tightly restricted. Herzog obtained special permission for six shooting days of four hours each, working with a crew of three, cinematographer Peter Zeitlinger, a sound recordist and an assistant, while lighting the scenes himself with cool, battery-powered lamps. The team had to stay on a narrow metal walkway, wear protective suits and limit their time inside because of high levels of carbon dioxide and radon. Initially sceptical of 3D, Herzog adopted it after visiting the cave, to capture how the painters used the bulges and contours of the rock. The score is by Ernst Reijseger.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2010, and IFC Films acquired U.S. rights days later. Released in 2011, it became the year's highest-grossing independently released documentary in the United States. Critics acclaimed it, with a 96% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 86, and it won best documentary awards from groups including the Los Angeles Film Critics Association and the National Society of Film Critics.

overview: Two brothers, on either side of the law, face off over organized crime in Brooklyn during the 1970s.
tagline: Crime runs in the family.
title: Blood Ties
plot:
Blood Ties is a French television series that premiered in 2009, not 2013. It was created by Luc Besson and Olivier Marchal.

The main themes of Blood Ties revolve around the complex relationships between family members, particularly the intricate web of connections between siblings, parents, and children. The show explores the dark secrets and lies that bind these families together, often leading to tragic consequences.

Throughout the series, the characters grapple with issues such as loyalty, betrayal, power struggles, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The show also delves into themes of identity, trauma, and the cyclical nature of violence within families.

The series features a large ensemble cast, including Rosamund Pike, Karl Urban, and Dougray Scott, among others. It consists of three seasons, each with its own unique storyline while maintaining connections to the overall narrative arc.

Blood Ties received critical acclaim for its writing, acting, and direction, as well as its thought-provoking exploration of complex themes.

overview: A biopic of writer Truman Capote and his assignment for The New Yorker to write the non-fiction book "In Cold Blood".
tagline: In Cold Blood.
title: Capote
plot:
Capote is a 2005 biographical drama film directed by Bennett Miller and written by Dan Futterman, based on Gerald Clarke's 1988 biography of the American novelist Truman Capote. Philip Seymour Hoffman stars in the title role, and the film concentrates on the years in which Capote researched and wrote his 1965 nonfiction book In Cold Blood. The cast also includes Catherine Keener, whose performance earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress.

In 1959, after reading in The New York Times about the murder of the Clutter family on their Kansas farm, Capote tells William Shawn, editor of The New Yorker, that he means to write about the crime. He travels to Kansas with his childhood friend Nelle Harper Lee, who helps him approach the people involved. The lead detective, Alvin Dewey, initially rebuffs him, but Dewey's wife Marie, an admirer of his writing, arranges a dinner, and Dewey gradually warms to him. The suspects, Perry Smith and Richard "Dick" Hickock, are soon caught, and through flattery, bribery and insight Capote gains access to them in prison. Growing attached to Smith, he decides to expand the story into a full-length book. After the two men are convicted and sentenced to death, Capote keeps visiting by bribing the warden, apart from a year writing in Morocco and Spain with his partner Jack Dunphy. Moved by Smith's life story and apparent remorse, Capote helps the killers obtain expert lawyers for an appeal, yet Smith refuses to describe the night of the murders. As the appeals drag on for years, Capote finds himself with a story that has no ending. When Smith finally recounts the killings in detail, Capote recognizes his own callousness. While Lee's novel To Kill a Mockingbird becomes a film, Capote cannot share in her success, sinking into drink. When the last appeal fails, Smith begs him to return, and only a telegram to Lee prompts Capote to go back to Kansas, where he witnesses the executions. When he tells Lee he could do nothing to stop it, she replies that he did not want to. An epilogue notes that the book made Capote famous but that he never finished another before dying of alcoholism-related complications in 1984.

Released by Sony Pictures Classics on September 30, 2005, what would have been Capote's 81st birthday, the film grossed $50 million worldwide on a $7 million budget. It was widely acclaimed, earning five Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, and Hoffman won the Oscar for Best Actor.

original_title: The House with a Clock in Its Walls
overview: When ten-year-old Lewis is suddenly orphaned, he is sent to live with his Uncle Jonathan in a creaky (and creepy) old mansion with a mysterious ticking noise that emanates from the walls. Upon discovering that his uncle is a warlock, Lewis begins learning magic, but when he rebelliously resurrects an evil warlock he must find the secret of the house and save the world from destruction.
tagline: This house knows what makes you tick.
title: The House with a Clock in Its Walls
plot:
The House with a Clock in Its Walls is a 2018 American fantasy horror film directed by Scott Derrickson, based on the 1973 novel of the same name by John Bellairs. The movie stars Jack Black as the protagonist, Lewis Barnavelt, and Owen Vaccaro as his young apprentice, Jonah.

Beginning:
The story starts with Lewis Barnavelt (Jack Black), a talented but reclusive magician who lives in a small town called New Enchantment. Lewis is an orphan who has been living with his cruel aunt, Florence (Catherine O'Hara). On the eve of his 13th birthday, Lewis receives a mysterious letter from a lawyer named Jonathan Barnavelt (Michael Caine), who claims to be his long-lost uncle.

Jonathan reveals that he was a magician and a scholar who had been studying the occult. He warns Lewis about an evil warlock named Zebulon Voldar (Patrick Warburton) who is trying to steal the magical clock in the house where Lewis lives. The clock, which has been ticking for over 100 years, holds the key to unlocking immense magical power.

Plot Development:
Lewis travels to New Enchantment with Jonathan and meets Jonah, a young boy who claims that he can see ghosts. Together, they embark on a journey to uncover the secrets of the house and the mysterious clock. Along the way, Lewis learns about his family's history and discovers that he has inherited his uncle's magical abilities.

As they delve deeper into the mystery, they realize that Zebulon Voldar is using the clock to gain control over the town. The group must work together to stop Voldar and save New Enchantment from destruction.

Ending:
In the climactic final confrontation, Lewis and Jonah face off against Zebulon Voldar in a magical showdown. With the help of his uncle's magic and his own growing powers, Lewis is able to defeat Voldar and shatter the clock, rendering it powerless.

The movie ends with Lewis and Jonah becoming friends and partners in their magical adventures. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that Lewis has found a new family and a sense of belonging in New Enchantment.

Overall, The House with a Clock in Its Walls is a heartwarming and thrilling tale of magic, friendship, and self-discovery. With its blend of humor, adventure, and supernatural elements, the movie is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

overview: After losing their baby, a married couple adopt 9-year old Esther, who may not be as innocent as she seems.
tagline: There's something wrong with Esther.
title: Orphan
plot:
Orphan is a 2009 American psychological horror-thriller film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra and written by Alex Mace. The movie stars Vera Farmiga, Peter Sarsgaard, and Isabelle Fuhrman.

The story begins with the adoption of Esther (Isabelle Fuhrman), an orphaned girl from Eastern Europe, by the Duncan family - Kate (Vera Farmiga) and John (Peter Sarsgaard) along with their six-year-old son Daniel. The Duncans are struggling to cope with the loss of their previous child, who died in a car accident.

Initially, Esther seems like an ideal addition to the family, but strange occurrences start to happen. She is extremely intelligent, obedient, and eerily mature for her age. As time passes, Kate begins to notice that Esther's behavior is not normal, and she starts to suspect that something is amiss.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Esther has a dark secret: she was born with a rare genetic disorder called "progeria," which causes accelerated aging. However, this condition also makes her extremely intelligent and manipulative. Esther's true intentions are slowly revealed as she begins to manipulate the Duncans, using her intelligence and charm to get what she wants.

As Kate becomes more suspicious of Esther, she starts to investigate her past, only to discover that Esther was actually a 12-year-old girl who had been abandoned by her parents in Eastern Europe. The truth about Esther's age is revealed when Daniel discovers an old photograph of Esther as a young girl, which shows her with a younger brother.

The climax of the movie takes place at a family dinner, where Kate confronts Esther about her true identity and intentions. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Esther had been planning to kill Daniel all along, using her intelligence and manipulation to make him believe she was his sister. The movie ends with Kate being killed by Esther, who then escapes.

The ending scene shows an elderly woman, believed to be Esther's mother, visiting the Duncans' home. She is revealed to be a 60-year-old woman, not the young girl Esther claimed to be. This twist suggests that Esther had been lying about her age and identity from the beginning, and that she had been manipulating the Duncans all along.

Overall, Orphan is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of identity, manipulation, and the dangers of underestimating others. The movie features strong performances from its cast, particularly Vera Farmiga and Isabelle Fuhrman, who bring depth and complexity to their characters.

overview: Kyuta, a boy living in Shibuya, and Kumatetsu, a lonesome beast from Jutengai, an imaginary world. One day, Kyuta forays into the imaginary world and, as he's looking for his way back, meets Kumatetsu who becomes his spirit guide. That encounter leads them to many adventures.
tagline: In a world of beasts, he found a family.
title: The Boy and the Beast
plot:
The Boy and the Beast (Bakemono no Ko) is a Japanese animated fantasy adventure of 2015 written and directed by Mamoru Hosoda. Kōji Yakusho voices the beast warrior Kumatetsu, with Shōta Sometani and Aoi Miyazaki as the older and younger Kyūta, Suzu Hirose as Kaede, Mamoru Miyano as Ichirōhiko and Lily Franky as Hyakushūbō.

Nine-year-old Ren has just lost his mother. With no word from his father and refusing to live with his relatives, he runs away into the streets of Shibuya. In the hidden Beast Kingdom, the Grandmaster announces that he will retire to be reborn as a god and names two possible successors: the popular Iōzen, a father of two, and the mighty but lonely and lazy Kumatetsu, whom he urges to take a disciple. Wandering Tokyo with his companion Tatara, Kumatetsu meets Ren and offers to train him. Ren refuses but follows him out of curiosity into the Beast Kingdom and cannot find his way back. Kumatetsu takes him as an apprentice and names him Kyūta. Their early lessons are disastrous, but Kyūta learns by copying his master's movements as he does the chores, soon anticipating his every move.

Eight years later, Kyūta has become a skilled fighter, and their bond has won Kumatetsu followers of his own, including Iōzen's younger son Jirōmaru. Kyūta finds a way back to the human world, where he befriends a student, Kaede, and is reunited with his father. Torn between his two lives, he rejects both his father and Kumatetsu and feels a dark void opening within him, until Kaede calms him and gives him a bracelet. At the succession duel, Kumatetsu falters until Kyūta appears and cheers him to victory. But Iōzen's elder son Ichirōhiko, secretly a human foundling raised as a beast, is consumed by the same darkness; he gravely wounds Kumatetsu and vanishes. Kyūta pursues him, and Ichirōhiko attacks him and Kaede in Tokyo in the form of a monstrous whale. Kyūta prepares to sacrifice himself by absorbing Ichirōhiko's darkness, but Kumatetsu uses his new right as lord to be reborn as a god in the form of a sword, which fills the emptiness in Kyūta's heart. Together they defeat Ichirōhiko without killing him, and he wakes among his adoptive family. Reconciled with his father, Ren chooses to live in the human world, with Kumatetsu forever in his heart.

Released in July 2015, the film topped the Japanese box office, grossed 5.85 billion yen and won Animation of the Year at the Japan Academy Prizes. It scored 88% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: With the first anniversary of her wedding to Tarzan beckoning, Jane ponders how to make it the perfect English celebration.
tagline: Two Worlds - One New Adventure!
title: Tarzan & Jane
plot:
Tarzan & Jane is a direct-to-video animated film produced by Disney Television Animation, released in 2002. The movie serves as a sequel to the original Tarzan film and follows the adventures of Tarzan, now a young adult, and his love interest, Jane Porter.

The story begins with Tarzan (voiced by Tony Goldwyn) living in the jungle with his adoptive father, Kerchak (voiced by Lance Henriksen), and his mother, Kala (voiced by Minnie Driver). However, their peaceful life is disrupted when a group of poachers, led by Clayton (voiced by Nigel Hawthorne), arrives in the jungle. Clayton is revealed to be a former friend of Tarzan's father, who was killed by Kerchak after he betrayed him.

As Tarzan tries to protect his home and family from the poachers, he meets Jane Porter (voiced by Mae Whitman), a young woman who has been stranded in the jungle with her uncle, Professor Archimedes Q. Porter (voiced by Jim Cummings). The two quickly form a bond, and Tarzan begins to learn more about his human heritage.

As the story unfolds, Clayton's true intentions are revealed: he plans to capture Jane and use her as leverage to get revenge on Kerchak and Kala for killing his father. Meanwhile, Tarzan must navigate his feelings for Jane while also confronting his destiny as a leader in the jungle.

The plot thickens when Clayton kidnaps Jane and takes her to his hideout, where he plans to use her as bait to lure Tarzan into a trap. However, Tarzan eventually tracks down Clayton's location and rescues Jane, leading to a thrilling confrontation between the two enemies.

In the end, Tarzan and Clayton engage in an epic battle, with Tarzan emerging victorious. With Clayton defeated, Tarzan is able to reconcile his past and present selves, embracing his human heritage while still honoring his jungle roots. The movie concludes with Tarzan and Jane sharing a romantic moment, as they look towards their future together.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the jungle and its inhabitants to life in a way that is both faithful to the original story and fresh for new audiences. The voice cast delivers solid performances, capturing the essence of the characters and bringing depth to the narrative.

Overall, Tarzan & Jane is a fun and action-packed adventure that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and love. While it may not be as groundbreaking as some other Disney films, it remains a charming and entertaining addition to the Tarzan franchise.

overview: A brilliant but clumsy high school senior vows to get into her late father's alma mater by transforming herself and a misfit squad into dance champions.
tagline: Dance to your own beat.
title: Work It
plot:
Work It is a 2020 American dance comedy film directed by Laura Terruso and written by Alison Peck, and produced by Alicia Keys among others. It follows a group of high school students of different backgrounds as they try to win the Work It dance competition of the title. Sabrina Carpenter stars as Quinn Ackerman, with Liza Koshy as her best friend Jasmine Hale, Keiynan Lonsdale as Julliard Pembroke, Michelle Buteau as the admissions counselor Veronica Ramirez and Jordan Fisher as Jake Taylor.

Quinn, a high school senior, is technical director for the Thunderbirds, her school's elite dance team and reigning Work It champions, until she accidentally starts a fire and is fired by the team's ruthless leader, Julliard. Hoping to attend Duke University, her late father's alma mater, she is told by Ramirez that her application will not stand out, and on impulse she claims to dance for the Thunderbirds. Ramirez vows to watch her perform at Work It. Committing to the lie, Quinn has Jasmine, a Thunderbirds dancer, teach her for the team's open auditions, but Julliard rejects her anyway and sarcastically suggests the two start their own team, so they do. They track down Jake, a former champion sidelined by a knee injury, but he refuses to coach them, insisting that dance comes from passion rather than thinking. The girls recruit a group of unknown dancers with different styles, and after seeing their potential Jake agrees to choreograph if they can qualify on their own, which they do on a technicality as "TBD". During a freestyle session she and Jake kiss. When Julliard reports the team for practising at the studio without paying, Jake loses his job; Quinn's grades fall and she learns that Ramirez has left Duke. Confessing to her mother, Quinn quits the team, angering Jasmine, who returns to the Thunderbirds, and ends things with Jake. Rediscovering her love of dance, she reconciles with Jake and Jasmine, and the team reunites, blending everyone's styles. On competition day Quinn tells her mother that Duke and medicine were her parents' dream, not hers, and arrives mid-performance. TBD narrowly beats the Thunderbirds, a New York Dance Academy scout approaches Jasmine and Julliard, and Ramirez, now at NYU, invites Quinn to apply there.

Work It was released by Netflix on August 7, 2020, topping viewing charts in its debut weekend. It holds an 85% Rotten Tomatoes rating, while Metacritic indicates mixed or average reviews.

overview: Ninja Assassin follows Raizo, one of the deadliest assassins in the world. Taken from the streets as a child, he was transformed into a trained killer by the Ozunu Clan, a secret society whose very existence is considered a myth. But haunted by the merciless execution of his friend by the Clan, Raizo breaks free from them and vanishes. Now he waits, preparing to exact his revenge.
tagline: Fear not the weapon, but the hand that wields it.
title: Ninja Assassin
plot:
Ninja Assassin is a 2009 action-thriller film directed by James McTeigue and written by Justin Marks. The movie stars Rain, Donnie Yen, and Scott Adkins.

The story begins with a young boy named Kai (played by Mika Nakashima), who lives in feudal Japan with his father, a samurai named Kage (played by Kazuki Kitamura). However, their peaceful life is disrupted when Kai's village is attacked by the ruthless Lord Hattori Hanzo (played by Takeshi Kitano) and his men. In an attempt to save his son, Kage sacrifices himself to protect Kai.

Years later, Kai grows up to become a deadly ninja assassin trained by Hanzo, who seeks revenge against those responsible for his father's death. As Kai navigates the treacherous world of ninjas, he begins to question his loyalty to Hanzo and the true nature of his existence as an assassin.

Kai is sent on a mission to kill a young woman named Harima (played by Yuki Morinaga), who has been accused of being a spy. However, Kai soon discovers that Harima is innocent and working for a secret organization known as the "Shadow Syndicate," which seeks to overthrow Hanzo's regime.

As Kai delves deeper into the world of espionage, he meets a mysterious woman named Mika (played by Lucy Liu), who becomes his ally in uncovering the truth about Hanzo's plans. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to stop Hanzo and bring down the Shadow Syndicate.

Throughout the film, Kai struggles with his dual identity as both a ninja assassin and a human being. He grapples with the moral implications of his actions and the consequences of his loyalty to Hanzo. As he navigates this complex web of intrigue, Kai must confront his own demons and make a choice between his duty as an assassin and his growing sense of humanity.

The film's climax features an intense showdown between Kai and Hanzo, with Kai ultimately emerging victorious but not without scars. In the end, Kai has found a new purpose in life, one that allows him to use his skills for good rather than evil. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that Kai may have finally found redemption and a chance to forge a new path.

Overall, Ninja Assassin is an action-packed thrill ride with stunning martial arts sequences and a gripping storyline. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the film has developed a loyal fan base over the years, thanks in part to its unique blend of Eastern and Western influences.

original_title: Dungeons & Dragons: Wrath of the Dragon God
overview: Due to a curse from his former master Profion, Damodar survived his death by Ridley Freeborn as an undead entity in pursuit of an evil artifact for some hundred years, so that he might be capable of unleashing unstoppable destruction on Izmir and the descendants of those who caused his demise.
title: Dungeons & Dragons: Wrath of the Dragon God
plot:
Dungeons & Dragons: Wrath of the Dragon God is an action-adventure film that delves into the world of fantasy and mythology, drawing inspiration from the popular tabletop game. The movie's narrative revolves around a group of characters who must band together to defeat an ancient evil that threatens to destroy their world.

At its core, the film explores themes of friendship, camaraderie, and the power of unity in the face of overwhelming adversity. The main characters, each with their unique skills and abilities, must put aside their differences and work together to overcome the challenges they face. This collective effort serves as a metaphor for the importance of collaboration and cooperation in overcoming even the most daunting obstacles.

The movie also touches on the idea of redemption and personal growth, as some of the characters grapple with past mistakes and seek to make amends. The film's portrayal of these themes is often lighthearted and humorous, adding a layer of depth and complexity to the narrative.

Furthermore, Dungeons & Dragons: Wrath of the Dragon God features a richly detailed world filled with mythical creatures, magical artifacts, and ancient prophecies. This fantastical realm serves as a backdrop for exploring broader themes such as the nature of good and evil, the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control, and the importance of respecting the power of the unknown.

Overall, Dungeons & Dragons: Wrath of the Dragon God is a film that celebrates the spirit of adventure, friendship, and self-discovery, while also acknowledging the complexities and challenges that come with navigating the world.

overview: When architect and Christmas amateur Steven finds himself hosting his family for Christmas, he recruits holiday coordinator Gretchen to bring holiday joy to his home. Gretchen’s expert Christmas spirit brings Steven’s family together, but neither expected it to bring them closer to each other. After a great opportunity presents itself to Gretchen, she and Steven must decide what’s really important in life.
title: Christmas Made to Order
plot:
Christmas Made to Order is a 2018 American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Sam Irvin and written by Matt Marx and Anna White, produced by Hybrid and Production Media Films for Hallmark and first broadcast in December 2018. It stars Alexa PenaVega and Jonathan Bennett, with Jo Marie Payton, Jacob Young, Chelsea Gilson, Andrew Roach and Bailee Michelle Johnson in supporting roles.

Steven (Bennett) is an all-business architect who is about to make partner at his firm if he can win over a major new client, and who even questions a colleague's festive tie. He has a painful meet-cute in his office lobby with Gretchen (PenaVega), a stager for a catalogue company who dreams of turning her hobby of holiday decorating into a business of her own, and who has covered the lobby in garlands and fake snow. When Steven learns that emergency construction work on his sister's house means his whole family will spend Christmas at his place, he panics: he does not even own a string of lights, and they are expecting a perfectly decorated home. He hires Gretchen to transform his bare house, and when the family arrives and is delighted, he persuades her to stay on as his family's Christmas activity coordinator, dangling the chance to become the official decorator for his company's properties. While Steven retreats into his work, Gretchen leads the family through picking out a tree, decorating, making mulled cider at her aunt's inn, personalised stockings and cookie decorating. Her expert Christmas spirit brings the family together; she mediates a squabble between Steven, his sister and her husband and his parents, and counsels his niece, who wants to be a singer rather than a doctor as her father expects. Gradually Steven is drawn back into family life, and he and Gretchen, both single and with her parents no longer living, grow closer. Meanwhile a demanding client rejects Steven's designs, and when a great opportunity presents itself to Gretchen, the two must decide what is really important in life.

Reviewers found it light, feel-good holiday fare. Fits of Fury thought the premise of hiring a "Christmas ambassador" bizarre, but singled out PenaVega for the film's best and funniest moments and her character's gumption, and credited the easy chemistry between the leads as a large reason the film works. The Avocado's tongue-in-cheek recap poked fun at the décor, the fake Christmas tree and the clichéd plot.

overview: When the Primm family moves to New York City, their young son Josh struggles to adapt to his new school and new friends. All of that changes when he discovers Lyle — a singing crocodile who loves baths, caviar and great music — living in the attic of his new home. But when Lyle’s existence is threatened by evil neighbor Mr. Grumps, the Primms must band together to show the world that family can come from the most unexpected places.
tagline: He knows every scale.
title: Lyle, Lyle, Crocodile
plot:
Lyle, Lyle, Crocodile is a 2022 American musical comedy-drama produced and directed by Will Speck and Josh Gordon from a screenplay by William Davies. Made by Columbia Pictures, it adapts Bernard Waber's children's book of the same name and its predecessor, The House on East 88th Street, which had earlier been turned into a 1987 animated HBO musical special. Shawn Mendes provides the singing voice of Lyle, a crocodile who communicates only through song, with Ben Palacios performing his motion capture. Filming took place in New York City in September 2021, and Sony Pictures Releasing opened the film on October 7, 2022.

Hector P. Valenti, a flamboyant showman who keeps failing auditions for a national talent show, finds a singing baby crocodile in an exotic pet shop and names him Lyle. He stakes his Victorian brownstone on their debut, but Lyle freezes with stage fright, Hector loses the house and leaves Lyle to fend for himself while he tries to earn money. Eighteen months later, the Primm family moves in: math teacher Joseph, his wife Katie, a cookbook author, and Joseph's nervous son, Josh, who struggles at his new school. Josh discovers the now fully grown Lyle, and they become friends after Lyle saves him from a mugger. Katie and Joseph overcome their fear and bond with Lyle too.

Hector returns, using an agreement that lets him live in the house part of the year, and tries again to put Lyle on stage, but the crocodile's stage fright returns. Meanwhile the Primms' unfriendly downstairs neighbor, Alistair Grumps, determined to stop the noise, bribes Hector into selling Lyle, who is locked up at the zoo after failing to sing for the authorities. Guilt-ridden, Hector helps Josh break Lyle out and apologizes to him. At the talent show Lyle finally conquers his fear and performs with Josh and the dance troupe of Josh's friend Trudy. When the Primms are taken to court for keeping Lyle, Hector produces his grandmother's deed to the house, which allows any exotic animal to be kept as a pet, and the judge rules in their favor.

Javier Bardem plays Hector, with Winslow Fegley as Josh, Constance Wu as Katie, Scoot McNairy as Joseph and Brett Gelman as Grumps. Reviews were generally positive, with 71% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and particular praise for Bardem, while audiences gave it an A− CinemaScore. It grossed $111 million worldwide against a $50 million budget.

overview: Russian terrorists conspire to hijack the aircraft with the president and his family on board. The commander in chief finds himself facing an impossible predicament: give in to the terrorists and sacrifice his family, or risk everything to uphold his principles - and the integrity of the nation.
tagline: Five miles up, The President of the United States is waging war on terrorism. Face to face.
title: Air Force One
plot:
Air Force One is a 1997 American action thriller film directed by Wolfgang Petersen and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer. The movie stars Harrison Ford as President James Marshall, a former Vietnam War hero who becomes the commander-in-chief of the United States.

The story begins with President Marshall's (Harrison Ford) family - his wife, Nancy (Sally Skerritt), and their two children, Sam (Joe Pesci) and Megan (Evelyn Hartt) - on board Air Force One as it takes off from Andrews Air Force Base in Maryland. The plane is headed to a summit meeting with Russian President Kirin (Gary Oldman).

As the plane reaches cruising altitude, a group of heavily armed terrorists, led by the ruthless and cunning Vladimir (Gary Oldman), infiltrate the cockpit and take control of the aircraft. They are seeking to hold the President hostage in exchange for the release of their imprisoned comrades.

The terrorists, who claim to be members of an anti-American organization, begin to make demands, including the withdrawal of U.S. troops from Russia and the recognition of Russian interests around the world. The President, determined to protect his family and the country, refuses to comply with their demands.

As the situation escalates, Air Force One is forced to fly over hostile territory, making it difficult for the President's team to respond effectively. Meanwhile, the terrorists continue to make threats against the passengers and crew, including a threat to kill the children if their demands are not met.

President Marshall, who has experience as a fighter pilot in Vietnam, takes charge of the situation and uses his military training to outsmart the terrorists. He also works closely with Colonel Thomas "Tom" Gillen (David Suchet), the Air Force One's pilot, to try and regain control of the plane.
