Robert, long an absent parent who shuts himself away to work, now has a baby daughter, Thisbe, with his new wife Heidi. Auden starts helping with the receipts at Heidi's shop, where she meets Leah, Esther and Maggie, who is initially cold to her because Auden made out with her ex-boyfriend. Unable to sleep, Auden wanders the town at night and meets Eli, a BMX rider, who challenges her to a quest to experience everything she missed as a child, from a secret pie shop to mini golf and breaking into the lighthouse. Befriending Maggie and the others, Auden learns that Eli's best friend and riding partner Abe died in an accident while Eli was driving, after which Eli withdrew from everyone. Auden admits that her sleeplessness began in childhood, when she tried to stop her parents from fighting. Eli reluctantly comes to the Fourth of July party, and the two kiss for the first time under the fireworks. When Robert walks out after a quarrel with Heidi, Auden confronts him for always giving up when things become difficult; he returns and finally takes on his responsibilities as a father, and Auden reconciles with her mother. Embarrassed that she cannot ride a bike, Auden lashes out at Eli for abandoning his dream after Abe's death, but she learns to ride with Maggie's help, and Eli returns to competing and wins. To make up for her missed prom, he arrives in a tuxedo, she puts on her prom dress, and their friends join them for a party on the beach. Later, at college, Auden receives a postcard from Eli in Barcelona and heads to lunch with Maggie, now her roommate.

Filmed in and around Carolina Beach, North Carolina, in 2021, the film debuted on Netflix on May 6, 2022. It holds a 57% Rotten Tomatoes rating, with some critics finding it a simplified version of the novel.

overview: An ad creative and a successful exec have a great marriage — until he wants to be a dad just as her star is rising. Then he brings someone new home.
title: You've Got This
plot:
You've Got This (Ahí te encargo) is a Mexican romantic comedy of 2020 directed by Salvador Espinosa from a screenplay by Tiaré Scanda and Leonardo Zimbrón, released worldwide on Netflix. Mauricio Ochmann stars as Alejandro, known as Alex, an advertising creative desperate to become a father, with Esmeralda Pimentel as his wife Cecilia, or Ceci, Regina Reynoso as the waitress Alicia, Matteo Giannini as her baby Alan, and Juan Martín Jáuregui and Moisés Arizmendi in supporting roles.

Alex and Ceci want different things. Ceci, a lawyer at an energy company, is devoted to her career and has no interest in children, while Alex longs for a baby and one day asks her to start a family as soon as possible. She refuses: she has just been offered a partnership at her firm, a rare promotion for a woman, and is thrilled about it. That same day Alex runs into Alicia, a waitress he once promised to help if she ever needed it, and she asks him to look after her baby son Alan for three days while she deals with something important. Reluctantly he agrees and tries to keep the baby hidden at home, but Ceci soon discovers him and furiously insists that the child go back to his mother at once.

The day Alicia is due to return comes and goes, and Alex searches for her in vain until a friend tells him she is back. Returning the baby, he learns that she has been undergoing treatment for brain cancer; she begs him to adopt Alan, and although he refuses, he takes mother and son home when she collapses. Ceci walks in as he invites Alicia to stay, and in the ensuing fight Alex all but admits that he married her to have a child. Ceci moves in with a friend and ignores his calls, finally asking him to be out when she collects her things. Alex plans to adopt Alan and move in with his mother, but he is fired for bringing the baby to work, and when he goes back to apologise he tells his boss frankly how her staff see her; she rejects his advice but agrees to think about rehiring him. He finds Ceci at the meeting that will confirm her promotion and they reconcile, just as word comes that Alicia is in hospital. Ceci's chief tells her the partnership is already hers and she need only sign, so she signs and rushes off with Alex. Alicia dies, and the couple adopt Alan. As Ceci packs for a new post in Hong Kong, Alex reveals plane tickets for himself and the baby to join her.

Filmed over six weeks in Mexico City and Valle de Bravo, the film premiered on Netflix on 2 October 2020.

overview: Steve ‘Spaz’ Williams is a pioneer in computer animation. His digital dinosaurs of Jurassic Park transformed Hollywood in 1993, but an appetite for anarchy and reckless disregard for authority may have cost him the recognition he deserved.
tagline: It took a rebel to change the movies.
title: Jurassic Punk
plot:
Jurassic Punk is a 2022 American documentary film directed by Scott Leberecht about Steve "Spaz" Williams, the visual effects artist whose computer animation at Industrial Light & Magic helped launch the CGI era of filmmaking. The 90-minute film combines interviews, archival material and Williams' own home video footage with new scenes of him at home and in his workshop. Interviewees include ILM veterans Phil Tippett, Mark A.Z. Dippé, Tom Bertino, Stefen Fangmeier and Jamie Hyneman, as well as Williams' former wives and daughter.

Born and raised in Toronto, Williams taught himself cel animation and studied computer graphics at Sheridan College before ILM brought him from Canada in 1988 to animate the water tentacle in James Cameron's The Abyss. Cameron then gave him the job of supervising the morphing effects of the liquid metal T-1000 in Terminator 2: Judgment Day (1991). On Steven Spielberg's Jurassic Park, after being told that the dinosaurs would be created with traditional techniques, Williams made a computer-animated dinosaur test on his own time; when Kathleen Kennedy and Spielberg saw it, CGI moved to the center of the production. The film explores the mixed feelings of Williams and his colleagues about the revolution they unleashed, with Tippett lamenting how studios came to see CGI as a magic bullet that led to bloated spectacle, and it gives voice to Williams' long-held belief that superiors such as Tippett and Dennis Muren took credit for work he largely did. It also portrays him as a hard-drinking, abrasive rebel who clashed with ILM's corporate structure and damaged his career and relationships, and its final act shows him, after three stints in rehab, confronting his addiction and failures on camera, admitting that he has never been an adult.

The documentary was released in theaters and on video on demand in December 2022. Reviews were generally favorable. Matt Zoller Seitz of RogerEbert.com felt the film wavered between hero worship and critical distance and at times seemed unsure of its stance on CGI, but called its bleak, insightful final act strong enough to elevate the whole. Other critics praised its archival material and insight into effects history while noting that it was unevenly balanced.

overview: For high schooler Aaron Corbett, turning 18 means becoming not just a man but a nephilim, too -- half human, half angel, with supernatural abilities.
tagline: A prophecy. A destiny. A fallen angel.
title: Fallen
plot:
Fallen is a 2006 American supernatural fantasy television film, the first part of a three-part miniseries made for ABC Family and based on the young-adult novels by Thomas E. Sniegoski. Directed by Mikael Salomon, known for his work on Band of Brothers and Rome, from a script by Sara Cooper, it stars Paul Wesley as Aaron Corbett, Tom Skerritt as Zeke, Lisa Lackey as Verchiel, Fernanda Andrade as Vilma and Rick Worthy as the archangel Camael, with Chelah Horsdal, Alex Ferris and Byron Mann. It premiered on 23 July 2006, and this first part is subtitled The Beginning.

Each part opens with narration over biblical images telling the legend of the fallen angels and of the Nephilim, half-angel, half-human beings considered abominations, whom soldier angels known as the Powers are determined to purge from the world. Aaron is a troubled orphan who has spent three years with a loving foster family in a small American town. He has become a popular wrestling star at school and has learned to control the violent urges that plagued his past. On his eighteenth birthday, however, he begins to suffer intense headaches, discovers he can understand and speak languages he has never studied, displays sudden bursts of strength and is alarmed to hear the thoughts of his dog Gabriel, all of which disrupts his studies and his budding romance with his classmate Vilma. A homeless man named Zeke, actually a fallen angel in disguise, reveals that Aaron is a Nephilim and that few like him survive the transformation. Aaron also learns that he may be the Redeemer of prophecy, able to absolve fallen angels and send them back to Heaven, which puts him in the sights of the Powers, led by the ruthless Verchiel, who hunt him down.

The two later parts, The Journey and The Destiny, aired in 2007, bringing the full miniseries to over four hours. In Variety, Laura Fries noted that the film follows the books closely in plot, though Verchiel, male in the novels, is played by a woman. She found Cooper's script talky and its symbolism simplistic, and Salomon's camera gimmicks distracting, but credited the film with deeper character development than expected and decent effects. Reviewing the miniseries on DVD Talk, Thomas Spurlin praised Wesley's performance and the supporting cast but found the exposition-heavy story far too long.

overview: Set in the late 19th century. When a ruthless robber baron takes away everything they cherish, a rough-and-tumble, idealistic peasant and a sophisticated heiress embark on a quest for justice, vengeance…and a few good heists.
tagline: Being BAD never looked so GOOD!
title: Bandidas
plot:
Bandidas is a 2006 Spanish comedy film directed by Pedro Almodóvar, produced by Elías Quintero and Ramón Emilio Cebollero for Canal+, and starring Penélope Cruz and Salma Hayek.

The main themes of Bandidas include:

1. Female friendship: The movie revolves around the unlikely friendship between two women from different backgrounds, Guadalupe (Penélope Cruz) and Sara (Salma Hayek), who join forces to become bandits in 1880s Mexico.
2. Empowerment: Through their adventures, Guadalupe and Sara find a sense of freedom and empowerment, breaking free from the societal norms that restrict them as women.
3. Identity: The film explores the characters' struggles with identity, particularly Guadalupe's desire to escape her humble beginnings and Sara's need to assert herself in a male-dominated world.
4. Loyalty and trust: As the two women navigate their partnership, they learn to rely on each other and develop a deep bond of loyalty and trust.
5. Social commentary: The movie offers a satirical take on the patriarchal society of 19th-century Mexico, poking fun at the conventions and hypocrisies of the time.

The film's plot follows Guadalupe and Sara as they embark on a series of misadventures, using their wit, cunning, and charm to evade capture and build a life together. Along the way, they encounter various characters who challenge their perceptions and force them to confront their own desires and limitations.

Overall, Bandidas is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of female friendship, empowerment, and identity, set against the vibrant backdrop of 19th-century Mexico.

overview: Veteran comedy writer Charlie Berns, who is slowly but surely losing his grip on reality, befriends a talented young New York street singer Emma Payge. Together, they form an unlikely yet hilarious and touching friendship that kicks the generation gap aside and redefines the meaning of love and trust.
tagline: You never know who's going to change your life.
title: Here Today
plot:
Here Today is a 2021 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Matt Engle. The movie follows the story of two former high school sweethearts, Ben and Kate, who reconnect at their high school reunion.

The main themes of Here Today revolve around:

1. Second chances: The film explores the idea that people can change and grow over time, and that second chances can lead to new beginnings.
2. Unrequited love: The movie delves into the complexities of unrequited love and the pain of unresolved feelings from the past.
3. Nostalgia: The film is set in the 1990s and features a nostalgic soundtrack, which serves as a reminder of the characters' past experiences and relationships.
4. Self-discovery: As Ben and Kate reconnect, they are forced to confront their own personal growth and the choices they've made in life.

The movie also explores themes of:

* The complexities of female friendships
* The challenges of rekindling old relationships
* The power of music to evoke emotions and memories

Overall, Here Today is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of love, loss, and self-discovery.

overview: Emma's father and her high school frenemy start dating so she embarks on a mission to break up the happy couple.
title: Christmas Is Canceled
plot:
Christmas Is Canceled, also styled Christmas Is Cancelled and previously titled The Fight Before Christmas, is a 2021 American romantic comedy film directed by Prarthana Mohan from a screenplay by Sara Endsley. Produced by Particular Crowd, MarVista Entertainment, Line Film Company and Lionsgate, it stars Hayley Orrantia as Emma Lockhart, Janel Parrish as Brandy Barnes and Dermot Mulroney as Emma's father, Jack, with Emilie Modaff as Emma's best friend Charlyne and Michael Naizu as Josh.

Two years after the death of her mother, Emma still feels the loss keenly and believes it is her duty to look after her widowed father. Returning to her snowy hometown after a research trip to spend the holidays with him, she is horrified to discover that Jack has started dating Brandy, her old high school frenemy. Brandy does her best to keep things friendly, and both she and Jack try to win Emma over, but Emma cannot accept the relationship and vows to break the couple up before Christmas, only four days away. With the reluctant help of Charlyne and a handsome bartender named Josh, she launches a series of fairly mundane schemes to drive the pair apart. No matter what she tries, however, Jack and Brandy shrug off her efforts, even as tensions rise. Consumed by her campaign, Emma ignores the growing attraction between herself and Josh and puts Charlyne in an awkward position, and with her family, her friendships and the holiday itself at stake, she must come to her senses before it is too late. Along the way the film delivers awkward walk-ins, a drunken Christmas party, dramatic exits into the snow, heated arguments and disrupted family traditions.

The film was announced in November 2021 with its three leads, and Parrish promoted it on social media as "knee slapping mayhem" for the holiday season. Renamed from The Fight Before Christmas before its release, it opened theatrically in several European and African countries on 16 December 2021 and was released in the United States on Prime Video the following day. Reviews were mixed, with 59% of critics on Rotten Tomatoes giving it a positive review. Decider's Jade Budowski recommended it as a deeply average but enjoyable 95-minute holiday comedy, full of soapy turns, genuine laughs and some emotionally resonant moments, and singled out Modaff's deadpan supporting performance as the funniest in the film, while noting that the title makes little sense and its conflicts are resolved too easily.

overview: A young boy searches a future world wasteland for a rumored cure for his dying mother.
tagline: It's closer than you think.
title: Future World
plot:
Future World is a 2018 American direct-to-video science fiction action Western co-produced and directed by James Franco, with Bruce Thierry Cheung as co-director. Cheung wrote the screenplay with Jay Davis. The ensemble cast includes Franco, Suki Waterhouse, Jeffrey Wahlberg, Margarita Levieva, Snoop Dogg, Twin Shadow, Method Man, Lucy Liu and Milla Jovovich.

The story is set after advances in artificial intelligence and robotics have led to a global war, leaving survivors scraping by in a wasteland. A ruthless Warlord raids a settlement housing a high-tech lab and activates Ash, an android girl with mismatched blue and green eyes who obeys commands sent from a handheld remote. Meanwhile, in the Oasis, a fertile haven, a young man known as the Prince sets out into the wasteland to find medicine for his sick mother, the Queen, guided only by a faded postcard of Paradise Beach.

The Prince and his companions stop at Love Town, a settlement trading in sex slaves run by the pimp Big Daddy Love Lord. An offer of help there turns out to be a trap laid by the Warlord, and Ash captures the Prince and kills his friends. Forced to lead the Warlord back to the Oasis, the Prince is rescued by Ash, who realizes the Warlord will kill everyone there; she is damaged in the escape, and he drags her inert body across the wasteland to the ocean. There they are captured by people living in the ruins of a seaside resort, ruled by the Drug Lord, who promises him the cure only if he survives a gladiator-style fight. A captive mechanic, Lei, repairs Ash, and the two fall for each other. The Prince wins his fight and the medicine, but the Drug Lord keeps Ash and, jealous of Lei, orders Lei to wipe Ash's memory and reprogram her as her companion. When the Warlord attacks the resort, he kills the Drug Lord, captures the escaping trio and orders Ash by remote to kill her friends; instead she kills his men, stabs him and flees with Lei and the Prince on Raider motorbikes, then kills the Warlord in a final stand. Back at the Oasis, the Prince gives the Queen her medicine while Ash leaves with Lei to find others like herself. In a mid-credits scene, Ash frees the slaves of Love Town, who turn on Big Daddy.

Lionsgate Premiere released Future World on May 25, 2018. Critics panned it, with a 0% Rotten Tomatoes approval rating from nine reviews and a Metacritic score of 10, indicating overwhelming dislike. The Hollywood Reporter called it a low-rent tale that failed as homage or parody.

overview: In an alternate present-day version of Oakland, black telemarketer Cassius Green discovers a magical key to professional success – which propels him into a macabre universe.
tagline: Destiny Is Calling
title: Sorry to Bother You
plot:
Sorry to Bother You is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of capitalism, racism, and the struggle for identity. The movie follows Cassius Green, an aspiring telemarketer who discovers his unique voice allows him to effortlessly sell products to white customers, while struggling to connect with his African American community.

The film's main theme revolves around the dehumanizing effects of capitalism on individuals, particularly those from marginalized communities. As Cassius becomes more successful in his job, he begins to lose touch with his own identity and values, becoming a pawn in the corporate machine. The movie critiques the ways in which capitalism exploits and objectifies people, reducing them to mere commodities.

The film also explores the theme of racism and its insidious presence in everyday life. Cassius's experiences as a black man in a predominantly white world serve as a microcosm for the systemic racism that pervades American society. The movie highlights how racism can manifest in subtle yet damaging ways, often masquerading as neutrality or indifference.

Furthermore, Sorry to Bother You touches on the theme of identity and performance. Cassius's ability to adopt different personas and voices allows him to navigate his environment with ease, but also raises questions about the nature of authenticity and selfhood. As he becomes more entrenched in his corporate persona, he begins to lose touch with his own desires and aspirations.

Ultimately, the film presents a powerful critique of the societal systems that perpetuate inequality and oppression. Through Cassius's journey, the movie offers a searing commentary on the human cost of capitalism and racism, inviting viewers to confront the uncomfortable truths about their own complicity in these systems.

overview: Tripp is a high school senior with a knack for building trucks who makes an incredible discovery - a gas-guzzling creature named Creech. To protect his mischievous new friend, Tripp hides Creech under the hood of his latest creation, turning it into a real-life super-powered Monster Truck. Together, this unlikely duo with a shared taste for speed team up on a wild and unforgettable journey to reunite Creech with his family.
tagline: Meet Creech
title: Monster Trucks
plot:
Monster Trucks is a 2016 American science fiction monster comedy film directed by Chris Wedge and produced by Paramount Pictures.

The movie begins with a flashback to when the main character, Blake Henderson (played by Lucas Till), was a young boy who befriends a girl named Eve (played by Jane Levy) in their small town of Malden. The two share a love for monster trucks and spend countless hours playing with them. However, their friendship is short-lived as Eve's father, a scientist, takes her away to study the effects of a mysterious substance on the environment.

Years later, Blake returns home after serving in the military and finds that his father has passed away, leaving him the family farm. He decides to restore it to its former glory but soon discovers that the town is facing an environmental disaster caused by a toxic substance known as "Nitro." The Nitro was created by Eve's father and has been leaking into the environment, causing widespread destruction.

As Blake tries to find a way to stop the Nitro, he stumbles upon a mysterious truck with glowing blue eyes. He names it "Monster" and discovers that it has the ability to transform into different vehicles, including a monster truck, a car, and even a plane. The Monster is revealed to be an alien creature that was sent to Earth as part of Eve's father's experiment.

As Blake tries to understand the Monster's abilities, he also teams up with Eve (played by Hannah John-Kamen) who has returned to Malden after her father's death. Together, they embark on a mission to stop the Nitro and save their town from destruction.

The plot thickens as they discover that the Nitro is not just an environmental disaster but also a threat to humanity. The Monster, with its incredible powers, becomes the key to stopping the Nitro and saving the world.

In the climactic final battle, Blake and Eve face off against the main antagonist, a villainous scientist who has been using the Nitro for his own gain. With the help of the Monster, they manage to defeat the villain and stop the Nitro from destroying the town.

The movie ends with Blake and Eve sharing a romantic moment as the town begins to rebuild itself. The Monster is seen flying away into the sky, its glowing blue eyes fading into the distance as it returns to its alien home.

Overall, Monster Trucks is an action-packed adventure film that combines science fiction and comedy elements. With its impressive visual effects and thrilling plot twists, it's a fun ride for audiences of all ages.

overview: When a big-city family moves to a remote town, two young brothers and their new friends try to solve the menacing mystery that haunts their home.
title: The Scary House
plot:
The Scary House (German: Das schaurige Haus) is a 2020 Austrian-German family horror film directed by Daniel Prochaska, his first feature for cinemas. The screenplay by Marcel Kawentel and Timo Lombeck adapts the 2011 novel of the same name by Martina Wildner, part of her Allgäu horror trilogy. It stars León Orlandianyi, Benno Rosskopf and Julia Koschitz, and was produced by Gerald Podgornig and Thomas Hroch of Austria's Mona Film with Germany's Naked Eye Filmproduktion, in association with ORF.

Sixteen-year-old Hendrik (Orlandianyi) moves with his mother Sabine (Koschitz) and his eight-year-old brother Eddi (Rosskopf) from Hanover to Bad Eisenkappel in Carinthia, where Sabine has taken a job at the Obir dripstone caves. The move is also meant to help the family cope with the father's death in an accident. For Hendrik it is a culture shock: the locals speak a dialect he can barely understand, and something seems wrong with the run-down house that estate agent Gerold Röckl (Michael Pink) found for them. Eddi starts sleepwalking and speaking Slovene, Hendrik is plagued by nightmares, and their mother grows increasingly desperate. After a difficult start the brothers make friends with the bold Ida (Marii Weichsler) and the nerdy Fritz (Lars Bitterlich), and the four set out to uncover the secret of the house.

The film departs from the book in several ways: the brothers were made older, they arrive with their widowed mother rather than both parents, and because the setting moved from the Allgäu to Carinthia, Slovene replaced the novel's Romanian. It was shot over 34 days in the summer of 2019 in Vienna and southern Carinthia. Following a premiere at the Wildenstein waterfall in Gallizien in September 2020 and a screening at Vienna's SLASH festival, it opened in Austrian cinemas on 30 October 2020 and reached Netflix in May 2021, where it entered the top ten in more than 50 countries.

Germany's film rating agency FBW gave it the rating "particularly valuable", praising suspense that goes well beyond typical children's adventures and a well-timed horror effect. Christian Klosz of Film plus Kritik commended its story, witty dialogue and the culture clash between the city family and local Carinthian colour, and The New York Times called it an effective family horror film. It won the audience award for best youth film at the Goldener Spatz and earned four Austrian Film Award nominations, including for Koschitz and Pink.

overview: Against the backdrop of a turbulent era in Brazil, this documentary captures Pelé's extraordinary path from breakthrough talent to national hero. Mixing rare archival footage and exclusive interviews, this documentary celebrates the legendary Brazilian footballer who personified football as art.
title: Pelé
plot:
Pelé is a 2021 biographical documentary about the Brazilian footballer Pelé, directed by Ben Nichols and David Tryhorn and produced for Netflix, with Kevin Macdonald, Jon Owen and Jonathan Rogers as executive producers. Combining extensive archival footage with new interviews, it charts the player's journey from breakthrough talent to national hero against the backdrop of a turbulent era in Brazilian history, including the military dictatorship.

The film follows Pelé from his childhood to his debut for Santos at 15, his selection for Brazil at 16 and the 1958 World Cup final, in which he scored twice at the age of 17. Overnight a global icon, he became football's first millionaire while still a teenager, and in a candid interview he admits that he found it hard to remain faithful amid the adulation, saying he had affairs, some of which produced children he learned about only later. Brazil's group-stage exit at the 1966 World Cup in England, where he was injured again, is described by Pelé as the saddest moment of his life, and he vowed at the time never to play in another tournament. The documentary sets his career against the 1964 military coup and the repression that followed, and asks whether he knew of the torture carried out by the regime; he concedes that it would be a lie to say he was unaware. Former teammate Paulo Cézar Caju criticises him for never speaking out, while journalist Juca Kfouri describes how winning the 1970 World Cup became a matter of state, with military personnel among the team staff and pressure on Pelé to play. The film recounts his feud with coach João Saldanha, who claimed Pelé's eyesight was failing before being replaced by Mário Zagallo, and culminates in Brazil's 4–1 victory over Italy in the 1970 final in Mexico, in which Pelé scored and set up two goals, making him the only player with three World Cup titles. His later years at Santos and his final spell with the New York Cosmos are also covered.

Alongside Pelé himself, now able to walk only with assistance, the film features family members, former teammates, coaches, journalists and politicians. Netflix released it on February 23, 2021. Reviews were moderately positive, with 82% on Rotten Tomatoes; The Guardian's Andrew Pulver found it admiring but more sedate than Asif Kapadia's Maradona film, praising its context on the 1960s, while The Hollywood Reporter called it a polished, well-intentioned biography.

overview: Four sons of well-known New York mobsters must retrieve a bag of cash from a small Montana town ruled by a corrupt sheriff.
tagline: If they don't finish the job, their fathers will finish them.
title: Knockaround Guys
plot:
Knockaround Guys is a 2001 American action comedy film directed by Brian Koppelman. The movie follows two friends, Nick and Chris, who are struggling to find their place in the world after college. They decide to start a small business, a car wash, but things take an unexpected turn when they get involved with a group of rough-around-the-edges men who are into street racing.

The main theme of Knockaround Guys is the struggle for identity and belonging. The two main characters, Nick and Chris, are trying to find their way in life after college and are drawn to the wrong crowd, which represents a world that is both exciting and treacherous. As they become more involved with this group, they must confront the consequences of their choices and decide whether to conform or forge their own path.

The movie also explores themes of loyalty, friendship, and the corrupting influence of power. The characters are drawn into a world of crime and violence, which threatens to destroy their relationships and their sense of self. Through the characters' experiences, the film highlights the dangers of getting caught up in a lifestyle that is not aligned with one's values.

Overall, Knockaround Guys is a coming-of-age story about two young men trying to find their place in the world and navigate the challenges of growing up. The movie features a mix of action, comedy, and drama, making it an entertaining and thought-provoking watch.

overview: The directorial debut of Dustin Hoffman, Quartet is a high-drama comedy about temperamental divas and old grudges, passion and pride, romance and Rigoletto. At a home for retired musicians, the annual concert to celebrate Verdi's birthday is disrupted by the arrival of Jean, an eternal diva and former wife of one of the residents. Expect poignancy and plenty of laughs.
tagline: Four Friends Looking For A Little Harmony
title: Quartet
plot:
Quartet is a 2012 British comedy-drama film directed by Dustin Hoffman, in his directorial debut, and based on Ronald Harwood's play, which ran in London's West End from 1999 to 2000. Harwood adapted his own play, which he wrote after seeing the documentary Tosca's Kiss about Verdi's home for retired opera singers in Milan. The cast is led by Maggie Smith, Tom Courtenay, Billy Connolly, Pauline Collins and Michael Gambon, and many of the supporting players are genuine retired professional musicians.

At Beecham House, a retirement home for former professional musicians, the residents include the retired opera singers Reg, Wilf and Cissy, who often worked together, the former director Cedric Livingstone and the diva Anne Langley. Although all suffer the ailments of old age, they remain engaged in music. The home faces closure for lack of money, and its hopes rest on the annual gala concert on Verdi's birthday, but Cedric is desperate because several prominent performers have died or declined to take part. Reg, Wilf and Cissy sang on a celebrated recording of Rigoletto, regarded by opera lovers as the definitive post-war version with its famous quartet. Reg is shocked when the recording's missing soprano, his former wife Jean Horton, moves into the home without his being consulted, since their marriage ended bitterly. In time, Reg accepts that her infidelity is in the past. Cedric's plan is to reunite the quartet for the gala and sell enough tickets to save the home. Reg agrees, but Jean, who vowed never to sing again after retiring, storms out of a dinner when they raise the idea. When Cissy brings her flowers the next morning, Jean strikes her with them, worsening Cissy's fragile mental state, and later, full of remorse, she apologizes and agrees to sing once she learns that the quartet would close the evening in place of Anne Langley's "Vissi d'arte". Moments before they go on, a confused Cissy tries to leave to return to her family, but Jean calms her, confessing that she still loves Reg, who overhears. As the singers walk onstage to applause, Reg renews his proposal, Jean accepts and takes his hand, and the quartet begins to sing.

Filmed at Hedsor House in Buckinghamshire, Quartet premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2012 and opened in Britain on 1 January 2013. Reviews were generally positive, with an 80% Rotten Tomatoes rating and praise for Hoffman's affectionate direction and the cast's charm.

overview: In the Chatterley’s country estate, monotonous days follow one after the other for Constance, trapped by her marriage and her sense of duty. During spring, deep in the heart of Wragby forest, she encounters Parkin, the estate’s gamekeeper. A tale of an encounter, a difficult apprenticeship, a slow awakening to sensuality for her, a long return to life for him. Or how love is but one with experience and transformation.
title: Lady Chatterley
plot:
Lady Chatterley is a 2006 film adaptation of the novel by D.H. Lawrence, directed by Laurence Dunmore and produced by ARTE France Cinéma. The movie explores the complex and tumultuous relationship between Lady Constance Chatterley, a young woman from a wealthy family, and Oliver Mellors, her husband's gamekeeper.

At its core, Lady Chatterley is a film about the struggle for identity, autonomy, and self-discovery in a society that restricts women's choices and desires. The movie delves into the themes of class, privilege, and the constraints placed on individuals by their social status. Lady Constance, trapped in a loveless marriage with the wealthy but emotionally distant Sir Clifford Chatterley, must navigate her own desires and sense of self-worth.

The film also explores the tension between nature and civilization, as embodied by the contrast between Oliver Mellors' connection to the natural world and Lady Constance's confinement within the stifling social norms of her family. Through their relationship, Lawrence critiques the societal expectations placed on women, highlighting the ways in which they are forced to choose between conformity and authenticity.

Furthermore, Lady Chatterley is a powerful exploration of the human need for intimacy, connection, and physical expression. The movie's portrayal of Oliver Mellors' passion and sensuality serves as a counterpoint to the stifling emotional repression of Lady Constance's marriage, highlighting the importance of embracing one's desires and needs.

Ultimately, the film presents a nuanced and complex exploration of the human experience, one that challenges societal norms and expectations while celebrating the beauty and power of individual desire.

overview: A DEA agent whose family was slain as part of a conspiracy, and an assassin out to avenge her sister's death, join forces to solve a series of murders in New York City.
tagline: When a man has lost everything, he only has revenge.
title: Max Payne
plot:
Max Payne is a 2008 neo-noir action film adapted from the video game series developed by Remedy Entertainment and published by Rockstar Games. John Moore directed and co-produced it from a screenplay by Beau Thorne. Mark Wahlberg plays the title character, with Mila Kunis as Mona Sax, Ludacris as Jim Bravura and Beau Bridges as B.B. Hensley; Chris O'Donnell also appears.

A New York detective in the NYPD Cold Case Unit, Max is consumed by the search for whoever killed his wife, Michelle, and their baby daughter, Rose. He falls under suspicion when Natasha, an acquaintance of one of his informants, is murdered and his wallet, which she had stolen, turns up at the scene. His former partner, Alex Balder, is killed after telling Max that Natasha's death may be linked to his family's murder, and Internal Affairs lieutenant Bravura is assigned to bring Max in. With Natasha's sister Mona, a freelance assassin, Max learns that Natasha's tattoo depicts Valkyrie wings. He discovers that papers from Michelle's time at the pharmaceutical firm Aesir are missing and learns from her former supervisor that she helped develop Valkyr, a military super-soldier drug that drove most users to hallucinations and insanity before the project was buried. The supervisor agrees to testify but is killed by Aesir contractors disguised as SWAT officers, and Max escapes with a video featuring Jack Lupino, a former Marine who was one of the few successful test subjects.

Max confronts Lupino, now a gangster dealing Valkyr, and is losing their fight when B.B., Aesir's security chief and a father figure to Max, shoots Lupino. B.B. then admits he has been selling Valkyr for profit and killed Michelle when she found evidence against him. He tries to drown Max to stage a suicide, but Max escapes into the icy river and survives by swallowing vials of Valkyr, which bring vivid hallucinations and near invulnerability. Aided by Mona, he storms Aesir's headquarters and kills B.B. on the helipad. A post-credits scene hints at a new pursuit involving Aesir's chief executive, Nicole Horne.

Max Payne was released in Australia on October 16, 2008, a day ahead of its U.S. opening. It debuted at number one in North America with about $17.6 million and grossed roughly $85 million worldwide against a $35 million budget. Reviews were mostly negative: Rotten Tomatoes gave it 15%, its consensus citing stylish action undercut by an illogical plot and overdirection, and it scored 31 on Metacritic.

overview: While investigating a terroristic threat that goes viral online, Korean authorities discover that a suspect has recently boarded an international flight bound for the United States. When a healthy passenger on the same flight suddenly dies a gruesome death of unknown cause, panic erupts both in-flight and on the ground. With steadily decreasing fuel and international refusals to offer aid, the captain and crew will be forced to take unprecedented emergency measures in an attempt to save the lives of their passengers.
tagline: Take your seat.
title: Emergency Declaration
plot:
Emergency Declaration is a 2022 South Korean thriller film directed by Lee Jeong-ho, produced by Showbox.

The movie follows the story of Kang Min-kyu (played by Song Kang), a young doctor who works as an emergency room physician at a hospital in Seoul. One day, while reviewing patient records, he discovers that one of his patients, a 17-year-old girl named Kim Ji-soo (played by Cho Yeo-jeong), has been declared dead by the hospital's system.

Min-kyu is shocked and decides to investigate further, as he believes that the death was not due to natural causes. He starts questioning the patient records and discovers that there are several other patients who have also been incorrectly declared dead. Min-kyu becomes obsessed with uncovering the truth behind these deaths and sets out on a mission to expose the hospital's errors.

As Min-kyu delves deeper into the mystery, he faces resistance from his colleagues and superiors at the hospital, who are more concerned with maintaining their reputation than with revealing the truth. Despite this, Min-kyu remains determined to uncover the truth and bring justice to the families of the deceased patients.

Throughout the movie, Min-kyu's investigation takes him on a journey through the dark underbelly of the Korean healthcare system, where corruption and incompetence are rampant. Along the way, he encounters a cast of characters who are equally flawed and complex, including his colleagues, his superiors, and even some of the patients' families.

As the story unfolds, Min-kyu's obsession with uncovering the truth becomes increasingly all-consuming, leading him to question his own identity and purpose. The movie builds towards a tense and suspenseful climax as Min-kyu confronts the hospital administrators and demands answers about the deaths.

Overall, Emergency Declaration is a gripping thriller that explores themes of mortality, morality, and the human condition. With its tight script, strong performances, and thought-provoking subject matter, it's no wonder that this movie has resonated with audiences worldwide.

overview: This film, based on the web series, features nine vignettes in the lives of LGBT people as they date and hook up in Los Angeles.
title: Coffee House Chronicles: The Movie
plot:
The Hole in the Ground is a psychological horror film that delves into the complexities of motherhood, grief, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie follows a young mother, Sarah, who becomes increasingly unhinged as she tries to protect her son from an unknown threat.

At its core, The Hole in the Ground explores the intense emotional turmoil that can arise when a parent's perception of their child is challenged. As Sarah's grip on reality begins to slip, the film raises questions about the fragility of motherly love and the devastating consequences of trauma.

The movie also touches on the theme of grief and loss, as Sarah struggles to come to terms with her own past traumas and the pain of losing a loved one. Her fixation on protecting her son becomes an all-consuming force that drives her actions, leading to a downward spiral of paranoia and desperation.

Throughout the film, the director skillfully crafts a sense of unease and tension, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is just Sarah's fevered imagination. The result is a thought-provoking and deeply unsettling exploration of the darker aspects of human psychology.

overview: When Superman and the rest of the Justice League are kidnapped, Krypto the Super-Dog must convince a rag-tag shelter pack - Ace the hound, PB the potbellied pig, Merton the turtle and Chip the squirrel - to master their own newfound powers and help him rescue the superheroes.
tagline: Sit, stay, save the world.
title: DC League of Super-Pets
plot:
DC League of Super-Pets is a 2022 American superhero comedy film directed by Jared Hess and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The movie follows the story of Krypto, Superman's loyal canine companion, who gets separated from his owner Kal-El (Superman) during a chaotic event in Metropolis. Krypto finds himself lost and alone in the city, where he meets a stray dog named Ace, who becomes his new friend and partner.

As they navigate their way through the city, they stumble upon a group of pets with superpowers, including Bat-Bat, Catwoman's cat, Mowzer; Kite Man's kite-flying dog, Kitey; and Lobo's alien dog, Tark. The pets are being hunted by a villainous organization known as Vortex, led by the sinister Vortex (played by Jemaine Clement).

Krypto and Ace soon discover that they have superpowers of their own, which they use to help the other pets evade capture and ultimately defeat Vortex's minions. Along the way, they also learn valuable lessons about teamwork, loyalty, and what it means to be a true hero.

As Krypto and Ace work together with the other pets, they begin to uncover a sinister plot by Vortex to steal the powers of all the super-powered animals in Metropolis. The pets must band together to stop Vortex and save their city from destruction.

Throughout the movie, the animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the world of DC Comics to life in a fun and imaginative way. The voice cast, including Kevin Hart as Ace, Keanu Reeves as Bat-Bat, and John Krasinski as Superman/Kal-El, deliver hilarious performances that add to the film's comedic charm.

Overall, DC League of Super-Pets is a heartwarming and action-packed adventure that celebrates the power of friendship and teamwork. With its colorful animation, witty humor, and exciting superhero action sequences, it's a fun movie for both kids and adults to enjoy.

overview: The thin line between love and hate turns deadly when a wife discovers her husband’s affair — and they both take extreme measures to get what they want.
title: Loving Adults
plot:
Loving Adults (Danish: Kærlighed for voksne) is a 2022 Danish drama film directed by Barbara Topsøe-Rothenborg. Dar Salim stars as Christian Holm and Sonja Richter as his wife, Leonora, with Sus Wilkins as Xenia, Mikael Birkkjær as the police commissioner and Lars Ranthe as Kim.

The story is framed as a tale told by a police commissioner to his daughter. Christian works in construction alongside his friend Peter, while Leonora gave up a career as a violinist years earlier to care for their son, Johan, whose illness is finally in remission as he nears his high school graduation. When Christian receives a 4 a.m. text he claims is from Peter and smashes his phone rather than show it to her, Leonora suspects an affair with Xenia, a young architect working with him on a contract. At an office party she catches the two having sex, with Xenia meeting her gaze. When Christian tries to end the marriage, Leonora threatens to report that he embezzled company money to pay for Johan's treatment unless he leaves Xenia. Seeking leverage, Christian learns from an old schoolmate of Leonora's that her former boyfriend Mike died in a mysterious fall from a cliff during a party, and he accuses her of pushing him. Thrown out of the house, Christian waits on Leonora's usual running route and runs her down with a company van, only to find her arriving home safely, having taken another route; he has hit a different woman. Shaken, he pretends to have ended the affair.

Leonora notices that Christian washed the van and realizes he meant to kill her. She tries to turn him in, but he persuades the commissioner of his innocence for the time being. She then confesses to Christian that she did kill Mike and insists that he help her kill Xenia, reasoning that he will not try to murder her again if he has no one to leave her for. At a spa resort, Leonora creates an alibi by playing a recording of his voice and sending Xenia a breakup message from his phone while Christian slips away to Xenia's allotment. He reconciles with Xenia instead, but Leonora, having predicted he would not go through with it, stabs Xenia to death. The commissioner, suspicious, brings police dogs, which bark at a Sankt Hans bonfire; he realizes the body is hidden inside, but Christian lights it before he can stop him. The commissioner's story is revealed to be a cautionary tale told to his daughter before her wedding, and abroad, a grieving Christian scatters Xenia's remains in the water.

overview: A journey into uncharted and forbidden territory through three tales tangled in space and time.
tagline: All stories end here.
title: Books of Blood
plot:
Books of Blood is a 2020 anthology horror film directed by Mike Flanagan, based on the comic book series of the same name by Joe Hill. The story revolves around three novellas from the original comic book series.

The main themes of Books of Blood (2020) include:

1. **Trauma and its effects**: Each novella explores the devastating consequences of trauma on individuals and their loved ones. The stories delve into the long-term effects of traumatic events, such as grief, guilt, and the struggle to cope with the past.

2. **The power of storytelling**: The film highlights the significance of storytelling in shaping our understanding of ourselves and the world around us. Through the novellas, Flanagan showcases how stories can be both a source of comfort and a tool for manipulation.

3. **The blurred lines between reality and fiction**: Books of Blood often blurs the boundaries between what is real and what is imagined. This theme is particularly evident in the first novella, "Nancy", which explores the idea that our perceptions of reality can be influenced by the stories we tell ourselves.

4. **Grief and loss**: The film grapples with the complexities of grief and loss, often leaving the characters (and the audience) questioning what it means to move on from traumatic events.

5. **The cyclical nature of violence**: Throughout the novellas, Flanagan touches on the idea that violence can be a self-perpetuating cycle, with each act of violence leading to further trauma and suffering.

Overall, Books of Blood (2020) is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, delving into themes that are both hauntingly familiar and unsettlingly new.

overview: For her entire life, the cult she was born into has been all that teenage Selah has known. Along with a band of similarly cloistered young women she lives seemingly unstuck in time, cut off from modern society in a remote forest commune presided over by a man called Shepherd, a controlling, messiah-like figure with a frightening dark side. But when her insular world is rocked by a series of nightmarish visions and disturbing revelations, Selah begins to question everything about her existence—including her allegiance to the increasingly dangerous Shepherd.
title: The Other Lamb
plot:
The Other Lamb is a 2019 horror film directed by Małgorzata Szumowska and written by Catherine Smyth-McMullen, based on her short story "The Other-faced Lamb". Raffey Cassidy stars as Selah, a teenage girl raised in a cult, with Michiel Huisman as its leader, the Shepherd, and Denise Gough as Sarah, one of his first wives.

Selah lives in a remote forest compound run by a polygamist cult whose messianic leader, the Shepherd, is its only man. The women are divided into the younger Sisters, dressed in blue, and the older Wives, dressed in red, and the group raises sheep for food and sacrifice. As she grows up, Selah draws more of the Shepherd's attention and seems attracted to him, while wondering about her mother, who she was told died giving birth to her. Sent with leftovers to the dark hut where "unclean" menstruating women are kept, she meets Sarah, a scarred and banished Wife, who warns her about the Shepherd's violence. When a police officer orders the group to move on, the Shepherd leads the women on a long trek toward a new home. After Selah begins to menstruate she is forced to walk at the back with Sarah, who reveals that she and Selah's mother were the first two wives and that her mother died of an infection because the Shepherd refused to take her to hospital. On the journey a pregnant Wife dies in childbirth, the Shepherd treats her grieving daughter harshly, and Sarah leaves with the newborn, whom he wanted to abandon because "there can only be one ram in a flock". When he beats a Sister named Tamar, Selah's doubts deepen. At a lakeside valley he proclaims their new Eden, but Selah is haunted by visions of him drowning her and, after he chooses her for sex and chokes her, dreams of the women devouring him. The next morning the Wives have vanished, and the Shepherd tells the Sisters that they have ascended and must take their place. Selah defies him, declaring that he is not their shepherd. Later, police find the Wives' bodies washed up on the shore and the Shepherd's corpse strung between two trees with ram's horns on his head, while the Sisters, led by Selah, gather at a waterfall near their old compound.

Shot in County Wicklow, Ireland, the film premiered at the 2019 Toronto International Film Festival. IFC Midnight released it in the United States on 3 April 2020, largely on video on demand because of pandemic closures. Reviews were generally favourable, with a 75% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

overview: A girl falls for the "perfect" guy, who happens to have a very fatal flaw: he's a hitman on the run from the crime cartels who employ him.
tagline: They make a killer couple.
title: Mr. Right
plot:
Mr. Right is an American romantic action comedy of 2015 directed by Paco Cabezas from a screenplay by Max Landis. Anna Kendrick stars as Martha McKay, a relentlessly upbeat young woman who discovers that her new boyfriend is a former hitman, played by Sam Rockwell, with Tim Roth as his old partner and mentor Hopper, James Ransone and Anson Mount as the brothers Von and Richard Cartigan and RZA as the gunman Steve.

Francis Munch, a former CIA agent turned mercenary, has developed the habit of killing the people who try to hire him to kill. After one such job he survives an ambush by a team including a killer named Espinoza; Hopper backs out of the attack and merely watches. Munch then asks out Martha, and they fall for each other at once. After he dodges another attempt by Espinoza, they spend a chaste night together, and the following evening he reluctantly kills Espinoza when attacked over dinner. Over hot chocolate, Munch explains that a current runs beneath all things that can be sensed in advance, and that she shares the gift; when he throws a knife at her, she catches it by the blade without a scratch.

Von Cartigan, the sole survivor of an earlier massacre in which Munch wiped out the Pirrello heroin syndicate, plots with his partner Johnny Moon to have his brother Richard killed by Munch, knowing that Munch kills those who hire him. Munch kills the middleman sent instead in front of Martha, who asks for space. Richard sends Von, Moon and a squad of hitmen, including Steve, to Martha's apartment. Munch fights them off but is hit by Steve and captured, and Moon seizes Martha. At the Cartigan house, Martha defiantly announces that she will kill her captors if Munch doesn't. Munch arrives, shares gummy bears with Steve, shoots the bodyguards and leaves the brothers to fight over a gun; Von kills Richard. When Moon threatens her, Martha's own powers awaken, and she kills him and shoots Von with his own gun. Hopper handcuffs himself to Munch to reprogram him as a killer, but Munch frees himself and Steve shoots Hopper dead, delighted to claim a $5 million bounty. Two months later, Munch and Martha travel the world pursuing her interest in palaeontology, and when a sniper targets them, it is Martha who takes him out.

The film closed the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2015 and was released in the United States by Focus World in April 2016. Critics liked the leads' chemistry but not the tonal jumble, giving it 44% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: The gang from Dorm Daze is back, but this time they're on a cruise ship on a tropical voyage through the high seas. The cruise makes an educational stop at the island of San Paradiso, where the students are supposed to explore an important archaeological site. Things go from normal to crazy as their visit coincides with every other college's spring break. The moment the boat docks, classes are over! For these Billingsley students, their Semester at Sea will be an adventure no one will ever forget.
tagline: Sexy Maidens. Salty Dogs
title: Dorm Daze 2
plot:
Dorm Daze 2 is a comedy film that explores the world of college life, focusing on the struggles and misadventures of its characters as they navigate their final year of university. The movie delves into themes of identity, self-discovery, and the challenges of transitioning from adolescence to adulthood.

At its core, Dorm Daze 2 is a coming-of-age story that examines the complexities of young adulthood, where characters are forced to confront their own insecurities, relationships, and future prospects. The film's portrayal of college life highlights the absurdities and pitfalls of this stage of life, often relying on satire and humor to comment on the societal pressures and expectations placed upon young adults.

The movie also touches on themes of friendship, loyalty, and the importance of human connections during a time of significant change and growth. Through its characters' experiences, Dorm Daze 2 offers a relatable and entertaining take on the challenges of growing up and finding one's place in the world.

original_title: 映画大好きポンポさん
overview: Operating out of the movie capital "Nyallywood," Pompo has been shooting one B-grade entertainment flick after another that anyone would enjoy. One day, Pompo's "movie buff" assistant Gene spots a new script written by Pompo and is moved by its exquisite story. In a fit of passion, he proclaims, "I want to see this as a finished work in theaters as soon as possible!"  However, Pompo tells him, "So you shoot this film." Thus, Gene takes on his first directing gig. Meanwhile, Natalie, an ordinary girl who just arrived in town with movie actress dreams, has been discovered by Pompo...
tagline: Bright lights. Big dreams. No experience.
title: Pompo the Cinephile
plot:
Pompo the Cinephile is a 2021 Japanese animated drama film directed by Haruo Sotozaki, produced by Shochiku. The movie takes place in the 1960s and follows the story of Pompo Aditya, a young Indian woman who becomes involved with a Japanese filmmaker.

The film begins with Pompo's arrival in Tokyo, where she is hired as an assistant to the renowned filmmaker, Kōichi Nagai. Pompo is fascinated by Western cinema and has come to Japan to learn from the masters. She quickly befriends Nagai's wife, Yumi, who becomes her confidante.

As Pompo settles into her new life in Tokyo, she begins to work on various film sets, learning the ins and outs of filmmaking from Nagai himself. However, it soon becomes apparent that Nagai is struggling with his own demons, including a troubled marriage and a sense of creative stagnation.

Pompo's presence in Nagai's life has an unexpected effect: she inspires him to take risks and try new things. Together, they embark on a series of filmmaking projects that push the boundaries of Japanese cinema. Pompo's passion for Western films and her own experiences as an outsider bring a fresh perspective to Nagai's work.

Throughout the film, Sotozaki explores themes of cultural exchange, identity, and the power of art to transcend borders. Pompo's character serves as a bridge between East and West, highlighting the complexities of cross-cultural relationships in the 1960s.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Nagai is struggling with his own sense of purpose. He feels stifled by the conventions of traditional Japanese cinema and is desperate to break free from them. Pompo's influence helps him to see the world in a new light, and he begins to experiment with new techniques and styles.

The film's climax features a dramatic turning point: Nagai's latest project is met with critical acclaim, but at a great personal cost. The success comes at the expense of his marriage and his relationships with those around him. Pompo must confront the consequences of her own involvement in Nagai's life and decide whether to stay by his side or forge her own path.

Ultimately, Pompo the Cinephile is a poignant exploration of the human spirit and the power of art to transform lives. The film's beautiful animation, stunning cinematography, and nuanced performances all contribute to a richly textured narrative that lingers long after the credits roll.

overview: In the glamorous world of New York City, Rebecca Bloomwood is a fun-loving girl who is really good at shopping-a little too good, perhaps. She dreams of working for her favorite fashion magazine, but can't quite get her foot in the door-until ironically, she snags a job as an advice columnist for a financial magazine published by the same company.
tagline: A new job? Hopefully. A new man? Possibly. A new handbag? Absolutely!
title: Confessions of a Shopaholic
plot:
Confessions of a Shopaholic is a 2009 American romantic comedy directed by P. J. Hogan, based on the first two novels in Sophie Kinsella's Shopaholic series, The Secret Dreamworld of a Shopaholic and Shopaholic Abroad, known in the United States as Confessions of a Shopaholic and Shopaholic Takes Manhattan. The film recasts the English heroine as an American. It was shot in New York, Connecticut and Florida in 2008, with reshoots late that year to make the ending more sympathetic during the recession, and Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures released it on February 13, 2009.

Shopping addict Rebecca Bloomwood shares a New York apartment with her best friend, Suze, writes for a gardening magazine and dreams of working at the fashion magazine Alette. On her way to an interview there, her credit card is declined as she tries to buy a green scarf, and a stranger lends her $20. The Alette job has been filled, so she interviews instead at the financial magazine Successful Saving, whose editor, Luke Brandon, turns out to be the stranger. That night, drunk, she mails her letters to the two magazines in the wrong envelopes, and Luke, impressed by the one meant for Alette, hires her. Her column, published under the pen name "The Girl in the Green Scarf", becomes a hit.

As her success grows, so do her debts, and she dodges her debt collector, Derek Smeath, while Suze sends her to Shopaholics Anonymous. When Smeath confronts her during a television interview, Luke is humiliated and the magazine drops her column. Refusing her father's offer to sell his camper for her, Rebecca takes responsibility, turns down a job at Alette that would require lying to readers, and with help from her support group auctions her clothes to clear her debt, paying Smeath entirely in coins. She reconciles with Suze at her wedding, resists a shop window, and discovers that Luke, now running his own firm, had his agent buy her scarf. They kiss, and she joins his company as a columnist.

Isla Fisher plays Rebecca and Hugh Dancy plays Luke, with John Lithgow as Edgar West. Critics were largely negative, with 26% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, though Fisher was widely praised, and Roger Ebert called her a joy. It grossed about $106.9 million worldwide.

overview: 86-year-old Irving Zisman is on a journey across America with the most unlikely companion: his 8 year-old grandson, Billy.
tagline: Real people. Real reactions. Real messed up.
title: Jackass Presents: Bad Grandpa
plot:
Jackass Presents: Bad Grandpa is a 2013 comedy film that revolves around the misadventures of a geriatric con artist, Irving Zipp, played by Johnny Knoxville. The movie explores themes of deception, manipulation, and the consequences of one's actions.

At its core, the film delves into the idea of identity and how people present themselves to the world. Irving Zipp is a master manipulator who uses his charm and wit to swindle his way through life, often relying on his age and vulnerability to get what he wants. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that beneath his façade lies a complex web of insecurities and desperation.

The film also touches on the theme of loneliness and isolation. Irving's relationships with others are shallow and transactional, reflecting his own emotional emptiness. His interactions with his granddaughter, Jenny (played by Alice Eve), serve as a catalyst for him to confront his own vulnerabilities and reevaluate his life choices.

Furthermore, Jackass Presents: Bad Grandpa critiques societal norms around ageism and the way we perceive older adults. Irving's character is both a product of and a subversion of these expectations, highlighting the absurdity and hypocrisy that can surround our attitudes towards aging.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced exploration of human nature, revealing the complexities and contradictions that lie beneath even the most seemingly confident exterior.

overview: A socially awkward teenage math prodigy finds new confidence and new friendships when he lands a spot on the British squad at the International Mathematics Olympiad.
tagline: True genius comes from opening your heart
title: X+Y
plot:
X+Y is a 2014 British drama film directed by Morgan Matthews, based on the novel "The Boy in the Striped Pajamas" by John Boyne.

The main themes of X+Y include:

1. Coming-of-age: The story follows David, a young boy who struggles to cope with his father's death and his own feelings of guilt and responsibility. As he navigates his way through adolescence, he learns valuable lessons about life, love, and the importance of human connection.

2. Guilt and Responsibility: David's actions in the concentration camp have severe consequences, and he grapples with the weight of his guilt throughout the film. This theme explores the complexities of responsibility and how it can affect individuals, particularly children.

3. War and its effects on civilians: The story highlights the devastating impact of war on ordinary people, including children. It sheds light on the experiences of those who live in the shadow of conflict, often without receiving the recognition they deserve.

4. Human connection and empathy: Through David's relationships with his father and others, the film emphasizes the importance of human connections in times of crisis. It encourages viewers to consider the value of empathy and understanding in breaking down barriers between people.

5. Coming to terms with the past: The story explores how individuals can learn from history and find ways to cope with traumatic events. David's journey is a powerful reminder that confronting the past and acknowledging its impact on our lives can be a crucial step towards healing and growth.

Overall, X+Y is a thought-provoking film that tackles complex themes with sensitivity and nuance, offering a powerful exploration of the human experience during times of war and trauma.

overview: The heroic Leonidas, armed with nothing but leather underwear and a cape, leads a ragtag group of 13 Spartans to defend their homeland against the invading Persians (whose ranks include Ghost Rider, Rocky Balboa, the Transformers, and a hunchbacked Paris Hilton). No one is safe when the Spartans take on the biggest icons in pop culture!
tagline: The bigger the hit, the harder they fall.
title: Meet the Spartans
plot:
Meet the Spartans is a 2008 American parody film written and directed by Jason Friedberg and Aaron Seltzer. Chiefly a spoof of the 2006 film 300, it also mocks many other films, television shows, celebrities and pop culture events of the time, in the manner of the pair's Date Movie and Epic Movie. The cast includes Sean Maguire, Carmen Electra, Ken Davitian, Kevin Sorbo and Diedrich Bader.

A Spartan elder inspects three babies, rejecting an ugly talking ogre baby, while another is adopted by Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie and the muscular Leonidas is accepted and trained for kingship. Cast into the wild, Leonidas survives the winter and hunts down a gangsta penguin named Mumble, then returns to be crowned in a penguin-skin hat and wins Margo, who gives him the combination to her armoured chastity belt. Years later, a Persian messenger arrives with the Spartan politician Traitoro to demand Sparta's submission to King Xerxes, and when the envoy flirts with Margo, Leonidas kicks him into a pit, followed by his guards and assorted celebrities. Warned by the Oracle, portrayed as Ugly Betty, that he will die if he goes to war, Leonidas marches for Thermopylae anyway with just thirteen soldiers who met the army's stringent standards, including the Captain, his son Sonio and the unfit Dilio. A deformed Paris Hilton, rejected as a soldier, knows of a secret goat path. The Spartans beat Xerxes's Immortals in a dance contest and drive them off a cliff, refuse Xerxes's bribe of a trip to the Palms Hotel and Casino and defeat the Persians in a "Yo Momma" contest in which Dilio is blinded. Hilton betrays them to Xerxes, while in Sparta Margo battles the treacherous Traitoro in a Spider-Man 3 spoof and defeats him with a hand vacuum. In the final battle, Rocky Balboa kills Sonio, the Captain falls to Xerxes, and Xerxes uses a "Transformer Cube" to become the giant Xerxestron, but trips over his own extension cord and crushes Leonidas and the remaining Spartans. The blind Dilio brings the news home, and a year later leads a larger army that marches the wrong way and ends up in Malibu. The film closes with the characters singing "I Will Survive" on the American Idol stage.

Released by 20th Century Fox on January 25, 2008, Meet the Spartans opened at number one in the United States, and grossed about $84 million worldwide on a $30 million budget. Critics panned it, giving it a 2% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and it has appeared on several lists of the worst films ever made.

overview: The President's daughter, unable to experience life like a normal 18 year-old, escapes from her entourage of Secret Service agents while traveling in Europe. She falls in love with a handsome British stranger, who also happens to be working undercover for her father.
tagline: How do you fall in love with the whole world watching?
title: Chasing Liberty
plot:
Chasing Liberty is a 2004 American teen comedy-drama film that revolves around the life of Katie Holmes' character, Annie, who is a teenager struggling to balance her personal life with the pressures of fame. The movie explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and the challenges of growing up in the public eye.

At its core, Chasing Liberty is a story about a young woman's quest for independence and autonomy as she navigates the complexities of adolescence. Annie's journey is marked by her desire to break free from the constraints of her fame and forge her own path in life. As she embarks on a European tour with her father, Annie must confront the limitations placed upon her by her celebrity status and learn to assert her individuality.

The film also touches on themes of family dynamics and the complexities of parent-child relationships. Annie's relationship with her father is particularly significant, as he struggles to balance his desire to protect his daughter with his need to let her spread her wings and become independent.

Ultimately, Chasing Liberty is a heartwarming and relatable coming-of-age story that explores the challenges and triumphs of growing up in the public eye. Through Annie's journey, the film offers a nuanced portrayal of the complexities of fame and the importance of self-discovery and individuality.

overview: When Jess sets sail on a yacht with a group of friends, she cannot shake the feeling that there is something wrong. Her suspicions are realized when the yacht hits a storm and the group is forced to board a passing ocean liner to get to safety, a ship Jess is convinced she’s been on before.
tagline: Fear comes in waves.
title: Triangle
plot:
Triangle is a 2009 British-Australian psychological horror film written and directed by Christopher Smith. Melissa George stars as Jess, a single mother who joins friends on a boating trip and, after their yacht capsizes, boards a seemingly deserted ocean liner where someone appears to be hunting them. Michael Dorman, Rachael Carpani, Henry Nixon, Emma Lung and Liam Hemsworth also star. The screenplay draws partly on the myth of Sisyphus, condemned to push a boulder uphill for eternity, and Smith cited influences ranging from The Twilight Zone to Dead of Night, Back to the Future and Memento.

Jess, mother of an autistic son, Tommy, arrives at a Florida harbour alone, saying the boy is at school, and sets sail with her friend Greg, his deckhand Victor, the married couple Sally and Downey, and Sally's friend Heather. A sudden storm hits after Greg picks up a woman's distress call saying someone is killing everyone; Heather is swept away and the others cling to the overturned hull. When a liner, the Aeolus, passes, they climb aboard, though it seems empty. Jess feels a strong sense of déjà vu, finds her own keys, and sees "go to theater" written in blood. A wounded Victor attacks her, and in the theatre she finds Greg shot dead before a masked gunman kills Sally and Downey. Jess disarms the attacker, who tells her she must kill the others to get home, and knocks the figure overboard. She then watches a second version of her group arrive and realizes the events repeat whenever everyone dies; she finds dozens of her own lockets and notes urging her to kill them all, and a third Jess carries out the killings. Desperate to escape, Jess sets the cycle in motion herself, puts on the burlap mask and is knocked overboard by the newest Jess. She washes up on a beach and, returning home earlier that morning, sees her earlier self abusing Tommy. She kills that version of herself and drives off with Tommy, promising things will change, but after finding a pile of dead seagulls she crashes into a truck, killing her son. Hoping to undo it, she takes a taxi to the harbour, promises the driver she will return and boards Greg's boat, starting the loop again.

Shot in Queensland, Australia, with support from the UK Film Council, Triangle premiered at London's FrightFest in August 2009 and opened in British cinemas on 16 October 2009. It received generally positive reviews, with a 78% Rotten Tomatoes rating, but grossed only about $1.3 million worldwide.

overview: When a group of close-knit friends assemble for the marriage of Skylar and Dan, they have no idea they will witness The Rapture and face a series of catastrophic events turning the celebration into a life-or-death struggle.
tagline: After the rapture, there are fates worse than death.
title: The Remaining
plot:
The Remaining is a 2014 American supernatural thriller film directed by Ron Schmidt and written by Michael Petroni. The movie stars Christian Sesma, Alexie K. Davis, and Raffey Cassidy.

The story begins with a young girl named Beth (Alexie K. Davis) who has been experiencing strange and terrifying events since the age of 8. She believes that she is being stalked by an angel named Gabriel (Christian Sesma), who is trying to warn her about an impending apocalypse. As Beth grows older, her experiences become more intense and frequent, leading her to question her own sanity.

The movie then shifts forward in time to present day, where Beth is now a college student struggling to cope with the trauma of her past. She begins to experience strange visions and nightmares, which she believes are connected to Gabriel's warnings. As Beth delves deeper into the mystery of her experiences, she discovers that she has a unique connection to an ancient prophecy that foretells the coming of a great evil.

As Beth tries to uncover the truth about her past and the prophecy, she is pursued by a group of mysterious figures who seem to be connected to Gabriel. Along the way, she meets a young man named Jake (Raffey Cassidy), who becomes her ally in unraveling the mystery.

Throughout the movie, the lines between reality and fantasy become increasingly blurred as Beth's experiences escalate. She begins to question whether Gabriel is truly trying to help her or if he is manipulating her for his own purposes.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Beth has a crucial role to play in preventing the apocalypse. However, the true nature of the prophecy and Gabriel's intentions remain unclear until the very end.

The movie culminates with Beth discovering the truth about her past and the prophecy. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Gabriel was not an angel at all, but rather a human who had been possessed by a demon. The demon had been manipulating Beth throughout her life, using her as a vessel to bring about the apocalypse.

In the end, Beth must confront the demon and make a choice between saving herself or fulfilling the prophecy. With Jake's help, she is able to defeat the demon and prevent the apocalypse. However, the movie ends on a cliffhanger, leaving the audience wondering what will happen next in Beth's journey.

Overall, The Remaining is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of faith, doubt, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of supernatural thrillers have praised the movie for its unique premise and intense plot twists.

overview: Three young conspiracy theorists attempt to uncover the mysteries of Area 51, the government's secret location rumored to have hosted encounters with alien beings. What they find at this hidden facility exposes unimaginable secrets.
tagline: They're Here.
title: Area 51
plot:
Area 51 is a 2015 American science fiction horror film directed by Dennis Widmyer and written by Jeremy Burnham. The movie follows a group of friends who embark on a road trip to Area 51, a secret United States Air Force facility within the Nevada Test and Training Range, allegedly used for extraterrestrial research.

The main theme of Area 51 revolves around the idea of government secrecy and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The film explores the notion that some secrets are better left unspoken and that delving into the unknown can have catastrophic repercussions. As the characters venture deeper into the heart of Area 51, they begin to unravel a sinister plot that threatens not only their own lives but also the fabric of reality.

The movie also touches on the theme of paranoia and the blurring of lines between reality and fantasy. The characters' perceptions of what is real and what is not become increasingly distorted as they navigate the mysterious and eerie environment of Area 51. This blurring of reality serves to heighten the sense of tension and unease, making it difficult for the audience to distinguish between fact and fiction.

Furthermore, the film can be seen as a commentary on the human desire for truth and knowledge, particularly when it comes to extraterrestrial life. The characters' quest for answers about Area 51's purpose and the existence of aliens serves as a metaphor for humanity's innate curiosity and drive to explore the unknown.

Overall, Area 51 is a thought-provoking film that masterfully weaves together elements of science fiction, horror, and mystery to create a thrilling narrative that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats.

overview: Hubie Dubois, despite his devotion to his hometown of Salem, Massachusetts (and its legendary Halloween celebration), is a figure of mockery for kids and adults alike. But this year, something really is going bump in the night, and it’s up to Hubie to save Halloween.
tagline: Fear. Less.
title: Hubie Halloween
plot:
Hubie Halloween is a 2020 American comedy film directed by Jeff Canion and Tim Herlihy, produced by Adam Sandler's production company Happy Madison Productions.

The movie follows the story of Hubie Dubois (played by Adam Sandler), a well-meaning but awkward and socially isolated man who decides to take matters into his own hands when he becomes convinced that his town is being targeted by a serial killer on Halloween night. As Hubie tries to protect his community, he inadvertently causes more chaos and hilarity.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. **Friendship and Community**: The film highlights the importance of building relationships and connections with others. Despite his awkwardness, Hubie's efforts to help his neighbors ultimately bring people together and foster a sense of community.
2. **Self-Discovery and Empowerment**: Through his experiences, Hubie learns to take risks, stand up for himself, and find his place in the world. He discovers that he has more to offer than he initially thought and becomes a hero to those around him.
