The film begins with Chloe's life in Beverly Hills, where she spends her days lounging on designer furniture and getting pampered by her loyal staff. However, when Vivian is kidnapped by a Mexican cartel, Chloe finds herself separated from her beloved owner and forced to embark on an adventure of a lifetime.

Along the way, Chloe meets a group of stray dogs who become her unlikely friends and allies. There's Delgado, a street-smart dog with a heart of gold; Lola, a sassy and confident Chihuahua who becomes Chloe's rival; and Tino, a lovable but dim-witted dog who often gets them into trouble.

As Chloe navigates the dangers of Mexico City, she learns valuable lessons about courage, loyalty, and friendship. With the help of her new friends, Chloe sets out to find Vivian and bring her home safely.

Throughout their journey, Chloe and her companions face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, fierce predators, and even a rival dog named Lola's owner, who seeks to capture Delgado for his own gain. Despite these obstacles, the group remains determined and resourceful, using their unique skills and personalities to overcome each hurdle.

As they near their destination, Chloe and her friends discover that Vivian is being held captive by a ruthless cartel leader. In a thrilling showdown, Chloe and her companions use all their wits and cunning to outsmart the cartel and rescue Vivian.

In the end, Chloe and Vivian are reunited, and the group returns home to Beverly Hills as heroes. Along the way, Chloe has undergone a significant transformation from a pampered pet to a confident and capable companion who has discovered her own strength and resilience.

The film features stunning animation, lovable characters, and plenty of humor, making it a delightful treat for both children and adults. With its uplifting message about friendship and perseverance, Beverly Hills Chihuahua is a heartwarming adventure that will leave viewers smiling long after the credits roll.

overview: In 1965, Takeshi Kitano drops out of a university and enters the Asakusa France Za, which is a performance theater. He becomes an apprentice to Senzaburo Fukami, who is a legendary entertainer. Senzaburo Fukami demands that Takeshi Kitano keep the mindset of an entertainer, not only on stage, but also in his daily life. Takeshi Kitano cultivates his dream of becoming an entertainer with other apprentices. Due to the popularity of TV, people attend the theater less and less, but Takeshi Kitano spends his youthful days with Senzaburo Fukami and other apprentices who are full of talent and unique personalities.
title: Asakusa Kid
plot:
Asakusa Kid is a 2021 Japanese biographical drama written and directed by Gekidan Hitori for Netflix, adapted from "Beat" Takeshi Kitano's 1988 memoir about his apprenticeship to the comedian Senzaburo Fukami, which had already been filmed in 2002 by Makoto Shinozaki. Produced by Django Film and Nikkatsu, it stars Yuya Yagira as Kitano and Yo Oizumi as Fukami, with Mugi Kadowaki as Chiharu, Nobuyuki Tsuchiya as Kitano's comic partner Kiyoshi, Honami Suzuki as Fukami's wife Mari, Hiroyuki Onoue and Morio Kazama. The film runs 123 minutes.

After opening with an older Kitano about to step on stage, the film flashes back to the early 1970s. Kitano, a university dropout, works as an elevator boy and general dogsbody at the France-za, a burlesque theater in Tokyo's Asakusa district whose shrinking audience cares more about the strippers than the comedians performing skits between their routines. The venue is run by Fukami, a famous old-school vaudevillian known for his dapper style and his contempt for the new manzai comedy duos making their names on television. Fukami at first gives the eager newcomer a hard time, then agrees to train him in comedy and tap dance, insisting that he keep an entertainer's mindset not only on stage but in everyday life. Kitano befriends Chiharu, a straight-talking stripper whose dreams of a singing career are behind her, and spends his youth among other gifted, eccentric apprentices as television draws audiences away from the theater. As Kitano's ambition outgrows the failing France-za, he leaves to form the manzai duo Two Beat with Kiyoshi and rises to stardom, while Fukami and his loyal wife Mari face growing misfortune. The film ends with the older Kitano walking through the neighborhood and theater where he learned his craft.

Asakusa Kid was released on Netflix on 9 December 2021. In Variety, Richard Kuipers described it as a safe, traditional and enjoyable biopic that offers little penetrating insight into Kitano but a respectful, touching portrait of Fukami, noting a slowish first half and praising its flights of fantasy, such as Fukami's tap routine and Chiharu's dream of being a torch singer. He called Yagira, a former best actor winner at Cannes, excellent in capturing Kitano's timing and tics, and Oizumi funny and dignified. Other critics similarly praised the leads while finding it conventional and more nostalgic than revealing.

overview: With the world under attack by deadly creatures who hunt by sound, a teen and her family seek refuge outside the city and encounter a mysterious cult.
tagline: They're listening.
title: The Silence
plot:
The Silence is a post-apocalyptic horror film of 2019 directed by John R. Leonetti from a screenplay by Carey and Shane Van Dyke, adapted from Tim Lebbon's 2015 novel of the same name. Kiernan Shipka stars as Ally Andrews, a deaf teenager, with Stanley Tucci as her father Hugh, Miranda Otto as her mother Kelly, Kate Trotter as her grandmother Lynn, John Corbett as the family friend Glenn, Dempsey Bryk as her boyfriend Rob and Billy MacLellan as a sinister reverend.

Cave researchers accidentally release a unknown species of pterosaur-like predators from a mine. The creatures, called Vesps, kill the team and swarm toward the noisiest places they can find. Ally lost her hearing in a car crash; when news footage reveals the attacks and the government tells people to stay inside and silent, she persuades her parents to head for the countryside. Glenn joins them, but on a jammed interstate he goes off-road and crashes into a herd of deer. The family dog's barking draws the Vesps, and Glenn fires his gun to lure them away and is devoured. Hugh realizes the creatures are blind and hunt purely by sound, so he burns Glenn's car as a decoy and the family continues on foot.

At a remote house the owner is killed and Kelly is bitten. While Hugh and Ally search a store for antibiotics, they discover Vesp eggs gestating in corpses and escape by setting off the sprinklers; they also meet the reverend of a cult called the Hushed. Kelly recovers, and Ally learns online that the Vesps cannot survive cold, so the family plans to go north. The tongueless reverend tracks them down and says Ally is fertile, revealing that he wants her for the cult; Hugh drives the members off at gunpoint. Later, phones planted by the cult ring around the house and summon the Vesps. The cultists seize Ally, and Lynn sacrifices herself by screaming, drawing the creatures onto herself and the captors. The family rescues Ally from the rest and Hugh beats the reverend to death. Weeks later they reach the Refuge in Alaska, where Ally reunites with Rob and hunts Vesps with a bow, wondering who will adapt first, the creatures or humanity.

Shipka and Tucci were cast in 2017, and filming began in Toronto that September. After its original distributor ran into financial trouble, Netflix released the film on 10 April 2019; it also played theatrically in seven countries, grossing $2.3 million. Reviews were largely negative; Rotten Tomatoes gave it 30%, with its consensus calling the premise derivative.

overview: When his long-lost outlaw father returns, Tommy "White Knife" Stockburn goes on an adventure-filled journey across the Old West with his five brothers.
title: The Ridiculous 6
plot:
The Ridiculous 6 is a 2015 American Western comedy film directed by Sean Anders and John Morris, written by Anders and Morris, and produced by Adam Sandler through his production company Happy Madison Productions.

The movie takes place in the late 19th century and follows the story of Tommy Stockton (played by Adam Sandler), a rough-riding cowboy who is on the run from the law. After being accused of stealing $100,000 from a bank, Tommy flees to the mountains of Montana, where he meets a group of outcasts and misfits.

Among them are Samson (played by Nick Swardson), a dim-witted but lovable simpleton; Django (played by Rob Schneider), a former slave who is also an expert in horse riding; and Tito (played by Terry Crews), a tough-as-nails cowboy with a heart of gold. The group, along with Tommy's half-brother, Danny Stockton (played by Taylor Lautner), sets out on a journey to find the legendary Golden Sombrero, a treasure that is said to be hidden somewhere in Mexico.

As they travel through the American West, the group faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including hostile Native Americans, treacherous terrain, and rival treasure hunters. Along the way, Tommy also learns more about his family's past and the reason behind his half-brother's betrayal.

The movie follows a classic Western plot structure, with the group facing various trials and tribulations as they journey towards their goal. However, it also incorporates plenty of comedic elements, thanks to the antics of the lovable but dim-witted Samson and the hilarious banter between Tommy and his half-brother Danny.

As the group gets closer to finding the Golden Sombrero, they are met with unexpected challenges and surprises. In the end, Tommy and his friends successfully find the treasure, but not before facing a final showdown with their rivals.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of humorous moments, witty one-liners, and entertaining action sequences. The Ridiculous 6 is a lighthearted, family-friendly comedy that pokes fun at traditional Western genre conventions while still delivering plenty of laughs and excitement.

Overall, The Ridiculous 6 is a fun, entertaining movie that is sure to delight fans of Western comedies and Adam Sandler's signature brand of humor.

overview: Six high school seniors decide to break into the Princeton Testing Center so they can steal the answers to their upcoming SAT tests and all get perfect scores.
tagline: The S.A.T is hard to take. It's even harder to steal.
title: The Perfect Score
plot:
The Perfect Score is a 2004 American teen comedy-drama film directed by Brian Robbins. The movie revolves around four high school students who concoct a plan to cheat on their SATs, with the ultimate goal of getting into an Ivy League college.

At its core, The Perfect Score explores themes of ambition, peer pressure, and the consequences of one's actions. The main characters are driven by a desire for success and acceptance, which leads them down a path of deception and risk-taking. As they navigate their relationships with each other and the pressures of high school life, they must confront the moral implications of their decisions.

The film also touches on the theme of class and social status, highlighting the disparities between those who have access to resources and opportunities, and those who do not. The characters' experiences serve as a commentary on the societal expectations placed upon students, particularly in the context of college admissions.

Furthermore, The Perfect Score delves into the complexities of friendship and loyalty, as the main characters grapple with the consequences of their actions and the impact they have on each other's lives. Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced portrayal of high school life, revealing both the excitement and anxiety that come with this pivotal stage in adolescence.

Overall, The Perfect Score is a thought-provoking film that explores the intricacies of human relationships, ambition, and the consequences of one's choices, all set against the backdrop of high school life.

overview: After saving the life of their heir apparent, tenacious loner Snake Eyes is welcomed into an ancient Japanese clan called the Arashikage where he is taught the ways of the ninja warrior. But, when secrets from his past are revealed, Snake Eyes' honor and allegiance will be tested – even if that means losing the trust of those closest to him.
tagline: Every warrior has a beginning.
title: Snake Eyes: G.I. Joe Origins
plot:
Snake Eyes: G.I. Joe Origins is a 2021 American action-adventure film directed by Robert Schwentke, based on the G.I. Joe franchise. The movie follows the origin story of Snake Eyes, a skilled ninja and member of the elite special forces team known as G.I. Joe.

The film begins with a young Orko (Henry Golding), a skilled warrior from the fictional nation of Serranocia, who is trained by his mentor, Storm Shadow's father, Lord Shen (Ronny Chieng). Orko is a member of an elite group of warriors known as the Arashikage clan. However, he soon discovers that his family has been betrayed and killed by the rival clan, led by Storm Shadow.

Orko escapes with his infant daughter, Akiko (Lola Tung), and flees to the United States, where he is taken in by a G.I. Joe team member, Duke (Chad Michael Murray). Orko adopts the codename "Snake Eyes" and joins the G.I. Joe team, using his skills to help protect the world from threats.

As Snake Eyes grows into his role as a G.I. Joe operative, he becomes embroiled in a conflict between the Arashikage clan and the rival clan, led by Storm Shadow (Lee Byung-hun). The two clans engage in a brutal battle, with Snake Eyes caught in the middle.

Meanwhile, Akiko is kidnapped by Storm Shadow's forces, leading Snake Eyes on a perilous mission to rescue his daughter. Along the way, he must confront his troubled past and learn to trust others in order to save those he cares about.

The film culminates in an epic showdown between Snake Eyes and Storm Shadow, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Snake Eyes emerges victorious, but not without scars from his past and a newfound sense of purpose as a G.I. Joe operative.

Throughout the movie, there are nods to the classic G.I. Joe franchise, including references to iconic characters like Scarlett (Zazie Beetz) and Destro (Idris Elba). The film's action sequences are fast-paced and intense, with Snake Eyes showcasing his impressive ninja skills.

Overall, Snake Eyes: G.I. Joe Origins is a thrilling origin story that explores the complexities of Snake Eyes' character and sets the stage for future adventures in the G.I. Joe franchise.

overview: Longtime friends and local radio hosts Maggie and Jack fake it as a couple for their families and listeners in hopes of getting their show syndicated.
tagline: This New Year's Eve, the countdown to love is on.
title: Midnight at the Magnolia
plot:
Midnight at the Magnolia is a 2020 Canadian romantic comedy television film directed by Max McGuire and written by Carley Smale. Produced by Neshama Entertainment, it stars Natalie Hall and Evan Williams, with Alison Brooks, Steve Cumyn, Michael Gordin Shore, Susan Hamann, Hannah Gordon, Victoria Maria, Peter Michael Dillon and Sean Williams. Although set in Chicago, it was shot in Ottawa in January 2020, before the COVID-19 pandemic, and was released on Netflix on 5 November 2020.

Maggie Quinn (Hall) and Jack Russo (Williams), best friends since childhood, host Windy City Wake-Up, a morning radio show known for its relationship advice. When an on-air chat about introducing their partners to their families becomes a hit, their producer Deb (Brooks) tells them that a larger network, run by Judd Crawford (Dillon), wants to syndicate them nationally, provided they introduce their partners live during a New Year's Eve broadcast. Jack proposes holding the event at the Magnolia, the struggling restaurant and jazz club co-owned by their fathers Steve (Cumyn) and Martin (Shore). Days after Christmas, however, both are dumped, Maggie by her boyfriend Seb (Sean Williams). To save the opportunity, Jack suggests they pretend to be a couple. When Jack's parents catch them in a staged kiss, both families are overjoyed, having long believed they belonged together. Maggie's sister Amanda (Maria) sees that Maggie has always loved Jack, and Steve hands Jack the ring of Maggie's late mother. Jack's high-school girlfriend Bianca Bell (Gordon) tells him that Maggie was heartbroken when he did not take her to the prom, and that she broke up with him because he loved Maggie. After Jack forgets a dinner marking the anniversary of her mother's death, Maggie tells him he always puts her second. At the party Judd floats the idea of giving them separate shows, and as midnight approaches the pair confess on air that the relationship was a sham. Maggie leaves the stage, but Jack declares his love, turns down a solo show and sings a song he wrote for her, and they share a real midnight kiss. A year later he proposes with her mother's ring.

Reviews were mixed. Kirsten Hawkes of Parent Previews gave it a B+, finding Hall and Williams charming enough to carry an unremarkable script, while Roger Moore of Movie Nation called it as bland as bargain-shelf white bread and lamented the leads' lack of chemistry. It was nominated for Best TV Movie at the 2022 Canadian Screen Awards.

overview: An average guy of an Estonian high-school decides to defend his bullied classmate. This starts a war between him and the informal leader of the class. As teenagers' honour is a touchy thing, everything ends in bloodshed.
tagline: The Chronicle of a Catastrophe.
title: The Class
plot:
The Class (Klass) is an Estonian drama film of 2007 directed by Ilmar Raag about bullying and school violence. Pärt Uusberg plays the persecuted teenager Joosep Rääk and Vallo Kirs plays Kaspar Kordes, the classmate who takes his side, with Lauri Pedaja as the ringleader Anders, Paula Solvak as Kaspar's girlfriend Thea, Mikk Mägi as Paul and Margus Prangel as Joosep's father. A seven-episode television sequel, Class: Life After, followed.

Joosep is tormented by his entire high school class, with Anders and his friends Paul, Toomas, Tiit and Olav leading the abuse: they beat him repeatedly and, after a basketball game, strip him and shove him into the girls' changing room. When Kaspar starts helping him, the class turns on Kaspar too, and Thea grows distant. After the teacher, Laine, catches Paul stealing Joosep's notebook, Paul blames Kaspar, and the school calls Joosep's parents. His father Margus, a gun enthusiast obsessed with making his son a real man, urges him to fight the ringleader. Anders's gang later locks Kaspar in a burned-out shed and makes him watch as they beat Joosep until he can barely breathe, warning that any further defense will only make things worse. Joosep asks Kaspar to stop protecting him, hoping simply to endure until graduation.

The class mocks the pair as supposedly gay, and Thea leaves Kaspar, believing he cares more for Joosep than for her. When Joosep's mother finds bruises on him and complains to the school, the class is blamed, and in revenge the students lure both boys to a beach with fake emails. There Thea publicly breaks up with Kaspar; when he knocks Anders down, a knife is drawn, and the two are forced into a sexual act that the class photographs.

Seeking revenge, Joosep takes his father's pistols, a sawed-off rifle and ammunition, and Kaspar apologizes to his grandmother before the two walk into school armed. Joosep tells a teacher to call the police, and the boys begin shooting their tormentors: Tiit, Olav and Thea's friend Riina die, Kaspar accidentally hits a younger girl, Paul is shot after he and Anders grab Joosep's rifle, and Joosep kills Anders. Kaspar stops him from shooting Thea. Facing each other, the boys agree to kill themselves on a count of three; Joosep fires, while Kaspar is left holding the gun to his head.

The film won awards at the Karlovy Vary and Warsaw film festivals in 2007 and was Estonia's submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

overview: At the end of WWII, an ambitious bootlegger and his nightclub-singing girlfriend assemble a ragtag bunch of misfits for an impossible heist: to steal Mussolini's treasure right from his headquarters.
title: Robbing Mussolini
plot:
Robbing Mussolini (Rapiniamo il Duce) is an Italian historical action comedy of 2022 directed by Renato De Maria and distributed by Netflix, which released it on 26 October 2022. Pietro Castellitto stars as the smuggler Pietro "Isola" Lamberti, with Matilda De Angelis as the singer Yvonne, Tommaso Ragno as Marcello, Isabella Ferrari as Nora, Maccio Capatonda as the former racing driver Fabbri and Filippo Timi as the Fascist federal secretary Achille Borsalino.

In the last days of the Second World War, Isola, a black-market dealer in Fascist-held Milan, is trying to raise enough money to flee with his lover Yvonne, a singer who is also the mistress of the cruel Borsalino. With his associates Marcello and Amedeo he intercepts a coded order to move a vast hoard of treasure looted by the regime to Switzerland. They plan to steal it from the heavily guarded Black Zone within a week, recruiting the runner Hessa, the anarchist bomb-maker Molotov and Fabbri. Borsalino and his aide Leonida catch Isola leaving a rendezvous with Yvonne and warn him off, but Yvonne agrees to steal Borsalino's personal stamp so the gang can enter the zone. Borsalino, unaware, even shows her the treasure; he plans to leave his wife Nora, who is sleeping with Leonida.

When Yvonne faints on stage and Isola rushes to her, a gunfight erupts, and the couple escape with Fabbri's help; Yvonne then tells Isola she is carrying his child. Nora, who has been spying on them, blackmails Isola into giving her half the loot and pulling off the robbery within a day. The night raid goes wrong when guards stop Isola, disguised as a prisoner, and the alarm sounds early; Molotov is fatally wounded but sets off his explosives, and in the confusion the gang drive off with the treasure. Meanwhile Borsalino seizes Yvonne but is beaten to death by Nora, who then double-crosses Isola at the meeting point, keeps Yvonne as a hostage and orders Leonida to kill the gang. Partisans arrive and save them, and Nora and Leonida flee toward the Alps in the truck. Chasing them in a racing car, Isola knocks down Leonida and Fabbri shoots the truck's driver, sending the vehicle into a lake. Isola and Yvonne surface as the radio announces the surrender of Axis forces in Italy; a mid-credits scene shows that Nora survived as well.

Reviewing it for Cineuropa, Davide Abbatescianni was unimpressed, faulting weak characterization, below-par performances and predictable subplots.

belongs_to_collection.name: The Fox and the Hound Collection

overview: Best friends Tod, a fox kit, and Copper, a hound puppy, visit a country fair when they see a band of dogs called "The Singin' Strays". The band has five members: Dixie, Cash, Granny Rose, and twin brothers Waylon and Floyd. It is important that they perform well because a talent scout is visiting.
tagline: Old Friends New Adventure
title: The Fox and the Hound 2
plot:
The Fox and the Hound 2 is a 2006 animated comedy-adventure film produced by DisneyToon Studios, serving as a sequel to the 1981 film The Fox and the Hound. The story takes place several years after the events of the first film.

The movie begins with Tod, now an adult fox, living in the forest with his wife, Vixey, and their three kits (baby foxes). However, their peaceful life is disrupted when a group of hunters arrives, threatening to destroy their home. The family must band together to protect themselves from the danger.

Meanwhile, Copper, the hound who was once Tod's best friend, has become a police dog in the nearby town. He is now married with two children and is struggling to balance his work as a law enforcement officer with being a devoted father.

As the story unfolds, Tod and Vixey send their kits on a journey to find food, which leads them into the city. There, they encounter Copper's son, Amos, who befriends one of the kits, and together they get into various misadventures. The kits' escapades lead to a series of comedic misunderstandings and exciting situations.

However, their fun is short-lived as they soon find themselves in trouble with the city authorities. Tod and Vixey must use their cunning and resourcefulness to help their kits escape from danger.

Throughout the film, Tod and Copper's past friendship is revisited, and they are forced to confront their differences. The movie explores themes of loyalty, friendship, and growing up, as both Tod and Copper navigate the challenges of adulthood.

In the end, Tod and Vixey successfully return home with their kits, while Copper learns a valuable lesson about being present for his family. The film concludes on a heartwarming note, with Tod and Copper sharing a poignant moment that highlights the enduring power of friendship.

Overall, The Fox and the Hound 2 is a lighthearted, entertaining film that offers plenty of laughs and exciting moments. While it may not be as emotionally resonant as its predecessor, it remains a charming addition to the beloved franchise.

original_title: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them
overview: In 1926, Newt Scamander arrives at the Magical Congress of the United States of America with a magically expanded briefcase, which houses a number of dangerous creatures and their habitats. When the creatures escape from the briefcase, it sends the American wizarding authorities after Newt, and threatens to strain even further the state of magical and non-magical relations.
tagline: From J.K. Rowling's wizarding world.
title: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them
plot:
Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them is a 2016 fantasy film directed by David Yates and written by J. K. Rowling, her first screenplay. The opening entry in the Fantastic Beasts series and the ninth film in the Wizarding World franchise, it serves as a spin-off and prequel to the Harry Potter films, inspired by the guide book Rowling published in 2001 under the name of its fictional author, Newt Scamander, to benefit Comic Relief. The new series was announced in 2013, with Potter veteran David Heyman producing. Filming ran from August 2015 to January 2016 at Warner Bros. Studios Leavesden and on location in England, and the film premiered at Alice Tully Hall in New York on 10 November 2016.

In 1926, British magizoologist Newt Scamander arrives in New York carrying a magically enlarged suitcase full of creatures. Chasing an escaped Niffler, he accidentally swaps cases with Jacob Kowalski, a non-magical would-be baker, and is detained by Tina Goldstein, a demoted Auror of the Magical Congress of the United States (MACUSA). When Jacob opens Newt's case, several beasts escape into the city. Newt, Tina, Jacob and Tina's mind-reading sister, Queenie, set out to recapture them, while Jacob and Queenie fall for each other despite laws banning such relationships. Meanwhile a destructive force rampages through the city and kills Senator Henry Shaw Jr. MACUSA blames an Obscurial, a dark parasitic force born of suppressed magic, found in Newt's case, and security director Percival Graves sentences Newt and Tina to death, but Queenie helps them escape.

Graves has been manipulating Credence Barebone, the abused adopted son of anti-witch campaigner Mary Lou Barebone, to find the true Obscurial, which kills Mary Lou. When Graves dismisses Credence as a squib, Credence reveals that he is the host and tears through the city. Aurors destroy the Obscurial after Newt and Tina try to calm him, and Newt exposes Graves as the dark wizard Gellert Grindelwald in disguise. Newt's Thunderbird spreads a rain that wipes the city's memories, seemingly including Jacob's, yet he later opens a bakery with silver eggshells Newt gave him and smiles in recognition when Queenie walks in.

Eddie Redmayne plays Newt, with Katherine Waterston, Dan Fogler, Alison Sudol, Ezra Miller, Samantha Morton and Colin Farrell. It scored 74% on Rotten Tomatoes, grossed $814 million worldwide on a $175 million budget, and it won the Academy Award for Best Costume Design, the franchise's first Oscar.

overview: A college student starts to experience extreme seizures. She soon learns that the violent episodes are a symptom of inexplicable abilities.
title: Thelma
plot:
Thelma is a 2017 Norwegian supernatural horror film that delves into the complexities of female identity, isolation, and the struggle for self-discovery. The movie follows the story of Thelma, a shy and introverted young woman who begins to experience strange and terrifying occurrences after moving to a new town.

At its core, Thelma explores the theme of female empowerment and the societal expectations placed upon women. Thelma's journey is marked by her desire for independence and autonomy, which is often at odds with the traditional feminine roles imposed upon her by her family and community. As she navigates her newfound powers and struggles to understand herself, Thelma must confront the constraints of patriarchal society and forge her own path.

The film also touches on the theme of isolation and loneliness, highlighting the ways in which women are often forced to navigate their lives alone, without support or understanding from those around them. Thelma's relationships with others are fraught with tension and uncertainty, leaving her feeling disconnected and adrift.

Furthermore, Thelma is a movie that explores the complexities of mental health and the struggles of living with anxiety and depression. The film's portrayal of Thelma's inner turmoil is both haunting and relatable, capturing the feelings of overwhelm and despair that can accompany these conditions.

Ultimately, Thelma is a powerful exploration of what it means to be a woman in a world that often seeks to constrain and define her. Through its atmospheric tension and eerie landscapes, the film creates a sense of unease and uncertainty, mirroring Thelma's own feelings of disorientation and confusion as she navigates her newfound powers and struggles to find her place in the world.

overview: A French family moves to a new neighborhood with during the summer holidays. The story follows a 10-year-old gender non-conforming child, Laure, who experiments with their gender presentation, adopting the name Mikäel.
tagline: There's a new kid in town.
title: Tomboy
plot:
Tomboy is a 2011 French drama film directed by Thomas Cailley. The story revolves around a young girl named Mathilde who, at the age of eight, decides to cut her hair short and adopt masculine attire in order to escape the societal expectations placed upon her as a girl.

The main theme of Tomboy is the struggle for identity and self-expression. Mathilde's decision to dress like a boy is not just a phase, but a desperate attempt to break free from the constraints of traditional femininity and find her own sense of belonging. As she navigates this new world, she must confront the complexities of gender roles and societal norms.

Throughout the film, Cailley explores the tension between Mathilde's desire for freedom and her need for acceptance. The character's relationships with others, particularly her mother and a young boy named Thomas, serve as a catalyst for her growth and self-discovery.

One of the most striking aspects of Tomboy is its nuanced portrayal of childhood innocence and vulnerability. Mathilde's journey is marked by moments of tenderness, curiosity, and wonder, which serve to underscore the fragility and beauty of childhood.

Ultimately, Tomboy is a poignant exploration of what it means to be oneself in a world that often seeks to define and constrain us. The film's thoughtful and understated approach invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences with identity, self-expression, and the complexities of growing up.

original_title: What We Did on Our Holiday
overview: Doug and Abi  and their three children travel to the Scottish Highlands for Doug's father Gordie's birthday party. It's soon clear that when it comes to keeping a secret under wraps from the rest of the family, their children are their biggest liability...
title: What We Did on Our Holiday
plot:
What We Did on Our Holiday is a 2014 British black comedy-drama written and directed by Andy Hamilton and Guy Jenkin, inspired by but unrelated to the BBC series Outnumbered. It stars David Tennant and Rosamund Pike as Doug and Abi McLeod and Billy Connolly as Doug's father, Gordie, with Ben Miller and Amelia Bullmore.

Separated after Doug's affair, Doug and Abi travel together with their three children, Lottie, Mickey and Jess, to the Scottish Highlands for Gordie's 75th birthday, pretending to still be a couple so as not to upset him; Gordie has terminal cancer. Doug's wealthy brother Gavin has planned a lavish party for him. After a congested journey and an overnight stop, the family reaches Gavin's mansion, where a tense rivalry between the brothers soon surfaces. Gordie, though gravely ill, is playful and urges his grandchildren, especially Lottie, to let go of their worries and enjoy life.

While the adults and Gavin's wife, Margaret, finalize the party, Gordie takes the children to the beach, telling them that he is descended from Vikings, and dies peacefully while they play. Lottie runs back to tell the adults but finds them quarreling, with Abi telling Doug that she is seeing someone and moving the children to Newcastle, so she returns without saying anything. Using fuel from Gordie's pickup, the children send his body out to sea on a burning makeshift raft, honoring his wish for a Viking funeral. When they confess, the horrified adults find the truck half submerged by the tide, and Gavin breaks down in Doug's arms. News of the children's act spreads around the world, the press swarms the house, and a social worker, Agnes Chisholm, considers taking the children into care. The children also accidentally broadcast a video revealing Margaret's depression to Gavin. Doug and Abi publicly defend their children's well-meant if misguided tribute, and in light of the support the children receive, Chisholm drops her inquiry. The brothers make peace and hold a memorial on the beach, Abi decides against moving, and the couple agree to an amicable divorce, apologizing to their children before the family plays together at the water's edge.

Lionsgate released the film in the United Kingdom on 26 September 2014, and it opened in the United States as What We Did on Our Vacation on 10 July 2015. It grossed about $8.4 million worldwide. Rotten Tomatoes gave it 73%, praising it as witty and well cast, while Metacritic scored it 54.

belongs_to_collection.name: In the Name of the King Collection

original_title: In the Name of the King: A Dungeon Siege Tale
overview: A man named Farmer sets out to rescue his kidnapped wife and avenge the death of his son -- two acts committed by the Krugs, a race of animal-warriors who are controlled by the evil Gallian.
production_companies: Boll Kino Beteiligungs GmbH & Co. KG
tagline: Rise and Fight
title: In the Name of the King: A Dungeon Siege Tale
plot:
In the Name of the King: A Dungeon Siege Tale is an action-adventure film that delves into the realms of power, redemption, and self-discovery. The story revolves around a humble blacksmith named Duncan, who finds himself thrust into a world of magic and politics after being betrayed by his king.

As Duncan navigates this new world, he must confront his own demons and grapple with the consequences of his past actions. He soon discovers that he has a crucial role to play in the fate of the kingdom, and that his very existence is tied to the prophecy of an ancient hero.

Throughout the film, the main theme of power and its corrupting influence is expertly woven throughout the narrative. The characters' struggles for dominance and control serve as a catalyst for Duncan's journey, forcing him to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the true cost of ambition.

The film also explores the idea of redemption and personal growth, as Duncan seeks to make amends for past mistakes and forge a new path forward. His transformation from an ordinary blacksmith to a hero is a powerful metaphor for the human capacity for change and the possibility of redemption in the face of adversity.

Ultimately, In the Name of the King: A Dungeon Siege Tale is a tale of self-discovery and empowerment, as Duncan finds his place in the world and learns to wield his newfound power with wisdom and humility. The film's themes of power, redemption, and personal growth are timeless and universal, making it a compelling watch for audiences seeking an epic adventure with depth and substance.

overview: In the mythical Elven world of Altera, an epic battle unfolds between the beautiful Princess Liya and the Dark Elf Elena, who has gained possession of a jewel so powerful it allows its holder complete authority over all Alterans.
title: Throne of Elves
plot:
Throne of Elves, also known as Dragon Nest 2: Throne of Elves, is a 2016 Chinese animated adventure romance directed by Song Yuefeng and the sequel to the 2014 film Dragon Nest: Warriors' Dawn, itself based on the video game Dragon Nest. The English dub features Ryan Potter as Little Fish, Ashley Boettcher as Princess Liya, Anika Noni Rose as Meyla, Julie Nathanson as Queen Mayre, Gavin Hammon as Prince Alyan, Kevin Michael Richardson as Barnac and Enn Reitel as the blacksmith Berlin.

Years after the first film, Liya's brother Alyan is to marry her friend Mayre, queen of the Elves, and Liya invites her human sweetheart, Little Fish, now apprenticed to Berlin, despite Mayre's reluctance. Meanwhile, Mayre's long-lost sister Meyla, consumed by evil, plots to rule all Elves by seizing the Gem of Life, the counterpart and power source of her own dark gem, and raises Elven ghosts from an ancient battlefield as her army. Sensing the threat, Mayre entrusts the gem to Liya, warning her to keep it from Fish because humans are prone to greed. Fish arrives with Berlin and Barnac to a cold welcome from the Elves, including Alyan, who distrust humans.

During the wedding, Meyla attacks, and failing to find the gem on Mayre, abducts her, infecting Fish with dark magic when he intervenes. She demands the gem from Alyan as ransom at the ancient battlefield. Alyan pursues her with Liya and his guards, and Fish follows on Berlin's hoverboard, but their attempt to free Mayre from Meyla's flying ship fails, and Meyla invades Fish's mind. She imprisons Mayre in the Dark Valley, a black mountain ringed by lava furnaces, and travels north to merge with the soul of a great dragon frozen in ice. Fish resists her control and rejoins Alyan's party, rescuing the few survivors of a ghost ambush, but Meyla later forces him to try to seize the gem from Liya. When they shoot at each other, his love lets him break free, and he fires a headless arrow while hers mortally wounds him; Liya heals him with the gem. United, humans and Elves head for the Dark Valley, where Liya sends the gem to Mayre by arrow. Meyla takes a demonic form, and Fish lures her into a lava furnace, killing them both. The Gem of Life then frees the ghosts, turns the furnace into a tree and revives Fish, convincing Alyan that humans can be selfless, while the overlooked Meyla also returns to life, cleansed of darkness.

Beijing Enlight Pictures released the film in China in 2D and 3D, where it grossed CN¥23.4 million.

overview: Allie, a veterinarian in Evergreen, reluctantly will spend Christmas with her long-distance boyfriend. Bound for the airport, she has engine trouble, and Ryan, headed to Florida with his daughter Zoe, stops to help. Sure they won’t meet again, they ignore their attraction, and part ways. At the diner, Zoe wishes on a snow globe, and a storm seems to grant her wish.
title: Christmas in Evergreen
plot:
Christmas in Evergreen is a heartwarming holiday film that explores the themes of love, family, and second chances. The movie follows Samantha, a successful businesswoman who returns to her small hometown of Evergreen after a painful loss, only to find herself rekindling old flames with a childhood sweetheart, Jake.

As Samantha navigates her complicated past and present, she must confront the choices that led her away from her roots and the people she loves. The film masterfully weaves together themes of nostalgia, forgiveness, and the power of community, highlighting the importance of embracing one's heritage and finding comfort in the familiar.

Through Samantha's journey, Christmas in Evergreen also touches on the idea of letting go of past regrets and embracing new beginnings. As she rediscovers the joys of small-town life and reconnects with Jake, she begins to see that sometimes, it's never too late to rediscover what truly matters in life.

Ultimately, the film presents a poignant exploration of the human experience during the holiday season, reminding viewers that love, family, and community are the greatest gifts of all.

overview: Best friends, Carl and Lester, find themselves magically transported into an alternate universe straight out of a real-life adult movie. Hilarity ensues as they embark upon a journey of adult-themed mayhem while Carl ultimately finds true love in the most unlikely of places.
tagline: Where Every Fantasy Comes True
title: Deep in the Valley
plot:
Deep in the Valley, released in the United Kingdom as American Hot Babes, is a 2009 American romantic comedy film written and directed by Christian Forte, the son of the 1950s and 1960s teen idol Fabian. It stars Chris Pratt as Lester Watts and Brendan Hines as his best friend Carl, with Scott Caan as the police officer Rod Cannon, Rachel Specter as Bambi Cummings, Christopher McDonald as "Diamond Jim", Denise Richards as Autumn Bliss, Kim Kardashian as Summa Eve, Blanca Soto as Suzi "Diablo" and Tracy Morgan as "Busta Nut".

Lester works in a liquor store, where he cheerfully sells alcohol to minors and spends whatever money he has left on his pornography collection. His best friend since the third grade, Carl, works a corporate job at the family company of his British fiancée, and when he says he wants to quit and find work elsewhere, she angrily tells him that he has no choice but to stay, making it clear that she controls every aspect of their relationship. That night, as the two friends share a beer, a delivery arrives: a vintage porn viewing booth that plays the films of the adult film mogul Diamond Jim. When they step inside, the machine transports them into a world where everyone behaves as if they are in a pornographic movie. They are soon arrested by police officers led by Rod Cannon, but they escape and are hidden from the authorities by Bambi Cummings at her sorority house, Tri-Pi. As the pair evade the police, Carl and Bambi fall in love. Eventually the friends make their way to a pool party at Diamond Jim's mansion, where Carl chooses to be sent home while Lester decides to stay behind, and it is revealed that Lester is in fact Diamond Jim's son. Back in the real world, Carl breaks up with his domineering fiancée, and Bambi is transported to him, reuniting the couple. Meanwhile, Lester takes over his father's adult entertainment empire. In a scene after the closing credits, Rod is revealed to have been transported to the real world, where he has taken over Lester's old job at the liquor store.

The film's soundtrack includes songs by Darius Holbert, Jake Keller and Bang Camaro, whose "Push, Push (Lady Lightning)" is featured.

original_title: ドラゴンボールZ 地球まるごと超決戦
overview: Goku and friends must stop a band of space pirates from consuming fruit from the Tree of Might before it's destructive powers drain Earth's energy.
title: Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might
plot:
Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might is a 1990 Japanese animated science fantasy martial arts film produced by Toei Animation, based on the popular manga and anime series Dragon Ball Z. The movie takes place during the Saiyan Saga of the original Dragon Ball Z series.

The story begins with Goku and his friends celebrating the defeat of Frieza on Planet Namek. However, their celebration is short-lived as a powerful being known as Turles arrives on Earth. Unbeknownst to Goku and his friends, Turles is actually the long-lost brother of Raditz, the Saiyan who killed Goku's father.

Turles reveals that he has come to Earth to destroy it and its inhabitants, and to claim the Tree of Might, a powerful being with the ability to grant wishes. The Tree of Might is located on Earth and is guarded by a group of powerful warriors known as the Guardians of the Tree.

Goku and his friends soon discover Turles' true intentions and band together to stop him. Along the way, they meet a new ally in the form of Tien Shinhan, a powerful warrior from the planet Capricorn who has come to Earth to help defend it against Turles.

As the battle between Goku and Turles intensifies, the two engage in an epic fight that pushes both warriors to their limits. Meanwhile, Vegeta, who had been watching the battle from afar, becomes increasingly frustrated with his own lack of power compared to Turles' abilities.

In the end, it is revealed that Turles was actually sent to Earth by Frieza as a test to see if Goku and his friends could defeat him. With this knowledge, Goku and his friends are able to gain the upper hand in their battle against Turles, and he is ultimately defeated.

The movie ends with Goku and his friends celebrating their victory over Turles, while Vegeta finally finds the strength and confidence to join them as a powerful warrior. The Tree of Might is also shown to be destroyed, but its legacy lives on through the power of the warriors who defended it.

Overall, Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might is an action-packed and entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and the power of determination. With its epic battles and memorable characters, it remains a beloved entry in the Dragon Ball Z franchise.

overview: When an international border dispute arises between the U.S. and Canada, the Super Troopers- Mac, Thorny, Foster, Rabbit and Farva, are called in to set up a new Highway Patrol station in the disputed area.
tagline: The mustache rides. Again.
title: Super Troopers 2
plot:
Super Troopers 2 is a comedy film that explores several themes, primarily revolving around the camaraderie and brotherhood among its characters. The movie delves into the idea of loyalty and friendship as the five Vermont state troopers - Mac, Thorny, Foster, Rabbit, and Farva - embark on a mission to protect the state's maple syrup industry from an invasive Canadian company.

The film also touches upon the theme of identity and growth, as the characters navigate their personal lives and confront their own limitations. The movie pokes fun at the idea of masculinity and traditional male roles, often using humor to comment on societal expectations and stereotypes.

Furthermore, Super Troopers 2 features a strong sense of community and regional pride, celebrating the unique culture and traditions of Vermont. The film's lighthearted tone and comedic approach allow it to tackle these themes in an entertaining and engaging way, making it a fun and entertaining ride for audiences.

overview: A long time ago in a distant fairy tale countryside, a young girl leads her little brother into a dark wood in desperate search of food and work, only to stumble upon a nexus of terrifying evil.
tagline: A grim fairy tale
title: Gretel & Hansel
plot:
Gretel & Hansel is a dark and atmospheric retelling of the classic fairy tale, Hansel and Gretel. The movie explores the darker aspects of human nature, particularly the theme of survival in a harsh environment. The story takes place in a foreboding forest, where the siblings are forced to fend for themselves after being abandoned by their father.

The film delves into the idea of the "other," as embodied by the witch who lives in the woods. This character represents the unknown, the feared, and the marginalized. She is a symbol of the dangers that lurk in the shadows, waiting to pounce on those who are vulnerable.

One of the main themes of Gretel & Hansel is the struggle for power and control. The witch seeks to exploit the siblings' innocence and vulnerability, while they must use their wits and resourcefulness to outsmart her. This theme is also reflected in the relationship between the two siblings, as they navigate their roles as caregiver and protector.

The movie also touches on the idea of trauma and its long-lasting effects. The siblings are forced to confront their dark past and the circumstances that led to their abandonment. This theme is woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and complexity to the story.

Overall, Gretel & Hansel is a haunting and atmospheric film that explores the darker aspects of human nature. It's a cautionary tale about the dangers of the unknown and the importance of resilience in the face of adversity.

overview: A video game expert Alex Rogan finds himself transported to another planet after conquering The Last Starfighter video game only to find out it was just a test. He was recruited to join the team of best Starfighters to defend their world from the attack.
tagline: He didn't find his dreams... his dreams found him.
title: The Last Starfighter
plot:
The Last Starfighter is a 1984 science fiction film directed by Nick Castle and produced by Universal Pictures.

The movie follows the story of Alex Rogan, an average teenager who discovers that he has been chosen to save the galaxy from an evil alien force. As Alex navigates his new role as a space fighter pilot, he must confront the harsh realities of war and the consequences of his own mortality.

At its core, The Last Starfighter is a film about the human condition, exploring themes of identity, duty, and the search for meaning in a chaotic universe. Through Alex's journey, the movie raises questions about what it means to be alive, to have purpose, and to leave a lasting impact on the world.

The film also delves into the idea of escapism, as Alex finds solace in his virtual reality game, which serves as a metaphor for the human desire to temporarily escape the difficulties of everyday life. However, as he becomes more immersed in the game, Alex must confront the consequences of his actions and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

Ultimately, The Last Starfighter is a classic tale of self-discovery, where Alex must come to terms with his own strengths and weaknesses, and find a way to reconcile his desire for adventure with the responsibilities that come with being a hero.

overview: A sheriff's deputy fights an alternate universe version of himself who grows stronger with each alternate self he kills.
tagline: Stealing the power of the universes one by one.
title: The One
plot:
The One is a 2001 science fiction action film directed by James Wong, starring Jet Li, Carla Gugino, Delroy Lindo, and Aram Rappaport. 

The movie revolves around the story of Fred Thompson (played by Jet Li), an immortal being who has been reincarnated multiple times throughout history to prevent a catastrophic event known as "the One" from occurring. The One is a powerful and ancient entity that will bring about the end of the world.

As the story unfolds, we see Fred's past lives, where he encounters various versions of himself in different time periods, each with their own unique abilities and struggles. Through his journeys, Fred discovers that he has been sent to prevent the One from being unleashed by a powerful sorcerer named Keanu Reeves' character, Soberan.

The main themes of The One include:

1. Destiny vs. Free Will: The movie explores the idea of whether our lives are predetermined or if we have control over our own destinies. Fred's multiple reincarnations raise questions about the nature of fate and whether he can truly change his course.
2. Immortality and the Human Condition: As an immortal being, Fred grapples with the consequences of living forever, including watching loved ones die and accumulating knowledge that is beyond human comprehension.
3. Good vs. Evil: The film's central conflict pits good (Fred) against evil (Soberan), highlighting the eternal struggle between light and darkness.
4. Self-Discovery: Throughout his journeys, Fred learns more about himself and his purpose in life, leading to a deeper understanding of who he is and what he wants.

The One received mixed reviews from critics but has since become a cult classic, praised for its unique blend of action, science fiction, and philosophical themes.

overview: Tortured by the ghosts of the demonized insane asylum that killed the crew of GRAVE ENCOUNTERS, film students fight to escape death as their own paranormal investigation goes terribly wrong in this horrifying sequel.
tagline: Fear is just a word. Reality is much worse.
title: Grave Encounters 2
plot:
Grave Encounters 2 is a 2012 Canadian found-footage horror film directed by The Goren brothers, not Death Awaits Cinema. 

The movie follows a group of friends who are invited to the same asylum where the events of the first Grave Encounters took place. They soon discover that they have been brought there for a sinister purpose.

The main themes of Grave Encounters 2 include:

1. The Power of Trauma: The film explores how traumatic experiences can shape individuals and lead them down dark paths.
2. Isolation and Confinement: The characters are trapped in the asylum, which serves as a metaphor for their own emotional confinement and feelings of isolation.
3. The Dangers of Curiosity: The group's curiosity about the asylum and its dark past ultimately leads to their downfall.
4. The Blurred Lines between Reality and Fantasy: As the story unfolds, it becomes increasingly difficult to distinguish between what is real and what is just a product of the characters' imaginations.

The film received mixed reviews from critics but has developed a cult following over the years.

overview: Lenny has relocated his family back to the small town where he and his friends grew up. This time around, the grown ups are the ones learning lessons from their kids on a day notoriously full of surprises—the last day of school.
tagline: Just because they're a little older doesn't mean they've grown up.
title: Grown Ups 2
plot:
Grown Ups 2 is a 2013 American comedy film directed by Dennis Dugan and written by Adam Sandler, Fred Wolf, and Tim Herlihy. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2009 film Grown Ups.

The story takes place two years after the events of the first film. Lenny Feder (Adam Sandler) is now married to Roxanne Chase (Salma Hayek), and they have twin babies. However, their happiness is short-lived as they face various challenges, including a messy divorce from Roxanne's family, who are wealthy and influential.

Meanwhile, Eric Lamonsoff (Kevin James) is struggling with his own life, feeling like he's lost touch with his friends and his sense of purpose. He decides to take a break from his wife and kids to attend the same summer camp where he spent his childhood, in an attempt to recapture some of that youthful energy.

As Lenny tries to navigate his new role as a father, he also has to deal with his own midlife crisis. He starts to question whether he's truly happy with his life choices and feels pressure from his friends to be more like them.

The movie follows the misadventures of the four main characters - Lenny, Eric, Marcus (Chris Rock), and Kurt (David Spade) - as they try to reconnect with each other and find their way in life. Along the way, they encounter a series of hilarious and chaotic situations, including a disastrous family reunion and a wild night at a summer camp.

Throughout the film, the characters grapple with themes of friendship, love, and growing up. While some of the jokes may feel a bit forced or predictable, the movie's lighthearted tone and comedic chemistry between the leads make for an entertaining watch.

Overall, Grown Ups 2 is a fun, if not entirely original, comedy that explores the ups and downs of adulthood and the importance of maintaining friendships.

overview: Long ago, in the fantasy world of Kumandra, humans and dragons lived together in harmony. But when an evil force threatened the land, the dragons sacrificed themselves to save humanity. Now, 500 years later, that same evil has returned and it’s up to a lone warrior, Raya, to track down the legendary last dragon to restore the fractured land and its divided people.
tagline: A quest to save her world.
title: Raya and the Last Dragon
plot:
Raya and the Last Dragon is a 2021 animated fantasy adventure film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. The movie takes place in the fictional world of Kumandra, where humans and dragons coexisted in harmony until a curse caused the dragons to disappear.

The story follows Raya (voiced by Kelly Marie Tran), a skilled warrior from the kingdom of Kumandra who is on a quest to find the last dragon, Sisu. According to legend, Sisu's tears have the power to heal the curse that has ravaged Kumandra, causing widespread destruction and chaos.

Raya sets out on her journey with her trusty companion, Namaari (voiced by Awkwafina), who is initially portrayed as a rival but later becomes an ally. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, ferocious creatures, and other warriors seeking to exploit the curse for their own gain.

As Raya delves deeper into the heart of Kumandra, she discovers that Sisu's disappearance is linked to her own past and the reason behind the curse. The film features stunning animation, action-packed sequences, and a richly detailed world inspired by Southeast Asian cultures.

Throughout her journey, Raya learns valuable lessons about courage, friendship, and the importance of embracing her own identity. With the help of Sisu, she ultimately discovers that the key to breaking the curse lies within herself and the power of unity among the people of Kumandra.

The film features a talented voice cast, including Gemma Chan as the voice of the dragon Sisu, and a memorable soundtrack by Alan Menken and Opetaia Foa'i. Raya and the Last Dragon is a heartwarming and visually stunning adventure that celebrates the beauty of diversity and the strength of community.

overview: Nagata works as a writer and director for theater company Oroka. His work has not received positive responses and ticket sales has not increased. Making things worse, his relationship with the theatrical troupe is not good. Nagata feels lonely. One day, he sees a woman named Saki  on the street. She is wearing the same sneakers as he is. Nagata talks to her. Saki is a university student and she dreams of becoming an actress. Nagata and Saki fall in love.
title: Theatre: A Love Story
plot:
Theatre: A Love Story (Japanese: Gekijō) is a 2020 Japanese romantic drama directed by Isao Yukisada from a screenplay by Ryūta Hōrai, adapted from the novel by comedian and author Naoki Matayoshi. The book, Matayoshi's first love story, was serialised in the literary magazine Shinchō in April 2017 and published by Shinchosha the following month; like his earlier Spark, it follows a young artist chasing success in Tokyo. The film's score was composed by Keiichi Sokabe.

Kento Yamazaki plays Nagata, a struggling playwright and director who co-founded the small theatre company Oroka with his school friend Nohara (Kanichiro Sato). His avant-garde productions draw poor reviews and few ticket sales, and his relations with the troupe are deteriorating. Wandering the streets in a daze, he stops at a gallery window and notices a young woman, Saki (Mayu Matsuoka), who is wearing the same sneakers as him. Saki has come to Tokyo from Aomori to study at a fashion college and dreams of becoming an actress, and the two fall in love. Nagata soon moves into her apartment, contributing nothing towards the rent while she works several jobs. Over the years his insecurity, jealousy of other people's success and possessive, dismissive treatment of her gradually wear Saki down, leaving her depressed and drinking heavily as she nears thirty. A former troupe member, Aoyama (Sairi Ito), and Nohara confront him about his behaviour, and Nagata ultimately turns their story into a stage play. Satoru Iguchi of the band King Gnu appears as Komine, a rival playwright of the same age, with Shusaku Kamikawa, Ritsu Otomo and Kodai Asaka in supporting roles.

The film, made by The Fool and distributed by Shochiku and Aniplex, was due to open on 17 April 2020, but the release was postponed indefinitely as COVID-19 spread in Japan. In June, Yoshimoto Kogyo took over distribution, and the film opened in cinemas on 17 July 2020 while also streaming worldwide on Amazon Prime Video the same day, reportedly the first time a Japanese live-action feature had done so.

Sairi Ito won the Blue Ribbon Award for Best Supporting Actress. Reviews were divided over the central character. The Japan Times headlined its review as a tortured romance with no sparks, while Windows on Worlds read the film as a portrait of toxic narcissism and abusive behaviour, seen only through Nagata's eyes, that ends with him rediscovering his love of theatre and accepting that a chapter of life has closed.

overview: The Minions, having been accidently dropped off at the North Pole, make the most of the situation by trying to become elves.
title: Santa's Little Helpers
plot:
Santa's Little Helpers is a 2019 American computer-animated Christmas comedy short film produced by Illumination and starring the Minions of the Despicable Me franchise. Running about four minutes, it was directed by Derek Drymon and Bruno Chauffard, with a story by David Feiss and a screenplay by Brett Kramer and Josh Lieb. Conceived as a "mini-movie" bonus feature, it debuted with the home-entertainment release of Illumination's 2018 feature The Grinch, appearing first with the digital release in January 2019 and then on the 4K Ultra HD, Blu-ray and DVD editions in February 2019. It follows the earlier Minions mini-movie Yellow Is the New Black and precedes Minion Scouts. Pierre Coffin voices the Minions, among them Kevin, Stuart and Bob, with Carlos Alazraqui as Santa Claus, Raymond S. Persi as the Head Elf, Tara Strong as a baby reindeer and Brian T. Delaney as an adult reindeer, several of the cast also voicing elves.

Kevin, Stuart and Bob have been mailed off to Miami, but they are accidentally dropped at the North Pole instead. Spotting a light in the snow, they discover Santa's Workshop, and since it has always been their dream to meet Santa and help deliver his presents, they make the most of the situation by trying to become elves. They are not very good at it. On the toy assembly line they produce a hybrid teddy bear and train, so they are moved to gingerbread house duty. Kevin builds a beautiful gingerbread house, only for Stuart to wreck it with his gingerbread crane, while Bob manages to get himself stuck inside his own creation and Stuart starts eating the house as Kevin tries to free him. The exasperated Head Elf banishes the trio to the reindeer stables. There Bob spots a baby reindeer apparently caught in a fence post and opens the gate to help, but it is a ruse to free the reindeer from their stalls, and before long the Minions have left the whole workshop in ruins. When Santa arrives, the Minions accidentally take off with his sleigh. The short ends with the three singing a Minionese version of "Jingle Bells" over a series of photos, one of which shows them delivering presents to Who-ville, the village from The Grinch.

The short gained a wider audience on 27 November 2020, when it was broadcast on NBC as one of four mini-movies in the Minions Holiday Special, Illumination's first television special, alongside Puppy, Training Wheels and Minion Scouts.

overview: A young woman unleashes terrifying demons when supernatural forces at the root of a decades-old rift between mother and daughter are ruthlessly revealed.
tagline: It's not a dream, it's not reality.
title: Demonic
plot:
Demonic is a 2021 American supernatural horror film directed by Will Bowden and written by Brian DeLeeuw. The movie follows the story of a young woman named Erin, played by Olivia Luccardi, who returns to her hometown of New Haven, Connecticut, after a traumatic event in her past.

Upon her return, Erin discovers that her childhood home has been taken over by a mysterious and malevolent presence, which seems to be connected to an ancient evil entity known as the "Demonic". The entity is said to have been awakened by a group of occultists who performed a dark ritual in the house, unleashing a powerful and malevolent force upon the world.

As Erin delves deeper into the mystery, she begins to experience strange and terrifying occurrences, including visions, nightmares, and unexplained events. She soon realizes that she is being stalked by the entity, which seems to be manipulating her perceptions of reality.

Erin's investigation leads her to a local occult shop, where she meets a mysterious woman named Sarah, played by Tati Gabrielle. Sarah claims to have knowledge about the entity and offers to help Erin understand what is happening to her. However, it becomes clear that Sarah has her own motivations and may not be entirely trustworthy.

As the story unfolds, Erin discovers that the entity is connected to an ancient cult that was thought to be extinct. The cult's leader, a charismatic figure known as Father, played by Jake Weber, seems to be behind the ritual that awakened the entity. However, it becomes clear that Father has his own agenda and may not be what he seems.

The plot thickens as Erin and Sarah work together to uncover the truth about the entity and its connection to the cult. Along the way, they encounter a series of terrifying and supernatural events, including possession, hallucinations, and unexplained deaths.

In the climactic final act, Erin and Sarah face off against Father and the entity in a desperate bid to stop the ritual and banish the evil presence from the world. The movie culminates in a shocking twist, as it is revealed that Erin herself may be connected to the entity and has been playing a crucial role in its awakening.

The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the true nature of the entity and its connection to Erin. The final shot of the movie shows Erin standing alone, surrounded by an eerie and unsettling atmosphere, suggesting that she may still be under the influence of the entity.

Overall, Demonic is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores themes of trauma, possession, and the supernatural. With its slow-burning tension and creepy atmosphere, it's sure to appeal to fans of the genre.

overview: The true story of British intelligence whistleblower Katharine Gun who—prior to the 2003 Iraq invasion—leaked a top-secret NSA memo exposing a joint US-UK illegal spying operation against members of the UN Security Council. The memo proposed blackmailing member states into voting for war.
tagline: Nothing is more dangerous than the truth
title: Official Secrets
plot:
Official Secrets is a 2019 British drama film directed by Gavin Hood, not Screen Yorkshire.

The main themes of Official Secrets include:

1. Whistleblowing: The film revolves around Katharine Gun, a British intelligence officer who leaks classified information about the UK's surveillance program on Saudi Arabia to The Guardian newspaper.
2. Government Secrecy and Accountability: The movie highlights the tension between national security and individual rights, as Katharine is forced to confront the consequences of her actions.
3. Feminism and Empowerment: Katharine Gun is a strong-willed and intelligent character who challenges the patriarchal norms of the intelligence agency and the government.
4. Morality and Ethics: The film raises questions about the morality of whistleblowing, the responsibility of those in power, and the consequences of taking a stand against injustice.

The movie also explores themes of loyalty, duty, and the personal cost of standing up for what one believes in.

Overall, Official Secrets is a thought-provoking drama that sheds light on the complexities of national security, individual rights, and the human cost of whistleblowing.

overview: Famed but tormented artist Vincent van Gogh spends his final years in Arles, France, painting masterworks of the natural world that surrounds him.
tagline: A Grain of Madness is the Best of Art
title: At Eternity's Gate
plot:
At Eternity's Gate is a 2018 biographical drama film directed by Justin Kurzel, produced by CBS Films, and written by Matthew Spiegel.

The main themes of At Eternity's Gate revolve around the life of Vincent van Gogh (played by Oscar Isaac), a renowned Dutch post-impressionist artist. The film explores several key aspects of Van Gogh's life, including:

1. **Mental Health**: The film delves into Van Gogh's struggles with mental illness, particularly his episodes of depression and anxiety. His struggles are portrayed as a constant companion throughout his life, influencing his art and relationships.
2. **Artistic Expression**: At Eternity's Gate highlights the intense passion and dedication that drove Van Gogh to create some of the most iconic works in art history. The film showcases his innovative techniques and bold use of color, which set him apart from other artists of his time.
3. **Relationships and Isolation**: The film explores Van Gogh's complex relationships with others, including his brother Theo (played by Guy Pearce) and his lover Sien (played by Mia Wasikowska). His struggles to connect with others are juxtaposed with his desire for solitude and the isolation that often accompanied his artistic pursuits.
4. **Existentialism and Faith**: The film touches on Van Gogh's spiritual struggles, particularly his conversion to Christianity and his subsequent questioning of its teachings. This internal conflict is reflected in his art, which often grappled with themes of mortality, suffering, and the search for meaning.

Throughout the film, these themes are intertwined, creating a nuanced portrait of an artist whose life was marked by both brilliance and turmoil. The title "At Eternity's Gate" refers to Van Gogh's famous painting "The Starry Night," which has become an iconic representation of his artistic style and emotional depth.

Overall, At Eternity's Gate is a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that continues to resonate with audiences today.

overview: When their trip to San Lorenzo takes a turn for the worst, Arnold and his classmate’s only hope of getting home is retracing the dangerous path that led to Arnold's parents' disappearance.
tagline: After all these years, all your questions will finally be answered.
title: Hey Arnold! The Jungle Movie
plot:
Hey Arnold! The Jungle Movie is a 2017 animated musical comedy-drama film that serves as a sequel to the original series. The movie follows Arnold Shortman and his friends as they navigate their final year of boarding school in Elwood City.

The main themes of Hey Arnold! The Jungle Movie revolve around:

1. **Growing Up and Goodbyes**: The movie explores the challenges of growing up, particularly for teenagers who are facing the prospect of leaving home and starting a new chapter in their lives. Arnold must come to terms with his own identity and the impending departure from his friends and family.
2. **Friendship and Loyalty**: The film highlights the importance of strong friendships and loyalty. Arnold's relationships with his friends, particularly Gerald, Helga, and Harold, are put to the test as they face various challenges and obstacles together.
3. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As Arnold navigates his final year of boarding school, he begins to explore his own identity and sense of purpose. He must confront his feelings about his family's past and his own place in the world.
4. **Family and Belonging**: The movie explores the complexities of family relationships and the importance of finding one's place within a community. Arnold's experiences with his family, particularly his parents and grandparents, help him understand what it means to belong and be accepted for who he is.

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together through music, humor, and heartwarming moments that celebrate the power of friendship and the challenges of growing up.

overview: After discovering a once-in-a-lifetime player with a rocky past abroad, a down on his luck basketball scout takes it upon himself to bring the phenom to the States without his team's approval. Against the odds, they have one final shot to prove they have what it takes to make it in the NBA.
tagline: Are you obsessed with this game?
title: Hustle
plot:
Hustle is a sports drama film released in 2022, directed by Jody Lee Lipes and produced by Happy Madison Productions. The movie stars Adam Sandler as Stanley Sugarman, a talent scout who discovers an unpolished basketball player with immense potential.

The story begins with Stanley Sugarman (Adam Sandler), a struggling talent scout who has lost his way after being fired from his previous job. He is desperate to revive his career and prove himself once again. One day, while watching a game in the park, he spots an unpolished but talented basketball player named Bo Cruz (Jonathan Majors). Stanley recognizes the potential in Bo and decides to take him under his wing.

As Stanley works with Bo, he realizes that the young man has incredible skills on the court, but lacks the confidence and polish required to succeed at the highest level. Despite this, Stanley is determined to help Bo become a star player. He takes Bo to various gyms and courts around New York City, where they face numerous challenges and setbacks.

Throughout their journey, Stanley and Bo develop an unlikely friendship, with Stanley serving as both a mentor and a father figure to Bo. As Bo's skills improve, he begins to attract attention from top college coaches and NBA scouts. However, Bo struggles with the pressure of living up to his potential, and Stanley must find ways to keep him grounded and focused.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Stanley's own life, including his troubled childhood and his experiences as a young talent scout. These scenes provide insight into Stanley's motivations and backstory, adding depth to his character.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Bo is offered a chance to play for a top college team, but he must decide whether to take the opportunity or stay with Stanley in New York City. In the end, Bo chooses to pursue his dreams, leaving Stanley heartbroken but proud of the young man he has helped become.

The film concludes with Stanley reflecting on his journey and the lessons he has learned from Bo. Despite facing numerous setbacks and disappointments throughout his career, Stanley remains optimistic and determined to continue helping talented athletes achieve their goals.

Overall, Hustle is a heartwarming and inspiring story about the power of mentorship and perseverance. With Adam Sandler delivering a standout performance as the charismatic but troubled talent scout, the movie is a must-see for sports fans and anyone looking for an uplifting underdog story.

overview: During China's Tang dynasty the emperor has taken the princess of a neighboring province as his wife. She has borne him two sons and raised his eldest. Now his control over his dominion is complete, including the royal family itself.
production_companies: Beijing New Picture Film Co. Ltd.
tagline: Unspeakable secrets are hidden within the Forbidden City.
title: Curse of the Golden Flower
plot:
Curse of the Golden Flower is a 2006 Chinese epic wuxia drama film written and directed by Zhang Yimou, based on Cao Yu's 1934 play Thunderstorm but set in imperial China. Chow Yun-fat stars as Emperor Ping and Gong Li as Empress Phoenix, with Jay Chou as their son Prince Jai, Liu Ye as Crown Prince Wan, Qin Junjie as Prince Yu, Ni Dahong as the Imperial Physician Jiang and Li Man as his daughter Jiang Chan. Costing US$45 million, it was then the most expensive Chinese film.

On the eve of the Double Ninth Festival, the Emperor and his second son, Prince Jai, return from a military campaign to celebrate with the family. The Empress has been having an affair with Crown Prince Wan, the Emperor's son by a previous wife, while Wan loves Jiang Chan and hopes to run away with her. Jai notices that his mother's health is failing and is puzzled by her sudden interest in chrysanthemums. She reveals that the Emperor has been poisoning her tea for some time and that she is planning a rebellion, which Jai agrees to lead. A mysterious woman the Empress hires to identify the poison is caught by Wan and brought to the Emperor; she is Jiang Shi, the physician's wife, once imprisoned by the Emperor and believed dead. When Wan learns from Jiang Chan that the Empress has had 10,000 scarves made bearing golden flower emblems, he confronts her and, anguished by her plot, tries to kill himself but survives. After the Emperor sends the physician to a new post as governor, assassins kill him on the road, and when Jiang Shi and her daughter return to confront him, the Empress reveals that Jiang Shi was the Emperor's first wife and Wan's mother, making Wan and Jiang Chan half-siblings. Both women are then murdered. The youngest prince, Yu, then kills Wan and demands the throne, and the Emperor beats him to death. Jai leads 10,000 soldiers bearing golden flower emblems into the palace, only to see them massacred by the Emperor's reserve army, and servants erase every trace of the battle before the midnight festival. Offered a pardon if he helps poison his mother, Jai kills himself instead, and the Empress hurls away the poisoned tea, which eats into the golden flower carved in the table.

China's submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, it received an Oscar nomination for costume design and won four Hong Kong Film Awards, including Best Actress for Gong Li. It grossed over $78 million worldwide and holds a 65% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

overview: Telly Paretta is a grieving mother struggling to cope with the loss of her 8-year-old son. She is stunned when her psychiatrist reveals that she has created eight years of memories about a son she never had. But when she meets a man who has had a similar experience, Telly embarks on a search to prove her son's existence, and her sanity.
tagline: You'll Never Forget The Ones You Love
title: The Forgotten
plot:
The Forgotten is an American science fiction psychological thriller of 2004 directed by Joseph Ruben from a screenplay by Gerald Di Pego. Julianne Moore stars as Telly Paretta, a mother still grieving her son, with Dominic West as Ash, Gary Sinise as her psychiatrist Dr. Jack Munce, Anthony Edwards as her husband Jim, Alfre Woodard as the detective Anne Pope and Linus Roache as a mysterious man.

Fourteen months after her nine-year-old son Sam died in a plane crash, Telly keeps his room untouched and sees Munce to cope, while Jim wants to move on. One day she finds that Sam's pictures have vanished from her photo album. When she accuses Jim of trying to forget, he tells her that they never had a son, and Munce explains that she had a miscarriage and invented Sam as a fantasy of the life she might have had.
