Mia is murdered by the owner of the diamonds, who wants them back. In prison, an inmate named Saunders extorts $100,000 from Vincent to keep his father safe. Sonny hides part of Biggs's $2 million in a teddy bear packed in a box, then falsely tells Biggs that Vincent has his money, and a meeting between Biggs and Vincent ends in a deadly shootout. Vincent escapes, kills the owner of the diamonds when he breaks into his home, and is finally ambushed by Sonny at his car. Doused in oil and forced to dig his own grave, Vincent confesses that he betrayed his friends because Saunders had threatened his father and he needed the money. Sonny spares him, but Vincent's father is then killed in prison. Dave's girlfriend receives the teddy bear with the money, and Sonny drives away reflecting that while he could live with Vincent remaining alive, the question was whether Vincent could.

Lionsgate's Grindstone Entertainment Group released Setup on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States on September 20, 2011. In a handful of international markets it grossed about $2.1 million.

overview: A comedy centered on three museum security guards who devise a plan to steal back the artworks to which they have become attached after they are transferred to another museum.
tagline: They're not bad guys, just bad thieves.
title: The Maiden Heist
plot:
The Maiden Heist is a 2009 American crime comedy directed by Peter Hewitt and written by Michael LeSieur. Christopher Walken plays Roger Barlow, Morgan Freeman plays Charles Peterson and William H. Macy plays George McLendon, three museum security guards, with Marcia Gay Harden as Roger's wife, Rose.

Roger spends long hours at the art museum where he works gazing at his favorite painting, The Lonely Maiden, a portrait of a woman gazing wistfully into the distance. Rose, his wife, wants him to retire so they can move to Florida. When Roger learns that the Maiden and several other works are to be sent permanently to a museum in Copenhagen, he sinks into despair, until he discovers that his colleague Charles feels the same about a painting of a woman with cats on another floor. George is devoted to a nude sculpture of a Greek warrior and often strips to pose beside it during his night shifts. George proposes that they steal their beloved pieces and substitute replicas.

Roger volunteers to tag the works being shipped while the others arrange copies. Charles, himself a painter, reproduces the cat picture flawlessly but cannot capture the Maiden, so the men hire a street artist, and Roger dips into Rose's Florida savings to pay him. Rose grows suspicious. With George's replica statue and the new Maiden finished, George hides in the crate with the statue on the night of the switch and successfully exchanges all three pieces, but he cannot resist posing naked once more, and when a guard appears he must hide in the crate without his clothes. The next morning, as Roger and Charles arrive to collect him, accompanied by an unwitting Rose, his crate is loaded onto the wrong van, and after a frantic chase they free George, who emerges naked to Rose's astonishment. Their heist undetected, the three men retire. On a trip to Florida, Roger is captivated by Rose as she gazes out at the ocean in a pose resembling the Maiden, and their romance revives. The friends keep their treasures in a shack on the roof of Charles's building, but Roger finds the painting no longer moves him as his wife does, while in Copenhagen a guard smiles at the fake.

Produced under the working title The Lonely Maiden, the film was shot mainly in Boston, with scenes at the Worcester Art Museum. A planned May 2009 release was shelved when distributor Yari Film Group went bankrupt; the film debuted at the Edinburgh International Film Festival on June 25, 2009.

overview: When an outbreak hits, Aidan barricades himself inside his apartment and starts rationing food. His complex is overrun by infected Screamers, and with the world falling apart into chaos, he is left completely alone fighting for his life.
tagline: First the pandemic. Then the chaos.
title: Alone
plot:
Alone, released in the United Kingdom as Final Days, is a 2020 American horror film directed by Johnny Martin and an American remake of the 2020 South Korean film #Alive. Tyler Posey stars as Aidan, a young man who barricades himself inside his apartment during a zombie-like outbreak, with Donald Sutherland as Edward, Summer Spiro as Eva, Robert Ri'chard as Aidan's neighbour Brandon and John Posey as Aidan's father.

One morning Aidan wakes after a one-night stand to find a violent outbreak spreading outside, as people are attacked by infected people known as Screamers. His neighbour Brandon takes refuge in his apartment, but Aidan notices a wound on his neck and forces him out before he finishes turning. News reports explain that the infection spreads through bites and scratches, causing bleeding eyes, rage and cannibalism. Unable to call his family, Aidan receives text messages from his father saying that his sister has escaped and telling him to stay alive and stay home until his parents arrive. He shuts himself in, marking the days on his bathroom mirror, but his food runs low, the water is cut off and he begins hallucinating about his parents. He fights off a Screamer that breaks in through the air ducts and seals the vent. When a voicemail from his mother reveals that his parents have died, he prepares to hang himself, but stops when he sees a living woman, Eva, on a balcony across from his. Communicating with handwritten cards and later radios, they become friends, and Aidan shares water and supplies with her. Searching the ducts for more food, he enters a well-stocked, barricaded apartment and is knocked out by Edward, an elderly survivor, who ties him up as an offering to his infected wife. A radio call from Eva distracts Edward, and Aidan escapes, feeding Edward to his wife. He then climbs down from his balcony on knotted bedsheets, fights through Screamers to reach Eva and brings her back to his apartment. Fearing that a bloody mark on his shirt means he has been bitten, Aidan considers jumping to his death, but finds no wound. Holding the refrigerator against the door to keep the Screamers out, the two promise to survive together.

The film was released on video on demand on October 16, 2020, followed by DVD and Blu-ray days later. Reviews were largely negative, with critics criticizing its thin plot and abrupt ending; it holds a 27% Rotten Tomatoes rating from a small sample of reviews.

overview: Writer Ernest Hemingway begins a romance with fellow scribe Martha Gellhorn.
tagline: We were good in war. And when there was no war, we made our own.
title: Hemingway & Gellhorn
plot:
Hemingway & Gellhorn is a 2012 film that explores the tumultuous relationship between Ernest Hemingway and Martha Gellhorn, two prominent American writers. The movie delves into the complexities of their romance, which was marked by passion, intensity, and a deep emotional connection.

At its core, the film grapples with the theme of love as a destructive force that can both liberate and devastate individuals. Hemingway & Gellhorn portrays how the all-consuming nature of their relationship led to a cycle of addiction, self-destruction, and creative fervor. The movie suggests that this toxic dynamic was fueled by their shared experiences as war correspondents, which brought them together in the midst of chaos and conflict.

The film also explores the theme of identity and the blurred lines between reality and fiction. Hemingway & Gellhorn delves into the world of literary fiction, where characters are often fictionalized versions of real people, and the line between fact and fiction becomes increasingly ambiguous. The movie raises questions about the nature of truth and how it is shaped by personal experiences, relationships, and creative expression.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of female empowerment and the struggles faced by women in a male-dominated field. Martha Gellhorn's character is portrayed as a strong-willed and independent individual who navigates the challenges of being a woman in a world dominated by men. The movie highlights her determination to forge her own path and establish herself as a respected writer, despite facing numerous obstacles along the way.

Ultimately, Hemingway & Gellhorn presents a nuanced portrayal of two complex individuals whose lives were intertwined by their passion for writing, love, and war. The film's exploration of these themes offers a thought-provoking commentary on the human condition, highlighting the complexities and contradictions that define our experiences as individuals and as a society.

overview: Struggling comic Lance Barton knows what it's like to die on stage. But when his life takes an unexpected turn - straight to heaven - Lance is sure there's been a mistake. Miraculously, he's right! An angel tells Lance he was taken prematurely but assures him he can be returned to Earth - in the aged body of a ruthless white billionaire. In this improbable reincarnation, Lance begins a hilarious quest to realize his showbiz dream...and, along the way, discovers the person he never imagined he could be. Chris Rock delivers a first-rate performance in this romantic comedy remake of HEAVEN CAN WAIT.
title: Down to Earth
plot:
Down to Earth is a 2001 American romantic comedy film directed by Ken Kwapis and starring Chris Rock, Regina King, and Eddie Murphy.

The movie follows the story of Chris Cooper's character, Frank, who makes a deal with a mysterious woman to trade places with his wealthy and arrogant twin brother, John (played by Chris Rock). As Frank navigates his new life in wealth and luxury, he learns valuable lessons about humility, kindness, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

One of the main themes of Down to Earth is the idea that wealth and material possessions are not the key to happiness. Through Frank's experiences, the film shows how a more simple and genuine way of living can bring greater fulfillment and joy. The movie also explores the theme of identity and self-discovery, as Frank struggles to reconcile his old life with his new one.

Another significant theme in Down to Earth is the power of relationships and human connections. The film highlights the importance of building strong bonds with others and finding common ground with people from different walks of life. Through Frank's interactions with various characters, including a kind-hearted woman named Daphne (played by Regina King), the movie demonstrates that true happiness comes from forming meaningful connections with others.

Overall, Down to Earth is a heartwarming film that explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and the importance of staying grounded in life.

overview: A female FBI agent is offered millions to help a thief escape from a hijacked airplane.
title: Altitude
plot:
Altitude is a 2017 American thriller film directed by Martin Gery and written by Martin Gery and Michael Golfer. The movie follows a young woman named Alex, who travels to Colorado for a skiing trip with her boyfriend, but finds herself in the middle of a mysterious and deadly situation.

The main themes of Altitude include:

1. Isolation: The film takes place in a remote location, where the characters are cut off from the rest of the world. This isolation creates a sense of vulnerability and heightens the tension as the characters try to survive.
2. Survival: The movie is centered around Alex's struggle to stay alive after she becomes trapped in an elevator with a group of strangers who seem to be hiding secrets.
3. Trust: As the story unfolds, Alex must learn to trust her instincts and the people around her in order to uncover the truth behind the mysterious events.
4. Deception: The film is full of twists and turns, keeping the audience guessing about the true intentions of the characters.

The movie received mixed reviews from critics but has gained a cult following for its tense atmosphere and unexpected plot twists.

overview: Reclusive and controversial author Bruce Cogburn is drawn out of hiding by an obsessive fan, forcing the novelist to confront a past that he thought he could escape, and to account for events set in motion by his bestseller decades earlier. Cogburn's search for who is behind the manipulation and mental torment he encounters leads to an emotional roller-coaster ride full of fear and danger, where things are not always as clear as they seem to be, and where past deeds can have dire consequences.
tagline: What he created will destroy him.
title: The Infernal Machine
plot:
The Infernal Machine is a psychological mystery thriller of 2022 written and directed by Andrew Hunt, based on a story by Louis Kornfeld. Guy Pearce stars as Bruce Cogburn, a reclusive novelist, with Alice Eve as the police officer Laura Higgins, Alex Pettyfer as the convicted gunman Dwight Tufford and Jeremy Davies as Elijah Barrett. Paramount Pictures released it in the United States on 23 September 2022 and in the United Kingdom that December.

Cogburn is the controversial author of a single famous book, The Infernal Machine. For 25 years he has lived in self-imposed isolation in the American Southwest, having fled there in 1981 after a young man opened fire at a university in Knoxville, Tennessee, killing 13 people, and blamed the massacre on the novel. His seclusion is disturbed when his post office box begins filling with letters from William DuKent, a writer who wants to interview him. Cogburn drives 45 minutes to the nearest phone booth to leave ever more threatening messages telling DuKent to stop, but the letters keep coming, and his drinking and paranoia deepen. Using a false name, he visits the gunman, Dwight Tufford, in prison. Tufford later breaks out and turns up at Cogburn's house, where the writer manages to kill him.

Cogburn did not write The Infernal Machine: he stole it from Elijah Barrett, one of his students when he taught creative writing. After finishing the manuscript, Barrett suffered a breakdown and set himself on fire, leaving him in a coma. Cogburn, whose own writing had been repeatedly turned down by publishers as mediocre, published the novel under his name once he heard that Barrett's family planned to switch off his life support. But Barrett survived, and in the present he has written a second book, The Divine Apostate, also under Cogburn's name. After forcing a confrontation, Barrett tries to burn both himself and his former teacher to death, but Cogburn crawls out of the fire, injured, and survives. Back home, he mails a letter to his agent admitting that he was not the real author of The Infernal Machine and that he had stolen it.

The film was shot over five weeks in the Algarve in Portugal, at Moviebox Studios and around Loulé, and was financed by executive producer Jack Christian's company, Filmology Finance. It received mixed reviews, with 46% of the 13 critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes giving it a positive notice.

original_title: A Christmas Prince: The Royal Baby
overview: Christmas brings the ultimate gift to Aldovia: a royal baby. But first, Queen Amber must help her family and kingdom by finding a missing peace treaty.
tagline: Baby Makes 3
title: A Christmas Prince: The Royal Baby
plot:
A Christmas Prince: The Royal Baby is a 2019 American romantic comedy film directed by Mark Jean and written by David L. Cunningham.

The movie follows the story of Amber, an American journalist who goes undercover at a royal palace in Wales to cover a story about the prince's visit to the country. As she spends more time with Prince Henry, she finds herself falling for him, but their social differences make it difficult for them to be together.

The main themes of A Christmas Prince: The Royal Baby include:

1. Love conquers all: Despite the obstacles and differences between Amber and Prince Henry, they ultimately find a way to be together.
2. Self-discovery: Amber's journey is also one of self-discovery as she learns more about herself and what she wants in life.
3. Social class differences: The movie explores the challenges of navigating social class differences and how it can affect relationships.
4. Family values: Prince Henry's family plays an important role in the story, highlighting the importance of family values and loyalty.

The plot development is driven by Amber's undercover assignment, which leads to a series of comedic misunderstandings and romantic moments with Prince Henry. As the story unfolds, Amber must confront her feelings for the prince and decide whether she can balance her career ambitions with her growing love for him.

The ending is a classic fairy tale romance, with Amber and Prince Henry finding happiness together despite the odds against them. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, with the couple embracing their differences and looking forward to a future together.

Overall, A Christmas Prince: The Royal Baby is a lighthearted, feel-good romantic comedy that explores themes of love, self-discovery, and social class differences in a charming and entertaining way.

overview: Jaded ex-CIA operative John Creasy reluctantly accepts a job as the bodyguard for a 10-year-old girl in Mexico City. They clash at first, but eventually bond, and when she's kidnapped he's consumed by fury and will stop at nothing to save her life.
tagline: Creasy's art is death, and he is about to paint his masterpiece.
title: Man on Fire
plot:
Man on Fire is a 2004 action-drama film directed by Tony Scott, starring Denzel Washington as John Creasy, a former CIA operative turned private security contractor. The movie follows the story of a man who forms an unlikely bond with a young girl and must fight to protect her from those who seek to harm her.

The film begins with John Creasy (Denzel Washington), a retired CIA operative living in Mexico City with his adopted daughter, Lupita (Pita) Ramirez (Dakota Fanning). Creasy has been working as a private security contractor, providing protection services for wealthy clients. However, he is struggling to connect with Lupita, who is being neglected by her mother and is in need of care.

One day, Creasy's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Lupita's mother, Lucia (Pilar Lopez de Ayala), at a bar. He learns that she has abandoned Lupita, leaving her in the care of a corrupt police officer, Captain Silas (Giovanni Ribisi). Creasy is horrified by this situation and decides to take matters into his own hands.

As Creasy delves deeper into the world of organized crime, he discovers that Lucia's husband, Carlos (Raymond Cruz), is involved in human trafficking. He also learns that Lupita has been kidnapped by a group of Mexican gangsters who are being paid to sell her on the black market.

Creasy embarks on a perilous journey to rescue Lupita, facing numerous dangers and obstacles along the way. He encounters a corrupt police officer, Captain Silas, who is working with Carlos's gang, and must use his CIA training to evade capture and stay one step ahead of his enemies.

As Creasy navigates the treacherous underworld of Mexico City, he forms an unlikely bond with Lupita, who has been traumatized by her experiences. He teaches her how to fight and defend herself, and she begins to trust him as a protector and father figure.

The film's climax features an intense showdown between Creasy and Carlos's gang, which ends in tragedy for many of the characters. In the end, Creasy manages to rescue Lupita, but not before suffering severe injuries.

The movie concludes with Creasy reflecting on his experiences and the bond he has formed with Lupita. He realizes that he has found a new purpose in life, one that goes beyond his CIA training or private security work. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Creasy and Lupita reunited and beginning a new chapter in their lives.

Overall, Man on Fire is a gripping action-drama that explores themes of redemption, sacrifice, and the power of human connection. Denzel Washington's performance as John Creasy is particularly noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to a complex and emotionally charged character.

overview: Kronk, now chef and Head Delivery Boy of Mudka's Meat Hut, is fretting over the upcoming visit of his father. Kronk's father always disapproved of young Kronk's culinary interests and wished that Kronk instead would settle down with a wife and a large house on a hill.
tagline: The groove is on the move.
title: Kronk's New Groove
plot:
Kronk's New Groove is a 2005 animated comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie is a spin-off of the original Emperor's New Groove, and it follows the character Kronk as he tries to find his place in the world.

The story begins with Kronk (voiced by Patrick Warburton) living a peaceful life on a remote island, where he spends most of his days gardening and enjoying nature. However, his tranquility is disrupted when Yzma (voiced by Eartha Kitt), the former advisor to the Emperor, escapes from prison and sets out to take over the throne.

Yzma's plan involves using Kronk as her pawn in order to get to the Emperor, who has been placed under a sleeping curse. Kronk, unaware of his true identity and purpose, is recruited by Yzma to help her on her quest. Along the way, he meets a new character, Chicha (voiced by Wendie Malick), a beautiful and charming woman who becomes Kronk's love interest.

As Kronk navigates through the jungle with Yzma, they encounter various obstacles and challenges that test their relationship and trust in each other. Meanwhile, Kronk begins to experience strange flashbacks of his past life as an advisor to the Emperor, which hints at a deeper connection between him and the throne.

Throughout the movie, Kronk's innocence and good-hearted nature are constantly tested by Yzma's manipulations and schemes. Despite this, Kronk remains loyal to Yzma, believing that he is doing what is best for her and himself.

However, as the story unfolds, Kronk begins to realize that something is amiss with Yzma's intentions. He starts to question his loyalty and ultimately decides to betray Yzma in order to save the Emperor from her clutches.

In a thrilling finale, Kronk confronts Yzma and saves the Emperor from his sleeping curse. In the process, he also finds love with Chicha and discovers his true identity as an advisor to the Emperor. The movie ends with Kronk returning to his life on the island, where he is welcomed back by his friends and family.

Overall, Kronk's New Groove is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and love. With its colorful animation, witty humor, and lovable characters, it is a must-watch for fans of Disney and comedy alike.

belongs_to_collection.name: Transformers: Rise of the Beasts Collection

overview: A ‘90s globetrotting adventure that introduces the Maximals, Predacons, and Terrorcons to the existing battle on earth between Autobots and Decepticons.
tagline: Power is primal.
title: Transformers: Rise of the Beasts
plot:
Transformers: Rise of the Beasts is a 2023 science fiction action film directed by Steven Caple Jr. and produced by Paramount Pictures.

The movie takes place during World War II, specifically in 1944, on the island of Okinawa, Japan. The story follows Optimus Prime (voiced by Peter Cullen), Bumblebee (voiced by Dylan O'Brien), and their human allies, Air Raid (voiced by Ron Perlman) and Mairax (voiced by Ramin Djavadi), as they attempt to stop the evil Decepticon leader, Megatron (voiced by Tony Curran).

The plot centers around a group of Autobots who are sent to Okinawa to protect the island from the Decepticons. The Autobots soon discover that the Decepticons have formed an alliance with the Japanese military, led by the ruthless General Vortex (voiced by John DiMaggio). As the war rages on, Optimus Prime and his team must navigate the treacherous landscape of Okinawa to stop Megatron's plans.

One of the unique aspects of this film is its focus on the Transformers' interactions with other animals, such as the giant prehistoric creatures known as the "Beasts." These Beasts are ancient Transformers who have been awakened by the war and are now wreaking havoc on the island. The Autobots must form an uneasy alliance with these Beasts to defeat their common enemy.

Throughout the movie, there are also flashbacks that explore Optimus Prime's past and his connection to the Beasts. These scenes provide insight into the Transformers' history and their motivations for fighting in World War II.

Overall, Transformers: Rise of the Beasts is an action-packed adventure that explores a new chapter in the Transformers franchise. With its unique setting and blend of science fiction and historical drama, it offers something fresh for fans of the series.

original_title: Middle School: The Worst Years of My Life
overview: A quiet teenage artist Rafe Katchadorian has a wild imagination and is sick of middle school and the rules that have been put before him. Rafe and his best friend Leo have come up with a plan: break every rule in the school hand book and as you expect trouble follows.
tagline: Rules aren't for everyone.
title: Middle School: The Worst Years of My Life
plot:
Middle School: The Worst Years of My Life is a heartwarming and humorous film that explores the challenges and triumphs of adolescence. At its core, the movie delves into the universal struggles of navigating middle school, where self-discovery, friendships, and growing pains converge.

The film masterfully captures the complexities of pre-teen life, where social hierarchies, peer pressure, and emotional turmoil can be overwhelming. The protagonist, Leigh, is a relatable and endearing character whose journey serves as a microcosm for many young viewers. As she navigates the ups and downs of middle school, Leigh must confront her own insecurities, learn to assert herself, and develop a sense of self-worth.

One of the primary themes of Middle School: The Worst Years of My Life is the importance of empathy and understanding in building strong relationships with others. Through Leigh's experiences, the movie highlights the value of kindness, compassion, and acceptance in creating a supportive community. The film also explores the consequences of bullying, cyberbullying, and social exclusion, emphasizing the need for inclusivity and respect.

The movie also touches on themes of family, love, and support. Leigh's relationships with her parents, particularly her mother, serve as a source of comfort and guidance throughout her journey. The film showcases the importance of having a loving and understanding family environment, where children feel safe to explore their emotions and make mistakes without fear of judgment.

Ultimately, Middle School: The Worst Years of My Life is a poignant and entertaining film that celebrates the resilience and adaptability of young people navigating the challenges of middle school. With its lighthearted tone, engaging characters, and relatable themes, the movie offers a reassuring message about the power of friendship, self-acceptance, and growing up with empathy and kindness.

overview: Kindhearted Griffin Keyes is one of the best-loved caretakers at the Franklin Park Zoo, but since he is more comfortable with the animals than with females of his own species, his love life is lacking. When Griffin decides that the only way to get a girlfriend is to find a more-glamorous career, the animals panic. To keep him from leaving, they reveal their secret ability to talk and offer to teach him the rules of courtship, animal-style.
tagline: Welcome to his jungle.
title: Zookeeper
plot:
Zookeeper is a 2011 American comedy film directed by Frédéric Auburtin and Ross Katz, produced by Happy Madison Productions, Columbia Pictures, and Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. The movie stars Jack Black, Kevin James, Rosario Dawson, and Ken Jeong.

The main themes of Zookeeper can be summarized as follows:

1. Friendship: The film highlights the importance of friendship and camaraderie among animals in the zoo. The main character, Griffin Keyes (played by Jack Black), forms a bond with various animals, including a lion named Phil, a giraffe named Binky, and an elephant named Stella.
2. Self-discovery: Throughout the movie, Griffin struggles to find his place in the world after being fired from his job as a zookeeper. He eventually discovers his true calling as a zookeeper and finds happiness in helping others.
3. Love and relationships: The film explores Griffin's romantic relationship with a zoo visitor named Lily (played by Rosario Dawson). Their love story is an integral part of the movie, adding a heartwarming touch to the comedy.
4. Overcoming fears and insecurities: Phil, the lion, is initially portrayed as a fearsome predator, but as the story progresses, his softer side is revealed. Griffin's friendship with Phil helps him overcome his own fears and insecurities, teaching him valuable lessons about trust and loyalty.

The movie features a mix of humor, heartwarming moments, and exciting animal encounters, making it an entertaining watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: Beatrice Prior and Tobias Eaton venture into the world outside of the fence and are taken into protective custody by a mysterious agency known as the Bureau of Genetic Welfare.
tagline: Break the boundaries of your world
title: Allegiant
plot:
Allegiant is a 2016 American science fiction action film directed by Robert Schwentke and written by Simon Beaufoy and James Duff, based on Veronica Roth's novel of the same name. The movie serves as the sequel to Divergent (2014) and concludes the Allegiant trilogy.

The story begins with Tris Prior (Shailene Woodley), a skilled Dauntless initiate, who has been living in the self-sustaining city of Chicago with her friends and allies, including Four (Theo James). The city is designed to be a safe haven for those with special abilities, known as Divergents, who are feared and persecuted by the rest of society.

As Tris struggles to come to terms with her past and her feelings for Four, she begins to experience strange visions and nightmares that hint at a dark secret about the city's true nature. She soon discovers that Chicago is not an independent city, but rather a prison designed to keep Divergents captive and under control.

Tris and Four embark on a perilous journey to uncover the truth behind their confinement and the sinister forces that govern their world. Along the way, they meet new allies, including Christina (Zoe Kravitz), a skilled fighter from the Dauntless faction, and Max (Ansel Elgort), a charming and resourceful young man who becomes Tris's love interest.

As they delve deeper into the mystery, Tris and Four learn that the city was created by the Erudite faction, led by Jeanine Matthews (Kate Winslet), to harvest Divergent blood for their own sinister purposes. The Erudite plan to use this blood to create a new breed of super-soldiers, known as Abnegation-born, who will serve as the ruling class in a post-apocalyptic world.

Tris and Four's quest takes them to the surface, where they encounter a harsh and unforgiving environment that challenges their skills and their relationship. They also discover that Tris is not just any ordinary Divergent, but rather a key player in the Erudite's plans, as her blood holds the secret to creating the Abnegation-born.

As the stakes grow higher, Tris and Four must confront their enemies and make difficult choices about their future. In the end, they manage to escape the city and find a new sense of purpose and belonging among a group of rebels who are fighting against the Erudite's tyranny.

The movie concludes with Tris and Four standing together, ready to face the challenges of their new world and forge a brighter future for themselves and those around them. However, the ending also sets up a cliffhanger, as Tris is forced to make an impossible choice between her love for Four and her duty to protect others.

Overall, Allegiant is a thrilling and action-packed conclusion to the Allegiant trilogy, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the series will appreciate the movie's epic scope and emotional depth.

overview: Three friends making a web series about their town discover that their neighbors are being killed and replaced by creatures who are perfect copies of their victims.
tagline: The enemy is you
title: Assimilate
plot:
Assimilate is a psychological sci-fi thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The film's narrative revolves around a young woman, Sarah, who undergoes an experimental procedure to enhance her cognitive abilities, only to find herself trapped in a world where she must confront the darkest corners of her own psyche.

At its core, Assimilate explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and perceptions. As Sarah navigates this alternate reality, she begins to question what is real and what is just a product of her own mind. This existential crisis serves as a catalyst for her journey, forcing her to confront the darkest aspects of herself and the true nature of her existence.

The film also touches on the theme of control and manipulation, highlighting how those in power often use their influence to shape and mold individuals to suit their own agendas. Sarah's situation is a prime example of this, as she finds herself trapped in a world where she is forced to conform to the desires of others, stripping her of any sense of autonomy or agency.

Furthermore, Assimilate explores the idea of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Sarah's experiences are marked by a deep-seated sense of pain and vulnerability, which serves as a driving force behind her actions throughout the film. The movie suggests that trauma can be both a source of strength and a crippling burden, leaving individuals to navigate the complexities of their own emotional landscapes.

Ultimately, Assimilate is a thought-provoking thriller that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the fragility of our perceptions.

overview: When most of the population of Earth is infected by a virus and transformed into flesh eaters and blood drinking creatures, a group of hunters lead by Tao and his sword chase the vampire zombies to eliminate them. Six non-infected survivors try to find the exit of an abandoned hospital crowded of the infected creatures. Meanwhile, the military is ready to bomb the whole area.
tagline: He lives by the sword. They will die by it.
title: Against the Dark
plot:
Against the Dark is a 2009 American action thriller film directed by John Hlattin. The movie follows a former Special Forces operative who must rescue his kidnapped daughter from a group of mercenaries in Eastern Europe.

The main theme of Against the Dark revolves around the struggle for survival and redemption. The protagonist, a rugged and skilled ex-Special Forces operative, is driven by his desire to protect his family and make amends for past mistakes. As he navigates the treacherous landscape of Eastern Europe, he must confront his own demons and face off against ruthless adversaries.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as the protagonist's determination to rescue his daughter puts him at odds with the mercenaries who are holding her captive. The movie takes a dark and gritty tone, exploring themes of violence, loyalty, and sacrifice.

One of the most striking aspects of Against the Dark is its portrayal of the human cost of war and violence. The film does not shy away from depicting the brutal realities of conflict, highlighting the devastating impact on civilians caught in the crossfire. This theme is particularly evident in the protagonist's relationship with his daughter, whose innocence and vulnerability serve as a stark contrast to the harsh world he finds himself in.

Ultimately, Against the Dark is a tense and gripping thriller that explores the complexities of human nature and the lengths people will go to protect those they love.

overview: As the home planet of the Green Lantern Corps faces a battle with an ancient enemy, Hal Jordan prepares new recruit Arisia for the coming conflict by relating stories of the first Green Lantern and several of Hal's comrades.
tagline: Witness the Color of Will.
title: Green Lantern: Emerald Knights
plot:
Green Lantern: Emerald Knights is a 2011 animated film that serves as a companion piece to the 2011 live-action film Green Lantern, directed by Martin Campbell. The movie takes place during the events of the original film and explores the history of the Green Lantern Corps through a series of vignettes.

The story begins with Hal Jordan (voiced by Jason O'Mara), who is struggling to come to terms with his failure as a test pilot and his subsequent recruitment into the Green Lantern Corps. He is visited by the Guardians of the Universe, who inform him that he has been chosen to be the new Green Lantern.

However, things take a turn when Hal discovers that the Guardians are planning to destroy the planet Oa, which serves as their homeworld, in order to prevent it from falling into the wrong hands. The Guardians believe that this is necessary to protect the universe from the evil Sinestro, who seeks to use the power of the yellow ring to conquer the cosmos.

As Hal tries to convince the Guardians to reconsider their decision, he is joined by other Green Lanterns, including John Stewart (voiced by Kevin Tanaka), Carol Ferris (voiced by Kyra Sedgwick), and Tom Kalmaku (voiced by Michael Dorn). Together, they embark on a series of adventures that take them across the galaxy.

One of these adventures takes Hal to the planet Poltarax, where he encounters the Green Lantern who was killed in action during the events of the original film. The Lantern's spirit is revealed to be that of Abin Sur (voiced by Nolan North), who had been a member of the Corps before his death.

Through a series of flashbacks, we learn about Abin's backstory and his struggles with the power of the ring. We also see how he came to be killed by Sinestro, who was seeking revenge against the Corps for their interference in his plans.

As Hal continues on his journey, he is joined by other Lanterns, including Laira (voiced by Mae Whitman) and Sojourner (voiced by Jennifer Hale). Together, they face off against Sinestro and his army of yellow-clad warriors.

The final battle takes place on the planet Oa, where Hal and the Guardians engage in a fierce struggle to prevent the destruction of their homeworld. In the end, it is revealed that the Guardians' plan was not entirely altruistic - they had been using the power of the ring to maintain control over the Corps for centuries.

The film ends with Hal coming to terms with his new role as a Green Lantern and his responsibilities to the Corps. He also begins to understand the true nature of the ring and its power, which he will continue to explore in future adventures.

Overall, Green Lantern: Emerald Knights is a visually stunning and action-packed film that explores the history and mythology of the Green Lantern Corps. While it may not be as well-known as some other DC Comics properties, it offers a unique perspective on the universe and its characters, and provides a compelling companion piece to the original live-action film.

overview: Ong Bak 3 picks up where Ong Bak 2 had left off. Tien is captured and almost beaten to death before he is saved and brought back to the Kana Khone villagers. There he is taught meditation and how to deal with his Karma, but very soon his arch rival returns challenging Tien for a final duel.
tagline: The biggest fight of all is with himself.
title: Ong Bak 3
plot:
Ong Bak 3 is a 2010 Thai martial arts film directed by Prachya Pinkaew and produced by Sahamongkolfilm, which is a subsidiary of Sahapath Pictures. The main themes of Ong Bak 3 include:

1. **Redemption**: The protagonist, Tien (played by Tony Jaa), seeks redemption for his past mistakes and the death of his brother, Khun Borom. Throughout the film, he faces various challenges that test his skills and character.
2. **Loyalty and Family**: Tien's loyalty to his family and friends is a recurring theme throughout the film. He goes to great lengths to protect those he cares about and prove himself as a worthy successor to his father's legacy.
3. **Self-Discovery**: As Tien navigates the challenges of his journey, he also undergoes a process of self-discovery. He learns more about his family's history, his own strengths and weaknesses, and the true meaning of honor and loyalty.
4. **Martial Arts and Philosophy**: The film explores the philosophical aspects of martial arts, particularly the concept of " Muay Boran" (the ancient art of Muay Thai). Tien's skills are not just physical but also spiritual, as he seeks to understand the deeper meaning behind his movements.

The plot of Ong Bak 3 follows Tien as he faces a series of challenges and battles against various enemies, including the ruthless General Khun Borom (played by Dan Chupong) and his loyal followers. Along the way, Tien discovers more about his family's past and the secrets behind his father's death.

Overall, Ong Bak 3 is an action-packed film that explores themes of redemption, loyalty, self-discovery, and martial arts philosophy, set against a richly detailed backdrop of Thai culture and history.

overview: When Maggie's sister Jenna saddles her with an autistic newborn named Cody she touches Maggie's heart and becomes the daughter she has always longed for. But six years later Jenna suddenly re-enters her life and, with her mysterious new husband, Eric Stark, abducts Cody. Despite the fact that Maggie has no legal rights to Cody, FBI agent John Travis takes up her cause when he realizes that Cody shares the same birth date as several other recently murdered children.
production_companies: Munich Film Partners & Company (MFP) BTC Productions
tagline: Mankind's last hope just turned six.
title: Bless the Child
plot:
Bless the Child is a supernatural thriller film that revolves around the story of a young girl who is accused of being involved in a series of mysterious events and murders. The movie explores the theme of demonic possession, which serves as the central plot device.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the main character, Angela Vidal, is not what she seems to be. She is actually possessed by a malevolent entity that is manipulating her actions. This possession serves as a metaphor for the darker aspects of human nature and the struggle between good and evil.

The film also touches on the theme of trauma and its effects on individuals, particularly children. Angela's past experiences have left her with emotional scars, which are exploited by the demonic entity to further its own agenda. The movie suggests that unresolved trauma can create vulnerabilities that can be exploited by malevolent forces.

Furthermore, Bless the Child explores the idea of faith and spirituality as a means of coping with adversity. The main character's Catholic upbringing and her priest's attempts to help her serve as a source of comfort and strength in the face of supernatural terror.

Overall, the movie presents a gripping narrative that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, trauma, and the struggle between good and evil.

overview: After a plane crash, a young therapist, Claire, is assigned by her mentor to counsel the flight's five survivors. When they share their recollections of the incident -- which some say include an explosion that the airline claims never happened -- Claire is intrigued by Eric, the most secretive of the passengers.
tagline: The line between this world and the next is about to be crossed
title: Passengers
plot:
Passengers is a 2008 romantic mystery thriller directed by Rodrigo García from a screenplay by Ronnie Christensen, starring Anne Hathaway and Patrick Wilson. TriStar Pictures released it in 125 North American theaters on October 24, 2008.

Psychotherapist Claire Summers is assigned to counsel five survivors of a plane crash: passengers Dean, Norman, Shannon and Eric, and flight attendant Janice. Eric is oddly euphoric and insists on private sessions, and he unnerves Claire by seeming to know personal details about her, including her strained relationship with her sister, Emma. The survivors' memories conflict, with Dean recalling an explosion that the others deny, while airline official Mr. Arkin insists the crash was due to pilot error. As patients begin missing sessions and a stranger appears to be following them, Norman suspects the airline is silencing witnesses to hide mechanical negligence and now claims to remember an engine exploding. Arkin warns Claire off the theory, and her supervisor, Perry, doubts her fears.

Encouraged by her kindly neighbor Toni, Claire gives in to her growing feelings for Eric and sleeps with him, while trying in vain to reach Emma. She tracks down Norman's stalker, another survivor who remembers an explosion, but he vanishes while she is confronting Arkin. Eric relives the engine blowing apart at the crash site and later recognizes a barking dog as a childhood pet that died. Realizing he is dead, he steps in front of a train, which passes harmlessly through him. Shannon, who earlier glimpsed her long-dead parents, leaves with a man and a woman. At Emma's house, Arkin leaves behind a briefcase containing a list of the crash's victims, with Claire's own name among them and Arkin listed as the pilot. Eric explains that every passenger had to discover the truth for themselves, guided by dead loved ones such as Toni and Perry, Claire's late aunt and teacher. Together they sail out of the harbor into the afterlife, and a flashback shows them meeting on the doomed flight. Later, Emma finds a note Claire had meant to send her.

The cast includes Clea DuVall as Shannon, Andre Braugher as Perry, David Morse as Arkin and Dianne Wiest as Toni. Reviews were generally negative, with 19% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 40, though some critics, including Manohla Dargis of The New York Times, praised the leads while noting an uneven script and direction. It grossed about $5.8 million, almost entirely overseas.

overview: Commercial airline pilot Whip Whitaker has a problem with drugs and alcohol, though so far he's managed to complete his flights safely. His luck runs out when a disastrous mechanical malfunction sends his plane hurtling toward the ground. Whip pulls off a miraculous crash-landing that results in only six lives lost. Shaken to the core, Whip vows to get sober -- but when the crash investigation exposes his addiction, he finds himself in an even worse situation.
title: Flight
plot:
Flight is a 2012 American drama film directed by Robert Zemeckis, starring Denzel Washington as Whip Whitaker, a commercial airline pilot.

The movie begins with Whip Whitaker (Denzel Washington) flying for Southern Air, a regional airline. Whip is a skilled and experienced pilot, but he has a troubled past. He was involved in a plane crash that killed everyone on board, except himself, when he was just 19 years old. The incident left him with severe anxiety and PTSD.

The story then jumps to the present day, where Whip is now flying for Southern Air again. He's still struggling with his demons, but has managed to keep them under control. However, during a flight from Atlanta to Charlotte, Whip becomes disoriented due to a combination of factors, including his medication, fatigue, and stress.

As the plane hits turbulence, Whip becomes increasingly agitated, and eventually loses consciousness. The plane crashes in a field, killing everyone on board except for one passenger, a young girl named Hyde (Nico Parker). The incident is ruled as an accident, but Whip's colleagues are suspicious of his involvement.

Whip is forced to take a leave of absence from flying due to the incident, and he becomes a recluse. He starts attending AA meetings and begins to rebuild his life. However, he struggles with feelings of guilt and shame over the crash, which affects his relationships with those around him, including his girlfriend, Nicole (Donna Freeman).

As Whip tries to come to terms with what happened, he meets a young girl named Hyde who was on board the plane. Despite the trauma she experienced, Hyde is determined to help others and make a difference in the world. Whip becomes a mentor to her, and through their interactions, he begins to confront his past and find redemption.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Whip's colleagues start investigating him for possible involvement in the crash. Whip's reputation is tarnished, and he faces pressure from the airline and the authorities. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Whip had been taking sedatives before the flight, which contributed to his loss of control.

In the end, Whip comes clean about what happened and takes responsibility for his actions. He also finds a way to make amends with those around him, including Hyde and Nicole. The movie ends on a hopeful note, as Whip begins to rebuild his life and find redemption through his relationship with Hyde.

Throughout the movie, Denzel Washington delivers a powerful performance as Whip Whitaker, bringing depth and nuance to the character. His portrayal of a complex and flawed individual is both heartbreaking and inspiring, making Flight a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film.

original_title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
overview: Returning for his fifth year of study at Hogwarts, Harry is stunned to find that his warnings about the return of Lord Voldemort have been ignored. Left with no choice, Harry takes matters into his own hands, training a small group of students to defend themselves against the dark arts.
tagline: Evil Must Be Confronted.
title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
plot:
Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix is a fantasy film directed by David Yates, based on the novel of the same name by J.K. Rowling. The movie was produced by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The story begins with Harry Potter (Daniel Radcliffe) returning to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry for his fifth year. However, he soon discovers that the wizarding world has denied the return of Lord Voldemort (Ralph Fiennes), the dark lord who murdered Harry's parents. The Ministry of Magic is interfering with Hogwarts, trying to control the curriculum and suppress the idea of Voldemort's return.

Harry forms a secret group called Dumbledore's Army (DA) to teach his fellow students defensive magic against the Dark Arts. Meanwhile, the new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher, Dolores Umbridge (Imelda Staunton), is appointed by the Ministry to replace the previous teacher, Gilderoy Lockhart (Kenneth Branagh). Umbridge is a sadistic and incompetent teacher who makes learning difficult for her students.

As the year progresses, Harry becomes increasingly frustrated with the Ministry's interference and the lack of support from the wizarding community. He also struggles with his own emotions, feeling isolated and angry. The Order of the Phoenix, a group of wizards and witches dedicated to fighting against Voldemort, is formed in secret to counter the Dark Lord's followers.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Sirius Black (Gary Oldman), Harry's godfather, is killed by Bellatrix Lestrange (Helena Bonham Carter) during a battle at the Ministry. This event sets off a chain reaction of events that ultimately leads to the Battle of the Department of Mysteries.

Throughout the movie, Harry's relationships with his friends Ron Weasley (Rupert Grint) and Hermione Granger (Emma Watson) are also explored. The trio faces numerous challenges as they navigate their personal struggles and work together to uncover the truth about Voldemort's return.

The film features stunning visual effects, impressive action sequences, and a gripping storyline that sets the stage for the next installment in the series. Overall, Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix is an exciting and emotional ride that showcases the characters' growth and development as they face the challenges of adolescence and the wizarding world.

overview: After a former elite agent rescues a 12-year-old Chinese girl who's been abducted, they find themselves in the middle of a standoff between Triads, the Russian Mafia and high-level corrupt New York City politicians and police.
tagline: She has the code. He is the key.
title: Safe
plot:
Safe is a 2012 American action thriller written and directed by Boaz Yakin. Jason Statham stars as Luke Wright, an ex-cop and former cage fighter who ends up protecting a gifted child hunted by the Russian mafia, Chinese triads and corrupt New York police, with Chris Sarandon, Robert John Burke and James Hong in supporting roles.

After Luke accidentally wins a fixed fight, Russian mob boss Emile Docheski has his son Vassily and his men murder Luke's pregnant wife and vows to kill anyone Luke grows close to, leaving him homeless and adrift. In China, the young math prodigy Mei is abducted by triad boss Han Jiao, who uses her as a human calculator so his operation leaves no digital trail, and is sent to New York under the watch of the brutal Quan Chang. A year later Han has her memorize a long number, but the Russians ambush them and seize her, only to be attacked in turn by police working for the corrupt Captain Wolf, who is in Han's pay. Mei escapes into a subway station where Luke is contemplating suicide; recognizing one of his wife's killers among her pursuers, Luke kills the Russians, saves her from two crooked detectives and flees with her. In a hotel she explains the number, which Luke guesses is a safe combination, but Quan tracks her through her phone and recaptures her.

The mayor, Danny Tremello, warns Wolf that Luke was really a government assassin lent to the city after 9/11 alongside his former partner, Alex Rosen, to eliminate crime bosses, until Luke quit after exposing Wolf's corrupt squad. Luke kidnaps Vassily and forces Emile to reveal that the number opens a guarded Chinatown safe holding $30 million. He recruits Wolf's detectives with the promise of money, fights through the triads to the safe, then kills the detectives when Wolf betrays him. He bribes Alex, now the mayor's aide, to rescue Mei, and learns that a second safe holds the mayor's disc of evidence against every crime syndicate in the city. After Alex kills Quan to take Mei, Luke obtains a copy of the disc, and Mei wounds Alex during a standoff, letting Luke finish him. Luke returns Vassily through Wolf, pays Han for Mei's freedom, hides copies of the disc as insurance and heads to Seattle so Mei can attend a school for gifted children.

Shot in Philadelphia and New York on a $30 million budget, Safe was released by Lionsgate on April 27, 2012, and grossed $40.6 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with 59% on Rotten Tomatoes and 55 on Metacritic.

overview: Folklore collectors and con artists, Jake and Will Grimm, travel from village to village pretending to protect townsfolk from enchanted creatures and performing exorcisms. However, they are put to the test  when they encounter a real magical curse in a haunted forest with real magical beings, requiring genuine courage.
tagline: Eliminating Evil Since 1812.
title: The Brothers Grimm
plot:
The Brothers Grimm is a 2005 fantasy adventure film directed by Terry Gilliam that reimagines the famous folklorists as travelling con artists in Napoleonic French-occupied Germany, who encounter a genuine fairy-tale curse requiring real courage rather than their usual fake exorcisms. Matt Damon, Heath Ledger and Lena Headey star, with Peter Stormare, Jonathan Pryce and Monica Bellucci in supporting roles. A British-Czech co-production shot in the Czech Republic, it was written by Ehren Kruger.

In 1811, Will and Jake Grimm and their assistants Hidlick and Bunst use Jake's deep knowledge of folklore to persuade villagers that they can banish the supernatural. Captured by the Italian torturer Mercurio Cavaldi and brought before the French general Delatombe, they are offered amnesty if they investigate the disappearance of young girls from the village of Marbaden. With the help of Angelika, a fur trapper whose younger sisters were the first to vanish, they learn of a tower in the nearby forest built centuries earlier by a vain Thuringian queen trying to escape the plague. That night an enchanted horse swallows a girl and carries her into the forest. Back in the forest, Jake climbs the tower, ringed by twelve crypts, and finds the ancient, decaying Queen, kept alive by a magic mirror that shows her youthful reflection. When a mud creature takes another girl, Sasha, a wolf-like huntsman places her in a crypt. The brothers rescue her and take the huntsman's axe, and Jake concludes that the girls are part of a ritual timed to a lunar eclipse to restore the Queen's youth. Delatombe executes Hidlick and Bunst, denounces the brothers as frauds and orders the forest burned with them inside, but Angelika frees them and recognizes the axe as her father's, revealing that the huntsman is her father under the Queen's spell. Angelika then becomes the twelfth and final victim. The Queen's wind puts out the fire, Will kills Delatombe, and when the Queen bewitches Will, Jake smashes the mirror; Angelika's father leaps from the tower with the rest of it, destroying the Queen. Jake revives Angelika with a kiss, the girls return home, and a raven flies off with a shard of the mirror.

Delayed for months by disputes between Gilliam and the Weinsteins, the film was released on 26 August 2005 and competed at the Venice Film Festival. It received mixed reviews, with a 38% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and grossed $105.3 million worldwide.

overview: In post-Sept. 11 Los Angeles, tensions erupt when the lives of a Brentwood housewife, her district attorney husband, a Persian shopkeeper, two cops, a pair of carjackers and a Korean couple converge during a 36-hour period.
tagline: You think you know who you are. You have no idea.
title: Crash
plot:
Crash is a 2004 American drama film directed by Paul Haggis, not Lionsgate (although it was distributed by Warner Bros.). The movie won several Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Original Screenplay.

The main themes of Crash include:

1. Racial tensions and stereotypes: The film explores the complexities of racial relationships in Los Angeles, highlighting the prejudices and biases that exist among different communities.
2. Identity and cultural differences: The characters' experiences and perspectives are shaped by their cultural backgrounds, leading to misunderstandings and conflicts.
3. Morality and personal responsibility: As the story unfolds, the characters' actions have unintended consequences, forcing them to confront their own moral compasses and take responsibility for their choices.
4. Social hierarchy and class divisions: The film critiques the social stratification in Los Angeles, where wealth and status are often used as a means of distinguishing oneself from others.

The plot revolves around a series of interconnected storylines that explore these themes through the characters' experiences with racism, prejudice, and personal growth.

original_title: Scooby-Doo! Curse of the Lake Monster
overview: Scooby-Doo and the gang are on the case when a mysterious lake monster starts scaring the guests at a summer resort in Erie Point, where Fred, Daphne, Velma and Shaggy have taken on seasonal jobs to pay for a barn they accidentally burned down. But in addition to sneaking suspicions, there's some romance in the air.
tagline: Ruh-Roh! They're in too deep and way over their heads!
title: Scooby-Doo! Curse of the Lake Monster
plot:
Scooby-Doo! Curse of the Lake Monster is an American made-for-television comedy horror mystery film of 2010 directed by Brian Levant for Cartoon Network, a sequel to Scooby-Doo! The Mystery Begins (2009). Robbie Amell (Fred), Hayley Kiyoko (Velma), Kate Melton (Daphne), Nick Palatas (Shaggy) and Frank Welker, the voice of Scooby-Doo, return, joined by Ted McGinley as Thorny Blake, Richard Moll as the lighthouse keeper Elmer Uggins, Marion Ross as Hilda Trowburg and Beverly Sanders as the witch Wanda Grubwort.

At the start of summer the friends go to work at the country club run by Daphne's uncle Thornton "Thorny" Blake V in Erie Point, to pay off damages from an earlier case. When a giant frog monster attacks the club's opening party, they question Uggins, the only person who has photographed it. He tells them a legend: when settlers first arrived, a witch named Wanda Grubwort ordered them to leave, and when they refused she used her moonstone-powered staff to turn a frog into a monster that attacked them, before she was burned at the stake. Velma finds security footage of the creature meeting a hooded figure on the beach, but spills green tea on the computer and destroys it.

Fred and Daphne are quarrelling, and Shaggy's crush on Velma is driving a wedge between him and Scooby. Velma is found unconscious on the beach with warts on her hand, which she shrugs off, and when Shaggy takes her on a date she panics at the sight of a match. Checking out a boat, Fred and Daphne are locked by the monster in a flooding room but escape. At the home of Wanda's descendant Hilda Trowburg they spot the hooded figure and discover it is Velma, who denies being herself and knocks them out. Trowburg explains that Wanda's spirit has possessed Velma, and the friends realize their squabbling made them miss the signs: the warts, the fear of fire, the fascination with moonstones and the spilled tea. In the underwater caves, Velma turns three frogs into monsters, but Shaggy reaches her by singing her favorite song, and she breaks free. When Wanda tries to recover her staff, Scooby smashes it, destroying the witch and turning the monsters back into frogs. Shaggy and Velma kiss but agree they are better as friends, and Shaggy makes up with Scooby. Thorny thanks them for saving his club and offers them a lawyer, and Daphne names the group Mystery Inc.

The film was shot in Santa Clarita and at Sherwood Country Club in Thousand Oaks, California, and premiered in October 2010.

overview: A teenage loner pushes his way into the underworld of a high school crime ring to investigate the disappearance of his ex-girlfriend.
tagline: A detective story.
title: Brick
plot:
Brick is a 2006 neo-noir mystery film that delves into the complexities of adolescent angst, identity, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

The movie follows Brendan Frye, a high school student who becomes embroiled in a murder investigation, navigating a complex web of relationships, rivalries, and unrequited love. As he digs deeper into the mystery, Brendan's perceptions of himself and those around him become increasingly distorted, leading to a thrilling and introspective exploration of his own psyche.

At its core, Brick is a film about the fragility of adolescence, where the lines between truth and fiction are constantly shifting. The movie's protagonist, Brendan, is a quintessential teenager struggling to find his place in the world, grappling with feelings of alienation, insecurity, and desire. His investigation into the murder serves as a metaphor for his own journey of self-discovery, as he grapples with the complexities of relationships, loyalty, and the search for meaning.

Through Brendan's character, the film explores themes of toxic masculinity, social hierarchy, and the performative nature of identity. The movie's use of cinematic tropes, such as the "whodunit" mystery, serves to underscore the fragility of reality in adolescence, where the stakes are high and the consequences of failure can be devastating.

Ultimately, Brick is a thought-provoking and haunting film that captures the essence of adolescent angst, exploring the complexities of identity, relationships, and the search for meaning in a world that often seems overwhelming and unforgiving.

overview: A hardcore US racist skinhead who, because of his intelligence, leads a gang dedicated to fighting the enemy: the supposed American-Jewish conspiracy for domination. However, he's hiding a secret: he's Jewish-born, a brilliant scholar whose questioning of the tenets of his faith has left him angry and confused, turning against those who he thinks have a tragic history of their own making.
tagline: He's a jew. He’s a Neo-Nazi. With one true enemy… Himself!
title: The Believer
plot:
The Believer is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of identity, morality, and redemption. At its core, the film explores the transformative journey of Ronnie Silverman, a Jewish-American man who discovers he was raised as an Orthodox Jew but has been living a life of violence and hatred towards Jews.

As Ronnie navigates his newfound faith and grapples with his past actions, the movie delves into themes of identity crisis and the struggle to reconcile one's true self with their perceived persona. The film raises questions about the nature of morality and whether it can be redeemed or if it is an inherent part of who we are.

The Believer also touches on the idea of found family and community, as Ronnie seeks acceptance and belonging within his newfound faith. This theme is intertwined with the exploration of violence and its consequences, highlighting the devastating impact it has on individuals and communities.

Ultimately, The Believer presents a nuanced portrayal of redemption and personal growth, suggesting that it is never too late to change one's path and seek forgiveness. Through Ronnie's journey, the film invites viewers to reflect on their own values and moral compass, encouraging them to consider the complexities of human nature and the power of transformation.

original_title: Spy Kids: All the Time in the World
overview: Eight years after the third film, the OSS has become the world's top spy agency, while the Spy Kids department has since become defunct. A retired spy Marissa is thrown back into the action along with her stepchildren when a maniacal Timekeeper attempts to take over the world. In order to save the world, Rebecca and Cecil must team up with their hated stepmother. Carmen and Juni have since also grown up and will provide gadgets to them.
title: Spy Kids: All the Time in the World
plot:
Spy Kids: All the Time in the World is a 2011 American spy action comedy written and directed by Robert Rodriguez, the fourth entry in the Spy Kids series. Released in "4D", it came with "Aroma-scope" scratch-and-sniff cards that let audiences smell scents from the screen. Jessica Alba, Joel McHale, Rowan Blanchard, Mason Cook, Ricky Gervais and Jeremy Piven join Alexa Vega and Daryl Sabara, who return from the first three films. It premiered at L.A. Live in Los Angeles on July 31, 2011, and Dimension Films released it in the United States on August 19.

Nine months pregnant and already in labor, OSS agent Marissa Wilson defies her boss, Danger D'Amo, to capture the criminal Tick Tock and recover data on a dangerous weapon called Project Armageddon. She then retires to family life with her husband, Wilbur, host of a spy-hunting television show, their new daughter and her stepchildren, twins Rebecca and Cecil, though Rebecca still resents her as a replacement for her late mother. When a villain called the Time Keeper begins speeding up time to punish a world that wastes it, Marissa is called back into service. His target is the Chronos Sapphire, the jewel in a necklace Marissa gave Rebecca. After henchmen raid the house, the twins learn the truth about their stepmother and discover that the family dog, Argonaut, is a talking robot. At OSS headquarters their step-cousin Carmen Cortez lets them pick gadgets from the defunct Spy Kids division, and their search leads them to Tick Tock's lair in a clock shop, where they learn of the Wells Experiment, a time-travel project that once froze a boy in time.

Wilbur, meanwhile, unknowingly films his family in battle and loses his job after destroying the footage. As Carmen's estranged brother, Juni, joins the case, the twins notice that Danger's name is an anagram of "Armageddon". He is the Time Keeper, the frozen boy grown up, desperate to go back and spend more time with his father, while Tick Tock and his henchmen are alternate versions of himself. Rebecca urges him to value the time he has, and after a trip through the vortex returns him an old man, he shuts the device down. The family reconciles, and Carmen and Juni relaunch the Spy Kids program.

Piven plays Danger and Gervais voices Argonaut. Reviews were largely negative, with 23% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a consensus that the franchise had run its course. It grossed about $85 million worldwide on a $27 million budget, the lowest total in the series.

overview: On Halloween, a group of friends encounter an "extreme" haunted house that promises to feed on their darkest fears. The night turns deadly as they come to the horrifying realization that some nightmares are real.
tagline: Some Monsters Are Real.
title: Haunt
plot:
Haunt is a 2019 American slasher film written and directed by Scott Beck and Bryan Woods and produced by Eli Roth, Todd Garner, Mark Fasano, Ankur Rungta and Vishal Rungta. Katie Stevens, Will Brittain, Lauryn McClain, Andrew Caldwell and Shazi Raja joined the cast in October 2017, and principal photography took place that autumn in Covington, Kentucky. The film premiered at the Popcorn Frights Film Festival in Fort Lauderdale on August 8, 2019, screened at FrightFest in London, and received a limited US release from Momentum Pictures on September 13, 2019.

On Halloween night in Carbondale, Illinois, Harper, who is trapped in an abusive relationship, goes to a party with friends Bailey, Angela and Mallory, where they meet college students Evan and Nathan. The group heads to a haunted house attraction, where a performer dressed as a clown makes them sign liability waivers and lock away their phones. Inside, a witch-masked woman burns a screaming girl's face with a poker; when the group splits up, Bailey is slashed by a razor and Mallory is killed by the witch. A man in a ghost mask who poses as a helpful employee traps Nathan, and the costumed killers pick the group off one by one: a devil kills Angela, and the ghost removes his mask to reveal a heavily modified face before killing Evan.

Harper takes refuge in an escape room resembling a child's bedroom, which brings back memories of hiding from her abusive father. She finds a key, stabs the devil in the eye and uses the room's timed shotgun trap to kill him, but in the confusion fatally stabs a gagged Bailey, disguised in a skull mask. Harper's boyfriend, Sam, summoned by Nathan's text, is killed on arrival. Harper and Nathan fight back, and a vampire-masked performer, whose face is unaltered, explains that the performers belong to an extreme body modification group that builds attractions in order to kill people. The pair escape in Sam's truck as the clown burns the house down. Realizing the waivers listed their home addresses, Harper prepares, and when the clown later turns up at her mother's house, she traps and shoots him.

Stevens plays Harper, with Brittain as Nathan, McClain as Bailey, Caldwell as Evan and Raja as Angela. Critics were broadly positive, with 71% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 69, though some noted its debt to familiar influences. It grossed $2.4 million worldwide and later became Shudder's most-watched film premiere of 2019.

overview: Michael Jennings is a genius who's hired – and paid handsomely – by high-tech firms to work on highly sensitive projects, after which his short-term memory is erased so he's incapable of breaching security. But at the end of a three-year job, he's told he isn't getting a paycheck and instead receives a mysterious envelope. In it are clues he must piece together to find out why he wasn't paid – and why he's now in hot water.
production_companies: Province of British Columbia Film Incentive BC
tagline: Remember the future.
title: Paycheck
plot:
Paycheck is a 2003 science fiction thriller film directed by John Woo, starring Ben Affleck, Uma Thurman, and Paul Giamatti.

The main themes of Paycheck revolve around identity, free will, and the consequences of playing with time. The movie follows Michael Jennings (played by Ben Affleck), an insurance claims adjuster who discovers that he has a unique ability to recall every detail of his life from the moment he was born until the day before he died.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Michael's memories are not just random recollections but are actually fragments of a complex web of time travel. He is sent back in time repeatedly, each time with a new mission or task to complete, and his memories are altered accordingly.

The film explores several themes:

1. **Identity**: As Michael's memories change, he struggles to maintain a sense of self. His identity becomes fragmented, and he must navigate the consequences of living multiple lives.
2. **Free will vs. determinism**: The movie raises questions about whether our choices are truly free or if they are predetermined by external forces. Michael's experiences suggest that his actions may be influenced by factors beyond his control.
3. **Consequences of playing with time**: As Michael travels through time, he creates new timelines and alters the course of events. This leads to a complex web of consequences, which ultimately threaten the fabric of reality.

Throughout the film, Woo expertly weaves together these themes, creating a thought-provoking narrative that challenges the audience to consider the implications of manipulating time.

Overall, Paycheck is a gripping sci-fi thriller that explores the complexities of identity, free will, and the consequences of playing with time.

overview: A woman, married and with a child but becoming increasingly distant from her husband who is already cheating on her, reluctantly enters a secret relationship with her neighbor, a teenage boy.
tagline: A good wife, a cheating husband, a very sexy family drama...
title: A Good Lawyer's Wife
plot:
A Good Lawyer's Wife is a 2003 South Korean drama film directed by Park Chan-wook. The movie revolves around the story of Cha Soo-hyun, a young and ambitious lawyer who marries into a wealthy family, only to discover that her husband's family is hiding dark secrets.

The main themes of A Good Lawyer's Wife include:

1. **Deception and Appearance vs Reality**: The film explores how people present themselves to the world, often hiding their true intentions and motivations behind a mask of respectability. Cha Soo-hyun must navigate this complex web of deception as she tries to uncover the truth about her husband's family.
2. **Class struggle and social inequality**: The movie highlights the stark contrast between the wealthy elite and the working class, with Cha Soo-hyun representing the latter. As she becomes embroiled in her husband's family's secrets, she must confront the harsh realities of their privileged lifestyle.
3. **Marital infidelity and relationships**: A Good Lawyer's Wife examines the complexities of marriage and relationships, particularly when one partner is hiding a dark secret from the other. The film raises questions about loyalty, trust, and the consequences of infidelity.
4. **Identity and self-discovery**: Throughout the movie, Cha Soo-hyun undergoes a transformation as she sheds her old identity and forges a new one. This theme speaks to the human desire for self-discovery and growth.

The film's narrative is driven by its intricate plot, which keeps viewers engaged until the very end. With its thought-provoking themes and complex characters, A Good Lawyer's Wife has become a cult classic in South Korean cinema.

overview: Sensitive study of a headstrong high school football star who dreams of getting out of his small Western Pennsylvania steel town with a football scholarship. His equally ambitious coach aims at a college position, resulting in a clash which could crush the player's dreams.
tagline: He has everything at stake. He can't afford to lose. He's got to make all the right moves.
title: All the Right Moves
plot:
All the Right Moves is a coming-of-age sports drama film that explores the complexities of adolescence and the struggles of growing up. The movie delves into the theme of identity, as the protagonist, Steve Myers, navigates his way through high school and grapples with his own sense of self-worth.

The film also touches on the idea of social hierarchy and cliques, highlighting the difficulties of fitting in and finding one's place within a group. The character of Steve, who is an outsider among his peers, must confront the challenges of being different and learning to accept himself for who he is.

Furthermore, All the Right Moves examines the theme of masculinity and the pressure to conform to traditional masculine norms. Steve's relationships with other characters, particularly his friend and rival, Tony D'Amato, serve as a catalyst for exploring these themes.

The movie also explores the idea of perseverance and hard work, as Steve strives to become a better football player and find success on and off the field. Through Steve's journey, the film conveys the importance of staying true to oneself and pursuing one's passions, even in the face of adversity.

Overall, All the Right Moves is a poignant and relatable exploration of the challenges and triumphs of adolescence, making it a timeless classic that continues to resonate with audiences today.

overview: When Ann, husband George, and son Georgie arrive at their holiday home they are visited by a pair of polite and seemingly pleasant young men. Armed with deceptively sweet smiles and some golf clubs, they proceed to terrorize and torture the tight-knit clan, giving them until the next day to survive.
tagline: You must admit, you brought this on yourself.
title: Funny Games
plot:
Funny Games, also known as Funny Games U.S., is a satirical psychological thriller of 2007 written and directed by Michael Haneke, a shot-for-shot English-language remake of his own 1997 Austrian film, relocated to the United States. Naomi Watts and Tim Roth play Ann and George Farber, with Devon Gearhart as their son Georgie, Michael Pitt and Brady Corbet as the intruders Paul and Peter, and Boyd Gaines as their neighbor Fred. Despite the setting, it was a six-country international co-production.

The Farbers arrive at their lake house with their dog Lucky. Their neighbor Fred, acting oddly, stops by with two young men, Paul and Peter, to help launch the boat. Peter then borrows eggs, drops them, and returns for more, which also end up broken. With Paul pestering Ann to try a golf club and Peter demanding yet more eggs, George orders them out and slaps Paul, and Peter breaks George's leg with the club. The pair take the family hostage, and Paul leads Ann in a game of hot and cold that ends at the body of Lucky, whom he has killed.

The captors force the family into a series of sadistic games, putting a pillowcase over Georgie's head and hurting him until Ann undresses. Georgie escapes to Fred's house, finds corpses there and a shotgun, but when he tries to fire it at Paul it proves unloaded.
