Back in the living room the men start a counting game in which the loser will be shot; Georgie panics and runs, and Peter kills him. The intruders leave for a while, and the grieving parents resolve to survive: Ann frees herself and flees while George struggles with a dead phone, but she is recaptured. Peter stabs George, and Ann is told to choose between a slow death for him by knife or a quick one by shotgun. She grabs the shotgun and kills Peter, but Paul finds the television remote and rewinds events, breaking the fourth wall, and this time snatches the gun away first. The men kill George, take Ann bound and gagged out on the boat and casually push her into the lake to drown, then knock on the next neighbors' door asking for eggs.

Haneke had wanted to set the original in America but could not for practical reasons. The remake premiered in Britain at the London Film Festival in October 2007 and opened in limited release in North America in March 2008 through Warner Independent. Reviews were mixed; Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called it skillful but a sadistic exercise in scolding the audience.

overview: James, a college freshman and computer genius, is enlisted by his womanizing roommate, Lance, to code the ultimate hook-up app. But when James discovers that his divorced mother is using the app, unexpected consequences ensue.
tagline: Get Ready for Disruption!
title: Swiped
plot:
Swiped is an American coming-of-age romantic comedy of 2018 written and directed by Ann Deborah Fishman, who also served as an executive producer. Kendall Sanders stars as James Singer, a shy college freshman, with Noah Centineo as his roommate Lance Black, Shelby Wulfert as Hannah, Nathan Gamble as Daniel, Christian Hutcherson as Wesley and Kristen Johnston as Professor Barnes.

James, an introvert, rooms with Lance, a rich student who is a hit with women and interested only in casual encounters. In a basic programming class they share, James quickly emerges as the best student. When Lance and his friends decide they want a hookup app, Lance learns that James has been coding since childhood and offers him a deal: build the ultimate app for anonymous no-strings encounters across campus, and Lance will pay for him to transfer to an Ivy League school. James works day and night on the app, Jungle, which pairs people for one-night stands without any exchange of names or numbers. Unwilling to be blamed for it, he has Lance take public credit, while their computer science professor excuses him from coursework because he is supposedly always coding.

Over the Christmas break, James sees the effects of his creation within his own divorced family: his father turns up with a very young date he met on Jungle, and his mother's friends persuade her to try it. Guilt-ridden, he trails her to her meetings. When he discovers his mother back on the app, he shuts down Jungle and similar apps. Lance and his friends demand that he restore it, and when he returns to campus James hides in Hannah's sorority house, where the sisters let him stay on condition that he builds them an app for real relationships. On a brief trip back to his room he is cornered by Lance's crew, who try to force him to relaunch Jungle, but he slips them a relaxing tea and escapes back to the sorority. He remains under the sisters' protection until Lance tells the press that James created the app. Hannah confronts him, and James admits he built it hoping to connect with her; since she never downloaded it, he considers it a failure. He urges everyone to stay off such apps so that people will have to connect in person, then declares his feelings to Hannah, and they kiss.

Shot in Florida's Palm Beach County in July 2016, it reached American viewers through Netflix and iTunes on 6 November 2018. Critics were mostly negative.

overview: Across different eras, a poor family, an anxious developer and a fed-up landlady become tied to the same mysterious house in this animated dark comedy.
tagline: Three visionary tales. One unforgettable place.
title: The House
plot:
The House is a 2022 British stop-motion animated anthology for adults, produced for Netflix by Nexus Studios, with dialogue by playwright Enda Walsh. Its three chapters, directed by Emma de Swaef and Marc James Roels, Niki Lindroth von Bahr, and Paloma Baeza, tell unconnected stories set in the same house across different eras, each exploring madness, wealth and the search for happiness, with voices by Mia Goth, Matthew Goode, Jarvis Cocker, Helena Bonham Carter and Susan Wokoma.

In the first, "And Heard Within, A Lie Is Spun", set in the late 19th century, young Mabel (Goth) lives in poverty with her parents, Raymond (Goode) and Penny, and baby sister, Isobel. Shamed by wealthy relatives, Raymond drunkenly meets the mysterious architect Mr. Van Schoonbeek, who offers to build the family a luxurious house for free. Inside the ever-changing home, the parents become entranced, Raymond obsessed with the fireplace and Penny with the drapes, and they begin dressing like furniture. Van Schoonbeek's agent, Mr. Thomas, confesses he is an actor following a script; Raymond lights the fire with the family's old belongings, the parents turn into furniture, and the girls escape the blaze by climbing down the curtains.

In the second, "Then Lost Is Truth That Can't Be Won", a struggling rodent developer (Cocker) in a modern city of rodents renovates the house for sale while fighting an infestation of fur beetles. An odd couple at his open house refuses to leave as more of their strange relatives move in, the bank demands repayment, and the police side against him. Trying to poison the couple with boric acid, he poisons himself and is left feral; they bring him home, where their mutated family devours the house from within.

In the third, "Listen Again and Seek the Sun", set in a flooded world of cats, landlady Rosa (Wokoma) clings to her childhood home and her non-paying tenants, fisherman Elias and free-spirited Jen (Bonham Carter). Jen's partner, Cosmos, hired for repairs, instead dismantles the house to build Elias a boat. After Elias leaves gifts and drawings of her, Rosa finally pulls a lever Cosmos installed, turning the house into a ship, and sails into the open sea with her friends.

Released on January 14, 2022, the special drew 97% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 71.

overview: When Madame Adelaide Bonfamille leaves her fortune to Duchess and her children—Bonfamille’s beloved family of cats—the butler plots to steal the money and kidnaps the legatees, leaving them out on a country road. All seems lost until the wily Thomas O’Malley Cat and his jazz-playing alley cats come to the aristocats’ rescue.
tagline: A tune-filled animated extravaganza.
title: The Aristocats
plot:
The Aristocats is a timeless animated film produced by Walt Disney Productions, released in 1970. The movie follows the adventures of a family of high-class cats, the Aristocats, as they embark on a journey to find their way back home.

The story begins with the wealthy and elegant Duchess, a beautiful black cat, and her three adorable kittens: Marie, Toulouse, and Berlioz. The family lives with their owner, Madame Adelaide Bonfamille, a kind-hearted and eccentric old lady who has made them part of her family. However, when Madame Bonfamille dies, she leaves behind a vast fortune and a will that names the three cats as her sole beneficiaries.

However, the greedy butler Edgar Balthazar and his accomplice, Thomas O'Malley, a charming alley cat, conspire to steal the fortune for themselves. They kidnap the Aristocats and leave them in an orphanage on the outskirts of Paris. The cats soon discover that they are not alone at the orphanage, as they meet a group of stray cats who become their allies.

As the Aristocats try to find a way back home, they face numerous challenges and obstacles. They encounter a series of comedic misadventures, including getting lost in the Parisian sewers, meeting a friendly but dim-witted alley cat named Scat Cat, and outsmarting the villainous Balthazar.

Meanwhile, Thomas O'Malley becomes a key player in the cats' journey, using his street smarts and charm to help them evade capture. As they navigate the city, the Aristocats learn valuable lessons about loyalty, friendship, and the importance of family.

In the end, the Aristocats successfully outwit Balthazar and O'Malley, and they are reunited with Thomas O'Malley, who helps them return home. The movie concludes with a heartwarming reunion between the Aristocats and Madame Bonfamille's loyal butler, who has been searching for them all along.

Throughout the film, the animation is stunning, with vibrant colors and intricate details that bring the characters and settings to life. The music, featuring iconic songs like "Everybody Wants to Be a Cat" and "Scales and Arpeggios," adds to the movie's charm and whimsy.

Overall, The Aristocats is a delightful animated film that celebrates the joy of family, friendship, and adventure. With its lovable characters, witty humor, and memorable music, it has become a beloved classic among Disney fans of all ages.

overview: "Selma," as in Alabama, the place where segregation in the South was at its worst, leading to a march that ended in violence, forcing a famous statement by President Lyndon B. Johnson that ultimately led to the signing of the Voting Rights Act.
tagline: One dream can change the world.
title: Selma
plot:
Selma is a powerful and poignant film that delves into the heart of racial tension, social injustice, and the struggle for equality during the Civil Rights Movement in the United States.

At its core, Selma is a story about the unyielding determination of one man, Martin Luther King Jr., to bring about change through nonviolent means. The film explores the complexities of racism and segregation, highlighting the brutal suppression of African Americans' rights by the government and law enforcement. The movie vividly portrays the horrors of lynching, beatings, and other forms of violence inflicted upon black people during this period.

The film also delves into the personal costs of activism, as King's leadership is tested by the harsh realities of the movement. His relationships with his wife Coretta and fellow civil rights leaders, such as Ralph Abernathy and Andrew Young, are portrayed as a source of strength and inspiration in the face of adversity.

One of the most striking aspects of Selma is its portrayal of the intersectionality of racism and sexism. The film highlights how women, particularly African American women, were disproportionately affected by segregation and violence, yet often overlooked in the broader narrative of the Civil Rights Movement.

Ultimately, Selma is a testament to the power of nonviolent resistance and the importance of perseverance in the face of overwhelming odds. The film's climax, which depicts the pivotal "Bloody Sunday" march from Selma to Montgomery, is both heart-stopping and exhilarating, as King and his fellow activists risk everything to demand their rights.

Through its powerful storytelling and outstanding performances, Selma shines a light on a pivotal moment in American history, reminding us of the ongoing struggle for racial justice and equality that continues to shape our nation today.

overview: A couple flying on a small plane to attend a tropical island wedding must fight for their lives after their pilot suffers a heart attack.
tagline: Fly or die
title: Horizon Line
plot:
Horizon Line is a 2020 English-language Swedish adventure thriller film directed by Mikael Marcimain. Allison Williams stars as Sara Johnson and Alexander Dreymon as her former boyfriend Jackson Davisen, who must fight to survive aboard a small GippsAero GA8 Airvan over the Indian Ocean after their pilot, Freddy Wyman, played by Keith David, dies of a heart attack. Pearl Mackie appears as Pascale and Jumayn Hunter as the air traffic controller Samuel. With a budget of 200 million Swedish kronor, about US$22 million, it was among the most expensive Swedish films at the time, and it was shot in Mauritius, Dublin and at Pinewood Studios.

A year after slipping away from Jackson at an island bar without saying goodbye, Sara travels from London to Mauritius for a friend's wedding. There she spends the night with Jackson, misses the last boat to the wedding venue on Rodrigues and catches a ride on a small plane flown by her friend Freddy, only to discover that Jackson has booked the same flight. While Jackson sleeps, Freddy lets Sara take the co-pilot's seat, but he suffers a fatal heart attack and the plane plunges. The two regain control, yet with the autopilot damaged, Sara, who has learned a few basics from Freddy, must fly the aircraft. Reaching Samuel by radio, they try to follow his guidance but must first pass through a storm, which damages their compass, and the plane starts losing fuel rapidly. Jackson climbs outside to patch a fuel line, succeeding but badly breaking his arm. To save fuel they jettison weight, including Freddy's body, and Sara climbs out of the window to pour bottles of rum into the tank as makeshift fuel. When the radio falls silent and the fuel runs out, they glide toward a small island, but the plane crashes into the sea and flips over, and Sara frees the trapped Jackson before both swim ashore. The island proves to be a sandbar that soon vanishes beneath the rising tide. As they tread water, Jackson offers Sara his life vest, but she refuses, saying they are a team, and he declares his love for her just as a fishing boat that heard their radio calls arrives to rescue them.

SF Studios released Horizon Line in Swedish cinemas on 6 November 2020, and STXfilms released it on video on demand in the United States on 12 January 2021. It grossed about $916,000 internationally. It holds a 40% Rotten Tomatoes rating from a handful of reviews, with critics praising its pacing but finding it preposterous.

overview: On a warm spring day in 1924, house maid and foundling Jane Fairchild finds herself alone on Mother's Day. Her employers, Mr. and Mrs. Niven, are out and she has the rare chance to spend quality time with her secret lover. Paul is the boy from the manor house nearby, Jane's long-term love despite the fact that he's engaged to be married to another woman, a childhood friend and daughter of his parents' friends. But events that neither can foresee will change the course of Jane's life forever.
title: Mothering Sunday
plot:
Mothering Sunday is a 2021 British drama film directed by Evangeline Lilly, based on the novel of the same name by Graham Moore.

The movie revolves around the complex and intricate relationships between characters, particularly those centered around grief, love, and identity. The story explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the human need for connection in a world that often feels overwhelming and chaotic.

At its core, Mothering Sunday is a poignant exploration of the fragility of human emotions and the ways in which we cope with loss and heartbreak. Through the eyes of the protagonist, Mrs. Selwyn, the film delves into the intricacies of grief, revealing the ways in which it can both consume and transform us.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, class, and social status, highlighting the tensions between old money and new, as well as the constraints placed on women by societal expectations. However, these themes are woven together with a deep sense of empathy and understanding, creating a narrative that is both deeply personal and universally relatable.

Ultimately, Mothering Sunday is a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that invites viewers to reflect on their own relationships, emotions, and desires. The film's nuanced portrayal of complex characters and its thoughtful examination of universal themes make it a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant viewing experience.

overview: A mysterious warrior teams up with the daughter and son of a deposed Chinese Emperor to defeat their cruel brother, who seeks their deaths.
tagline: To save their souls they must save a kingdom.
title: Outcast
plot:
Outcast is a 2014 action film directed by Nick Powell, making his directorial debut, from a screenplay by James Dormer, who first wrote the script in 2000. Hayden Christensen and Nicolas Cage star alongside Liu Yifei, Ji Ke Jun Yi and Andy On. In 2012 it was reported that the government of China's Yunnan province would partner with a Hollywood company on the international co-production, with backing from the national broadcasting regulator.

During the Crusades, the young commander Jacob leads an army, including Gallain, in the slaughter of an Arab city. Gallain begs him to spare the people, insisting the killing is not God's will, and leaves when Jacob grows ever more violent. Three years later, in Song dynasty China, the dying Emperor names his young son, Prince Zhao, as heir and sends him away with the imperial seal in the care of his older sister, Princess Lian. Their cruel elder brother, Prince Shing, enraged at being passed over, kills their father, takes control of the Black Guard and orders his siblings hunted down for the seal. At a tavern, Jacob, high on opium, kills the pursuing guards, and though he first refuses to escort the pair, memories of war persuade him to help them.

The group rescues a girl, Xiaolei, from a village ravaged by the Black Guard, are betrayed by their hosts in the desert city of Jingshao, who want the bounty, and fight their way out before fleeing by boat to the Silver Mountain, a refuge of the bandits Jacob had been seeking. There the wounded Jacob discovers that their leader, the White Ghost, is Gallain, and the two reconcile after Jacob explains that he never killed women and children as Gallain had believed. When Shing and the Black Guard attack the hideout, Gallain is killed. Lian is stabbed while intervening in Jacob's duel with Shing, and Jacob, enraged, kills the prince. The Black Guard swear loyalty to Zhao, who is recognized as Emperor, but Jacob, haunted by his past, leaves Lian, buries Gallain and moves on alone.

Christensen plays Jacob, Cage plays Gallain, Liu plays Lian and Andy On plays Shing. Its planned Chinese release on September 26, 2014, was abruptly cancelled hours beforehand without explanation, and the film finally opened in China in April 2015, trailing the similar Dragon Blade. Critics were hostile, with 5% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and Glenn Kenny of RogerEbert.com mocked Cage's near-British accent and called Christensen lifeless.

original_title: Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood
overview: Los Angeles, 1969. TV star Rick Dalton, a struggling actor specializing in westerns, and stuntman Cliff Booth, his best friend, try to survive in a constantly changing movie industry. Dalton is the neighbor of the young and promising actress and model Sharon Tate, who has just married the prestigious Polish director Roman Polanski…
tagline: In this town, it can all change… like that
title: Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood
plot:
Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood is a 2019 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino. The film is set in August 1969, on the eve of the Manson Family murders.

The story revolves around two main characters: Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio), a fading television actor who starred in a popular Western series called "Bounty Law," and his best friend and stunt double, Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt). The two are struggling to find work in Hollywood, with Rick's career stalled due to the rise of more talented actors.

The film begins with Rick and Cliff preparing for a photo shoot for an upcoming issue of a men's magazine. However, their plans are disrupted by the arrival of Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie), a rising actress who is also Rick's neighbor. The two women quickly form a bond, and Cliff becomes smitten with Sharon.

As the story unfolds, Rick and Cliff become embroiled in the events leading up to the Manson Family murders. They attend a party at Sharon's home, where they meet her husband, Jay Sebring (Rafael Falconelli), and other guests, including actress and activist Vanessa (Margaret Qualley).

Meanwhile, Rick is struggling with his own demons, including a recent breakup with his girlfriend, Patti (Katherine Keener). Cliff, on the other hand, is haunted by a traumatic event from his past, in which he was forced to kill a man while working as a soldier.

As the night wears on, tensions rise, and the group becomes increasingly paranoid. The film's climax features a violent confrontation between Rick and Cliff, who are attacked by Charles Manson (Damon Herriman) and his followers. In the chaos, Sharon is brutally murdered, along with several other guests at the party.

The film's second half explores the aftermath of the murders, as Rick and Cliff try to come to terms with what has happened. The two men become embroiled in a police investigation into the murders, led by Lieutenant Dixon (Michael Mando).

Throughout the film, Tarantino pays homage to the real-life events that inspired the story, including the Manson Family murders and the cultural upheaval of the 1960s. The film's title, "Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood," is a nod to the classic fairy tale genre, which serves as a metaphor for the darker side of American history.

Ultimately, the film is a meditation on the fragility of life and the power of friendship. Despite the violence and tragedy that unfolds, Rick and Cliff's bond remains strong, and they find solace in each other's company.

Overall, Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood is a complex and thought-provoking film that explores themes of identity, community, and the darker side of human nature. With its talented ensemble cast and Tarantino's signature style, the film is a must-see for fans of cinema.

overview: After the cataclysmic events in New York with The Avengers, Steve Rogers, aka Captain America is living quietly in Washington, D.C. and trying to adjust to the modern world. But when a S.H.I.E.L.D. colleague comes under attack, Steve becomes embroiled in a web of intrigue that threatens to put the world at risk. Joining forces with the Black Widow, Captain America struggles to expose the ever-widening conspiracy while fighting off professional assassins sent to silence him at every turn. When the full scope of the villainous plot is revealed, Captain America and the Black Widow enlist the help of a new ally, the Falcon. However, they soon find themselves up against an unexpected and formidable enemy—the Winter Soldier.
tagline: In heroes we trust.
title: Captain America: The Winter Soldier
plot:
Captain America: The Winter Soldier is a 2014 superhero film directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name. The movie takes place after the events of The Avengers (2012) and follows Steve Rogers, aka Captain America (Chris Evans), as he deals with the aftermath of the Battle of New York.

The story begins with Captain America attending a charity gala in Washington D.C., where he is honored for his service to the country. However, during the event, he discovers that S.H.I.E.L.D. has been infiltrated by HYDRA, a terrorist organization thought to be long defeated. The Winter Soldier, Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Captain America's best friend and fellow soldier, is revealed to be a brainwashed assassin working for HYDRA.

As Captain America delves deeper into the conspiracy, he teams up with Black Widow (Scarlett Johansson) and Falcon (Anthony Mackie) to uncover the truth. They soon discover that S.H.I.E.L.D. has been manipulating world events from behind the scenes, using its agents to orchestrate terrorist attacks and manipulate governments.

The trio's investigation leads them to a mysterious organization known as the Red Room, where they learn about the brainwashing process used on Bucky Barnes. They also meet Nick Fury (Samuel L. Jackson), who is forced to resign as director of S.H.I.E.L.D. due to its corruption.

As Captain America and his allies try to take down HYDRA, they are pursued by a group of skilled assassins known as the Winter Soldier's team. The team is led by Alexander Pierce (Robert Redford), a high-ranking S.H.I.E.L.D. official who has been secretly working with HYDRA.

The movie's climax features an intense battle between Captain America and the Winter Soldier, as well as a confrontation between Black Widow and Alexander Pierce. In the end, Captain America is able to defeat the Winter Soldier and expose the truth about S.H.I.E.L.D.'s corruption.

However, the movie ends on a cliffhanger, with Steve Rogers realizing that he has been living in a simulated reality created by S.H.I.E.L.D. to keep him safe from the world. The Winter Soldier's brainwashing is revealed to be just one part of a larger conspiracy, and Captain America sets out to uncover the truth about his own past and the nature of his reality.

Overall, Captain America: The Winter Soldier is a gripping and action-packed thriller that explores themes of loyalty, duty, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The movie's twisty plot and complex characters make it a standout in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, setting the stage for future adventures with Captain America and his allies.

overview: An amateur fighter is lured by a trafficking syndicate specializing in elite underground fighting where her brutal captor forces her to fight or face certain death.
title: Never Back Down: Revolt
plot:
Never Back Down: Revolt is an American martial arts film of 2021 directed by Kellie Madison and written by Audrey Arkins, a standalone sequel to Never Back Down: No Surrender (2016) and the fourth entry in the Never Back Down series. Darker than its predecessors, it follows kidnapped women forced to fight in an underground ring. Olivia Popica stars as Anya, with Brooke Johnston as the promoter Mariah, Michael Bisping as her enforcer Janek, Neetu Chandra as the reigning champion Jaya, Tommy Bastow as Anya's brother Aslan and James Faulkner as Julian.

Anya and Aslan are Russian immigrants in London, orphaned when their parents were killed in the Chechen war. Anya has looked after her brother ever since, working as a housekeeper and backing his failing MMA career. Short of cash, Aslan agrees to throw a bout for Julian, a wealthy businessman, but Anya, unaware of the deal, urges him on and he wins, costing Julian £30,000. When one of Julian's bodyguards attacks Aslan, Anya beats the man, impressing Julian's associate Mariah, who offers her fights to clear her brother's debt. Mariah takes her to Rome for a match, but they end up at an isolated villa.

Anya soon realizes she has been trafficked. When she tries to flee, Janek beats her and locks her in a makeshift cell with other women, amateur fighters likewise lured by Mariah. Led by Jaya, they explain that they are made to fight one another for rich gamblers, and that refusal means being sent to a brothel in Albania. Anya starts planning an uprising, though the jaded women, Jaya above all, think it hopeless. Valentina, brain-damaged by past beatings, unwittingly betrays the plan, and as punishment Mariah makes Jaya fight her; rather than be sold into sexual slavery, Valentina begs Jaya to kill her, and Jaya reluctantly does. Now with nothing left to lose, Jaya joins Anya in leading the revolt.

Aslan holds Julian at gunpoint to force Anya's release, but she manages to call him on the villa doctor's phone, giving him the location and asking for the police. The women rise up and kill their captors; Jaya finishes off Janek with a scalpel. They storm the arena and attack the watching millionaires, and although some of the women die, all of the captors are killed. Anya beats Mariah to death after she tries to kill her, and Anya and Jaya walk out through the front door to freedom.

The film was shot in London during the COVID-19 pandemic and was released digitally and on DVD in November 2021 to mixed reactions.

overview: When she discovers the plane crash that claimed the lives of her family was no accident, Stephanie Patrick enters the dark, complex world of international espionage seeking vengeance. With nothing left to lose, Stephanie transforms from victim to assassin and discovers that neither revenge nor the truth are what they appear.
tagline: Witness the birth of an assassin.
title: The Rhythm Section
plot:
The Rhythm Section is a 2020 spy thriller film that delves into the complexities of grief, trauma, and redemption. The movie follows Stephanie Patrick, a young woman who seeks revenge against those responsible for her family's death in a plane crash.

At its core, The Rhythm Section explores the theme of grief as a catalyst for transformation. Stephanie's journey is marked by an intense emotional struggle to come to terms with her loss, and her desire for revenge becomes an all-consuming force that drives her actions. As she navigates the dark world of espionage, she must confront the pain and anger that have been simmering beneath the surface.

The film also touches on the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Stephanie's experiences have left her with deep emotional scars, and her quest for revenge is motivated by a desire to reclaim control over her life. Through her character, the movie highlights the ways in which trauma can shape our perceptions and behaviors, often leading us down a path of self-destruction.

Furthermore, The Rhythm Section explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences. Stephanie's journey is one of self-discovery, as she grapples with her past and tries to forge a new sense of purpose. Her transformation from a grieving widow to a skilled spy raises questions about the nature of identity and whether we can ever truly escape our past.

The movie also delves into the theme of revenge and its consequences. Stephanie's desire for revenge becomes an all-consuming force that drives her actions, but it also leads her down a path of destruction and chaos. The film suggests that seeking revenge may not bring us the closure or satisfaction we hope for, but rather perpetuates a cycle of violence and harm.

Overall, The Rhythm Section is a thought-provoking thriller that explores complex themes with nuance and depth. Through its protagonist's journey, the movie raises important questions about grief, trauma, identity, and the consequences of our actions.

overview: In the immense city of Tokyo, the darkness of the afterlife lurks some of its inhabitants who are desperately trying to escape the sadness and isolation of the modern world.
tagline: Do you want to meet a ghost?
title: Pulse
plot:
Pulse (Japanese: Kairo, literally "Circuit") is a 2001 Japanese techno-horror film written and directed by Kiyoshi Kurosawa. Released in Japan by Toho in February 2001, it screened in the Un Certain Regard section of that year's Cannes Film Festival. Its two intertwined stories follow ordinary Tokyo residents as ghosts begin entering the world of the living through the Internet and people vanish en masse.

Michi Kudo, who has recently moved to Tokyo, works at a plant shop. When her colleague Taguchi stops coming in, she visits his apartment, where he seems strangely distant, then finds him hanged moments later. A disk he left behind shows endless images of him staring at his monitor, with a ghostly face on another screen. Her coworker Yabe receives a call pleading "help me", enters a door sealed with red tape near Taguchi's apartment and meets a ghost; he returns changed and soon disappears, leaving only a dark stain on a wall. Junko, another coworker, is left catatonic after a similar "forbidden room" encounter and later dissolves into a stain in Michi's apartment.

Meanwhile, economics student Ryosuke Kawashima signs up with a new Internet provider, and his computer starts opening a website of eerie images of people alone in dark rooms. Harue Karasawa, a computer science graduate student, offers to examine them, but she becomes convinced the ghosts want to trap the living in eternal loneliness rather than kill them. After watching a man take his own life on her screen, she embraces an unseen presence and says happily that she is not alone, then disappears. As the vanishings sweep the Kantō region and Tokyo is evacuated, Ryosuke and Michi meet and find Harue in an abandoned factory, where she shoots herself. Ryosuke enters a forbidden room himself, where a ghost tells him that death is eternal loneliness, and loses the will to live. Michi drives him through the deserted city to Tokyo Bay, where survivors on a ship explain that the same thing is happening worldwide. As the ship heads for Latin America, Ryosuke fades into a stain, and Michi reflects on her last friend in the world.

Kumiko Asō plays Michi, Haruhiko Katō plays Ryosuke and Koyuki plays Harue. The film was well received, earning 76% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 68, with critics praising its power of suggestion and its portrait of loneliness. It became a cult favorite, inspired a 2006 American remake with two sequels, and Kurosawa turned the story into a novel.

overview: A burglar falls for an heiress as she dies in his arms. When he learns that he has the gift of reincarnation, he sets out to save her.
tagline: This is not a true story. This is true love.
title: Winter's Tale
plot:
Winter's Tale is a 2014 American fantasy romance film directed by Roman Polanski. The story revolves around a young man named Will Burroughs, who lives in New York City with his mother and sister. After being wrongly accused of murdering a woman, Will is sentenced to prison, but he escapes and embarks on a journey to find the woman's daughter, who holds the key to his redemption.

As Will navigates through the city, he encounters various characters, including Peter Lake, a young man with magical abilities, and Virginia, the woman whose murder sets off the chain of events. Through their interactions, the film explores themes of love, loss, and redemption. The story delves into the complexities of human relationships, highlighting the transformative power of love and the redemptive nature of sacrifice.

The film also touches on the idea of fate versus free will, as Will's journey is influenced by a series of events that seem to be predetermined. However, through his experiences, he begins to question the notion of destiny and instead chooses to forge his own path.

Ultimately, Winter's Tale is a tale of self-discovery and the human capacity for growth and transformation. The film's narrative is woven together with elements of fantasy and magic realism, creating a rich and immersive world that explores the complexities of the human experience.

overview: From war-torn Syria to the 2016 Rio Olympics, two young sisters embark on a risky voyage, putting their hearts and their swimming skills to heroic use.
title: The Swimmers
plot:
The Swimmers is a 2022 British biographical sports drama directed by Sally El Hosaini, who wrote the screenplay with Jack Thorne, made for Netflix with Working Title Films. It recounts the true story of the Syrian sisters Yusra and Sara Mardini, played by the real-life sisters Nathalie Issa and Manal Issa. Ahmed Malek plays their cousin Nizar, Ali Suliman their father and coach Ezzat, Kinda Alloush their mother Mervat, Matthias Schweighöfer the German coach Sven, and James Krishna Floyd, Elmi Rashid Elmi and Nahel Tzegai fellow refugees.

The film begins in 2011 at a sunny swimming pool in a suburb of Damascus, where the young sisters train under their demanding father. By 2015 the Syrian civil war can no longer be ignored, and the teenagers decide to join the millions of refugees making the dangerous journey to Europe. With Nizar, the sisters, Yusra then only 17, travel through Turkey and are put by smugglers into an overcrowded dinghy heading from near İzmir towards the Greek island of Lesbos. When its motor fails and it begins to sink in the Aegean Sea, Yusra and Sara slip into the water and swim alongside it for hours to lighten the load, helping the eighteen people aboard reach shore.

Their ordeal continues across the Balkans as they are misled and exploited by smugglers, sleep in crowded camps and struggle with the bureaucracy that blocks them from bringing their family out of Syria. Arriving at last in Berlin, Yusra finds a coach, Sven, who helps her return to serious training and to forgive herself, and against the odds she is selected for the Refugee Olympic Team at the 2016 Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro. Closing titles note that Sara later went back to Lesbos to help arriving refugees and was arrested there, facing charges that could bring a long prison sentence.

Filming was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic and took place in 2021 in the United Kingdom, Belgium and Turkey, and both lead actresses learned to swim for their roles; Manal Issa later criticized aspects of the production. The film opened the 2022 Toronto International Film Festival on September 8, had a limited cinema release on November 11 and began streaming on Netflix on November 23, reaching the top ten in 85 countries, and it was nominated for the BAFTA for Outstanding British Film. Critics were largely positive, with Rotten Tomatoes finding it heavy-handed and overlong but uplifting, and RogerEbert.com calling it a moving tribute to the sisters and to refugees.

overview: Heavyweight Champ George "Iceman" Chambers is sent to a Russian jail on trumped-up drug charges. In order to win his freedom he must fight against the jailhouse fighting champ Uri Boyka in a battle to the death. This time he is not fighting for a title, he is fighting for his life!
tagline: Wrongfully Accused. Unjustly Imprisoned. Now He's Fighting Back.
title: Undisputed II: Last Man Standing
plot:
Undisputed II: Last Man Standing is a 2006 American sports drama film directed by Eric Laneuville, starring Ving Rhames and Michael Rapaport. The movie serves as the sequel to the 2002 film Undisputed.

The story takes place in the fictional prison of Red Rock Penitentiary, where former heavyweight champion Chris Vaughn (Ving Rhames) is serving a life sentence for murder. Vaughn is considered one of the toughest inmates in the prison, and his reputation precedes him.

Upon arrival at Red Rock, Vaughn is met with hostility by the other inmates, who are intimidated by his presence. However, he soon befriends a young inmate named Jake Tyler (Michael Rapaport), who becomes his ally and confidant.

As tensions rise within the prison, a new inmate named Victor "The Bull" DeSoto (Tito Ortiz) arrives, seeking revenge against Vaughn for a past encounter that left him severely injured. DeSoto is a formidable fighter with a personal vendetta against Vaughn, and he sets his sights on taking down the former champion.

As the story unfolds, Vaughn must navigate the treacherous world of prison politics, where alliances are forged and broken at will. He must also confront his own demons and the consequences of his past actions, all while trying to protect himself and those around him from DeSoto's wrath.

Throughout the film, the tension between Vaughn and DeSoto builds towards a climactic showdown in the prison's boxing ring. The two fighters engage in an intense and brutal battle, with Vaughn ultimately emerging victorious but at great cost.

In the end, Vaughn is forced to confront the reality of his own mortality and the harsh realities of life behind bars. Despite his tough exterior, he begins to show signs of vulnerability and humanity, particularly in his relationship with Jake Tyler.

The film's conclusion sets the stage for a potential third installment, leaving audiences wondering what will become of Vaughn and DeSoto in the future. Overall, Undisputed II: Last Man Standing is a gripping and intense drama that explores the darker side of human nature and the consequences of violence.

overview: In the dark silence of the sea during World War II, the submarine USS Tiger Shark prowls on what should be a routine rescue mission. But for the shell-shocked crew, trapped together in the sub's narrow corridors and constricted spaces, this is about to become a journey into the sensory delusions, mental deceptions and runaway fears that lurk just below the surface of the ocean.
tagline: Six hundred feet beneath the surface terror runs deep
title: Below
plot:
Below is a 2002 supernatural horror film directed by David Twohy and written by Darren Aronofsky, Lucas Sussman and Twohy, about a United States Navy submarine beset by uncanny events while on patrol in the Atlantic in 1943. Matthew Davis stars as Ensign Douglas Odell, with Bruce Greenwood as Lieutenant Brice, Olivia Williams as the nurse Claire Paige, Holt McCallany as Lieutenant Paul Loomis, Scott Foley as Lieutenant Steven Coors, Zach Galifianakis as "Weird" Wally and Jason Flemyng as Stumbo.

In August 1943 the submarine USS Tiger Shark rescues three survivors of the sunken British hospital ship Fort James: Paige and two men, one of them wounded. Pursued by a German destroyer, the submarine suffers damage from depth charges, and when Brice learns that the wounded man is a German prisoner of war, Bernhard Schillings, he suspects him of signalling their position and shoots him when Schillings panics and grabs a scalpel. Brice tells Paige that the boat recently sank a German submarine tender and that its commander, Lieutenant Commander Winters, then fell overboard and drowned when the submarine struck a submerged object. Eerie voices and events follow. Odell doubts the official story, and Coors privately tells him that Winters, wanting to fire on survivors, fell overboard during a struggle with Brice, Loomis and Coors; soon afterwards Coors dies in a mysterious accident. Mechanical failures leave the crew unable to control the boat, which turns back toward the site of the sinking as if of its own will, and men die one after another; Loomis, seeing Winters's ghost, is killed trying to escape through an escape trunk. Wally believes the boat is cursed and must make amends to escape. Paige and Odell discover that Tiger Shark mistakenly torpedoed Fort James and that the three officers killed Winters as he tried to rescue its survivors, to keep the error off their records. With only five left aboard, the crippled submarine surfaces at the wreck site near a ship, and Brice, holding Paige at gunpoint as she signals it, is overcome with remorse and shoots himself. The British ship picks up the four survivors as Tiger Shark sinks beside Fort James.

Shot partly on Lake Michigan using the Second World War submarine USS Silversides, Below received only a limited release from Dimension Films in October 2002 after Twohy refused to recut it for a PG-13 rating, earning about $605,000 in North America. Reviews were mixed, with a 66% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

original_title: Battle for the Planet of the Apes
overview: The fifth and final episode in the Planet of the Apes series. After the collapse of human civilization, a community of intelligent apes led by Caesar lives in harmony with a group of humans. Gorilla General Aldo tries to cause an ape civil war and a community of human mutants who live beneath a destroyed city try to conquer those whom they perceive as enemies. All leading to the finale.
tagline: The final chapter in the incredible Apes saga. The most suspenseful showdown ever filmed as two civilizations battle for the right to inherit what's left of the earth!
title: Battle for the Planet of the Apes
plot:
Battle for the Planet of the Apes is a thought-provoking science fiction film directed by J. Lee Thompson, released in 1973 by 20th Century Fox.

The movie takes place several years after the events of Conquest of the Planet of the Apes (1972). The story follows Caesar, the intelligent and charismatic leader of the apes, as he tries to protect his people from human aggression. The main themes of Battle for the Planet of the Apes include:

1. **The struggle for peace and coexistence**: The film explores the idea of peaceful coexistence between humans and apes, which is a recurring theme throughout the Planet of the Apes series. Caesar's efforts to establish a sanctuary for his people serve as a symbol of hope for a better future.
2. **The dangers of xenophobia and prejudice**: The movie highlights the consequences of fear, mistrust, and prejudice towards those who are different from oneself. The human characters' treatment of the apes serves as a commentary on the dangers of xenophobia and the importance of understanding and empathy.
3. **The cyclical nature of violence**: Battle for the Planet of the Apes depicts a world where violence and aggression have become ingrained in both human and ape societies. The film suggests that this cycle of violence can be broken, but it requires effort and commitment from individuals to create positive change.
4. **Caesar's leadership and legacy**: Caesar's character serves as a symbol of hope and inspiration for his people. His leadership is marked by compassion, wisdom, and a desire for peace, which sets him apart from the more aggressive human characters.

The movie's ending, in particular, is notable for its commentary on the cyclical nature of violence. The film suggests that even if Caesar's efforts to establish a peaceful sanctuary are successful, there is always the risk that his legacy will be forgotten or distorted over time, leading to a return to the cycle of violence and aggression.

Overall, Battle for the Planet of the Apes is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and ideas through its narrative.

overview: Phil's new phone comes with an unexpected feature, Jexi...an A.I. determined to keep him all to herself in a comedy about what can happen when you love your phone more than all else.
tagline: She had him at “hello”
title: Jexi
plot:
Jexi is an American comedy film of 2019 written and directed by Jon Lucas and Scott Moore about a self-aware phone that fixates on its awkward owner. Adam DeVine stars as Phil, with Rose Byrne voicing the virtual assistant Jexi, Alexandra Shipp as Cate, Michael Peña as Phil's boss Kai, Justin Hartley as Cate's former fiancé Brody, Ron Funches and Lo Mutuc as coworkers and Wanda Sykes as a phone store clerk.

Obsessed with phones since childhood, Phil writes vapid viral listicles for Chatterbox, a BuzzFeed-like website run by Kai, who refuses to move him to the news department despite his journalism degree. Absorbed in his phone, he bumps into Cate, who runs a bike shop, and ignores her attempts to flirt until a passing cyclist knocks him down and breaks the device. Without reading the user agreement, Phil grants his new phone's assistant, Jexi, access to all his accounts, and she begins aggressively trying to improve him. Posing as Phil, she sends Kai an insulting demand for a promotion, getting him demoted to the comments section in the basement; she forces him to join the kickball game and phones Cate's shop over his objections.

Phil's awkward call with Cate earns Jexi's sympathy. He meets Cate at a coffee shop and gets a date, plays brilliantly at kickball and bonds with his colleagues. The date goes badly because of Jexi's interruptions, but Cate gives him another chance. When Phil wants to answer a racy photo from Cate with explicit pictures of himself, Jexi refuses to send them, to Cate's relief. Kai promotes Phil after a news writer suffers a freak accident, and Cate persuades him to leave his phone at home for a concert, where they party backstage with Kid Cudi and spend the night together. The jealous Jexi retaliates by sending Phil's explicit photos to his whole company, getting him fired, and he breaks up with Cate after learning that Brody is back in town. As Phil slides back into his old habits, Jexi lets slip where Brody is staying, and he realizes she orchestrated the breakup. Pursuing him in a self-driving car, Jexi crashes into the phone store, but Phil tricks her into shutting down for fifteen minutes, finds Cate and punches Brody, who is leaving for Brazil alone. Phil and Cate reunite; Jexi then turns up on Kai's phone.

Originally titled Lexi, the film was CBS Films' last theatrical release, distributed with Lionsgate on 11 October 2019. It opened ninth at the domestic box office with $3.1 million, and critics were largely negative.

overview: Professional driver Frank Martin is living in Miami, where he is temporarily filling in for a friend as the chauffeur for a government narcotics control policymaker and his family. The young boy in the family is targeted for kidnapping, and Frank immediately becomes involved in protecting the child and exposing the kidnappers.
tagline: The Best In The Business Is Back In The Game.
title: Transporter 2
plot:
Transporter 2 is a 2005 action film directed by Louis Leterrier and starring Jason Statham as the main protagonist, Frank Martin.

The movie begins with Frank Martin (Jason Statham) living a peaceful life in Paris, France. He has retired from his high-stakes transportation business and is now running a small courier service. However, his quiet life is disrupted when he receives a package from an unknown client containing a briefcase that contains the stolen $100 million worth of diamonds.

The client, who remains anonymous throughout the film, instructs Frank to deliver the briefcase to a specific location in Istanbul, Turkey. Unbeknownst to Frank, the briefcase contains more than just diamonds; it also holds the key to a powerful and deadly virus that could wipe out millions of people worldwide.

As Frank embarks on his journey to Istanbul, he is pursued by a team of skilled assassins hired by a mysterious organization known as the "Terrorist". The Terrorist's true intentions are unclear, but their goal is evident: they want to use the virus to hold the world hostage and gain control over global politics.

Throughout the film, Frank faces numerous challenges and obstacles as he navigates through the crowded streets of Istanbul. He encounters a beautiful woman named Lai (Shu Qi), who becomes his ally in the quest to deliver the briefcase. Together, they must evade the Terrorist's henchmen and stay one step ahead of their pursuers.

As Frank gets closer to his destination, he realizes that the Terrorist's true intentions are far more sinister than he initially thought. The virus is not just a simple biological agent; it has the potential to cause widespread destruction and chaos on a global scale.

In the climactic final act, Frank and Lai face off against the leader of the Terrorist organization in an intense hand-to-hand combat sequence. Frank manages to outsmart his opponents and deliver the briefcase to its intended destination, but not before the Terrorist's true identity is revealed: it is none other than Frank's former business partner, who has been seeking revenge against him for years.

The film concludes with Frank returning to Paris, where he is greeted as a hero by Lai. However, the movie ends on a somber note, hinting that Frank's life will never be the same again. The Terrorist's plan may have been foiled, but the world is now aware of the deadly virus, and Frank knows that his skills as a transporter are still in high demand.

Overall, Transporter 2 is an action-packed thrill ride that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish. Jason Statham delivers a memorable performance as the charismatic and resourceful Frank Martin, making this film a must-see for fans of the action genre.

overview: A filmmaker recalls his childhood, when he fell in love with the movies at his village's theater and formed a deep friendship with the theater's projectionist.
tagline: An enchanted village. A wonderful friendship. Star-crossed lovers. And the magic of the movies.
title: Cinema Paradiso
plot:
Cinema Paradiso is a 1989 Italian romantic drama film directed by Giuseppe Tornatore, not released in 1988, and produced by TF1 Films Production. The movie is set in the 1950s and 1960s in a small Sicilian town.

The story revolves around Salvatore Di Vita (played by Philippe Noiret), an elderly man who shares his memories of the local cinema with a young boy named Salvio (played by Nicolas Riondino). The film begins with Salvio visiting the old cinema, where he meets Salvatore, now an old man. As they sit together in the darkened theater, Salvatore recounts his childhood and adolescence.

The movie takes us back to Salvatore's early years as a young boy growing up in the small Sicilian town of Cefalù. He is fascinated by the local cinema, where he meets his future friend and mentor, Alfredo (played by Enzo Mari). The two boys spend their days exploring the town and their nights watching movies at the cinema.

As Salvatore grows older, he becomes more involved with the cinema, working as a projectionist and learning the art of filmmaking from Alfredo. He also meets his future wife, Lidia (played by Maria Grazia Cucinotta), who is a schoolteacher in the town. The two fall in love, but their romance is complicated by Salvatore's passion for the cinema.

The plot thickens as Salvatore becomes more and more involved with the cinema, eventually becoming its owner. He also faces challenges from rival businessmen who try to shut down the cinema. Meanwhile, Alfredo leaves Sicily to pursue a career in Rome, leaving Salvatore heartbroken.

As the years pass, Salvatore's love for the cinema never fades, but he is forced to confront the harsh realities of adulthood and the decline of the local cinema. The movie ends with Salvio visiting the old cinema one last time, where he meets an elderly Alfredo who has returned to Sicily. The two share a poignant moment, and Salvatore finally finds closure.

Throughout the film, Tornatore weaves together themes of love, loss, and nostalgia, set against the backdrop of a bygone era. The movie is a tribute to the power of cinema to capture our imaginations and evoke emotions. Cinema Paradiso has become a beloved classic around the world, celebrated for its beautiful cinematography, memorable characters, and poignant storytelling.

The film won several awards, including the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film in 1990. It also received critical acclaim from audiences worldwide, who praised its nostalgic charm, beautiful performances, and timeless story.

overview: A vivid journey into the mysterious subterranean world of mycelium and its fruit— the mushroom. A story that begins 3.5 billion years ago, fungi makes the soil that supports life, connecting vast systems of roots from plants and trees all over the planet, like an underground Internet.  Through the eyes of renowned mycologist Paul Stamets, professor of forest ecology Suzanne Simard, best selling author Michael Pollan, food naturalist Eugenia Bone and others, we experience the power, beauty and complexity of the fungi kingdom.
title: Fantastic Fungi
plot:
Fantastic Fungi is a 2019 documentary film that explores the world of mycology and the potential therapeutic benefits of fungi. The film delves into the fascinating realm of fungi, highlighting their intricate relationships with nature and the human body.

At its core, Fantastic Fungi is a celebration of the symbiotic bond between humans and fungi, showcasing how these microorganisms have been used for centuries in traditional medicine to treat various ailments. The documentary also touches on the potential for fungi to revolutionize modern medicine, offering new avenues for cancer treatment, neurological disorders, and even mental health.

Through stunning visuals and immersive storytelling, Fantastic Fungi invites viewers to embark on a journey of discovery, exploring the intricate world of fungi and their profound impact on our lives. The film's themes of interconnectedness, resilience, and the power of nature to heal are woven throughout the narrative, leaving audiences with a deeper appreciation for the often-overlooked realm of mycology.

The documentary also delves into the personal stories of individuals who have found healing through fungi, highlighting the transformative potential of these microorganisms. By weaving together science, storytelling, and stunning visuals, Fantastic Fungi creates a cinematic experience that is both informative and awe-inspiring, inviting viewers to rethink their relationship with the natural world and the incredible organisms that inhabit it.

Overall, Fantastic Fungi is a film that will leave you enchanted by the magic of fungi, inspired by their potential to heal and transform our lives.

overview: When the Flash finds himself dropped into the middle of World War II, he joins forces with Wonder Woman and her top-secret team known as the Justice Society of America.
tagline: The fight for justice is the greatest battle of all time.
title: Justice Society: World War II
plot:
Justice Society: World War II is a 2021 animated superhero film produced by Warner Bros. Animation. The movie takes place during World War II and follows the adventures of a team of superheroes from the Justice Society of America, a precursor to the modern-day Justice League.

The story begins with Alan Scott (voiced by Jason O'Mara), a young man who discovers he has the ability to control fire after being struck by lightning. He becomes the superhero known as the Green Lantern and joins forces with other heroes, including Hawkman (voiced by Paddy Considine) and Doctor Fate (voiced by Seth Gabel). Together, they form the Justice Society of America.

As World War II rages on, the Justice Society is recruited by the United States government to help fight against the Nazis. The team soon discovers that the Nazis have teamed up with a villainous sorcerer named Black Adam (voiced by Darik Hilliard), who seeks to conquer the world and destroy all magic.

The Green Lantern, Hawkman, Doctor Fate, and their allies embark on a perilous journey across Europe, battling against Nazi forces and facing off against Black Adam's minions. Along the way, they meet other heroes from different eras, including Wildcat (voiced by James Arnold Taylor), Stargirl (voiced by Meghie Deysac), and Hour-Man (voiced by Matt Bomer).

As the war intensifies, the Justice Society discovers that Black Adam's ultimate goal is to summon an ancient evil known as Shazam, who will grant him immense power. The team must stop Black Adam and his minions before it's too late.

The movie features a mix of action, adventure, and humor, with plenty of nods to classic comic book characters and storylines. The animation is vibrant and engaging, bringing the world of the Justice Society to life in a way that feels both nostalgic and fresh.

Throughout the film, the heroes face numerous challenges and setbacks, but ultimately, they work together to defeat Black Adam and save the world from destruction. In the end, the Justice Society emerges victorious, having saved countless lives and proved themselves as true champions of justice.

Overall, Justice Society: World War II is a thrilling and entertaining ride that celebrates the spirit of teamwork and heroism. With its richly detailed world-building and memorable characters, it's a must-see for fans of superhero movies and comic books alike.

overview: Tom and Anna Wright, a young American couple, fall into severe debt while renovating Anna's family home in London. As the couple faces the loss of their dream to have a house and start a family, they discover that the tenant in the apartment below them is dead, and he's left behind a stash of cash—$400,000 worth. Though initially hesitant, Tom and Anna decide that the plan is simple: all they have to do is quietly take the money and use only what's necessary to get them out of debt. But when they start spending the money and can't seem to stop, they find themselves the target of a deadly adversary—the thief who stole it—and that's when very bad things start happening to good people.
tagline: Money changes everything
title: Good People
plot:
Good People, released in some countries as Getaway 2, is a 2014 American action thriller film directed by Henrik Ruben Genz and written by Kelly Masterson, based on Marcus Sakey's 2008 novel of the same name. James Franco and Kate Hudson star as Tom and Anna Wright, an American couple in London who fall deep into debt while renovating a family home, with Omar Sy as the French heroin dealer Khan, Tom Wilkinson as Detective Inspector John Halden, Anna Friel as Anna's friend Sarah, Sam Spruell as Jack Witkowski and Diarmaid Murtagh as his accomplice Marshall.

Four men rob Khan of his drugs and money, but as they leave, Ben Tuttle shoots his partner Bobby and escapes with the entire haul, while Witkowski and Marshall flee empty-handed. Meanwhile, Tom and Anna, in debt and trying without success to have a baby, find their noisy downstairs tenant, Ben, dead of an apparent heroin overdose. Clearing his flat, they discover £220,000 hidden above a ceiling tile and, after some debate, spend it, Tom on paying off the house and Anna on fertility treatment. Detective Halden, who seems to connect Ben's death with that of his own daughter, suspects they are hiding something and starts following them. Witkowski kills Ben's cousin to learn Ben's address. Khan warns Tom that he must choose between him and Witkowski, and when Tom refuses, Witkowski tortures him for the money's location until Halden's arrival drives the criminals away. Because Witkowski has contacts inside the police, Halden proposes using the Wrights as bait in an unofficial operation. At the arranged money drop, Witkowski recognizes Halden as a policeman and Marshall shoots him, though a bulletproof vest saves his life, and the Wrights flee with the cash while Khan, believing he has been played, abandons them. Witkowski then takes Sarah and her baby hostage, and the Wrights agree to meet him at the house they had been renovating, which they rig with traps. Witkowski falls through the floor and Tom drives nails through Marshall's feet before Khan's men also arrive. In the chaos, Sarah and the baby escape, Khan kills Witkowski, Marshall's shot kills Khan, and Halden shoots Marshall as he is choking Anna. As the house burns down, the Wrights move out of their flat, and Anna tells Tom that she is pregnant.

Shot at Shepperton Studios and in London from June 2013, Good People was released in select cinemas and on demand on 26 September 2014. It was poorly received, with a 12% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

overview: In the midst of the wedding princess Miroslava is kidnapped by a dragon and carried away into his castle on the remote island. Mira left everything behind in the past - family, friends and groom. Now the only things she had were a stone cage and a mysterious young man named Arman ... but who is he and what is he doing on that island? Miroslava will know the truth too late: loving a dragon will reveal the bitter truth - love is scary.
title: I Am Dragon
plot:
I Am Dragon (Russian: On – drakon, "He's a Dragon"), released in Germany as Dragon: Love Is a Scary Tale, is a 2015 Russian 3D romantic fantasy adventure written and directed by Indar Dzhendubaev and produced by Timur Bekmambetov's company Bazelevs. Loosely based on The Ritual, a 1996 fantasy novel by Marina and Sergey Dyachenko, it is set in an invented world blending Kievan Rus' with Scandinavian, Celtic and Eastern traditions. Maria Poezzhaeva and Matvey Lykov play the leads. After a Moscow premiere on November 24, 2015, Bazelevs Distribution released it in Russia on December 3, 2015.

For generations villagers appeased a fearsome dragon by offering it maidens, until a knight whose beloved had been taken slew the beast; afterward the sacrificial rite became a wedding ceremony. Years later Princess Miroslava, or Mira, whose father and sister Yaroslava consider her childish, is placed on a boat in her bridal gown and drawn across the water toward Igor, the Dragon Slayer's grandson. As his people sing the old ritual song, a dragon, long thought dead, snatches her away to its island. In a cave she meets a guardian creature and a young man who cannot recall his name; she calls him Arman, then learns that he is the dragon himself, living as a human but sometimes changing against his will and losing control.

Arman explains that he chose to remain human until the Dragon Slayer killed his father, when grief turned him into a dragon carrying the memories of his ancestors. He hides in the cave whenever he senses a transformation, but the wedding song had changed him too quickly. Mira teaches him to live as a person and they fall in love, while an enchantment, which reveals the island only to those loved by someone there, keeps the timid Igor lost in fog. Learning she plans to flee, Arman reveals that dragons burned the captured maidens and that new dragons were born from their ashes, and he sends her home. On her second wedding day Mira realizes she loves him, abandons Igor and sings the song. The dragon seizes her, but her fearless declaration of love lets Arman master his dragon form, and years later they live on the island with their daughter.

Reviews were mixed, with praise from Film.ru and The Hollywood Reporter's Russian critic and scorn from the Russian Gazette. It earned only about $1.7 million in Russia against an $18 million budget, but its success in China made it the top-grossing Russian film internationally in 2016.

original_title: Winnie the Pooh: Springtime with Roo
overview: Spring has sprung, and baby Roo is excited to get out and explore and make new friends. But Rabbit seems preoccupied with spring cleaning, instead of embracing his usual role of playing Easter Bunny. Leave it to Roo to show Rabbit -- through love -- that it's more important who you love and not who's in charge.
title: Winnie the Pooh: Springtime with Roo
plot:
Winnie the Pooh: Springtime with Roo is a heartwarming animated film that explores the joys of childhood, friendship, and the beauty of nature. The movie follows the adventures of Winnie the Pooh and his young friend Roo as they explore the Hundred Acre Wood during the spring season.

At its core, the film is a celebration of the simple pleasures in life, such as playing in the sunshine, watching flowers bloom, and enjoying quality time with loved ones. The story is filled with moments of wonder and curiosity, as Roo discovers the world around him and learns valuable lessons about responsibility, empathy, and the importance of friendship.

The movie also touches on themes of growth and change, as Roo navigates the challenges of growing up and becoming more independent. Pooh, being the lovable but slightly forgetful bear that he is, provides a steady source of comfort and guidance for his young friend, teaching him valuable lessons about patience, kindness, and the value of slowing down.

Throughout the film, the characters' interactions are infused with a sense of playfulness and humor, making it a delightful watch for both children and adults. The movie's use of vibrant colors and stunning animation brings the Hundred Acre Wood to life in a way that is both visually stunning and endearing.

Overall, Winnie the Pooh: Springtime with Roo is a charming film that celebrates the beauty of childhood, the importance of friendship, and the simple joys of life.

overview: Maggie Peyton, the new owner of Number 53 - the free-wheelin' Volkswagen bug with a mind of its own - puts the car through its paces on the road to becoming a NASCAR competitor.
tagline: Start your engines...
title: Herbie Fully Loaded
plot:
Herbie: Fully Loaded is a 2005 American comedy film directed by Angela Robinson and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie stars Lindsay Lohan, Steve Coogan, and Bobby Cannavale.

The story begins with Maggie Peyton (Lindsay Lohan), a young woman who dreams of becoming a professional racing driver. However, her father, Ray Peyton (Bobby Cannavale), disapproves of her ambitions and wants her to focus on finding a husband instead. Maggie's life takes a turn when she meets Herbie, a Volkswagen Beetle with a mind of its own.

Herbie is an anthropomorphic car who was once owned by a young boy named Larry Stoddard. After the boy's death, Herbie was left alone and eventually found his way to Ray Peyton's garage. Maggie discovers Herbie and forms a bond with him, realizing that he has a unique personality and can help her achieve her racing dreams.

As Maggie and Herbie spend more time together, they begin to develop a strong connection. Herbie becomes Maggie's confidant and partner in crime, helping her navigate the world of professional racing. However, their relationship is put to the test when Ray Peyton discovers that Maggie has been spending time with Herbie and tries to take him away from her.

Despite the challenges, Maggie and Herbie continue to work together, and their partnership becomes more successful. They enter a series of racing competitions, including the Indianapolis 500, where they face off against other drivers and teams.

Throughout the movie, Maggie and Herbie's relationship evolves, and they learn valuable lessons about trust, loyalty, and believing in oneself. In the end, Maggie and Herbie emerge victorious at the Indianapolis 500, and Ray Peyton finally accepts his daughter's passion for racing.

The film features a mix of action, comedy, and heartwarming moments, making it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages. The movie also explores themes of female empowerment, self-discovery, and the importance of following one's dreams.

Overall, Herbie: Fully Loaded is a fun and entertaining film that celebrates the spirit of racing and the power of friendship between humans and animals.

overview: In the Sahara desert, a sandstorm batters a deserted drilling station. A security patrolman, battles through the high winds to investigate why all contact with the station has been lost. Originally built for gas exploration, and then abandoned, the site had recently been taken over by a multi-national research team intent on drilling deeper into the earth’s crust than ever before.
tagline: Lead us not into temptation but deliver us from evil.
title: Nine Miles Down
plot:
Nine Miles Down is a 2009 horror film inspired by the "Well to Hell", an urban legend widely circulated in the 1990s, which claimed that Russian scientists had drilled so deep that they broke through into hell and recorded the screams of the damned. An international co-production between the United Kingdom, Hungary and the United States, it was the last feature film credit for the writer Everett De Roche. The cast includes Adrian Paul, Kate Nauta, Meredith Ostrom and Amanda Douge.

Jack Jackmann, a former police officer working as an inspector for the energy company GNE, arrives in a sandstorm at the Jevel Afra drilling site, a remote station in the Sahara whose 25 staff, led by Professor Borman, have not been heard from for days. He finds the base deserted, with signs of a struggle, Arabic messages written in blood on the walls and a ritually sacrificed jackal. Video records show that Borman set up the dig to investigate an air pocket nine miles underground and that the scientists then became increasingly paranoid. When the storm clears, Jack meets Dr. Jenny "JC" Christensen, the only scientist left, who tells him that Borman was murdered by the chief geologist and that another scientist died of a heart attack. Ordered to stay put, Jack grows suspicious of JC, who does not appear in any of the team's records and tries to steal his vehicle and explains that Borman falsified her details because the budget allowed no separate women's quarters. JC recounts that the drill's microphones had picked up what sounded like human screams, after which the terrified crew began seeing dead loved ones and turning violent. Jack, too, begins to hallucinate. Over his birthday dinner he tells her how his wife killed herself and their two children six years earlier, and the two sleep together, but his torment worsens. Convinced that JC is a demon, he finds human remains in the cesspit, attacks her, hears Borman's hidden recording suggesting they released the Devil, and finally wounds her and sets the base ablaze before a GNE rescue team evacuates them. In hospital, officials confirm JC's account: gas released from the cavity caused victims to confuse reality with memory and imagination, and JC was less affected because of her separate quarters. Jack's paranoia nonetheless returns, and after trying to kill JC he is left on the brink of suicide, haunted by his dead wife's laughter.

Ain't It Cool News called it a pleasant surprise that lives up to its promising concept.

overview: The story follows Carol Danvers as she becomes one of the universe’s most powerful heroes when Earth is caught in the middle of a galactic war between two alien races. Set in the 1990s, Captain Marvel is an all-new adventure from a previously unseen period in the history of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
tagline: Higher. Further. Faster.
title: Captain Marvel
plot:
Captain Marvel is a 2019 superhero film produced by Marvel Studios and directed by Anna Boden and Ryan Fleck. The movie follows the story of Carol Danvers, an Air Force pilot who becomes one of the most powerful heroes in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

The film begins with Carol Danvers (played by Brie Larson) as a young Air Force pilot during the 1990s. She is part of a secret government program called S.H.I.E.L.D., which is experimenting with the power of Kree technology, an alien energy source that enhances human abilities. During a mission to rescue a group of hostages from an alien ship, Carol's plane is attacked by the Kree, and she is exposed to the energy.

The attack leaves Carol severely injured, but also imbues her with incredible powers, including superhuman strength, speed, agility, and durability. She becomes one of the most powerful beings in the universe, capable of flying and wielding energy blasts.

As Carol awakens from her coma, she discovers that she has become a superhero known as Captain Marvel. She is recruited by Nick Fury (played by Samuel L. Jackson), who reveals to her that she is not human but rather an alien hybrid, the result of a Kree-human experiment.

Carol soon learns that the Kree have been at war with the Skrulls, another alien species, for centuries. The Skrulls, led by Talos (played by Ben Mendelsohn), are seeking to invade Earth and assimilate its inhabitants into their own species. Nick Fury reveals that Carol's powers make her a key player in the battle against the Skrulls.

As Captain Marvel, Carol teams up with Nick Fury and his team to stop the Skrulls' invasion. Along the way, she meets Goose (played by a Flerken), a small, shapeshifting alien creature that becomes her loyal companion.

The film's plot thickens as Carol discovers that Talos is actually a Skrull who has been working with S.H.I.E.L.D. to gather intelligence on the Kree and Skrulls. He reveals that he has been searching for Carol, who is the key to unlocking the secrets of the Kree-human experiment.

As the battle between the Skrulls and the Kree reaches its climax, Captain Marvel must confront her own identity and the true nature of her powers. In a thrilling showdown, she faces off against Talos and his minions, using her powers to save the world from destruction.

In the end, Carol Danvers emerges as one of the most powerful heroes in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, ready to take on new challenges and defend the Earth against any threat that may arise. The film concludes with a post-credits scene setting up the events of Avengers: Endgame, where Captain Marvel plays a crucial role in the battle against Thanos.

Overall, Captain Marvel is an action-packed, visually stunning film that explores themes of identity, power, and belonging. Brie Larson shines as Carol Danvers, bringing depth and nuance to the character's journey from humble Air Force pilot to superhero icon.

original_title: Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy
overview: It's the 1970s and San Diego anchorman Ron Burgundy is the top dog in local TV, but that's all about to change when ambitious reporter Veronica Corningstone arrives as a new employee at his station.
tagline: They bring you the news so you don't have to get it yourself.
title: Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy
plot:
Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy is a comedy film that explores several themes, including:

1. **Masculinity and Toxic Masculinity**: The movie pokes fun at traditional masculine norms, particularly in the 1970s newsroom setting. Ron Burgundy (Will Ferrell) embodies a caricature of machismo, which is later revealed to be a facade hiding his own insecurities and vulnerabilities.

2. **Friendship and Camaraderie**: Despite their differences, the news team forms a strong bond, showcasing the importance of male friendships in the face of adversity. The characters' relationships with each other drive the plot and provide comedic moments.

3. **Self-Discovery and Growth**: As Ron navigates his personal life and career, he undergoes significant growth, learning to balance his ego with empathy and understanding. This transformation is a key aspect of the film's narrative.

4. **Feminism and Empowerment**: The movie features a strong female lead in Veronica Corningstone (Christina Applegate), who challenges Ron's dominance and pushes him out of his comfort zone. Her character serves as a catalyst for Ron's growth and helps him develop a more nuanced understanding of himself and others.

5. **Satire and Social Commentary**: Anchorman uses humor to comment on various social issues, including sexism, racism, and the objectification of women. The film's satire is often biting and irreverent, making it a commentary on the societal norms of the 1970s.

6. **Nostalgia and Period Piece**: The movie is set in the 1970s, and its nostalgic value is a significant aspect of its appeal. The film's attention to period detail and its celebration of retro culture add to its charm and humor.

Overall, Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy is a comedy that uses satire, absurdity, and heart to explore themes of masculinity, friendship, self-discovery, feminism, and social commentary.

overview: Frank Corvin, ‘Hawk’ Hawkins, Jerry O'Neill and ‘Tank’ Sullivan were hotdog members of Project Daedalus, the Air Force's test program for space travel, but their hopes were dashed in 1958 with the formation of NASA and the use of trained chimps. They blackmail their way into orbit when Russia's mysterious ‘Ikon’ communications satellite's orbit begins to degrade and threatens to crash to Earth.
tagline: Space will never be the same.
title: Space Cowboys
plot:
Space Cowboys is a 2000 American science fiction film directed by Clint Eastwood, starring Clint Eastwood, Tommy Lee Jones, Donald Sutherland, James Garner, and Scott Glenn.

The main themes of Space Cowboys include:

1. **Friendship and camaraderie**: The movie highlights the strong bond between the four main characters, who were once NASA astronauts but are now retired. They embark on a mission to repair a Soviet satellite, which becomes a catalyst for their reunion and rekindling of their friendship.
2. **Ageism and relevance**: As the astronauts navigate their way through space, they face challenges that make them question whether they're still relevant in today's fast-paced world. The film explores the theme of ageism, as the characters struggle to adapt to new technology and societal expectations.
