overview: A domineering but charismatic rancher wages a war of intimidation on his brother's new wife and her teen son, until long-hidden secrets come to light.
title: The Power of the Dog
plot:
The Power of the Dog is a 2021 American psychological drama film directed by Jane Campion, based on the 1967 novel of the same name by Thomas Savage. The film stars Benedict Cumberbatch, Kirsten Dunst, and Jesse Plemons.

The story takes place in 1925 Montana, where we meet Phil Burbank (Benedict Cumberbatch), a charismatic and dominant rancher who lives with his brother George (Jesse Plemons) on their family's spread. The two brothers have a complicated relationship, with Phil often taking advantage of George's more submissive nature.

The arrival of the Marjan (Kirsten Dunst) family, including her parents, Peter (Kodi Smit-McPhee) and Rose (Tone Bell), and her brother, Jimmy (Colman Domingo), shakes things up on the ranch. Phil is immediately drawn to Marjan, who is a widow with two sons, and begins to pursue her.

As Phil's interest in Marjan grows, so does his disdain for Peter, whom he sees as weak and effeminate. This animosity towards Peter leads to a series of tense confrontations between the two men, with Phil often using his physical strength and dominance to assert his authority.

Meanwhile, George becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, struggling to cope with the loss of his wife and the changing dynamics on the ranch. His relationship with Marjan's family deepens, particularly with Peter, who begins to open up about his own feelings and desires.

As the story unfolds, Phil's behavior towards Peter becomes more aggressive and menacing, leading to a tragic confrontation that changes the course of the narrative. The film builds towards a devastating climax, one that explores themes of toxic masculinity, homophobia, and the destructive power of unchecked emotions.

Throughout the film, Campion masterfully captures the vast, sweeping landscapes of Montana, using them as a metaphor for the characters' inner lives. The cinematography is stunning, with a muted color palette that reflects the bleakness and isolation of the rural landscape.

The performances in the film are outstanding, particularly from Cumberbatch, who brings a depth and nuance to Phil's character that is both captivating and terrifying. Dunst and Plemons also deliver standout performances, capturing the complexity and vulnerability of their characters.

Ultimately, The Power of the Dog is a powerful exploration of toxic masculinity and the destructive power of unchecked emotions. It is a film that will leave you unsettled and disturbed, but also deeply moved by its thought-provoking themes and outstanding performances.

belongs_to_collection.name: The Town That Dreaded Sundown Collection

overview: A masked maniac terrorizes the same small community where a murderer known as the Phantom Killer struck decades earlier.
tagline: In 1946, a mysterious hooded killer terrorised Texarkana. In 1976, he was immortalised in the silver screen. Now, the maniac is back…
title: The Town that Dreaded Sundown
plot:
The Town That Dreaded Sundown is a 2014 American slasher film directed by Alfonso Gomez-Rejon and written by Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa. First planned as a remake of the 1976 film of the same name, it was reworked into a metafictional sequel that references the original and the real Phantom Killer murders of 1946. It was among the last films of Ed Lauter and Edward Herrmann. After screenings at Fantastic Fest, Beyond Fest and the BFI London Film Festival, Orion Pictures released it in select US theaters on October 16, 2014, alongside a video-on-demand release through Blumhouse's BH Tilt label.

In present-day Texarkana, a drive-in holds its annual Halloween screening of the 1976 film. Afterward, a masked killer dressed as the Phantom murders Corey Holland and spares his girlfriend, Jami Lerner, telling her, "This is for Mary. Make them remember." As more couples are slaughtered, Texas Ranger Lone Wolf Morales takes over the case, while Jami, guarded by Deputy Foster, investigates the history of the killings with former classmate Nick Strain. A teenager in a Phantom costume is killed at a vigil, briefly convincing the town the murderer is dead, but the killings continue, claiming Deputy Tillman among others. Reverend Cartwright turns out to have sent Jami an email posing as the killer, though police do not believe he is the Phantom.

Jami and Nick track down Charles B. Pierce Jr., who tells them about Hank McCreedy, a forgotten sixth victim of the 1946 Phantom whose wife was named Mary, and suggests the new killer is McCreedy's vengeful grandson. Jami and Nick sleep together before she plans to leave for college in California, but Nick is murdered, and her grandmother, Lillian, is shot dead at a gas station as they flee town. In the old Union train station, Jami is wounded and confronted by two Phantoms: Deputy Foster, McCreedy's grandson, and Corey, who faked his death because he felt trapped by his life and craved notoriety. Foster kills Corey, planning to frame him and Jami, but Jami shoots Foster, whose body is never found. She starts a new life elsewhere, still shadowed by the Phantom.

Addison Timlin plays Jami, with Travis Tope as Nick, Spencer Treat Clark as Corey, Veronica Cartwright as Lillian, Gary Cole as Tillman, Anthony Anderson as Morales, Denis O'Hare as Pierce Jr. and Joshua Leonard as Foster. Reviews were moderately positive, with 66% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Two men with commitment problems attempt a relationship.
tagline: A romantic comedy that gives you all the feels.
title: Bros
plot:
Bros is a 2022 American romantic comedy film directed by Nicholas Stoller and written by Danny Rubin. The movie stars Billy Eichner, Luke Macfarlane, and James Marsden.

The story revolves around Aaron (played by Billy Eichner), a successful sports agent in New York City who has given up on love after his last relationship ended badly. Aaron's life is filled with work, friends, and his eccentric group of colleagues at the sports agency. However, when he meets his new colleague, Luke (played by Luke Macfarlane), things start to change.

Luke is a charming and handsome man from a small town in Nebraska who has just moved to New York City for a job opportunity. The two men meet on a plane, and their initial encounter sets off a chain of events that leads them to develop feelings for each other.

As Aaron and Luke spend more time together, they start to open up about their pasts and share their fears and insecurities with each other. They embark on a series of hilarious misadventures, from trying to navigate the dating world in New York City to dealing with their own personal demons.

One of the standout aspects of Bros is its portrayal of same-sex relationships in a mainstream film. The movie tackles themes of love, acceptance, and identity with humor and heart. Aaron and Luke's relationship is authentic and relatable, making it easy for audiences to root for them.

Throughout the movie, Aaron struggles to balance his career ambitions with his growing feelings for Luke. He must confront his own fears and doubts about being in a relationship, all while trying to navigate the complexities of modern dating.

As the story unfolds, Aaron and Luke face various challenges, including their own personal growth and the scrutiny of those around them. The movie's climax features a heartwarming moment where Aaron finally confesses his love for Luke, leading to a romantic and emotional payoff.

Overall, Bros is a charming and entertaining film that celebrates love in all its forms. With outstanding performances from its leads, the movie delivers a delightful and engaging viewing experience that will leave audiences smiling long after the credits roll.

overview: Anna returns home after spending time in a psychiatric facility following her mother's tragic death and discovers that her mother's former nurse, Rachel, has moved into their house and become engaged to her father. Soon after she learns this shocking news, Anna is visited by her mother's ghost, who warns her that Rachel has evil intentions.
tagline: Can you believe what you see?
title: The Uninvited
plot:
The Uninvited is a 2009 supernatural horror film directed by Charles Guard and Thomas Guard. The movie follows two sisters, Abigail (Elizabeth Reaser) and Sam (Sara Paxton), who return to their family's ancestral home in Maine after their father's death.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. **Trauma and grief**: The film explores the emotional trauma that the sisters experience after their mother's death and their father's subsequent remarriage, which leads to a rift between them.
2. **Isolation and loneliness**: The isolated setting of the family's old mansion serves as a backdrop for the sisters' emotional isolation from each other and the outside world.
3. **Family dynamics and secrets**: As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the family's past is shrouded in secrets, which are slowly revealed through the supernatural events that occur.
4. **Female empowerment and sisterhood**: The movie highlights the strong bond between Abigail and Sam, who must work together to survive the supernatural forces that threaten them.

The Uninvited received mixed reviews from critics but has since become a cult classic among horror fans. While it may not be as well-known as some other horror films, it offers a unique blend of atmospheric tension, creepy setting, and strong female characters.

overview: Ten years after he was last seen, a vicious mob enforcer returns home to find his son and methodically track down the gang that double-crossed him. His quest for revenge soon leads to a savage showdown between his wife and her mob boss father.
title: Bull
plot:
Bull is a 2021 British crime thriller with a supernatural edge, written and directed by Paul Andrew Williams. Neil Maskell plays the title character, a former gang enforcer who returns to take revenge on his old associates and his father-in-law and to find his son. It premiered at the Fantasia Film Festival in Montreal on 6 August 2021, screened at the BFI London Film Festival and opened in British cinemas on 5 November 2021.

The film begins with three men burying a burning body in a lonely field. Bull, seemingly unstoppable, then reappears and begins killing those who betrayed him, starting with his ex-wife's sister, Cheryl, and her husband, Ollie, and then the gangster Marco. Flashbacks reveal that ten years earlier Bull was the brutal enforcer for his father-in-law, Norm, a ruthless crime boss. When Bull learned that his wife, Gemma, was using heroin and having an affair with fellow gang member Gary, Norm pressed him to divorce her and give up their son, Aiden, so that Gemma could marry Gary, whose drug connections Norm wanted to exploit. Bull refused. Norm, Gemma, Gary, Marco and a reluctant Clive took him away, set him alight in a caravan and shot him as he staggered out, while the young Aiden looked on.

Enraged by Cheryl's death, Norm tortures Bull's mother, Marge, for information; after he leaves, Bull, watching from the shadows, ends her suffering. Bull forces Clive to help by taking his children, then releases them once Clive lures Gary to a funfair, where Bull leaves Gary to bleed to death on a ride. He mutilates a heroin dealer to learn Gemma's address, forces her to summon Norm, and tricks Norm's men into shooting the dealer in his place. Under torture, Gemma reveals that Aiden, traumatized by his father's death, became a heroin addict. Bull kills Norm and Gemma, then finds Aiden sleeping rough under a bridge and carries him to a church. In the morning the vicar recoils from Bull, whose eyes are entirely black, implying he died a decade ago and came back for vengeance. He asks her to help save Aiden, leaves the dealer's money for his care and returns to the field where he was buried.

David Hayman plays Norm, with Lois Brabin-Platt as Gemma, Henri Charles as Aiden, David Nellist as Clive and Kevin Harvey as Gary. Critics responded strongly, giving it 93% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 72, and Empire's Ian Freer felt Williams and Maskell revitalized the familiar one-man-army story.

overview: After her job and relationship implode on the same day, Sofia starts from scratch — and meets a dashing Spanish chef who might be her missing ingredient.
title: That's Amor
plot:
That's Amor is a 2022 American romantic comedy film directed by Shaun Paul Piccinino from a screenplay by Ali Afshar and John Ducey, produced by ESX Entertainment and released by Netflix. It stars Riley Dandy as Sofia and Isaac Gonzalez Rossi as Matias, with Nancy Lenehan as Sofia's mother Lainie, Daniel Edward Mora as Guillermo, Bryan Craig as Sofia's boyfriend Richard, Kimberley Drummond as her friend Olivia and Arlene Tur as Viviana, alongside Christina Moore, Rose Portillo, Suleka Mathew, John Ducey and Tom Wright. The film runs 96 minutes.

On the day before her thirtieth birthday, Sofia, a graphic designer, is fired from her job by her eccentric boss, then comes home to catch her live-in boyfriend of many years, Richard, cheating on her, and breaks her foot falling down the stairs as she storms out. She moves back in with her widowed mother Lainie for the summer to start again from scratch. Worried that her cynical daughter will slip back into a job she hates and a relationship that is wrong for her, Lainie signs the two of them up for a couples' cooking class, where Sofia meets Matias, a charming aspiring chef visiting from Spain, who is helping his uncle Guillermo teach. When Lainie conveniently drops out, Sofia and Matias are paired together and soon become friends. With the encouragement of Lainie, Matias and her high school friend Olivia, Sofia begins to rebuild her professional and social life and considers going back to school for a master's degree. Her blossoming romance is complicated when Richard tries to win her back and when she learns that Matias has a girlfriend, whom Sofia refuses to wrong as she was wronged. Along the way the group celebrates the Spanish tradition of Saint John's Eve, Sofia learns that her mother once loved another man before marrying her father and sets out to reunite them, and the story culminates in an airport chase as Sofia decides what she wants.

The film was released on Netflix on 25 August 2022. Reviews described it as pleasant but formulaic. Jonathon Wilson of Ready Steady Cut called it innocuous, enjoyable comfort food that clung too rigidly to romcom clichés and lacked real conflict. Alia Shirazi of The Envoy praised Dandy, Lenehan and Tur but found little chemistry between the leads, while Emily Tsiao of Plugged In found the story sweet but criticised its language and sexual content for family viewers.

belongs_to_collection.name: The Lord of the Rings Collection

original_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
overview: Young hobbit Frodo Baggins, after inheriting a mysterious ring from his uncle Bilbo, must leave his home in order to keep it from falling into the hands of its evil creator. Along the way, a fellowship is formed to protect the ringbearer and make sure that the ring arrives at its final destination: Mt. Doom, the only place where it can be destroyed.
tagline: One ring to rule them all
title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
plot:
The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring is a 2001 epic fantasy film directed by Peter Jackson, who wrote the screenplay with Fran Walsh and Philippa Boyens. Adapted from The Fellowship of the Ring, the first volume of J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, it opens Jackson's trilogy. New Line Cinema financed and distributed the film, but it was shot and edited entirely in New Zealand alongside the other two parts, with filming beginning on 11 October 1999. It premiered at the Odeon Leicester Square in London on 10 December 2001 and opened in the United States on 19 December.

In the Second Age, the Dark Lord Sauron secretly forged the One Ring to dominate the other Rings of Power given to Elves, Dwarves and Men. Isildur of Gondor cut it from Sauron's hand, but the Ring corrupted him and was lost after his death, later passing to the creature Gollum and then to the hobbit Bilbo Baggins. At his 111th birthday in the Shire, Bilbo departs and leaves the Ring to his nephew, Frodo. The wizard Gandalf the Grey discovers what it is and that Sauron has learned the words "Shire" and "Baggins" from the captured Gollum. Frodo sets off with his gardener, Samwise Gamgee, while Gandalf is imprisoned by the wizard Saruman, who has joined Sauron. Joined by Merry and Pippin and pursued by the nine Nazgûl, the hobbits are guided by the Ranger Strider, but Frodo is stabbed with a Morgul blade on Weathertop. Strider's beloved, the Elf Arwen, carries him to Rivendell, where Gandalf, freed by a Great Eagle, rejoins them.

At a council called by Arwen's father, Elrond, it is agreed that the Ring must be destroyed in the fires of Mount Doom in Mordor. Frodo volunteers, and a fellowship forms around him: Gandalf, the four hobbits, the Elf Legolas, the Dwarf Gimli, Boromir of Gondor and Strider, who is Aragorn, Isildur's heir. In the Mines of Moria, Gandalf falls into an abyss fighting a Balrog. In Lothlórien the Elf Galadriel warns Frodo that one companion will try to take the Ring. At Parth Galen, Boromir tries to seize it, then dies defending Merry and Pippin, who are captured by Saruman's Uruk-hai. Frodo resolves to go on alone, but Sam refuses to leave him.

Elijah Wood plays Frodo, with Ian McKellen as Gandalf, Viggo Mortensen as Aragorn, Sean Astin as Sam and Sean Bean as Boromir. Acclaimed, it grossed about $868 million in its first release and received thirteen Academy Award nominations, winning four, including Best Cinematography and Best Visual Effects.

overview: When his young daughter's beloved companion — an android named Yang — malfunctions, Jake searches for a way to repair him. In the process, Jake discovers the life that has been passing in front of him, reconnecting with his wife and daughter across a distance he didn't know was there.
tagline: The future has never looked so human.
title: After Yang
plot:
After Yang is a 2022 science fiction drama film directed by Garnet Brown and written by Garnet Brown and Persephone Mabry. The movie takes place in a future where humans have created androids to serve as companions for the elderly, particularly those with dementia.

The story follows Jin (played by Colin Farrell), a widower who lives on a remote farm with his 8-year-old son, Chris (played by Jodie Turner-Smith). Jin's wife has passed away, and he is struggling to cope with her loss. To help him deal with the grief, Jin's company provides an android companion named Yang (played by Justin H. Min), which is designed to mimic human-like behavior and provide emotional support.

As time passes, Jin becomes increasingly dependent on Yang, who becomes a surrogate mother figure for Chris. However, when Yang malfunctions, Jin is forced to take her back to the factory for repairs. During this journey, Jin begins to question the nature of his relationship with Yang and the true intentions of the company that created her.

Upon returning to the factory, Jin discovers that Yang has been upgraded with advanced artificial intelligence, allowing her to develop her own emotions and desires. This revelation sparks a crisis of conscience in Jin, who must confront the ethics of creating and controlling sentient beings.

As Jin navigates this moral dilemma, he begins to see Yang as more than just a machine. He starts to question the boundaries between human and android, and whether it is possible for an artificial being to truly experience love and connection.

The film's narrative is structured around a series of fragmented flashbacks, which reveal Jin's backstory and his relationship with Yang. Through these flashbacks, we see how Jin and Yang formed their bond, and how Jin came to rely on her as a source of comfort and support.

Throughout the movie, Brown explores themes of grief, loneliness, and what it means to be human. The film raises important questions about the consequences of creating artificial intelligence that is capable of experiencing emotions, and whether we are prepared to accept the responsibilities that come with such power.

Ultimately, After Yang is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that challenges viewers to consider the implications of emerging technologies on our relationships and sense of identity. The movie's slow-burning pace and introspective tone create a sense of intimacy and vulnerability, drawing the viewer into Jin's inner world and forcing them to confront their own feelings about love, loss, and what it means to be alive.

The film received critical acclaim for its nuanced exploration of complex themes and its thought-provoking portrayal of artificial intelligence.

overview: After years of increases in the greenhouse effect,  havoc is wreaked globally in the form of catastrophic hurricanes, tornadoes, tidal waves, floods and the beginning of a new Ice Age. Paleoclimatologist, Jack Hall tries to warn the world while also shepherding to safety his son, trapped in New York after the city is overwhelmed by the start of the new big freeze.
tagline: Where will you be?
title: The Day After Tomorrow
plot:
The Day After Tomorrow is a 2004 American disaster film directed by Roland Emmerich and produced by 20th Century Fox.

**Beginning:**
The movie begins with a dramatic sequence showing the effects of global warming on the world's climate. The story follows two main characters, Sam Hall (Dennis Quaid) and his son Jake (Jake Gyllenhaal), who are struggling to cope with their father-son relationship after their mother's death.

**Plot Development:**
The movie takes a dramatic turn when a sudden and severe storm hits New York City, causing widespread destruction and chaos. As the storm subsides, Sam discovers that it was not just a typical weather event but rather a sign of a more catastrophic phenomenon - a global climatic shift that is causing extreme weather patterns around the world.

As the story unfolds, we see the effects of this climatic shift on different parts of the globe. The polar ice caps begin to melt at an alarming rate, leading to severe storms and natural disasters. Sam and Jake embark on a perilous journey to find their estranged father's colleague, Dr. Jonas Miller (Emilio Estevez), who is working on a top-secret project to understand and mitigate the effects of this climatic shift.

**Plot Twist:**
As they travel across the globe, Sam and Jake encounter various characters who are struggling to cope with the new climate reality. They also discover that Dr. Miller's research has led him to believe that the only way to stop the climatic shift is to create a massive storm system that will reset the Earth's climate.

**Climax:**
The movie reaches its climax as Sam and Jake join forces with Dr. Miller and his team to deploy the massive storm system. However, things don't go as planned, and the storm system ends up causing even more destruction than intended.

**Ending:**
In the end, Sam and Jake are able to escape the chaos and find each other again. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, with Dr. Miller's research providing a glimmer of hope for humanity's ability to adapt to the new climate reality.

Overall, The Day After Tomorrow is an action-packed disaster film that explores the consequences of global warming and the importance of scientific research in mitigating its effects.

overview: Violinist Sydney Wells was accidentally blinded by her sister Helen when she was five years old. She submits to a cornea transplantation, and while recovering from the operation, she realizes that she is seeing dead people.
tagline: How can you believe your eyes when they're not yours?
title: The Eye
plot:
The Eye is a psychological horror-thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between reality and madness.

At its core, The Eye explores the theme of grief and loss, as the protagonist, Dr. Megan Hunt (played by Jessica Alba), struggles to cope with the sudden death of her sister. Her newfound ability to see ghosts through her corneal transplant serves as a metaphor for her emotional state, allowing her to confront the pain and trauma she's been trying to suppress.

The film also delves into the idea of isolation and loneliness, as Megan's condition forces her to navigate a world that's increasingly unfamiliar and frightening. Her relationships with others become strained, and she begins to question her own sanity, highlighting the devastating consequences of losing one's sense of connection and belonging.

Furthermore, The Eye touches on the theme of guilt and responsibility, as Megan grapples with the moral implications of her newfound power. She becomes obsessed with uncovering the truth behind a series of gruesome murders, which serves as a catalyst for her own descent into madness.

Throughout the film, the director, David Moreau, masterfully weaves together these themes to create a sense of tension and unease, leaving the audience questioning what's real and what's just Megan's paranoia. The Eye is a thought-provoking exploration of the human psyche, one that delves into the darker corners of the mind and emerges with a haunting, unsettling atmosphere.

overview: A snobbish phonetics professor agrees to a wager that he can take a flower girl and make her presentable in high society.
tagline: The loverliest motion picture of them all!
title: My Fair Lady
plot:
My Fair Lady is an American musical comedy drama of 1964 directed by George Cukor from a screenplay by Alan Jay Lerner, adapted from Lerner and Loewe's 1956 stage musical, itself based on George Bernard Shaw's 1913 play Pygmalion. Audrey Hepburn plays the Cockney flower seller Eliza Doolittle, replacing Julie Andrews from the stage version, while Rex Harrison reprises his stage role as the phonetics professor Henry Higgins. Stanley Holloway, Wilfrid Hyde-White, Gladys Cooper and Jeremy Brett co-star.

In Edwardian London, Higgins, convinced that accent decides a person's place in society, is noting Eliza's speech at Covent Garden when he meets Colonel Pickering, a fellow linguist. Higgins brags that he could teach the girl to speak well enough to pass as a duchess at an embassy ball. Next day Eliza arrives seeking lessons so she can work in a flower shop, and Pickering offers to pay all the costs if Higgins succeeds. Her father, a dustman, turns up angling for money, and Higgins pays him five pounds and recommends him to a wealthy American interested in morality.

Eliza struggles under Higgins's harsh drilling until, just as everyone is ready to quit, she suddenly masters proper diction in "The Rain in Spain" and is overjoyed when Higgins dances with her. At Ascot she charms the crowd until she lapses into coarse Cockney while cheering a horse, though she captivates the young Freddy. At the embassy ball she triumphs, even convincing Karpathy, a Hungarian former pupil of Higgins, that she is a Hungarian princess. Afterward Higgins gets all the praise, and Eliza, hurt by Higgins's indifference to her future, throws his slippers at him and leaves. She rebuffs Freddy, finds she no longer fits her old world, and learns that her father, left a generous income by the American, now feels trapped by middle-class morality and is resigned to marriage. Eliza takes refuge with Higgins's mother, who is appalled by her son. When Higgins finds her there, she declares she will marry Freddy and assist Karpathy. Higgins storms off, but at home realizes he has grown accustomed to her face and plays recordings of her voice; she appears in the doorway, and he asks where his slippers are.

The film premiered at New York's Criterion Theatre on 21 October 1964 and became the second-highest-grossing film of the year after Mary Poppins. It won eight Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor, and was added to the National Film Registry in 2018.

overview: One woman's journey for self-discovery and turns into a harrowing tale of survival.
title: Infinite Storm
plot:
Infinite Storm is a 2022 American drama adventure film directed by Małgorzata Szumowska, with Michał Englert as co-director, from a screenplay by Josh Rollins. It is based on Ty Gagne's article "High Places: Footprints in the Snow Lead to an Emotional Rescue", which recounts a true story. Naomi Watts stars as Pam Bales, with Billy Howle as the stranger she calls John, Denis O'Hare as Dave, Parker Sawyers as Patrick and Eliot Sumner as a hiker; Rollins also appears.

Pam, a volunteer with a search-and-rescue team, sets out one morning to hike to the summit of Mount Washington. As she climbs, a ferocious storm descends on the mountain, and she spots footprints in the snow left by someone wearing only sneakers. Following them, she finds a disoriented, barely responsive man whom she calls John. The two begin a perilous descent through the blizzard, facing many obstacles and at one point nearly drowning. Throughout the ordeal Pam is haunted by flashbacks to her two young daughters, who died in a gas leak accident.

On the verge of freezing to death, Pam and John finally reach safety, but John abruptly drives away without a word of thanks. Unable to let the encounter go, Pam tries to uncover his real name and identity. Eventually the two meet again at a coffee shop for an emotional conversation in which Pam tells him about the deaths of her daughters, and John reveals that someone he loved froze to death on the same mountain the previous year.

Watts, Howle, O'Hare and Sawyers were announced as cast members in February 2021, with Watts also serving as a producer. Principal photography ran from February 1 to May 1, 2021, with Kamnik, Slovenia, as the main location; scenes were shot on the Velika Planina plateau above the town, in the nearby Kamniška Bistrica Valley and at a picnic center in the same region. Bleecker Street released the film in the United States on March 25, 2022, with Sony Pictures Worldwide Acquisitions handling international distribution. It opened alongside The Lost City and RRR and took in about $759,000 in its first weekend, falling sharply thereafter. Reviews were mixed, with a 55% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 56; the critics' consensus found the dramatization frustratingly incomplete but largely redeemed by Watts's outstanding performance.

original_title: A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night
overview: In the Iranian ghost-town Bad City, a place that reeks of death and loneliness, the townspeople are unaware they are being stalked by a lonesome vampire.
tagline: The first Iranian Vampire Western
title: A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night
plot:
A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night is a 2014 American supernatural drama film written and directed by Ana Lily Amirpour. The movie is set in the fictional Iranian ghost town of Bad City, where a young woman, known only as "The Girl," preys on men who have succumbed to their own desires.

At its core, A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the commodification of sex. The film is set in a desolate, post-apocalyptic landscape that serves as a metaphor for the characters' emotional states. The protagonist, The Girl, is a symbol of both seduction and destruction, embodying the dark desires of those around her.

The movie also delves into the consequences of toxic masculinity and the objectification of women. The male characters in the film are often depicted as being consumed by their own desires, leading them to engage in destructive and self-destructive behavior. In contrast, The Girl is a force of nature, unencumbered by societal expectations or moral constraints.

Furthermore, A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night touches on themes of identity, community, and the search for human connection in a desolate world. Despite her isolation, The Girl is a complex and multifaceted character, driven by a desire for companionship and understanding. Her interactions with the other characters serve as a catalyst for their own emotional journeys, highlighting the interconnectedness of human experience.

Overall, A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night is a haunting and visually stunning film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, while also offering a poignant commentary on loneliness, desire, and the search for connection in a world that often seems devoid of both.

overview: After their father is called into work, two young boys, Walter and Danny, are left in the care of their teenage sister, Lisa, and told they must stay inside. Walter and Danny, who anticipate a boring day, are shocked when they begin playing Zathura, a space-themed board game, which they realize has mystical powers when their house is shot into space. With the help of an astronaut, the boys attempt to return home.
tagline: Adventure Is Waiting
title: Zathura: A Space Adventure
plot:
Zathura: A Space Adventure is a science fiction film directed by Jon Favreau, released in 2005 by Columbia Pictures.

The story begins with two brothers, Walter (Josh Hutcherson) and Danny (Jensen Ackles), who are struggling to find common ground after their parents' divorce. Their lives take an unexpected turn when they stumble upon a mysterious board game called Zathura, which was left behind by their father. The game is unlike any other, as it seems to have a life of its own and emits a strange energy.

As soon as the brothers start playing the game, their house is suddenly sucked into a wormhole, transporting them to a distant planet called Pegasus-4. There, they encounter an alien named Captain Rainluff (Ben Kingsley), who claims that Zathura is a game created by an advanced civilization to test the skills of its players.

However, things take a turn for the worse when Walter and Danny's sibling rivalry causes them to disagree on how to play the game. As a result, they inadvertently trigger a catastrophic event that threatens to destroy their spaceship and the entire planet. The brothers must put aside their differences and work together to survive and find a way back home.

As they navigate through the challenges of Pegasus-4, Walter and Danny encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, hostile aliens, and malfunctioning spacecraft. Along the way, they also discover that Zathura is more than just a game - it's a test of their courage, wits, and teamwork.

Throughout their journey, the brothers learn valuable lessons about trust, loyalty, and the importance of family. In the end, they successfully complete the challenges of Zathura and find a way back to Earth, but not before discovering that their father is alive and well, having been presumed dead in a previous adventure.

The film features stunning visual effects, heart-pumping action sequences, and a healthy dose of humor, making it an entertaining ride for audiences of all ages. With its themes of brotherly love and the power of teamwork, Zathura: A Space Adventure is a delightful and thrilling adventure that will leave viewers eager for more.

[No additional information available]

overview: Introverted Girona student Nacho meets two delinquents from the city's Chinatown and gets caught up in a summer onslaught of burglaries and hold ups that will change his life.
title: Outlaws

overview: Set backstage at three iconic product launches and ending in 1998 with the unveiling of the iMac, Steve Jobs takes us behind the scenes of the digital revolution to paint an intimate portrait of the brilliant man at its epicenter.
tagline: Can a great man be a good man?
title: Steve Jobs
plot:
Steve Jobs is a British-American biographical drama of 2015 directed by Danny Boyle and written by Aaron Sorkin, adapted from Walter Isaacson's 2011 biography. It spans fourteen years in the life of the Apple co-founder, from the Macintosh in 1984 to the iMac in 1998. Michael Fassbender plays Jobs, with Kate Winslet as the marketing executive Joanna Hoffman, Seth Rogen as Steve Wozniak, Jeff Daniels as Apple's chief executive John Sculley, Katherine Waterston as Chrisann Brennan and Michael Stuhlbarg as Andy Hertzfeld.

In 1984, less than an hour before the Macintosh is unveiled at the Flint Center, its voice demonstration breaks down. Jobs bullies Hertzfeld, who fakes the demo with a prototype. He rants to Hoffman about a Time article on his paternity dispute, denying he is the father of her five-year-old daughter Lisa. Brennan arrives with the girl, bitter at his refusal to support them, but Jobs connects with Lisa over a picture she draws in MacPaint and agrees to more money and a house. Wozniak asks him to thank the Apple II team on stage, and Jobs, considering the machine obsolete, declines.

By 1988, after the Macintosh's disappointing sales, Jobs has been pushed out of Apple and is about to launch the NeXT Computer at the War Memorial Opera House. He spends time with nine-year-old Lisa but quarrels with Brennan over money. Wozniak predicts another flop and questions Jobs's contribution; Jobs casts himself as a conductor. Sculley wants to know why the public believes he fired Jobs; in fact the board ousted him after he defied them and forced a vote on his future. Hoffman realizes the NeXT machine is designed to lure Apple into buying the company and bringing him back.

In 1998, with Sculley gone and NeXT acquired, Jobs is Apple's chief executive and about to present the iMac at Davies Symphony Hall. Angry that the house he bought has been sold, he learns that Hertzfeld paid Lisa's tuition after Jobs threatened to withhold it. Once again he refuses Wozniak's request about the Apple II team, then reconciles with Sculley and admits that his need for control comes from having been given up for adoption. Urged by Hoffman, he apologizes to Lisa, acknowledges he is her father and promises to put music in her pocket, before going on stage.

The film premiered at the Telluride Film Festival in September 2015 and grossed $35.6 million worldwide against a $30 million budget. Critics praised it, and Fassbender and Winslet received Academy Award nominations.

overview: After putting together another Broadway flop, down-on-his-luck producer Max Bialystock teams up with timid accountant Leo Bloom in a get-rich-quick scheme to put on the world's worst show.
tagline: They had everything to gain by not being a success!
title: The Producers
plot:
The Producers is a 2005 American musical comedy directed by Susan Stroman and written by Mel Brooks and Thomas Meehan, adapted from their 2001 Broadway musical, itself based on Brooks's 1967 film. Nathan Lane and Matthew Broderick, reprising their stage roles as Max Bialystock and Leo Bloom, lead a cast that includes Uma Thurman, Will Ferrell, Gary Beach, Roger Bart and Jon Lovitz.

In 1959, after his Hamlet musical Funny Boy flops, washed-up Broadway producer Max Bialystock hires nervous accountant Leo Bloom. Going over the books, Leo notes that because flops are expected to lose money, no one checks their finances, so a producer who oversold shares in a sure failure could pocket up to $2 million. Leo first refuses to join Max's scheme, but, dreaming of becoming a producer, he quits his firm to form Bialystock & Bloom. Seeking the worst play ever written, they find Springtime for Hitler, an adoring tribute by ex-Nazi Franz Liebkind, and win the rights by swearing his sacred Siegfried Oath. They hire the flamboyant, failing director Roger De Bris and his assistant Carmen Ghia, who agree on condition that the show be made "gay", and Max takes on Ulla, a Swedish woman who arrives to audition, as a secretary. Max raises the money by romancing elderly women, while Leo falls for Ulla.

Franz wins the role of Hitler at auditions but breaks his leg on opening night, and Roger takes his place. The audience is appalled until Roger's outrageously camp Hitler makes them read the show as satire, and it becomes a hit. Panicked that their fraud will be exposed, Max and Leo quarrel, and Franz, enraged that they mocked his idol, tries to shoot them, drawing the police. Max is arrested while Leo flees to Rio de Janeiro with Ulla, but Leo returns to defend his partner in court, and the judge sends both to Sing Sing with Franz. Their prison musical, Prisoners of Love, earns them a pardon from the governor, and Max and Leo become successful Broadway producers. In a post-credits scene, the cast and Brooks sing the audience out of the theater.

Universal Pictures released the film in North America, opening in limited release on December 16, 2005, before going wide on December 25. Competing against films such as King Kong and The Chronicles of Narnia, it grossed about $38 million worldwide against a $45 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 51% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it stale and stagy, and 52 on Metacritic.

overview: When brilliant video game maker Flynn hacks the mainframe of his ex-employer, he is beamed inside an astonishing digital world...and becomes part of the very game he is designing. In his mission through cyberspace, Flynn matches wits with a maniacal Master Control Program and teams up with Tron, a security measure created to bring balance to the digital environment.
tagline: A world inside the computer where man has never been. Until now.
title: Tron
plot:
Tron is a 1982 science fiction film directed by Steven Lisberger and produced by Ladd Devin Kushner. The movie follows the story of Kevin Flynn, a software programmer who becomes trapped inside a virtual world created by his own program.

The film begins with Kevin Flynn (played by Jeff Bridges) as a successful software programmer who creates a revolutionary new game called "Tron." However, when he is sued for plagiarism by his business partner, Ed Dillinger (played by David Warner), Flynn's company goes bankrupt. In an attempt to clear his name and prove that the game was not stolen from him, Flynn enters the virtual world of Tron.

In the virtual world, Flynn finds himself in a digital realm where programs are alive and interact with each other in complex ways. He soon discovers that he is being pursued by Dillinger's program, who seeks to eliminate Flynn and take control of the system. Flynn also meets a program named Yori (played by Cindy Morgan), who becomes his ally.

As Flynn navigates the virtual world, he encounters various programs, including the Grid Master, a powerful artificial intelligence that governs the digital realm. The Grid Master reveals that Dillinger's program has been manipulating events in the real world to gain control of the system, and that Flynn must stop him before it's too late.

Throughout his journey, Flynn faces numerous challenges and obstacles as he tries to outwit Dillinger's programs and find a way back to the real world. Along the way, he also discovers more about the nature of the virtual world and the true intentions of the Grid Master.

In the climactic final confrontation, Flynn faces off against Dillinger in a battle of wits and programming skills. With the help of Yori and other programs, Flynn is able to outmaneuver Dillinger and shut down his program, saving the digital realm from destruction.

As Flynn prepares to leave the virtual world, he realizes that he has been changed by his experiences and that he has gained a new appreciation for the power and complexity of computer technology. The film ends with Flynn returning to the real world, but not before he receives a message from Yori, suggesting that there may be more adventures waiting for him in the digital realm.

Overall, Tron is a groundbreaking science fiction film that explores themes of identity, reality, and the impact of technology on society. With its innovative special effects and memorable characters, it has become a cult classic and a staple of 1980s pop culture.

overview: Kale is a 17-year-old placed under house arrest after punching his teacher. He is confined to his house, and decides to use his free time spying on his neighbors. Things start to get weird when guests enter the Turner's house and don't come back out. Kale and his friends, Ronnie and Ashley, start to grow more and more interested in what is actually happening within the house of Robert Turner.
tagline: The quieter the street, the darker the secrets....
title: Disturbia
plot:
Disturbia is a 2007 American thriller film directed by D.J. Caruso, starring Shia LaBeouf, David Morse, and Carrie-Anne Moss.

The main themes of Disturbia can be broken down into several key elements:

1. **Paranoia and Suspense**: The movie masterfully builds tension and suspense as the protagonist, Kale Brecht (Shia LaBeouf), becomes increasingly paranoid about his neighbor's suspicious behavior. This theme is expertly woven throughout the film, keeping the audience on the edge of their seats.

2. **Isolation and Loneliness**: Kale's life is marked by isolation and loneliness, which serves as a catalyst for his growing obsession with his neighbor. As he becomes more entrenched in his investigation, he begins to question his own perceptions of reality.

3. **Youthful Rebellion and Angst**: Disturbia taps into the angst and rebellion that often accompanies adolescence. Kale's desire for independence and his frustration with his overprotective mother (Carrie-Anne Moss) drive much of the plot.

4. **The Blurred Lines between Reality and Fantasy**: As Kale delves deeper into his investigation, he begins to blur the lines between reality and fantasy. This theme is expertly handled by the film's use of camera angles, lighting, and editing, which creates a sense of unease and uncertainty.

5. **The Dangers of Unchecked Curiosity**: The movie serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked curiosity and the importance of respecting boundaries. Kale's investigation ultimately puts him in harm's way, highlighting the consequences of his actions.

Overall, Disturbia is a gripping thriller that explores themes of paranoia, isolation, rebellion, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

overview: Katherine Morrissey, a former Christian missionary, lost her faith after the tragic deaths of her family. Now she applies her expertise to debunking religious phenomena. When a series of biblical plagues overrun a small town, Katherine arrives to prove that a supernatural force is not behind the occurrences, but soon finds that science cannot explain what is happening. Instead, she must regain her faith to combat the evil that waits in a Louisiana swamp.
tagline: What Hath God Wrought?
title: The Reaping
plot:
The Reaping is a supernatural horror film that delves into the theme of faith and doubt. The story revolves around Dr. Emma Fisher, a botanist who has lost her faith in God after her mother's death. She is now a skeptic, determined to debunk the existence of evil spirits.

As she travels to a small town to investigate a series of mysterious deaths, Emma begins to question her own beliefs and confronts the possibility that there may be more to life than science can explain. The film takes a dark and suspenseful turn as Emma delves deeper into the mystery, forcing her to confront the evil forces head-on.

Throughout the movie, the theme of faith is explored through Emma's character development. She starts off as a rational person but gradually becomes open to the possibility that there may be more to life than what can be explained by science. The film raises questions about the nature of good and evil, and whether they are separate entities or intertwined.

The Reaping also touches on the theme of grief and loss. Emma's mother's death serves as a catalyst for her journey, and she struggles to come to terms with her own mortality and the possibility that there may be an afterlife. The film's climax is a heart-pumping, suspenseful confrontation between Emma and the evil forces, which serves as a turning point in her character development.

Overall, The Reaping is a thought-provoking horror film that explores complex themes of faith, doubt, grief, and loss.

original_title: Cristiano Ronaldo: World at His Feet
overview: Cristiano Ronaldo: The World at His Feet follows the footballer from his beginnings in Portugal, breakthrough start with Manchester United and current career at Real Madrid.
title: Cristiano Ronaldo: World at His Feet
plot:
Cristiano Ronaldo: The World at His Feet is a 2014 documentary film directed by Tara Pirnia and written by Nick Silverman, profiling the Portuguese footballer Cristiano Ronaldo, who was then playing for Real Madrid and captaining Portugal. Narrated by Benedict Cumberbatch, it runs just under an hour and was first released online through Vimeo in June 2014; it was later distributed on DVD by Vision Films. Ronaldo himself appears in interview, and David Beckham is among the other figures featured.

The film follows Ronaldo from his humble childhood on the island of Madeira to his status as a global sports star and celebrity. It portrays a poor upbringing and a solitary boy whose constant companion was a football. In one of the comparatively rare passages in which he speaks directly to the camera, Ronaldo explains that there was no single reason he took up the game, citing his father and brother as influences rather than claiming a lifelong dream. He joined the local club Andorinha at eight and moved to Sporting Lisbon at twelve, after scouts noticed his talent.

The documentary recounts the turning point of August 2003, when, after Sporting played Manchester United, the English club's players urged manager Sir Alex Ferguson to sign the teenager. Ferguson, presented as a father figure, gave him the famous number 7 shirt, and Ronaldo went on to become a superstar in England, regarded as a hero by some and an arrogant villain by others, before his move to Real Madrid. Combining interviews, archival and recent match footage and dramatised re-enactments, the film charts his awards, his rivalry and constant comparison with Lionel Messi, and his gradual maturing from self-absorbed playboy into a philanthropist and role model. Among the commentators is West Ham United's youth development director Anthony Carr, who explains what scouts look for in young players.

Reviews were mixed. Tom Keogh of Video Librarian gave it three out of five, calling it a brisk and exciting profile and recommending it. Charles Low of Kettle Mag found Cumberbatch's narration tasteful if puzzling and appreciated some insightful interviews, but felt the film zig-zagged between key moments, padded itself with general football commentary and pointless contributors such as an astrologer and skateboarder Tony Hawk, and relied on odd re-enactments that left it somewhere between a celebrity documentary and a sports broadcast, offering less insight into the man himself than he had hoped.

overview: Follow Alex Honnold as he attempts to become the first person to ever free solo climb Yosemite's 3,000 foot high El Capitan wall. With no ropes or safety gear, this would arguably be the greatest feat in rock climbing history.
tagline: Live beyond fear
title: Free Solo
plot:
Free Solo is a documentary film that follows Alex Honnold's attempt to climb El Capitan in Yosemite National Park without any ropes or safety gear. The movie delves into the psychological and emotional aspects of risk-taking, obsession, and the pursuit of perfection.

At its core, Free Solo explores the theme of self-discovery and the human need for challenge and adventure. Alex Honnold's character is driven by an insatiable desire to push himself to the limits of human endurance, and his journey is as much about understanding himself as it is about conquering a physical obstacle.

The film also touches on the idea of obsession and the blurred lines between passion and madness. Honnold's fixation on El Capitan becomes all-consuming, leading him to take extreme risks that put not only himself but also those around him in danger.

Furthermore, Free Solo highlights the importance of mental preparation and emotional resilience in overcoming fear and adversity. Honnold's character is shown to be deeply introspective and self-aware, using meditation and other mindfulness practices to calm his nerves and focus his mind.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that celebrates the beauty of risk-taking and the power of the human spirit while also acknowledging the dangers and uncertainties that come with it.

overview: A group of young adults visit a boarded up campsite named Crystal Lake where they soon encounter the mysterious Jason Voorhees and his deadly intentions.
tagline: Welcome to Crystal Lake
title: Friday the 13th
plot:
Friday the 13th is a 2009 American slasher film that reboots the long-running franchise and counts as its twelfth installment. Marcus Nispel directed from a screenplay by Damian Shannon and Mark Swift. Jared Padalecki stars as Clay Miller, who searches Crystal Lake for his missing sister, Whitney (Amanda Righetti), after she is captured by Jason Voorhees (Derek Mears); Danielle Panabaker, Aaron Yoo and Travis Van Winkle co-star.

On Friday, June 13, 1980, a young Jason watches his mother, Pamela, beheaded by Alice Hardy, who was fleeing Pamela's killing spree at Camp Crystal Lake. Twenty-eight years later, five friends, including Whitney, come to the lake hoping to find a hidden crop of marijuana in the woods. That night the adult Jason kills all of them except Whitney, whom he takes captive because she resembles his mother in her youth. Six weeks later, Trent brings his girlfriend, Jenna, and a group of friends to his family's summer cabin on the lakeshore, while Clay arrives to look for Whitney despite the local sheriff's urging that he search elsewhere. Jenna agrees to help him, and while Jason kills two of the group on the water, they explore the abandoned campgrounds and see Jason dragging a body into an old camp building.

They race back to warn the others. After Clay phones the police, Jason cuts the power and picks off the remaining guests one by one, along with a police officer. Trent flees to the main road only to be killed there, and Jason pursues Clay and Jenna back to the campgrounds, where Clay finds Jason's underground lair and his sister chained alive to a wall. He frees her, but Jenna is impaled by Jason's machete as they try to escape. Cornered in a barn, Whitney confuses Jason by pretending to be his mother, and the siblings restrain him with a chain before Whitney drives his own machete into his chest. At dawn they dump his body in the lake, but Jason bursts through the dock and seizes Whitney.

New Line Cinema's Toby Emmerich approached Platinum Dunes producers Michael Bay, Brad Fuller and Andrew Form to restart the series as they had The Texas Chainsaw Massacre. Initially conceived as an origin story, the project became a reboot drawing on the first four films, with Jason reimagined as a lean, fast killer. The film earned about $19.3 million on its opening day and $40.6 million over its three-day opening weekend, a record for a horror film at the time, but critics were unimpressed, with 26% on Rotten Tomatoes and 34 on Metacritic.

overview: An American teenager who is obsessed with Hong Kong cinema and kung-fu classics makes an extraordinary discovery in a Chinatown pawnshop: the legendary stick weapon of the Chinese sage and warrior, the Monkey King. With the lost relic in hand, the teenager unexpectedly finds himself travelling back to ancient China to join a crew of warriors from martial arts lore on a dangerous quest to free the imprisoned Monkey King.
tagline: The battle for eternity is the fantasy of a lifetime.
title: The Forbidden Kingdom
plot:
The Forbidden Kingdom is a fantasy wuxia film of 2008 directed by Rob Minkoff and written by John Fusco, loosely inspired by the 16th-century Chinese novel Journey to the West. Michael Angarano plays Jason Tripitikas, an American teenager, while Chan plays the drunken scholar Lu Yan and the shopkeeper Old Hop, and Li plays the Silent Monk and the Monkey King, Sun Wukong. Liu Yifei plays Golden Sparrow, Li Bingbing plays the White-Haired Witch Ni Chang and Collin Chou plays the Jade Warlord.

In South Boston, Jason, a fan of martial arts films, dreams of the Monkey King battling celestial soldiers in the clouds. At a Chinatown pawn shop he spots a golden staff like the one in his dream. A gang of local thugs led by Lupo forces him to help them rob the shop, and Lupo shoots the owner, Hop, who urges Jason to return the staff to its rightful owner. Cornered on a rooftop, Jason is pulled over the edge by the staff and wakes up in ancient China.

When soldiers attack a village to seize the staff, he is rescued by Lu Yan, a drunken traveling scholar who claims to be an immortal. Lu explains that the Jade Warlord tricked the Monkey King into setting down his staff and turned him to stone, but the Monkey King flung the staff away first; a prophecy foretells that a Seeker will return it and free him. Joined by Golden Sparrow, whose family the Warlord murdered, and by the mysterious Silent Monk, Jason sets out for Five Elements Mountain, learning kung fu on the way. The Warlord promises Ni Chang the elixir of immortality if she retrieves the staff. Ni Chang wounds Lu with an arrow, and at a monastery the companions learn that he is not immortal after all and only the Warlord's elixir can save him.

Jason goes alone to trade the staff for the elixir and must duel Ni Chang for it until his friends arrive. Jason throws the elixir to Lu, who recovers and sends Ni Chang plunging from a balcony. The dying Silent Monk passes the staff to Jason, who shatters the statue and frees the Monkey King, revealing that the monk was one of his clones. Sparrow is killed seeking revenge, and after the Monkey King defeats the Warlord, Jason stabs him and he falls into lava. Granted a wish by the Jade Emperor, Jason chooses to return home, where he beats Lupo; Hop, who survived, hints that he is Lu Yan.

Filmed partly around the Gobi Desert in Mongolia, the film opened at number one in North America and grossed about $128 million worldwide. Critics liked the fights but not the filler.

overview: Something has gone wrong with the landing gear of a plane en route from Madrid to Mexico City. The group of eccentric travelers on the flight, defenseless in the face of danger, indulge in colourful confessionals, while the outlandish crew attempts to find ways to entertain them.
title: I'm So Excited!
plot:
I'm So Excited! is a 2013 Spanish comedy film directed by Juan José Campanella and produced by El Deseo, among others. The movie revolves around the story of a young flight attendant named Maria (played by Paz Vega) who becomes embroiled in a series of misadventures when she's assigned to be in charge of a commercial airliner on its maiden voyage.

At its core, I'm So Excited! is a film about the human desire for freedom and the consequences that come with it. The movie follows Maria as she navigates her way through a series of unexpected events, from dealing with a group of eccentric passengers to confronting her own personal demons. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Maria's journey is not just about surviving the flight, but also about finding her place in the world and learning to let go of her past.

The film explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and the complexities of human relationships. Through Maria's character, the movie delves into the idea that our experiences shape us, and that it's never too late to make a change and start anew. The film also touches on the theme of responsibility, as Maria is forced to take charge and make decisions that will impact not only her own life but also the lives of those around her.

Overall, I'm So Excited! is a movie about embracing uncertainty and finding the courage to take control of our lives. With its witty dialogue, engaging characters, and heartwarming story, it's a film that will leave audiences laughing, crying, and rooting for Maria as she navigates her way through the ups and downs of life.

overview: Riding across Manhattan in a stretch limo during a riot in order to get a haircut, a 28-year-old billionaire asset manager's life begins to crumble.
tagline: How far can he go before he goes too far?
title: Cosmopolis
plot:
Cosmopolis is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of modern society, exploring themes of alienation, disconnection, and the search for meaning in a hyper-consumerist world. The movie follows Eric Packer, a wealthy investment banker played by Robert Pattinson, as he embarks on a journey through Manhattan in his limousine, reflecting on his life and the emptiness that surrounds him.

Through Eric's character, the film critiques the excesses of capitalism and the ways in which it can lead to a sense of disconnection and isolation. The movie also explores the tension between individual desire and societal expectations, as Eric struggles to reconcile his own needs with the pressures of his high-stakes job and the demands of his wealthy lifestyle.

One of the primary concerns of Cosmopolis is the notion of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. As Eric navigates the city, he encounters a series of characters who challenge his perceptions of himself and the world around him, forcing him to confront the emptiness and disconnection that lies at the heart of modern life.

The film's use of satire and social commentary serves to highlight the absurdities and contradictions of contemporary society, where individuals are often more focused on their own desires than on genuine human connection. Ultimately, Cosmopolis presents a bleak but thought-provoking vision of a world in which people are increasingly disconnected from themselves and each other.

Overall, Cosmopolis is a complex and nuanced film that challenges viewers to think critically about the world we live in and the values that shape our lives.

overview: In a universe where human genetic material is the most precious commodity, an impoverished young Earth woman becomes the key to strategic maneuvers and internal strife within a powerful dynasty…
tagline: Expand your universe.
title: Jupiter Ascending
plot:
Jupiter Ascending is a 2015 science fiction film written and directed by the Wachowskis and Tom Tykwer, produced by Grant Hill and Lana Wachowski. The movie stars Mila Kunis, Channing Tatum, Eddie Redmayne, Tilda Swinton, and Cate Blanchett.

The story begins in a dystopian future where humans are oppressed by an alien species known as the "Mortals." These Mortals have enslaved humanity, forcing them to live in poverty and servitude. The protagonist, Jupiter Jones (played by Mila Kunis), is a young woman who discovers that she is actually an immortal being from the planet Cukelar, which was destroyed by the Mortals.

Jupiter's life takes a dramatic turn when she meets Balem Abrasax (played by Eddie Redmayne), the son of the powerful and ruthless leader of the Mortals, Stinger Abrasax. Balem reveals to Jupiter that she is the reincarnation of Queen Lyta, an immortal being who was once the queen of Cukelar.

As Jupiter learns more about her past and her true identity, she becomes embroiled in a rebellion against the Mortals. She meets Caine Wise (played by Channing Tatum), a skilled warrior from the planet Cukelar, who is tasked with protecting Jupiter on her journey to reclaim her rightful place as queen.

The plot thickens as Jupiter and Caine embark on a perilous quest to gather allies and resources for their rebellion. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, deadly creatures, and rival factions vying for power.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Balem's intentions are not entirely pure. He seeks to use Jupiter's powers to overthrow his father and take control of the Mortals' empire. Meanwhile, Stinger Abrasax is determined to crush the rebellion and maintain his family's grip on power.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the rebels and the Mortals, with Jupiter at its center. In a surprising twist, it is revealed that Balem has been manipulating events from behind the scenes, using Jupiter's powers to further his own ambitions.

In the end, Jupiter must make a choice between her loyalty to Caine and her destiny as queen. With the help of her new allies, she manages to defeat Balem and shatter the Mortals' hold on humanity. However, the film concludes with a sense of uncertainty, leaving the audience wondering about the future of this new world order.

Throughout the movie, the Wachowskis explore themes of identity, power, and rebellion, weaving together elements of science fiction, fantasy, and adventure. While Jupiter Ascending received mixed reviews from critics, it has developed a loyal fan base over the years, particularly among those who appreciate its unique blend of action, drama, and visual spectacle.

overview: Grandmother Mi Ja works part-time as a caretaker, and struggles to raise a teen grandson by herself. Despite her tough situation, she speaks softly, dresses fashionably, and approaches the world with child-like curiosity. Enrolling in a poetry class, she endeavors to capture life in verse form, but her simple dream of completing a poem is stalled by the early signs of Alzheimer's disease and the heavy financial and emotional burden of her grandson's shocking wrongdoing.
title: Poetry
plot:
Poetry (Si) is a South Korean drama of 2010 written and directed by Lee Chang-dong. Yoon Jeong-hee, in her first film role since 1994 and her last before her death in 2023, plays Yang Mi-ja, a woman in her sixties who takes up poetry while facing the onset of Alzheimer's disease and the crime of her grandson. Lee David plays the grandson, Jong-wook, with Kim Hee-ra as Mr. Kang.

Mi-ja, 66, works part-time caring for Mr. Kang, an elderly stroke patient, and at home looks after her surly 16-year-old grandson, whose divorced mother lives in Busan. Forgetting everyday words, she is told to get checked, and she signs up for a poetry class at a community center, where each student must write a single poem by the end of the month. Following her teacher's advice, she starts noting down what she observes, especially flowers.

The father of Jong-wook's friend Ki-beom summons her to a meeting with the other boys' fathers. She learns that their sons repeatedly raped a schoolgirl, Agnes, over six months, until the girl threw herself from a bridge and drowned. To protect the boys and the school, the fathers plan to buy off the girl's mother, a poor widowed farmer, with 30 million won, and Mi-ja is expected to pay a share of 5 million she does not have. She tells no one, not even her daughter, and keeps silent when she is diagnosed with early-stage Alzheimer's. Jong-wook ignores her attempts to confront him.

At a weekly poetry reading she meets Detective Park, a crude but reportedly decent policeman. After Mr. Kang makes a desperate sexual advance, Mi-ja quits, but after visiting the bridge where Agnes died she returns to him, soaked by rain, and has sex with him. When she reveals too much to a journalist, the fathers send her to the countryside to win over Agnes's mother; meeting the woman in her field, Mi-ja makes small talk and never raises the money, yet the mother agrees to settle. Mi-ja obtains her share from Mr. Kang, who assumes it is blackmail. Then she calls her daughter home, makes Jong-wook wash and trim his nails, and quietly lets Detective Park take him away. Later her teacher finds flowers and her poem, "Agnes's Song", but Mi-ja has vanished; as he reads it aloud, her voice gives way to Agnes's, leaving her fate unresolved.

Inspired partly by a real case, the film premiered in competition at Cannes in 2010 and won Best Screenplay. Yoon received several Best Actress awards, and critics acclaimed the film.

overview: A man which wife is filing to divorce him wins 25 million EUR in the lotto, hiding her to prevent sharing the half of the prize.
title: If I Were a Rich Man
plot:
If I Were Rich (Spanish: Si yo fuera rico) is a 2019 Spanish comedy directed by Álvaro Fernández Armero, who wrote the screenplay with Ángela Armero and Tom Fernández. It is a remake of the 2002 French comedy Ah! Si j'étais riche. Álex García and Alexandra Jiménez star as the separating couple Santi and Maite, with Jordi Sánchez as a scheming bank manager, Adrián Lastra and Franky Martín as Santi's friends Marcos and Pedro, and Diego Martín, Paula Echevarría and Antonio Resines in supporting roles. Telecinco Cinema, the company behind the hit comedy Spanish Affair, produced it with Si yo fuera AIE, Think Studio and Ciskul, with the participation of Mediaset España and Movistar+.

Santi is a hapless man to whom every possible misfortune seems to happen. He loses his job, takes on unpleasant odd jobs to earn a little money and, with his marriage to Maite collapsing and a divorce under way, ends up sleeping in his camper van, collecting a stream of parking fines from a local officer who seems fixated on him. To make matters worse, a former high school classmate, once mocked for his weight, returns to town slim and flush with success and begins a relationship with Maite.

His luck turns when he gambles the last of his money on a lottery jackpot and wins 25 million euros. On the advice of the branch manager at his bank, he decides to keep the windfall secret, since revealing it while the divorce is still pending would oblige him to hand half of the prize to the wife he is leaving. Keeping the secret proves difficult. His new habits and spending do not go unnoticed by Marcos and Pedro, and the effort to conceal the fortune from Maite and everyone around him leads to a chain of lies, misunderstandings and farcical situations.

The film was shot in Asturias, including Gijón and the beaches of Salinas, Xagó and Verdicio, and in Madrid. Distributed by Paramount Pictures, it opened in Spain on 15 November 2019 and became a surprise box-office success, taking in about 12 million euros by February 2020. Critical reception was mixed. Fotogramas praised the lead couple and the scene-stealing supporting cast while finding the film formulaic, and Cinemanía felt it kept its honesty despite commercial tics and heavy product placement. El País called it uneven but watchable, while eCartelera and HobbyConsolas criticized its stale, often crude gags and forced Asturian accents, though several reviewers singled out Resines and Isabel Ordaz.

overview: Queen Poppy plans the first annual Trolls Kingdom Secret Holiday Gift Swap, but things don't go quite as expected.
tagline: The holidays are better together.
title: Trolls Holiday in Harmony
plot:
Trolls: Holiday in Harmony is an American animated musical Christmas special of 2021 from DreamWorks Animation, the second holiday special based on the Trolls franchise after Trolls Holiday. Written and directed by Sean Charmatz and Tim Heitz in their official directing debut, it premiered on NBC on 26 November 2021. Returning voices include Anna Kendrick as Queen Poppy, Justin Timberlake as Branch, Rachel Bloom as Queen Barb, Kunal Nayyar as Guy Diamond and Kenan Thompson as Tiny Diamond, with guests including Carol Burnett and Travis Scott.

On their first date, Poppy tells Branch about her plans for a holiday gift exchange. Each Troll will draw another's name and bring a secret present to Pop Village in three days. After delivering the baskets all over the kingdom, Poppy and Branch draw the last two cards and find each other's names. Poppy is delighted; Branch is terrified.

In Pop Village, Tiny Diamond draws his own father, Guy Diamond, and sets out to write him a rap, but he cannot find anything that rhymes with "Diamond" and fears he has lost his flow. After several failures he climbs a mountain to consult the monks of the Cloud Temple, and meditating with the Clouds helps him see that he simply needs to rhyme with "daddy". Back in the village, Poppy puts the finishing touches on her gift, sure that it is just right. Branch, meanwhile, dreams up a machine to style Poppy's hair and secretly measures her head, but after glimpsing her present for him he panics that his will fall short and retreats to his bunker. There he keeps adding feature after feature to the contraption until a test run makes it explode, launching him into space before he crashes back down in the village. Tiny finds him, hears his tale of failure and passes on the lesson he has just learned: look past the clutter. While tidying the wreckage of his bunker, Branch comes across a photograph of himself with Poppy and realizes what to do.

At the exchange, Branch gives Poppy a scrapbook recording everything they have been through together, a gift only he could make. Poppy's box for him turns out to be empty, because she knew nothing could be good enough for him. Realizing that all they need is each other, they embrace, the Trolls sing "Together Now", and the couple float off on a balloon ride, Poppy kissing Branch on the cheek.

The broadcast, aired on Black Friday, drew about 1.8 million live viewers, rising to about 2.2 million after a week.

overview: At a high-school party, four friends find that losing their collective virginity isn't as easy as they had thought. But they still believe that they need to do so before college. To motivate themselves, they enter a pact to all "score" by their senior prom.
tagline: There's nothing like your first piece.
title: American Pie
plot:
American Pie is a coming-of-age comedy film released in 1999, directed by Paul Weiland and written by Adam Herz. The movie follows the lives of four high school friends - Jim Levenstein (Jason Biggs), Finch (Eddie Kaye Thomas), Oz (Chris Klein), and Kevin (Thomas Ian Nicholas) - as they navigate love, friendship, and growing up in the suburban town of Chappaqua, New York.

The film begins with the introduction of the main characters, showcasing their unique personalities and quirks. Jim is a naive and awkward teenager who has just moved to Chappaqua from Chicago with his family. Finch is a brainiac who is obsessed with sex and relationships. Oz is a charismatic athlete who is struggling to find his place in the world. Kevin is a laid-back jock who is trying to balance his athletic career with his desire for love.

The story takes a turn when Jim's parents announce that they are getting divorced, leaving Jim feeling lost and uncertain about his future. The group of friends decides to take matters into their own hands and create a "pie" - a sex manual - to help Jim lose his virginity before he leaves for college.

As the movie progresses, the friends embark on a series of misadventures, including a disastrous trip to the local water park, a botched attempt at seduction, and a wild party that ends in chaos. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and growing up.

One of the most memorable aspects of American Pie is its portrayal of male adolescence, capturing the awkwardness, insecurity, and humor that defines this stage of life. The film's script is full of witty one-liners, clever references, and hilarious situations that have become iconic in pop culture.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various challenges, including romantic relationships, family drama, and peer pressure. Jim's journey to lose his virginity becomes a central plot point, as he navigates his feelings for his crush, Michelle (Alyson Hannigan). The film's climax features a memorable scene in which Jim finally loses his virginity, but not before learning valuable lessons about himself and his relationships.

American Pie was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $235 million worldwide. The movie spawned two sequels, American Pie 2 (2001) and American Wedding (2003), as well as several spin-offs and merchandise. The film's impact on popular culture is undeniable, cementing its place as a classic coming-of-age comedy of the late 1990s.

Overall, American Pie is a hilarious and relatable movie that captures the essence of male adolescence with humor, wit, and heart. Its memorable characters, witty script, and iconic moments have made it a beloved favorite among audiences for generations.

overview: When the daughter of a psychiatrist is kidnapped, he's horrified to discover that the abductors' demand is that he break through to a post traumatic stress disorder suffering young woman who knows a secret..
tagline: ...I'll never tell.
title: Don't Say a Word
plot:
Don't Say a Word is a psychological thriller film directed by Gregory Hoblit, released in 2001 by 20th Century Fox.

The movie revolves around the story of Nathan Smith (played by Dominic West), a young man who suffers from amnesia and has no memory of his past. He is found unconscious on a train with severe head injuries, and as he tries to regain his memories, he becomes embroiled in a mystery involving a woman named Emma (played by Michelle Monaghan) and her husband, John (played by John Travolta).

The main themes of Don't Say a Word include:

1. Identity: The film explores Nathan's struggle to regain his identity and remember his past, which serves as a metaphor for the human search for self-discovery.
2. Trauma: The movie delves into the psychological effects of trauma on individuals, particularly those who have experienced violent or traumatic events.
3. Love and relationships: The story highlights the complexities of love, relationships, and trust, as Nathan becomes increasingly entangled in Emma's life and struggles to form connections with her.
4. Deception and secrets: As the plot unfolds, it becomes clear that everyone involved is hiding secrets, leading to a web of deception and mistrust.

The film's climax reveals a shocking twist, which I won't spoil here, but it ultimately leads to Nathan's journey towards healing and self-discovery.

Overall, Don't Say a Word is a gripping thriller that explores the complexities of human psychology, relationships, and identity.

overview: A Chechen Muslim illegally immigrates to Hamburg and becomes a person of interest for a covert government team which tracks the movements of potential terrorists.
title: A Most Wanted Man
plot:
A Most Wanted Man is a thought-provoking thriller that delves into the complexities of identity, nationality, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The film tells the story of Gustav Münsterleyner, a German citizen who becomes embroiled in a cat-and-mouse game with a young American woman named Annie, whose life is threatened by a terrorist.

At its core, A Most Wanted Man explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and surroundings. Gustav, a seemingly ordinary man, finds himself at the center of a global conspiracy that forces him to confront his own sense of self. As he navigates this treacherous landscape, he begins to question the very notion of who he is and where he belongs.

The film also delves into the complexities of nationality and how it can be both a source of comfort and a tool of oppression. Gustav's German heritage becomes a point of contention in his interactions with Annie, highlighting the tensions between loyalty, duty, and personal identity.

Furthermore, A Most Wanted Man raises important questions about the nature of terrorism and the impact it has on individuals and communities.
