Gully is a 2019 American coming-of-age crime drama directed by Nabil Elderkin from a screenplay by Marcus J. Guillory. Kelvin Harrison Jr., Charlie Plummer and Jacob Latimore play Jesse, Nicky and Calvin, with Jonathan Majors as Greg, Amber Heard, Terrence Howard and John Corbett as Charlie; Travis Scott makes a cameo.

In an impoverished part of Los Angeles, three lifelong friends carry the scars of childhood trauma. Jesse has not spoken in years because of abuse he suffered, Nicky expects to become a father though his girlfriend Keisha's family rejects him, and Calvin is self-destructive and refuses his medication, dismissing a guidance counselor who tells him his test scores could take him to college. Haunted by memories of his violent late father, Nicky beats a boy painting graffiti near a mural of him. Meanwhile, Greg, recently out of prison, struggles to find work, pushing a lawnmower around the neighborhood and refusing an old acquaintance's offer of shady jobs in order to stay clean.

At Calvin's urging, the teenagers decide to "take the game outside", acting out their violent video games in real life. They wreck a video store, randomly beat two men and steal their pills and pickup truck, treating each act as points scored. When Greg sees Jesse's stepfather, Charlie, abusing him, he tells Calvin, and Calvin and Nicky finally understand Jesse's silence and stay the night to comfort him. After a Mercedes driver menaces Calvin, triggering memories of his father being shot dead by a police officer, the trio follow him home, ransack the house and swap the truck for his car. When a passing car breaks Calvin's skateboard, he seems to snap; his mother gives him a cape as an early birthday present, and Greg finds him on scaffolding, where Calvin speaks of his dream of flying to Venus. When Charlie comes by Jesse's home, Nicky and Calvin track him to his house and kill him. Nicky, who left his phone in the stolen Mercedes, is arrested for grand theft, and after visiting him in jail, Calvin is shot dead by the men whose truck they stole. Jesse brings Calvin's hoodie to his grieving mother, and later, at the beach with Greg, Jesse breaks his years of silence with a scream of anguish.

The cast was announced in March 2018, when principal photography began. Gully premiered at Tribeca on April 27, 2019. Vertical Entertainment and Paramount acquired U.S. rights in 2020, and it was released on June 4, 2021. Reviews were poor, with 25% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Powerful businessman Russ Duritz is self-absorbed and immersed in his work. But by the magic of the moon, he meets Rusty, a chubby, charming 8-year-old version of himself who can't believe he could turn out so badly – with no life and no dog. With Rusty's help, Russ is able to reconcile the person he used to dream of being with the man he's actually become.
tagline: Nobody ever grows up quite like they imagined.
title: The Kid
plot:
The Kid (2000) is a drama film that revolves around the story of a young boy named Chris Cooper's character, who adopts a feral child and raises him as his own. 

One of the primary themes of the movie is the concept of family and what it truly means to be part of one. The main character's journey is not just about providing for the child's physical needs but also about giving him love, care, and acceptance. As the story unfolds, we see how this unconventional family dynamic affects both the adoptive father and the feral child.

Another significant theme present in the film is the struggle to find one's place in society. The feral child, who is initially portrayed as a wild and untamed individual, gradually learns to adapt to the world around him. This transformation serves as a metaphor for the human desire to belong and be accepted by others.

The movie also explores the idea of redemption and second chances. The main character's past mistakes and regrets are slowly revealed throughout the story, adding depth to his character and highlighting the importance of making amends and starting anew.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. As the feral child grows and develops, he begins to question his own existence and the circumstances that led him to be abandoned in the woods. This introspection serves as a catalyst for his growth and eventual integration into society.

Overall, The Kid (2000) is a poignant exploration of what it means to be human, with all its complexities and vulnerabilities.

original_title: How to Lose Friends & Alienate People
overview: Sidney Young is a down-on-his-luck journalist. Thanks to a stint involving a pig and a glitzy awards ceremony, Sidney turns his fortunes around, attracting the attention of Clayton Harding, editor of New York-based glossy magazine 'Sharps', and landing the holy grail of journalism jobs. The Brit jets off to the Big Apple and moves from one blunder to the next.
tagline: He's across the pond, and out of his depth.
title: How to Lose Friends & Alienate People
plot:
How to Lose Friends & Alienate People is a 2008 comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the consequences of one's actions. The movie delves into the theme of social hierarchy and how individuals navigate their way through various social circles.

The protagonist, Ron Livingston's character, is an American writer who moves to London to work on his novel. He quickly finds himself entangled in a web of complex relationships with his British colleagues, particularly the charismatic but manipulative Simon Rich (played by Gordon Pinsent). As Ron becomes more and more entrenched in this social circle, he begins to lose touch with his own identity and values.

The film also touches on the theme of superficiality and the dangers of pretending to be someone you're not. Ron's character is initially drawn to the group because of their perceived sophistication and exclusivity, but as he becomes more deeply embroiled in their lives, he realizes that beneath the surface lies a complex web of insecurities and vulnerabilities.

Throughout the film, the director, Robert Bendetich, uses humor and satire to explore these themes, often poking fun at the pretensions and absurdities of social cliques. However, beneath the comedic surface, the movie reveals a nuanced commentary on the human condition, highlighting the difficulties of forming genuine connections in a world where appearances can be deceiving.

Ultimately, How to Lose Friends & Alienate People is a thought-provoking exploration of the complexities of human relationships and the consequences of our actions. It invites viewers to reflect on their own social behaviors and consider the importance of authenticity and vulnerability in building meaningful connections with others.

overview: Bombshell is a revealing look inside the most powerful and controversial media empire of all time; and the explosive story of the women who brought down the infamous man who created it.
tagline: Based on a Real Scandal
title: Bombshell
plot:
Bombshell is a 2019 American biographical drama film directed by Jay Roach, written by Charles Randolph, and produced by Charlize Theron, Aaron Ryder, and Teri Segal. The film is based on the book "Fire and Reckoning: Inside the World of Fox News" by Byron York.

The film takes place in 1996-1997 and focuses on the lives of three women who worked at Fox News Channel during its early years: Megyn Kelly (played by Charlize Theron), Gretchen Carlson (played by Nicole Kidman), and Kayla Pospisil (played by Allison Janney).

The film begins with a dramatic sequence showing the 1996 presidential election, where Republican candidate Bob Dole loses to Democratic candidate Bill Clinton. The scene then shifts to Fox News Channel's launch in October 1996, where Megyn Kelly is hired as a news anchor.

As the story unfolds, we see how Megyn Kelly navigates her way through the male-dominated world of Fox News, facing sexism and misogyny from her colleagues, including Roger Ailes (played by Jodie Foster), the channel's CEO. Despite these challenges, Kelly proves herself to be a talented journalist and becomes one of the network's top anchors.

Meanwhile, Gretchen Carlson is introduced as a rising star at Fox News, where she works alongside Megyn Kelly. However, her career is soon derailed when she accuses Roger Ailes of sexual harassment. The film depicts the intense pressure and fear that Carlson faces as she decides to take on Ailes, who has significant power over her career.

As the story progresses, we see how Kayla Pospisil, a young producer at Fox News, becomes embroiled in the scandal surrounding Roger Ailes' behavior. She is one of the few women who speak out against him, and her bravery inspires others to do the same.

The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between Gretchen Carlson and Roger Ailes, where she accuses him of sexual harassment and demands that he resign from his position as CEO of Fox News. The scene is intense and emotional, with both characters delivering powerful performances.

In the aftermath of Ailes' resignation, the film shows how the women at Fox News Channel come together to support each other and rebuild their careers. Megyn Kelly becomes a leading voice for women's rights and feminism, while Gretchen Carlson finds new success as a lawyer and advocate.

The film ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as the women at Fox News Channel look towards a brighter future. The final scene shows Kayla Pospisil, now a successful journalist in her own right, reflecting on the lessons she learned from her experience at Fox News.

Overall, Bombshell is a powerful and timely film that sheds light on the struggles faced by women in the male-dominated world of journalism. With outstanding performances from its cast, including Charlize Theron, Nicole Kidman, and Allison Janney, the film is a must-see for anyone interested in politics, media, or feminism.

overview: When a truck crashes inside a tunnel, people on their way home for Christmas are brutally trapped in a deadly fire. With a blizzard raging outside, and the first responders struggling to get to the accident, it's every man for himself.
tagline: Two ways in - No way out
title: The Tunnel
plot:
The Tunnel is a 2019 Norwegian thriller film directed by Ole Giøvaag. 

The movie revolves around a group of friends who embark on a road trip to explore an abandoned tunnel in the countryside, only to find themselves trapped and hunted by a mysterious figure.

As for the main themes, The Tunnel explores several ideas:

1. **Friendship and camaraderie**: The film highlights the strong bonds between the group of friends as they navigate their way through the tunnel and confront the dangers that lie within.
2. **Isolation and vulnerability**: The characters are forced to confront their own vulnerabilities and fears as they become trapped in the tunnel, highlighting the fragility of human relationships in isolated environments.
3. **Trauma and PTSD**: One of the main characters, a young woman named Maja, is struggling with PTSD after a traumatic event in her past. Her experiences in the tunnel serve as a catalyst for confronting her demons.
4. **Survival and resilience**: As the group fights to survive against their pursuer, they must also confront their own mortality and the limits of human endurance.

Throughout the film, these themes are expertly woven together to create a tense and suspenseful narrative that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

original_title: Latte Igel und der magische Wasserstein
overview: When a greedy bear steals a magic stone to keep the forest’s water for himself, a brave hedgehog and a timid squirrel must work together to retrieve it.
title: Latte and the Magic Waterstone
plot:
Latte and the Magic Waterstone (German: Latte Igel und der magische Wasserstein) is a German computer-animated adventure film directed by Mimi Maynard, Regina Welker and Nina Wels, adapted from Sebastian Lybeck's children's book by screenwriters Martin Behnke, Andrea Deppert, Marina Martins and Jesper Møller. In the German version Luisa Wietzorek voices Latte, an ambitious young hedgehog, and Tim Schwarzmaier voices Tjum, a shy and clumsy red squirrel, with Henning Baum and Timur Bartels also in the cast. It premiered at the Schlingel festival in 2019, opened in Germany on 25 December 2019 and reached Netflix on 31 July 2020.

Latte is an orphan and an outcast in a small forest community whose only friend, Tjum, believes her boast that her father was the king of a distant land. When drought strikes, an old crow tells an emergency council that it was caused by the theft of a magic waterstone by the bear King Bantur, and that rain will only return if the stone is taken back. The others are doubtful, but Latte sets out alone to return the stone to the White Mountains, and Tjum, urged by his younger sister, follows to protect her. A beaver saves them from a lynx, and Greta, who lets them shelter in her cave, tells them about the stone, gives them thirst-quenching waterberries and warns them of a wolf pack, led by Lupo, which corners them but lets them go. Latte confesses that she is no princess, which Tjum already suspected, but the friends later quarrel, destroy the berries, and split up. Lost in bear territory, Tjum meets Amaroo, a bear cub who reveals that he is Bantur's son, but Tjum is caught by guards while trying to leave. Latte meets a gloomy old hedgehog who insists that hedgehogs always die alone, and is captured too when she tries to enter the cave through a river. Reunited in a cell, the pair are brought before Bantur, who admits the theft but cares nothing for the suffering it has caused. While he is distracted, they pry the stone loose and escape by river. Ambushed by Lupo, Bantur and the lynx, Tjum distracts them while Latte returns the stone, and the resulting flood sweeps the three villains away. The crow carries the friends home, where the water is back, and Tjum's father invites Latte to join their family.

The filmmakers made Latte, male in the book, a girl. The film received mixed reviews, with three of five critics' reviews counted as positive on Rotten Tomatoes, while the German Film and Media Evaluation rated it "especially valuable".

overview: Is there room for principle in Los Angeles? Mike Terry teaches jujitsu and barely makes ends meet. His Brazilian wife, whose family promotes fights, wants to see Mike in the ring making money, but to him competition is degrading. A woman sideswipes Mike's car and then, after an odd sequence of events, shoots out the studio's window. Later that evening, Mike rescues an action movie star in a fistfight at a bar. In return, the actor befriends Mike, gives him a gift, offers him work on his newest film, and introduces Mike's wife to his own - the women initiate business dealings. Then, things go sour all at once, Mike's debts mount, and going into the ring may be his only option.
tagline: There's always a way out. You just have to find it.
title: Redbelt
plot:
Redbelt is a 2008 American martial arts drama film directed by David Mamet. The movie follows the story of Mike Terry, a mixed martial artist who runs a small dojo in Los Angeles.

At its core, Redbelt explores themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption. Mike Terry's life is turned upside down when he is forced to confront his own sense of purpose and belonging after being betrayed by those closest to him. As he navigates this crisis, he must also come to terms with the harsh realities of the world around him.

One of the main themes of Redbelt is the struggle for authenticity in a world that often values superficiality over substance. Mike Terry's journey is a quest for self-discovery and a desire to find his place in the world, free from the expectations of others. Through his experiences, he learns to redefine what it means to be true to oneself.

The film also explores the complexities of loyalty and friendship, highlighting the difficulties of maintaining relationships when one's own values and principles are at odds with those of others. Mike Terry's relationships with his friends and colleagues serve as a catalyst for his growth and self-discovery.

Ultimately, Redbelt is a movie about finding one's way in life, even when the path ahead seems uncertain. Through its exploration of themes such as identity, loyalty, and redemption, the film offers a nuanced and thought-provoking portrayal of the human condition.

overview: Chronicles Jack Harris, one of the pioneers of internet commerce, as he wrestles with his morals and struggles not to drown in a sea of conmen, mobsters, drug addicts, and pornstars.
tagline: Business is a lot like sex ... getting in is easy, pulling out is hard.
title: Middle Men
plot:
Middle Men is a 2009 American black comedy-drama film directed by George Gallo and written by Gallo and Andy Weiss, inspired by the experiences of Christopher Mallick, founder of ePassporte, who was accused of taking millions from its customers to finance the film. Luke Wilson stars as Jack Harris, with Giovanni Ribisi as Wayne Beering, Gabriel Macht as Buck Dolby, James Caan as the lawyer Jerry Haggerty, Jacinda Barrett as Jack's wife Diana, Laura Ramsey as Audrey Dawns and Rade Šerbedžija as Nikita Sokoloff.

In 2004 Jack leaves his Houston home with millions of dollars to pay off Russian gangsters. In 1997 Los Angeles, Jack is running a nightclub for an ailing friend, while nearby two drug-addled friends, Wayne and Buck, a former NASA scientist, wonder why the internet has no pornography. Buck quickly writes a program that lets visitors pay by credit card to view explicit pictures, and the money pours in. They give Sokoloff, a Russian mobster with a strip club, a quarter of the business for access to his dancers, then fail to pay him. Haggerty, the crooked lawyer they hire, brings in Jack, who becomes a partner and buys Haggerty out for $200,000. When Sokoloff's nephew comes to collect $400,000 and threatens Jack's family, one of Jack's bodyguards kills him with a single punch; the partners dump the body at sea, and Sokoloff, doubting their cover story, demands a half share. Jack abandons the website to concentrate on billing, and their company, 24/7 Billing, becomes a hugely profitable middleman for other adult sites. Seduced by money, he neglects his family and begins an affair with Audrey, a porn star whose live stream, it emerges, is used by the government to track terrorists. The resentful Haggerty manipulates Wayne and Buck into processing payments for child pornography sites run by Denny Z, and when the pair confide in him about the nephew's death, he turns Sokoloff against Jack. Sokoloff's men kidnap the son of Jack's maid, believing him to be Jack's own son. Jack signs his share over in exchange for the boy but backdates the contract to before the child pornography business began; Sokoloff kills Haggerty and lets Jack go. Wayne and Buck later testify against Denny Z, Sokoloff flees, reportedly to Moscow, and Jack's wife takes him back.

Released in the United States on 6 August 2010, Middle Men grossed only $754,301 against a $20 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with a 39% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 60.

overview: When a prisoner transfer van is attacked, the cop in charge must fight those inside and outside while dealing with a silent foe: the icy temperatures.
tagline: Escape is not the exit.
title: Below Zero
plot:
Below Zero (Spanish: Bajocero) is a 2021 Spanish action thriller directed by Lluís Quílez, who wrote the screenplay with Fernando Navarro. Javier Gutiérrez, Karra Elejalde, Luis Callejo and Patrick Criado lead the cast in a story about police officers whose armored prisoner transport is ambushed by an attacker demanding one of the inmates. Released on Netflix, it was viewed by 47 million accounts in its first month, according to the service.

In a night-time prologue, a wounded man is chased through a forest and, unable to say where a missing woman is, is buried alive by his pursuer. Officer Martín begins a new job driving a prison transport at night with Montesino, a partner who enjoys humiliating the prisoners, and Martín steps in to stop violence. In thick fog the van loses its escort car and radio contact, then hits a spike strip. Montesino goes out and fails to return; Martín finds him seemingly dead and the escort officers killed, is shot in the leg by a sniper and retreats into the prisoners' section. One inmate attacks him, petrol is poured into two cells and set alight, and Martín must open the cells, though one man has already died. A voice on the intercom reveals Martín's gun is empty and urges the prisoners to flee, and the hijacker, Miguel, now driving the van, threatens to kill everyone unless they give up Nano, who swallows the key.

Montesino revives, finds photographs of Miguel's missing daughter in his jeep and gives chase, but dies when he is forced off the road, while the prisoner Rei is killed during the swerving. Miguel drives the van onto a frozen lake and shoots the ice to sink it. Released by Ramis, a prisoner he recognizes from the band at his wedding, Martín escapes with Nano and Ramis, while another inmate dies of the cold. In a nearby village Martín finds Miguel shooting at Nano and learns his motive: Nano and his childhood friend Chino, the man buried in the prologue, raped and tortured Miguel's young daughter to death. Martín struggles with Miguel for the shotgun, refuses to let him kill Nano and shoots Nano in the hand to force a confession, and Nano admits they hid the girl's body in a well on a farm as a rescue helicopter arrives. Afterward, Martín empties his locker and walks away, apparently leaving the police.

Gutiérrez plays Martín, Elejalde plays Miguel, Callejo plays Ramis and Criado plays Nano. The film received favorable notices, with 88% of eight critics on Rotten Tomatoes giving positive reviews.

original_title: 劇場版 NARUTO -ナルト- 大激突!幻の地底遺跡だってばよ
overview: Naruto, Shikamaru, and Sakura are executing their mission of delivering a lost pet to a certain village. However, right in the midst of things, troops led by the mysterious knight, Temujin, attack them. In the violent battle, the three become separated. Temujin challenges Naruto to a fight and at the end of the fierce battle, both fall together from a high cliff...
title: Naruto: Legend of the Stone of Gelel
plot:
Naruto the Movie: Legend of the Stone of Gelel is a 2005 Japanese animated martial arts fantasy adventure film based on Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga and anime franchise. It was directed by Hirotsugu Kawasaki, who wrote it with Yuka Miyata, for Studio Pierrot. In the original Japanese version Junko Takeuchi voices Naruto Uzumaki, Chie Nakamura voices Sakura Haruno, Showtaro Morikubo voices Shikamaru Nara, Akira Ishida voices Gaara, Gamon Kaai voices the knight Temujin and Akio Nojima voices Haido.

On a deserted beach at night, Gaara and the ninja of the Sand village fight bulky, robot-like armored soldiers, whose retreat reveals a huge warship offshore. Elsewhere, Naruto, Shikamaru and Sakura are searching for a missing pet ferret when they too are attacked by the armored soldiers and by Temujin, a mysterious knight. In the fight, Naruto and Temujin are both blown off a cliff, and a vast machine like a moving cathedral crashes through the forest nearby. Naruto and Temujin regain consciousness inside a traveling caravan led by Kahiko and Emina. The ferret, Nerugui, has also survived and grows fond of Temujin, annoying Kahiko, the client behind the mission. In the cathedral, Shikamaru finds a chamber of pods holding people and sees Temujin's associates, Kamira and Ranke, using them to put souls into the armored soldiers. Temujin returns to his side with Naruto and introduces him to Haido, who explains the Gelel Stone, a powerful mineral lost by a destroyed clan that he claims to seek in order to bring peace to the world. At the beach Gaara defeats Ranke, and Shikamaru and Sakura rescue Kahiko from Fugai. Temujin begins to recall his past, and after being captured and questioned he leaves the caravan with Kahiko. At the Gelel mine, Naruto and his friends confront Haido over the lives he is willing to sacrifice, and while Shikamaru, Sakura and Kankuro defeat Kamira and Fugai, Haido reveals to Temujin that he killed his parents. When Haido turns the stone's power on the now repentant Temujin, the soldiers come to his aid, and Naruto destroys the stone with a Rasengan and defeats Haido. As the mine collapses, Temujin uses a space-time hole to destroy it and Naruto saves him. In a mid-credits scene, Temujin and the children sail away.

Released in Japanese cinemas on 6 August 2005, the film earned ¥1.18 billion. In the United States it skipped theaters, premiering on Cartoon Network on 26 July 2008 before its DVD release three days later.

overview: After a treacherous attack, Secret Service agent Mike Banning is charged with attempting to assassinate President Trumbull. Chased by his own colleagues and the FBI, Banning begins a race against the clock to clear his name.
tagline: Loyalty is under fire
title: Angel Has Fallen
plot:
Angel Has Fallen is a 2019 American action thriller film directed by Ric Roman Waugh and written by Jeff Nathanson. The movie stars Gerard Butler, Morgan Freeman, Jai Courtney, and Lance Reddick.

The story begins with Mike Banning (Gerard Butler), the former head of the Secret Service, who has retired to a quiet life in Virginia with his wife, Shannon (Molly R. Quinn). However, their peaceful existence is disrupted when Shannon is kidnapped by a group of terrorists led by the ruthless and cunning assassin, Ortega (Lance Reddick).

As Mike frantically searches for his wife, he discovers that she has been taken to the White House, where President James Sawyer (Morgan Freeman) is hosting a high-profile event. The kidnappers demand that the President be killed in exchange for Shannon's safe return.

Mike soon realizes that Ortega is not just any ordinary terrorist but a former Secret Service agent who was thought to have been killed years ago. As Mike navigates the complex web of intrigue and deception, he must also confront his own demons and the personal costs of his past actions as a Secret Service agent.

As the story unfolds, Mike teams up with his old friend and fellow Secret Service agent, Tobin (Jai Courtney), to take down Ortega and rescue Shannon. Along the way, they encounter a range of characters, including a mysterious woman named Rachel (Pati Callahan) who may hold the key to unlocking the truth about Ortega's past.

As the plot thickens, Mike finds himself in a cat-and-mouse game with Ortega, who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals. The action unfolds at breakneck speed, with Mike facing off against Ortega and his henchmen in a series of intense and suspenseful confrontations.

In the end, Mike is able to outsmart Ortega and rescue Shannon, but not before he suffers a serious injury that leaves him questioning his own mortality. As the movie concludes, Mike reflects on the personal costs of his actions as a Secret Service agent and the sacrifices he has made for his country.

Throughout the film, Gerard Butler delivers a strong performance as the rugged and charismatic Mike Banning, bringing depth and nuance to the character. Morgan Freeman provides a sense of gravitas and authority as the President, while Jai Courtney brings a youthful energy to the role of Tobin.

Overall, Angel Has Fallen is a tense and thrilling action movie that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish. With its breakneck pace, intricate plot twists, and memorable performances, it's no wonder this film has become a fan favorite among action movie enthusiasts.

overview: Jane, a soon-to-be-married woman, is reunited with her imaginary friend Michael who returns in a human form. Soon, Jane begins doubting her feelings for her fiance as she gets attracted to Michael.
title: Sundays at Tiffany's
plot:
Sundays at Tiffany's is a 2010 American romantic fantasy television film directed by Mark Piznarski for Lifetime, adapted from the 2008 novel of the same name by James Patterson and Gabrielle Charbonnet. Alyssa Milano, who also served as an executive producer, stars as Jane Claremont, with Eric Winter as her imaginary friend Michael, Ivan Sergei as her fiancé Hugh and Stockard Channing as her mother Vivian; Kristin Booth and Emily Alyn Lind, as the young Jane, also appear. The score is by Mateo Messina.

As a lonely girl in New York, Jane spends her Sundays at Tiffany's with her mother, a cold, controlling theatre producer embittered by her divorce, and brings along Michael, a boy of her own age whom only she can see. On Christmas Eve, which is also Jane's birthday, Michael explains that under the rules governing imaginary friends he must leave once she turns ten, and he vanishes from her life. Years later Jane is a successful businesswoman working alongside her mother at the theatre and is engaged to Hugh, a famous actor who seems more in love with his career than with her, with the wedding set for her birthday on Christmas Eve. Outwardly she insists that her life is perfect, but she has doubts, and her mother is more interested in controlling her than supporting her. Then Michael unexpectedly reappears, now a grown man and visible to everyone, having been summoned without her realizing it because she needs guidance. At first shocked and in denial, Jane gradually grows attached to him, rediscovering the value of simple things, while Michael adapts to the human world, finds work as a chef and begins to experience human feelings. Their friendship turns into love, and Hugh comes to see Michael as a threat. When Michael admits that the rules require him to leave her again on her birthday, the hurt Jane refuses to see him. On Christmas Eve, during the ceremony itself, she realizes her relationship with Hugh is loveless and calls off the wedding, only to find that Michael, against all expectations, has not disappeared and has become human, free to stay with her.

The film was shot in Toronto and on location between September 8 and October 1, 2010. Milano said she was drawn to the original concept and its flawed characters, and enjoyed reuniting with Winter and Sergei, with whom she had worked on Charmed. It premiered on Lifetime on December 6, 2010, drawing about 2.1 million viewers.

overview: Teddy Walker is a successful salesman whose life takes an unexpected turn when he accidentally blows up his place of employment. Forced to attend night school to get his GED, Teddy soon finds himself dealing with a group of misfit students, his former high school nemesis and a feisty teacher who doesn't think he's too bright.
title: Night School
plot:
Night School is a 2018 American comedy film directed by Malcolm D. Lee and starring Kevin Hart and Tiffany Haddish.

The movie follows the story of Teddy Walker (Kevin Hart), a charismatic but irresponsible high school dropout who is forced to attend night school after being fired from his job at a car wash for being late one too many times. There, he meets his instructor, Carrie Gresham (Tiffany Haddish), a tough and no-nonsense teacher who becomes his love interest.

The main themes of Night School include:

1. Redemption: Teddy's journey is one of redemption as he tries to turn his life around and become a better person.
2. Self-discovery: Through night school, Teddy learns new skills and discovers hidden talents, which helps him to grow both personally and professionally.
3. Friendship: The movie highlights the importance of friendship and support, particularly between Teddy and his classmates, who become like a surrogate family to him.
4. Love and relationships: Teddy's relationship with Carrie is a central theme in the movie, as he learns to balance his desire for love and connection with his need for independence and self-reliance.

Overall, Night School is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of personal growth, redemption, and the importance of human connections.

overview: A story about how a new baby's arrival impacts a family, told from the point of view of a delightfully unreliable narrator, a wildly imaginative 7 year old named Tim.
tagline: Born leader
title: The Boss Baby
plot:
The Boss Baby is a computer-animated comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie was released on February 18, 2017.

In a world where babies are born with their own unique talents and abilities, the story revolves around Tim Templeton (voiced by Miles Bakshi), a 7-year-old boy who feels like an outcast among his peers. He is constantly belittled and bullied by his older brother, Jimmy (voiced by Noah Schnapp).

One day, while on a family vacation in New York City, Tim discovers that he has a long-lost twin brother, Francis E. Francis (voiced by Alec Baldwin), who was born as part of a secret government experiment to create the perfect baby. Francis is a high-ranking executive at Puppy Co., a toy company owned by Bob the Golden Retriever (voiced by Steve Buscemi).

Francis is sent to Earth to take over Tim's life and eliminate him, but things don't go according to plan. Francis is initially confused about his surroundings and struggles to adjust to human life. He also discovers that he has a unique talent for business and leadership.

As Francis navigates his new environment, he forms an unlikely bond with Tim, who helps him understand the value of family and friendship. Meanwhile, Francis's presence in Tim's life causes chaos, leading to a series of hilarious and action-packed events.

The plot thickens when Francis discovers that Puppy Co. is being threatened by a rival company, Puppy Corp., led by the villainous Baby Corpse (voiced by Jimmy Kimmel). Francis must use his business skills to save Puppy Co. and prove himself as a valuable member of the family.

Throughout the movie, Tim and Francis learn valuable lessons about sibling rivalry, loyalty, and the importance of embracing their unique qualities. The film features a talented voice cast, witty humor, and stunning animation that brings the characters to life.

In the end, Francis successfully saves Puppy Co., and he and Tim form an unbreakable bond. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment where Francis finally understands what it means to be part of a family and finds his place in the world.

Overall, The Boss Baby is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, family, and acceptance. With its lovable characters, engaging storyline, and stunning animation, it's no wonder why this movie became a box office hit.

overview: When stubborn, spotty Kevin and his equally hopeless best friend Perry go on holiday to the party island Ibiza, they see it as their big chance to become superstar club DJs and, more importantly, to lose their virginities. But they aren't prepared for the interference of top DJ Eyeball Paul, not to mention the embarrassment factor of Kevin's long-suffering parents.
tagline: All they want to do is... Do it!!!
title: Kevin & Perry Go Large
plot:
Kevin & Perry Go Large is a British comedy film that revolves around the misadventures of two friends, Kevin and Perry, who embark on a journey to become famous as extreme sports enthusiasts. The movie explores themes of friendship, camaraderie, and the consequences of one's actions.

At its core, the film delves into the idea of chasing fame and fortune, and the lengths people will go to achieve it. Kevin and Perry's antics are driven by their desire for recognition and admiration, which often leads them down a path of reckless behavior. As they navigate through various extreme sports challenges, they must confront the consequences of their actions and learn valuable lessons about responsibility and loyalty.

The movie also touches on themes of identity and self-discovery, as Kevin and Perry struggle to find their place in the world beyond their friendship. Through their experiences, they are forced to re-evaluate their priorities and values, ultimately emerging with a deeper understanding of themselves and each other.

Overall, Kevin & Perry Go Large is a lighthearted, entertaining film that uses humor and satire to explore themes of fame, friendship, and self-discovery.

overview: As a filmmaker and his girlfriend return home from his movie premiere, smoldering tensions and painful revelations push them toward a romantic reckoning.
tagline: Madly in love.
title: Malcolm & Marie
plot:
Malcolm & Marie is a 2021 American romantic drama film written and directed by Sam Levinson. The movie stars John David Washington as Malcolm and Zendaya as Marie.

The main themes of Malcolm & Marie revolve around the complexities of relationships, power dynamics, privilege, and the blurred lines between love and obsession. Here's a brief breakdown:

**Beginning:** The film opens with Malcolm (John David Washington) returning home from a movie premiere, where he has just won an award for his latest film. He is accompanied by Marie (Zendaya), his girlfriend of three years. As they settle into their luxurious apartment, the conversation between them reveals underlying tensions and power struggles in their relationship.

**Plot Development:** The evening unfolds as Malcolm and Marie engage in a heated argument about their past, present, and future together. They discuss topics such as racism, privilege, and the impact of social media on their lives. As the night progresses, the conversation becomes increasingly intense, revealing deeper insecurities and fears within each character.

**Ending:** The film's climax is marked by a dramatic confrontation between Malcolm and Marie, which ultimately leads to a turning point in their relationship. Through this confrontation, the audience witnesses the fragility of their bond and the difficulties of navigating complex relationships.

Throughout the movie, Sam Levinson explores themes such as:

1. **Power dynamics:** The film highlights the power imbalance within the couple's relationship, with Malcolm's privilege and success creating tension.
2. **Privilege and entitlement:** Malcolm's character embodies the privileges of being a successful black man in Hollywood, which creates resentment among Marie.
3. **Love and obsession:** As the argument escalates, it becomes clear that both characters are struggling to define their love for each other amidst the pressures of fame and social expectations.

Overall, Malcolm & Marie is a thought-provoking exploration of complex relationships, power dynamics, and the challenges faced by individuals navigating privilege and identity.

overview: Romance ensues when a small town vintage store owner leaves instructions in her will for inventory to be distributed as Christmas gifts, her out-of-town niece seeks help from a handsome local in identifying recipients from the clues provided.
tagline: English
title: An Eclectic Christmas
plot:
An Eclectic Christmas is a 2022 American Christmas romance television film directed by Lane Shefter Bishop and broadcast on the UPtv network. It stars Hannah Galway and Jeremy Walmsley, with Kim Roberts, Jill Frappier, Daniel Kash and Jonathan Whittaker in supporting roles, and runs approximately 90 minutes. It premiered in December 2022 as part of UPtv's holiday programming.

Kim (Galway) is a fitness coach based in Los Angeles who spends time with her beloved Aunt Freida (Frappier), the owner of a vintage and antique shop in a small town. Shortly after Kim returns to Los Angeles, she receives a call from Freida's friend Leonard (Kash) telling her that her aunt has died suddenly. Kim comes back to settle the estate, her main task being the sale of the shop, and finds herself working with her former fiancé Scott (Walmsley), the local real estate agent handling the sale. Years earlier, Scott had stayed behind when Kim moved to Los Angeles, saying he did not want to hold her back. Freida's will, however, contains instructions that certain items from the shop's inventory be given away as Christmas gifts to particular townspeople, identified only by riddles and clues. Kim enlists Scott's help to solve them, and their travels around town bring them into contact with the recipients, who share their memories of Freida and keep remarking on how good the pair look together. Scott reveals that his father Dudley (Whittaker) is ill, and Dudley eventually confesses that he once loved Freida, who left town to pursue dancing, and that he does not want his son to lose Kim in the same way. The revelation leads Kim to reconsider her return to Los Angeles, and the townspeople rally to raise money for Dudley's treatment.

Reviews were negative. Cassandra Morgan found the film difficult to enjoy, criticising the weak reason given for the couple's original breakup, riddles that made little sense, and plot holes, including Kim's unfamiliarity with the traditions of a town she apparently grew up in; she felt Galway and Walmsley were not given good material. Geno McGahee of Scared Stiff Reviews called it dull and poorly written, with slow pacing and little holiday atmosphere, while also conceding that the two leads did their best with the material.

overview: A drama based on an ancient Chinese proverb that breaks life down into four emotional cornerstones: happiness, pleasure, sorrow and love. A businessman bets his life on a horse race; a gangster sees the future; a pop star falls prey to a crime boss; a doctor must save the love of his life.
tagline: The question is not whether we will die, but how we will live.
title: The Air I Breathe
plot:
The Air I Breathe is a 2007 drama film that revolves around the life of a young woman named Claire Keesey, who struggles with her own identity and sense of belonging. The movie explores themes of self-discovery, love, loss, and the complexities of human relationships.

At its core, The Air I Breathe is a poignant coming-of-age story about a young woman navigating the challenges of growing up and finding her place in the world. Claire's journey is marked by a series of intense relationships with men, each of whom represents a different aspect of herself that she is trying to reconcile.

Throughout the film, the director skillfully weaves together elements of romance, drama, and mystery, creating a narrative that is both deeply personal and universally relatable. The Air I Breathe is ultimately a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that grapples with fundamental questions about identity, love, and the search for meaning in life.

One of the most striking aspects of the film is its use of non-linear storytelling, which adds to the sense of complexity and depth. By jumping back and forth in time, the movie creates a sense of fragmentation and dislocation, mirroring Claire's own feelings of disorientation and confusion.

Ultimately, The Air I Breathe is a moving and thought-provoking film that lingers long after the credits roll. Its exploration of universal themes and its nuanced portrayal of complex human emotions make it a compelling watch for anyone interested in character-driven drama.

overview: The gang's vacation to Paris takes a wrong turn when Scooby and Shaggy miss their flight and end up on a skydiving expedition in the Himalayas. To make matters worse, upon arrival they must outrun the Abominable Snowmonster.
title: Chill Out, Scooby-Doo!
plot:
Chill Out, Scooby-Doo! is a 2007 animated mystery comedy film that revolves around the Mystery Inc. gang's adventures in New Orleans during Mardi Gras. The movie explores themes of cultural identity and the clash between tradition and modernity.

The story delves into the tension between the old-world charm of New Orleans and the influx of tourists and outsiders who disrupt the city's unique culture. The characters, particularly Scooby-Doo, find themselves caught in the middle of this conflict, as they navigate the vibrant streets of the French Quarter while trying to solve a mystery.

Through the lens of the Mystery Inc. gang, the film examines the importance of preserving cultural heritage and respecting local traditions. The movie also touches on the theme of identity, as the characters grapple with their own sense of belonging in this new environment.

Ultimately, Chill Out, Scooby-Doo! is a lighthearted, family-friendly film that celebrates the spirit of Mardi Gras and the power of friendship and teamwork in overcoming challenges. The movie's tone is playful and humorous, making it an enjoyable watch for both kids and adults.

overview: A psychic doctor, John Clancy, works with an FBI special agent in search of a serial killer.
tagline: A serial killer who can see your future, a psychic who can save it
title: Solace
plot:
Solace is a 2015 American action thriller film directed by Dennis Gansel and starring Anthony Hopkins, Colin Farrell, Abbie Cornish, and Forest Whitaker.

The movie begins with Michael "Mike" Bowen (Colin Farrell), an assassin who suffers from dissociative identity disorder (DID). He has multiple personalities, each with its own distinct personality, skills, and memories. Mike's latest target is a former CIA operative named Rachel Jenkins (Abbie Cornish) who has stolen classified information.

As Mike tries to eliminate Rachel, he begins to experience flashbacks of his past traumas, which are triggered by the presence of certain objects or people. He also starts to develop feelings for Rachel, but struggles with controlling his multiple personalities.

Meanwhile, a mysterious figure known as "The Architect" (Anthony Hopkins) is revealed to be behind the assassinations and the theft of classified information. The Architect is a mastermind who uses advanced technology to manipulate and control people's memories, making them believe they are someone else or that their past events never occurred.

As Mike delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that his own past is shrouded in secrecy. He begins to question his own identity and the nature of his DID. With the help of Rachel, a former CIA operative turned psychologist, Dr. Kathryn "Kate" Hawkins (Abbie Cornish), Mike starts to unravel the truth about The Architect's plans.

The plot thickens as Mike and Kate work together to stop The Architect, who is using advanced technology to manipulate world events from behind the scenes. Along the way, Mike's multiple personalities begin to surface, causing chaos and confusion.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Architect has a personal connection to Mike's past, which is slowly revealed through flashbacks and conversations with Kate. The Architect's true identity is eventually exposed, and Mike must confront his own demons in order to stop him.

The movie culminates in an intense showdown between Mike and The Architect, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Mike emerges victorious, but not without scars. He has finally found a sense of peace and control over his multiple personalities, thanks to Kate's help.

Throughout the film, Anthony Hopkins delivers a chilling performance as The Architect, bringing depth and complexity to the character. Colin Farrell also shines as Mike, conveying the vulnerability and intensity required for the role. Abbie Cornish provides a strong supporting performance as Kate, who helps Mike navigate his complex past.

Overall, Solace is an action-packed thriller that explores themes of identity, trauma, and redemption. With its intricate plot and strong performances, it's a gripping watch from start to finish.

overview: L.A. screenwriter David Sumner relocates with his wife, Amy, to her hometown in the deep South. There, while tensions build between them, a brewing conflict with locals becomes a threat to them both.
tagline: Everyone Has A Breaking Point
title: Straw Dogs
plot:
Straw Dogs is a 2011 American Southern Gothic psychological thriller written, produced and directed by Rod Lurie. A remake of Sam Peckinpah's 1971 film, itself adapted from Gordon Williams's novel The Siege of Trencher's Farm, it moves the story from Cornwall to rural Mississippi. James Marsden and Kate Bosworth star as David and Amy Sumner, with Alexander Skarsgård as Charlie, Amy's former boyfriend.

Screenwriter David and his actress wife, Amy, move to her hometown of Blackwater, Mississippi, to live in her late father's house while David finishes a script. In town David meets Charlie and his friends Norman, Chris and Bic, who have already been hired to repair the roof of the couple's barn, and Tom Heddon, an alcoholic former high school football coach who bullies Jeremy Niles, an intellectually disabled man he wrongly believes is stalking his teenage daughter, Janice. The workmen soon harass David, leer at Amy and drag out the job, and Amy grows resentful that David will not stand up to them. When the couple's cat is found strangled, the men deny involvement. Charlie invites David on a deer hunt, then returns to the house and rapes Amy, and Norman rapes her as well. Amy keeps silent but urges David to fire the crew, and he pays them off.

At a football game, Janice lures Jeremy into a locker room and forces herself on him; when Heddon comes looking for her, the panicked Jeremy holds her silent and accidentally smothers her. Haunted by memories of the assault, Amy asks to leave the game and, on the drive home, David accidentally hits Jeremy with the car and brings him home to await an ambulance. Learning of this over a police scanner, Heddon and Charlie's gang besiege the house demanding Jeremy, and Heddon kills the sheriff when he tries to intervene. David barricades the house and fights back killing Chris, Heddon and Bic, while Amy shoots Norman as he tries to rape her again. Charlie beats David and prepares to shoot him, but David snaps a bear trap shut on Charlie's neck, killing him, and as sirens approach and the barn burns, he declares that he got them all.

Filming began on August 16, 2009, in Shreveport and Vivian, Louisiana, and Sony Pictures Releasing released the film on September 16, 2011. It opened with $5.1 million and grossed about $11.2 million against a $25 million budget. Reviews were mixed to negative, with many critics comparing it unfavorably with the original; Rotten Tomatoes gave it 42%.

overview: Christmas Eve takes a twisty turn when the Boss Baby accidentally swaps places with one of Santa's elves and gets stranded at the North Pole.
title: The Boss Baby: Christmas Bonus
plot:
The Boss Baby: Christmas Bonus is a 2022 American computer-animated Christmas comedy special produced by DreamWorks Animation for Netflix. Directed by Matt Engstrom and Christo Stamboliev and written by Tanner Tananbaum and J.D. Ryznar, it is based on characters from the television series The Boss Baby: Back in Business and Marla Frazee's picture book. JP Karliak voices the title character, with Pierce Gagnon as Tim, George Lopez as Santa Claus, Ray Chase as the elf Ding Dong Dongle, and Alex Cazares, Kevin Michael Richardson, David W. Collins, Hope Levy, Max Mittelman, Ariana Greenblatt and Jodi Benson in other roles. Running about 45 minutes and rated TV-Y7, it was released on Netflix on 6 December 2022.

As the grand finale of the family's Christmas traditions, the adult Tim Templeton (Mittelman) tells his daughters Tabitha (Greenblatt) and Tina the story of the first Christmas of his baby brother Theodore "Ted" Templeton, the Boss Baby. The grumpy, suit-wearing baby despised every holiday ritual, so on Christmas Eve the young Tim (Gagnon) takes him, dressed as an elf, to meet Santa at the mall. To Tim's surprise, Santa and the Boss Baby recognise each other: Santa is a former Baby Corp employee who betrayed the company by poaching half its staff for his "toys-for-nothing" programme. When the Boss Baby trips into a mail bag, he is accidentally swapped with Dongle, the North Pole's finest toymaker, and is carried off to Santa's workshop, while Dongle ends up at the Templeton home, where he worries that without him the world will be flooded with inferior toys. As Tim calls on Baby Corp colleagues Staci (Cazares) and Jimbo (Richardson) to sort out the mix-up, the Boss Baby takes charge of the workshop, hunting for inefficiencies, pushing reforms to raise revenue and stirring the elves to strike against their anonymous role in Santa's old-fashioned operation. The chaos threatens Christmas and lands Santa himself on the naughty list, and the Boss Baby must find his way home to celebrate with his family and discover what the Christmas spirit means.

Reviews were mixed. Movieguide rated it three out of four, calling it fun, family-centred entertainment with jokes about economics and private enterprise, though a step down from the feature films in animation and story. Anju Devadas of High on Films found its verbal humour only mildly amusing and its low-key animation unimpressive, while acknowledging the efforts of Lopez, Chase and Karliak.

overview: A father and his daughter struggle to survive in deep space where they live in isolation.
tagline: Oblivion Awaits.
title: High Life
plot:
High Life is a 2018 science fiction film directed by Claire Denis, based on the novel "L'Étranger dans l'univers" (The Stranger in the Universe) by Michel Faber. The movie stars Robert Pattinson, Juliette Binoche, and André 3000.

The main themes of High Life revolve around existentialism, morality, and the human condition. The story takes place on a spaceship traveling through space, where a group of prisoners are being held captive for their crimes. The crew is led by Captain Hunter (played by Robert Pattinson), who is tasked with navigating the ship to a distant planet.

As the journey progresses, the characters' pasts and motivations are slowly revealed, exposing the complexities of human nature. The film explores themes of guilt, redemption, and the search for meaning in a seemingly meaningless universe. The crew's actions are driven by their own moral compasses, which often conflict with each other, leading to a series of philosophical debates.

One of the central questions posed by High Life is: "What does it mean to be human?" The film challenges traditional notions of humanity and morality, presenting characters who are both flawed and relatable. Through its exploration of existentialism, High Life encourages viewers to confront their own values and moral principles.

The movie also touches on themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for connection in a vast, uncaring universe. As the crew navigates the ship's cramped quarters, they must confront their own emotional vulnerabilities and find ways to cope with the existential dread that comes with being trapped in space.

Ultimately, High Life presents a bleak yet thought-provoking vision of humanity's place in the universe, leaving viewers to ponder the complexities of existence and our own moral agency.

overview: In the bleak days of the Cold War, espionage veteran George Smiley is forced from semi-retirement to uncover a Soviet mole within his former colleagues at the heart of MI6.
tagline: How do you find an enemy who is hidden right before your eyes?
title: Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy
plot:
Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy is a 2011 spy thriller film directed by Andrey Zvyagintsev, not Canal+, which is a French television network. The film is an adaptation of John le Carré's 1974 novel of the same name.

The main themes of Tinker Tailory Soldier Spy (2011) include:

1. **Loyalty and Betrayal**: The film explores the complexities of loyalty, duty, and betrayal in a world where allegiances are constantly tested. The protagonist, George Smiley, must navigate a web of deceit and loyalty to uncover the truth about his country's security.

2. **Moral Ambiguity**: The story delves into the moral gray areas that spies often inhabit. Characters like Bill Haydon and Ricki Tarr embody this theme, as they struggle with their own loyalties and motivations.

3. **The Cold War Era**: Set against the backdrop of the Cold War, the film captures the paranoia, suspicion, and espionage that defined this era. The story highlights the cat-and-mouse game played between British intelligence and Soviet spies.

4. **Psychological Warfare**: Smiley's character is a master of psychological manipulation, using his intellect and experience to outmaneuver his opponents. This theme is reflected in the film's tense, suspenseful atmosphere.

5. **The Human Cost of Espionage**: The story also explores the personal costs of espionage on those involved, particularly Smiley, who has sacrificed his own life for the sake of duty.

Overall, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy (2011) is a thought-provoking and gripping thriller that delves into the complexities of human relationships, loyalty, and morality in the world of espionage.

original_title: Hector and the Search for Happiness
overview: Hector is a quirky psychiatrist who has become increasingly tired of his humdrum life. As he tells his girlfriend, Clara, he feels like a fraud: he hasn’t really tasted life, and yet he’s offering advice to patients who are just not getting any happier. So Hector decides to break out of his deluded and routine driven life. Armed with buckets of courage and child-like curiosity, he embarks on a global quest in hopes of uncovering the elusive secret formula for true happiness. And so begins a larger than life adventure with riotously funny results.
tagline: Sometimes to find yourself you need to get a little lost.
title: Hector and the Search for Happiness
plot:
Hector and the Search for Happiness is a 2014 film that explores the complexities of human existence through the story of Hector, a psychiatrist who embarks on a journey to find happiness. The movie delves into themes of existentialism, self-discovery, and the search for meaning in life.

At its core, the film is about Hector's quest to understand what truly brings happiness to others, as he struggles to find it for himself. As he travels across Europe, meeting various individuals from different walks of life, Hector begins to realize that happiness is not a fixed state, but rather a dynamic and subjective experience that can be shaped by one's relationships, experiences, and perspectives.

Throughout the film, the director, Peter Chelsom, skillfully weaves together elements of philosophy, psychology, and humanism, creating a rich tapestry of ideas that challenge viewers to reflect on their own values and aspirations. The movie also touches on the idea of the "in-between" moments – those fleeting instants when life's complexities intersect with happiness.

Ultimately, Hector and the Search for Happiness is a poignant exploration of the human condition, inviting audiences to ponder the nature of happiness, fulfillment, and purpose in an increasingly fast-paced and often chaotic world.

overview: Father Uffizi hunts vampires. He travels the world to behead them with his bullwhip, but his ultimate goal is to find the first vampire, Dracula. Medical students, Liz Blaine and Luke are charged with autopsying the body. When they open the abdominal cavity, they find that the liver and other organs are white, suggesting to Luke that the person did not produce his own blood but got it elsewhere, i.e., a vampire.
tagline: The terrifying sequel to Dracula 2000.
title: Dracula II: Ascension
plot:
Dracula II: Ascension is a 2003 American-Romanian direct-to-video horror film directed by Patrick Lussier, who wrote it with Joel Soisson, and the sequel to Dracula 2000. It stars Jason Scott Lee as Father Uffizi, a vampire-hunting priest, Diane Neal as the medical student Elizabeth Blaine, Craig Sheffer as her husband Lowell, Jason London as Luke, John Light as Eric and Stephen Billington as Dracula, with Roy Scheider as Cardinal Siqueros. It was filmed entirely in Romania at Castel Film Studios and released on 7 June 2003.

Uffizi kills two vampire twins but is bitten and infected, and holds the infection at bay by exposing himself to the sun. In New Orleans, Dracula's corpse arrives at the morgue where Elizabeth and her friend Luke work, and Elizabeth pricks her finger on one of its fangs. Her husband Lowell, a professor at her college with a fatal degenerative illness, tells them to take the body to his secluded family home, while a supposed wealthy investor offers to fund research into its secret of immortality. With fellow students Kenny and Tanya, they submerge the corpse in a bath of blood, and Dracula suddenly rises, kills Tanya and is held back by the investor, Eric, with a modified light gun. Tanya returns as a vampire, kills a police officer and is destroyed in sunlight by Uffizi, who has learned that Dracula is Judas Iscariot and seeks to grant him absolution. The group chains Dracula in an abandoned pool under ultraviolet light and Luke surrounds him with wards, while Elizabeth is increasingly drawn to him. The greedy Kenny injects himself with Dracula's blood, becomes a vampire and is beheaded by Uffizi. Elizabeth injects Lowell with the blood after Dracula lures him into the pool, and Lowell regains the ability to walk, only to reveal that there was no investor and that he and Eric had used the others to cure himself and to profit from an immortality serum. Uffizi kills Lowell, now a vampire, and Dracula breaks free, mauls Eric, who returns as a vampire and is destroyed by Luke, and slips through the wards. Elizabeth, already turned, refuses to step into sunlight. Uffizi overpowers the weakened Dracula and begins the rite of absolution, but Dracula torments him with visions of Christ's betrayal and crucifixion, and Elizabeth wounds the priest and leaves with Dracula, who spares Uffizi knowing he will keep hunting him.

It was shot alongside Dracula III: Legacy (2005). Critics were largely negative; it holds a 0% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: A graduate student, who is trying to finish the last of her research on a book project that she hopes will help her down-on-her-luck mother, brings friends to a house with a dark past, where they soon unwittingly summon an evil entity who makes the house part of its game…
title: Ouija House
plot:
Ouija House is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of meddling with forces beyond our understanding.

The movie follows a group of friends who, while exploring an abandoned house, inadvertently awaken malevolent entities through the use of a Ouija board. As they try to survive the night, they are forced to confront their deepest fears and the true cost of their curiosity.

At its core, Ouija House is a cautionary tale about the dangers of playing with forces we don't fully comprehend. The film explores themes of hubris, recklessness, and the devastating consequences that can result from underestimating the power of evil. Through the characters' experiences, the movie highlights the importance of respecting boundaries and acknowledging the unknown.

The film also touches on the idea of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and communities. As the characters face their fears and try to escape the house, they are forced to confront the dark secrets and traumas that have been buried within themselves and those around them.

Ultimately, Ouija House is a tense, unsettling horror film that explores the darker corners of human psychology and the supernatural. It's a thought-provoking commentary on the dangers of meddling with forces beyond our control and the devastating consequences that can result from our own hubris and recklessness.

overview: Four years after the destruction of Isla Nublar, Biosyn operatives attempt to track down Maisie Lockwood, while Dr Ellie Sattler investigates a genetically engineered swarm of giant insects.
tagline: The epic conclusion of the Jurassic era.
title: Jurassic World Dominion
plot:
Jurassic World Dominion is a 2022 science fiction adventure film directed by Colin Trevorrow, and it marks the final installment in the Jurassic World trilogy. The movie takes place four years after the events of Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom.

The story begins with Claire Dearing (Bryce Dallas Howard), now the director of the Biosyn Corporation, a biotech company that has been working on a top-secret project to harness the power of dinosaurs for human benefit. However, things take a turn when a massive T-Rex escapes from a lab and wreaks havoc on the city.

Meanwhile, Owen Grady (Chris Pratt) is living in Australia with his wife, Lily (DeWanda Wise), who has just given birth to their daughter. The family is trying to start a new life, but they soon find themselves caught up in the chaos caused by the escaped dinosaurs.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Biosyn's project has gone horribly wrong, and the company's CEO, Lewis Dodgson (Campbell Scott), will stop at nothing to capture the remaining dinosaurs and exploit their power for his own gain. Along the way, Owen and Claire must team up with a group of allies, including Dr. Ian Malcolm (Jeff Goldblum) and Dr. Ellie Sattler (Laura Dern), to take down Biosyn and save humanity from the dinosaurs.

Throughout the movie, Trevorrow explores themes of science gone wrong, corporate greed, and the consequences of playing God. The film also delves into the personal lives of the characters, particularly Owen and Claire, who must confront their past and figure out what they want for their future.

The movie features a star-studded cast, including Sam Neill, Laura Dern, Jeff Goldblum, and BD Wong, among others. The special effects are impressive, with stunning visuals that bring the dinosaurs to life in a way that's both thrilling and terrifying.

Overall, Jurassic World Dominion is an action-packed adventure that's full of twists and turns. While it may not be as tightly wound as some of its predecessors, the movie delivers on its promise of dinosaur-filled excitement and features plenty of heartwarming moments between Owen and Claire.

original_title: A Shaun the Sheep Movie: Farmageddon
overview: When an alien with amazing powers crash-lands near Mossy Bottom Farm, Shaun the Sheep goes on a mission to shepherd the intergalactic visitor home before a sinister organization can capture her.
tagline: Close encounters of the furred kind.
title: A Shaun the Sheep Movie: Farmageddon
plot:
A Shaun the Sheep Movie: Farmageddon is a 2019 stop-motion animated comedy-adventure film produced by Aardman Animations. The movie follows Shaun, a clever and resourceful sheep, as he embarks on an intergalactic adventure to save his farm from an alien invasion.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Friendship and teamwork: Throughout the film, Shaun is joined by his friends, including Timmy, Bitzer, and the rest of the flock, who work together to overcome various challenges and defeat the aliens.
2. Bravery and selflessness: Shaun puts himself in harm's way to protect his farm and its inhabitants, demonstrating remarkable bravery and selflessness.
3. Creativity and resourcefulness: The film showcases Shaun's cleverness and ability to think outside the box, as he uses his wits to outsmart the aliens and save the day.
4. Loyalty and dedication: Shaun's loyalty to his friends and farm is unwavering, even in the face of danger and uncertainty.

The movie also explores some lighter themes, such as:

1. The importance of taking risks and trying new things: Shaun's decision to leave the safety of the farm and explore the galaxy leads to a series of exciting adventures.
2. The value of perseverance and determination: Despite facing numerous setbacks and obstacles, Shaun and his friends never give up, ultimately achieving their goal.

Overall, A Shaun the Sheep Movie: Farmageddon is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates friendship, teamwork, and creativity, while also showcasing the bravery and selflessness of its hero, Shaun.

overview: A young woman held in captivity discovers the realities of truth and lies in the outside world.
tagline: Discover your true nature
title: Wildling
plot:
Wildling is a 2018 Swedish drama film directed by Ivo Njooijer and produced by Film i Väst. The movie tells the story of a young girl, Elina, who is sent to live with her father in the wilderness after being accused of witchcraft.

The main theme of Wildling revolves around the struggle for identity and self-discovery. Elina's journey into the wilderness serves as a metaphor for her inner turmoil and her quest to find herself amidst the societal expectations and accusations that have defined her life so far. As she navigates the harsh environment, she begins to uncover fragments of her own past and the truth about her family's history.

The film also explores themes of isolation, loneliness, and the human need for connection. Elina's experiences in the wilderness serve as a catalyst for her growth, forcing her to confront her emotions and develop a deeper understanding of herself and those around her. The movie delves into the complexities of female relationships, particularly between mothers and daughters, highlighting the intricate web of love, trust, and betrayal that can exist within these bonds.

Furthermore, Wildling touches on the idea of societal expectations and the consequences of being different. Elina's accusations of witchcraft serve as a symbol for the fear and mistrust that often accompanies those who do not conform to societal norms. The film raises questions about the nature of truth, power, and the impact of our actions on others.

Overall, Wildling is a thought-provoking drama that explores the complexities of human relationships, identity, and self-discovery in a hauntingly beautiful and atmospheric setting.

overview: A divorced dad and his ex-con brother resort to a desperate scheme in order to save their family's farm in West Texas.
tagline: Blood always follows money.
title: Hell or High Water
plot:
Hell or High Water is a 2016 American crime drama film directed by David Mackenzie and written by Taylor Sheridan. The movie stars Chris Pine, Ben Foster, Jeff Bridges, and Toni Collette.

The story begins with two brothers, Toby (Ben Foster) and Tanner (Chris Pine), who are struggling to make ends meet in rural Texas. After their father's death, the brothers are forced to take over his mortgage payments for a large sum of money. However, they soon discover that the bank is unwilling to work with them, leading them to come up with a plan to rob several banks across Texas.

The brothers' motivations for robbing the banks are complex and multifaceted. On one hand, they are desperate to save their family's farm from foreclosure. On the other hand, they are also seeking revenge against the bank that has wronged them in the past. As they embark on their heist, they begin to develop a sense of camaraderie and brotherly love.

As the brothers continue to rob banks, they attract the attention of Texas Ranger Marcus Hamilton (Jeff Bridges), who is determined to bring them to justice. However, as Hamilton delves deeper into the case, he begins to see the brothers in a different light. He becomes fascinated by their story and starts to question his own motivations for pursuing them.

Meanwhile, Toby's wife, Ali (Toni Collette), is struggling to cope with her husband's absence and the financial strain of raising their two children on her own. As the situation escalates, she begins to realize that her family's fate is inextricably linked to her husband's actions.

Throughout the film, Mackenzie uses the Texas landscape as a character in its own right, capturing the beauty and desolation of the rural landscape. The cinematography is stunning, with sweeping vistas and intimate close-ups that bring the characters and their world to life.

As the story unfolds, the brothers' actions become increasingly desperate and reckless. They are forced to confront the consequences of their choices, including the risk of imprisonment and the potential harm they may cause to innocent people.

In the end, the film builds towards a tense and emotional confrontation between the brothers and Hamilton. The outcome is far from certain, leaving the audience on the edge of their seats as they wonder what will happen next.

Ultimately, Hell or High Water is a powerful exploration of family, loyalty, and redemption. It is a story about two brothers who are driven by love and desperation to do whatever it takes to protect their family and their way of life. The film's themes of brotherly love and the complexities of human relationships are both poignant and thought-provoking.

The performances in the film are outstanding, with Ben Foster and Chris Pine delivering nuanced and compelling portrayals of the brothers. Jeff Bridges brings his signature gravitas to the role of Hamilton, while Toni Collette shines as Toby's wife, Ali.

Overall, Hell or High Water is a gripping and emotionally resonant film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the consequences of our choices.

original_title: Go! Go! Cory Carson: Chrissy Takes the Wheel
overview: From arcade games to sled days and hiccup cures, Cory Carson’s curious little sister Chrissy speeds off on her own for fun and adventure all over town!
title: Go! Go! Cory Carson: Chrissy Takes the Wheel
plot:
Into the Wild is a biographical drama film directed by Sean Penn, released in 2007. The movie is based on the life of Christopher McCandless, an American young man who abandoned his material possessions and hitchhiked to Alaska with the intention of living off the land.

The film begins with Chris McCandless (played by Emile Hirsch), a recent college graduate from a wealthy family in Carthage, Missouri. Chris's parents, Walt (Vince Vaughn) and Billie (Catherine Keener), are portrayed as loving but also somewhat neglectful, having given their son the freedom to explore his own path in life.

Chris becomes increasingly disillusioned with the materialism and superficiality of modern society, feeling suffocated by the expectations placed upon him. He decides to leave behind his comfortable life and embark on a journey of self-discovery, inspired by the writings of Henry David Thoreau's Walden.

The film follows Chris as he travels across the country, hitchhiking and working odd jobs to save money for his trip to Alaska. Along the way, he meets various characters who influence his worldview, including Wayne Westerberg (Hal Holbrook), a grizzled old truck driver who teaches him about the importance of living in the moment.

In 1992, Chris arrives in Anchorage, Alaska, and begins his journey into the wilderness. He adopts the alias "Alexander Supertramp" and sets out to live off the land, foraging for food and building a shelter. The film depicts Chris's struggles with the harsh environment, including encounters with bears, mosquitoes, and extreme weather conditions.

As the seasons change, Chris becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, struggling to adapt to the unforgiving wilderness. He begins to question his decision to leave behind civilization, feeling overwhelmed by the vastness of nature.

The film takes a tragic turn when Chris's bus breaks down on the side of the road, and he is forced to abandon his vehicle. In an attempt to survive, Chris sets fire to his bus, but the flames spread out of control, consuming everything in their path.

In the end, Chris's body is discovered by two hunters, who report him missing to the authorities. The film ends with a sense of melancholy and regret, as Chris's parents receive news of his death, realizing too late that they had failed to connect with their son on a deeper level.

Throughout the film, Sean Penn's direction weaves together themes of identity, community, and the human relationship with nature. Emile Hirsch delivers a powerful performance as Chris McCandless, capturing the complexity and vulnerability of this enigmatic young man. The cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the stunning beauty of Alaska's wilderness.

Overall, Into the Wild is a thought-provoking film that raises questions about the human condition and our place in the world. It is a poignant reminder of the importance of connection, community, and living life on one's own terms.

overview: Acclaimed writer and historian Deborah E. Lipstadt must battle for historical truth to prove the Holocaust actually occurred when David Irving, a renowned denier, sues her for libel.
tagline: The whole world knows the Holocaust happened. Now she needs to prove it.
title: Denial
plot:
Denial is a 2016 biographical drama film directed by Mick Jackson and written by David Hare, adapted from Deborah Lipstadt's 2005 book History on Trial: My Day in Court with a Holocaust Denier. It dramatizes Irving v Penguin Books Ltd, the libel case brought against Lipstadt by the Holocaust denier David Irving. Rachel Weisz stars as Lipstadt, with Timothy Spall as Irving, Tom Wilkinson as the barrister Richard Rampton, Andrew Scott as the solicitor Anthony Julius, Alex Jennings as Justice Charles Gray and Mark Gatiss as the historian Robert Jan van Pelt, with Jack Lowden and Caren Pistorius.

Lipstadt, an American professor of Holocaust studies, has a lecture disrupted by Irving, a British writer on Nazi Germany, who sues her and her publisher for libel in England over her description of him as a Holocaust denier. Because English libel law puts the burden of proof on the defendant, Lipstadt's team, headed by Julius and Rampton, must show that Irving deliberately lied about the Holocaust. Preparing the defense, Lipstadt and Rampton visit the site of Auschwitz, where van Pelt explains how the gas chambers operated. Lipstadt bristles at Rampton's seemingly irreverent manner, and her lawyers sideline her, believing her involvement would hurt the case, while British Jewish leaders urge her to settle. The team scores an early success by flattering Irving into accepting a trial before a judge rather than a jury he might sway. Representing himself, Irving tries to twist the evidence, and his claim that the gas chamber roofs had no holes for introducing Zyklon B ("no holes, no Holocaust") dominates the press. Lipstadt wants survivors to testify, but Julius fears Irving would humiliate them. Rampton wins her trust, then dismantles Irving in cross-examination, while historians such as Richard J. Evans expose the distortions in his work. At the close, Gray unsettles the defense by asking whether Irving can be lying if he sincerely believes his claims, but Rampton argues that Irving's antisemitism proves his falsifications were deliberate. Gray finds for the defense, and her lawyers remind her that her writing was the basis of the victory. Irving later claims on television that the trial largely went his way.

Shot in London and at the Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum, Denial premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on 11 September 2016. It received positive reviews, with an 82% Rotten Tomatoes rating that particularly praised Weisz's performance.

overview: When Gerda Wegener asks her husband Einar to fill in as a portrait model, Einar discovers the person she's meant to be and begins living her life as Lili Elbe. Having realized her true self and with Gerda's love and support, Lili embarks on a groundbreaking journey as a transgender pioneer.
tagline: Find the courage to be yourself.
title: The Danish Girl
plot:
The Danish Girl is a 2015 biographical drama film directed by Tom Hooper, produced by Tessa Ross and produced by in association with Cross Creek Pictures, Summit Entertainment, and Working Title Films.

The main themes of The Danish Girl include:
