1. Self-discovery: The film tells the story of Lili Elbe, a Danish artist who undergoes sex reassignment surgery to become a woman. The movie explores her journey of self-discovery and acceptance as she navigates her identity.
2. Love and relationships: The film highlights the complex and loving relationship between Lili and her wife, Gerda Wegener. Their bond is tested as Lili's transition unfolds, but ultimately proves to be a source of strength and support for both characters.
3. Identity and authenticity: The Danish Girl explores the tension between societal expectations and individual identity. Lili's desire to live authentically as a woman is met with resistance from those around her, leading to a struggle for acceptance and understanding.
4. Artistic expression: As an artist, Lili finds solace in her work, which becomes a means of self-expression and empowerment. The film showcases her talent and creativity, highlighting the importance of art in navigating the challenges of identity.

The movie features stunning performances from Eddie Redmayne as Lili Elbe and Alicia Vikander as Gerda Wegener, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

overview: When a frightening wave of violence sweeps through New York City, troubled cop Sarchie fails to find a rational explanation for the bizarre crimes. However, his eyes are opened to a frightening alternate reality when renegade Jesuit priest Mendoza convinces him that demonic possession may be to blame for the gruesome murders. Together, they wage a valiant supernatural struggle to rid the city of an otherworldly evil.
tagline: You haven’t seen true evil.
title: Deliver Us from Evil
plot:
Deliver Us from Evil is a supernatural thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between good and evil. The movie follows an NYPD detective, Jack O'Malley, who teams up with a priest to solve a series of gruesome murders in New York City.

At its core, Deliver Us from Evil explores the theme of demonic possession and the struggle for redemption. The film's protagonist, Jack O'Malley, is a complex character whose own personal demons (literally and figuratively) make him an unlikely partner for the priest. As they delve deeper into the mystery, they must confront their own faith and the existence of evil in the world.

The movie also touches on the theme of corruption and the moral decay that can occur when individuals are consumed by their own darkness. The villainous character, Malus, is a master manipulator who uses his cunning and intelligence to spread chaos and destruction throughout the city. Through Malus's character, the film highlights the dangers of unchecked ambition and the devastating consequences of allowing evil to consume one's soul.

Furthermore, Deliver Us from Evil explores the theme of faith and spirituality in a world that often seems devoid of both. The priest's character serves as a symbol of hope and redemption, offering a sense of comfort and solace in a time of great turmoil. As the story unfolds, the film raises questions about the nature of evil and whether it can be defeated through faith alone.

Overall, Deliver Us from Evil is a gripping thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes of demonic possession, corruption, faith, and redemption.

overview: Stevie is a sweet 13-year-old about to explode. His mom is loving and attentive, but a little too forthcoming about her romantic life. His big brother is a taciturn and violent bully. So Stevie searches his working-class Los Angeles suburb for somewhere to belong. He finds it at the Motor Avenue skate shop.
tagline: fall. get back up.
title: mid90s
plot:
"Mid90s" is a 2018 coming-of-age drama film directed by Jonah Hill, not produced by Scott Rudin Productions.

The movie follows the story of Stevie, a young skater who moves to Los Angeles with his single mother. He finds solace in a group of friends at a skate park, where he learns valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and growing up.

Some of the main themes of "Mid90s" include:

1. Friendship: The film explores the strong bonds between Stevie and his friends, who become like a surrogate family to him.
2. Identity: As Stevie navigates adolescence, he struggles to find his place in the world and define himself outside of his relationships with others.
3. Family: The movie highlights the complexities of Stevie's relationship with his mother, who is trying to rebuild her life after a divorce.
4. Coming-of-age: "Mid90s" is a classic coming-of-age story, where Stevie learns to navigate the challenges of growing up and finding his own path in life.

Scott Rudin Productions was not involved in the production of this film.

belongs_to_collection.name: Nobody Sleeps in the Woods Tonight Collection

original_title: W lesie dziś nie zaśnie nikt 2
overview: When something horrible happens to the only survivor of a bloody massacre, an insecure rookie cop must overcome his fears to stop further carnage.
title: Nobody Sleeps in the Woods Tonight 2
plot:
Nobody Sleeps in the Woods Tonight 2 (Polish: W lesie dziś nie zaśnie nikt 2) is a 2021 Polish supernatural slasher film, the sequel to Nobody Sleeps in the Woods Tonight (2020). Bartosz M. Kowalski again directed, writing the screenplay with Mirella Zaradkiewicz. Julia Wieniawa, Wojciech Mecwaldowski, Izabela Dabrowska and Michal Zbroja return from the first film, while Mateusz Więcławek and Zofia Wichlacz take over as the new leads.

Lonely young policeman Adam Adamiec learns from his boss, Sergeant Waldek, that a pair of deformed twin brothers have been arrested on the word of teenager Zosia, the only survivor of a massacre of her friends at a nearby camp. Waldek takes Zosia back to the twins' cabin to investigate, leaving Adam in charge. While the sergeant is away from her, part of the meteorite that mutated the twins splits open and releases a substance that turns Zosia into a mutant like them, and she kills Waldek. When he stops answering, Adam and his colleague Wanessa find the cabin wrecked and Waldek dead. Wanessa calls in two hunters, Mariusz and Slawek, but after Slawek traps his hands in a bear trap, the group shelters at the abandoned camp, where they find a frightened prostitute, Janeczka, whose companion Oliwier has been murdered outside.

Slawek bleeds to death, and a plan to lure Zosia using Janeczka as bait backfires when Zosia kills both Mariusz and Janeczka. Cornered in a cabin, Adam cannot bring himself to shoot her, and Wanessa shoves him toward Zosia and escapes. Zosia infects him through a stinger in her throat, and, able to talk with her in a language only they share, Adam learns they are monsters carrying an evil from the moon. Persuaded to kill whomever he chooses, he murders a man who abuses his dog, and the two become lovers. Zosia plans to free the twins and bring about the apocalypse, but the brothers refuse to leave their cell. Wanessa arrives armed with a machine gun and throws a grenade that fails to go off. When Adam hesitates, Zosia kills Wanessa herself, calls him a coward and walks out, only to be run down by special forces vehicles. Adam is captured, and one of the twins accidentally sets off the grenade, killing both brothers and destroying the station. Adam ends up in a laboratory as a test subject.

Więcławek plays Adam, Wichlacz plays Wanessa, Wieniawa plays Zosia, Andrzej Grabowski plays Waldek, Sebastian Stankiewicz plays Mariusz, Dabrowska plays Janeczka, Mecwaldowski plays Oliwier and Zbroja plays the twins.

overview: Two fugitives land in hot water when they take a hostage who poses a threat to their well-being.
tagline: Seclusion. Seduction. Survival.
title: Restraint
plot:
Restraint is a 2008 Australian thriller directed by David Denneen and written by Dave Warner. Teresa Palmer and Travis Fimmel star as Dale and Ron, a pair of fugitives, and Stephen Moyer plays Andrew Shepard, the reclusive estate owner they take hostage; Vanessa Redgrave makes a cameo.

Before the story opens, Ron has killed Dale's boss, the owner of a strip club. On the run, the couple murder a gas station attendant who notices the body in their car's trunk. They stumble upon Andrew's grand country estate and decide to hide there until the manhunt dies down. Andrew is an agoraphobic art dealer. The volatile Ron abuses him and threatens to kill him until Dale intervenes. Andrew offers them 40,000 Australian dollars and valuable jewelry to help them escape, but someone must collect them from the bank, so he proposes that Dale go in the guise of his fiancée, Gabrielle. Dale twice visits the bank without arousing suspicion.

Meanwhile Andrew tells Ron that Gabrielle left him after an affair with his father, who paid her to go, and that he then hired a hit man to kill his father. To save his own life, Andrew offers Ron a photograph proving the murder as leverage, and while supposedly fetching it, he locks Ron in the cellar, but Ron escapes and takes control again. When Dale returns, partly seduced by Andrew and his way of life, she turns their shotgun on Ron as he moves to kill Andrew, not realizing that it is unloaded. Ron knocks her out and leaves her in a locked car filling with exhaust fumes, taunting Andrew to overcome his agoraphobia to save her. Andrew rescues her and wounds Ron, and the revived Dale finishes Ron off. When Andrew reaches for the phone to call the police, Dale stops him by resuming her role as Gabrielle and, at his prompting, tells him in Gabrielle's voice that she loves him, and they sleep together. Asked what would happen if Gabrielle came back, Andrew assures Dale that she is gone as he burns Gabrielle's passport, suggesting he may have killed her. Later he plays Wagner alone downstairs in apparent triumph while Dale gazes sadly from an upstairs window.

More than half the budget came from the Film Finance Corporation, and the film was shot in 2005 near Goulburn and Camden in New South Wales. Planned for release by Accent Entertainment in May 2006, it was cut from 120 to 90 minutes after several test screenings, which also led to a more ambiguous ending. It eventually played in a single Sydney cinema in April 2009.

overview: Wallace rents out Gromit's former bedroom to a penguin, who takes up an interest in the techno pants created by Wallace. However, Gromit later learns that the penguin is a wanted criminal.
title: The Wrong Trousers
plot:
The Wrong Trousers is a stop-motion animated comedy film directed by Nick Park, produced by Peter Lord and David Sproxton, and released in 1993. 

The main theme of The Wrong Trousers revolves around the story of Fidget, an eccentric inventor who creates a pair of robotic trousers that become self-aware and start causing chaos in his life. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that the true antagonist is not the robots but rather Fidget's own insecurities and fears.

The film explores themes of loneliness, rejection, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. Fidget's creation of the robotic trousers serves as a metaphor for his desire to be accepted and loved by others, which ultimately leads to his downfall.

Throughout the film, Park uses humor, satire, and clever storytelling to poke fun at societal norms and expectations, particularly those related to masculinity and relationships. The Wrong Trousers is also notable for its commentary on the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of humility.

The character of Fidget himself serves as a symbol of vulnerability and the human need for connection. His journey from loneliness to acceptance is both poignant and entertaining, making The Wrong Trousers a heartwarming and hilarious film that has become a beloved classic in the world of animation.

overview: A single mom and her two boys help take care of their grandmother with mystical powers.
title: Mercy
plot:
Mercy is a 2014 American supernatural horror film directed by Peter Cornwell from a screenplay by Matt Greenberg, loosely based on Stephen King's short story "Gramma", collected in Skeleton Crew. Chandler Riggs stars as George, with Joel Courtney as his brother Buddy, Frances O'Connor as their mother Rebecca, Shirley Knight as their grandmother Mercy, Mark Duplass as their Uncle Lanning, Dylan McDermott as the neighbour and photographer Jim Swann, and Eddie Jones as the local pastor. Jason Blum produced it through Blumhouse Productions with McG, who brought Greenberg's script to Blum.

The film opens with a young Mercy nursing a child as her husband Frank kills himself with an axe. Years later, when the elderly Mercy suffers a medical episode and slips into a strange stupor, the single mother Rebecca brings George and Buddy to live in the old woman's isolated, dilapidated country house so the family can care for her rather than send her to a home. George loves his grandmother, but he soon senses that something supernatural is wrong with her. By questioning the pastor and his hard-drinking, wisecracking uncle, he gradually pieces together the dark family secrets connected to a mysterious book of black magic: unable to have children, Mercy once read from the forbidden Necronomicon and made a pact with a demon named Hastur so that she could become a mother.

In a sequence drawn most directly from King's story, Rebecca takes Buddy to the hospital and George is left alone in the house with his grandmother. He believes she has died, only to be assailed by her witchcraft, and he flees to look for help, discovering that Jim, who has grown close to Rebecca, is not the ally he seemed. In the climax, the demon tries to drive George to kill himself in the same way as his grandfather, but he turns the axe on Mercy instead, and the family later buries her beneath a tree, a different ending from the short story's.

Mercy was eventually issued straight to DVD, Blu-ray and video on demand by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment on October 7, 2014. Reviews were largely unfavourable. Dread Central called it an absorbing if quirky suspense drama with strong performances, especially Knight's, but found its story unoriginal and its CGI excessive, and CinemaBlend argued that it buried King's personal, atmospheric tale under invented subplots and lacked any real scares.

overview: A long forgotten ancient spacecraft discovered on Earth. Investigations carried out by Scout transport her to the moon whereupon she meets the impressive machines preserving the wisdom of that long lost civilization.
title: Moontrap: Target Earth
plot:
Moontrap: Target Earth is a 2017 American science fiction film directed by Robert Dyke and written by Dyke and Tex Ragsdale, the team behind the 1989 cult film Moontrap, to which it is a belated follow-up with only a few nods to the original. Produced by MT2 Productions, it stars Sarah Butler as Sharon "Scout" Turner, Damon Dayoub as Daniel Allen and Charles Shaughnessy as Richard Kontral, with Jennifer Kincer, Niki Spiridakos, Chris Newman, Cara AnnMarie and Steven Dutton. First reported in 2014, it was released directly to DVD after a long delay.

An enormous ancient artifact is unearthed in a desert quarry. When its discoverer, Brian Carter (Newman), is murdered by Nicole (Kincer), the henchwoman of Kontral, an agent of a shadowy cabal, Kontral hires the researcher Daniel Allen and his assistant and lover Scout to translate the inscriptions on it, which reveal a 14,000-year-old love letter from a woman to her god. The object proves to be a spacecraft left behind by an advanced human civilization that predates recorded history, and it still appears to be functional. Once their work is done, the cabal tries to eliminate them; Daniel is killed and Scout, framed for his death, goes on the run, troubled by visions of an unknown woman who seems to be guiding her. Captured, she turns out to have a mysterious connection with the craft, and her presence awakens a red robot, which takes her and Kontral aboard and flies them to the Moon. There a blue robot attacks; Kontral tries to escape in the ship, and the two machines fight until the red one is destroyed. Using a stone it carried, Scout activates an ancient temple that gives the Moon a breathable atmosphere. Inside she finds Garen, the god of the Krell people, in stasis, and learns from Mya, the woman of her visions, that she has been chosen to fulfill Mya's failed destiny. Scout joins Garen in suspended animation, and the first plants sprout on the lunar surface.

Sony released the film on DVD in the United States in early 2017, and Gilt Edge Media issued it in the United Kingdom. Reviews were negative. Phil Wheat of Nerdly, a fan of the original, found it structurally confusing, like a fevered dream, and slow to reach the Moon, though he welcomed the return of the robots and its grotesque finale. Mana Pop called the script incoherent and the effects among the cheapest it had seen, and the German Lexikon des internationalen Films judged that it failed through both lack of competence and lack of money.

overview: Three friends in their mid-20s struggle to navigate their professional and personal lives, colliding head on with the messy, hilarious and dreadful growing pangs of adulthood.
tagline: Love, sex, relationships and everything in between
title: All About Sex
plot:
All About Sex, also known as Natural Disasters, is a 2021 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Dakota Gorman in her feature directorial debut. Gorman loosely based the story on her own experiences of battling depression and the anxieties of early adulthood. Produced by Salt & Light Films in association with Warrior Woman Productions, with Nicole Rio and Kelly Bumford as producers, it stars Gorman, Natalee Linez and Emma Deckers, with Dillon Lane, Matt Angel, Chris Costanzo, James Hyde and Parvesh Cheena in supporting roles. Gravitas Ventures acquired the North American rights in January 2021 and Myriad Pictures handled international sales; in the United Kingdom, Signature Entertainment released it digitally on 26 July 2021. The film runs about 75 minutes.

The film follows three best friends in their mid-twenties, Sage (Gorman), Casey (Linez) and Morgan (Deckers), who are caught in the grip of quarter-life crises as they try to balance their careers and their love lives and stumble through the messy, embarrassing and confusing pitfalls of becoming adults. Sage is a talented graphic artist who spends her time complaining in a coffee shop, and the friends talk frankly about sex and lean on one another as each of them stalls on the way to true adulthood. Morgan's extracurricular activities eventually catch up with her, even as she falls in love with Lowick (Angel), a kind and ordinary man. Across the intersecting storylines the women's sexual encounters, from the absurd to the upsetting, serve as a springboard for exploring mental illness and the expectations society places on young people.

Umar Ali of The Upcoming found the film unabashedly crude and frank but said its script balances the ribald jokes with genuine pathos and strong character development; he praised the three leads for carrying the film where the screenplay falters and called it an ambitious, if rough-edged, and thoroughly entertaining exploration of adulthood. Shane A. Bassett of The People's Movies described it as a kind of millennial mumblecore romance that goes nowhere yet remains enlightening, singling out Deckers as the standout and comparing Gorman's potential to that of Greta Gerwig. Other reviewers felt the script was contrived and unfocused.

overview: Less than 24 hours into his parole, charismatic thief Danny Ocean is already rolling out his next plan: In one night, Danny's hand-picked crew of specialists will attempt to steal more than $150 million from three Las Vegas casinos. But to score the cash, Danny risks his chances of reconciling with ex-wife, Tess.
tagline: Are you in or out?
title: Ocean's Eleven
plot:
Ocean's Eleven is a heist film directed by Steven Soderbergh, released in 2001 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie follows the story of Danny Ocean (played by George Clooney), a charismatic thief who plans to rob three Las Vegas casinos simultaneously.

The story begins with Danny Ocean, a former casino security expert, being released from prison after serving a five-year sentence for a previous heist. He reunites with his old friend and partner-in-crime, Rusty Ryan (played by Brad Pitt). The two men devise a plan to rob three of the most secure casinos in Las Vegas: the Bellagio, the Mirage, and the MGM Grand.

The team consists of Danny's old crew, including Basher Tarr (Carl Reiner), Saul Bloom (Scott Caan), Livingston Dell (Eddie Jemison), and Yen (Shaobo Qin). They also recruit a few new members, including Terry Benedict's (Andy García) ex-wife, Tess Ocean (Julia Roberts), who becomes an integral part of the team.

The plan is to infiltrate the casinos by posing as high-rollers, gaining access to the vaults, and using advanced technology to disable the security systems. The team faces numerous challenges, including a rival thief, Reuben Tishkoff's (Elliott Gould), who tries to sabotage their plans.

As the heist unfolds, Danny's personal life becomes complicated. He is still in love with Tess, but she has moved on and is now married to Terry Benedict, a ruthless casino owner. The team must navigate the complex web of relationships and alliances to achieve their goal.

The climax of the movie takes place at the Bellagio, where the team executes their plan flawlessly. However, things take a turn when Danny's true intentions are revealed, and he decides to rob Terry Benedict instead of just the vaults. The team successfully pulls off the heist, but not without some unexpected twists and turns.

In the end, Danny and his crew escape with millions of dollars, leaving behind a trail of chaos and destruction. As for Tess, she finally finds her way back to Danny, and they share a romantic moment together.

Overall, Ocean's Eleven is a clever and entertaining heist film that features a talented ensemble cast, witty dialogue, and impressive action sequences. The movie's success can be attributed to its well-crafted plot, memorable characters, and Soderbergh's direction, which brings the story to life with style and sophistication.

overview: A high school swim champion with a troubled past enrolls in the U.S. Coast Guard's 'A' School, where legendary rescue swimmer, Ben Randall teaches him some hard lessons about loss, love, and self-sacrifice.
tagline: How Do You Decide Who Lives Or Who Dies?
title: The Guardian
plot:
The Guardian is a 2006 British drama film directed by Andrew Levitas and written by Andrew Levitas and David Nicholls. 

The movie revolves around the story of Will McLeod, played by Kevin Durand, who is a young man struggling to find his place in the world after being released from prison. He meets a homeless man named Jack McBeef, played by Nick Nolte, who teaches him about life and helps him discover his own identity.

The main themes of The Guardian include:

1. Redemption: Will's journey is one of redemption as he tries to make amends for past mistakes and find a new path in life.
2. Friendship: The unlikely friendship between Will and Jack serves as the heart of the film, highlighting the importance of human connection and mentorship.
3. Self-discovery: Through his experiences with Jack, Will learns to let go of his anger and bitterness, and discovers his own strengths and weaknesses.
4. Social commentary: The film touches on issues such as homelessness, poverty, and social inequality, raising awareness about these pressing concerns.

The Guardian received positive reviews for its nuanced portrayal of complex characters and its thought-provoking themes.

overview: Based on the true nail-biting mission that captivated the world. Twelve boys and the coach of a Thai soccer team explore the Tham Luang cave when an unexpected rainstorm traps them in a chamber inside the mountain. Entombed behind a maze of flooded cave tunnels, they face impossible odds. A team of world-class divers navigate through miles of dangerous cave networks to discover that finding the boys is only the beginning.
tagline: 5000 people, 17 countries, 1 miracle that united the world.
title: Thirteen Lives
plot:
Thirteen Lives is a 2022 biographical drama film directed by Ron Howard, based on the true story of the 2018 Thai cave rescue. The movie stars Dwayne Johnson, Yeasmin "Yaya" Fonseca, and Samson Kayo.

The film begins with Aron Ralston (played by Jake Gyllenhaal), an American outdoorsman who becomes trapped in a narrow canyon in Utah while on a solo hike. He is forced to amputate his own arm to free himself from the boulder that has pinned him down for five days. The incident leaves him emotionally scarred and sets him on a path of self-discovery.

The story then shifts to the 2018 Thai cave rescue, where a group of young soccer players, led by 12-year-old Lukman (played by Chaiyaphum Suntivong), become trapped in the Tham Luang Nang Non cave in northern Thailand. The cave's narrow passages and fast-flowing water make it impossible for them to escape on their own.

As the rescue efforts begin, a team of international experts, led by John Volanthen (played by Viggo Mortensen) and Rick Stanton (played by Joel Edgerton), is assembled to help locate the missing boys. The team faces numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, flooding, and limited access to medical supplies.

Meanwhile, back in the United States, Aron Ralston becomes involved with a group of young Thai soccer players who are training in Utah. He begins to mentor them, sharing his expertise on wilderness survival and teamwork. One of these players, Lukman, is particularly drawn to Aron's teachings and eventually joins him on an expedition to the cave.

As the rescue efforts progress, the team faces numerous setbacks, including a failed attempt to extract one of the boys using a makeshift rope. The situation becomes increasingly dire as the days turn into weeks, and the world watches anxiously for news of the missing boys.

In a dramatic climax, John Volanthen and Rick Stanton finally locate Lukman and his friends in the cave. They work tirelessly to guide them out of the cave, facing numerous challenges along the way. The rescue is ultimately successful, but not without its costs: one of the boys dies during the ordeal.

The film ends with Aron Ralston reflecting on the experience and how it has changed him. He realizes that his own near-death experience in the canyon had prepared him for the challenges he faced in the cave. The movie concludes with a message about the power of teamwork, perseverance, and the importance of never giving up.

Overall, Thirteen Lives is a gripping and emotional drama that explores themes of survival, redemption, and the human spirit.

overview: A quest that begins as a personal vendetta for the fierce Cimmerian warrior soon turns into an epic battle against hulking rivals, horrific monsters, and impossible odds, as Conan realizes he is the only hope of saving the great nations of Hyboria from an encroaching reign of supernatural evil.
tagline: Enter an age undreamed of
title: Conan the Barbarian
plot:
Conan the Barbarian is a 2011 American sword-and-sorcery film based on Robert E. Howard's character, directed by Marcus Nispel and written by Thomas Dean Donnelly, Joshua Oppenheimer and Sean Hood. Jason Momoa stars as Conan, with Leo Howard as the young Conan, Rachel Nichols as Tamara, Stephen Lang as the warlord Khalar Zym, Rose McGowan as his daughter Marique, Ron Perlman as Conan's father Corin, Saïd Taghmaoui as the thief Ela-Shan and Nonso Anozie as Artus, while Morgan Freeman narrates.

Conan, born on a battlefield, is the son of Corin, a Cimmerian chieftain and blacksmith. His village is destroyed by Khalar Zym, who is gathering the pieces of the Mask of Acheron, an artifact made by sorcerers to enslave the world and later broken up among the barbarian tribes, so that he can resurrect his dead wife, the evil sorceress Maliva, and conquer Hyboria. Zym takes the Cimmerians' fragment, kills Corin and leaves Conan the only survivor. Years later, Conan has become a pirate still hunting Zym. In Messantia, he gets himself captured with Ela-Shan to reach Lucius, one of Zym's men, and learns that Zym needs a pure-blooded female descendant of the Acheronians to unleash the mask's power before Conan frees Lucius's prisoners, who kill him. When Zym and Marique attack a monastery, the monk Fassir sends his pupil Tamara, the descendant they seek, to flee. Conan rescues her, captures Zym's lieutenant Remo and catapults him back into Zym's camp as a message. In a confrontation, Zym recognizes the boy he spared, and Marique poisons Conan, who is saved by Tamara and recovers on his ship. Conan heads for Zym's kingdom, and Tamara, sent after him by Artus, spends the night with him, but is captured on her way back to the ship. With Ela-Shan's help, Conan breaks into Zym's castle, where Zym uses Tamara's blood to restore the mask and plans to make her body a vessel for Maliva's soul. Conan fights a tentacled creature guarding the dungeons, frees Tamara, reclaims his father's sword and cuts off Marique's hand before she is killed. As Maliva's spirit begins to possess Tamara on a bridge, Conan destroys it, sending Zym into the lava below. He returns Tamara to her birthplace and visits his old village, content that he has avenged his father.

Released in August 2011, it was a critical and commercial failure that grossed about $48.8 million against a $90 million budget and holds a 25% Rotten Tomatoes rating, though it earned a Saturn Award nomination for its makeup.

original_title: デジモンアドベンチャー tri. 第１章「再会」
overview: After years of inactivity, the DigiDestined regroup with their Digimon to save their world, but have the years changed their characters too much?
title: Digimon Adventure tri. Part 1: Reunion
plot:
Digimon Adventure tri. Part 1: Reunion (Japanese: Saikai) is a 2015 Japanese animated adventure film produced by Toei Animation, the first of six films in the Digimon Adventure tri. series created to celebrate the fifteenth anniversary of the Digimon franchise. Directed by Keitaro Motonaga from a screenplay by Yūko Kakihara, with character designs by Atsuya Uki, it serves as a direct sequel to the television series Digimon Adventure and Digimon Adventure 02 and follows the original eight DigiDestined during their high school years. The project was announced in 2014 as a television series and was reconceived in May 2015 as a theatrical film series.

Set in 2005, six years after the first adventure, the film finds Tai Kamiya restless and without direction: his friends have drifted apart, he cannot gather them for one of his soccer games, and he has no plans for the future. When a Kuwagamon tears through Odaiba, Tai races to the scene, and Agumon arrives to digivolve and fight back as the battle spreads to the airport. Watching the destruction and the injured bystanders, Tai is shaken by the realization that the DigiDestined's battles cause real harm. A new connection to the Digital World is letting through infected Digimon more powerful than before, and the children of the second series appear to have been overwhelmed. Supported by a government task force aided by Gennai, the group reunites, including Mimi, who returns from America, but Tai clashes with Matt, who insists that only they can protect people. When the Royal Knight Alphamon attacks, apparently hunting a mysterious new DigiDestined named Meiko Mochizuki and her partner Meicoomon, Matt pulls Tai out of his paralysis and their partners combine into Omnimon, yet Tai hesitates at the decisive moment and Alphamon escapes, while the enigmatic Hackmon watches from the shadows.

Reunion opened in Japanese theaters on 21 November 2015 in a limited release, and was simulcast outside Japan by Crunchyroll in episodic form on the same day. It grossed about ¥230 million in Japan. An English dub distributed by Eleven Arts premiered at a Fathom Events screening in North America on 15 September 2016. Den of Geek's Shamus Kelley called it a model for how continuations of famous franchises should be made, praising its faithful characters and Tai's arc about responsibility, though he wished the female characters had more to do.

overview: Features Rev Run as he brings audiences on a hip-hop reimagining of The Nutcracker ballet set in NYC.
title: The Hip Hop Nutcracker
plot:
The Hip Hop Nutcracker is a 2022 American holiday dance special released on Disney+ that adapts the long-running stage production of the same name, a reimagining of Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker set to a remixed version of his score. Directed for the screen by Nikki Parsons and Elizabeth Avellan, it is emceed by the legendary Rev Run and features the dancer Mikhail Baryshnikov and the dance crew Jabbawockeez alongside Cache Melvin as Maria-Clara, Allison Holker and Stephen Boss as her parents, Comfort Fedoke as Drosselmeyer, Fik-Shun Stegall as a nut vendor and Jean Sok as the Mouse King.

The story moves the classic tale to a contemporary New York setting. The only thing young Maria-Clara wants for Christmas is for her mother and father, who once lit up the dance floor together, to reunite. Her wish might come true thanks to Drosselmeyer, a mysterious toy shop owner and wizard played as a voguing figure in a red cape, a vendor of nuts and a little midnight magic, while the Mouse King tries to stand in the way. Rather than dialogue, the plot is carried mostly by brief narrative captions and by the dancing itself, with Rev Run contributing rapped verses. The choreography tours roughly forty years of hip-hop dance, including breaking, voguing, turfing, popping and locking, while keeping traditional ballet in the mix. Sets include a row of brownstones that serves as the backdrop for the Baryshnikov and Jabbawockeez number, dreamlike expressionist designs and a combination nightclub and soda shop that replaces the ballet's Land of Sweets, where the moves and fashions of successive decades of hip-hop are celebrated.

The special premiered on Disney+ on 25 November 2022. Brett White of Decider recommended it, finding that the filmed version captured the kinetic energy of the stage show without feeling like a static recording, praising the sets, Fedoke's captivating Drosselmeyer and the way the special brings decades of hip-hop dance history into viewers' homes, and suggesting it would delight young dancers. He noted that the stage production predates Hamilton by several years and that a full-length filmed version of the stage show was also available to stream through PBS. Other reviewers praised the dancing while criticizing the editing and camera work.

overview: Six Californians start a club to discuss the works of Jane Austen. As they delve into Austen's literature, the club members find themselves dealing with life experiences that parallel the themes of the books they are reading.
tagline: You don't have to know the books to be in the club
title: The Jane Austen Book Club
plot:
The Jane Austen Book Club is a 2007 romantic comedy-drama film that explores the lives of four women who form a book club based on the works of Jane Austen. At its core, the movie delves into themes of female empowerment, friendship, and personal growth.

As the story unfolds, we see how these women, each with their own unique struggles and insecurities, find solace and support in their shared love of literature. Through their discussions and debates about Austen's novels, they begin to confront their own lives, relationships, and societal expectations. The film masterfully captures the complexities of female relationships, highlighting both the bonds of sisterhood and the challenges of navigating personal identity.

The movie also explores the theme of escapism, as the women use literature as a means of temporarily escaping the mundanity and difficulties of their daily lives. However, as they delve deeper into Austen's world, they begin to realize that the lines between reality and fiction are blurred, and that the lessons they learn from her novels can be applied to their own lives.

Furthermore, The Jane Austen Book Club touches on the theme of social class and status, as the women navigate their relationships with men and confront the societal expectations placed upon them. Through their interactions with the male characters in their lives, they are forced to reevaluate their own values and priorities.

Ultimately, the film is a heartwarming exploration of the transformative power of literature, friendship, and self-discovery. As the women find themselves and grow as individuals, they come to realize that true happiness and fulfillment can be found in the most unexpected places – within themselves, with each other, and through the timeless wisdom of Jane Austen's works.

overview: When nerdy high schooler Dani finally attracts the interest of her longtime crush, she lands in the cross hairs of his ex, a social media celebrity.
title: #realityhigh
plot:
#RealityHigh (stylized #REALITYHIGH) is a 2017 American teen comedy directed by Fernando Lebrija and released on Netflix on September 8, 2017. Set in Southern California, it follows a studious high school senior who is swept into the world of a social media celebrity and briefly loses sight of what matters to her. Nesta Cooper stars as the heroine, Dani Barnes, alongside Keith Powers as Cameron Drake, Alicia Sanz as Alexa Medina, Jake Borelli as Freddie Myers and Kate Walsh as Dr. Fiona Shively.

Dani is a straight-A student who loves dogs, volunteers at a local dog clinic and is determined to win a scholarship to the University of California, Davis. Seen as an unfashionable nerd, she has one real friend, Freddie, who secretly has feelings for her that she fails to notice, because she has been infatuated since childhood with Cameron, one of the most popular boys at school. Cameron dates Alexa, Dani's childhood best friend turned tormentor, an admired influencer with a large following across social media. When Alexa drops Cameron for another online star, Fousey, Dani and Cameron grow closer.

Suddenly Alexa wants to be friends again. She apologizes for the past, offers Dani a fresh start and draws her into her circle of extravagant shopping trips and parties. Dani enjoys the attention and new status, starts dressing and styling herself like Alexa and gradually loses her grip on what is important. She lets Freddie down by skipping his first paid gig and losing the venue for their animal rescue event, and she fails Cameron by missing his meet and his big television appearance and by staying silent about his UCLA acceptance in front of his father. Cameron breaks up with her, and Alexa then turns on her, posting a viral video that uses supposed evidence to paint Dani as a drunk and a stalker, which spawns cruel memes.

Dani's younger sister shows her support by unfollowing Alexa, and Dani patches things up with Freddie. She persuades the Bob's Big Boy restaurant to host the animal rescue event, and its success earns her the college recommendation Fiona had promised. At the senior class bonfire on the beach, where everyone gathers except Alexa, who is mourning the loss of her YouTube channel, Dani and Cameron kiss and reconcile.

The film received mostly negative reviews, holding a 40% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, while Common Sense Media gave it one star.

overview: When minor-league hockey player Derek Thompson -- who has a penchant for knocking out his opponents' teeth every time he plays -- disillusions a fan, he is sentenced to a stint for one week as a bona fide, tutu-clad, real-life tooth fairy. Soon, Derek is inspired to rekindle his youthful dreams.
tagline: You can't handle the tooth.
title: Tooth Fairy
plot:
Tooth Fairy is a family comedy film released in 2010, directed by Tom Shadyac and starring Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, Ashley Judd, and Regan Mitchell.

The movie begins with Derek Thompson (Johnson), a former hockey player who has lost his way in life. He's now working as an airport security guard, but he's unhappy with his job and feels unfulfilled. On Christmas Eve, Derek is involved in a car accident that kills the mother of his young daughter, Maggie (Regan Mitchell).

Feeling guilty and responsible for her mother's death, Derek decides to take care of Maggie on his own. However, he soon realizes that taking care of a child is not as easy as he thought it would be. Maggie's father, Mike (Jon Heder), is nowhere to be found, and Derek must navigate the challenges of single parenthood.

As part of the tradition of exchanging gifts for teeth under their pillow on Christmas Eve, Maggie loses her first tooth, which leads to a series of events that changes Derek's life forever. He discovers that he has the ability to fly by using his "fairy dust," a magical substance that allows him to leave gifts and collect teeth.

As Derek navigates his new role as a single father, he also starts to develop feelings for his colleague, Wendy (Ashley Judd). However, their relationship is complicated, and they must navigate their differences in order to be together.

Throughout the movie, Derek's character undergoes significant development. He learns to let go of his past and find a new sense of purpose as a single father. With the help of Maggie and his fairy dust, he discovers that being a good parent is not just about providing for your child's physical needs but also about being there for them emotionally.

The movie ends with Derek and Wendy finally getting together, and Derek finding a way to balance his life as a single father with his relationship. The film concludes on a heartwarming note, with Derek and Maggie flying off into the sky, ready for their next adventure together.

Overall, Tooth Fairy is a lighthearted and entertaining movie that explores themes of family, love, and redemption. With its blend of humor, action, and heart, it's a fun and engaging film that's suitable for both children and adults.

overview: Americans Amy, Stacy, Jeff and Eric look for fun during a sunny holiday in Mexico, but they get much more than that after visiting an archaeological dig in the jungle.
tagline: Terror has evolved.
title: The Ruins
plot:
The Ruins is a 2008 natural horror film directed by Carter Smith in his feature debut and written by Scott B. Smith from his own 2006 novel. Ben Stiller's Red Hour Films bought the screen rights from an outline while the author was still finishing the book, and asked him to write the script as well. Produced by Stuart Cornfeld, Jeremy Kramer and Chris Bender, with Stiller as executive producer, it was shot in Queensland, Australia, and the director said the killer vine was designed from elements of many real plants so it would look believable. DreamWorks and Paramount released the film in the United States on 4 April 2008.

Two young American couples, Amy and Jeff and Stacy and Eric, are vacationing in Mexico when they meet Mathias, a German tourist searching for his brother, Heinrich, last seen at an archaeological dig at a remote Mayan ruin. With Mathias's friend Dimitri, they reach the temple, where armed Mayan villagers confront them. When Amy steps on the vines covering the site, the villagers grow frantic and kill Dimitri, and the others flee up the temple steps. At the top they find an abandoned camp, a deep shaft and the sound of a phone ringing somewhere below. Lowering Mathias down the shaft, they lose him when the rope snaps and he is left paralyzed. The villagers, who fear the vines, will not let anyone who has touched them leave, and when Amy angrily throws a clump of vine at a boy, they kill him too.

Over the following days the vines creep into a cut on Stacy's leg and eat away Mathias's legs to the bone. Exploring the shaft, Amy and Stacy find a dead archaeologist and realize the "ringing" is made by the vine's flowers mimicking sound. Jeff amputates Mathias's legs, but the vines smother him while the others quarrel over Stacy's jealous accusation that Amy and Eric slept together. Convinced the vines are inside her, Stacy cuts at her own body, fatally stabs Eric and begs to die, and Jeff ends her life. To save Amy, Jeff covers her in blood, carries her down as though she were dead and distracts the villagers, who kill him while she runs for the jeep and escapes. Later, Dimitri's Greek friends arrive at the temple looking for him.

Jena Malone plays Amy, with Jonathan Tucker as Jeff, Shawn Ashmore as Eric, Laura Ramsey as Stacy and Joe Anderson as Mathias. Reviews were mixed, with 51% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and the film grossed about $22.8 million, short of its $25 million budget.

overview: In the 1820s, a frontiersman, Hugh Glass, sets out on a path of vengeance against those who left him for dead after a bear mauling.
production_companies: Hong Kong Alpha Motion Pictures Co.
tagline: (n. One who has returned, as if from the dead.)
title: The Revenant
plot:
The Revenant is a historical drama film directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu, released in 2015 by Regency Enterprises and New Line Cinema.

The story begins in 1823, during the early 19th century American fur trade era. Hugh Glass (played by Leonardo DiCaprio), a skilled trapper and explorer, is part of an expedition led by Captain Andrew Henry (Tom Hardy) to the western territories of North America. The group faces numerous challenges, including harsh weather conditions, hostile Native American tribes, and treacherous terrain.

During one of their hunting trips, Glass is brutally mauled by a bear while trying to protect his son, Hawk (Forrest Goodluck), who is also part of the expedition. Despite being left for dead, Glass manages to crawl back to the campsite, where he finds that his fellow trappers have abandoned him.

Glass's quest for revenge against those who betrayed and left him for dead becomes the central focus of the film. He sets out on a perilous journey across the wilderness, facing numerous obstacles, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and hostile Native American tribes.

As Glass navigates the unforgiving environment, he encounters John Fitzgerald (Tom Hardy), a fellow trapper who had been part of the expedition but was also left for dead. However, instead of helping Glass, Fitzgerald betrays him and steals his valuable possessions, including his rifle and supplies.

Glass's determination to survive and exact revenge on those who wronged him drives him forward, despite the numerous challenges he faces. He encounters various characters, including a Native American tribe that takes him in and teaches him their ways, as well as a group of fur traders who are also seeking to exploit the region's resources.

Throughout his journey, Glass undergoes a transformation from a broken and defeated man to a strong and determined individual. His physical and emotional scars serve as a reminder of his past traumas, but they also fuel his determination to survive and exact revenge on those who wronged him.

The film's climax features an intense and brutal confrontation between Glass and Fitzgerald, which ultimately leads to the death of both men. In the end, Glass emerges victorious, having survived against all odds and exacted his revenge on those who betrayed him.

The Revenant is a visually stunning film that showcases the harsh beauty of the American wilderness. The cinematography is breathtaking, with sweeping vistas and intimate close-ups that immerse the viewer in the world of the film. The performances by DiCaprio and Hardy are also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, The Revenant is a powerful and haunting film that explores themes of survival, revenge, and redemption in the face of unimaginable hardship.

overview: Attempting to recover from a recent family trauma by escaping into the woods for a peaceful hiking trip, an ex-lawman and his young son stumble across a dangerous contract killer.
tagline: Every killer meets his equal.
title: The Contract
plot:
The Contract is a German-American action thriller of 2006 directed by Bruce Beresford and written by the television writer Stephen Katz and John Darrouzet. Morgan Freeman stars as the professional assassin Frank Carden and John Cusack as Ray Keene, a teacher who becomes entangled in Carden's latest job during a camping trip with his son. Jamie Anderson, Alice Krige, Megan Dodds and Corey Johnson co-star.

Carden has been hired to kill Lydell Hammond Sr., a reclusive billionaire and outspoken opponent of stem cell research, but his plan collapses when he is hurt in a car crash. Hospital staff find his gun, and federal marshals come for him. Meanwhile Ray, a widower, ex-cop and awkward gym teacher, takes Chris on a wilderness hike to reconnect after catching him smoking marijuana. In the same forest, Carden's men ambush the marshals' convoy; the last survivor, before he dies, asks Ray to deliver the prisoner to the authorities.

Ray and Chris set out to march Carden out of the wilderness, pursued by his crew of highly trained former soldiers. The chase draws in a couple, Sandra and Lochlan, and Lochlan is killed. In a tense standoff at a cabin, Ray agrees to release Carden, but when one of the gunmen strikes Chris, Ray kills him and Sandra shoots another. Local police rescue Ray and Sandra, but Carden escapes, taking Chris as a hostage. Miles then orders Davis, Carden's newest recruit, to kill Carden and the boy and pin the blame on Carden, and to eliminate Ray too in case he knows anything.

Back home, Ray sees a news report describing Carden as someone who removes obstacles to progress, which helps him deduce the target. He goes to the funeral of Hammond's son to intercept Carden and unwittingly saves him from Davis, whom Carden kills with his own sniper rifle. The fight costs Carden his chance at Hammond, and he hands Ray the keys to the hotel room where Chris is being held before vanishing. In Washington, D.C., Carden confronts Miles, letting her know he is aware she ordered his death and warning her to leave Ray's family alone. Two weeks later, Ray is seeing Sandra, and during a barbecue a radio bulletin reports that Hammond has died in a boating accident; Ray realizes that Carden has completed his contract.

The film was shot almost entirely in Bulgaria, with the headquarters of DSK Bank among its main sets and scenes filmed on the Vitosha mountain. Despite its cast, it went direct to video in the United States and Europe, and reviews were negative.

overview: In a world where walking, talking, digitally connected bots have become children's best friends, an 11-year-old finds that his robot buddy doesn't quite work the same as the others do.
tagline: Best Friend Forever* (*battery life may vary)
title: Ron's Gone Wrong
plot:
Ron's Gone Wrong is a 2021 stop-motion animated comedy film directed by Sam Fell and Joel Crawford, produced by Illumination Entertainment and Universal Pictures.

The story revolves around Ron, an ordinary family dog who lives with his owner, Nick (voiced by Ben Schwartz), and his wife, Val (voiced by Jenny Slate). Ron's life is turned upside down when he discovers that he has the ability to grant wishes. Initially, Ron uses this power for personal gain, but soon realizes the consequences of his actions.

As Ron's wish-granting abilities grow stronger, chaos erupts in the town, and the family must navigate the mayhem caused by their mischievous dog. The film explores themes of responsibility, friendship, and the importance of learning from one's mistakes.

Throughout the movie, Ron's character undergoes significant development as he struggles to balance his desire for power with his loyalty to his family. Along the way, he befriends a stray cat named Chloe (voiced by Octavia Spencer), who becomes an unlikely ally in his quest to right the wrongs he has caused.

The film features stunning stop-motion animation, bringing the characters and their world to life in vivid detail. The voice cast delivers memorable performances, adding depth and humor to the story.

Ultimately, Ron must confront the consequences of his actions and learn to use his powers for good. With the help of his friends and family, Ron finds a way to restore balance to the town and rediscover the value of being a loyal companion.

Overall, Ron's Gone Wrong is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of responsibility, friendship, and personal growth.

overview: Anthony and his partner move into a loft in the now gentrified Cabrini-Green. After a chance encounter with an old-timer exposes Anthony to the true story behind Candyman, he unknowingly opens a door to a complex past that unravels his own sanity and unleashes a terrifying wave of violence.
tagline: Dare to say his name.
title: Candyman
plot:
Candyman is a 2021 supernatural horror film directed by Nia DaCosta, who wrote the screenplay with Jordan Peele and Win Rosenfeld. A direct sequel to the 1992 film and the fourth entry in the series derived from Clive Barker's short story "The Forbidden", it was produced by Peele's Monkeypaw Productions. Filming took place in Chicago in August and September 2019, and after three pandemic delays Universal released it in the United States on August 27, 2021.

In 1977, a boy at Chicago's Cabrini–Green housing project sees police beat to death Sherman Fields, a hook-handed man wrongly accused of hiding razor blades in candy. In 2019, artist Anthony McCoy, partner of gallery director Brianna Cartwright, hears the story of Helen Lyle, blamed for murders and a baby's abduction at Cabrini–Green decades earlier. There he is stung on the hand by a bee and meets laundromat owner William Burke, the boy who saw Sherman die, who tells him the legend of the Candyman: say the name five times into a mirror and the spirit will appear and kill you. Anthony builds an installation called "Say My Name" around the myth. After a gallery dealer and his girlfriend, then a critic, are murdered, and teenagers are killed after summoning the Candyman, Anthony grows obsessed, painting grisly portraits as the sting spreads over his body.

William explains that the legend began in the 1890s with Daniel Robitaille, an artist mutilated and burned alive after a white client's daughter, his lover, accused him of rape, and that other murdered innocent Black men have since joined the Candyman "hive"; these are the men Anthony has been painting. Anthony learns from his mother, Anne-Marie, that he was the baby taken the night Helen died, and that the killings blamed on Helen were the Candyman's. William, plotting revenge against gentrifiers, kidnaps Brianna, cuts off Anthony's hand, fits him with a hook and calls the police to make him the next martyr. Brianna kills William, but Anthony is shot dead by officers, who then pressure Brianna to back their story. She summons the Candyman in a car mirror; he appears as Anthony, slaughters the police and, taking Robitaille's face, tells her to "tell everyone".

Yahya Abdul-Mateen II plays Anthony, with Teyonah Parris as Brianna and Colman Domingo as William. Tony Todd and Vanessa Williams return. The film earned 84% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and grossed $77.4 million; DaCosta became the first Black female director with a US number one.

overview: Newly engaged Shelby John and Ruby Red want a fresh start after their struggles with addiction, but when Shelby discovers his beloved Ruby dead on their porch, he embarks on a vengeful killing spree of the dealers who supplied her. Armed with nothing but adrenaline and a nail gun, Shelby begins to unleash chaos on the town’s criminal underbelly, as he hunt’s down crime lord Coyote. Sheriff Church must race against the clock to put an end to Shelby's vigilante justice before the entire town descends into a bloodbath.
tagline: Payback is dirty.
title: Savage Salvation
plot:
Savage Salvation is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Randall Emmett. Jack Huston stars as a recovering addict who seeks revenge on the drug trade after his fiancée dies of an overdose, pursued by a sympathetic sheriff played by Robert De Niro, with John Malkovich, Willa Fitzgerald and Quavo in supporting roles. Developed under the title Wash Me in the River, it was released in the United Kingdom as Savage Justice.

Sheriff Mike Church, who lost his own son to drugs, laments how opioids have ravaged his once-close community. Shelby John wins a plastic ring from a claw machine and proposes to his girlfriend Ruby Red, promising her a diamond one day, and after another binge the couple resolve to get clean together. They endure a brutal withdrawal and begin rebuilding their lives: Ruby volunteers at the local church and works in a thrift store, Shelby saves for a real ring, and at a family birthday party Ruby's brother-in-law Peter offers him a job. But their dealer, Elvis, noticing that Shelby has stopped buying, lies to Ruby that Shelby has relapsed, and she injects heroin and dies of an overdose. Shelby works his way up the supply chain. He tortures Elvis with a nail gun until he names his supplier, Darius, before killing him; Darius in turn points him to a dealer called Coyote, whose men Shelby wipes out. Church, whose late son played on Shelby's high school team, arrives and urges him to surrender, but when one of Coyote's men badly wounds Church's partner, Shelby kills the gunman and Church shoots Coyote. A number Coyote called before dying leads Shelby to the true head of the local drug trade: Peter, who years earlier took over the business of a man he had delivered for. Shelby tries to make him inject himself as Ruby did; wounded in the ensuing fight, he overpowers Peter and kills him with the drug. Keeping a promise to Ruby, Shelby is baptised in the river while Church waits on the bank.

Huston plays Shelby, with De Niro as Church, Malkovich as Peter, Fitzgerald as Ruby, Quavo as Coyote, Swen Temmel as Elvis, Clay Wilcox as Darius and Meadow Williams as Detective Zeppelin. De Niro and Malkovich joined in 2020, with Huston replacing Taylor Kitsch, who had replaced Machine Gun Kelly; filming ran from November 2020 to January 2021. The Avenue Entertainment released it on December 2, 2022. The Guardian's reviewer enjoyed it as deliciously camp pulp, and it made about $750,000 from home video sales.

overview: The coming-of-age tale of 16-year-old Lina Vilkas who is deported to Siberia amid Stalin's reign of terror in the Baltic region during WWII. An aspiring artist, she secretly documents her harrowing journey with her drawings.
tagline: One girl's voice breaks the silence of history
title: Ashes in the Snow
plot:
Ashes in the Snow is a 2018 drama film directed by Marius Martynas. The movie tells the story of a young Lithuanian girl, Lina, who is sent to a Siberian labor camp with her mother after being accused of being a spy during World War II.

The main theme of Ashes in the Snow revolves around the resilience and strength of the human spirit in the face of unimaginable hardship and oppression. The film portrays the harsh realities of life in the labor camp, where Lina and her mother are forced to endure extreme cold, starvation, and physical labor. Despite these challenges, they find ways to hold on to their humanity, love for each other, and hope for a better future.

The movie also explores the theme of survival and the human need to survive against all odds. Lina's determination to protect her mother and keep her safe in the camp is a testament to the power of maternal love and the will to live. The film also touches on the theme of identity and cultural heritage, as Lina struggles to maintain her Lithuanian roots in the face of Soviet oppression.

Throughout the movie, the director uses powerful imagery and cinematography to convey the brutality and beauty of life in the labor camp. The film's title, Ashes in the Snow, is a poignant metaphor for the destruction and devastation caused by war and oppression, as well as the resilience and hope that can be found even in the darkest of times.

Overall, Ashes in the Snow is a powerful and emotional drama that explores themes of survival, love, and identity in the face of unimaginable hardship.

overview: For Pierre Brochant and his friends, Wednesday is “Idiots' Day”. The idea is simple: each person has to bring along an idiot. The one who brings the most spectacular idiot wins the prize. Tonight, Brochant is ecstatic. He has found a gem. The ultimate idiot, “A world champion idiot!”. What Brochant doesn’t know is that Pignon is a real jinx, a past master in the art of bringing on catastrophes...
tagline: A feast for the senseless.
title: The Dinner Game
plot:
The Dinner Game (Le Dîner de cons, literally "The Dinner of Idiots") is a French comedy of 1998 written and directed by Francis Veber, adapted from his own stage play. Thierry Lhermitte plays the Parisian publisher Pierre Brochant and Jacques Villeret plays François Pignon, the hapless guest he plans to mock, with Francis Huster, Daniel Prévost, Alexandra Vandernoot and Catherine Frot.

Every week Brochant and his fashionable, successful friends hold an "idiots' dinner", to which each must bring an unsuspecting fool, ideally someone obsessed with an absurd hobby, to be quietly ridiculed all evening. Brochant finds a prize candidate: Pignon, a cheerful employee of the Finance Ministry, an institution Brochant, a tax cheat, detests, who builds famous landmarks out of matchsticks. But after inviting Pignon to his apartment, Brochant throws out his back on the golf course, and his wife Christine, disgusted by his cruelty, walks out just before Pignon arrives.

Immobilized, Brochant has to rely on his guest, who bungles everything he touches. Asked to help track down Christine by phone, Pignon reveals Brochant's mistress Marlène, whom he takes for Brochant's sister, and invites her over. Mistaking the briefly returning Christine for the mistress, he advises her on how to win Brochant back, so that she learns of the affair and leaves again. Fearing Christine has returned to her former lover Juste Leblanc, Brochant's old best friend, Brochant coaches Pignon to call him posing as a film producer, but Pignon gives out Brochant's number. Leblanc, unexpectedly sympathetic, comes over to help. To find a womanizer Christine might have fled to, Pignon invites the tax inspector Lucien Cheval, forcing Brochant to hide his valuables; by coincidence Cheval's own wife turns out to be with the same man.

Gradually forced to face his faults, Brochant comes close to reconciling with Christine when Pignon calls her of his own accord, eloquently describing how Brochant has spent the day putting his life in order, and insists he is calling alone. Brochant apologizes for his arrogance. But when Christine calls back, Pignon absent-mindedly picks up the phone, and she hangs up convinced Brochant set him up, leaving Brochant once again calling Pignon an idiot.

The year's top French film at the domestic box office, second only to Titanic, it won three César Awards, including Best Actor for Villeret, and is widely regarded as a cult classic.

overview: San Jose, California, 1906. Isolated in her labyrinthine mansion, eccentric firearm heiress Sarah Winchester believes that she is being haunted by the souls of those killed by the guns manufactured by her company.
tagline: Terror is building.
title: Winchester
plot:
Winchester is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the devastating consequences of trauma. The story revolves around Sarah Winchester, the widow of William Winchester, heir to the Winchester rifle fortune.

At its core, Winchester explores the theme of grief and the destructive power of unresolved emotional pain. Sarah's life is marked by tragedy, including the loss of her only child, which sets off a chain reaction of guilt, anger, and desperation. Her journey becomes an attempt to outrun her demons, but ultimately, she finds herself trapped in a cycle of violence and self-destruction.

The film also touches on the idea of trauma as a catalyst for madness. Sarah's experiences with the supernatural forces that haunt her mansion serve as a manifestation of her inner turmoil, blurring the lines between reality and delusion. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, creating a sense of unease and tension that propels the viewer towards the film's haunting conclusion.

Furthermore, Winchester critiques the notion of female agency and the societal expectations placed upon women during the late 19th century. Sarah's struggles to assert her independence and make decisions about her own life are constantly thwarted by the patriarchal norms of her time. This theme adds a layer of depth to the story, highlighting the ways in which women were marginalized and silenced throughout history.

Ultimately, Winchester is a haunting exploration of the human psyche, delving into the darkest recesses of the mind and revealing the devastating consequences of unresolved trauma and societal oppression.

overview: Based on the novel of the same name, the film depicts the endless battles of four kingdoms as they fight for power and domination of the one ultimate realm.Based on his 2 beloved fantasy novels with 6 million copies sold, L.O.R.D is acclaimed writer and director Guo Jingming’s follow up to his Tiny Times films.  The action-adventure odyssey is set in a world of warring Sorcerers, Lords and Beasts. The first CGI Film to come from China
title: L.O.R.D: Legend of Ravaging Dynasties
plot:
L.O.R.D.: Legend of Ravaging Dynasties is a 2016 Chinese animated motion-capture action fantasy adventure film written and directed by Guo Jingming. Produced by Le Vision Pictures, which handled distribution in Greater China, it opened on 30 September 2016 in 3D and IMAX 3D, while Lionsgate released it the same day in the United Kingdom and Ireland, Australia and New Zealand, and the United States and Canada. Le Vision said Lionsgate saw the film's appeal to young adult audiences, comparing it to the studio's Hunger Games and Twilight franchises. A sequel premiered on the streaming platform Tencent Video on 4 December 2020 and later reached Netflix.

The film is set on the Odin Mainland, divided into four countries, each protected by soul masters who wield supernatural soul powers; the seven mightiest are known as the Noble Lords. In the Aslan Empire, the realm of the water element, Qi Ling (Cheney Chen), who has worked as a busboy at an inn since childhood, tames the legendary soul beast Ice Fang during a clash between soul masters. Yin Chen (Kris Wu), the Seventh Lord, arrives on the orders of the Silver Priest (Roy Wang) to take Qi Ling as his disciple, and guides him toward the Grave of the Souls, where he must find his soul weapon.

Impatient, Qi Ling ignores his master's instructions and enters the Grave with Tianshu You Hua (Lin Yun) and Guishan Lian Quan (Fan Bingbing), drawing himself into the Upcoming Storm, a contest of soul powers among the lords. Meanwhile a conspiracy long hidden within the Aslan Empire begins to surface. While searching for his disciple, Yin Chen learns that his own former master, Gilgamesh, the former First Lord, may still be alive, and risks everything to find him. At the same time the Corroders You Ming (William Chan) and Thalia (Amber Kuo) are ordered by the Silver Priest to kill Guishan Lian Quan and her brother, Feng Hun (Yan Yikuan), setting lords and disciples against one another in a battle over truth and honor.

The film opened strongly, earning about $29.2 million in its first weekend across four markets, almost all of it from China, where it benefited from the National Day holiday and placed second behind I Belonged to You. Poor word of mouth and competition from Operation Mekong caused takings to fall sharply after its opening day, and it finished with about $53.8 million, $53.6 million of it from China.

overview: What Jake Vig doesn't know just might get him killed. A sharp and polished grifter, Jake has just swindled thousands of dollars from the unsuspecting Lionel Dolby with the help of his crew. It becomes clear that Lionel wasn't just any mark, he was an accountant for eccentric crime boss Winston King. Jake and his crew will have to stay one step ahead of both the criminals and the cops to finally settle their debt.
tagline: It's not about the money. It's about the money.
title: Confidence
plot:
Confidence is a 2003 American crime drama directed by James Foley and written by Doug Jung. Edward Burns, Rachel Weisz, Dustin Hoffman and Andy García head a cast that also includes Morris Chestnut.

After a group of grifters cheat their latest target and celebrate, their unofficial leader, Jake Vig, explains the art of the con. When one of them, Big Al, is found shot dead, the others discover that the money they took belonged to Winston King, a ruthless local crime lord known as the King. Jake proposes working for the King by robbing Morgan Price, a rival who owns a bank. He enlists partners Gordo and Miles and con artist Lily, with the King's man Lupus as a minder. The plan centers on bribing a bank vice president to wire money offshore. Complications arise when Special Agent Gunther Butan, who has pursued Jake for years, comes to Los Angeles and forces two crooked police detectives, to switch their loyalty from Jake to him. Rattled, Jake calls off the con and berates Lily, who walks out. Lupus warns that the King will torture and kill the grifters if they fail, and the job resumes without her.

The bribed executive wires the money to Gordo in Belize, who carries $5 million in a duffel bag to Ontario Airport, where both Butan and the King's men are waiting. Butan arrests the King and seizes the cash, and Gordo vanishes. Believing the King has the money, Lupus admits that he killed Big Al and pulls a gun on Jake, but he is shot by Travis, a henchman of Price, to whom Lily had revealed the entire scheme after leaving. Travis takes Jake to a vacant lot and makes him explain how the con worked, and a furious Lily shoots Jake before Travis orders them both to disappear. Minutes later Butan pulls up and Jake rises from a pool of fake blood, unhurt. The final twists are revealed: Lily's departure was staged to fool Lupus, Butan is actually Jake's longtime confederate who used his position to grab the money and arrest the King at once, and Jake wore squibs to fake his death. Everyone was in on the scheme except the King and Lupus, Price and Travis, and the two corrupt detectives, who end up under arrest. The money is split five ways, and the grifters drive off into the night to celebrate.

The film was shot at Hollywood's Deep Nightclub and elsewhere around Los Angeles and Ontario, California, and opened on April 25, 2003. Reviews were mixed to positive: Rotten Tomatoes gave it 68%, Metacritic scored it 59,, and Roger Ebert gave it two stars.

overview: Gentleman gangster Max and his partner, Riton, pull off their last, most successful heist and find themselves comfortable enough to retire in the style they enjoy. However, Max confides the details of the theft to his younger mistress, Josey -- who has secretly taken up with ambitious young rival gangster Angelo. Angelo then has Riton kidnapped and demands the stash of gold as ransom, which threatens Max's dreams of the perfect retirement.
tagline: It Bristles With Violence!
title: Touchez Pas au Grisbi
plot:
Touchez Pas au Grisbi is a classic French New Wave film that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of one's actions. The movie delves into the world of petty crime, where the protagonist, Jean Pedel, played by Jean Gabin, navigates a complex web of moral ambiguity.

At its core, Touchez Pas au Grisbi is a cautionary tale about the dangers of getting involved in illicit activities and the devastating impact it can have on one's life. The film masterfully weaves together themes of loyalty, betrayal, and redemption, as Jean Pedel becomes increasingly entangled in a world of crime that threatens to consume him.

The movie also explores the concept of identity and how our choices shape who we become. As Jean Pedel navigates this treacherous landscape, he is forced to confront his own moral compass and the consequences of his actions. The film raises questions about the nature of right and wrong, leaving the audience to ponder the complexities of human morality.

Furthermore, Touchez Pas au Grisbi is a powerful commentary on the social and economic conditions of post-war France. The film sheds light on the struggles of working-class individuals who are forced to turn to crime as a means of survival. This adds a layer of depth to the narrative, highlighting the harsh realities faced by many during this period.

Overall, Touchez Pas au Grisbi is a gripping and thought-provoking film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, identity, and morality. Its themes are timeless and continue to resonate with audiences today.

overview: In Bodeen, Texas, Land Of The Dragon, an indie-rock loving misfit finds a way of dealing with her small-town misery after she discovers a roller derby league in nearby Austin.
tagline: Be Your Own Hero
title: Whip It
plot:
Whip It is indeed a 2009 film directed by Drew Barrymore, and it's distributed by Dune Entertainment.

The movie follows Bliss Cavendar, a young woman who discovers her passion for roller derby while feeling suffocated by the expectations of her family and society. As she navigates this new world, Bliss must confront her own identity, independence, and the constraints placed upon her.

At its core, Whip It explores themes of self-discovery, empowerment, and the struggle for individuality in a world that often seeks to conform. The film delves into the complexities of female relationships, particularly those between mothers and daughters, as well as the challenges faced by women who refuse to be bound by societal norms.

Through Bliss's journey, Whip It also touches on the idea of finding one's true passion and purpose, even if it means challenging the status quo. The movie celebrates the spirit of rebellion and nonconformity, highlighting the importance of embracing one's uniqueness and living life on one's own terms.

Overall, Whip It is a heartwarming and humorous film that explores themes of identity, empowerment, and self-expression, making it a relatable and engaging watch for audiences.

overview: A new mother’s memories of her own youth prepare her to navigate motherhood in the increasingly challenging world that polar bears face today.
tagline: Join their incredible adventure.
title: Polar Bear
plot:
"Polar Bear" is a 2022 documentary film directed by Victor Maldonado, produced by Disneynature.

The main theme of "Polar Bear" revolves around the life cycle and struggles of a mother polar bear and her cubs in the Arctic. The film showcases the harsh realities of survival in the Arctic environment, where the mother bear must protect her cubs from predators, hunger, and the ever-changing climate.

Throughout the documentary, the filmmakers follow the mother bear's journey as she navigates the challenges of raising her cubs, teaching them essential skills to survive in the wild. The film also highlights the impact of climate change on polar bears, including the melting of sea ice, which is crucial for their hunting and breeding habits.

The documentary explores themes such as:

1. Motherhood: The film showcases the selfless love and dedication of a mother bear as she risks her life to protect her cubs.
2. Survival: The documentary highlights the incredible adaptability and resilience of polar bears in the face of adversity.
3. Climate Change: The film raises awareness about the devastating impact of climate change on polar bears and their habitats.

Overall, "Polar Bear" is a heart-wrenching and visually stunning documentary that offers a glimpse into the lives of these majestic creatures and the challenges they face in the wild.

original_title: The Men Who Stare at Goats
overview: A reporter in Iraq might just have the story of a lifetime when he meets Lyn Cassady, a guy who claims to be a former member of the U.S. Army's New Earth Army, a unit that employs paranormal powers in their missions.
tagline: No goats. No glory.
title: The Men Who Stare at Goats
plot:
The Men Who Stare at Goats is a 2009 film that delves into the world of military psychology and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. At its core, the movie explores the theme of the human psyche's capacity for both good and evil. The story follows Lyn Cassady, a charismatic con artist who becomes embroiled in a government experiment to develop psychic warfare capabilities.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that the film is not just about the military's attempts to harness supernatural abilities but also about the darker aspects of human nature. The movie delves into the concept of the "warrior archetype," where individuals are driven by a primal urge for violence and control. This theme is expertly woven throughout the story, as characters like Lyn Cassady and Bob Wilton grapple with their own demons and the moral implications of their actions.

The film also touches on the idea of the power of storytelling and the manipulation of reality. The military's use of propaganda and disinformation serves as a metaphor for the ways in which individuals can shape their perceptions of the world to suit their own purposes. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Lyn Cassady, who uses his charisma and cunning to navigate the complexities of the government experiment.

Ultimately, The Men Who Stare at Goats is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of our nature and the ways in which we can be manipulated by those in power.

overview: Chance Harris looks to find a balance between his school, work, relationships and opportunity to perform at the nationally televised step competition during homecoming weekend at Truth University.
title: Stomp the Yard 2: Homecoming
plot:
Stomp the Yard 2: Homecoming, also titled Stomp the Yard: Homecoming, is an American dance drama released in 2010, helmed by Rob Hardy with Will Packer producing, and serves as a direct-to-video sequel to the 2007 hit Stomp the Yard. Collins Pennie leads the cast as Chance Harris, with Keith David as his father Terry and Tika Sumpter as his girlfriend Nikki; the ensemble also features Jasmine Guy as Janice, David Banner as Jay, Pooch Hall, Teyana Taylor, Kiely Williams, Terrence J, Columbus Short and Stephen "tWitch" Boss.

The film returns to the fictional Truth University in Atlanta, where the Theta Nu Theta fraternity is determined to dethrone its chief rival, Mu Gamma Xi, at a nationally televised step competition held during homecoming weekend, with full college scholarships at stake for the winners. Chance, who left home after his mother's death, has come back to Georgia to study while working at his father's struggling diner. Now a full member of the fraternity rather than a pledge, he is ready to contribute his own choreography to the team. At the start of the film, however, he is hustled in a rigged underground dance battle while trying to raise money for tuition, and ends up owing money to a dangerous gambler and his thugs, who threaten him with violence if he does not pay.
