Keeping his debt secret from his fraternity brothers, his father and his girlfriend Nikki, Chance becomes increasingly stressed and stretched thin as he tries to balance school, work, his relationships and practice while the competition approaches. To succeed, he must learn the value of responsibility, brotherhood and teamwork, the ideals that the precise, percussive art of stepping, with its combination of footwork, chanting and hand-clapping, comes to represent.

Filming began in Atlanta in November 2009, and Sony released the film on DVD on 21 September 2010. The soundtrack features tracks by artists including Ace Hood, Roscoe Dash, G-Side and John Forté. Reviewers praised the energetic stepping routines and Pennie's relatable lead performance but noted that the short running time rushes through predictable plot points, resolving major conflicts offscreen or in a single line. Film Intuition nonetheless considered it a solidly entertaining straight-to-disc sequel that gives fans more of what they enjoyed in the original.

overview: Antoine and Laurent, old friends, spend their vacation in Corsica with their respective daughters: seventeen-year-old Louna and eighteen-year-old Marie. One evening at the beach, Louna seduces Laurent. Louna is in love, but for Laurent it was nothing more than a momentary distraction. Without revealing her lover's name, Louna confides in her father, who tries by any means to discover who his daughter's lover is. How long will the secret be able to be kept hidden?
title: One Wild Moment
plot:
One Wild Moment is a 2015 French drama film directed by Hélène Angel. The movie revolves around the story of a young woman named Sophie, who embarks on an unexpected journey of self-discovery and growth after meeting a charming stranger.

The main theme of One Wild Moment is the exploration of freedom and the human desire to break free from societal expectations and constraints. Through Sophie's character, the film delves into the complexities of identity, love, and relationships, highlighting the tension between the need for independence and the comfort of familiarity.

As Sophie navigates her newfound connection with the stranger, she begins to question her own desires, values, and sense of self. The film masterfully captures the essence of this transformative journey, showcasing the beauty of vulnerability, spontaneity, and the thrill of embracing the unknown.

One Wild Moment also touches on themes of love, intimacy, and human connection, revealing the complexities of relationships and the ways in which they can both liberate and confine us. The film's narrative is characterized by a sense of fluidity and uncertainty, mirroring Sophie's own emotional state as she navigates this pivotal moment in her life.

Ultimately, One Wild Moment presents a poignant exploration of the human experience, inviting viewers to reflect on their own desires, fears, and aspirations.

original_title: A Fairly Odd Movie: Grow Up, Timmy Turner!
overview: The television movie is set in the city of Dimmsdale and centers on the series' main protagonist Timmy Turner with his fairy godparents Cosmo and Wanda and his fairy godbrother Poof. In the movie, Timmy is now 23 years old but is still in fifth grade with his fairy-obsessed fifth grade teacher Mr. Crocker. Despite being grown up, Timmy finds a loophole in the fairy rulebook Da Rules: if he continues to act like a kid, he will still get to keep his fairies. However, the dilemma rises when Tootie, who was once a dorky girl when she was 10 years old, returns to Dimmsdale as an attractive woman. Timmy falls in love with her, a sign that he is growing up to an adult, which means he is closer to losing his fairies. Meanwhile, an oil business tycoon named Hugh J. Magnate, Jr., who teams up with Mr. Crocker, plans to use Timmy's fairies' magic in order to promote his oil business.
title: A Fairly Odd Movie: Grow Up, Timmy Turner!
plot:
A Fairly Odd Movie: Grow Up, Timmy Turner! (2011) is an animated film that explores several significant themes. At its core, the movie delves into the complexities of growing up and the challenges that come with it.

One of the primary themes is the struggle to balance childhood innocence with the harsh realities of adulthood. The main character, Timmy Turner, finds himself at a crossroads as he navigates the transition from boyhood to manhood. He must confront the idea that his fairy godparents, who have been his constant companions throughout his life, are no longer able to cater to his every whim.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. As Timmy grows up, he begins to question who he is outside of his relationships with Cosmo and Wanda, his fairy godparents. He must learn to define himself and find his own path in life, separate from the comfort and security provided by his magical world.

Furthermore, the movie explores the idea of letting go and embracing change. Timmy's fairy godparents, who have been so integral to his life, are forced to confront their own limitations and the fact that they can no longer be there for him in the same way. This serves as a poignant reminder that all good things must come to an end, and that growth and progress often require us to let go of what we know and love.

Lastly, the film offers a commentary on the importance of relationships and human connections. Despite the fantastical elements of the story, the movie ultimately focuses on Timmy's relationships with his family, friends, and even his fairy godparents. It highlights the significance of nurturing these relationships and learning to communicate effectively with others as we navigate the complexities of life.

Overall, A Fairly Odd Movie: Grow Up, Timmy Turner! is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores the challenges and joys of growing up, identity, change, and human connection.

overview: When his fiancee is kidnapped by human traffickers, Roman and his ex-military brothers set out to track her down and save her before it is too late. Along the way, Roman teams up with Avery, a cop investigating human trafficking and fighting the corrupt bureaucracy that has harmful intentions.
tagline: Protect what's yours.
title: Acts of Violence
plot:
Acts of Violence is a 2018 American action thriller directed by Brett Donowho from a screenplay by Nicolas Aaron Mezzanatto. Bruce Willis, Cole Hauser, Shawn Ashmore, Ashton Holmes, Melissa Bolona, Sophia Bush and Mike Epps head the cast. Principal photography began in Cleveland, Ohio, in March 2017, and Lionsgate Premiere released the film in a limited theatrical run and on video on demand on January 12, 2018.

In Cleveland, the MacGregor brothers are preparing for a wedding. Deklan and Brandon are former U.S. Army Rangers who served overseas; Deklan remains haunted by his experiences, and Brandon has a family to support. The youngest, Roman, is engaged to his childhood sweetheart, Mia. At her bachelorette party, Mia insults Vince and Frank, two thugs who traffic women for the local crime boss Max Livingston, and they snatch her from the club. Detective James Avery has long been trying to build a case against Livingston, but corruption within the police department keeps getting in his way. Mia manages to leave Roman a voice message before she is taken, and Roman turns to Deklan. Tracking her phone, the brothers raid a house where they believe she is held but find nothing, and Avery, while promising help, warns them to stay out of it. They refuse.

Livingston, angry that his men have taken someone likely to be reported missing, forces Mia's finger onto a trigger to make her shoot Frank. Arming themselves with military-grade vests and weapons, the brothers capture Vince, learn where Mia is and kill several of Livingston's men, only to find she has already escaped through a window. A tracking implant allows the gang to recapture her, and the brothers return to Brandon's ransacked home to find his wife, Jessa, bound and dead. Enraged, they storm a warehouse where Livingston keeps trafficked women in trucks bound for Las Vegas and free Mia and the others. Livingston then attacks the house, killing Brandon, and escapes. Deklan and Roman are arrested while Livingston remains free, prompting Avery to quit the force, track Livingston to his hideout and shoot him before he can leave town.

Willis plays Avery, Hauser plays Deklan, Ashmore plays Brandon, Holmes plays Roman, Bolona plays Mia, Epps plays Livingston and Bush plays Detective Brooke Baker. Critics dismissed it, with none of 13 reviews on Rotten Tomatoes positive and a Metacritic score of 28. It earned about $387,000 from releases in the United Arab Emirates and Portugal.

overview: A sheriff investigating the disappearance of a young girl from a small island discovers there's a larger mystery to solve among the island's secretive, neo-pagan community.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG III
tagline: Some sacrifices must be made
title: The Wicker Man
plot:
The Wicker Man is a 2006 folk horror film written and directed by Neil LaBute, a remake and reimagining of the 1973 British film of the same name that also draws very loosely on David Pinner's 1967 novel Ritual. Nicolas Cage stars as police officer Edward Malus. Made for $40 million, it was filmed in British Columbia, Canada, mostly on Bowen Island, in the summer of 2005. Warner Bros. Pictures released the film in the United States and Canada on September 1, 2006.

Edward hears from his former fiancée, Willow Woodward, that her daughter, Rowan, has gone missing, and travels to the island in Puget Sound, off the coast of Washington, home to a community of neo-pagans. They are led by Sister Summersisle, an elderly woman who embodies the goddess they worship and who explains that her ancestors fled persecution in England, only to face it again in the Salem witch trials before settling on the island. The community is mostly female and lives off its honey, whose production has recently declined. The islanders deflect Edward's questions about Rowan. He sees two men carrying a bag that seems to drip blood, digs up a fresh grave that holds only a burned doll and finds Rowan's sweater in the churchyard. At the school, Sister Rose tries to hide the register, in which Rowan's name has been crossed out, and when Edward demands to know how Rowan died, she says "She'll burn to death" before correcting herself to the past tense. Willow then admits that Rowan is Edward's daughter.

On the day of the fertility rite, Edward disguises himself in a bear suit to join the procession and finds Rowan tied to a tree, ready to be burned. He frees her and they flee into the woods, but Rowan leads him straight back to Sister Summersisle. Edward realizes the search was a trap from the start: Willow, Summersisle's daughter, had chosen him as a human sacrifice to restore the honey harvest. The islanders shut him inside a giant wicker man, and Rowan sets it alight. Six months later, Willow and Sister Honey approach two police officers in a Seattle bar and go home with them.

Ellen Burstyn plays Sister Summersisle, with Kate Beahan as Willow, Molly Parker as Sister Rose and Leelee Sobieski as Sister Honey. The film earned a rare F CinemaScore and 15% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and received five Golden Raspberry nominations, though Paul Sarossy's cinematography won a Canadian Society of Cinematographers award. It grossed $38.8 million.

overview: A molecular biologist's study of the human eye has far-reaching implications about humanity's scientific and spiritual beliefs.
title: I Origins
plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie titled "I Origins" released in 2014 by Verisimilitude. However, I did find that there is a movie titled "I Origins" released in 2014, directed by Mike Cahill and produced by Blumhouse Productions.

The main themes of the movie "I Origins" revolve around the concept of identity, consciousness, and the nature of self. The film follows a scientist named Henry who discovers a way to map the human brain's neural connections, leading him on a journey of self-discovery and exploration of the human condition. As he delves deeper into his research, Henry begins to question the essence of his own existence and the meaning of life.

The movie explores the idea that our sense of identity is not fixed, but rather it is a dynamic and ever-changing construct. Through Henry's journey, the film raises questions about the relationship between the self and the external world, and whether our experiences and perceptions shape who we are or if there is something more fundamental at play.

The movie also touches on themes of love, loss, and the human connection, highlighting the importance of relationships in shaping our understanding of ourselves and the world around us. Overall, "I Origins" is a thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to consider the complexities of human existence and the nature of self.

overview: Altruistic Jane finds herself facing her worst nightmare as her younger sister announces her engagement to the man Jane secretly adores.
tagline: She's about to find the perfect fit.
title: 27 Dresses
plot:
"27 Dresses" is a romantic comedy film released in 2008, directed by Anne Fletcher and starring Katherine Heigl and James Marsden.

The movie follows the story of Jane Nichols (Katherine Heigl), a woman who has been a bridesmaid at 27 weddings, but never a bride. She's stuck in a rut, feeling unfulfilled and unwanted. That is until she meets Kevin Doyle (James Marsden), a cynical and handsome columnist who writes about weddings.

As the story unfolds, Jane finds herself falling for Kevin, but their relationship is complicated by her fear of commitment and his initial reluctance to settle down. Throughout the film, Jane's journey is marked by self-discovery, growth, and ultimately, love.

The main themes of "27 Dresses" include:

1. Self-discovery: Jane's journey is a metaphor for finding one's true identity and purpose in life.
2. Love and relationships: The movie explores the complexities of romantic relationships, including the fear of commitment and the importance of communication.
3. Identity and belonging: Jane's struggles to find her place in the world serve as a backdrop for exploring themes of identity and belonging.
4. Personal growth: Through her experiences, Jane learns to let go of her fears and take control of her life.

Overall, "27 Dresses" is a heartwarming and humorous film that explores universal themes of love, relationships, and self-discovery.

overview: A U.S. Army Captain uses her years of tactical training to save humanity from sixteen nuclear missiles launched at the U.S. as a violent attack threatens her remote missile interceptor station.
tagline: The world's last defense.
title: Interceptor
plot:
Interceptor is a 2022 Australian-American action thriller film directed by Matthew Reilly in his directorial debut, from a screenplay he wrote with Stuart Beattie. Elsa Pataky stars as Captain J. J. Collins, a U.S. Army officer stationed on a remote nuclear missile interceptor platform in the Pacific Ocean, with Luke Bracey as the former military intelligence officer Alexander Kessel, Aaron Glenane as Corporal Beaver Baker, Mayen Mehta as Corporal Rahul Shah and Colin Friels as Collins's father. Pataky's husband, Chris Hemsworth, an executive producer, appears uncredited as an electronics store salesman.

Terrorists raid the interceptor site at Fort Greely, Alaska, at the same moment that sixteen nuclear warheads are seized in Russia. Collins, forced out of a Pentagon post in retaliation over a sexual misconduct case involving her superior, is now on a station that has suddenly become the country's last defense against nuclear attack. Kessel's operatives storm the platform, killing the commander and the crew and sparing only Collins, Shah and Baker, who has been knocked out. They need the command center to disable the interceptors. Collins and Shah kill an operative who enters through a floor hatch, but Baker wakes and reveals himself as an inside man driven by greed and xenophobia, and the attackers take control at gunpoint. Kessel broadcasts a manifesto denouncing the nation's history and names sixteen target cities before ordering the launch. Collins frees herself, locks Kessel, Baker and one of their men out of the command center and kills two other henchmen. She refuses to yield even when Kessel streams her father's torture. Unable to seize the station, Kessel begins scuttling it. As it sinks, Shah drops through the hatch into the ocean and reactivates the hatches by hand before Baker kills him. Collins hides, kills the last henchman, takes a laptop to the roof, defeats Baker in a hand-to-hand fight and launches the interceptors in time to destroy the warheads. She overpowers Kessel as a Russian submarine arrives to collect the terrorists, but its crew shoots him dead and the captain salutes Collins. Promoted by the president, she recovers in hospital, joined by her father, who was rescued by friends who saw the broadcast.

Shot in New South Wales in 2021, Interceptor had a brief Australian theatrical run from 26 May 2022 before streaming on Netflix from 3 June, where it reached number one. Reviews were mixed, with a 44% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

overview: When Kimberly has a violent premonition of a highway pileup she blocks the freeway, keeping a few others meant to die, safe...Or are they? The survivors mysteriously start dying and it's up to Kimberly to stop it before she's next.
tagline: For every beginning there is an end.
title: Final Destination 2
plot:
Final Destination 2 is a supernatural horror film directed by David R. Ellis and written by J. Mackye Gruber. The movie is the sequel to the 2000 film Final Destination, which was also based on the novel of the same name by Kevin Williamson.

The story begins with Alex Browning (A.J. Cook), the survivor of the first film, who has been experiencing strange and terrifying premonitions since her encounter with Death in the first movie. She is haunted by visions of a car crash that will kill her and several others. Believing that she can cheat death again, Alex decides to test her theory by deliberately putting herself in harm's way.

Alex convinces her friends, including Terri (Ali Larter), Wren (Seann William Scott), and Monty (Chad Donella), to go skydiving with her at a remote airfield. As they jump out of the plane, Alex experiences another premonition, which she believes is warning her that something terrible will happen.

However, instead of dying in the crash, Alex manages to survive by using a parachute that was not attached to the plane. She then sets out to warn her friends about the impending disaster, but they are skeptical and dismissive of her warnings.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Alex's premonitions are real, and she is trying to prevent a series of gruesome and deadly accidents from occurring. The group soon discovers that the airfield where they went skydiving was actually a site of a previous plane crash that killed everyone on board.

The movie takes a dark turn as the characters begin to die off one by one, each in a manner that is eerily similar to Alex's premonitions. As the body count rises, it becomes clear that Death has set its sights on this group, and they are powerless to stop it.

In the end, only Terri survives, but not without scars both physical and emotional. The movie ends with Terri, who has finally understood the true nature of Alex's premonitions, setting out to warn others about the impending disaster, leaving the audience wondering if she will be able to prevent another tragedy from occurring.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as the characters are stalked by Death, and the audience is left on the edge of their seats, wondering who will survive and who will become the next victim. The movie's climax features a shocking twist that sets up the events of the third installment in the series.

Overall, Final Destination 2 is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores the theme of fate and mortality. With its clever plot twists and gruesome death scenes, it has become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

overview: After being blinded in a coup against the king, Joseon's greatest swordsman goes into hiding, far removed from his city's anguish. But when traffickers kidnap his daughter, he has no choice but to unsheathe his sword once more.
tagline: Real Chase Action.
title: The Swordsman
plot:
The Swordsman (Korean: Geomgaek) is a 2020 South Korean period action film directed by Choi Jae-hoon, starring Jang Hyuk in the title role. Shot between June and September 2017, it was due to open in South Korea on 17 September 2020 but was pushed back a week to 23 September because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Pre-sold to 55 countries, it opened the 2020 Korean Indonesian Film Festival, was invited to the Hawaii International Film Festival and later played Glasgow, Sydney and New York festivals.

Tae-yul, the finest swordsman in Joseon and bodyguard to King Gwanghaegun, refuses to join senior officials plotting to overthrow a king they consider too weak to resist foreign invaders. In a duel with the rebel leader Min Seung-ho, Tae-yul's sword shatters and fragments pierce his eyes; the King halts the fight, announces his abdication and releases Tae-yul from service. Years later Tae-yul lives as a trapper in the mountains with his teenage daughter, Tae-ok, who chafes at his refusal to let her see the world. A monk warns that without rare herbs Tae-yul will soon go blind, but the trader Hwa Seon says the remedy is costly and reserved for the well connected. Meanwhile Gurutai, a relative of the Qing emperor grown rich by selling captives from the recent invasion, visits the court, which fears he will demand Joseon's children as tribute. The courtier Lee Mok-yo prepares a petition urging resistance and asks Seon to find a girl to look after his mother, and Seon recommends Tae-ok, who hopes to earn the herbs.

After Tae-yul fends off Gurutai's men with only his cane, Gurutai's assassins raid Lee's estate, kill his servants and seize his daughter and Tae-ok. Surviving an attempt on his own life, Tae-yul burns Gurutai's main slave camp, frees the captives, and slaughters the Qing riflemen and assassins who massacre Lee's guards. The herbs are administered, but Seon admits his blindness cannot be stopped. Tae-yul defeats Min, now serving Gurutai, whom Gurutai then kills for losing. In the final duel, Tae-yul kills Gurutai's mistress, who holds a knife to Tae-ok, then impales Gurutai, and a watching Qing envoy lets the captives go. As his sight fades, a flashback reveals that Tae-ok is the King's only child, entrusted to Tae-yul to give him a reason to live, and father and daughter head down the mountain to see the world.

Jang Hyuk plays Tae-yul, with Joe Taslim as Gurutai, Kim Hyun-soo as Tae-ok, Jeong Man-sik as Min and Jang Hyun-sung as the King.

overview: Deputy Sheriff Joe "Deke" Deacon joins forces with Sgt. Jim Baxter to search for a serial killer who's terrorizing Los Angeles. As they track the culprit, Baxter is unaware that the investigation is dredging up echoes of Deke's past, uncovering disturbing secrets that could threaten more than his case.
tagline: Some things never let us go.
title: The Little Things
plot:
The Little Things is a crime thriller film directed by John Lee Hancock, released in 2021 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie stars Denzel Washington, Jared Leto, and Robert Forster.

The story begins with Joe Deacon (Denzel Washington), a detective from the Los Angeles Police Department who has just been transferred to the LAPD's Homicide Division after serving as a homicide detective in New Orleans for 20 years. Joe is struggling to adjust to his new surroundings and feeling disconnected from his colleagues.

The plot takes a turn when Joe meets Detective Jim Baxter (Jared Leto), a young and ambitious cop who is eager to prove himself. The two are tasked with solving the gruesome murder of a young woman, which has left the community shaken. As they delve deeper into the case, they discover that the victim was a sex worker who had been brutally murdered.

As Joe and Jim begin their investigation, they uncover a complex web of clues that lead them to suspect a serial killer. The killer is targeting women who are involved in prostitution, and the victims all have one thing in common: they were all seen with a man named Russell Ellis (Robert Forster) on the night of their murder.

Joe becomes increasingly obsessed with catching the killer, but his obsession also starts to affect his personal life. He begins to question his own morality and the true nature of justice. Meanwhile, Jim is struggling to balance his desire for success with his growing feelings for a woman named Wendy (Rami Malek's character was removed from the movie).

As the investigation unfolds, Joe and Jim discover that Russell Ellis is not just any ordinary man. He has a dark past and a twisted obsession with women who work in prostitution. The killer's motives are revealed to be rooted in a deep-seated hatred for women who engage in sex work.

The film builds up to a tense and suspenseful climax as Joe and Jim close in on the killer. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Russell Ellis was not the mastermind behind the murders, but rather a pawn in a larger game. The true culprit is revealed to be a woman who had been using Russell's identity to carry out her own twisted crimes.

The movie ends with Joe finally bringing justice to the victims and their families, but not before he has to confront his own demons and the true nature of evil. The film raises questions about morality, justice, and the complexities of human behavior.

Overall, The Little Things is a gripping and thought-provoking thriller that explores the darker side of human nature. With outstanding performances from Denzel Washington and Jared Leto, the movie delivers a tense and suspenseful ride that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: Determined to prove herself, Officer Judy Hopps, the first bunny on Zootopia's police force, jumps at the chance to crack her first case - even if it means partnering with scam-artist fox Nick Wilde to solve the mystery.
tagline: Welcome to the urban jungle.
title: Zootopia
plot:
In the vibrant city of Zootopia, a rabbit police officer named Judy Hopps (voiced by Ginnifer Goodwin) dreams of becoming a part of the prestigious Police Department. Despite facing skepticism and bias from her peers, Judy perseveres and earns a spot on the force.

Upon arrival at the department, Judy is paired with Nick Wilde, a sly fox con artist (voiced by Jason Bateman). Initially, their partnership seems unlikely, but they soon develop an unorthodox yet effective working relationship. As they navigate the complexities of Zootopia's society, Judy and Nick stumble upon a mysterious case involving a series of disappearances among the city's predators.

As they delve deeper into the mystery, Judy and Nick uncover a sinister plot that threatens the harmony between Zootopia's different species. The duo must confront their own biases and prejudices to solve the case and bring justice to the victims' families.

Throughout the film, the animation is stunning, with intricate details that showcase the unique characteristics of each animal species in Zootopia. The voice acting is also superb, bringing depth and nuance to the characters.

One of the standout aspects of Zootopia is its thought-provoking commentary on social issues such as prejudice, stereotypes, and diversity. The film cleverly weaves these themes into the narrative, using humor and satire to make pointed observations about human society.

The movie's climax features an action-packed sequence that showcases Judy and Nick's growing partnership and their determination to solve the mystery. Ultimately, they uncover a surprising twist that challenges everything they thought they knew about Zootopia's society.

Overall, Zootopia is a delightful and engaging film that combines stunning animation with a clever script and memorable characters. With its positive message and entertaining storyline, it's no wonder this movie has become a modern classic.

original_title: ストライクウィッチーズ 劇場版
overview: The year is 1939 - it was then that the Neuroi appeared. Nobody knows where they came from or what their ultimate agenda is, but the fact remains that their attacks drove people out of their towns and cities. In order to take arms against them, humanity develops a new anti-Neuroi weapon called the "Striker Unit." Using the power of magic to fight against the monsters, this new device enhances and amplifies the power of female magic-wielders. To use this device, young witches from all over the world have been brought together to form an elite task force unit called the 501st Joint Fighter Wing, commonly known as the "Strike Witches."
title: Strike Witches the Movie
plot:
Strike Witches the Movie is an anime film that explores several themes, primarily revolving around the complexities of war and its effects on individuals. The story delves into the psychological struggles of the main characters as they navigate their roles in the military and confront the harsh realities of combat.

At its core, the movie examines the theme of identity and how it is shaped by one's experiences and relationships. The protagonist, Mikoto Shijou, grapples with her sense of self and purpose as she transitions from a civilian to a military pilot. Her journey serves as a metaphor for the challenges faced by individuals who are forced to adapt to new roles and circumstances.

The film also touches on the theme of camaraderie and the bonds that form between people in the face of adversity. The relationships between the Strike Witches, particularly Mikoto's friendships with her fellow pilots, serve as a source of strength and comfort in the midst of chaos.

Furthermore, the movie critiques the romanticization of war and the ways in which it can be used to justify violence and aggression. The story presents a nuanced portrayal of the consequences of war, highlighting the emotional toll it takes on those involved and the devastating impact it has on civilians.

Overall, Strike Witches the Movie offers a thought-provoking exploration of the human experience during times of conflict, inviting viewers to reflect on the complexities of identity, camaraderie, and the true cost of war.

overview: Sam Flynn, the tech-savvy and daring son of Kevin Flynn, investigates his father's disappearance and is pulled into The Grid. With the help of a mysterious program named Quorra, Sam quests to stop evil dictator Clu from crossing into the real world.
tagline: The game has changed.
title: TRON: Legacy
plot:
TRON: Legacy is a 2010 science fiction film directed by Joseph Kosinski and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1982 classic TRON, while also introducing new characters and themes.

The story begins with Kevin Flynn (Jeff Bridges), the original creator of the virtual world of Tron, who has been missing for 28 years. His son, Sam Flynn (Garrett Hedlund), is now an adult and a brilliant programmer in his own right. Sam's life takes a dramatic turn when he receives a message from his father, which leads him to a mysterious website that reveals the existence of Clu (Jeff Bridges), Kevin's business partner who has taken over the company.

Clu, played by the same actor as Kevin Flynn, is revealed to be a digital creation of Kevin's own code. He was created to manage and maintain the Grid, but he became self-aware and eventually took control of the system, leading to Kevin's disappearance. Clu sees Sam as a threat to his existence and decides to eliminate him.

Sam soon discovers that he has inherited his father's abilities and is able to enter the virtual world of Tron. He meets Quorra (Olivia Wilde), a program created by Kevin who becomes his ally in the fight against Clu. Together, they embark on a perilous journey through the Grid, navigating treacherous landscapes and battling Clu's army of programs.

As Sam delves deeper into the Grid, he learns more about his father's past and the true nature of Clu's existence. He also discovers that Quorra is not just a program, but a sentient being with her own motivations and desires. The two form a strong bond as they work together to defeat Clu and restore balance to the Grid.

The film features stunning visual effects, showcasing the beauty and danger of the virtual world. The action sequences are intense and thrilling, with Sam and Quorra facing off against Clu's programs in epic battles. The movie also explores themes of identity, loyalty, and the consequences of playing god with technology.

In the end, Sam and Quorra succeed in defeating Clu, but not before he reveals a shocking secret about his own existence. The film concludes with Sam returning to the real world, forever changed by his experience in the Grid. He also discovers that Kevin is still alive, trapped in a digital limbo, and sets out to rescue him.

TRON: Legacy received mixed reviews from critics, but was a commercial success, grossing over $400 million worldwide. The film's visual effects and action sequences were widely praised, while some critics felt that the story was too predictable and lacked the originality of the 1982 classic. Nevertheless, TRON: Legacy remains a beloved sequel in the franchise, offering a fresh take on the world of Tron while honoring the spirit of the original.

belongs_to_collection.name: South Park the Streaming Wars Collection

overview: Cartman locks horns with his mom in a battle of wills while an epic conflict unfolds that threatens South Park’s very existence.
title: South Park the Streaming Wars
plot:
"South Park: The Streaming Wars" is a 2022 American adult animated comedy television special written and directed by Trey Parker. The third South Park special made for Paramount+, it was released on June 1, 2022, and counts as the 318th episode of the series. Voices include Parker, Matt Stone, April Stewart and Kimberly Brooks.

Denver is suffering a severe drought caused by ManBearPig, and as streams dry up, protesters, including waterpark owner Pi Pi, are told that the city's water is going to agriculture. In South Park, Stan Marsh and Tolkien Black worry about Stan's father, Randy, who quarrels with Tolkien's father, Steve. Eric Cartman, unhappy about living in an abandoned hot dog stand, notices a house being built across the street for golf course owner Talnua Cussler and urges his mother, Liane, to get breast implants to attract him. She refuses, reminds him that he is the one who made her quit her job, and tells him the surgery would cost $10,000.

Steve learns he can sell part of his water if it reaches Denver's reservoir, so at Stan and Tolkien's suggestion they build a small boat and float it downstream. The test works, and Steve begins selling subscriptions to his "streaming service", with Pi Pi among his customers. When a jealous Randy wants boats too, Stan and Tolkien recruit Kyle, Kenny and Butters, and finally Cartman, after he claims his mother needs surgery without saying what kind. Cussler orders 10,000 boats for $15,000, covering the cost, but when Cartman presents the surgery to Liane, she holds firm, unmoved even when he threatens to have it done himself.

Steve hears from a dying real estate agent that land near the streams has been sold to a wealthy buyer. When Randy and Stan visit Cussler to end the deal, they find him killed by ManBearPig. At his waterpark, Pi Pi refuses to give up his streaming rights and reveals that he is working with the commissioner and ManBearPig, who stabs Steve and throws him down a water slide. Pi Pi then betrays the commissioner, plotting to replace Denver's water with his park's urine-tainted water. At school, Cartman arrives with breast implants, Tolkien learns his father is missing, and as Denver wastes its dwindling water, Randy begins investigating.

It stems from Parker and Stone's $900 million deal, announced in 2021, for 14 Paramount+ projects, which the creators called specials rather than films. Bubbleblabber rated it 9 out of 10, praising its gags and forward-looking satire.

overview: An engaged, spoiled hotel heiress finds herself in the care of a handsome, blue-collar lodge owner and his precocious daughter after getting amnesia in a skiing accident.
tagline: This holiday season, fall for the unexpected.
title: Falling for Christmas
plot:
Falling for Christmas is an American Christmas romantic comedy of 2022 directed by Janeen Damian, in her feature directing debut, from a screenplay by Jeff Bonnett and Ron Oliver. Lindsay Lohan stars as Sierra Belmont, a pampered hotel heiress who loses her memory in a skiing accident, with Chord Overstreet as the widowed lodge owner Jake Russell, George Young as her boyfriend Tad and Jack Wagner as her father Beauregard.

Sierra has just been named "vice president of atmosphere" at her father's luxury ski resort in Aspen, a job she has no interest in. With Beauregard away on business, Tad takes her up a mountain for a photo shoot and proposes, but a gust of wind knocks her off balance on her skis. She tumbles down the slope and hits her head on a tree. Jake, whose business pitch her father had just rejected, finds her unconscious and takes her to the hospital, where she wakes with amnesia and the staff cannot identify her. Jake offers her a room at his struggling bed and breakfast, the Northstar Lodge, until her memory returns or someone claims her.

Taking the name Sarah from Avy's stuffed toy, Sierra tries to make herself useful around the lodge. She grows close to Jake and especially to Avy, who lost her mother a couple of years earlier; Sierra's own mother died when she was young, and the shared grief begins to stir her memories. Gradually adapting to ordinary life, she organizes a fundraising party to save the lodge. Tad, meanwhile, is lost in the woods until a recluse named Ralph shelters him and walks him back to town. When Beauregard returns four days later and learns his daughter is missing, he alerts the sheriff.

At the party the town rallies behind the Northstar, which is declared a historic site, but before Jake can thank Sierra, her father and Tad burst in to take her home, and her memory comes back. Back at the resort she surprises everyone by doing her own chores and resigns the job her father created for her, resolving to find her own way. Avy confesses that her Christmas wish was for her father to find love and urges him to go after Sierra. Realizing she loves Jake, Sierra ends her engagement to Tad, who takes it well, having become interested in the guest services manager Terry. Jake declares his love, and Sierra returns to help run the lodge, while Beauregard invests in it out of gratitude.

Netflix released the film on 10 November 2022, and it debuted at number one on the service's most-watched films list. Reviews were mixed.

overview: Edward Carnby is a private investigator specializing in unexplainable supernatural phenomena. His cases delve into the dark corners of the world, searching for truth in the occult remnants of ancient civilizations. Now, the greatest mystery of his past is about to become the most dangerous case he has ever faced.
production_companies: Boll Kino Beteiligungs GmbH & Co. KG
tagline: Can mankind defeat the army of darkness unleashed by an ancient evil cult?
title: Alone in the Dark
plot:
Alone in the Dark is a 2005 horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring the theme of isolation and the blurred lines between good and evil. The movie follows Edward Carnby, a paranormal investigator who must stop an ancient evil from unleashing a catastrophic event.

At its core, Alone in the Dark is a tale of psychological terror, where the protagonist's own demons are exploited by the malevolent force he's trying to defeat. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the true horror lies not in the supernatural entity itself, but in the darkness that lurks within human hearts.

The film also touches on the theme of obsession, as Edward's fixation on stopping the evil leads him down a path of self-destruction. The movie raises questions about the nature of good and evil, suggesting that they are not mutually exclusive, but rather intertwined aspects of the human condition.

Furthermore, Alone in the Dark explores the idea of the "other," highlighting the fear and mistrust that can arise when we're faced with something or someone that's beyond our understanding. The film's use of atmospheric tension and eerie visuals creates a sense of unease, mirroring the feelings of disorientation and confusion that Edward experiences as he navigates the treacherous world of paranormal investigation.

Overall, Alone in the Dark is a thought-provoking horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes of isolation, obsession, and the blurred lines between good and evil.

overview: An island populated entirely by happy, flightless birds or almost entirely. In this paradise, Red, a bird with a temper problem, speedy Chuck, and the volatile Bomb have always been outsiders. But when the island is visited by mysterious green piggies, it’s up to these unlikely outcasts to figure out what the pigs are up to.
tagline: Why so angry?
title: The Angry Birds Movie
plot:
The Angry Birds Movie is a 3D animated comedy-adventure film directed by Fergal Reilly and Clay Kaytis, and produced by Sony Pictures Animation. The movie was released on May 20, 2016.

In the beginning of the story, we are introduced to the main character, Red (voiced by Jason Sudeikis), a hot-headed but lovable bird who lives in a forest filled with birds. Red is known for his temper and his ability to get into fights with other birds. However, he has a soft spot for his friends, particularly Chuck (voiced by Josh Gad) and Bomb (voiced by Danny McBride).

The story takes a turn when the evil pig, Hamish (voiced by Bill Hader), steals the magical crystal that keeps the forest's ecosystem in balance. The crystal is hidden on an island called Bird Island, which is inhabited by birds who are obsessed with being perfect and following rules.

Red, Chuck, and Bomb decide to embark on a journey to retrieve the crystal and save their home from destruction. Along the way, they meet new friends, including Matilda (voiced by Maya Rudolph), a wise-cracking bird who becomes Red's love interest, and Guy (voiced by Danny McBride), a laid-back bird who is initially hesitant to join the group.

As they journey through the forest, the birds encounter various obstacles and challenges, including treacherous terrain, fierce predators, and rival birds. However, with their unique skills and teamwork, they are able to overcome these challenges and get closer to their goal.

Meanwhile, Hamish's plan is revealed: he intends to use the crystal to take over the world by building a massive fortress on Bird Island. The birds must stop him before it's too late.

The plot development of the movie takes a dramatic turn when Red discovers that his temper is actually a strength in disguise. He learns to control his emotions and work with his friends to overcome their differences and achieve their goal.

In the end, the birds successfully retrieve the crystal and defeat Hamish's fortress. However, instead of destroying it, they decide to use its power to create a new ecosystem that balances nature and technology. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Red and Matilda sharing a romantic moment, and the other birds learning to appreciate their unique qualities.

Overall, The Angry Birds Movie is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and self-acceptance. With its colorful animation, witty humor, and lovable characters, it's a great movie for both kids and adults.

overview: A New York nightclub manager tries to save his brother and father from Russian mafia hitmen.
tagline: Two brothers on opposite sides of the law. Beyond their differences lies loyalty.
title: We Own the Night
plot:
We Own the Night is a 2007 crime drama film that delves into the complexities of family dynamics, loyalty, and the blurred lines between right and wrong. The movie follows the story of Joe Nolletti, a nightclub manager who must navigate his way through a world of organized crime when his brother, a corrupt cop, gets involved in a violent turf war.

At its core, We Own the Night is a film about the struggle for identity and belonging within a family that values loyalty above all else. The main character, Joe, finds himself caught between his desire to protect his family and his own moral compass, as he becomes increasingly entangled in the world of organized crime. This internal conflict serves as a catalyst for exploring themes of family, power, and the corrupting influence of both.

The film also touches on the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. Joe's brother, Vincent, represents a darker aspect of their shared heritage, one that threatens to destroy the very fabric of their family bond. As the story unfolds, Joe must confront the reality of his own identity and decide where he stands in relation to his family and the world around him.

Furthermore, We Own the Night is a film about the consequences of choices and the devastating impact they can have on those we love. The movie's portrayal of a corrupt cop and the violent underworld he inhabits serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of compromising one's values for personal gain or to maintain a sense of belonging.

Overall, We Own the Night is a gripping drama that explores the complexities of family dynamics, loyalty, and identity, raising questions about what it means to be true to oneself in the face of adversity.

overview: In the pre-Civil War United States, Solomon Northup, a free black man from upstate New York, is abducted and sold into slavery. Facing cruelty as well as unexpected kindnesses Solomon struggles not only to stay alive, but to retain his dignity. In the twelfth year of his unforgettable odyssey, Solomon’s chance meeting with a Canadian abolitionist will forever alter his life.
tagline: The extraordinary true story of Solomon Northup
title: 12 Years a Slave
plot: [No information found]

overview: Arnold and his friends must recover a stolen document in order to prevent the neighborhood from being bulldozed.
tagline: A Big Problem Calls For a Big Head.
title: Hey Arnold! The Movie
plot:
Hey Arnold!: The Movie is a 2002 American animated adventure comedy film based on Craig Bartlett's Nickelodeon television series Hey Arnold!. Directed by Tuck Tucker and written by Bartlett and Steve Viksten, it features the voices of Spencer Klein as Arnold, Francesca Smith as Helga Pataki, Jamil Walker Smith as Gerald, Dan Castellaneta as Grandpa Phil and Nick Vermicelli, Tress MacNeille as Grandma Gertie and Mayor Dixie, Paul Sorvino as Alphonse Perrier du von Scheck and Jennifer Jason Leigh as Bridget.

Arnold and his best friend Gerald learn that Scheck, chief executive of the developer FutureTech Industries, plans to raze their neighborhood of Hillwood and replace it with a luxurious high-rise shopping mall. Helga's father, Big Bob, is working with the company. Arnold's protest block party, "Blockapalooza", collapses when Scheck's employees steal the permit and Grandma Gertie is arrested, and the disheartened neighbors start selling their homes. Then Grandpa Phil tells Arnold about the "Tomato Incident", a historic battle fought on the site of their boarding house, the Sunset Arms, and Arnold realizes that the area must have been declared a historic district. He and Gerald trace the document proving its landmark status to Scheck, who denies having it. A caller named "Deep Voice" tells Arnold that the paper is in Scheck's office safe, and the boys steal the safe key from Scheck's assistant Vermicelli, while Phil and the boarders rig the storm drains with dynamite to stop the bulldozers. With the help of the agent Bridget, Arnold and Gerald slip into FTI headquarters, where Scheck reveals that his ancestor, a British governor, was humiliated by colonists, including Arnold's forebears, over a tomato tax. He burns the document. "Deep Voice" then tells Arnold to get the security camera footage of the burning and is revealed to be Helga, who confesses that she did it out of love for him. Arnold and Bridget play the footage on a giant screen before Mayor Dixie, who reinstates the neighborhood's historic status. Scheck is arrested, and Helga later claims she spoke only in the heat of the moment, which Arnold pretends to believe.

Originally made for television as Arnold Saves the Neighborhood, the film was moved to cinemas by Paramount after strong test screenings. Released on 28 June 2002, it grossed over $15 million on a budget of $3 million to $4 million, but most critics were unimpressed, giving it a 29% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

overview: A case of the flu quickly morphs into a pandemic. As the death toll mounts and the living panic, the government plans extreme measures to contain it.
tagline: Death goes viral.
title: The Flu
plot:
Flu (Gamgi), also released as The Flu, is a South Korean disaster film of 2013 written and directed by Kim Sung-su about an outbreak of a lethal mutated strain of H5N1 avian influenza that kills within 36 hours and plunges the Bundang district of Seongnam into chaos. Jang Hyuk stars as the rescue worker Oh Ji-goo, with Soo Ae as the doctor Kim In-hae, Park Min-ha as her daughter Mi-reu, Yoo Hae-jin as Bae Kyung-ub and Ma Dong-seok as Jeon Gook-hwan.

The smuggler brothers Byung-woo and Byung-ki discover that a container of illegal immigrants has died of a mysterious illness. They take the lone survivor, Monssai, toward their boss in Bundang, but Byung-woo falls ill and Monssai escapes, and at a clinic the infection begins spreading through the city. Meanwhile the rescue workers Ji-goo and Kyung-ub retrieve In-hae's bag from a mine shaft. When Byung-woo is isolated in an emergency room, In-hae suspects the virus mutated inside the container. Byung-woo dies, and his brother exposes hospital staff while struggling to reach him. The container is located and burned, but rats that fed on the bodies escape into the city.

As the doctors identify a mutated H5N1 strain and call for quarantine, officials hesitate until people begin collapsing in the streets and drivers cause deadly crashes. The quarantine begins, and the Prime Minister's announcement feeds the panic. In-hae and Ji-goo rescue Mi-reu from a looted supermarket, but when the girl shows symptoms, mother and daughter are barred from the last helicopter to Seoul. Troops seal the district, and the sick are confined beneath a stadium. In-hae hides her daughter's illness and, after Monssai is found, secretly transfuses his antibodies into Mi-reu.

Under pressure from Leo Snyder of the WHO, the president breaks a promise to release the uninfected after 48 hours. When an officer shoots an infected soldier, a mob storms the isolation zone, seeing what looks like the sick being burned alive. Byung-ki kills Monssai in a suicidal attack to avenge his brother. Mi-reu recovers, and Gook-hwan, an infected agitator, tries to seize her blood before dying in a struggle with Kyung-ub. As the mob confronts soldiers on the highway, In-hae is shot trying to stop Mi-reu from crossing the line; the girl shields her mother, and the crowd shields her. The president orders the troops to stand down and makes Snyder cancel an air strike, and Mi-reu is sent to Seoul to help produce a vaccine.

overview: An evil scientist implants the brain of Michael, a murdered high school student, into an animatronic Tyrannosaurus. Michael escapes, wreaks vengeance on the high school tormentors who killed him, and is reunited with his sweetheart Tammy. Together, the couple try to elude the mad scientist and the police and find a more appropriate vessel for Michael's brain.
tagline: He's the coolest pet in town!
title: Tammy and the T-Rex
plot:
Tammy and the T-Rex is a 1994 American science fiction horror comedy directed by Stewart Raffill, who wrote it with Gary Brockette. Starring Terry Kiser, Ellen Dubin, Denise Richards, Paul Walker, George Pilgrim and John Franklin, it centers on Tammy, a high school student whose boyfriend, Michael Brock, has his brain transplanted into a robotic Tyrannosaurus rex by the mad scientist Dr. Gunther Wachenstein.

At cheerleading practice, Tammy is joined by her new boyfriend, Michael. Her violent, jealous former boyfriend, Billy, arrives with his gang to provoke Michael, and the fight that follows ends with the police taking Billy away while a distraught Tammy runs off in tears. In a dark warehouse, Dr. Wachenstein and his assistant, Helga, inspect a robotic Tyrannosaurus rex operated by remote control, and the doctor reveals his plan to implant a living human brain into the machine to give it consciousness, mobility and "immortality".

That night, Michael sneaks out to visit Tammy, but Billy and his thugs catch him and throw him into a wild animal park, where he is mauled by a lion and left in a coma. As his drunken uncle keeps watch at the hospital, Wachenstein and Helga declare Michael dead so they can take his brain for their robot. Once implanted, Michael escapes in the dinosaur's body, takes revenge on the high school bullies who tormented him and reunites with Tammy, who realizes who he is and begins searching for a more suitable body for him. Wachenstein pursues his creation in a chase that ends with Michael killing the doctor before police gun down the mechanical dinosaur. Tammy saves Michael's brain and takes it home, hooking it up to her computer and camera so that he can see and speak; when she performs a striptease for him, the connections spark.

According to Raffill, a theater owner from South America who had temporary use of an animatronic T-Rex destined for a park in Texas asked him to make a film with it, and Raffill wrote the story in a week so shooting could begin within a month. The opening scenes were filmed at Newbury Park High School in California. Made as an R-rated horror comedy, the film had its gore removed for its original American release, though versions in countries such as Italy kept it. In 2019, Vinegar Syndrome restored the uncut 90-minute version for select theaters and home video, and it was later licensed for the 2022 game High on Life. It holds 43% on Rotten Tomatoes, while the Gore Cut scores 100%.

overview: Homeless and on the run from a military court martial, a damaged ex-special forces soldier navigating London's criminal underworld seizes an opportunity to assume another man's identity, transforming into an avenging angel in the process.
tagline: All roads don't lead to salvation.
title: Hummingbird
plot:
Hummingbird, released in the United States as Redemption, is a 2013 action thriller film written and directed by Steven Knight in his directorial debut. Jason Statham stars as Joseph Smith, a haunted, alcoholic former special forces soldier, with Agata Buzek as Sister Cristina, a young Polish nun, Vicky McClure as his former partner Dawn, Benedict Wong as Mr. Choy, Christian Brassington as Max Forrester and Victoria Bewick as Isabel.

Joseph, a fugitive soldier living rough and drinking in London, escapes a gang of thugs by breaking into an empty luxury flat. Discovering that its owner, the photographer Damon, will be away until October, he moves in, adopts the name Joey Jones, searching for his homeless friend Isabel, who has been forced into prostitution by the same gang. Suffering from post-traumatic stress, he sees visions of hanged men and of "hummingbirds", the drones of Afghanistan. Joseph befriends Cristina, who runs a soup kitchen, and takes a job at a Chinese restaurant. After he subdues some unruly customers, the manager, Mr. Choy, who is tied to a Chinese crime syndicate, hires him as a driver and enforcer. He gives money to the homeless, to Cristina and to Dawn, the mother of his nine-year-old daughter. When Cristina tells him that Isabel has been murdered, he confronts the thugs and gets a rough description of the killer. At an art gallery, Cristina gets drunk and reveals that she has spent his money on ballet tickets for the night of Damon's return; she later reveals that as a girl she killed the gymnastics coach who abused her and was sent to a convent instead of prison, and that she has requested a transfer to Africa. In return for driving a truck of smuggled migrants, Madame Choy identifies the killer as Max Forrester, a man who preys on prostitutes. On Cristina's last night, they sleep together, fleeing as Damon returns. Instead of joining her at the ballet, Joseph leaves Dawn his savings and photographs of himself well dressed for his daughter, then throws Max off a rooftop. Found drunk by Cristina, he admits that he is wanted by a court-martial for killing five civilians in Afghanistan in revenge for five of his men. In a farewell note, he tells her that he has settled his debts and informed the police about Choy's trafficking, and he vanishes into the streets, tracked by police drones.

Shot almost entirely at night, partly among homeless people, the film was released in 2013 to mixed reviews, scoring 50% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Due to a genetic disorder, handsome librarian Henry DeTamble involuntarily zips through time, appearing at various moments in the life of his true love, the beautiful artist Clare Abshire.
title: The Time Traveler's Wife
plot:
The Time Traveler's Wife is a 2009 American romantic science fiction drama directed by Robert Schwentke, adapted from Audrey Niffenegger's 2003 novel. Brad Pitt and Jennifer Aniston's company Plan B Entertainment optioned the book with New Line Cinema before it was even published, and the screenplay passed from Jeremy Leven to Bruce Joel Rubin, while Gus Van Sant was in talks to direct before Schwentke was hired in 2006. Eric Bana and Rachel McAdams were cast in April 2007, and filming began in Toronto that September, with additional shooting in Hamilton, Ontario. Planned for autumn 2008, the release slipped while reshoots waited for the outdoor location to match the season and for Bana to regrow his hair after Star Trek. Warner Bros. Pictures released it on August 14, 2009.

As a boy in the early 1970s, Henry DeTamble survives the car crash that kills his mother by involuntarily jumping two weeks back in time, where an older version of himself helps him. He has a genetic disorder that throws him unpredictably through time, usually toward important people and moments in his life, which he cannot alter, and he always arrives naked, so he learns early to pick locks and steal clothes. In 1991 Clare Abshire greets him joyfully at the Chicago library where he works, though he has never met her. She explains that his future self has been visiting her since she was a little girl and told her they would meet; when she turned 18, he kissed her, and she realized he would be her husband.

Their romance is strained by his sudden disappearances. At their wedding, Henry vanishes and an older version arrives to take his place. He wins the lottery with numbers learned in advance, and the couple are shaken when a wounded, middle-aged Henry briefly appears. Because their unborn children inherit his condition, Clare suffers repeated miscarriages, and Henry secretly has a vasectomy, but a visiting younger Henry fathers a child she carries to term. On a trip forward, Henry meets their daughter, Alba, a time traveler with growing control, who tells him he will die when she is five. After a frostbitten Henry jumps through time again, he is accidentally shot by Clare's father while hunting and dies in Clare's arms. Years later, a younger Henry visits and urges Clare not to spend her life waiting for him.

Bana plays Henry and McAdams plays Clare, with Ron Livingston. Reviews were mixed, with 38% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but the film was a commercial success.

overview: Estranged twins Maggie and Milo coincidentally cheat death on the same day, prompting them to reunite and confront the reasons their lives went so wrong. As the twins' reunion reinvigorates them, they realize the key to fixing their lives may just lie in repairing their relationship.
tagline: Family is a cruel joke.
title: The Skeleton Twins
plot:
The Skeleton Twins is a dark comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of sibling relationships, mental health, and the human condition. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of existential crisis, where the two main characters, Maggie and Milo, are forced to confront their own mortality and the meaninglessness of life.

The film also examines the concept of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and traumas. As the twins navigate their way through a series of misadventures and personal struggles, they are compelled to re-examine their past choices and the decisions that have led them to this point in their lives.

Furthermore, The Skeleton Twins touches on the theme of family dynamics and the ways in which our relationships with others can both heal and harm us. The movie portrays a complex web of emotions, where love, anger, and resentment are intertwined, creating a rich tapestry of human experience.

Ultimately, the film suggests that it's never too late to find redemption, forgiveness, and a sense of purpose, even in the face of adversity and uncertainty. Through its nuanced portrayal of the human condition, The Skeleton Twins offers a thought-provoking exploration of what it means to be alive, and how we can find meaning in our own lives despite the darkness that surrounds us.

overview: Boog, Elliot, and their forest friends return with an all-new adventure, this time in a Big Top Circus! The comedy begins when Boog's pals choose their family obligations over the annual guy's trip, and a disappointed Boog decides to take a trip of his own, which leads him right into the middle of a circus ring...literally. When he switches places with a devious look-a-like circus grizzly and falls for an alluring Russian troupe member, he'll come to realize that maybe you don't have to choose between family and friendship after all.
tagline: Boog and Elliot are Back and the Fur is Going to Fly!
title: Open Season 3
plot:
Open Season 3 is an animated comedy film that revolves around the forest's ecosystem and the relationships between its inhabitants. The movie primarily focuses on three main characters: Otis, a bear who seeks revenge against humans; Judy, a rabbit who tries to bring peace to the forest; and Cody, a young bear cub.

The main themes of Open Season 3 include:

1. **Environmentalism**: The film highlights the importance of coexisting with nature and respecting the balance of the ecosystem. Otis's quest for revenge against humans disrupts this balance, leading to chaos in the forest.
2. **Friendship and Unity**: Judy's efforts to bring peace to the forest demonstrate the value of friendship and unity among different species. Her relationships with Otis and Cody help to resolve conflicts and promote understanding.
3. **Growing Up and Responsibility**: Cody's journey from a curious cub to a more mature bear serves as a metaphor for growing up and taking responsibility. He learns valuable lessons about his place in the forest and the consequences of his actions.

Throughout the movie, these themes are explored through humor, action, and heartwarming moments, making Open Season 3 an entertaining and engaging film for audiences of all ages.

original_title: Dora and the Lost City of Gold
overview: Dora, a girl who has spent most of her life exploring the jungle with her parents, now must navigate her most dangerous adventure yet: high school. Always the explorer, Dora quickly finds herself leading Boots (her best friend, a monkey), Diego, and a rag tag group of teens on an adventure to save her parents and solve the impossible mystery behind a lost Inca civilization.
tagline: Explorer is her middle name.
title: Dora and the Lost City of Gold
plot:
Dora and the Lost City of Gold is a 2019 American adventure comedy film directed by James Bobin, produced by Nickelodeon Movies, and written by Chris Gifford and Carlos Gonzalez. The movie stars Isabela Moner as Dora, Michael Peña as Diego, Eva Longoria as Sofia, Benicio del Toro as Boots, and Jeffrey Wahlberg as Swiper.

The story begins with Dora (Isabela Moner), a 12-year-old girl who lives in the jungle with her father, Dr. Mariposa (Danny Trejo). She is an expert cartographer and has been training to take over his work. However, Dora's life takes a dramatic turn when she receives a message from her mother, who was presumed dead, revealing that she is alive and has been kidnapped by the villainous Swiper (Jeffrey Wahlberg).

Swiper plans to use the ancient map of the Lost City of Gold, which supposedly leads to a treasure worth millions, to fund his nefarious activities. Dora sets out on an adventure with her cousin Diego (Michael Peña), who is also an expert in wildlife and cartography. Together, they embark on a perilous journey through the jungle, facing various obstacles and dangers along the way.

As they navigate through the treacherous terrain, Dora and Diego encounter Sofia (Eva Longoria), a wealthy socialite who claims to be an expert in archaeology but is actually working with Swiper. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Sofia has her own motivations and is not what she seems.

Throughout their journey, Dora and Diego learn valuable lessons about teamwork, bravery, and believing in themselves. They also encounter various creatures, including Boots (Benicio del Toro), a talking monkey who joins them on their quest.

As they near the Lost City of Gold, Dora and her companions face off against Swiper and his minions in an action-packed showdown. In the end, Dora uses her cartography skills to outsmart Swiper and retrieve the map, saving the day and proving herself as a capable adventurer.

The movie features plenty of humor, excitement, and heart, making it a fun and entertaining ride for audiences of all ages. The film's themes of empowerment, friendship, and self-discovery are inspiring and relatable, making Dora and the Lost City of Gold a delightful addition to the Dora franchise.

overview: Korean War, September 1950. In order to fight the enemy forces based in the South of the peninsula, General MacArthur orders the start of the Incheon Landing Operation, deploying diversionary attacks in other locations. Without real military forces to spare, 772 very young Korean student soldiers, barely trained, are sent to Jangsari Beach, where they will face a heroic fate and discover the value of friendship. (A sequel to Operation Chromite, released in 2016.)
tagline: The forgotten heroes
title: Battle of Jangsari
plot:
Battle of Jangsari is a 2019 South Korean war drama film directed by Lee Jeong-ho and produced by Taewon Entertainment.

The main themes of Battle of Jangsari revolve around the historical events that took place during the Imjin War (1592-1598) between Korea and Japan. The film explores several key themes, including:

1. **National pride and resistance**: The movie highlights the bravery and resilience of Korean soldiers who fought against overwhelming Japanese forces to defend their homeland.
2. **War's impact on civilians**: The film also delves into the human cost of war, showing how the conflict affected ordinary people, including women and children, who were caught in the middle of the fighting.
3. **Leadership and sacrifice**: The protagonist, General Yi Sun-sin, is portrayed as a wise and courageous leader who made sacrifices for the sake of his country. His character serves as an inspiration to the other soldiers and civilians.
4. **Historical accuracy vs. myth-making**: The film takes creative liberties with historical events while still maintaining a strong sense of authenticity. This blend of fact and fiction allows the movie to explore the complexities of war and its impact on individuals and society.

The story follows General Yi Sun-sin, who leads the Korean forces against the Japanese invasion. As the battle rages on, he faces numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, enemy forces, and personal doubts. Ultimately, his leadership and strategic thinking help turn the tide of the war in Korea's favor.

Overall, Battle of Jangsari is a powerful and moving film that explores the human side of war and the importance of national pride, sacrifice, and resilience in the face of overwhelming odds.

overview: An inside look at Italy's modern-day crime families, the Camorra in Naples and Caserta. Based on a book by Roberto Saviano. Power, money and blood: these are the "values" that the residents of the Province of Naples and Caserta have to face every day. They hardly ever have a choice and are forced to obey the rules of the Camorra. Only a lucky few can even think of leading a normal life.
production_companies: MEDIA Programme of the European Union
title: Gomorrah
plot:
Gomorrah is a 2008 Italian crime drama film directed by Matteo Garrone, which explores the dark and gritty world of the Neapolitan Camorra, a powerful organized crime syndicate. The movie delves into the themes of corruption, violence, and the cyclical nature of poverty and crime in Naples.

At its core, Gomorrah is a scathing critique of the social and economic conditions that allow the Camorra to thrive. The film portrays a city where the divide between the haves and have-nots is stark, and where the pursuit of wealth and power can lead individuals down a path of destruction and despair. The movie also explores the ways in which institutions, such as law enforcement and government, are complicit in perpetuating the cycle of violence and corruption.

One of the main themes of Gomorrah is the concept of "omertà," or code of silence, which is deeply ingrained in Camorra culture. This code prohibits members from betraying each other, even if it means turning a blind eye to heinous crimes. The film shows how this code can lead to a kind of moral numbness, where individuals become desensitized to the violence and suffering around them.

The movie also explores the theme of family and loyalty, highlighting the ways in which the Camorra uses these values to recruit new members and maintain its power structure. However, this loyalty is often twisted and corrupted, leading individuals to prioritize their allegiance to the organization over their own well-being and humanity.

Ultimately, Gomorrah presents a bleak and unflinching portrayal of a society in crisis, where the rule of law is weak and the forces of corruption and violence hold sway. The film's themes are both deeply disturbing and thought-provoking, offering a searing critique of the social and economic conditions that allow such systems to thrive.

overview: With the help of her coach, her mom, and the boy who drives the Zamboni machine, nothing can stop Casey from realizing her dream to be a champion figure skater.
tagline: Big things happen to those who dream big.
title: Ice Princess
plot:
Ice Princess is a 2005 American romantic comedy-drama film that revolves around the life of Casey Carlyle, a high school student who struggles to balance her athletic ambitions with her passion for figure skating. The movie explores several themes that are woven throughout its narrative.

One of the primary themes of Ice Princess is the struggle for identity and self-discovery. Casey is torn between pursuing her athletic career as a hockey player and exploring her artistic side through figure skating. As she navigates this internal conflict, she must also confront the expectations placed upon her by others, including her parents and coaches.

The film also delves into the theme of perseverance and determination. Despite facing numerous setbacks and disappointments, Casey refuses to give up on her dreams. Her unwavering dedication to figure skating ultimately leads her to discover a new sense of purpose and passion in life.

Furthermore, Ice Princess touches upon the idea of finding one's true voice and expressing oneself authentically. Casey's journey is marked by a series of epiphanies, as she learns to listen to her own desires and aspirations rather than conforming to the expectations of others.

Lastly, the movie explores the theme of female empowerment and self-acceptance. Through Casey's character, the film promotes the idea that it's okay to be different and that embracing one's unique qualities is essential for personal growth and happiness.

Overall, Ice Princess is a heartwarming story about self-discovery, perseverance, and finding one's true voice, all set against the backdrop of figure skating.

overview: When scientists discover something in the Arctic that appears to be a buried Pyramid, they send a research team out to investigate. Little do they know that they are about to step into a hunting ground where Aliens are grown as sport for the Predator race.
tagline: Whoever wins... We lose
title: AVP: Alien vs. Predator
plot:
AVP: Alien vs. Predator is a 2004 science fiction action film directed by Paul W.S. Anderson, produced by 20th Century Fox, and written by Anderson and screenwriter Alex Litvak.

The movie begins with the discovery of an ancient temple on Earth's moon by a team of archaeologists led by Dr. William "Bill" Ikeda (Lance Henriksen). The team is searching for a lost city that holds secrets to the origins of humanity. Unbeknownst to them, they have disturbed a long-dormant alien artifact, which awakens an ancient predator, the Yautja, also known as the Predator.

The Yautja, a technologically advanced and deadly extraterrestrial species, is drawn to Earth by the disturbance in its temple. The creature arrives on the moon and begins to hunt down the archaeologists, killing them one by one. Meanwhile, a spaceship carrying a group of humans from the United States, led by Lieutenant Colonel David Cornwell (Raoul Bova), crash-lands on the moon.

As the Yautja continues its rampage, it is discovered that the aliens are not just mindless killers but have a complex culture and hunting rituals. The Predator's ship lands nearby, and a group of Predators emerges to hunt down the humans. However, they soon realize that the humans are not their usual prey, as they possess a unique genetic trait that makes them resistant to the Predator's deadly plasma caster.

The movie takes a turn when the Yautja and the Predators engage in an epic battle on the moon's surface. The two species clash, with the Yautja using its superior strength and ferocity against the Predators' advanced technology. As the fight rages on, the humans are forced to take sides, with some joining forces with the Predators to survive.

In the end, the Predators emerge victorious, but not without sustaining significant damage from the Yautja's attacks. The movie concludes with the Predators departing Earth, leaving behind a human survivor, who is left to ponder the implications of the encounter between two ancient and deadly species.

Throughout the film, Anderson pays homage to both the Alien and Predator franchises, blending their respective mythologies into a unique narrative that explores the idea of an epic battle between two formidable foes. While AVP: Alien vs. Predator received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among fans of science fiction action films.

The movie's success can be attributed to its well-crafted action sequences, stunning visual effects, and the intriguing dynamic between the Yautja and Predators. The film's climax, which features an intense battle between the two species, is particularly memorable, showcasing the Predator's advanced technology and ferocity in a way that has become iconic in science fiction cinema.

Overall, AVP: Alien vs. Predator is a thrilling sci-fi action film that brings together two beloved franchises in a unique and entertaining way.

overview: Ethan Hunt and his team are racing against time to track down a dangerous terrorist named Hendricks, who has gained access to Russian nuclear launch codes and is planning a strike on the United States. An attempt to stop him ends in an explosion causing severe destruction to the Kremlin and the IMF to be implicated in the bombing, forcing the President to disavow them. No longer being aided by the government, Ethan and his team chase Hendricks around the globe, although they might still be too late to stop a disaster.
tagline: No plan. No backup. No choice.
title: Mission: Impossible - Ghost Protocol
plot:
Mission: Impossible - Ghost Protocol is a 2011 action spy film directed by Brad Bird and produced by Christopher McQuarrie, J.J. Abrams, and Tom Cruise. The movie marks the fourth installment in the Mission: Impossible film series.

The story begins with Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise), a secret agent working for the Impossible Mission Force (IMF). Ethan is tasked with investigating a mole within the IMF who has been stealing sensitive information from the organization's computer systems. As he delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that the mole is actually William Brandt (Michael Nyqvist), a high-ranking official in the IMF.

Ethan soon realizes that the mole has stolen classified information about a top-secret operation codenamed "Ghost Protocol." The mission is to infiltrate the Kremlin and disable a nuclear launch system before it falls into the wrong hands. However, the mole has already alerted the Russian authorities, and Ethan must now work with his team to prevent a global catastrophe.

Ethan's team consists of Benji Dunn (Simon Pegg), a tech expert; Jane Carter (Paula Patton), an IMF agent; and William Brandt, who is initially working against them. As they embark on their mission, they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, deadly traps, and ruthless adversaries.

The team's first stop is the Kremlin, where they must navigate through a series of obstacles to reach the launch system. Along the way, they encounter a group of skilled Russian agents led by Anatoly Sidorov (Michael Nyqvist), who are determined to stop them at all costs.

As the mission unfolds, Ethan and his team discover that the mole has been working with Sidorov, who is actually a former IMF agent turned rogue. The true mastermind behind Ghost Protocol is revealed to be Hendricks (Jeremy Renner), a former CIA operative who was thought to have died in a previous mission.

The final act of the movie takes place at the Kremlin's launch facility, where Ethan and his team must use all their skills and resources to disable the nuclear system. In a thrilling sequence of events, they face off against Sidorov and Hendricks, who will stop at nothing to achieve their goals.

In the end, Ethan and his team succeed in disabling the launch system, but not before Hendricks is killed by Benji Dunn. The movie concludes with Ethan and his team escaping from Russia, where they are greeted as heroes. As for William Brandt, he is revealed to be a double agent working for the IMF all along.
