Overall, Mission: Impossible - Ghost Protocol is an action-packed thrill ride that showcases Tom Cruise's signature stunts and impressive physicality. The movie features stunning set pieces, clever plot twists, and memorable characters that add depth to the story.

overview: In October 1991, a confluence of weather conditions combined to form a killer storm in the North Atlantic. Caught in the storm was the sword-fishing boat Andrea Gail. Magnificent foreshadowing and anticipation fill this true-life drama while minute details of the fishing boats, their gear and the weather are juxtaposed with the sea adventure.
tagline: The storm is coming.
title: The Perfect Storm
plot:
The Perfect Storm is a biographical drama film directed by Wolfgang Petersen, released in 2000 by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The movie is based on the non-fiction book of the same name by Sebastian Junger and is inspired by the true story of the commercial fishing boat Andrea Gail, which was caught in the infamous Hurricane Grace in 1991 off the coast of New England.

The film begins with a dramatic opening sequence showing the stormy weather conditions, setting the tone for the rest of the movie. We are introduced to Billy Tyne (played by George Clooney), a young and ambitious fisherman who is part of a crew on the Andrea Gail, a commercial fishing boat that sets sail from Gloucester, Massachusetts.

The crew, led by Captain Bobby Shatford (played by Mark Wahlberg), includes seasoned fishermen like First Mate Dale "Murph" Murphy (played by Diane Lane) and Deckhand Bobby's brother, Mike (played by John C. Reilly). The crew is on a mission to catch the largest lobster in history, but their journey takes an unexpected turn when they are caught in Hurricane Grace.

As the storm intensifies, the crew faces numerous challenges, including treacherous seas, equipment failure, and personal conflicts. Despite these obstacles, Captain Shatford's leadership skills and experience prove invaluable as he navigates the boat through the raging tempest.

Meanwhile, Billy Tyne finds himself drawn to First Mate Murphy, who becomes a love interest for him. The tension between them is palpable, but their relationship is put to the test as they face the harsh realities of being at sea during a hurricane.

As the storm rages on, the crew faces an unprecedented challenge: the boat is taking on water at an alarming rate, and it's unclear if they'll make it back to shore. The tension builds as the crew fights to keep their vessel afloat, but ultimately, the Andrea Gail succumbs to the fury of the hurricane.

The film's climax is both heart-wrenching and awe-inspiring, as the crew members fight for survival against all odds. In the end, only one member of the crew survives: First Mate Murphy, who finds herself washed up on the shore, her body battered but alive.

The Perfect Storm is a gripping drama that explores themes of courage, sacrifice, and the human spirit in the face of nature's fury. The film features outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Mark Wahlberg as Captain Bobby Shatford, who brings depth and nuance to his portrayal of the seasoned fisherman.

Overall, The Perfect Storm is an intense and emotional ride that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish.

overview: When a girl named Jamie repeatedly tries to contact her grandmother to no avail, she investigates by going to her apartment in Omaha Nebraska - only to find that it's been condemned and overtaken by possessed children. As she digs deeper, she discovers a dark secret about her grandmother and awakens a dark, demonic force that wants Jamie dead and will stop at nothing.
tagline: The All-New, Terror-Filled Chapter!
title: Children of the Corn: Revelation
plot:
Children of the Corn: Revelation is an American slasher horror film of 2001 directed by Guy Magar, the seventh installment in the Children of the Corn series. Claudette Mink stars as Jamie Lowell, a young woman searching for her missing grandmother, with Kyle Cassie as Detective Armbrister, Troy Yorke as the manager Jerry Ulrich and Michael Ironside as a mysterious priest.

After her calls to her grandmother go unanswered, Jamie travels to Omaha, Nebraska, and finds the old woman's apartment building, which stands beside a cornfield, almost deserted apart from two strange children wandering its halls. Her grandmother has been served an eviction notice, Armbrister is unhelpful, and a priest watches Jamie from the street. Back at the apartment she finds a message telling her to go home. In the basement she discovers carrots and tomatoes growing and flees at the sound of children laughing, then meets an armed tenant who warns her to stay out of there, a foul-mouthed old man in a wheelchair and a stripper, Tiffany.

Jerry invites Jamie to a rooftop barbecue, but before she arrives he bites into an ear of corn full of blood and is pushed off the roof by the children. Jamie learns from Armbrister that her grandmother, as a child, belonged to a religious cult whose young members, led by a boy preacher named Abel, burned themselves to death in a tent. Only her grandmother survived, and the apartment building stands on the site of the fire. One by one the tenants die: Tiffany is strangled with corn in her bath, the old man is pushed through a stair railing, and the armed tenant dies of fright in an elevator.

The priest tells her about the history of Gatlin and the devilish creature known as He Who Walks Behind the Rows, warning that her grandmother is dead and she will be too if she stays. The children then drag Jamie to the basement, now filled with rows of corn, where Abel appears and one child reveals herself as Jamie's grandmother, speaking in an old woman's voice. Pretending to accept their invitation to join them, Jamie sets off a gas explosion that leaves Abel unharmed; he binds her with cornstalks, but Armbrister rescues her and they escape before the building blows up, destroying the corn and, it is implied, freeing the children's souls.

Released direct to video, the film was poorly reviewed; DVD Talk called it uninvolving and unremarkable, and Total Film ranked it 49th of 50 Stephen King adaptations.

overview: A battle-scarred War on Terror bounty hunter is forced to go to London on a manhunt for a disavowed CIA operative, which leads him into a deadly running battle with a former military comrade and his private army.
tagline: The world is a battlefield
title: All the Devil's Men
plot:
All the Devil's Men is a 2018 British action thriller written and directed by Matthew Hope. Milo Gibson stars as Jack Collins, a former Navy SEAL turned bounty hunter, with Sylvia Hoeks as his CIA handler Leigh Allen, William Fichtner as Mike Brennan, Gbenga Akinnagbe as Pete Samuelson, Joseph Millson as Tony Deighton and Elliot Cowan as Terry McKnight, alongside Perry Fitzpatrick and Yavor Baharov.

Collins is a war junkie who makes his living hunting terrorists for a private company, part of the CIA's practice of outsourcing such operations to contractors. He is struggling with personal demons, and his superiors have begun to see him as a liability. Leigh offers him one last chance to keep doing the only work he knows and sends him to London on a new assignment. There he joins a three-man team with the veteran operative Brennan and Samuelson. Their target is McKnight, a disavowed CIA operative who is trying to buy a weapon of mass destruction from Russian gangsters before vanishing for good.

The mission is complicated by McKnight's protection: he has hired Deighton, a former colleague of the team, and his private army. What follows is a running urban battle through London between two groups of professionals who know each other's methods and fight intelligently. As the operation goes on, casualties mount on both sides, loyalties shift, and Collins finds that betrayal can come from within his own camp as easily as from the enemy, with a series of double and triple crosses keeping it unclear who is working for whom. Refusing to accept defeat, he battles on toward an explosive final confrontation over the weapon and the men who want it.

The film was released theatrically in the United States on 7 December 2018 and came out on Blu-ray, DVD and digital platforms there on 5 February 2019. Critical reception was largely negative, and the film holds a 23% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Barbara Shulgasser-Parker of Common Sense Media gave it two stars out of five. Dennis Harvey of Variety noted the heavy use of double- and triple-crossing and felt the ending went one plot twist too far for narrative coherence, while Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter considered it so routine, formulaic and forgettable an example of the genre that watching it became an exercise in endurance.

overview: An American hypochondriac who is working as a baggage handler is forced to confront his fears when a British teenager with a terminal illness enlists him to help her carry out her eccentric bucket list.
tagline: Living in the moment is hard to do alone.
title: Then Came You
plot:
Then Came You, also known as Departures, is an American romantic comedy-drama of 2018 directed by Peter Hutchings and written by Fergal Rock. Asa Butterfield plays Calvin Lewis, a young hypochondriac, and Maisie Williams plays Skye Aitken, a teenager with terminal cancer, with Nina Dobrev as the flight attendant Izzy, Tyler Hoechlin as Calvin's brother Frank, David Koechner as their father and Margot Bingham as Frank's wife Lucy.

Skye has been told that her cancer is in its final stages and that she has little time left. Calvin, an airport baggage handler, has a crush on Izzy and lives in constant fear of dying. His doctor sends him to a cancer support group for perspective. There he meets Skye, who takes an instant interest in him, and although he tries to explain that he does not actually have cancer, the two become friends and he agrees to help her complete her list of things to do before she dies. At first irritated by her bluntness and unpredictability, Calvin comes to treasure her company, and as they spend more time together his fear of death begins to fade.

Skye arranges a date between Calvin and Izzy, telling Izzy that he has cancer too, and the pair start dating. Skye admits she always knew Calvin was healthy, but he hesitates to tell Izzy, fearing she only likes him for his illness. From Lucy, Skye learns that Calvin's mother withdrew from life after his twin sister was killed at the age of eight in a car crash while their mother was driving. When Calvin finally confesses the truth, Izzy, hurt by the lie, breaks up with him, and he sinks into depression until his father persuades him to return to work. Skye, meanwhile, loses her virginity to Will, a boy she has a crush on, and finds the experience a letdown.

When Skye collapses and is taken to the hospital, Lucy goes into labor at the same time, and Frank and Lucy ask Calvin and Skye to be their baby's godparents. Calvin panics, but Frank reminds him that Skye still needs him. With help from Izzy and Skye's parents, he helps her finish her list, and he tells her that he stopped celebrating his birthday for his mother's sake after his sister's death. After Skye dies, birthday cards from her arrive in the mail to make up for the ones he missed. Overcoming his fear of heights, Calvin takes a flight, exchanging hopeful glances with Izzy.

 The film premiered at the Woodstock Film Festival in October 2018 and was released by Shout! Factory on 1 February 2019, to mixed reviews.

overview: A sudden and mysterious inheritance brings Danny and his friends to Hobb Springs, a forgotten resort deep in the West Virginia hills. Hobb Springs is being looked after under the watchful care of Jackson and Sally, a socially awkward couple who introduce Danny to the long lost family he's never known. A clan by the name of Hillicker. But soon Danny learns his relatives have a different way of living, that for generations, the Hillickers have observed ancient traditions rooted in cannibalism and other taboo rituals.
title: Wrong Turn 6: Last Resort
plot:
Wrong Turn 6: Last Resort, styled on screen as Wrong Turn VI, is a 2014 slasher film directed by Valeri Milev and the sixth installment in the Wrong Turn series, which it reboots. Milev replaced Declan O'Brien after plans for a film completing a prequel trilogy that began with Wrong Turn 5: Bloodlines were dropped, and shooting reportedly began in Bulgaria in March 2014. 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment released it on DVD and digital platforms on October 21, 2014.

In the West Virginia hills, a pair of bikers are murdered by the cannibal Hillicker brothers, Three Finger, Saw Tooth and One Eye, who are looked after by their deranged kin Jackson and Sally, caretakers of the remote Hobb Springs resort. Danny arrives to claim an unexpected inheritance, accompanied by his girlfriend, Toni, her brother, Rod, and friends Vic, Charlie, Bryan and Bryan's girlfriend, Jillian. Meanwhile an elderly guest, Agnes Fields, is killed with an axe. When Sheriff Doucette warns Bryan and Jillian that townspeople and hotel guests have been disappearing, he is killed at a roadblock by Three Finger. The friends grow suspicious of Danny's cousins, and Danny's growing attachment to his newfound family strains his relationships with the others, though they reluctantly stay when he plans to reopen the hotel.

Planning to leave, Bryan and Jillian steal valuables and find a hidden bathhouse beneath the hotel, where the cannibals ambush them; Jillian is dismembered, and Bryan, left brain-damaged, is assaulted and smothered by Sally. Jackson and Sally reveal to Danny that he is a Hillicker and introduce him to his cannibal relatives, while Vic, who followed them, is captured and disemboweled for the clan's feast. The survivors discover Jackson cooking their friends' remains, and Charlie and Rod are killed as they try to flee. Toni arms herself with a rifle, maims Sally in a fight and kills Jackson with the door keys after Danny lets her go, but Danny, furious at Jackson's death, lets the cannibals kill her. A year later the reopened resort, now Hillicker Springs, is managed by Danny, who carries on the family's sordid traditions with Sally.

Anthony Ilott plays Danny, with Aqueela Zoll as Toni, Chris Jarvis as Jackson and Sadie Katz as Sally. Reviews were negative: Dread Central's Steve Barton gave it 1.5 out of 5 while praising Katz, though Starburst's Joel Harley called it one of the best entries yet. It earned about $1 million in home sales before Wrong Turn (2021) followed.

overview: Quentin Jacobsen has spent a lifetime loving the magnificently adventurous Margo Roth Spiegelman from afar. So when she cracks open a window and climbs back into his life-dressed like a ninja and summoning him for an ingenious campaign of revenge-he follows. After their all-nighter ends and a new day breaks, Q arrives at school to discover that Margo, always an enigma, has now become a mystery. But Q soon learns that there are clues-and they're for him. Urged down a disconnected path, the closer he gets, the less Q sees of the girl he thought he knew.
tagline: Get Lost. Get Found.
title: Paper Towns
plot:
Paper Towns is a coming-of-age comedy-drama film directed by Jake Schreier, based on the novel of the same name by John Green.

The movie follows Quentin "Q" Jacobsen (played by Nat Wolff) as he navigates his senior year of high school and tries to find his place in the world. The story centers around Margo Roth Spiegelman (played by Cara Delevingne), a charismatic and mysterious classmate who sets out on a series of pranks and adventures with Q.

The main themes of Paper Towns include:

1. **Identity Crisis**: Q's journey is also one of self-discovery, as he tries to figure out who he is and where he fits in the world. He struggles with feelings of inadequacy and insecurity, particularly when it comes to his relationships with Margo and his family.
2. **The Elusiveness of Perfection**: Margo represents an unattainable ideal for Q, a symbol of freedom and adventure that he can never quite reach. This theme is reflected in the film's portrayal of Margo as a mythical figure, always one step ahead of Q.
3. **The Power of Human Connection**: Throughout the movie, Q forms deep connections with his friends and family, particularly Ben (played by Austin Abrams) and Lacey (played by Halston Sage). These relationships help him navigate the complexities of life and find his place in the world.
4. **Growing Up and Letting Go**: Paper Towns is a bittersweet film that explores the challenges of growing up and moving on from childhood. Q's experiences with Margo force him to confront the reality of adulthood and the impermanence of relationships.

Overall, Paper Towns is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of identity, connection, and the complexities of growing up.

keywords.name: in love with best friend's guy

overview: Though Rachel is a successful attorney and a loyal, generous friend, she is still single. After one drink too many at her 30th-birthday celebration, Rachel unexpectedly falls into bed with her longtime crush, Dex -- who happens to be engaged to her best friend, Darcy. Ramifications of the liaison threaten to destroy the women's lifelong friendship, while Ethan, Rachel's confidant, harbors a potentially explosive secret of his own.
tagline: It's a thin line between love and friendship.
title: Something Borrowed
plot:
Something Borrowed is a 2011 American romantic comedy film directed by Jason Stone and written by Gwyneth Hughes. The movie stars Kate Hudson, Ginnifer Goodwin, Colin Egglesfield, and John Krasinski.

The main themes of Something Borrowed revolve around the complexities of female friendships, love, and personal growth. The story follows Rachel White (Ginnifer Goodwin), a young lawyer who has been friends with Darcy Rhone (Kate Hudson) since childhood. However, their friendship is put to the test when Rachel falls for Darcy's fiancé, Dex (Colin Egglesfield).

As the plot unfolds, it becomes clear that Rachel and Darcy have different values and priorities in life. While Darcy is more carefree and spontaneous, Rachel is more responsible and driven. The movie explores how these differences affect their friendship and ultimately lead to a dramatic confrontation.

Throughout the film, the theme of female friendships is also explored. The relationship between Rachel and Darcy is portrayed as complex and multifaceted, with moments of deep affection and loyalty, but also periods of tension and conflict. The movie suggests that true friends can be both supportive and challenging, and that their relationships are shaped by a mix of emotions, experiences, and personal growth.

The theme of love is another central aspect of the film. Rachel's unrequited love for Dex serves as a catalyst for her personal growth and self-discovery. As she navigates her feelings for Dex, Rachel must confront her own desires, values, and priorities, leading to a transformation that ultimately changes the course of her life.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, class, and social status. The contrast between Darcy's wealthy upbringing and Rachel's more modest background serves as a backdrop for exploring issues of privilege, entitlement, and social mobility.

Overall, Something Borrowed is a story about navigating complex relationships, personal growth, and self-discovery, all set against the backdrop of a romantic comedy.

overview: It’s a new school year at Monster High™, and the little sister of Clawdeen Wolf™, Howleen, is determined to be more fangtastic than ever.  Her dream of popularity turns out to be easier than anyone imagined when she stumbles upon a genie named Gigi Grant™ who grants her not 3, but 13 Wishes!  But the ghouls quickly learn to be s-careful what you wish for because each wish comes with a dark side, and soon the student disem-body of Monster High™ is turned upside-down!  Join Frankie Stein™, Clawdeen Wolf™, Draculaura™ and the rest of their creeperiffic ghoulfriends as they journey deep inside the magic lantern to save the very soul of Monster High™… while flashing their killer style every step of the way!
tagline: Be scare-ful what you wish for
title: Monster High: 13 Wishes
plot:
Monster High: 13 Wishes is a 2013 American computer-animated fantasy film based on Mattel's Monster High fashion doll franchise, produced by Mattel with animation by Nerd Corps Entertainment. Directed by Steve Sacks with Andrew Duncan and Audu Paden, and written by Ted Zizik and Mike Montesano, it runs 73 minutes and was released on DVD and Blu-ray on 8 October 2013 before airing on Nickelodeon on 25 October. It tied in with the 13 Wishes and Haunt the Casbah doll lines and a video game, and its score is by Paul Robb and Michael Kotch.

A prologue set a thousand years earlier shows the genie Gigi Grant breaking the rules of her lantern to stop her shadow sister, Whisp, from using an eclipse to seize power through the last wish of a finder. In the present, a new school year begins at Monster High, and Clawdeen Wolf's little sister Howleen, tired of being overlooked, is determined to become popular. Serving detention in the school attic with Frankie Stein, Clawdeen, Draculaura, Lagoona Blue and Ghoulia Yelps, she discovers the lantern and frees Gigi, who grants her not three but thirteen wishes, unwittingly releasing Whisp as well.

Howleen first uses her wishes to help her friends, getting the ghouls out of detention, making Abbey Bominable student body president and putting Clawd and his friends on a dangerous television show. Under Whisp's secret influence, however, she wishes herself popular, turns Cleo de Nile into a nobody and banishes Clawdeen into the lantern, leaving a shadow double behind. Each wish has a dark side, and the school turns upside down. Gigi, forbidden to influence her finder, confides in Frankie, revealing that Whisp plans to use the coming eclipse to replace everyone with shadow versions and rule the world. Frankie, Draculaura and Ghoulia have Howleen wish them into the lantern, where they rescue Clawdeen and search for the shards of a shattered magic mirror. Returning on magic carpets in time for the eclipse, they join Howleen's shy shadow friend Twyla, who assembles the mirror and breaks Whisp's spell. Howleen undoes her earlier wishes and spends the last one freeing Gigi while letting Whisp become a real genie of the lantern.

The voice cast includes America Young as Howleen, Jonquil Goode as Gigi, Whisp and Twyla, Salli Saffioti as Clawdeen and Cleo, Kate Higgins as Frankie, Debi Derryberry as Draculaura and Erin Fitzgerald as Abbey. The film was also released in several European countries that October.

original_title: Batman: The Long Halloween, Part One
overview: Following a brutal series of murders taking place on Halloween, Thanksgiving, and Christmas, Gotham City's young vigilante known as the Batman sets out to pursue the mysterious serial killer alongside police officer James Gordon and district attorney Harvey Dent.
tagline: Naughty or nice. Trick or treat. Hero or villain.
title: Batman: The Long Halloween, Part One
plot:
Batman: The Long Halloween, Part One is a 2021 animated superhero film directed by Chris Palmer and produced by Bruce Timm, Sam Register, and Michael Goguen. The movie is based on the comic book series of the same name by Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale.

The story begins with James Gordon Jr., the son of Commissioner James Gordon, being kidnapped by a group of thugs. Young James Jr. is taken to an abandoned warehouse where he witnesses a murder committed by a mysterious figure known as Holiday Killer. The film then jumps forward in time to show James Gordon Sr. becoming the new commissioner of Gotham City.

As Commissioner Gordon, he faces various challenges and villains, including the Riddler (Edward Nigma), who has returned to Gotham after a long absence. The Riddler is determined to prove his intellectual superiority over Batman by committing a series of murders and leaving clues for him to solve.

Meanwhile, Bruce Wayne is struggling with his own demons as he tries to balance his life as a billionaire philanthropist with his nocturnal activities as the Dark Knight. He is haunted by nightmares and struggles to connect with his parents' memory.

The story takes a dark turn when the Holiday Killer strikes again, targeting Commissioner Gordon's family. The killer is revealed to be none other than Harvey Dent, who has been driven mad by his own guilt and sense of justice.

As Batman delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that the Holiday Killer is using an antique calendar as a symbol of their crimes. He also encounters the Riddler, who is determined to outsmart him at every turn.

The film ends with Batman and Harvey Dent forming an uneasy alliance to take down the Holiday Killer, but not before the killer reveals that they have one final target in mind: Commissioner Gordon's family.

Overall, Batman: The Long Halloween, Part One sets the stage for a thrilling and complex story that explores the darker side of Gotham City. With its intricate plot, memorable characters, and stunning animation, this film is sure to delight fans of the Batman franchise.

overview: A burger-loving hit man, his philosophical partner, a drug-addled gangster's moll and a washed-up boxer converge in this sprawling, comedic crime caper. Their adventures unfurl in three stories that ingeniously trip back and forth in time.
tagline: Just because you are a character doesn't mean you have character.
title: Pulp Fiction
plot:
Pulp Fiction is a crime film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino, released in 1994 by Miramax Films. The film interweaves the stories of two mob hitmen, a boxer, and a pair of diner bandits.

The story begins with Vincent Vega (John Travolta) and Jules Winnfield (Samuel L. Jackson), two hitmen working for Marsellus Wallace (Ving Rhames). They are tasked with retrieving a briefcase from a group of young men in Los Angeles, but the mission is complicated when they discover that the briefcase contains heroin, not money.

Meanwhile, we meet Butch Coolidge (Bruce Willis), a boxer who has been ordered by Marsellus to throw a fight. However, Butch double-crosses Marsellus and plans to win the fight instead. He meets Fabienne (Maria de Medeiros), a French woman he had an affair with in Paris.

The film's narrative is presented out of chronological order, jumping back and forth between different storylines. We see Vincent and Jules on a mission to retrieve the briefcase from the young men, who are being held captive by Zed (Peter Greene). The two hitmen engage in a philosophical discussion about the meaning of life and the nature of violence.

As the story unfolds, we learn that Butch's fight is rigged, and he must confront Marsellus when he discovers the truth. Vincent and Jules also face a series of challenges as they try to retrieve the briefcase, including a memorable dance sequence at Jack Rabbit Slim's diner.

The film's climax features a violent confrontation between Vincent and Marsellus, which ultimately leads to the death of one of the main characters. The story concludes with Butch escaping from Marsellus' henchmen and reuniting with Fabienne in Paris.

Throughout the film, Tarantino pays homage to various genres, including crime dramas, martial arts films, and exploitation movies. The dialogue is witty and engaging, with memorable lines such as "Ezekiel 25:17" and "You know what they call a Quarter Pounder with cheese in Paris?"

Pulp Fiction received widespread critical acclaim upon its release, with many praising Tarantino's non-linear storytelling and the performances of the cast. The film was nominated for seven Academy Awards and won one for Best Original Screenplay.

Overall, Pulp Fiction is a complex and engaging film that explores themes of violence, redemption, and the human condition. With its witty dialogue, memorable characters, and non-linear narrative, it has become a cult classic and one of the most influential films of the 1990s.

overview: 19-year-old Billy Lynn is brought home for a victory tour after a harrowing Iraq battle. Through flashbacks the film shows what really happened to his squad - contrasting the realities of war with America's perceptions.
tagline: To walk the path of a hero, you have to see how it all began.
title: Billy Lynn's Long Halftime Walk
plot:
Billy Lynn's Long Halftime Walk is a 2016 American war drama film directed by Ang Lee, based on the 2012 novel of the same name by Ben Fountain. The movie follows the story of Billy Lynn, a U.S. Army soldier who returns home after being deployed to Iraq for 18 months.

The main themes of the film include:

1. **Trauma and PTSD**: The movie explores the psychological effects of war on soldiers, particularly those who have experienced traumatic events. Billy's struggles with PTSD are evident throughout the film, as he grapples with flashbacks, nightmares, and feelings of guilt.
2. **Reality vs. Perception**: The film blurs the lines between reality and perception, as Billy's experiences in Iraq are contrasted with his life back home. This theme is reflected in the film's use of non-linear storytelling and multiple timelines.
3. **The Cost of War**: The movie highlights the human cost of war, particularly on soldiers who are sent to fight in foreign lands. Billy's experiences in Iraq serve as a reminder of the sacrifices made by those who serve their country.
4. **Family and Belonging**: The film explores the theme of family and belonging, as Billy struggles to adjust to life back home after his deployment. His relationships with his family members are complex and multifaceted, reflecting the challenges of readjusting to civilian life.
5. **The Power of Storytelling**: The movie showcases the power of storytelling as a way to process trauma and make sense of one's experiences. Billy's story is told through various media, including video games, TV shows, and even a Thanksgiving dinner, highlighting the ways in which stories can be used to cope with difficult emotions.

Overall, Billy Lynn's Long Halftime Walk is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes related to war, trauma, and identity.

overview: After security expert Ray Breslin is hired to rescue the kidnapped daughter of a Hong Kong tech mogul from a formidable Latvian prison, Breslin's girlfriend is also captured. Now he and his team must pull off a deadly rescue mission to confront their sadistic foe and save the hostages before time runs out.
tagline: This time it’s personal
title: Escape Plan: The Extractors
plot:
Escape Plan: The Extractors is a 2019 action thriller film directed by John Hlavin and starring Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, and Adria Arjona. 

The main themes of Escape Plan: The Extractors revolve around the exploitation of vulnerable individuals, particularly women, in the sex trade industry. The story follows a former CIA operative (Stallone) who teams up with a skilled hacker (Arjona) to rescue his kidnapped sister from a human trafficking ring.

Throughout the film, the theme of female empowerment is prominent as the protagonist's sister and other female characters fight against their oppressors. The movie also explores the consequences of corruption and the exploitation of power by those in positions of authority.

Additionally, the film touches on the theme of redemption, as the protagonist seeks to make amends for past mistakes and protect his loved ones from harm. The action-packed plot is driven by a sense of urgency and revenge, adding an element of tension and suspense to the narrative.

Overall, Escape Plan: The Extractors is a gripping thriller that delves into complex themes such as exploitation, corruption, and female empowerment, set against a backdrop of high-stakes action and adventure.

overview: Brazil is a contract killer, willing to take any job if the price is right. Flint left the assassin game when a ruthless drug dealer’s brutal attack left his wife in a coma. When a contract is put out on the same coldblooded drug dealer, both Brazil and Flint want him dead – one for the money, the other for revenge. With crooked Interpol agents and vicious members of the criminal underworld hot on their trail, these two assassins reluctantly join forces to quickly take out their target before they themselves are terminated.
tagline: Twice the fire... double the power!
title: Assassination Games
plot:
Assassination Games is a 2011 American action thriller directed by Ernie Barbarash from a screenplay by Aaron Rahsaan Thomas, starring Jean-Claude Van Damme and Scott Adkins as rival contract killers, with Ivan Kaye as their common enemy. Produced by the Motion Picture Corporation of America with Mediapro Studios and Rodin Entertainment on a budget of about $8 million, it was shot in Bucharest, Romania, and New Orleans in the autumn of 2010, with a score by Neal Acree.

Vincent Brazil is an assassin and master of bladed weapons who will take any job if the price is right. Roland Flint, a top marksman, has walked away from the profession since the drug kingpin Polo Yakur launched a brutal attack that left Flint's wife, Anna, in a coma from which she has never awoken. When a contract is put out on Yakur, both men want it: Brazil for the money, Flint for revenge. The two strangers start out as competitors working the same target, but with crooked Interpol agents protecting the dealer and vicious members of the criminal underworld closing in on them both, they reluctantly join forces to take Yakur down before they themselves are eliminated.

Van Damme plays Brazil and Adkins plays Flint, with Kevin Chapman as Culley, Valentin Teodosiu as Blanchard, Alin Panc as Kovacs, Michael Higgs as Godfrey and Marija Karan as October, Bianca Bree as Anna Flint and Kris Van Damme as Schell.

The project began life under the working title The Weapon, with Russell Mulcahy attached to direct and Steven Seagal set to co-star with Van Damme. After Seagal dropped out, Vinnie Jones was considered for the part before it went to Adkins. The film received a limited theatrical release in the United States on 29 July 2011, followed by a DVD release from Sony Pictures Home Entertainment that September, and opened in France and Russia later in 2011 and 2012.

Reviews were mixed. IGN rated it 6 out of 10 and called it a quick dose of action that should leave viewers moderately pleased, and Indiewire's Gabe Toro gave it a C, noting that it at least showed filmmakers who still understood how to shoot action. DVD Talk's Rohit Rao gave it two stars out of five, complaining of a convoluted script that mistakes meanness for grit, and DVD Verdict found it cheesy, pretentious and poorly paced.

overview: Diego, Manny and Sid return in this sequel to the hit animated movie Ice Age. This time around, the deep freeze is over, and the ice-covered earth is starting to melt, which will destroy the trio's cherished valley. The impending disaster prompts them to reunite and warn all the other beasts about the desperate situation.
tagline: Kiss Your Nuts Goodbye
title: Ice Age: The Meltdown
plot:
Ice Age: The Meltdown is a 2006 animated adventure comedy film produced by Blue Sky Studios and distributed by 20th Century Fox. The movie serves as a sequel to the original Ice Age film.

The story begins with Manny, a woolly mammoth, Sid, a sloth, and Diego, a saber-toothed tiger, living in their respective habitats during the Pleistocene era. However, due to climate change, the ice caps are melting, causing chaos throughout the world. The trio is forced to embark on an epic journey to reach the fabled "Paradise Falls," a lush oasis that has been hidden beneath the melting ice.

As they travel through treacherous landscapes and encounter various obstacles, Manny, Sid, and Diego begin to realize that their friendship is more important than their individual goals. Along the way, they meet new characters, including Buck, a weasel who becomes an unlikely ally, and Scrat, Manny's obsessive acorn-loving companion.

As the group nears Paradise Falls, they discover that it has been taken over by a group of ruthless pirates led by Captain Gutt, a giant prehistoric crocodile. The pirates are determined to claim the falls' resources for themselves, putting the entire ecosystem at risk.

Manny, Sid, and Diego must use their unique skills and work together to defeat the pirates and save Paradise Falls. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, trust, and the importance of preserving their natural habitats.

The movie features stunning animation, witty humor, and lovable characters that have become iconic in popular culture. The voice cast, including Ray Romano, John Leguizamo, Denis Leary, and Queen Latifah, delivers memorable performances that bring the characters to life.

In the end, Manny, Sid, and Diego successfully defeat Captain Gutt and his pirates, saving Paradise Falls and restoring balance to the ecosystem. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of friendship and camaraderie between the three main characters as they look out upon their newly preserved home.

Overall, Ice Age: The Meltdown is a fun, action-packed adventure that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and environmentalism. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's no wonder this movie has become a beloved classic among both children and adults alike.

overview: Ben Tennyson falls through a wormhole and encounters Rex. The two heroes must unite against a foe that can absorb their powers.
tagline: Two Heroes. One Epic Battle.
title: Ben 10 Generator Rex Heroes United
plot:
Ben 10/Generator Rex: Heroes United is an animated crossover special uniting Ben 10: Ultimate Alien and Generator Rex, written by Man of Action, the creative team behind both series. Structured as a double-length episode of Generator Rex, covering the third and fourth episodes of its third season, it brings Ben Tennyson into Rex's universe and redraws him and his alien forms in that show's art style. It premiered at New York Comic Con 2011 before airing in a one-hour slot on Cartoon Network on November 25, 2011, the network's second crossover special after 2007's The Grim Adventures of the KND.

A mysterious rift opens over Manhattan, and Rex Salazar, a former agent of the peacekeeping organization Providence, arrives with Agent Six and Bobo. Something comes through: Ben, transformed into Humungousaur. Mistaking him for an EVO, a human mutated by rogue nanites, Rex fights him across the city as Ben shifts into Diamondhead, Lodestar and Rath, while a strange metallic creature that also emerged from the rift slips away. Back in human form, Ben is stunned that nobody knows him. The creature self-destructs in front of Six, leaving him in a coma, and Rex blames Ben. Doctor Holiday finds the creature was nanite-based but unlike any EVO. Ben escapes confinement as Big Chill, and he and Rex meet Caesar, who admits he created the creature, Alpha, to manufacture adaptable nanites, then banished it to another dimension after it became sentient and began seizing human bodies. Ben realizes Caesar sent it into the Null Void, the alien prison where it took a cyborg body before returning.

Alpha now aims to absorb EVOs and capture Rex's Omega Nanite, the key to its perfection. At the Bug Jar, a quarantined city of EVOs, Ben fights as XLR8, Four Arms and the new Shocksquatch, but Alpha copies the Ultimatrix and takes Rex's Omega Nanite, becoming the giant Alpha-Omega. Ben merges with Rex as Upgrade and together they compress Alpha into a dense sphere. Caesar recovers the Omega Nanite and opens a rift home for Ben, who, as Upchuck, swallows the compacted Alpha before leaving. Six recovers, Caesar restores Rex's nanite, and Alpha stirs in the Null Void, hinting at a return.

Daryl Sabara voices Rex, with Yuri Lowenthal as Ben, Wally Kurth as Six, Grey DeLisle as Holiday, John DiMaggio as Bobo, J. K. Simmons as White Knight, Michael Emerson as Alpha and Freddy Rodriguez as Caesar. Fans of both series embraced the special, which reached the iTunes top 100.

overview: Donna's senior prom is supposed to be the best night of her life, though a sadistic killer from her past has different plans for her and her friends.
tagline: A Night To Die For.
title: Prom Night
plot:
Prom Night is an American slasher film of 2008 directed by Nelson McCormick and written by J. S. Cardone, the fifth and final entry in the Prom Night series and a loose remake of the original 1980 film. Brittany Snow stars as Donna Keppel, a high school senior stalked by the man who murdered her family, with Scott Porter as her boyfriend Bobby, Jessica Stroup and Dana Davis as her friends Claire and Lisa, Johnathon Schaech as the killer Richard Fenton, and Idris Elba and James Ransone as the detectives Winn and Nash.

In Bridgeport, Oregon, Donna, then a freshman, comes home one night to find her father and younger brother murdered and watches her mother being killed before the attacker turns on her. He is Richard Fenton, her former biology teacher, whose obsession with her had cost him his job and earned him a restraining order. Arrested, he vows that he will always love her and that nothing can keep them apart.

Three years later, Donna lives with her uncle Jack and aunt Karen and is in therapy for her trauma. She and her friends are getting ready for their senior prom at a luxury hotel when Detective Winn learns that Fenton has escaped from a psychiatric hospital. Certain he will go after Donna, Winn heads for the hotel with his partner Nash. Fenton kills a maid to obtain a master key card, slips into the friends' shared suite and murders Claire and Michael there. Lisa recognizes him and tries to warn Donna, but Fenton chases her onto a mezzanine under construction and slits her throat.

In the hotel garage Winn finds a car holding the corpse of the man whose identity Fenton stole, then the dead maid, and orders an evacuation. Returning to her room to look for Lisa and retrieve her mother's shawl, Donna encounters Fenton but escapes. A SWAT team searches the building in vain, and Winn realizes that the killer slipped out disguised as a bellhop. Donna and Bobby are escorted to her house under police protection. After a nightmare about Fenton, Donna wakes, closes the bathroom window and finds Bobby dead in her bedroom with his throat cut. Hiding in her closet, she finds Fenton already inside. Winn arrives to find Nash dead, and as Fenton is about to stab Donna, the detective shoots him dead.

Made for about $20 million and shot mostly in Los Angeles, the film was released by Screen Gems on 11 April 2008 and opened at number one in North America, eventually grossing about $57 million worldwide. Critics savaged it as dim and predictable.

overview: The little swift Manou grows up believing he's a seagull. Learning to fly he finds out he never will be. Shocked, he runs away from home. He meets birds of his own species and finds out who he really is. When both seagulls and swifts face a dangerous threat, Manou becomes the hero of the day.
title: Manou the Swift
plot:
Manou the Swift, also released as Birds of a Feather and Swift, is a 2019 German animated adventure comedy produced in English and directed by Christian Haas and Andrea Block, founders of the animation house LUXX Studios. The English-language voice cast features Josh Keaton as Manou, Kate Winslet as Blanche, Willem Dafoe as Yves, Cassandra Steen as Kalifa, Mikey Kelley as Luc, David Shaughnessy as Percival, Arif S. Kinchen and Nolan North as Kalifa's brothers Poncho and Yusuf, Julie Nathanson as Francoise and Rob Paulsen.

On a rocky cliff overlooking the sea on France's Côte d'Azur, a colony of seagulls lives on one side and a colony of swifts on the other, and the two species regard each other with contempt. Manou is a swift whose parents are killed before he even hatches. Left alone in the world, the chick finds his way into the nest of the seagull couple Blanche and Yves, the strong-willed but stubborn leader of the colony. Blanche is the first to discover him and take him in, and the pair raise him as their son alongside their own chick, Luc, with whom Manou forms a close bond.

As he grows up, however, Manou becomes painfully aware that he is not like the other gulls. At sailing school he clashes with a rival, Francoise, and he must win an important race to prove himself worthy of the seagull community. Eventually exiled to the swifts' side of the rock, he meets his own kind for the first time and falls for Kalifa, while Percival, a flightless, neurotic bird who lives in a cemetery and laments a lost love, provides comic relief. The real threat to both colonies comes from a swarm of rats that raid nests and steal eggs. Their attacks finally force the feuding gulls and swifts to unite, and Manou, accepting his identity as a swift, helps fight off the rats and earns the respect of both seagulls and swifts.

The film was released in various international markets during 2019, reaching British cinemas on 26 July 2019, and opened in limited release and on demand in the United States in February 2020. Reviews were largely negative. Cath Clarke of The Guardian found it virtually laugh-free and indebted to The Jungle Book. Josh Bell of Crooked Marquee praised the detailed backgrounds but found the character animation clumsy, the plot lurching between set pieces and the message of tolerance delivered without conviction, while other critics admired its scenery but faulted its predictable story and weak humor.

overview: During a dinner, a group of friends decide to share whatever message or phone call they will receive during the evening, with unforeseen consequences.
tagline: Everyone has three lives: A public life. A private life... and a secret life.
title: Perfect Strangers
plot:
Perfect Strangers (Perfetti sconosciuti) is an Italian psychological comedy-drama of 2016 directed and co-written by Paolo Genovese. The ensemble cast features Kasia Smutniak and Marco Giallini as the hosts Eva and Rocco, Alba Rohrwacher and Edoardo Leo as the newlyweds Bianca and Cosimo, Anna Foglietta and Valerio Mastandrea as Carlotta and Lele, Giuseppe Battiston as Peppe and Benedetta Porcaroli as Eva and Rocco's teenage daughter Sofia.

On the night of a total lunar eclipse, Eva, a psychotherapist, and her husband Rocco, a plastic surgeon, whose marriage is in trouble, host a dinner for old friends: Cosimo, a taxi driver, and Bianca, a veterinarian, recently married and hoping for a child; Lele and Carlotta, married for ten years and also struggling; and Peppe, a divorced, unemployed former physical education teacher whose new girlfriend Lucilla is ill and cannot come. Eva, convinced that many couples would break up if they saw each other's phones, proposes a game: everyone puts their phone on the table and shares every message and call that arrives during the evening. Rocco is the most reluctant, but all agree.

The game begins harmlessly but soon spins out of control. It emerges that Rocco has secretly been seeing an analyst and that Eva plans breast surgery with another surgeon. Lele, who receives racy photos from another woman every night, persuades Peppe to swap their identical phones, only for messages from a man named Lucio to arrive on Peppe's phone, leading everyone to believe that Lele is secretly gay. Carlotta is devastated, and Cosimo, offended that his best friend never confided in him, reacts with open homophobia. Cosimo, jealous of Bianca's ex, is exposed in turn: his lover, a taxi dispatcher, is pregnant, and a call hints that he has also been sleeping with Eva. Carlotta, caught exchanging suggestive messages with another man, confesses that years earlier she killed a pedestrian while driving drunk and Lele took the blame. Peppe admits that Lucio is his partner, whom he shields from his friends, and Bianca, heartbroken, leaves after telling Peppe he is right. When the eclipse ends, it turns out the game never happened, because Rocco refused to play.

The film won the David di Donatello for Best Film and was a major hit, opening at number one in Italy and grossing more than €16 million there. Guinness World Records later recognized it as the most remade film in history, with versions in 24 languages.

overview: Fusion spent two years with the production team of Disney's smash hit film. In 'Imagining Zootopia,' you will travel with the team to Africa to explore the animals in their natural habitat and find out how the storytellers and animators dealt with the very real themes of prejudice and bias.
tagline: What did it take to bring the world of 'Zootopia' to life?
title: Imagining Zootopia
plot:
Imagining Zootopia is a 2016 American documentary film about the making of Walt Disney Animation Studios' feature Zootopia, released in some territories as Zootropolis. Directed by Natalie Osma and Kristofer Rios for Fusion, the millennial-oriented digital network that was then half-owned by Disney, it runs about 47 minutes. Although not an official Disney production, it was made with extensive access: the filmmakers spent two years following the crew through production. It features directors Byron Howard and Rich Moore, co-director and screenwriter Jared Bush, head of story Josie Trinidad, production designer Dave Goetz, producer Clark Spencer and John Lasseter, then chief creative officer of Disney and Pixar Animation.

The documentary follows the creative process from character conception to animation. It accompanies the team on a research trip to Kenya, where they study animals in their natural habitats, and examines the artwork produced for the film, from sketches of its expressive animal characters to its highly detailed environments. The filmmakers explain the film's roots in their love of Disney films in which animals walk upright and wear clothes, such as the studio's 1973 version of Robin Hood. Rather than cataloguing every aspect of production, however, most of the film concentrates on the evolution of the story, which changed dramatically during development. In early versions, the con artist fox Nick Wilde was the protagonist instead of the rabbit police officer Judy Hopps, and the fragile peace between predators and prey was maintained only because the predators were forced to wear shock collars. The documentary traces in depth how the storytellers moved from that version to the finished film, and how they approached the real-world themes of prejudice and bias in what is essentially a family film.

Fusion released the documentary online in early April 2016, about a month after Zootopia opened in theaters to critical acclaim; by then the film had grossed nearly $800 million worldwide. Amid Amidi of Cartoon Brew called it well worth watching, describing it as a counterpart to The Sweatbox that highlights the positive changes Lasseter had brought to Disney's feature animation division, and praising its choice to focus on story development, which he felt offered real insight into what the filmmakers were trying to achieve.

original_title: The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh
overview: Whether we’re young or forever young at heart, the Hundred Acre Wood calls to that place in each of us that still believes in magic. Join pals Pooh, Piglet, Kanga, Roo, Owl, Rabbit, Tigger and Christopher Robin as they enjoy their days together and sing their way through adventures.
tagline: Hip Hip Poohray!
title: The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh
plot:
The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh is a 1977 animated film produced by Walt Disney Productions. The movie is based on the stories created by A.A. Milne and features the beloved characters from the Hundred Acre Wood.

The main themes of The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh can be interpreted in several ways, but some of the most prominent ones include:

1. Friendship: The film showcases the strong bond between Winnie the Pooh, Piglet, Eeyore, Tigger, and other characters from the Hundred Acre Wood. Their friendship is built on trust, loyalty, and understanding, which helps them navigate various challenges and adventures.
2. Imagination and Fantasy: The movie celebrates the power of imagination and fantasy, as seen in Winnie the Pooh's love for honey and his ability to create fantastical worlds with his friends. This theme encourages viewers to think creatively and explore their own imagination.
3. Growing Up and Letting Go: The story also touches on the theme of growing up and letting go. Eeyore, in particular, struggles with the idea of growing older and losing his youthful energy. However, through his friendships and adventures, he learns to accept and appreciate the changing seasons of life.
4. Simple Joys: The film highlights the importance of simple joys and pleasures in life. Winnie the Pooh's love for honey is a prime example, as it brings him immense happiness and contentment. This theme encourages viewers to appreciate the small things in life and find joy in everyday moments.

The movie features several segments, each with its own unique storyline and themes. The film's blend of humor, adventure, and heartwarming moments has made it a beloved classic among audiences of all ages.

Overall, The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh is a timeless tale that celebrates the power of friendship, imagination, and simple joys in life.

overview: A family returns from a Grand Canyon vacation with a supernatural presence in tow.
tagline: Evil comes home
title: The Darkness
plot:
The Darkness is an American supernatural horror film of 2016 directed by Greg McLean, who co-wrote it with Shayne Armstrong and Shane Krause, about a family that brings home a malevolent force from the Grand Canyon. Kevin Bacon and Radha Mitchell play Peter and Bronny Taylor, with David Mazouz as their autistic son Mikey, Lucy Fry as their daughter Stephanie, and Matt Walsh and Jennifer Morrison as their friends the Carters.

On a holiday at the Grand Canyon in Arizona with another family, the Carters, Mikey wanders into a small cave and finds black stones carved with symbols, which he takes home. Soon strange things begin to happen in the Taylors' house: the kitchen taps keep turning on, and handprints appear on a mirror, incidents Mikey blames on someone he calls "Jenny". Stephanie, who has been secretly bulimic, is caught hiding vomit under her bed, and her parents take her for treatment, leaving Mikey with Bronny's mother, who catches him trying to kill her cat.

Searching online, Bronny learns that the Anasazi believed demons were bound to stones hidden in caves; if the stones are removed, the spirits take the forms of a crow, a snake, a coyote, a wolf and a buffalo, attach themselves to young children and draw them into their world in an event called the Darkness. The only way to banish the demons is for someone without fear to return the stones to where they were found. The haunting intensifies: after a fire in his room, Mikey is found soot-marked and bleeding from the mouth; Bronny, plagued by nightmares of a wolf, starts drinking; and invisible hands choke Stephanie until Peter, who has seen a coyote and a shadowy figure, rushes in. The burned patch of Mikey's wall turns out to be a portal.

Peter calls a healer named Teresa, recommended by his boss, who arrives with her granddaughter Gloria as interpreter. As they cleanse the house, they find that the true evil resides in Mikey's room and begin a chant while the boy walks into the portal with the demons. Peter follows with the stones but is too afraid to set them down and offers to take his son's place. Mikey, who is not afraid, puts the stones down himself, ending the Darkness, and father and son leap back out before the portal vanishes and Gloria declares the house cleansed.

Filmed in Los Angeles in April and May 2014, the film was released on Friday 13 May 2016 by Blumhouse Tilt and High Top Releasing. It was panned by critics but earned $10.9 million on a $4 million budget.

overview: An immigrant in search of the American dream is forced to take a room in a boarding house and soon finds herself in a nightmare from which she can't escape.
tagline: Don’t try to leave. It’ll only make things worse.
title: No One Gets Out Alive
plot:
No One Gets Out Alive is a British supernatural horror film of 2021 directed by Santiago Menghini, in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Jon Croker and Fernanda Coppel, loosely adapted from Adam Nevill's 2014 novel of the same name. Cristina Rodlo stars as Ambar, an undocumented Mexican immigrant, with Marc Menchaca as the landlord Red, David Figlioli as his brother Becker and David Barrera as Ambar's uncle Beto. Netflix released it on 29 September 2021.

After her mother's death, Ambar leaves Mexico for Cleveland, Ohio, where she works off the books and lives on her savings. Looking for somewhere to stay, she takes a room in a run-down boarding house run by Red, who demands the first month's rent in advance. Strange things begin to happen almost at once. She glimpses Red's mentally ill brother Becker beating his head against a door; some rooms are crammed with odd artifacts, including images of ritual sacrifice; and Ambar starts seeing ghostly women around the house. A coworker steals the rest of her savings, promising a fake ID, and Ambar loses her job.

Terrified by her visions, Ambar flees the house, but penniless, she has to turn to Red, who promises to return her deposit if she comes back for it. The money is not there; instead, Becker forces wine on her. Two Romanian women who have also moved in visit her; she falls asleep and wakes to find the brothers tying up the women. She fights back and Beto, coming to look for her, is attacked by Becker. Red explains that their archaeologist father brought a stone box back from Mexico in 1963 and, with their mother Mary, murdered women for it, the ghosts Ambar has seen; after the brothers killed their father for sacrificing their mother, Becker insisted on continuing, because each sacrifice made him healthier.

Becker ties Ambar to a stone slab before the box, where the other woman has been beheaded, and opens it. Beto frees her, but she is drawn into a vision of her dying mother, who tries to strangle her, while a huge moth-like creature emerges from the box. Ambar fights back, smothering her mother in the vision, and the creature retreats. Arming herself with an obsidian-edged macuahuitl, she wounds Red and kills Becker, then ties the injured Red to the slab and watches the monster bite off his head. As she leaves, her broken ankle heals, and with a moth on her hand she turns back toward the basement, her veins darkening like Becker's.

Reviews were mixed.

overview: Alexandra "Alex" Delgado, a pairs figure skater, found her career come to an abrupt halt after her partner (on and off the ice) became injured. As their love affair cooled, a heartbroken Alex stopped competing and turned to teaching. Enter James Van Behr the smoldering bad boy of speed skating, who has had fiery Alex in his sights as a skating partner ever since he was banned from speed skating. There aren't many girls who say no to him but she may well be the first. However, he pushes her buttons, challenging her like no one else - and her fighting spirit returns. She agrees to be his partner and they begin a grueling practice regimen fueled (and occasionally derailed) by their own tempestuous relationship, which heats up as they get closer to competition. But will their passion destroy Alex's chance to bring home the gold again?
title: The Cutting Edge: Fire & Ice
plot:
The Cutting Edge: Fire & Ice is a 2010 American sports romance television film directed by Stephen Herek and written by Holly Brix. Made for the ABC Family cable channel, which first aired it on March 14, 2010, it is the sequel to The Cutting Edge: Chasing the Dream (2008) and the fourth instalment of The Cutting Edge series. Francia Raisa reprises her role as figure skater Alexandra "Alex" Delgado from the third film, opposite Brendan Fehr as a hot-headed speed skater who wants to become her pairs partner.

Alex's competitive career came to an abrupt end when her skating partner, who was also her boyfriend, was injured, and as their romance cooled she stopped competing altogether. Heartbroken, she now earns her living teaching children to skate, avoids dating, and worries her mother, who fears she is throwing away her dreams and will end up alone. James McKinsey, meanwhile, is the cocky bad boy of speed skating, banned from his sport after punching a teammate. With his agent he hatches a plan to switch to pairs figure skating, recruiting Zhen Zheng, a coach who loves a challenge but speaks no English and works through a translator, Mr. Wan. Finding a partner is harder, since most assume the move is merely a publicity stunt until his suspension is lifted. James has long had the fiery Alex in his sights, and she becomes perhaps the first woman to turn him down, but his provocations rekindle her fighting spirit and she agrees to partner him. Their gruelling training regime is repeatedly derailed by their tempestuous relationship. James parties the night before practice and shows up hungover, while the disciplined but cautious Alex hesitates over a daring new move he devises. Gradually, though, they find common ground: they bond during a bar fight, Alex learns that James is good with children, and he discovers she can shoot pool. A game of strip poker is interrupted when Alex's mother drops by. As their mutual attraction grows and the national championships in Montreal draw near, Alex must stay focused and learn to trust both her partner and her own feelings, while James works to overcome his selfish reputation.

Raisa plays Alex and Fehr plays James, with Zhenhu Han as Zhen Zheng, Russell Yuen as Mr. Wan and Dan Jeannotte as Angus Dwell. Reviewers considered it sweet but predictable, praising the chemistry between Raisa and Fehr and the energetic skating sequences, while noting the film's heavy reliance on montages.

overview: A fictionalized account of the last days of Edgar Allan Poe's life, in which the poet is in pursuit of a serial killer whose murders mirror those in the writer's stories.
tagline: The only one who can stop a serial killer is the man who inspired him.
title: The Raven
plot:
The Raven is a 2012 American horror film directed by James McTeigue and starring John Cusack as Edgar Allan Poe. 

The movie begins with Poe's life in Baltimore, where he has just lost his young wife, Virginia. He becomes obsessed with solving the murder of a young woman named Lenore, who bears an uncanny resemblance to his late wife.

As Poe delves deeper into the mystery, he encounters a series of eerie and supernatural events that lead him to believe that the killer is trying to communicate with him through cryptic messages and riddles. The film's plot is heavily influenced by Poe's own works, particularly "The Murders in the Rue Morgue" and "The Pit and the Pendulum".

Throughout the movie, Poe's character grapples with his own demons, including his grief over Virginia's death and his struggles with addiction and poverty. The film also explores themes of love, loss, and the power of art to transcend mortality.

As the story unfolds, Poe becomes increasingly entangled in a web of mystery and horror, ultimately leading him to confront the killer in a thrilling showdown. Along the way, he must also navigate the complexities of his own psyche and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

The Raven features a blend of historical fact and fiction, drawing on Poe's life and works to create a unique and captivating narrative. The film's themes of love, loss, and the power of art are timeless and universal, making it a compelling watch for fans of horror and mystery alike.

Overall, The Raven is a gripping and atmospheric horror film that explores the darker corners of the human psyche, all while paying homage to one of literature's most iconic figures.

overview: Employees at a cosmetics firm grapple with their respective desires by arguing with themselves in the mirror, ahead of their company’s anniversary party.
title: Mirror, Mirror
plot:
Mirror, Mirror (Spanish: Espejo, espejo) is a 2022 Spanish satirical comedy written and directed by Marc Crehuet, his second feature after El rey tuerto (2016). Santi Millán, Malena Alterio, Natalia de Molina and Carlos Areces lead an ensemble that also includes Toni Acosta, Carlos Bardem, Loles León, Silvia Abascal, Antonio Resines and Verónica Forqué, who died in December 2021 and appears here in her final screen role.

The film is set on a single day at Medina Cosmetics, a beauty company preparing a lavish celebration of its fiftieth anniversary. Four employees in crisis are at its centre: Álvaro (Millán), Cristina (Alterio), Paula (de Molina) and Alberto (Areces). Each is pulled between conflicting desires, and the film gives that inner conflict a literal form. Whenever they stand before a mirror, their reflections come alive and talk back, acting as a kind of nagging conscience or hidden other self that contradicts the face they show the world, voicing what they should have done or dared not say. Arguing with their doubles, they wrestle with ambition, fear, love and betrayal as office rivalries, pettiness and backstabbing build towards the party.

Through these confrontations the comedy pokes at narcissism, beauty standards, self-esteem and the advertising business, along with social-media stigma, harassment and questions of gender identity and inclusion. One running thread follows a vain character who believes himself perfect while everyone laughs at him, and another the company's attempt to sell the idea of being perfectly imperfect, with the cynical reminder that the aim is to sell products rather than change the world. The tensions finally explode in a cathartic, chaotic climax.

Produced by Rodar y Rodar and Nos gusta el cine AIE with the participation of RTVE, TV3 and Netflix, the film was shot in Pamplona and Barcelona in August and September 2020. It opened the 6th BCN Film Fest on 21 April 2022 and was released in Spanish cinemas by Filmax on 20 May 2022. Critics were divided. Fotogramas praised its ingenious premise and superb comic ensemble, singling out Areces and a brief, fierce turn by Loles León, but felt it eventually retreated into safe, didactic political correctness. Cinemanía appreciated its grotesque humour and honesty, while El País called the execution atrocious and embarrassing despite a promising idea, and Contraste regretted that a talented cast was wasted on crude humour and preachy messaging.

overview: When Ester becomes King Xerxes’ queen, her Cousin Mordecai and that despicable Haman engage in a dangerous game of intrigue for control of the young Persian King Xerxes.
tagline: Who Is Your Hero?
title: The Book of Esther
plot:
The Book of Esther is a 2013 film that tells the story of Esther, a young Jewish woman who becomes queen of Persia and saves her people from persecution. At its core, the movie explores themes of faith, courage, and redemption.

One of the main themes of The Book of Esther is the power of prayer and trust in God's sovereignty. The film highlights Esther's journey as she navigates a treacherous court and confronts the evil plans of Haman, who seeks to destroy the Jewish people. Through her prayers and reliance on God, Esther finds the strength and wisdom to outsmart her enemies and ultimately save her people.

Another significant theme in The Book of Esther is the importance of identity and belonging. As a young woman from a humble background, Esther must navigate the complexities of royal life while remaining true to her faith and heritage. The film explores the tension between assimilation and cultural identity, as Esther struggles to balance her loyalty to her people with her new role in the palace.

The movie also touches on themes of redemption and forgiveness. Haman's backstory reveals a complex web of motivations and emotions that drive his actions, highlighting the need for understanding and compassion rather than simply condemning evil. Through Esther's character, the film shows how forgiveness can be a powerful tool for healing and restoration.

Finally, The Book of Esther celebrates the triumph of good over evil, as Esther's bravery and faith ultimately lead to the salvation of her people. The film's portrayal of Esther as a strong and courageous leader serves as a testament to the enduring power of God's love and redemption.

Overall, The Book of Esther is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores themes of faith, identity, redemption, and forgiveness in a way that is both entertaining and thought-provoking.

original_title: Garfield: A Tail of Two Kitties
overview: Jon and Garfield visit the United Kingdom, where a case of mistaken cat identity finds Garfield ruling over a castle. His reign is soon jeopardized by the nefarious Lord Dargis, who has designs on the estate.
tagline: The Ego has landed.
title: Garfield: A Tail of Two Kitties
plot:
Garfield: A Tail of Two Kitties is a 2006 American computer-animated comedy film produced by 20th Century Fox. The movie is the sequel to the 2004 film Garfield: The Movie and serves as a continuation of the original story.

The plot begins with Garfield (voiced by Bill Murray) and his owner Jon Arbuckle (voiced by Breckin Meyer) living in Muncie, Indiana. However, their peaceful life is disrupted when they receive an invitation to the royal wedding of Prince Lenny (voiced by Billy Connolly) and Princess Odie (voiced by Jennifer Love Hewitt). The couple's wedding is a grand affair, and Garfield sees it as an opportunity to indulge in the luxurious food and drink that comes with royalty.

Upon arrival at the palace, Garfield meets Prince Lenny's evil twin brother, Prince Nermal (voiced by Jason Alexander), who seeks revenge against his long-lost twin for being abandoned. The twins' rivalry leads to a series of hilarious misadventures as they compete for the affections of Princess Odie.

Meanwhile, Jon becomes infatuated with Princess Odie and tries to win her heart, but Garfield's attempts to sabotage their relationship only lead to more chaos. As the wedding day approaches, Prince Nermal's plan to steal the royal jewels comes to fruition, and Garfield must use his cunning and wit to stop him.

Throughout the movie, Garfield's sarcastic humor and witty one-liners provide plenty of comedic relief. The film also features a range of colorful characters, including Dr. Liz Wilson (voiced by Daryl Sabara), Jon's veterinarian girlfriend, who becomes entangled in the royal wedding shenanigans.

As the story unfolds, Garfield must confront his own insecurities and learn to put aside his rivalry with Prince Nermal. In the end, he helps save the day and wins over Princess Odie's heart. The movie concludes with a grand finale of laughter, excitement, and plenty of cat-titude.

Overall, Garfield: A Tail of Two Kitties is a lighthearted, entertaining film that delivers on its promise of humor and adventure. While it may not be as sophisticated as some other animated films, the movie's colorful characters, witty dialogue, and comedic antics make it a fun watch for both kids and adults.

Rating: 3.5/5 stars

overview: Timon the meerkat and Pumbaa the warthog are best pals and the unsung heroes of the African savanna. This prequel to the smash Disney animated adventure takes you back -- way back -- before Simba's adventure began. You'll find out all about Timon and Pumbaa and tag along as they search for the perfect home and attempt to raise a rambunctious lion cub.
tagline: You Don't Know The ½ Of It!
title: The Lion King 1½
plot:
The Lion King 1½, released internationally as The Lion King 3: Hakuna Matata, is a 2004 American animated direct-to-video musical comedy film directed by Bradley Raymond and produced by Disneytoon Studios. The third film in the Lion King series, it retells the events of the 1994 original from the point of view of the meerkat Timon and the warthog Pumbaa, voiced again by Nathan Lane and Ernie Sabella, with Julie Kavner as Timon's mother, Ma, Jerry Stiller as his Uncle Max, Matthew Broderick as Simba, Robert Guillaume as Rafiki and Moira Kelly as Nala. The structure was inspired by Tom Stoppard's Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead.

Watching the first film in a home theater, Timon and Pumbaa rewind it to tell how they met. Timon, a misfit in his meerkat colony at the edge of the Pride Lands, lets his daydreams distract him while on lookout duty, allowing the hyenas Shenzi, Banzai and Ed to attack, and he leaves home convinced he will never belong. Rafiki teaches him "Hakuna Matata" and tells him to "look beyond what you see", which Timon takes literally, heading for Pride Rock and meeting Pumbaa. Their arrival at Simba's presentation explains why the animals bow, since Pumbaa, who is claustrophobic, breaks wind in the crowd. In search of a perfect home, the pair stumble through key moments of the original story, including the stampede that kills Mufasa, before being swept down a river and over a waterfall. Realizing they are each other's only friends, they find a lush jungle. Meanwhile Ma and Uncle Max leave the colony to search for Timon. The friends rescue and raise Simba, but when the grown lion reunites with Nala, they try to sabotage the romance, fearing for their friendship. After Simba returns home to challenge Scar, Pumbaa follows him, while Timon, feeling betrayed, refuses, until loneliness and Rafiki's guidance show him that his true Hakuna Matata lies with those he loves. Back in the Pride Lands, Timon and Pumbaa distract the hyenas with a hula dance and meet Ma and Max, who dig tunnels beneath the hyenas; Timon breaks the last support, sweeping them away along with Scar. Timon invites the colony to live in the jungle, where they hail him as a hero.

Released on home video in February 2004, the film sold 1.5 million DVDs on its first day and six million DVD and VHS copies in North America by March. Critics were broadly positive, with Frank Lovece of TV Guide calling it one of Disney's rare direct-to-video sequels worthy of the original.

overview: Inspired by one of the longest and bloodiest real-life events in police history, Officer Mike Chandler and a young civilian passenger find themselves under-prepared and outgunned when fate puts them squarely in the crosshairs of a daring bank heist in progress by a fearless team of highly-trained and heavily-armed men.
tagline: Your life can change in an instant.
plot:
211 is a 2018 American crime action film directed by York Shackleton and written by John Rebus from a screenplay by Shackleton. Nicolas Cage leads a cast that includes Dwayne Cameron, Alexandra Dinu, Michael Rainey Jr., Sophie Skelton and Ori Pfeffer. Very loosely inspired by the 1997 North Hollywood shootout, it follows a police officer and a teenager caught in a gun battle with heavily armed bank robbers.

In Afghanistan, the ruthless mercenaries Tre, Rob, Luke and Hyde torture a war profiteer who owes them money, learning before they kill him that it was wired to a bank in Chesterford, Massachusetts, while Interpol agent Rossi is reassigned to pursue them. In Chesterford, quiet student Kenny Ralston is suspended for fighting off a bully, and his mother, the emergency nurse Shawnee, is told he must go on a police ride-along or be expelled. He is paired with Officer Mike Chandler, a widower estranged from his daughter, Lisa, and Mike's son-in-law, Officer Steve MacAvoy, who reveals that Lisa is pregnant. Kenny clashes with the officers, irritating Mike by filming them.

The mercenaries plant a bomb in a diner as a diversion and storm the bank to seize the $1.3 million, taking hostages. Mike, who has noticed an illegally parked SUV outside, stays on his beat with Kenny when other units rush to the explosion. Hyde opens fire on their cruiser, wrecking it, and the officers kill him while Kenny tries to record the shootout. Steve is wounded, and as backup arrives the robbers gun down hostages, bystanders and officers. Fearing death, Steve has Kenny record a farewell to Lisa before he is evacuated, and Kenny becomes separated from Mike. As state police, SWAT and Rossi surround the bank, Tre frees the hostages, but one carries a bomb, and Captain Horst dies shielding others from the blast. Rob and Luke are killed charging the police, and Tre escapes to the parking lot, killing Officer Hanson and wounding Mike, until Kenny and Rossi shoot him dead. A year later, Mike celebrates his birthday with Steve, Lisa, Kenny and his new granddaughter, and asks Kenny to take pictures.

Cage joined the project in January 2017, and the film was shot at Nu Boyana Film Studios in Sofia, Bulgaria. Momentum Pictures released it on June 8, 2018, and it earned $1.1 million. Critics were overwhelmingly negative, giving it 4% on Rotten Tomatoes, and 21 on Metacritic; Richard Roeper called it a muddled, cliché-ridden heist movie, though Forbes's reviewer was kinder.

overview: In a small town in Massachusetts, four high school girls perform a ritual in an attempt to debunk the lore of Slender Man. When one of the girls goes mysteriously missing, they begin to suspect that she is, in fact, his latest victim.
tagline: Can you see him?
title: Slender Man
plot:
Slender Man is a 2018 American supernatural horror film directed by Sylvain White and written by David Birke, based on the internet creepypasta character created in 2009. Joey King, Julia Goldani Telles, Jaz Sinclair, Annalise Basso, Taylor Richardson and Alex Fitzalan star, with Javier Botet as the title figure.

In the small town of Winsford, Massachusetts, Katie, Hallie, Chloe and Wren hold a sleepover at Katie's house and, curious about Slender Man, an internet legend who lures and abducts children, watch an unsettling video showing how to reach him. A week later, during a class field trip, Katie senses a presence among the trees and soon vanishes without a trace. Going through her laptop, her friends discover that Katie, unhappy at home with her alcoholic father, had grown obsessed with Slender Man and had contacted someone named Allison Riley about reaching him, hoping he would offer her an escape. Allison tells them that Slender Man infects people's minds, driving them mad or taking them, and that to recover Katie they must perform a ritual in which each surrenders a cherished object.

Wren warns the others to wear blindfolds and never look at his face, but during the ritual Chloe panics, flees and sees him up close; he later enters her home and drives her insane. Wren is attacked while researching in the library. When Hallie's sister, Lizzie, is hospitalized after a severe panic attack, Hallie finds that Lizzie and Wren had tried to contact Slender Man. At Wren's house she discovers research on his victims, among them Allison, and talks Wren out of suicide. Wren confesses that she took Lizzie into the woods, where Lizzie offered her teddy bear, and that their offerings were not enough, since Slender Man will rest only once he has physically claimed them all. He then smashes through the window and drags Wren away. Hallie goes into the woods and offers herself in her sister's place, and he takes her, the two merging into a tree. Lizzie recovers and reflects on the four friends' fate.

Sony's Screen Gems developed the film from 2016, and it was shot in Massachusetts in mid-2017.
