Shadowed by the 2014 Slender Man stabbing in Wisconsin, the studio required a PG-13 rating and cuts that left continuity errors. Released by Sony Pictures Releasing on August 10, 2018, it grossed $51.7 million on a $10 million budget, but reviews were poor, with 8% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Sinclair received a Golden Raspberry nomination for Worst Supporting Actress.

overview: Syd March is an employee at a clinic that sells injections of live viruses harvested from sick celebrities to obsessed fans. When he becomes infected with the disease that kills super sensation Hannah Geist, Syd becomes a target for collectors and rabid fans. He must unravel the mystery surrounding her death before he suffers the same fate.
tagline: What If You Could Feel Like They Do... We Can Help.
title: Antiviral
plot:
Antiviral is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and our obsession with celebrity culture. The movie takes place in a world where fans can pay to have their bodies infected with a virus that contains a piece of a famous person's DNA, allowing them to experience a brief moment of connection with their idol.

The main theme of Antiviral is the commodification of intimacy and the exploitation of human desire for validation. The film critiques our society's tendency to reduce complex emotions and relationships to consumerist transactions, where people are willing to sacrifice their own well-being for a fleeting sense of connection with someone they admire.

Through the character of Justin, a struggling musician who becomes obsessed with the virus, the movie explores the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. As Justin's obsession grows, he begins to lose touch with his own identity and relationships, highlighting the dangers of allowing celebrity culture to define our sense of self-worth.

The film also touches on themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for meaning in a hyper-consumerist world. The virus itself becomes a metaphor for the ways in which technology can both connect and isolate us, leaving us feeling empty and unfulfilled despite our attempts to fill the void with material possessions and superficial relationships.

Overall, Antiviral is a thought-provoking commentary on the darker aspects of human nature and our society's obsession with celebrity culture.

overview: Three years after Mike bowed out of the stripper life at the top of his game, he and the remaining Kings of Tampa hit the road to Myrtle Beach to put on one last blow-out performance.
tagline: Back to the grind.
title: Magic Mike XXL
plot:
Magic Mike XXL is a 2015 American comedy-drama film directed by Gregory Jacobs and written by Reid Carolin, Justin Zackham, and Fred Gwynne. The movie stars Channing Tatum, Matt Bomer, Joe Manganiello, Kevin Nash, Adam Rodriguez, and Elizabeth Banks.

The story begins with Mike (Channing Tatum), a former male stripper who has retired from the business to start a family with his girlfriend, Katie (Elizabeth Banks). However, when Katie leaves him for another man, Mike is forced back into his old life. He reunites with his friends, including Ken (Matt Bomer), Tug (Joe Manganiello), and Zeke (Adam Rodriguez), who are also struggling to find their place in the world.

The group decides to embark on a road trip from Miami to New Orleans for the annual stripper convention, where they hope to relive their glory days and make some money. Along the way, they pick up a new recruit, Winston (Matt McConaughey), who joins them as a stripper. As they travel through the American South, they encounter various challenges, including run-ins with the law, romantic entanglements, and personal struggles.

As the group navigates their journey, Mike begins to confront his past and the reasons why he retired from stripping. He also starts to develop feelings for Winston, who becomes a key figure in his life. Meanwhile, Ken and Tug struggle with their own identities and sense of purpose, leading to some comedic moments and heartfelt revelations.

The movie's climax takes place at the stripper convention, where Mike and his friends face off against a rival stripper, played by Matt McConaughey, who is determined to take down Mike as the top stripper. In the end, Mike emerges victorious, but not without some emotional scars and a newfound appreciation for his life.

Throughout the movie, there are also several subplots that explore themes of masculinity, friendship, and identity. The film features a mix of humor, drama, and music, with a soundtrack that includes hits from various artists.

Overall, Magic Mike XXL is a fun and entertaining movie that explores the complexities of male relationships and the struggles of finding one's place in the world. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and engaging storyline, it's no wonder why this film became a box office hit.

overview: When 4 year old Amanda McCready disappears from her home and the police make little headway in solving the case, the girl's aunt, Beatrice McCready hires two private detectives, Patrick Kenzie and Angie Gennaro. The detectives freely admit that they have little experience with this type of case, but the family wants them for two reasons—they're not cops and they know the tough neighborhood in which they all live.
tagline: Everyone wants the truth... until they find it.
title: Gone Baby Gone
plot:
Gone Baby Gone is a 2007 crime drama film directed by Ben Affleck, based on the novel of the same name by Dennis Lehane.

The main themes of Gone Baby Gone revolve around:

1. **Child Abduction and the Search for Truth**: The story revolves around the disappearance of a young girl, Amanda McCann, and the subsequent investigation by two detectives, Patrick Kenzie (Leonardo DiCaprio) and Angela Gennaro (Minnie Driver). As they delve deeper into the case, they uncover a complex web of secrets and lies that challenge their perceptions of truth.

2. **Corruption and Institutional Failure**: The film critiques the flaws in the Boston child protective services system, highlighting how corruption and bureaucratic inefficiency can lead to the failure to protect vulnerable children. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Detective Gennaro, who struggles with her own demons and institutional constraints.

3. **Family Dynamics and Trauma**: The story explores the complex relationships within the McCann family, particularly between the parents, Terry (Casey Affleck) and Kelly (Michelle Monaghan), and their daughter Amanda. As the investigation unfolds, it becomes clear that the family's dynamics are marked by trauma, secrets, and unresolved conflicts.

4. **Social Class and Inequality**: The film touches on issues of social class and inequality in Boston, highlighting the disparities between the affluent and working-class communities. This theme is subtly woven throughout the narrative, particularly in the character of Terry McCann, who struggles to provide for his family amidst economic hardship.

5. **Morality and Gray Areas**: Gone Baby Gone presents a nuanced exploration of morality, encouraging viewers to question their assumptions about right and wrong. The characters are multidimensional, with no clear-cut heroes or villains, making it difficult for the audience to categorize them as simply good or evil.

Overall, Gone Baby Gone is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and moral ambiguities, leaving audiences to ponder the consequences of human actions and the importance of seeking truth.

overview: Toto and his friends must rescue his egg children after they're taken away for a gourmet food event in Africa.
title: An Egg Rescue
plot:
Little Eggs: An African Rescue, released in Mexico, Latin America and the United States as Un rescate de huevitos, is a 2021 Mexican computer-animated adventure comedy produced by Huevocartoon Producciones and directed by brothers Gabriel and Rodolfo Riva Palacio Alatriste. The fourth film in the Huevos franchise and a sequel to Un gallo con muchos huevos (2015), it brings back the Spanish voice cast alongside newcomers including Jesús Ochoa and the comedy duo Freddy and Germán Ortega. Rodolfo drew the story of an overprotective father from raising his daughter, Dione, who voices one of the chicks, and the plot from articles about rare eggs and endangered animals sold as luxury food. About 350 people worked on it, many remotely during the COVID-19 pandemic. Delayed from 2019 and 2020, it opened in Mexico on 12 August 2021, with a limited US release through Pantelion Films on 27 August.

At the Granjas el Pollón farm, the rooster Toto and his wife, Di, welcome two golden eggs, the twins Max and Uly. Their unusual color wins a ranch contest and attracts La Duquesa, a Russian egg collector, whose offer to buy them is refused. Toto, newly anxious and overprotective, tears up the twins' prize ribbons in a fit of worry and frightens them. That night Duquesa's henchmen, Panzovich and Gordimitri, send moles in mind-control helmets to steal the twins. Toto's friends Bibi and Willy free one mole, Toporocho, who helps the group board the cargo plane bound for Congo, but Toto and Di are thrown off mid-flight and saved by parachute.

The twins are taken to the African mansion of Barón Roncovich, where a Master Chef orders the captured eggs, from a peacock, an eagle, a parrot and other rare species, chilled for a gourmet auction. Max and Uly lead the others in a breakout, while Toto and Di, caught up in an animal talent show run by the lion king Leonidas I, find the courage to stand up to him and recruit an army of animals. They storm the dinner, rescue the eggs and escape a fire, and Toto apologizes to his children. When Duquesa ambushes them on the flight home, Toto trusts the twins to fight back, and a newly hatched eagle sends her out of the plane.

Bruno Bichir voices Toto and Maite Perroni voices Di. Reviews were mixed to favorable; Common Sense Media called it well made, while The Guardian gave it one star. It earned about MX$50 million in Mexico, making Huevos the country's most-watched domestic film franchise.

overview: High school loner Bird Fitcher has no idea what dark secrets are tied to the mysterious Polaroid vintage camera she stumbles upon, but it doesn't take long to discover that those who have their picture taken meet a tragic end. Bird and her friends must survive one more night as they race to solve the mystery of the haunted Polaroid before it kills them all.
tagline: Beware This Camera...Once You Take It, It Takes You.
title: Polaroid
plot:
Polaroid is a psychological thriller film that revolves around a young woman named Mia, who discovers a mysterious Polaroid camera that allows her to capture and relive memories from different timelines. As she delves deeper into the camera's secrets, Mia becomes entangled in a complex web of time travel and alternate realities.

The main theme of Polaroid is the exploration of the consequences of playing with time and the fragility of human relationships. The film raises questions about the nature of memory, identity, and the impact of our choices on those around us. Through Mia's journey, the movie delves into the idea that every decision we make has a ripple effect, affecting not only ourselves but also those closest to us.

The film also touches upon the theme of isolation and loneliness, as Mia struggles to form connections with others in her life. The camera becomes a tool for her to escape her emotional pain, but ultimately, it also serves as a reminder of her disconnection from the world around her.

Furthermore, Polaroid explores the concept of nostalgia and the allure of revisiting past experiences. The film's use of time travel and alternate realities creates a sense of disorientation, mirroring Mia's own feelings of disconnection and confusion. As she navigates different timelines, Mia is forced to confront the choices she has made and the consequences that have unfolded.

Overall, Polaroid is a thought-provoking thriller that explores the complexities of human relationships, time, and memory, leaving the audience questioning the nature of reality and the consequences of our actions.

overview: A college class project on creation and destruction of modern myth, turns terrifying when a trio of young people come to realize the urban legends surrounding the famed Buckout Road may, in fact, be REAL.
title: The Curse of Buckout Road
plot:
The Curse of Buckout Road is a 2017 American supernatural horror film directed by David Guy Levy. The movie follows a group of friends who embark on a road trip to a remote location, only to find themselves facing a series of terrifying and supernatural events.

At its core, the main theme of The Curse of Buckout Road revolves around the idea of isolation and how it can bring out the darkest aspects of human nature. As the characters venture deeper into the wilderness, they are forced to confront their own personal demons and the true meaning of friendship and loyalty.

The film also explores the concept of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. The main character's backstory is slowly revealed throughout the movie, showcasing how past experiences can shape one's perception of reality and lead to a downward spiral of madness.

Furthermore, The Curse of Buckout Road touches upon the theme of the supernatural as a metaphor for the unknown terrors that lurk within ourselves. The film's use of eerie atmosphere and jump scares serves to heighten the sense of unease and uncertainty, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is just a product of the characters' fragile mental states.

Overall, The Curse of Buckout Road is a tense and unsettling horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human psychology, exploring themes of isolation, trauma, and the supernatural.

overview: Super-assassin John Wick returns with a $14 million price tag on his head and an army of bounty-hunting killers on his trail. After killing a member of the shadowy international assassin’s guild, the High Table, John Wick is excommunicado, but the world’s most ruthless hit men and women await his every turn.
tagline: Every action has consequences.
title: John Wick: Chapter 3 - Parabellum
plot:
John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum is a 2019 action-thriller film directed by Chad Stahelski and written by Derek Kolstad. The movie takes place immediately after the events of John Wick: Chapter 2.

The story begins with John Wick (Keanu Reeves) on the run from the High Table, a council of powerful crime lords who have declared him "excommunicado" due to his killing of a member of the Adjudicator's guard. With a $14 million bounty on his head, John Wick must navigate a treacherous landscape of assassins and hitmen to survive.

As he tries to stay one step ahead of his pursuers, John Wick is aided by Sofia (Halle Berry), an old acquaintance who helps him evade capture. However, their partnership is short-lived, as they soon find themselves facing off against the Adjudicator's guard, led by The Bowery King (Asia Kate Dillon).

Meanwhile, a new player enters the scene: Zero (Mark Dacascos), a legendary assassin with ties to John Wick's past. As the body count rises and the stakes grow higher, John Wick must confront his own demons and face off against some of the deadliest assassins in the world.

Throughout the film, Stahelski employs innovative action sequences that showcase Reeves' impressive physicality and stunt work. The movie's climax features an epic showdown between John Wick and Zero, with the fate of the High Table hanging in the balance.

One of the standout aspects of John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum is its exploration of the world-building and mythology that underpins the franchise. The film delves deeper into the rules and hierarchies of the High Table, revealing a complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various crime lords.

Ultimately, John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum is a non-stop thrill ride that delivers on its promise of high-octane action and stylish visuals. With its breakneck pacing and intricate plot twists, it's a must-see for fans of the franchise and action enthusiasts alike.

overview: Two South Africans set out to discover what happened to their unlikely musical hero, the mysterious 1970s rock 'n' roller, Rodriguez. The film won Best Documentary at the 85th Academy Awards.
tagline: Great Art Always Survives
title: Searching for Sugar Man
plot:
Searching for Sugar Man is a 2012 documentary film that delves into the life of American singer-songwriter Rodriguez, whose music was discovered years after its initial release in South Africa. The film's narrative weaves together the story of Rodriguez's rise to fame in South Africa, his subsequent disappearance from the music scene, and the efforts of two journalists, Stephen Segerman and Craig Bartholomew-Stryzinski, to uncover the truth about his life and music.

At its core, Searching for Sugar Man is a film about identity, cultural exchange, and the power of music to transcend borders and time. The documentary explores how Rodriguez's music became an anthem for the anti-apartheid movement in South Africa, yet he himself remained largely unknown outside of his adopted homeland. This paradox raises questions about the nature of fame, artistic ownership, and the complexities of cultural appropriation.

Through its narrative, Searching for Sugar Man also touches on themes of perseverance, redemption, and the human desire to be understood. Rodriguez's story is one of a man who, despite facing numerous setbacks and rejections, continued to create music that spoke to people from all walks of life. The film ultimately reveals a complex and multifaceted individual, whose legacy extends far beyond his own experiences.

The documentary also delves into the complexities of cultural exchange and the ways in which art can be both a unifying force and a source of tension. Rodriguez's music, with its blend of American folk and South African rhythms, became an unlikely hit in a country struggling to come to terms with its troubled past. The film raises important questions about the role of art in shaping our understanding of ourselves and others.

Overall, Searching for Sugar Man is a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that celebrates the transformative power of music and the enduring legacy of artistic expression.

overview: Liberty, a socially awkward 16-year-old, returns from two months at camp to a blindsided introduction of her mother’s fiancé, John Smith, whose charm, intelligence, and beauty paint the picture of a man too perfect to be human.
tagline: Fear comes to the surface.
title: What Lies Below
plot:
What Lies Below is a 2020 American horror film written and directed by Braden R. Duemmler. Ema Horvath stars as Liberty "Libby" Wells, with Mena Suvari as her mother, Michelle, Trey Tucker as Michelle's boyfriend, John Smith, and Haskiri Velazquez as Libby's friend Marley.

Sixteen-year-old Libby returns from summer camp to her family's lake house, where her mother, a romance novelist, introduces her to her new boyfriend, John, an aquatic geneticist who says his work helps creatures adapt to changing environments. He gives Libby a bracelet bearing symbols of a fertility goddess. That night Libby overhears loud lovemaking, then pretends to sleep as John stands watching in her doorway. Michelle falls ill and announces that she has accepted John's marriage proposal, while Libby learns that John studies parasites. John's behavior toward her grows increasingly invasive: he touches her while cleaning up her menstrual blood and sneaks into the bathroom while she showers. Removing the bracelet, Libby finds a red mark on her wrist, and she invites Marley to stay.

That night Libby sees John wade into the lake, which glows red, yet soon appears dry, claiming to sleepwalk. Michelle begins vomiting and sends Libby to town for medicine and a pregnancy test. When Libby tells Marley that John groped her and Michelle announces she is pregnant, Michelle accuses her daughter of lying. Noticing that John has a nictitating membrane, Libby tries to pull her mother away, and Michelle slaps her. In the basement, Libby finds symbols on her own wrist matching those on the walls and discovers Michelle in a water tank hooked to an IV, then watches from hiding as her mother gives birth to a dying creature. After calling the police, she finds Marley's body being devoured by parasites in another tank. John overpowers Libby as she tries to flee with Michelle, and she wakes bound as several identical copies of John peel back the walls to reveal many unconscious women in tanks. John forces her to swallow a glowing substance he regurgitates, and Libby awakens in a tank among women seemingly in pupal states; as water fills it, she panics, then smiles, able to breathe underwater.

Cath Clarke of The Guardian gave the film one star out of five, writing that its baffling erotic plot was less damaging than its wooden acting and poor judgment. Screen Rant's Jack Wilhelmi rated it three out of five, praising Horvath and Suvari while finding the rest of the film derivative.

overview: When Max, who is recovering from a traumatic accident, takes a job as a nighttime security guard, he begins to see visions of a young mysterious woman in the store's mirror.
tagline: Behind the world you know is a darkness you never imagined.
title: Mirrors 2
plot:
Mirrors 2 is an American supernatural horror film of 2010 directed by Víctor García and written by Matt Venne, a standalone sequel to Mirrors (2008) with none of the original's cast or crew. Released direct to video by 20th Century Fox, it stars Nick Stahl as Max Matheson, with Emmanuelle Vaugier as Elizabeth Reigns, William Katt as Max's father Jack, Christy Carlson Romano as Jenna McCarty and Lawrence Turner as Keller Landreaux.

Max briefly died in a car crash that killed his fiancée, Kayla. Revived, he remains consumed by guilt, though a drunk driver was to blame. His father Jack is reopening the Mayflower department store in New Orleans and hires Max as a security guard. Max meets the manager Keller, the buyer Jenna and the executive Ryan Parker. Before his first shift he sees a dead woman in a mirror, then Jenna's reflection tearing off its head. That night Jenna, frightened by her reflection, crashes through her glass shower door and is decapitated by a shard. Max realizes that mirrors are showing him deaths before they happen; he tries to warn Ryan after seeing his reflection disemboweled, but Ryan dies the same way. When Max sees his father's face covered in cuts, he races over and saves Jack from his own reflection, then agrees to stay at the store, telling whatever controls the mirrors that he will do as it wishes if it spares his father.

Max returns to the store's main mirror, where his reflection guides him to the ID of Eleanor Reigns, a new employee who vanished two months earlier. He contacts her sister Elizabeth, and they find that the security footage from the night of Eleanor's disappearance was deleted. The former guard, Henry, whose mouth was scarred after his reflection made him eat broken glass, tells them the truth: at the store's groundbreaking party, Jenna drugged Eleanor's drink while Ryan distracted her, and Keller raped her and killed her when she tried to flee, then forced Henry, who saw him bury her in the basement, to erase the footage. Eleanor's spirit, trapped in the mirror world, has been taking revenge and used Max, whose near-death experience let him see her, to reach her sister. In the basement, Keller attacks and nearly strangles Elizabeth, but Max saves her and pushes Keller into the main mirror, where Eleanor drags him in and kills him. Henry confesses to police, but Eleanor finds him in the interrogation room's mirror.

Filmed mainly in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, in late 2009, it earned $4.5 million on home video.

overview: Great Dane Marmaduke epitomizes the overgrown lapdog, with an irascible streak and a penchant for mischief that is tempered with a deep sense of love and responsibility for his human family, the Winslows. The new animation is set in the world of elite dog shows, rife divas, rivalries and slapstick comedy.
tagline: Man's biggest friend.
title: Marmaduke
plot:
Marmaduke is a 2022 animated comedy directed by Mark Dippé, with Phil Nibbelink, Youngki Lee and Matt Whelan as co-directors, based on Paul and Brad Anderson's comic strip. Pete Davidson voices the title Great Dane, with J.K. Simmons as his rival, the Afghan Hound Zeus, David Koechner as Phil Winslow, Brian Hull as dog trainer Guy Hilton and Julie Nathanson as Dottie Winslow.

Phil and Dottie live in Maryland with their children, Barbara and Billy, and their clumsy but good-natured Great Dane, Marmaduke. At Billy's birthday party, Marmaduke cannonballs from the second floor into the pool, unleashing a tidal wave, and Barbara's video of the stunt goes viral. It catches the eye of the celebrated trainer Guy, who offers to turn Marmaduke into a champion show dog, and the hesitant family agrees once Phil learns of a $1 million top prize. After early resistance, Marmaduke starts to improve, and Guy enters him in a local show as a test. There Zeus tempts him into eating before the event, and the bloated Marmaduke fills the arena with noxious gas before relieving himself in the winner's trophy. Humiliated, Guy quits, and Marmaduke runs away.

On the street, Marmaduke rescues the family cat, Carlos, from an intersection, and with Carlos's encouragement he travels around the world performing heroic feats, which persuades Guy to take him back for the World Dog Championship. There he meets Zeus again along with rivals including the corgi Juan Pedro, the pink poodle Shantrelle and the Staffordshire Bull Terrier Vinnie. After the second of three challenges, Marmaduke lands on Guy, sending him to the hospital, so the family steps in as trainers, and for the final round Marmaduke and Billy perform a crowd-pleasing cowboy act with Carlos. Zeus is declared the winner, but Marmaduke exposes the rigged scores, and Zeus is disqualified. When Zeus tries to seize the trophy, he topples a camera platform, and Marmaduke is struck while saving his family and the cameraman. Feared dead, he survives, and the family lives happily.

Announced in 2017, with Davidson, Simmons and Koechner cast in 2018, the film was animated by Dippé's WonderWorld Studios. Planned for 2019 and then 2020 before COVID-19 delays, it was acquired by Netflix, which released it in the United States on May 6, 2022, while SC Films handled other territories. Critics panned it, with 0% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Davidson received a Golden Raspberry nomination for Worst Actor.

overview: Placed in a foster home that doesn't allow pets, 16-year-old Andi and her younger brother, Bruce, turn an abandoned hotel into a home for their dog. Soon other strays arrive, and the hotel becomes a haven for every orphaned canine in town. But the kids have to do some quick thinking to keep the cops off their tails.
tagline: No stray gets turned away.
title: Hotel for Dogs
plot:
Hotel for Dogs is an American family comedy of 2009 directed by Thor Freudenthal and written by Jeff Lowell, Bob Schooley and Mark McCorkle, based on Lois Duncan's 1971 novel. Emma Roberts and Jake T. Austin star as Andi and Bruce, orphaned siblings in foster care who secretly shelter stray dogs in an abandoned hotel, with Johnny Simmons and Kyla Pratt as the pet store workers Dave and Heather, Troy Gentile as their neighbor Mark, Lisa Kudrow and Kevin Dillon as the uncaring foster parents Lois and Carl Scudder, and Don Cheadle as the social worker Bernie Wilkins.

Andi and Bruce con a pawnbroker to buy food for their dog Friday and end up at the police station, from which Bernie collects them and returns them to the Scudders, who care little for the children or the dog. When Friday is caught by animal control, the siblings learn from Dave and Heather to check the pound, where they cannot claim him without a parent, so they bribe a guard to get him back. On the way home they find Friday sheltering in a derelict hotel along with two strays, a tiny Boston Terrier and an English Mastiff, whom they name Georgia and Lenny. When Andi tells Dave that her parents often rescue dogs, he asks her to take three more that no one wants.

With Mark's help, the friends fix up the hotel to meet the dogs' needs and rescue more strays to fill it. Dave invites Andi to a party, but it is ruined when an old acquaintance reveals that she and Bruce are orphans, while Bruce, caught stealing a hairdryer, is questioned by the Scudders. Escaping, he finds the hotel in chaos, and the Scudders follow him there. The dogs are sent to the pound to be put down, the children are taken by the police, and when the Scudders refuse to take them back, Bernie must place them in separate foster homes. Friday escapes and leads Dave, Heather and Mark to the siblings, while Bernie, exploring the hotel, finds a remaining dog and understands what the children have built. Andi and Bruce break into the pound and free the dogs, who head back to the hotel, followed by crowds, reporters and police. Bernie wins everyone over by describing the family of dogs and their stories, the children are allowed to keep them, and Bernie and his wife adopt Andi and Bruce. With the city's support, the hotel reopens as a place to adopt or board dogs.

Shot in Los Angeles and Universal City, California, from November 2007, the film was released on 16 January 2009 and grossed about $117 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed.

overview: Emma Corrigan, a girl with a few secrets on a turbulent plane ride, thinks she’s about to die, Emma spills them all to the handsome stranger sitting next to her. At least, she thought he was a stranger. But then, her company’s young and elusive CEO, arrives at the office. It’s him. And he knows every single humiliating detail about Emma.
title: Can You Keep a Secret?
plot:
Can You Keep a Secret? is a 2019 romantic comedy film directed by Elissa Down and starring Alexandra Daddario, Zac Efron, and Piper Perabo. The movie follows the story of Emily Nelson (Alexandra Daddario), a young woman who witnesses her boyfriend's infidelity on their first date.

The main themes of Can You Keep a Secret? include:

1. **Trust and Betrayal**: The film explores the consequences of trust being broken, particularly in relationships. Emily's experience serves as a catalyst for her to re-evaluate her own life and relationships.
2. **Self-Discovery**: As Emily navigates her new reality, she begins to discover aspects of herself that she had previously overlooked or suppressed. This journey of self-discovery is a central theme of the film.
3. **Love and Vulnerability**: The movie highlights the importance of vulnerability in relationships. Emily's experiences teach her that true love requires openness and honesty, rather than secrecy and deception.
4. **Friendship and Support**: The film showcases the value of strong friendships and support systems. Emily finds solace and guidance from her friends, particularly her best friend, Olivia (Piper Perabo).
5. **Personal Growth**: Throughout the story, Emily undergoes significant personal growth, learning to let go of past hurts and embracing new experiences.

Overall, Can You Keep a Secret? is a heartwarming and engaging film that explores themes of love, trust, self-discovery, and personal growth.

overview: The story of Henry, a stand-up comedian with a fierce sense of humour and Ann, a singer of international renown. In the spotlight, they are the perfect couple, healthy, happy, and glamourous. The birth of their first child, Annette, a mysterious girl with an exceptional destiny, will change their lives.
tagline: As dangerous, as intense, as love.
title: Annette
plot:
Annette (2021) is a musical drama film directed by Leos Carax, starring Adam Driver and Marion Cotillard. The movie revolves around the story of Henry McHenry (Adam Driver), a young musician who marries Annette (Marion Cotillard), a mysterious and powerful singer with supernatural abilities.

The main themes of Annette include:

1. **Love and Sacrifice**: The film explores the complexities of love, sacrifice, and devotion. Henry's all-consuming passion for Annette drives him to make impossible choices, ultimately leading to his downfall.
2. **Identity and Performance**: Annette's character is a masterclass in performance art, blurring the lines between reality and fiction. Her ability to manipulate her appearance and voice raises questions about identity, authenticity, and the power of performance.
3. **Motherhood and Maternity**: The film delves into the themes of motherhood, maternity, and the complexities of female relationships. Annette's character is both a mother figure and a symbol of femininity, challenging traditional notions of motherhood and womanhood.
4. **Guilt and Redemption**: Henry's guilt over his past mistakes and Annette's supernatural abilities create a sense of tension and foreboding. The film ultimately explores the possibility of redemption and forgiveness, albeit in a bittersweet and unconventional manner.

Throughout the movie, Carax employs a non-linear narrative structure, blending music, dance, and visual effects to create a dreamlike atmosphere. The result is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that challenges audiences to confront the complexities of human relationships and the nature of reality itself.

overview: Gwendolyn Shepherd is a normal 16-year-old, but her family holds a secret: A time-travel gene is expressed in the clan inherited, but not every member of the family is blessed with. Everyone is certain that Gwen's cousin Charlotte has the gene.  However, someday Gwendolyn suddenly finds herself in London at the end of the 19th century and realizes that it is her, who was born a time traveler. While she is not very enthusiastic about it, she will do everything possible to solve the ancient mysteries of the red ruby.
title: Ruby Red
plot:
Ruby Red is a 2013 German fantasy romance film that tells the story of a young girl named Greta who discovers she has the ability to time travel. The movie explores the complexities of Greta's relationships with her family, particularly her grandmother, Helene, and her struggles to cope with the consequences of her newfound power.

At its core, Ruby Red is a poignant exploration of the human experience, delving into themes of love, loss, and the bittersweet nature of time. The film grapples with the idea that our lives are shaped by the choices we make and the relationships we form, and that even the smallest actions can have far-reaching consequences.

Through Greta's journey, the movie also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery, as she navigates her own desires and aspirations amidst the pressures of family expectations. The film's portrayal of Helene, a strong-willed and independent woman, serves as a powerful counterpoint to Greta's more vulnerable nature, highlighting the complexities of female relationships and the ways in which women can both support and complicate each other.

Ultimately, Ruby Red is a movie about the fragility and beauty of human connection, and the ways in which our experiences shape us into who we are meant to be.

original_title: Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One
overview: The seventh instalment of the Mission: Impossible franchise.
tagline: We all share the same fate.
title: Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning Part One
plot:
Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning Part One is a 2023 American action spy film directed by Christopher McQuarrie, who wrote it with Erik Jendresen, and the seventh film in the series, following Fallout (2018). Shooting began in Italy in February 2020, was halted by the COVID-19 pandemic and wrapped in September 2021, with locations including Norway, Britain and the UAE. With a gross budget estimated at $291 million, it is among the most expensive films ever made. After several delays, it premiered in Rome on June 19, 2023, and Paramount Pictures released it in the United States on July 12.

On its first mission, the Russian stealth submarine Sevastopol activates an experimental artificial intelligence through a two-part cruciform key. The AI, which comes to call itself the Entity, tricks the crew into torpedoing themselves and vanishes into cyberspace, and world powers race to obtain the key and control it. IMF agent Ethan Hunt recovers one half from former MI6 agent Ilsa Faust, faking her death to protect her from a bounty, then confronts CIA director Eugene Kittridge and vows to destroy the Entity. With teammates Benji Dunn and Luther Stickell he tries to intercept the second half at Abu Dhabi airport, but a thief named Grace steals his piece, and Ethan recognizes Gabriel, a figure from his past who now serves the Entity. After a chase through Rome with Grace, Ethan and Ilsa follow her to a party in Venice thrown by arms dealer Alanna Mitsopolis, who holds the other half and plans to sell the complete key aboard the Orient Express. Gabriel, aided by the assassin Paris, kills Ilsa.

On the train, Gabriel murders Denlinger, the director of national intelligence, who alone knew that the key opens a chamber on the sunken Sevastopol holding the Entity's source code. Grace, disguised as Alanna, pickpockets the key back from Kittridge, the buyer. Gabriel takes it after a fight atop the train and blows up a bridge, and Ethan and Grace escape the runaway carriages, helped by Paris, whom Gabriel has turned on. Grace asks to join the IMF while Ethan, having lifted the key from Gabriel, flies off to continue the mission.

Cruise stars with Hayley Atwell as Grace, Ving Rhames, Simon Pegg, Rebecca Ferguson, Vanessa Kirby and Esai Morales as Gabriel. It won near-universal acclaim, with 96% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and Oscar nominations for sound and visual effects, the series' first, yet its $571.1 million gross was seen as a disappointment.

overview: During the Iraq War, a Sergeant recently assigned to an army bomb squad is put at odds with his squad mates due to his maverick way of handling his work.
tagline: You'll know when you're in it.
title: The Hurt Locker
plot:
The Hurt Locker is a 2008 American war film directed by Kathryn Bigelow and written by Mark Boal, who drew on his time as a journalist embedded with a U.S. Army bomb squad in Iraq in 2004. Jeremy Renner stars as Sergeant First Class William James, with Anthony Mackie as Sergeant J. T. Sanborn, Brian Geraghty as Specialist Owen Eldridge, Guy Pearce as Staff Sergeant Matthew Thompson, Ralph Fiennes as the leader of a private military unit and Evangeline Lilly as James's former wife, Connie.

In the second year of the Iraq War, a U.S. Army explosive ordnance disposal team from Bravo Company is trying to destroy a roadside bomb when its robot fails, and team leader Thompson is killed when an insurgent detonates the device with a mobile phone as he places a charge by hand. Eldridge blames himself for not shooting the man in time. Thompson's replacement, James, clashes with Sanborn by defusing bombs by hand and keeping his plans to himself. He disarms one device moments before an insurgent can set it off, and later insists on dismantling a complex car bomb despite Sanborn's protests, pulling off his headset and making an obscene gesture. Alarmed, Sanborn even raises the idea of fragging James. Returning from the field, the team meets a group of British private contractors with a disabled vehicle, and when snipers open fire, James and Sanborn take over the counter-sniping and Eldridge kills an insurgent trying to outflank them. In a warehouse, James finds a child's body rigged as a bomb that he believes is Beckham, a boy who sells DVDs outside the base, and Eldridge's counselor, Lieutenant Colonel Cambridge, is killed by a blast. James slips off base to find Beckham's family but ends up at the house of an unrelated professor. After a fuel tanker explosion, James leads Sanborn and Eldridge after the bombers; Eldridge is captured and, though rescued, shot in the leg, blaming James. Near the end of their rotation, the team cannot free a man locked into a bomb vest, and a shaken Sanborn admits that he wants to leave the army and have a son. At home with Connie and their baby, James finds civilian life empty, and he returns to Iraq for another tour with Delta Company.

The Hurt Locker premiered at the Venice Film Festival in September 2008 and was released in the United States by Summit Entertainment in June 2009. Widely acclaimed, it won six of its nine Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, making Bigelow the first woman to win Best Director.

overview: With the wedding of her younger sister fast approaching, Kat Ellis faces the undesirable prospect of traveling alone to London for the ceremony. While this is bad enough, Jeffrey, the man who left her as they moved closer to marriage, happens to be the groom's best man. Determined to show everyone -- most of all Jeffrey -- that her romantic life is as full and thrilling as ever, Kat hires a charming male escort as her date.
tagline: Love doesn't come cheap.
title: The Wedding Date
plot:
The Wedding Date is a 2005 American romantic comedy film directed by Dennis Dugan and starring Matthew McConaughey and Jennifer Lopez.

The main theme of The Wedding Date revolves around the idea of self-discovery, love, and taking risks. The story follows Kevin Doyle (played by Matthew McConaughey), a successful but unlucky-in-love advertising executive who hires a beautiful woman, Darby (played by Jennifer Lopez), to be his fake girlfriend for a wedding.

As the story unfolds, Kevin and Darby embark on a series of hilarious misadventures, and their initial arrangement gradually turns into genuine feelings. The film explores themes of vulnerability, trust, and embracing one's true self.

Throughout the movie, Kevin learns to let go of his fear of commitment and rejection, while Darby discovers her own worth and independence. Their relationship serves as a catalyst for personal growth, allowing them to confront their insecurities and fears.

The Wedding Date also touches on the idea of societal expectations and the pressure to conform to certain norms. The film pokes fun at the traditional wedding date scenario, where men are often expected to play the role of the "perfect" partner, while women are expected to be the perfect bride.

Ultimately, the movie concludes with Kevin and Darby finding love in each other's arms, having learned valuable lessons about themselves and the importance of taking risks and being true to oneself.

original_title: ドラゴンボールGT 悟空外伝! 勇気の証しは四星球(スーシンチュウ)
overview: Son Goku Jr. is the great-great-great-great-grandson of the legendary martial artist Son Goku. However, unlike his predecessor he's not a brave fighter. He's constantly picked on by school bullies, his grandmother Pan sees this and she's worried, but even though Goku Jr. is not a strong and powerful Saiyan, he has a kind heart, and Pan loves him. When Pan gets sick Goku Jr. realizes he must do something if he doesn't want to lose Pan. Then he will remember about the legends of the Dragon Balls. It was told they granted a wish to the bearer, Goku Jr. needs a magical wish more than ever.
title: Dragon Ball GT: A Hero's Legacy
plot:
Dragon Ball GT: A Hero's Legacy is a Japanese animated television special, the only one made for the Dragon Ball GT series. Directed by Osamu Kasai and credited to writers Akira Toriyama and Takao Koyama, it aired in Japan on March 26, 1997, between episodes 41 and 42, as a prelude to the very end of the series. The Japanese voice cast includes Masako Nozawa, Yuko Minaguchi and Shin Aomori.

A hundred years after Goku's defeat of Baby, all of his friends and family have died except his granddaughter Pan, now an old woman. Her great-great-grandson, Goku Jr., looks just like his famous ancestor but lacks his courage and fighting spirit. Pan takes the boy to visit Goku's grave and tries to train him, but he has no confidence and is bullied at school by his classmate Puck and his gang. While scolding Goku Jr. for not standing up for himself, Pan collapses and is hospitalized. Remembering stories of the wish-granting Dragon Balls, Goku Jr. resolves to find one on Mount Paozu to cure her. Mocked by Puck's gang, he loses his temper and knocks them out with a burst of hidden power, then sets off on foot. On the road he meets Puck again. Puck agrees to come along, at first hoping to see Goku Jr. eaten by a monster, and steals a cart of food for the trip; though he does not believe in the Dragon Balls, he decides to help because he admired Pan's strength.

After many obstacles, the pair reach a rickety rope bridge over a deep chasm. Puck crosses first, but Goku Jr. stumbles in the wind, and Puck falls when the bridge collapses while trying to save him. Continuing alone, Goku Jr. is attacked by a pig-like demon; a mother bear whose cub he had helped earlier comes to his defense, and in a rage Goku Jr. becomes a Super Saiyan, easily beats the demon and passes out with no memory of the change. At the summit he finds an old house holding the four-star Dragon Ball, but his wish fails, and he throws the ball away in tears. It rolls to the feet of the adult Goku, who explains that all seven balls are needed and tells his descendant that he is stronger and braver than he believes. A helicopter then lands carrying Pan and Puck, both safe. When Goku Jr. turns back, Goku has vanished, but his voice tells the boy that his own bravery saved them. Goku Jr. boards the helicopter with new confidence and the Dragon Ball.

 Funimation released an English dub on DVD in the United States on November 16, 2004, and a separate English version produced by AB Groupe aired on Toonami UK.

overview: Unlucky assassin Ladybug is determined to do his job peacefully after one too many gigs gone off the rails. Fate, however, may have other plans, as Ladybug's latest mission puts him on a collision course with lethal adversaries from around the globe—all with connected, yet conflicting, objectives—on the world's fastest train.
tagline: The end of the line is just the beginning.
title: Bullet Train
plot:
Bullet Train is an action-thriller film directed by David Leitch, released in 2022 under Columbia Pictures. The movie follows the story of Ladybug (played by Brad Pitt), a skilled assassin working for an international crime syndicate.

The plot revolves around Ladybug's mission to retrieve a briefcase containing $40 million from a high-speed train traveling across Japan. However, things take a turn when Ladybug discovers that he is not the only one on the train with his sights set on the briefcase.

As Ladybug navigates through the crowded train, he encounters other assassins, including Lemon (played by Brian Tyree Henry), Tangerine (played by Aaron Taylor-Johnson), and Hornet (played by Joey King). Each of these characters has their own agenda, making it difficult for Ladybug to determine who is friend or foe.

Throughout the film, Ladybug engages in a series of intense battles with his fellow assassins, showcasing his exceptional fighting skills. As the train hurtles through Japan's countryside, Ladybug must use his wits and cunning to outmaneuver his opponents and stay one step ahead of the game.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that each assassin has their own personal vendetta against someone on the train, adding an element of complexity to the plot. The film's pacing is fast-paced and action-packed, with a series of thrilling set pieces that keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

One of the standout aspects of Bullet Train is its ensemble cast, which brings together a diverse range of characters with unique personalities and motivations. The chemistry between the actors is palpable, making it easy to become invested in their respective storylines.

Overall, Bullet Train is an adrenaline-fueled thrill ride that will keep viewers entertained from start to finish. With its breakneck pace, witty dialogue, and impressive action sequences, this film is a must-see for fans of the action-thriller genre.

overview: Life for the residents of a tower block begins to run out of control.
tagline: Leave the real world behind
title: High-Rise
plot:
High-Rise (2015) is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, class struggle, and the consequences of unchecked ambition. The movie is set in a futuristic high-rise building where the wealthy elite reside in luxury, while the lower classes are relegated to squalor and poverty.

At its core, High-Rise is a commentary on the social and economic disparities that can lead to violence, paranoia, and the breakdown of society. The film's protagonist, Dr. Robert Laing (played by Tom Hiddleston), is a young doctor who moves into the high-rise building with his wife, Daphne (played by Elisabeth Moss). As he becomes increasingly disillusioned with the class divisions and the decadent lifestyle of the wealthy residents, he begins to question the morality of their actions.

The film also explores themes of power, control, and the corrupting influence of privilege. The high-rise building becomes a symbol of the elite's desire for exclusivity and superiority, while the lower classes are forced to live in squalor and desperation. As tensions rise and violence escalates, the boundaries between the haves and have-nots become increasingly blurred.

Through its exploration of these themes, High-Rise raises important questions about the nature of humanity and the consequences of our actions. The film is a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of empathy and understanding in breaking down social barriers.

Overall, High-Rise (2015) is a gripping and thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of our choices.

original_title: In the Shadow of the Moon
overview: In 1988, Philadelphia police officer Thomas "Locke" Lockhart, hungry to become a detective, begins tracking a serial killer whose crimes defy scientific explanation. When the killer mysteriously resurfaces nine years later, Locke's obsession with finding the truth threatens to destroy his career, his family, and possibly his sanity.
title: In the Shadow of the Moon
plot:
In the Shadow of the Moon is a 2019 American science fiction thriller film directed by Jim Mickle and written by Gregory Weidman and Geoff Tock. Boyd Holbrook stars as the Philadelphia police officer Thomas Lockhart, with Cleopatra Coleman as Rya, Michael C. Hall as Lockhart's brother-in-law, Holt, Bokeem Woodbine as his partner Maddox and Rudi Dharmalingam as the physicist Naveen Rao.

In Philadelphia in 1988, several people die of brain hemorrhages, each with a similar puncture wound. The police learn from a dying victim that the attacker is a black woman with an injured hand. Chasing the suspect into the subway, Lockhart hears her reveal details of his life, including that his wife is giving birth to a girl that day, before she is crushed by a train in a struggle, just as she predicted. The case is closed, but Lockhart's wife dies in childbirth. Nine years later, a new wave of identical killings begins. Lockhart, now a detective raising his daughter Amy, discovers that keys found on the dead woman belong to an aircraft built in 1996, and Rao claims the killings prove time travel. At an airfield, Lockhart finds the same woman, alive and unaged; she accidentally kills Maddox, takes Lockhart on a small plane and pushes him into the sea before crashing. By 2006 Lockhart is a drunken private investigator, and Amy lives with Holt. Learning that one of the 1988 victims ran a white nationalist militia, he concludes that the woman is moving back in time and eliminating its members, but Holt dismisses him. Using Holt's stolen badge, Lockhart reaches the leader's extremist former girlfriend just after her murder, shoots the fleeing assassin in the hand and sees her vanish into a time machine on the beach where her plane crashed, before Holt arrests him. In 2015, Rao abducts him and explains that he devised the remotely triggered injections the woman uses, aimed at people who inspired a future atrocity. Escaping, Lockhart confronts the woman, who reveals that she is Rya, his granddaughter, born that very day, and that a militia attack starts a civil war in 2024. Realizing that he caused her death in 1988, he lets her continue her mission. Later, the elderly Rao triggers the injections, erasing the attack and the war, and Lockhart reunites with his family and his newborn granddaughter.

Shot in Toronto in 2018, the film premiered at Fantastic Fest on 21 September 2019 and began streaming on Netflix six days later. Reviews were mixed (59% on Rotten Tomatoes).

overview: A chilling vision of the House of Saddam Hussein comes to life through the eyes of the man who was forced to become the double of Hussein's sadistic son.
tagline: The 80's were brilliant, if you were in charge.
title: The Devil's Double
plot:
The Devil's Double is a 2011 biographical drama film that tells the story of Uday Hussein, the son of Saddam Hussein, and his doppelganger, Toby Young. 

At its core, the movie explores the themes of identity, loyalty, and the blurred lines between reality and fiction. The film delves into the complexities of Uday's life, showcasing his struggles with his own identity as he navigates the treacherous world of Saddam Hussein's regime.

The movie also examines the theme of obsession, highlighting Toby Young's fixation on Uday and his desire to become him. This obsession serves as a metaphor for the human tendency to idealize or idolize others, often leading to destructive consequences.

Furthermore, The Devil's Double touches upon the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and families. The film portrays the devastating effects of war, violence, and abuse on those who experience them, leaving deep emotional scars that can be difficult to overcome.

Ultimately, the movie presents a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, raising questions about the nature of identity, loyalty, and the consequences of our actions.

overview: When Carol Vanstone, CEO of the technology company Zenotek, expresses her intention to close the Chicago branch, run by her brother Clay, he and his co-workers organize a Christmas party in an effort to impress a potential client and save their jobs. But the party gets out of control…
tagline: Party like your job depends on it
title: Office Christmas Party
plot:
Office Christmas Party is a 2016 American comedy film directed by Greg Mottola and written by Robert Carlock. The movie stars Jason Bateman, Jennifer Aniston, Tad Hilgenbrandt, and Kate McKinnon.

The story revolves around Josh Parker (played by Jason Bateman), the CEO of a mid-sized paper company called Harper-Dole. Josh is married to Carol (played by Jennifer Aniston) and they have two children together. The office Christmas party is an annual tradition at Harper-Dole, where employees are encouraged to let loose and have fun.

However, things take a turn when Josh's new business partner, Todd (played by Tad Hilgenbrandt), starts to exert his influence over the company. Todd is a ruthless and cunning businessman who wants to modernize the company and make it more profitable. He sees the office Christmas party as an opportunity to boost morale and increase productivity.

Todd convinces Josh that he needs to take the party to the next level, which means hiring a professional DJ and renting out a luxurious venue. However, things quickly spiral out of control when Todd's true intentions are revealed. He plans to use the party as a way to impress potential investors and secure funding for his own business ventures.

As the party gets underway, Josh starts to realize that Todd is not what he seems. He tries to intervene, but it's too late. The party descends into chaos, with employees getting drunk and wild, and Todd using the opportunity to schmooze with potential investors.

Meanwhile, Carol is struggling to balance her work and personal life. She's feeling overwhelmed and stressed out, and she starts to question whether she can keep up with Josh's demanding schedule.

As the night wears on, Josh realizes that he needs to take control of the situation. He rallies his employees and together they stage a rebellion against Todd's plans. In the end, Josh emerges victorious, but not before the party has descended into complete chaos.

The movie ends with Josh and Carol reflecting on the events of the previous night. They realize that they need to find a better balance between work and personal life, and that they can't let their careers define them. The final shot is of the office Christmas party decorations being taken down, symbolizing the end of an era.

Overall, Office Christmas Party is a hilarious and entertaining movie that explores the challenges of modern worklife. With its talented cast and witty script, it's a must-see for anyone who loves comedy and satire.

original_title: Scooby-Doo! and the Curse of the 13th Ghost
overview: Mystery Inc. withdraws from solving crimes after botching a case. When Vincent Van Ghoul contacts the gang about an unfinished investigation from Daphne, Shaggy and Scooby's past, the gang springs into action to finish the job that involves catching the 13th Ghost that escaped from the Chest of Demons and is still at large.
title: Scooby-Doo! and the Curse of the 13th Ghost
plot:
Scooby-Doo! and the Curse of the 13th Ghost is a 2019 American animated direct-to-video comedy mystery film produced by Warner Bros. Animation and the thirty-second entry in the direct-to-video Scooby-Doo film series. It continues the 1985 series The 13 Ghosts of Scooby-Doo, giving that show's unfinished storyline an ending. The voice cast features Frank Welker as Scooby-Doo and Fred Jones, Grey DeLisle as Daphne Blake, Matthew Lillard as Shaggy Rogers, Kate Micucci as Velma Dinkley, Maurice LaMarche as Vincent Van Ghoul and Bernie Alan, Noshir Dalal as Flim Flam and Nolan North as Asmodeus and Mortifer Quinch.

In a flashback, the young Vincent Van Ghoul and his partner Mortifer Quinch seal the 13th Ghost in the Chest of Demons, but Mortifer is seemingly killed by minion ghosts. In the present, the Mystery Inc. gang catch the costumed "Farmer Morgan" at a shopping mall, only for the sheriff to arrive with the true culprit, scold them for nabbing the wrong suspect and order them to stop solving mysteries. At a garage sale, a customer named Bernie Alan finds a crystal ball that Shaggy and Scooby recognize from their 13 Ghosts adventures, and Van Ghoul then contacts them about the last ghost. Daphne drives everyone in her red van, the Miss-tery Machine, to Van Ghoul's castle, outmaneuvering a phantom car on the way, while Fred, watching her take charge, feels he has lost his role. At the castle they are attacked by the 13th Ghost, the winged demon Asmodeus, and when Shaggy confesses that he shipped the chest to Van Ghoul's Himalayan home, the gang flies there. In the mountains the phantom car sets off an avalanche, and Fred and Velma meet a grown-up Flim Flam, now selling Chest of Demons merchandise before being snatched away. Asmodeus chases the others through a temple until Van Ghoul destroys his crystal ball to transport them to safety. Fred raises the gang's spirits, and after they rescue Van Ghoul, Asmodeus opens the chest, which Velma notes only a living person can do. Unmasked by Daphne, the demon proves to be Mortifer, who faked his death and planned to sell the chest to Flim Flam for $10 million. Bernie reveals himself to be Interpol agent Vance Linklater and arrests him. Velma debunks the earlier ghosts as hallucinations caused by thin Himalayan air.

The film was released on DVD and digital on 5 February 2019. While it follows on from the 1985 series, it retcons most of its events, dropping Scrappy-Doo and the show's supernatural elements.

overview: A comedy that follows the chaos that ensues when a meteor hits the Earth carrying alien life forms that give new meaning to the term "survival of the fittest." David Duchovny, Orlando Jones, Seann William Scott, and Julianne Moore are the only people standing between the aliens and world domination... which could be bad news for the Earth.
tagline: Coming to wipe that silly smile off your planet.
title: Evolution
plot:
Evolution is a 2001 American science fiction comedy film directed by Ivan Reitman and written by Peter Farrelly and Bobby Farrelly. The movie stars David Duchovny, Orlando Jones, and Julianne Moore.

The story begins with Dr. Ira Levinson (David Duchovny), a paleontologist who has spent his entire career studying dinosaurs. He is obsessed with the idea of finding a way to bring back these prehistoric creatures to life. After years of research, he finally succeeds in creating a serum that can reanimate dead tissue.

However, things take a turn for the worse when Ira's lab is attacked by a group of thieves who steal his serum and use it to create an army of dinosaurs in modern-day New York City. The dinosaurs, including a Tyrannosaurus Rex, Velociraptors, and Triceratops, wreak havoc on the city, causing destruction and chaos.

Enter Ray Finkle (Orlando Jones), a former minor league baseball player who is now working as a security guard at a museum. He teams up with Ira's daughter, Dr. Maggie Levinson (Julianne Moore), to stop the dinosaurs and find a way to reverse the effects of the serum.

As the story unfolds, Ray and Maggie must navigate through the city, avoiding the dinosaurs and trying to find a way to shut down the serum's effects. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including a group of bumbling scientists who are trying to exploit the situation for their own gain.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of humorous moments, courtesy of Ray's witty one-liners and his fish-out-of-water experiences in the scientific world. The special effects are also impressive, bringing the dinosaurs to life in a way that is both convincing and entertaining.

As the plot reaches its climax, Ray and Maggie finally discover the location of the serum's source: a secret laboratory hidden beneath the city streets. They must use all their wits and cunning to outsmart the villains and shut down the serum, saving the city from destruction.

In the end, Ray and Maggie succeed in stopping the dinosaurs and reversing the effects of the serum. The movie ends with a comedic twist, as Ray is hailed as a hero for his role in saving the city, despite having no scientific expertise whatsoever.

Overall, Evolution is a fun and entertaining movie that combines humor, action, and adventure. While it may not be a masterpiece of science fiction cinema, it is a lighthearted and enjoyable ride that is sure to delight fans of dinosaurs and comedy.

overview: Jacob, a bank manager haunted by a violent heist that took the life of a coworker, teams up with his ex-cop neighbor, James, to bring down the assailant. While the two men work together to figure out the thief’s next move, Gabriel, the highly-trained criminal, is one step ahead. When Gabriel kidnaps Jacob’s wife and daughter, Jacob barrels down a path of bloodshed that initiates an explosive counterattack and brings all three men to the breaking point.
tagline: A life for a life.
title: Reprisal
plot:
Reprisal is an American action thriller of 2018 directed by Brian A. Miller and written by Bryce Hammons. Frank Grillo stars as Jacob, a bank manager, with Bruce Willis as his neighbor James, a retired police officer, Johnathon Schaech as the bank robber Gabriel, Olivia Culpo as Jacob's wife Christina and Natali Yura as Maribel.

Jacob, the son of a police officer who died, manages a bank branch and is struggling financially because of the mounting medical bills of his daughter Sophia, who suffers from an extremely aggressive form of type 1 diabetes. One day a robber storms the bank, kills a guard, forces Jacob to open the vault and hand over the money, and then uses Jacob and another employee as decoys to make his getaway. Jacob and James study the robbery alongside earlier heists. Picking out the thief's signature habits, Jacob identifies him as a man named Gabriel and predicts that his next target will be an armored car.

He is right. During the armored car robbery Gabriel kills one guard and wounds another, Maribel, who knows Jacob from the bank; Jacob intervenes and saves her, and she is taken to the hospital. Jacob also sees where Gabriel stashes the stolen money, and while the robber is burning down his hideout in his late father's abandoned factory, Jacob takes the cash and hides it behind his house. Gabriel soon discovers the loss and realizes who is responsible. To get to Jacob, he tracks Maribel to the hospital, guns down an investigator interviewing her and forces her at gunpoint to call Jacob and ask him to come. He then kills her and heads for Jacob's house, where he kidnaps Christina and Sophia.

Arriving too late with James, Jacob receives a call from Gabriel demanding that he come alone with the stolen money as ransom. With James's help, Jacob arranges the drop-off and an attempt to rescue his family, but the exchange goes badly wrong and turns into a bloody shootout in which Gabriel kills several police officers before James finally shoots him dead. Six months later, Jacob has left banking and joined the local police force as a rookie officer, following in his father's footsteps.

The project was announced in February 2017, with Emmett/Furla/Oasis Films producing and Willis attached to star, and principal photography began in Cincinnati, Ohio, that August. The film was released in 2018 and received overwhelmingly negative reviews, with an approval rating of 8% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 19.

overview: Erin and Garrett are very much in love. When Erin moves to San Francisco to finish her journalism degree and Garrett stays behind in New York to work in the music industry, they gamely keep the romance alive with webcams and frequent-flyer miles. But just when it seems the lovers will soon be reunited, they each score a big break that could separate them for good.
tagline: A comedy about meeting each other halfway.
title: Going the Distance
plot:
Going the Distance is a romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of long-distance relationships and personal growth. The movie follows the story of a young woman, Erin, who embarks on a cross-country road trip to meet her boyfriend, Garrett, in San Francisco after they've been together for three years.

As Erin navigates this journey, she is forced to confront her own identity, desires, and sense of self-worth. The film delves into themes of independence, vulnerability, and the challenges of maintaining a relationship while pursuing individual goals and aspirations.

Through Erin's character development, the movie highlights the importance of self-discovery and embracing one's true nature. As she faces various obstacles on her journey, Erin learns to let go of her fears and insecurities, ultimately discovering a newfound sense of confidence and purpose.

The film also explores the tension between personal growth and relationship commitment, raising questions about whether it's possible to maintain a healthy connection with someone while pursuing one's own path in life. Ultimately, Going the Distance presents a nuanced portrayal of love, relationships, and the complexities of human connection.

overview: A mild-mannered father is transformed into a killing machine after his family is torn apart by a violent act.
tagline: How Far Would You Go To Protect Your Family?
title: Death Wish
plot:
Death Wish is a 2018 American vigilante action thriller film directed by Eli Roth, written by Joe Carnahan and produced by Roger Birnbaum. A remake of the 1974 film and the sixth entry in the series, it stars Bruce Willis as Paul Kersey, a Chicago trauma surgeon, with Vincent D'Onofrio as his brother Frank, Elisabeth Shue as his wife Lucy, Camila Morrone as his daughter Jordan, Dean Norris and Kimberly Elise as the detectives Kevin Raines and Leonore Jackson, and Beau Knapp as Knox.

During a family dinner at a restaurant, a valet named Miguel secretly copies the Kerseys' address after overhearing their plans. While Paul is called away to the hospital, Lucy and Jordan come home to find three armed burglars, and in the struggle Lucy is fatally shot and Jordan is left in a coma. Frustrated by the slow police investigation, Paul takes a pistol that falls from a wounded gang member at the hospital and uses it to stop a carjacking. A video goes viral and the media dub him the "Grim Reaper", and after treating a boy hurt for refusing to deal drugs, Paul shoots the dealer known as the Ice Cream Man in broad daylight. Paul recognizes a dying Miguel on his operating table wearing a watch stolen from his home. Miguel's phone leads him to a liquor store that fences stolen goods, where the gunman Fish accidentally kills the owner while trying to shoot Paul. Fish names Joe as another robber before Paul kills him, and Joe, tortured at a body shop, reveals that a third man, Knox, killed Lucy. Paul kills Joe, then exchanges fire with Knox in a nightclub restroom, and both are wounded. Knox describes Paul to the police, and Paul learns that Jordan has woken from her coma. When Knox rides the hospital elevator with them a week later, Paul realizes that he will come after the family, and he legally buys guns. As Knox's crew attacks the house, Paul sends Jordan to hide and call the police, kills the intruders and uses a hidden rifle to kill Knox. The police accept his account after he suggests that he is finished with vigilantism. Months later, dropping Jordan off at New York University, Paul sees a thief snatch a bag and points a finger gun at him.

Shot in Chicago and Montreal from September 2016, the film was released by MGM on 2 March 2018, less than three weeks after the Parkland school shooting, which several critics noted. It grossed $55.9 million on a $30 million budget but received largely negative reviews, earning a 17% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

overview: A bride's wedding night takes a sinister turn when her eccentric new in-laws force her to take part in a terrifying game.
tagline: In-laws will be the death of her.
title: Ready or Not
plot:
Ready or Not is a 2019 American horror comedy film directed by Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett, written by Rafe Kukendat, and produced by Jason Blum, James DeMonaco, and others.

The movie follows the story of Grace Le Domas (Samara Weaving), a young woman who marries into a wealthy family, the Hesmonds, on her 21st birthday. The Hesmonds are part of an ancient tradition called "the game," where the bride must participate in a deadly game of hide and seek with the groom's family members.

The game is a twisted test of survival, where each player is eliminated until only one remains. The Hesmond family consists of Sam (Adam Brody), Paula (Andi Matichak), Jack (Mark O'Brien), Alexis (Samara Weaving's real-life sister, Mia Wasikowska was initially cast but dropped out and the role went to  Millicent Simmonds' friend), and Daniel (Henry Czerny). The family is led by Sam's father, Ben (André Holland).

As the game begins, Grace soon realizes that she must use her wits and resourcefulness to survive. However, as the night progresses, it becomes clear that the Hesmond family has a dark secret: they are all connected to an ancient curse that has been passed down through generations.

Throughout the movie, the tension builds up as Grace tries to outsmart each player, while also trying to understand the true nature of the game and the family's motivations. The film features a blend of horror, comedy, and social commentary, with a focus on class inequality and the exploitation of wealth.

As the game reaches its climax, it becomes clear that the Hesmond family is not just playing a harmless game, but are actually trying to eliminate Grace as part of their twisted tradition. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Ben has been manipulating the game all along, using his wealth and influence to ensure that only one player remains.

In the end, Grace manages to outsmart the Hesmond family and escape with her life, but not before she exacts a sense of revenge on those who have wronged her. The movie ends with a darkly comedic tone, as Grace is seen driving away from the Hesmond estate, ready to start a new life free from the curse.

Overall, Ready or Not is a tense and entertaining horror comedy that explores themes of class inequality, family dynamics, and survival. With its blend of humor, suspense, and social commentary, it has become a modern classic in the horror genre.

overview: While on a forgettable first date together in Ohio, a black man and a black woman are pulled over for a minor traffic infraction. The situation escalates, with sudden and tragic results.
title: Queen & Slim
plot:
Queen & Slim is a 2019 American romantic drama film directed by Melina Matsoukas. The movie follows the story of two young black lovers, Queen (Danielle Brooks) and Slim (John Boyega), who are in a tumultuous relationship.

The main themes of Queen & Slim include:

1. **Racial injustice and police brutality**: The film highlights the systemic racism and police violence faced by African Americans, particularly in the context of the Black Lives Matter movement.
2. **Love and relationships**: The movie explores the complexities of love, intimacy, and commitment between two people from different backgrounds and with different personalities.
3. **Identity and self-discovery**: Queen & Slim is also a story about finding one's identity and purpose in life. Both characters are struggling to find their place in the world and navigate their relationships with themselves and others.
4. **Social justice and activism**: The film features several scenes of protests, marches, and conversations about social justice, highlighting the importance of speaking out against systemic racism and advocating for change.
5. **Trauma and healing**: Throughout the movie, Queen & Slim face various forms of trauma, including police violence, incarceration, and emotional abuse. The film explores their journeys towards healing and recovery.

The movie received critical acclaim for its thought-provoking themes, powerful performances, and timely commentary on contemporary social issues.

overview: In this romantic comedy, several friends, each dealing with unhappy love lives, turn to each other for help - but not always with the best results.
title: F*ck Love Too

overview: When their computer hacker friend accidentally channels a mysterious wireless signal, a group of co-eds rally to stop a terrifying evil from taking over the world.
tagline: You are now infected.
title: Pulse
plot:
Pulse (2006) is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and technology's impact on society. The movie revolves around a group of college students who discover an internet chat room where they can interact with each other in real-time, but soon find themselves being stalked by a mysterious presence that begins to take control of their bodies.

At its core, Pulse explores the theme of isolation and disconnection in the digital age. The film highlights how technology can both unite and isolate individuals, leading to a sense of emptiness and disconnection from one another. As the characters become increasingly enthralled with the chat room, they begin to lose touch with reality, illustrating the dangers of becoming too reliant on virtual connections.

The movie also touches on the idea of possession and control, as the supernatural entity takes hold of the students' bodies, manipulating them to do its bidding. This serves as a metaphor for how external forces can exert control over our lives, often without us even realizing it.

Furthermore, Pulse critiques the notion of online anonymity, suggesting that this perceived freedom can be a facade for true vulnerability and exposure. The film's use of the chat room as a hub for social interaction raises questions about the nature of intimacy and connection in the digital age.

Ultimately, Pulse presents a cautionary tale about the dangers of becoming too enthralled with technology and losing sight of our humanity.

overview: Dylan Sprouse, Jim Belushi and Kris Kristofferson lend their voices to this family-friendly tale about a feisty pack of golden retriever puppies that embarks on an Alaskan adventure. When they find themselves stranded in the northern wilderness, the canine offspring of famed sports star Air Bud team up with an experienced sled dog and a husky pup, who teach them the importance of working together.
title: Snow Buddies
plot:
Snow Buddies is a heartwarming animated adventure film that revolves around a group of golden retriever puppies who embark on an exciting journey to save their owner, a young boy named Cody. The movie explores several key themes that resonate with audiences of all ages.

At its core, Snow Buddies is a story about the unbreakable bond between humans and animals. The film showcases the deep affection and loyalty that exists between Cody and his canine companions, highlighting the ways in which these relationships can bring joy, comfort, and a sense of belonging to our lives. Through the puppies' adventures, the movie demonstrates the importance of empathy, compassion, and understanding towards all living beings.

The film also touches on themes of perseverance, teamwork, and problem-solving. As the puppies face various obstacles and challenges in their quest to rescue Cody, they learn valuable lessons about working together, using their unique skills and strengths to overcome seemingly insurmountable hurdles. This emphasis on collaboration and creative thinking serves as a powerful reminder of the value of cooperation and mutual support.

Furthermore, Snow Buddies features a narrative that celebrates the beauty of nature and the great outdoors. The movie's stunning winter landscapes and picturesque settings serve as a backdrop for the puppies' exciting escapades, highlighting the importance of appreciating and respecting the natural world.

Ultimately, Snow Buddies is a film that will leave viewers feeling uplifted, inspired, and perhaps even a little bit nostalgic for their own childhood adventures. With its lighthearted tone, engaging storyline, and endearing characters, this animated adventure is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

overview: The true story of the Mauritanian Mohamedou Ould Slahi, who was held at the U.S military's Guantanamo Bay detention center without charges for over a decade and sought help from a defense attorney for his release.
title: The Mauritanian
plot:
The Mauritanian is a 2021 American drama film directed by Kevin Macdonald, based on the book "Guantánamo Diary" by Mohamedou Ould Slahi. The movie stars Tahar Rahim as Mohamedou Ould Slahi, a Mauritanian citizen who was detained at Guantánamo Bay for over 14 years without charge.

The main themes of The Mauritanian include:

1. **Detention and Torture**: The film highlights the inhumane treatment of detainees at Guantánamo Bay, particularly Mohamedou Ould Slahi, who was subjected to physical and psychological torture.
