Yasha, descended from swift demons once stripped of divine status by the supreme god Ōkuninushi, steals the gourd and bracelet and beats Kanna in a race, but ends up joining the journey. At Lake Suwa the dragon god Ryūjin, a son of Ōkuninushi, draws out Kanna's real wish, to see her mother again, and shares his own separation from his father. Near the end of the route, a vision of Yayoi lures Kanna away, but it is her own dark side in disguise. Despairing, Kanna tears off the bracelet and can no longer hear her companions as a typhoon strikes. A vision reveals that Yayoi, too, was a descendant of the Idaten, the runners who once performed this task. Inspired, Kanna ties up her hair with the bracelet and runs on through the storm to the shrine, where Ōkuninushi appears and the feast begins. He thanks the three but says even his matchmaking cannot bring Yayoi back and that time must move on. Back in Tokyo, Kanna takes up running again in the spring.

Aju Makita voices Kanna, with Maaya Sakamoto as Shiro, Miyu Irino as Yasha, Akira Kamiya as Ōkuninushi, Wataru Takagi as Ryūjin, Ko Shibasaki as Yayoi and Arata Iura as Norimasa. All six critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes gave it positive reviews.

overview: Chan Wing Yan, a young police officer, has been sent undercover as a mole in the local mafia. Lau Kin Ming, a young mafia member, infiltrates the police force. Years later, their older counterparts, Chen Wing Yan and Inspector Lau Kin Ming, respectively, race against time to expose the mole within their midst.
tagline: Loyalty. Honor. Betrayal.
title: Infernal Affairs
plot:
Infernal Affairs is a 2002 Hong Kong crime thriller film directed by Andrew Lau and Alan Mak. The movie follows two main storylines that eventually intersect, exploring themes of deception, loyalty, and redemption.

The first storyline revolves around Chan Wing-yan (played by Andy Lau), an undercover cop working for the Hong Kong Police Force's Narcotics Squad. Chan is tasked with infiltrating a triad organization known as the 14K Triad, led by the ruthless and cunning Big Brother (played by Tony Leung). As Chan gains the trust of the triads, he becomes embroiled in their world, forming close relationships with his colleagues and even falling for one of them.

The second storyline centers around Lau Kin-ming (played by Louis Koo), a low-ranking member of the 14K Triad. Kin-ming is assigned to investigate Chan's activities, suspecting that he may be an undercover cop. As Kin-ming delves deeper into the case, he becomes increasingly entangled in the world of organized crime.

Throughout the film, both storylines unfold simultaneously, with each character unaware of the other's true identity. The tension builds as Chan and Kin-ming engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with neither side willing to back down. As their paths continue to cross, they begin to develop feelings for each other, adding an emotional layer to the narrative.

The plot thickens when Big Brother orders Kin-ming to kill Chan, but Kin-ming is torn between his loyalty to the triad and his growing affection for Chan. Meanwhile, Chan's colleagues become suspicious of his activities, putting him in a precarious position.

As the story reaches its climax, both Chan and Kin-ming are forced to confront their true identities and make difficult choices. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Big Brother has been manipulating both characters from the beginning, using them for his own purposes.

In the end, Chan and Kin-ming must work together to take down Big Brother and bring an end to the triad's reign of terror. The film concludes with a sense of redemption and closure, as both characters find a way to reconcile their past mistakes and forge a new path forward.

Infernal Affairs was widely praised for its gripping storyline, strong performances, and nuanced exploration of themes such as loyalty, deception, and redemption. The film's success can be attributed to the talented cast, particularly Andy Lau and Tony Leung, who deliver memorable performances that bring depth and complexity to their characters.

overview: Immigrants from around the world enter Los Angeles every day, with hopeful visions of a better life, but little notion of what that life may cost. Their desperate scenarios test the humanity of immigration enforcement officers. In Crossing Over, writer-director Wayne Kramer explores the allure of the American dream, and the reality that immigrants find – and create -- in 21st century L.A.
tagline: Every day thousands of people illegally cross our borders... only one thing stands in their way. America.
title: Crossing Over
plot:
Crossing Over is a 2009 American drama film directed by Wayne Kramer. The movie explores the lives of several characters from different ethnic backgrounds who are brought together at a Los Angeles immigration center, where they must navigate the complexities of the US immigration system.

At its core, Crossing Over delves into the universal themes of identity, community, and the human condition. It highlights the struggles of immigrants seeking a better life in America, often facing bureaucratic red tape, cultural dislocation, and personal sacrifice. The film also touches on issues of loneliness, isolation, and the search for belonging.

Through its diverse cast of characters, Crossing Over sheds light on the complexities of identity formation, particularly among first-generation Americans who must reconcile their ancestral heritage with their adopted American culture. The movie also explores the tensions between tradition and assimilation, as well as the resilience and resourcefulness required to thrive in a new country.

Ultimately, Crossing Over presents a poignant portrayal of the human experience, revealing the intricate web of relationships that bind people together across cultural boundaries. By exploring the complexities of identity, community, and belonging, the film offers a nuanced and thought-provoking commentary on the immigrant experience in America.

overview: Follows Callie and Joseph one year after they fell in love, now running a dairy farm and winery, but their romance is threatened when business and family obligations call Joseph back to the city.
title: A California Christmas: City Lights
plot:
A California Christmas: City Lights is a heartwarming holiday film that explores the complexities of love, family, and identity. The movie delves into the life of a young woman named Samantha, who returns to her hometown in California after years away, seeking solace and connection.

As Samantha navigates her way through the festive atmosphere of her hometown, she is forced to confront her past and reevaluate her sense of belonging. Through her interactions with the people around her, particularly a handsome and charming stranger, Samantha begins to rediscover the true meaning of Christmas and the importance of human connection in her life.

One of the main themes of A California Christmas: City Lights is the power of homecoming and the idea that one's roots can be a source of strength and inspiration. The film celebrates the warmth and hospitality of small-town America, where community and tradition are deeply ingrained.

The movie also explores the theme of identity and self-discovery, as Samantha grapples with her sense of purpose and belonging in the world. Her journey is marked by moments of vulnerability, introspection, and growth, as she learns to let go of her past and embrace her future.

Ultimately, A California Christmas: City Lights is a feel-good holiday film that reminds us of the importance of love, kindness, and connection during the most wonderful time of the year. The movie's lighthearted tone and festive atmosphere make it a perfect watch for anyone looking to get into the holiday spirit.

overview: In the prehistoric past, Keda, a young and inexperienced hunter, struggles to return home after being separated from his tribe when bison hunting goes awry. On his way back he will find an unexpected ally.
tagline: Leaders are born from survival
title: Alpha
plot:
Alpha is a 2018 American epic drama film directed by Charlie McDowell and written by Dan O'Bannon and Alexander Dinelaris Jr. The movie stars Kodi Smit-McPhee, Alia Shawkat, and Justin Kelley.

The story takes place in the late Stone Age, around 20,000 years ago, during a time of great change for early humans. The film follows the journey of Oena (Kodi Smit-McPhee), a young hunter who lives with his tribe in the wilderness. After a devastating event that kills many of his people, Oena is left alone and must navigate the harsh environment to survive.

As he travels through the forest, Oena encounters a wolf pup, which he names Kenai (also known as Wahya). The two form an unlikely bond, with Kenai becoming Oena's companion and protector. However, their relationship is put to the test when they are attacked by a pack of wolves, and Kenai is killed.

Consumed by grief and anger, Oena decides to take revenge on the wolves that killed his friend. He begins to hunt them down, but as he does, he starts to transform into a wolf-like creature himself. This transformation is not just physical, but also emotional and spiritual, as Oena struggles to come to terms with his new identity.

As Oena navigates his newfound powers, he must confront the harsh realities of his tribe's existence. He witnesses their brutal treatment of animals and their disregard for the natural world. This realization sparks a transformation within him, as he begins to see himself as part of the natural world rather than separate from it.

The film's climax features Oena facing off against a rival tribe that has been threatening his people. In a symbolic confrontation, Oena uses his newfound powers to defend his tribe and restore balance to the natural world. The movie ends with Oena standing alone in the forest, having found a new sense of purpose and belonging.

Throughout the film, McDowell explores themes of identity, community, and the human relationship with nature. The movie features stunning cinematography and a haunting score, which complements the emotional depth of the story. While Alpha received mixed reviews from critics, it has developed a loyal following among fans of epic dramas and those interested in exploring the early history of humanity.

Overall, Alpha is a visually stunning and emotionally resonant film that explores the complexities of human nature and our relationship with the natural world.

overview: Quincy McCall and Monica Wright grew up in the same neighborhood and have known each other since childhood. As they grow into adulthood, they fall in love, but they also share another all-consuming passion: basketball.  As Quincy and Monica struggle to make their relationship work, they follow separate career paths though high school and college basketball and, they hope, into stardom in big-league professional ball.
tagline: All's fair in love and basketball.
title: Love & Basketball
plot:
Love & Basketball is a poignant coming-of-age romance that explores the complexities of love, friendship, and the sacrifices one must make for their passions. The film delves into the intense bond between two young souls, Monica Wright (Sanaa Lathan) and Quincy McCall (Omar Epps), who grow up together in a small town in Indiana.

As they navigate their way through adolescence and young adulthood, Monica and Quincy's relationship is put to the test by their individual aspirations. Monica dreams of becoming a professional basketball player, while Quincy aspires to become a doctor. Their love for each other becomes a source of strength and motivation, but also creates tension and conflict as they struggle to balance their personal ambitions with their desire for each other.

Throughout the film, the director, Gina Prince-Bythewood, masterfully weaves together themes of identity, loyalty, and the power of relationships. Monica and Quincy's love becomes a catalyst for growth, forcing them to confront their own desires, fears, and limitations. The film also explores the complexities of family dynamics, particularly the strained relationship between Monica's father (Denzel Washington) and her mother (Debbi Morgan), which serves as a backdrop for Monica and Quincy's own struggles with commitment and loyalty.

Ultimately, Love & Basketball is a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that celebrates the beauty of love, friendship, and the pursuit of one's passions. The film's nuanced portrayal of complex relationships and its thoughtful examination of the sacrifices we make for those we love make it a timeless classic in contemporary cinema.

overview: An American girl on vacation in Italy finds an unanswered "letter to Juliet" -- one of thousands of missives left at the fictional lover's Verona courtyard, which are typically answered by the "secretaries of Juliet" -- and she goes on a quest to find the lovers referenced in the letter.
tagline: What if you had a second chance to find true love?
title: Letters to Juliet
plot:
Letters to Juliet is a 2010 romantic comedy-drama film directed by Gary Ross, starring Amanda Seyfried, Christopher Egan, and Vanessa Redgrave.

The main themes of Letters to Juliet revolve around love, self-discovery, and the power of letters. The story follows Sophie (Amanda Seyfried), a young woman who discovers that she has inherited a villa in Italy from her recently deceased grandmother. While exploring the villa, Sophie finds a cache of old love letters addressed to Juliet Capulet, a fictional character from Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet.

As Sophie reads through the letters, she becomes fascinated by the stories of the women who wrote them, each with their own unique tale of love, heartbreak, and longing. Inspired by these stories, Sophie decides to respond to the letters on behalf of the women, hoping to bring happiness and closure to those who wrote them.

Throughout the film, the themes of Letters to Juliet unfold as follows:

1. **The Power of Letters**: The film highlights the transformative power of letters in bringing people together, providing comfort, and offering a sense of connection. Sophie's actions demonstrate that even small gestures can have a profound impact on someone's life.
2. **Self-Discovery**: As Sophie navigates her own feelings and relationships, she begins to uncover more about herself and her place in the world. The film encourages viewers to explore their own emotions and desires, just as Sophie does through her interactions with the women whose letters she responds to.
3. **Love and Heartbreak**: Letters to Juliet explores the complexities of love and heartbreak, showcasing the pain and joy that can come from both experiences. The film suggests that even in the midst of sorrow, there is always hope for healing and new beginnings.
4. **Female Empowerment**: Sophie's journey is also one of female empowerment, as she takes control of her life and finds a sense of purpose through her interactions with the women whose letters she responds to. The film celebrates the strength and resilience of women who have been marginalized or overlooked throughout history.

Overall, Letters to Juliet is a heartwarming and engaging film that explores themes of love, self-discovery, and the power of human connection.

overview: When immense pressure threatens a ballerina in a new lead role, she and another dancer escape into a friendship that isolates them from the real world.
title: Dancing on Glass
plot:
Dancing on Glass (Las niñas de cristal) is a 2022 Spanish psychological drama directed by Jota Linares, his third feature, from a screenplay he wrote with Jorge Naranjo. Produced for Netflix by Federation Spain, the new Spanish branch of Federation Entertainment, it stars María Pedraza and Paula Losada as two young dancers drawn together by the pressures of a national ballet company, with Mona Martínez, Marta Hazas, Olivia Baglivi, Ana Wagener and Iria del Río in supporting roles.

After María, the star of the National Classical Ballet, takes her own life, Irene Solís is chosen to replace her in the lead of the company's biggest production, Giselle. The decision devastates Ruth, who believed she was the obvious successor, and Irene becomes the target of the jealousy and cruelty of the other dancers, struggling under the impossible expectations of the company's tyrannical director, Norma, and her own family while battling bulimia. Her dancing begins to suffer until she befriends Aurora Ruiz, a lonely newcomer dominated by her mother, a former ballerina who pushes her daughter to succeed in her place, and who hides a large birthmark on her face behind her hair. Aurora teaches Irene her trick of disappearing into an imaginary world while she dances, and Irene finds that she performs at her best when Aurora is in the room. Isolated from everyone else and crushed by the sacrifices that success in dance demands, the two young women lean on one another as rehearsals intensify, and their relationship becomes ever closer and more obsessive, a joint flight forward in search of themselves, while Norma watches their friendship with suspicion. As opening night approaches, it becomes clear that, as the story began with the death of one of their own, the premiere will be a matter of life and death.

Filming took place in Madrid between February and April 2021. The film was presented in the official selection of the 25th Málaga Film Festival on March 25, 2022, and released worldwide on Netflix on April 8, 2022. In El País, Javier Ocaña praised Pedraza's commendable physical and artistic work and the solidity of Martínez and Baglivi, calling it a more than worthwhile film from a director perhaps overwhelmed by ambition in an excessively harsh ending. Decider's Jade Budowski admired Pedraza's mesmerizing dancing and her chemistry with Losada but found the story too familiar from films such as Black Swan and the running time overlong.

overview: Light years from Earth, 26 years after being abducted, Peter Quill finds himself the prime target of a manhunt after discovering an orb wanted by Ronan the Accuser.
tagline: All heroes start somewhere.
title: Guardians of the Galaxy
plot:
Guardians of the Galaxy is a 2014 American superhero film directed by James Gunn and produced by Marvel Studios. The movie follows the story of Peter Quill, a human who was abducted by aliens as a child and became a space pirate.

The film begins with Peter Quill (played by Chris Pratt), a young boy who is abducted by a group of aliens called the Ravagers, led by Yondu Udonta (Michael Rooker). The aliens take Peter to their spaceship, where he grows up surrounded by their culture. However, when Peter discovers that his mother's music is playing on one of the ship's speakers, he becomes obsessed with finding her.

Years later, Peter is now a grown man who has become a space pirate, using the alias Star-Lord. He steals valuable artifacts and sells them to the highest bidder. During one of his missions, Peter encounters Gamora (Zoe Saldana), a deadly assassin working for the villainous Ronan the Accuser (Lee Pace). The two engage in a fierce battle, but eventually form an uneasy alliance.

The group also meets Drax the Destroyer (Dave Bautista), a powerful warrior who seeks revenge against Ronan for killing his family. There's also Rocket Raccoon (voiced by Bradley Cooper), a genetically engineered raccoon with enhanced abilities and a sarcastic attitude. Finally, there's Groot (voiced by Vin Diesel), a tree-like humanoid who can only say three words: "I am Groot."

The group soon discovers that Ronan is searching for the Orb, a powerful artifact that could destroy entire planets. They also learn that Gamora was once a member of Ronan's crew but has since defected.

As they journey through space, the Guardians face numerous challenges and obstacles, including battles with Ronan's minions and navigating treacherous asteroid fields. Along the way, Peter begins to form close bonds with his new allies, particularly Gamora and Drax.

The movie reaches its climax when the Guardians confront Ronan on the planet Morag. In a final showdown, Peter and his friends manage to defeat Ronan, but not before he destroys the Orb, which shatters into pieces.

In the aftermath, the Guardians come together to celebrate their victory and form an unbreakable bond. The movie ends with Peter returning home to Earth, where he is reunited with his long-lost father, Ego (Kurt Russell), who reveals that he is actually Peter's celestial being father.

The film concludes on a hopeful note, as the Guardians set out on new adventures together, ready to face whatever challenges come their way. The movie's success can be attributed to its unique blend of humor, action, and heart, which has made it a beloved classic among fans of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

overview: A look at the life of the astronaut, Neil Armstrong, and the legendary space mission that led him to become the first man to walk on the Moon on July 20, 1969.
tagline: One giant leap into the unknown
title: First Man
plot:
First Man is a 2018 American biographical drama directed by Damien Chazelle from a screenplay by Josh Singer, based on James R. Hansen's 2005 biography First Man: The Life of Neil A. Armstrong. It covers the years leading to the Apollo 11 Moon landing in 1969 and the toll they took on Armstrong, his family and his colleagues. First announced in 2003 with Clint Eastwood attached to direct, the project was revived with Chazelle, Ryan Gosling and Singer by 2015, and filming began in Atlanta in November 2017. It premiered at the Venice Film Festival on August 29, 2018, and Universal Pictures released it in the United States on October 12.

In 1961, test pilot Neil Armstrong narrowly lands an X-15 that bounces off the atmosphere, while at home his two-year-old daughter, Karen, is dying of a brain tumor. After her death, he applies for Project Gemini and moves to Houston with his wife, Janet, and son Rick as one of NASA's second group of astronauts, befriending Elliot See and Ed White as the United States trails the Soviet Union in the Space Race. He is given command of Gemini 8 with David Scott; after docking with an Agena target, a malfunction sends the capsule into a violent spin, and Armstrong, close to blacking out, regains control and aborts the mission. See dies in a jet crash before the flight, and in 1967 White and the rest of the Apollo 1 crew are killed in a launch-pad fire.

After surviving the crash of a lunar landing training vehicle, Armstrong is chosen to command Apollo 11. As the launch nears he withdraws from his family, until Janet insists that he explain to their sons that he may not return. In lunar orbit, Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin descend in the Eagle, and with the planned site too rough, Armstrong takes manual control and lands with less than 30 seconds of fuel left. On the surface he quietly drops Karen's bracelet into a crater. In quarantine after their return, he and Janet share a tender moment.

Gosling stars as Armstrong, with Claire Foy as Janet, Jason Clarke as White, Kyle Chandler as Deke Slayton, Corey Stoll as Aldrin and Christopher Abbott as Scott. Critics praised the direction, the performances of Gosling and Foy, the score and the landing sequence, giving it 87% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and it won the Academy Award for Best Visual Effects among four nominations. It underperformed commercially, however, grossing about $105.7 million on a $59 million budget.

overview: 12-year-old Regan MacNeil begins to adapt an explicit new personality as strange events befall the local area of Georgetown. Her mother becomes torn between science and superstition in a desperate bid to save her daughter, and ultimately turns to her last hope: Father Damien Karras, a troubled priest who is struggling with his own faith.
tagline: Something almost beyond comprehension is happening to a girl on this street, in this house… and a man has been sent for as a last resort. This man is The Exorcist.
title: The Exorcist
plot:
The Exorcist is a classic horror film directed by William Friedkin, released in 1973 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie tells the story of a young girl's demonic possession and the two priests who attempt to exorcise the evil spirit.

The film begins with the introduction of Regan MacNeil (Linda Blair), a 12-year-old girl who lives with her actress mother Chris (Ellen Burstyn) in Washington, D.C. Regan is a happy and energetic child, but she starts to exhibit strange behavior, such as unexplained noises, convulsions, and changes in her appearance.

As the symptoms worsen, Chris seeks medical attention, but the doctors are unable to diagnose the cause of Regan's illness. Desperate for help, Chris turns to two Catholic priests, Father Damien Karras (Jason Miller) and Father Lankester Merrin (Max von Sydow), who specialize in cases of demonic possession.

Father Karras is a troubled priest who struggles with his faith due to the death of his mother and his own feelings of guilt. He is initially hesitant to take on the case, but eventually agrees to help Regan after feeling a sense of responsibility towards her.

Meanwhile, Father Merrin is an older, more experienced priest who has spent years studying the rituals of exorcism. He is tasked with performing the ritual to free Regan from the demon's grasp.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Regan is possessed by a malevolent entity known as Pazuzu, which is an ancient demon from Assyrian mythology. The demon begins to exert its influence over Regan, causing her to become increasingly violent and erratic.

The exorcism ritual is a tense and suspenseful sequence of events, with Father Merrin performing the ancient rituals to try and banish the demon. However, the demon proves to be a formidable foe, and it takes all of Father Merrin's strength and faith to complete the ritual.

In the climactic final scene, Regan is seen being thrown across the room by an unseen force, and she utters the words "Get me out!" as the demon is finally banished. The film ends with a sense of relief and redemption for Chris, who has been through a traumatic experience, but also leaves the audience with a haunting sense of unease.

The Exorcist was widely praised for its chilling portrayal of demonic possession and its thought-provoking exploration of faith and doubt. It is considered one of the greatest horror films of all time, and its influence can still be felt in popular culture today.

overview: Two college students share a ride home for the holidays. When they break down on a deserted stretch of road, they're preyed upon by the ghosts of people who have died there.
tagline: There Are Worse Things Than Dying
title: Wind Chill
plot:
Wind Chill is a psychological thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the effects of isolation on the human psyche. The movie follows two college students, Katie and Ben, who embark on a road trip to retrieve Katie's car from her estranged father in rural Minnesota.

As they navigate through the treacherous winter landscape, their relationship is put to the test, and they begin to experience strange and terrifying occurrences that blur the lines between reality and paranoia. The film masterfully builds tension by exploiting the characters' deep-seated fears and insecurities, creating an atmosphere of creeping dread that permeates every aspect of their journey.

At its core, Wind Chill explores the theme of vulnerability and how it can be exploited by those who seek to manipulate or harm others. Katie and Ben's relationship is built on a foundation of trust and mutual support, but as they face the harsh realities of their situation, they are forced to confront their own vulnerabilities and weaknesses.

The film also touches on the idea of isolation and how it can affect people in different ways. The rural setting serves as a character in its own right, with the vast expanse of snow-covered landscape seeming to close in on the characters like a vise. This sense of claustrophobia heightens the tension and creates an atmosphere of unease that is both unsettling and captivating.

Ultimately, Wind Chill is a film about the fragility of human relationships and the ways in which our deepest fears can be used against us. It's a gripping and unsettling thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

overview: Live-action feature film based on the popular line of Barbie dolls.
title: Barbie
plot:
Barbie is a 2023 fantasy comedy film directed by Greta Gerwig from a screenplay she wrote with her husband, Noah Baumbach. Based on Mattel's fashion dolls, it is the first live-action Barbie film, following numerous animated films and specials. Margot Robbie stars as Barbie and Ryan Gosling as Ken, with a supporting cast that includes America Ferrera, Michael Cera, Kate McKinnon, Issa Rae, Rhea Perlman and Will Ferrell.

A "stereotypical" Barbie lives in Barbieland, a matriarchal world born of human imagination, where the Barbies hold jobs in law, science, politics and the media while the Kens spend their days at the beach. During a dance party, Barbie is suddenly struck by thoughts of death, and overnight she develops bad breath, cellulite and flat feet. Weird Barbie, a disfigured doll, tells her that she must find the child playing with her in the real world. Barbie sets off, with Ken stowing away in her convertible. In Venice Beach, she is arrested after punching a man who gropes her, and both are arrested again for not paying for clothes. Barbie finds her supposed owner, the teenager Sasha, who scorns her for promoting unrealistic beauty standards, and learns that Sasha's mother, Mattel employee Gloria, caused her crisis by drawing Barbies with dark thoughts. Mattel tries to box Barbie up for remanufacturing, but an elderly woman named Ruth helps her escape, and Gloria and Sasha take her back to Barbieland. Ken, meanwhile, has discovered patriarchy and persuaded the Kens to take over, indoctrinating the Barbies into submissive roles. Barbie falls into despair until Gloria's speech about the contradictory expectations placed on women restores her confidence, and Gloria deprograms the Barbies, who turn the Kens against one another before they can change the constitution. Having learned from the experience, the Barbies resolve to treat the Kens and outcasts better, and Barbie encourages Ken to find his own identity. Meeting the spirit of Ruth Handler, Mattel's co-founder and Barbie's creator, Barbie chooses to become human, and later, as "Barbara Handler", she goes to her first gynecologist appointment.

Filmed at Warner Bros. Studios Leavesden and in Los Angeles in 2022, the film was released on 21 July 2023, alongside Oppenheimer in the "Barbenheimer" phenomenon. It grossed $1.448 billion, the highest of 2023, and earned eight Academy Award nominations, winning Best Original Song for "What Was I Made For?".

overview: Ulrich Mott  is an eccentric and versatile social climber with grandiose plans to affect United States foreign policy. Encouraged  in his attempts by his strategically chosen (and much older) wife, the well-connected journalist Elsa Brecht, Mott has a knack for making himself indispensable and impossible to ignore. The only one seemingly immune to his charms is Elsa's daughter Amanda, who might simply disapprove of her mother marrying a much younger man - or perhaps she senses something more sinister beneath the smooth-talking surface?
title: Georgetown
plot:
Georgetown is a 2019 American crime drama directed by Christoph Waltz in his feature directorial debut and written by David Auburn. It is based on Franklin Foer's 2012 New York Times Magazine article "The Worst Marriage in Georgetown", about the 2011 killing of 91-year-old socialite Viola Herms Drath by her much younger husband. Waltz stars as Ulrich Mott, with Vanessa Redgrave as Elsa Breht, Annette Bening as her daughter, Amanda.

Told out of sequence, the story follows Ulrich, a fifty-year-old conman and social climber interning for a congressman, using his boss's ID card to slip into a banquet, where he meets Elsa, a wealthy, elderly journalist and socialite living in Georgetown. Posing as a doctoral student, he arranges a lunch with her. After her husband dies, Elsa retreats from society, worrying Amanda, until Ulrich calls on the eve of 2000 and invites her to a concert. Amanda, delighted by her mother's renewed energy, announces she has been offered a tenured law professorship at Harvard and asks Elsa to move to Boston, but Elsa declines, and Ulrich tells the dismayed gathering that he and Elsa will marry.

Elsa uses her connections to advance Ulrich's one-man consulting agency, which he fills with prominent names through lies. In 2004, after Iraqi diplomats humiliatingly reject his offer to broker peace talks, he comes home drunk and nearly causes Elsa to fall down the stairs. She grows suspicious of his sexuality and, in 2006, finds him in bed with a man in a New York hotel; after he throws her out, she reports him to police for assault. Ulrich then vanishes for two years, claiming to be a freelance peace envoy in Iraq, and returns hailed as a diplomatic miracle worker. After an argument following a dinner party, he goes for a walk and later says he came home to find Elsa dead. Charged with murder, he hides key facts from his lawyers, then fires them, goes on a hunger strike and is hospitalized. An epilogue shows Ulrich being rebuffed by his former lover that night, then confronted by Elsa, who has discovered that he spent his absence as a motel desk clerk in Miami; as she calls him an idiot, he rushes up the stairs toward her.

Filmed in Toronto in 2017, Georgetown premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on April 27, 2019, and received a limited U.S. release from Vertical Entertainment on May 14, 2021. Reviews were mixed, at 63% on Rotten Tomatoes and 49 on Metacritic, with The New York Times calling Waltz a pleasure to watch.

overview: After fighting his way through an apartment building populated by an army of dangerous criminals and escaping with his life, SWAT team member Rama goes undercover, joining a powerful Indonesian crime syndicate to protect his family and uncover corrupt members of his own force.
tagline: It's not over yet.
title: The Raid 2
plot:
The Raid 2 (Indonesian title: The Raid 2: Berandal) is a 2014 Indonesian action thriller written, edited and directed by Welsh filmmaker Gareth Evans. A sequel to The Raid (2011), it brings back Iko Uwais as the tactical officer Rama, joined by Arifin Putra, Oka Antara, Tio Pakusadewo, Alex Abbad and Julie Estelle. As in Evans's earlier films, the fight scenes showcase the Indonesian martial art of pencak silat.

Hours after the first film, Rama brings his wounded colleague Bowo and the corrupt officer Wahyu to Lieutenant Bunawar, head of a secret unit investigating police corruption, who executes Wahyu and asks Rama to help expose the network of corrupt commissioner Reza. Rama refuses until he learns that his brother, Andi, has been killed by the rising gangster Bejo and that his own wife and son are in danger. To infiltrate the Bangun family, a crime syndicate that shares control of Jakarta with a Japanese yakuza clan led by Hideaki Gotō, Rama is sent to the same prison as Bangun's volatile son, Uco, and earns his trust by saving him during a riot. Rama then joins the family and, planting a bug in Uco's wallet, learns that the resentful Uco is secretly plotting with Bejo to provoke a war with the Gotō clan.

Bejo's assassins murder Bangun's loyal enforcer Prakoso and the killing is blamed on Gotō, but Bangun refuses to retaliate, and when Uco embarrasses him at a meeting with Gotō, Bangun cedes territory to keep the peace and later beats his son. Bejo's men then storm Bangun's office, where Uco kills his father and wounds Bangun's aide Eka. Rama, having just survived an ambush by Reza's officers, helps Eka escape but is captured and driven off to be killed; Eka rescues him and, dying, reveals that he too was an undercover officer, urging Rama to bring down the whole underworld. Learning that Reza has sided with Bejo and Uco, Gotō declares war on all three. Bunawar tells Rama that Reza is meeting the others at Bejo's restaurant, and Rama storms it alone. Uco, realizing he was manipulated, kills Reza and Bejo before Rama kills him. Badly hurt, Rama declines a deal from Gotō's son Keiichi, saying he is done.

Evans adapted it from Berandal, a 2009 script of his. The Raid 2 premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on 21 January 2014, and Sony Pictures Classics released it in North America on 28 March 2014. It sold more than 1.4 million tickets in Indonesia and earned about $6.8 million abroad. Critics praised it: 82% on Rotten Tomatoes and 71 on Metacritic.

overview: While attending a party at James Franco's house, Seth Rogen, Jay Baruchel and many other celebrities are faced with the apocalypse.
tagline: Nothing ruins a party like the end of the world.
title: This Is the End
plot:
This Is the End is a 2013 American apocalyptic comedy film directed by Evan Goldberg and Seth Rogen, written by Goldberg and Rogen, Jay Baruchel, and Bryan Callen, and starring James Franco, Jonah Hill, Craig Robinson, Danny McBride, and Seth Rogen.

The movie begins with Jay Baruchel's character, Evan, visiting his friend Seth Rogen's character, Jay Baruchel (also known as Jay), in Los Angeles. Jay is a successful actor who has just finished filming a movie, and he invites Evan to join him for the premiere of his film. However, things take a dark turn when Jay announces that he will be attending a party at James Franco's house, which is rumored to be haunted by the devil.

Jay convinces Evan to come with him to the party, despite Evan's reservations. When they arrive at the party, they are greeted by James Franco's character, Jay (also known as Jay), who is hosting a gathering of his friends, including Jonah Hill, Craig Robinson, and Danny McBride. The group spends the night drinking, smoking, and engaging in various forms of debauchery.

As the night wears on, the partygoers begin to experience strange and terrifying events, which they initially attribute to the devil's presence at the party. However, it becomes clear that the apocalypse is actually upon them, and the group must band together to survive the impending doom.

The movie takes a turn for the absurd when the group discovers that the apocalypse has come in the form of an alien invasion. The aliens, who are depicted as being obsessed with 80s music, begin to wreak havoc on the party, destroying everything in their path.

As the night descends into chaos, the group must use their wits and whatever resources they can find to survive the apocalypse. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including a possessed James Franco, who is determined to kill them all.

In the end, the group manages to escape the party and make their way to a safe haven, where they are able to ride out the apocalypse in safety. However, not before they have a series of hilarious and intense encounters with the aliens, which provide some of the movie's most memorable moments.

Throughout the movie, the cast plays themselves, and their characters' personalities and quirks are on full display. The movie is known for its raunchy humor, absurdity, and over-the-top performances from the cast.

Overall, This Is the End is a hilarious and action-packed comedy that explores themes of friendship, survival, and the apocalypse. With its talented cast and outrageous humor, it has become a cult classic among fans of comedy and horror movies.

overview: SIRIUS 6B, Year 2078. On a distant mining planet ravaged by a decade of war, scientists have created the perfect weapon: a blade-wielding, self-replicating race of killing devices known as Screamers designed for one purpose only -- to hunt down and destroy all enemy life forms.
tagline: The last scream you hear will be your own.
title: Screamers
plot:
Screamers is a 1995 science fiction horror film directed by Christian Duguay. The movie takes place on a remote space station where a team of scientists and engineers are sent to investigate an abandoned research facility. Upon arrival, they discover that the facility has been overrun by genetically engineered super-intelligent and aggressive creatures known as "Screamers".

The main theme of Screamers revolves around the dangers of playing God with genetic engineering and the consequences of scientific hubris. The film explores how the creation of life forms beyond human control can lead to catastrophic outcomes, highlighting the importance of responsible innovation and the need for caution when tampering with nature.

Furthermore, the movie delves into the theme of isolation and confinement, as the characters are trapped on the space station with no clear way to escape. This setting serves as a metaphor for the claustrophobic and suffocating feeling that can come from being cut off from the outside world, leading to increased paranoia and desperation among the characters.

The film also touches on the idea of humanity's relationship with technology, showcasing how even the most advanced scientific tools can be used against us if not handled properly. The Screamers themselves serve as a manifestation of this theme, representing the unpredictable and uncontrollable nature of technological advancements.

Overall, Screamers is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores the darker aspects of scientific progress and human ingenuity, leaving viewers with a sense of unease and caution when it comes to tampering with forces beyond our control.

overview: When a Miami dentist inherits a team of sled dogs, he's got to learn the trade or lose his pack to a crusty mountain man.
tagline: Get ready for mush hour!
title: Snow Dogs
plot:
Snow Dogs is a heartwarming family comedy that explores several endearing themes. At its core, the film revolves around the transformative power of friendship and community. The story follows a wealthy businessman who inherits a team of sled dogs from his late brother, forcing him to reevaluate his priorities and reconnect with his roots.

As our protagonist navigates this new chapter in his life, he discovers that the true value of these canine companions lies not only in their athletic prowess but also in the joy they bring to those around them. Through his interactions with the dogs and the people of the small Alaskan town where he's forced to settle, he learns the importance of embracing his inner child, letting go of his ego, and finding a sense of belonging.

The film also touches on themes of redemption, forgiveness, and second chances. Our protagonist is given a chance to redeem himself and make amends for past mistakes, not only with the dogs but also with those around him. As he works to restore the sled team to its former glory, he begins to heal old wounds and form new connections with the people in his life.

Ultimately, Snow Dogs is a feel-good movie that celebrates the beauty of friendship, community, and the healing power of nature. The film's lighthearted tone and adorable canine characters make it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: In this fully animated, all-new take on the Smurfs, a mysterious map sets Smurfette and her friends Brainy, Clumsy and Hefty on an exciting race through the Forbidden Forest leading to the discovery of the biggest secret in Smurf history.
title: Smurfs: The Lost Village
plot:
Smurfs: The Lost Village is a 2017 American computer-animated comedy-adventure film produced by Columbia Pictures Animation, and directed by Kelly Asbury. The movie follows the story of Smurfette, who was created by Gargamel to infiltrate and cause trouble for the Smurfs.

The film begins with Papa Smurf telling the story of how Smurfette was created by Gargamel using a magical potion that turns clay into living beings. However, when the potion is used on Smurfette, it also imbues her with human-like emotions and thoughts, making her different from the other Smurfs.

As the years pass, Smurfette becomes isolated and lonely, feeling like an outcast among her fellow Smurfs. She longs for friendship and acceptance but struggles to connect with them due to her unique nature. Meanwhile, Gargamel is searching for a way to break the curse that makes him vulnerable to the Smurfs' magic.

The story takes a turn when Smurfette sets out on a journey to find her true purpose in life. She meets a group of female warriors known as the "Forest Creatures," who are led by the fearless and skilled warrior, Katagaru. The Forest Creatures are on a quest to defeat the evil sorcerer, Malicia, who is threatening their forest home.

Smurfette joins forces with the Forest Creatures and together they embark on a perilous journey to stop Malicia and save their homes. Along the way, Smurfette discovers her own strength and courage, and begins to find her place among the other characters.

As the story unfolds, Smurfette and the Forest Creatures face numerous challenges and obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, ferocious creatures, and Gargamel's attempts to capture them. However, with their combined skills and determination, they are able to overcome these hurdles and draw closer to defeating Malicia.

In the end, Smurfette and the Forest Creatures successfully defeat Malicia, saving their homes and finding a sense of belonging and purpose. The movie concludes with Smurfette returning to the Smurfs' village, where she is welcomed back as one of their own. Papa Smurf reveals that he had been searching for her all along and is proud of the strong and confident Smurfette she has become.

Throughout the film, the characters undergo significant development, particularly Smurfette, who learns to accept herself and find her place among others. The movie features stunning animation, engaging humor, and a heartwarming story that celebrates friendship, acceptance, and self-discovery.

overview: Lyndon B. Johnson's amazing 11-month journey from taking office after JFK's assassination, through the fight to pass the 1964 Civil Rights Act and his own presidential campaign, culminating on the night LBJ is actually elected to the office – no longer the 'accidental President.'
tagline: Politics is war.
title: All the Way
plot:
All the Way is a 2016 American biographical drama television film about the first year of Lyndon B. Johnson's presidency, from his succession after the assassination of John F. Kennedy to his victory in the 1964 election. Directed by Jay Roach and adapted by Robert Schenkkan from his 2012 play, it stars Bryan Cranston, reprising his Broadway role as Johnson, with Melissa Leo as Lady Bird Johnson, Anthony Mackie as Martin Luther King Jr. and Frank Langella as Senator Richard Russell Jr. of Georgia.

In 1963, Johnson takes office after Kennedy's assassination, supported and advised by his wife, Lady Bird, and soon turns to passing the Civil Rights Act. King presses him to pass the bill without weakening amendments, while Southern Democrats led by Russell oppose it so fiercely that they threaten to abandon the party,. After the Gulf of Tonkin incident, wary of being outflanked by Republicans, he asks Congress for a resolution backing retaliation against North Vietnam.

Once the Civil Rights Act passes over a filibuster, Johnson campaigns against Barry Goldwater. Johnson orders J. Edgar Hoover to investigate the murders of civil rights workers Chaney, Goodman and Schwerner in Mississippi. At the Democratic National Convention in Atlantic City, Mississippi sends two rival delegations: the regular Dixiecrat delegation, which threatens to walk out, and the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party, backed by the civil rights movement. Johnson's compromise pleases neither side. Though he attacks Goldwater as a dangerous fanatic, Johnson remains anxious, especially when his aide and friend Walter Jenkins is arrested after a sexual encounter with a man in a public restroom. King wins the Nobel Peace Prize, and Hoover, still distrustful, sends him an anonymous letter urging him to kill himself, which King ignores. Johnson wins decisively but loses the Deep South, and after a phone call with Russell he closes with a paranoid monologue about those around him.

HBO Films acquired the rights in 2014, with Steven Spielberg producing, and Schenkkan reimagined the play cinematically rather than simply filming it. Broadcast on HBO on May 21, 2016, the film earned strong reviews, with 85% on Rotten Tomatoes and 78 on Metacritic. It received eight Primetime Emmy nominations, including Outstanding Television Movie and acting nods for Cranston and Leo.

overview: Married small-time crooks Lou-Jean and Clovis Poplin lose their baby to the state of Texas and resolve to do whatever it takes to get him back. Lou-Jean gets Clovis out of jail, and the two steal their son from his foster home, in addition to taking a highway patrolman hostage. As a massive dragnet starts to pursue them across Texas, the couple become unlikely folk heroes and even start to bond with the captive policeman.
tagline: Every cop in the state was after her. Everybody else was behind her.
title: The Sugarland Express
plot:
The Sugarland Express is an American crime drama of 1974 and Steven Spielberg's first theatrical feature as director, following his television film Duel. Hal Barwood and Matthew Robbins wrote the screenplay from a story they developed with Spielberg. Based on real events, it stars Goldie Hawn as Lou Jean Poplin and William Atherton as her husband Clovis, who take a state trooper hostage and flee across Texas to reclaim their child, with Michael Sacks as the trooper Maxwell Slide and Ben Johnson as Captain Tanner. It began his partnership with John Williams.

In April 1969, Lou Jean visits Clovis in prison to tell him that their young son is about to be placed with foster parents. Although he is only four months from release, she persuades him to escape and help her get the boy back. The pair hitch a ride away from the prison with a couple, but when Patrolman Slide of the Texas Department of Public Safety pulls the car over, they make off in it. After the car crashes, they overpower Slide and take him hostage in his own patrol car.

What follows is a slow-moving chase across Texas, with the fugitives and their captive at the head of an ever-growing convoy, first of police cars and later of news vans, helicopters and ordinary citizens who join in. Holding Slide allows the couple to keep refueling and to obtain food and supplies, some from sympathetic locals, and over the long journey the three come to like and respect one another. When the trio stop at a used car lot to commandeer a camper, local vigilantes attack them, but Tanner lets the Poplins drive on after further bargaining.

When they reach Sugarland, Tanner urges Clovis to give himself up, but he refuses. Slide, and then Clovis, sense that something is wrong at the foster parents' house, yet Lou Jean insists that her husband go in for their son. Two Texas Rangers shoot Clovis, mortally wounding him, and after a further chase Lou Jean is arrested; Slide is found unharmed. A closing epilogue explains that Lou Jean served fifteen months of a five-year sentence and later won the right to live with her son.

Parts of the film were shot in Sugar Land, where some of the real events took place, and around San Antonio and other Texas towns. It won the award for Best Screenplay at the 1974 Cannes Film Festival and drew positive reviews, but with a worldwide gross of about $12 million it remains the lowest-grossing film of Spielberg's career, and Universal pulled it from theaters after two weeks.

overview: Two years into the pandemic, a group of friends throw an online party with a night of games, drinking and drugs. After taking an ecstasy pill, things go terribly wrong and the safety of their home becomes more terrifying than the raging chaos outside.
tagline: Isolation is a killer.
title: Safer at Home
plot:
Safer at Home is a 2020 American romantic comedy film directed by Chris Renz and written by Chris Renz and Brian Duffield. The movie was released on Netflix in 2021.

The story revolves around Mike (played by Mike Epps), a man who has been living with his wife, Beth (played by Kristin Davis), for over 20 years. They have two children together but are now empty nesters. After Beth's mother passes away, she leaves behind a large inheritance that includes a house in the countryside.

Mike and Beth decide to leave their city life behind and move to the country to start a new chapter in their lives. However, things take an unexpected turn when they discover that the house is infested with raccoons. The couple must navigate this challenge while also dealing with their own relationship issues and learning to adapt to their new life together.

As Mike tries to find ways to evict the raccoons from the house, he begins to reconnect with Beth on a deeper level. They start to rekindle their romance and rediscover the things that brought them together in the first place. Along the way, they also learn valuable lessons about communication, trust, and compromise.

Throughout the movie, Mike's character undergoes significant development as he learns to let go of his insecurities and become more confident in himself. He also becomes more patient and understanding, which helps him to better connect with Beth.

The ending of the movie is heartwarming and uplifting, as Mike and Beth finally find a sense of peace and happiness together. They learn to appreciate the simple things in life and find joy in each other's company once again.

Overall, Safer at Home is a charming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, relationships, and personal growth. The movie features strong performances from its leads, Mike Epps and Kristin Davis, and offers plenty of laughs and heartwarming moments along the way.

original_title: Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason
overview: Bridget Jones is becoming uncomfortable in her relationship with Mark Darcy. Apart from discovering that he's a conservative voter, she has to deal with a new boss, a strange contractor and the worst vacation of her life.
tagline: Same Bridget. Brand new diary.
title: Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason
plot:
Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason is a romantic comedy of 2004 directed by Beeban Kidron and written by Andrew Davies, Helen Fielding, Richard Curtis and Adam Brooks, based on Fielding's 1999 novel and serving as the sequel to Bridget Jones's Diary (2001). Renée Zellweger returns as Bridget, with Colin Firth as her boyfriend Mark Darcy, Hugh Grant as her former lover Daniel Cleaver, and Jim Broadbent and Gemma Jones as her parents.

Bridget is blissful in her new relationship with Mark, until she meets his young and beautiful assistant, Rebecca Gillies, and her confidence collapses. At work in morning television, she reluctantly agrees to co-host a travel series with Daniel. Hoping for a proposal, she attends a Law Council dinner with Mark that becomes a string of humiliations. After a row, Mark comes to her flat to apologize, tells her for the first time that he loves her and takes her skiing in Lech, Austria, where Rebecca also turns up. A pregnancy scare proves negative.

At a lunch with their parents, Mark's brush-off of questions about marriage wounds Bridget, and when he declines to answer her suspicions about a phone message from Rebecca, she ends the relationship. She heads to Thailand with her friend Shazza and Daniel to film the travel show. After accidentally eating hallucinogenic mushrooms, she grows flirtatious with Daniel again, but the arrival of a prostitute he had ordered convinces her he has not changed. Shazza's young fling, Jed, gives her a decorative snake bowl that ends up in Bridget's luggage, and when airport sniffer dogs find cocaine hidden inside, Bridget is thrown into a crowded cell. She befriends her cellmates, teaching them Madonna's "Like a Virgin". Mark arrives to tell her she will soon be free, but when she lets him believe she slept with Daniel, he coolly leaves.

Back in London, Mark brawls with Daniel in a fountain for abandoning Bridget, and Bridget returns home a minor celebrity. Her friends reveal that Mark personally tracked down Jed and secured the confession that cleared her. Rushing to his house, she finds Rebecca there, but Rebecca confesses that she is attracted to Bridget herself and kisses her; Bridget gently declines. Bridget asks Mark for another chance, and he proposes. At her parents' renewal of their vows, she catches the bouquet.

Shot in London and Austria between October 2003 and February 2004, the film grossed about $265 million worldwide, though critics found it predictable.

overview: A mysterious new villain known only as Hush uses a gallery of villains to destroy Batman's crime-fighting career as well as Bruce Wayne's personal life, which has been further complicated by a relationship with Selina Kyle/Catwoman.
tagline: Trust, betrayal...and death.
title: Batman: Hush
plot:
Batman: Hush is a 2019 animated superhero film based on the DC Comics storyline of the same name. The movie follows Bruce Wayne, aka Batman, as he faces off against a mysterious villain known as Hush.

The main themes of Batman: Hush include:

1. Identity and Deception: The film explores the theme of identity and deception through the character of Hush, who is revealed to be Thomas Elliot, a childhood friend of Bruce Wayne's. Hush uses his knowledge of Bruce's past and his own traumatic experiences to manipulate him and create chaos in Gotham City.

2. Trauma and PTSD: The movie delves into the theme of trauma and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) through Bruce Wayne's character. His experiences as a child, including witnessing his parents' murder, have left emotional scars that continue to haunt him as an adult.

3. Guilt and Redemption: As Batman struggles with Hush's manipulation, he is forced to confront his own guilt over not being able to protect his parents or prevent their death. The film suggests that redemption may be possible through self-sacrifice and a willingness to face one's demons.

4. Loyalty and Betrayal: The movie explores the theme of loyalty and betrayal through the relationships between Bruce Wayne, Alfred Pennyworth, and Commissioner James Gordon. Hush's actions test these bonds and force Batman to confront the consequences of his own decisions.

5. Corruption and Power: The film touches on the theme of corruption and power through the character of Hush, who uses his intelligence and cunning to manipulate others and gain control over Gotham City. This serves as a commentary on the dangers of unchecked power and the corrupting influence it can have on individuals.

Overall, Batman: Hush offers a complex and thought-provoking exploration of these themes, adding depth and nuance to the character of Bruce Wayne and the world of Batman.

overview: Susan Murphy (a.k.a. Ginormica) and the Monsters are now working with the US government as special ops. So when an alien presence is detected in Susan's hometown of Modesto, California -- right before Halloween -- the team is dispatched to investigate. Everything appears normal, right down to the jack-o-lanterns peering out from every doorstep and windowsill. But when Halloween arrives, those innocent-looking carved pumpkins reveal themselves for what they really are mutant aliens. The altered pumpkins then start to implement their fiendish plan to take over Earth. The Monsters are there to combat the mutant gourds and try to smash their wicked scheme!
title: Mutant Pumpkins from Outer Space
plot:
Monsters vs. Aliens: Mutant Pumpkins from Outer Space is an animated Halloween television special of 2010 from DreamWorks Animation, based on the Monsters vs. Aliens franchise and directed by Peter Ramsey in his directing debut. The voice cast returns, with Reese Witherspoon as Susan Murphy, also known as Ginormica, Seth Rogen as B.O.B., Hugh Laurie as Dr. Cockroach, Will Arnett as the Missing Link and Kiefer Sutherland as General Monger, joined by Rainn Wilson as the villainous pumpkin Wicked Jack and Jeffrey Tambor and Julie White as Susan's parents. It premiered on RTÉ One in Ireland on 26 October 2010 and on NBC in the United States two days later.

One night a UFO drops a strange green goo onto a pumpkin field, and Farmer Jeb, going out to investigate, is seized by something among the pumpkins. On Halloween, Susan and her friends prepare to celebrate, except Dr. Cockroach, who hates the holiday because bullies once stole his favorite candy, a swirly pop. General Monger then reports aliens in Modesto, California, and sends the team to investigate. Meanwhile Jeb's pumpkins are being given away for free, and one family takes home the biggest, which their son names Wicked Jack.

While Susan checks the pumpkin patch, the others search the suburbs: Cockroach scans passersby, Link fails to frighten anyone and B.O.B. forgets what to say at each door, until an old lady's gift of a swirly pop rekindles Cockroach's love of the holiday. Susan finds the captive Jeb and learns that the goo has brought the pumpkins to life. As they attack trick-or-treaters, the monsters defend the children and discover that the creatures grow by eating candy. Led by a now giant Wicked Jack, the pumpkin army marches on the Murphy house, where Jack fuses with the others into an even larger monster.

Noticing B.O.B.'s indigestion after gorging on sweets, Cockroach plans to overfeed the pumpkins. While Susan distracts Jack, the children, backed by Link and a candy-firing Gatling platform, carry it out, and Cockroach sacrifices his swirly pop as the last ammunition. Susan knocks Jack's head off and Insectosaurus finishes him; Cockroach gives his swirly pop to a little girl, and Susan's parents accept sharing her with the world. In a final twist, goo from a stray pumpkin creates a mutant carrot.

The special came out on DVD in the United Kingdom in September 2010 and in the United States in 2011, and was followed by the short sequel Night of the Living Carrots.

overview: Dr. Lily Houghton enlists the aid of wisecracking skipper Frank Wolff to take her down the Amazon in his dilapidated boat. Together, they search for an ancient tree that holds the power to heal – a discovery that will change the future of medicine.
title: Jungle Cruise
plot:
Jungle Cruise is a 2021 American adventure comedy film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie is based on the classic theme park attraction of the same name, which has been entertaining audiences since 1967.

The story follows Dr. Lily Houghton (Emily Blunt), a brilliant and determined botanist who embarks on an expedition to find the legendary plant, "Shrubs," which is said to have healing properties that can cure any disease. According to legend, the plant only blooms once every 100 years, and its location is hidden deep within the Amazon rainforest.

Lily's quest becomes a mission when she meets Frank Wolff (Dwayne Johnson), a rough-around-the-edges but charismatic boat captain who has been hired by her father, Captain William Houghton (Jemaine Clement), to take her on a journey through the treacherous waters of the jungle. However, Frank is not just any ordinary boat captain; he's also a skilled fighter and survivalist with a troubled past.

As they navigate through the jungle, Lily and Frank encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and rival treasure hunters. Along the way, they develop a banter-filled relationship that gradually turns into a deep affection for each other.

However, their journey is not without its challenges. They soon discover that they are not alone in their quest for the "Shrubs." A ruthless corporation, led by Captain K. Miller (Rafael de la Fuente), is also on the hunt, and they will stop at nothing to get their hands on the plant.

As Lily and Frank draw closer to their goal, they must confront their own demons and work together to overcome the dangers that lie ahead. In the process, they learn valuable lessons about trust, loyalty, and the importance of preserving the natural world.

The movie features stunning visuals, heart-pumping action sequences, and a healthy dose of humor, making it an entertaining ride for audiences of all ages. The chemistry between Emily Blunt and Dwayne Johnson is undeniable, and their characters' banter adds a delightful layer to the story.

In the end, Lily and Frank successfully find the "Shrubs," but not without sacrifices. They must confront the consequences of their actions and decide what's truly important: personal gain or preserving the natural world for future generations.

Overall, Jungle Cruise is an exciting adventure that combines humor, action, and heart, making it a fun and thrilling ride for audiences.

overview: A Texan traveling across the wild West bringing the news of the world to local townspeople, agrees to help rescue a young girl who was kidnapped.
tagline: Find where you belong.
title: News of the World
plot:
News of the World is a 2020 American Western drama film directed by Paul Greengrass and written by Bong Joon-ho and Peter Craig, based on the 2016 novel "News of the World" by Paulette Jiles.

The main themes of News of the World include:

1. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: The protagonist, Captain Jefferson Kyle Kidd (played by Tom Hanks), is a traveling news reader who has lost his way after the death of his wife. Through his journey with the young girl, Johanna (played by Scarlett Johansson), he finds redemption and learns to care for someone other than himself.

2. **Loneliness and Human Connection**: The film highlights the importance of human connection in overcoming loneliness. Captain Kidd's relationship with Johanna helps him to confront his past and find a new sense of purpose.

3. **Racism and Prejudice**: Set against the backdrop of post-Civil War America, News of the World explores themes of racism and prejudice. The film critiques the treatment of Native Americans by white settlers and highlights the injustices faced by indigenous communities.

4. **Empowerment and Independence**: Johanna's journey from being a captive to becoming an independent individual is a powerful symbol of empowerment. Her growth serves as a catalyst for Captain Kidd's transformation, illustrating that personal growth often requires letting go of past traumas.

5. **The Power of Storytelling**: News of the World celebrates the power of storytelling and its ability to bring people together. Through his news readings, Captain Kidd connects with communities and shares their stories, fostering understanding and empathy.

Overall, News of the World is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes through its engaging narrative and memorable characters.

overview: It is 1967, and Larry Gopnik, a physics professor at a quiet Midwestern university, has just been informed by his wife Judith that she is leaving him. She has fallen in love with one of his more pompous acquaintances Sy Ableman.
tagline: …seriously!
title: A Serious Man
plot:
A Serious Man is a 2009 American black comedy-drama written, produced, edited and directed by Joel and Ethan Coen. Set in 1967 in the Jewish suburbs of Minnesota, it stars Michael Stuhlbarg as Larry Gopnik, with Richard Kind as his brother Arthur, Fred Melamed as Sy Ableman, Sari Lennick as his wife Judith, Aaron Wolff as his son Danny and Amy Landecker as the neighbor Vivienne Samsky.

The film opens with a Yiddish folktale prologue set in a nineteenth-century shtetl, in which a wife stabs a visitor she believes to be a dybbuk. In 1967 Larry, a physics professor in St. Louis Park, sees his life unravel at once. Judith wants a ritual divorce so that she can marry the widower Sy; his son owes a classmate $20 for marijuana, but the money is hidden in a radio his teacher confiscated; his daughter avoids school; and his homeless brother Arthur sleeps on the couch while filling a notebook with a "probability map of the universe". A failing South Korean student leaves an envelope of cash in his office, and the student's father threatens to sue whether Larry returns it or not, while anonymous letters urge the tenure committee to reject him.

Pushed out to a motel with Arthur and left penniless when Judith empties their account, Larry seeks guidance from a succession of rabbis, receiving advice about perspective and a baffling story about Hebrew letters found on a patient's teeth, while the senior rabbi will not see him. Sy dies in a car crash, Larry ends up paying for the funeral, and Arthur is charged with gambling and solicitation. After his son's bar mitzvah, things briefly seem to improve: Judith reveals that Sy had written the letters, and tenure appears within reach. But when Larry quietly changes the student's grade, his doctor calls about an X-ray, and a tornado bears down on Danny's school.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival and opened in limited release in October 2009. It was widely acclaimed, holding an 89% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a score of 85 on Metacritic, and Roger Ebert gave it four stars. It was nominated for the Academy Awards for Best Picture and Best Original Screenplay, Stuhlbarg received a Golden Globe nomination, and it grossed about $31 million worldwide. It is now often counted among the Coens' finest work.

overview: A young widow discovers that her late husband has left her 10 messages intended to help ease her pain and start a new life.
tagline: His life ended. Now, a new one will begin.
title: P.S. I Love You
plot:
P.S. I Love You is a 2007 romantic drama film directed by Richard LaGravenese, produced by Debra Hill and Bruce Cohen, and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The movie tells the story of Holly Kennedy (played by Hilary Swank), a young widow who struggles to cope with the loss of her husband, Gerry (played by Gerard Butler). After his death, Holly receives a series of letters and tasks from Gerry, designed to help her move on with her life and find love again.

The main themes of P.S. I Love You include:

1. **Grief and Loss**: The film explores the intense emotional pain of losing a loved one, and the struggle to come to terms with the loss.
2. **Love and Relationships**: The movie highlights the complexities of romantic relationships, the importance of communication, and the need for intimacy in a relationship.
3. **Self-Discovery**: Through her journey, Holly learns to rediscover herself, her passions, and her sense of purpose, which helps her heal and move forward.
4. **Mourning and Letting Go**: The film shows how Holly must learn to let go of the past and find a way to honor Gerry's memory while moving on with her life.

The movie features a poignant performance by Hilary Swank as Holly Kennedy, who brings depth and nuance to the character. Gerard Butler also delivers a memorable performance as Gerry, making their on-screen relationship all the more believable and heart-wrenching.

Overall, P.S. I Love You is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of love, loss, and self-discovery, leaving audiences with a sense of hope and renewal.

overview: Top secret government experiments with time travel have been shut down and declared as too dangerous to continue. The lead scientist has disappeared with the technology and a government manhunt is underway. When his name appears on an airline manifest after the flight has departed, the government orders the plane to turn back. But the plane drops from the radar, disappearing into thin air! As special agents try to locate the plane, scientists must deal with the repercussions from the time ripples that threaten to destroy the Earth.
tagline: Their only Hope is to Turn Back Time
title: Termination Point
plot:
Termination Point is a 2007 Canadian science fiction action thriller made for television, directed by Jason Bourque from a screenplay by Peter Sullivan and produced by Insight Film Studios with CineTel Films. It stars Jason Priestley as federal agent Caleb Smith and Lou Diamond Phillips as Dr. Daniel Winter, a scientist who has vanished with a secret government device.

Top-secret government experiments in teleportation and time travel have been shut down as too dangerous, and their lead scientist, Winter, has disappeared with the technology, a portable teleporter that opens a wormhole through space and time and had previously been tested only on small animals such as mice. A passenger jet crashes in the American Midwest with no survivors, yet investigators discover that the aircraft, Flight 507 to Mexico, is not due to depart until the following day: it has apparently travelled into the past. When Winter's name turns up on the flight's manifest, the government orders the plane turned back and, to protect the project, the President authorises fighter jets to shoot it down, despite the pleas of Caleb, whose wife Claire and daughter Sarah are on board for a holiday.

At the last moment Winter activates the device by remote control and the plane vanishes into another dimension; only the passengers closest to the teleporter survive the jump. Aboard, the corrupt agent David Martin and his accomplice Liam take the survivors hostage and try to force Winter to send the aircraft back to coordinates of their choosing. On the ground, Caleb tracks down Winter's girlfriend and recovers a second remote hidden in her house, while the open wormhole spawns a swelling vortex in the sky whose lightning makes helicopters, buildings and people disappear, and which scientists warn will destroy the universe unless it is closed. Sarah restores the failing teleporter's power, and Caleb opens a wormhole of his own to reach the plane. In the ensuing struggle Claire is killed, Liam is struck by the lightning and Martin is thrown from the fuselage, before Caleb sends the plane back to the moment before Flight 507 took off. Forewarned by a photograph he sends to his own phone, he has Winter and the two conspirators arrested before departure.

The cast also includes Stefanie von Pfetten as Claire, Ashley Whillans as Sarah, Gary Hudson as Martin, Michael Eklund as Liam, Garwin Sanford and Erin Karpluk. The film premiered on German television on RTL II in March 2009.

overview: A wealthy New York investment banking executive hides his alternate psychopathic ego from his co-workers and friends as he escalates deeper into his illogical, gratuitous fantasies.
tagline: I think my mask of sanity is about to slip.
title: American Psycho
plot:
American Psycho is a psychological thriller film directed by Mary Harron, released in 2000 by Lionsgate. The movie is an adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis's 1991 novel of the same name.

The film begins with Patrick Bateman (played by Christian Bale), a wealthy investment banker living in New York City in the late 1980s. On the surface, Patrick appears to be a successful and charismatic individual, but beneath his polished exterior lies a complex web of insecurities and dark impulses.

As the story unfolds, we see Patrick's life as a series of superficial social interactions, where he navigates the cutthroat world of finance with ease. However, these scenes are juxtaposed with Patrick's inner monologues, which reveal his deep-seated feelings of inadequacy and jealousy towards those around him.

Patrick's obsession with material possessions and status symbols is evident in his lavish lifestyle, but beneath this façade lies a growing sense of disconnection from reality. He becomes increasingly fixated on the idea of being a serial killer, using his wealth and influence to lure victims into his trap.

Throughout the film, Patrick's relationships with those around him are portrayed as shallow and transactional. His girlfriend, Evelyn (played by Reese Witherspoon), is depicted as a trophy wife who is more concerned with her own social status than with genuinely connecting with Patrick. Similarly, his colleagues at Pierce & Pierce, a prestigious investment firm, are shown to be ruthless and competitive, fueling Patrick's growing sense of resentment.

As the story reaches its climax, Patrick's dark impulses become increasingly difficult to contain. He begins to murder a series of people, including his business rivals, his mistress, and even his own doppelganger. The film's final act is marked by a surreal and unsettling sequence of events, as Patrick's perceptions of reality begin to blur.

Ultimately, the film raises questions about the nature of identity and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. Is Patrick truly a serial killer, or is he simply a product of his own twisted imagination? The film's ambiguous ending leaves the audience questioning what is real and what is just a manifestation of Patrick's inner turmoil.

Throughout its runtime, American Psycho features a blend of dark humor, satire, and social commentary, critiquing the excesses of 1980s yuppie culture. Christian Bale's performance as Patrick Bateman is widely regarded as one of the most iconic roles in recent cinema history, earning him critical acclaim for his portrayal of the complex and troubled protagonist.

Overall, American Psycho is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores the darker aspects of human nature. With its blend of dark humor, satire, and social commentary, it has become a cult classic, continuing to fascinate audiences with its exploration of identity, reality, and the blurred lines between them.

overview: A student tries to fix a problem he accidentally caused in OZ, a digital world, while pretending to be the fiancé of his friend at her grandmother's 90th birthday.
tagline: Always protect your network.
title: Summer Wars
plot:
Summer Wars is a 2009 Japanese animated science fiction film directed by Mamoru Hosoda. The movie follows the story of Konno Shoko, an 11-year-old girl who becomes involved in her father's online gaming world and must use his skills to save the world from a catastrophic virus.

The main themes of Summer Wars include:

1. **Family and Relationships**: The film explores the complex relationships between family members, particularly between Shoko and her father, Kazuo. Their bond is put to the test as Shoko navigates her father's online gaming world and confronts his past.
2. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As Shoko delves deeper into her father's virtual world, she begins to understand more about herself and her place in the world. She learns to balance her own identity with her connection to her father's online persona.
3. **Loneliness and Isolation**: The movie highlights the consequences of social isolation and loneliness, particularly in the context of modern technology. Shoko's father is a recluse who has become increasingly isolated from society, leading to his emotional detachment from his daughter.
4. **Gaming Culture and Addiction**: Summer Wars critiques the gaming culture and the potential risks associated with excessive gaming. The film portrays the darker side of online gaming addiction and its impact on individuals and relationships.
5. **Coming-of-Age and Maturity**: Through Shoko's journey, the movie explores themes of growing up, maturity, and responsibility. As she navigates her father's virtual world, she learns valuable lessons about life, love, and the importance of human connection.

Overall, Summer Wars is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes through its engaging storyline and memorable characters.
