overview: A salesman for a natural gas company experiences life-changing events after arriving in a small town, where his corporation wants to tap into the available resources.
tagline: What's your price?
title: Promised Land
plot:
Promised Land is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of human relationships and the consequences of one's actions. The film revolves around the story of George, a charismatic oil executive who travels across rural America to sell natural gas to small towns, often using his charm and persuasive abilities to win over the locals.

As George navigates through these communities, he forms connections with the people he meets, including a young couple, Julia and Luke, who become entangled in his world. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that George's intentions are not entirely altruistic, and his actions have far-reaching consequences for those around him.

One of the primary themes of Promised Land is the exploration of the human condition, particularly in relation to relationships and trust. The film raises questions about the nature of intimacy, loyalty, and deception, highlighting the complexities of human interaction and the ease with which people can be manipulated or used.

The movie also touches on the theme of power dynamics, as George's influence over others is both a blessing and a curse. His ability to charm and persuade those around him serves as a double-edged sword, allowing him to achieve his goals but also leaving a trail of emotional scars in his wake.

Furthermore, Promised Land critiques the notion of small-town America, revealing the darker underbelly of seemingly idyllic communities. The film exposes the tensions between tradition and progress, highlighting the difficulties faced by those who are caught between preserving their way of life and embracing modernity.

Ultimately, Promised Land is a nuanced exploration of human relationships, power dynamics, and the consequences of one's actions. Through its thought-provoking narrative, the film invites viewers to reflect on their own values and the complexities of human interaction.

overview: A married workaholic, Michael Newman doesn't have time for his wife and children, not if he's to impress his ungrateful boss and earn a well-deserved promotion. So when he meets Morty, a loopy sales clerk, he gets the answer to his prayers: a magical remote that allows him to bypass life's little distractions with increasingly hysterical results.
tagline: What If You Had A Remote... That Controlled Your Universe?
title: Click
plot:
Click is a 2006 American fantasy comedy film directed by Frank Coraci and produced by Adam Sandler Productions. The movie stars Adam Sandler, Kate Beckinsale, Christopher Walken, and Rosario Dawson.

The story revolves around Michael Newman (played by Adam Sandler), a workaholic advertising executive who feels unfulfilled with his life. He is married to Donna (played by Kate Beckinsale) and has two children, Charlie (played by Logan Lerman) and Sarah (played by Cole Hawkins). Michael's job requires him to constantly be on the go, and he often neglects his family in the process.

One day, while working late at the office, Michael meets a mysterious door-to-door salesman named Morty (played by Christopher Walken), who sells him an "Universal Remote Control" that can control not only his TV but also his life. The remote has the power to fast-forward through time, allowing Michael to skip over mundane tasks and experiences.

Initially, Michael uses the remote to speed up his daily routine, skipping over boring meetings, traffic jams, and other tedious activities. However, he soon discovers that the remote's power comes with a price: every time he uses it, he loses a year of his life. The more he uses the remote, the younger he becomes.

As Michael struggles to cope with the consequences of his newfound power, he begins to reevaluate his priorities and relationships. He starts to appreciate the small moments in life and reconnects with his family. However, Morty's true intentions are revealed: he is a collector of souls, and Michael has become his latest acquisition.

In a desperate attempt to break free from Morty's control, Michael must find a way to reverse the effects of the remote and reclaim his life. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about the importance of family, friendship, and living in the present moment.

The movie culminates with Michael using the remote one last time to fast-forward through the final year of his life, allowing him to spend quality time with his loved ones and make amends for past mistakes. In the end, Michael is able to break free from Morty's control and find a sense of peace and fulfillment.

Overall, Click is a heartwarming story about the importance of living in the present moment and appreciating the little things in life. The movie features a talented cast, witty dialogue, and a unique blend of humor and drama that makes it a must-see for fans of Adam Sandler and fantasy comedies.

overview: In a time of starvation, a survivalist lives off a small plot of land hidden deep in forest. When two women seeking food and shelter discover his farm, he finds his existence threatened.
tagline: Every Stranger Is The Enemy
title: The Survivalist
plot:
The Survivalist is a 2015 Irish post-apocalyptic drama film directed by Stephen Fingleton. The movie follows the story of a lone survivor, known only as "The Survivalist", who lives in a remote cabin in rural Ireland after an unspecified global catastrophe.

At its core, The Survivalist explores themes of isolation, loneliness, and the human need for connection. The protagonist's solitary existence is a result of his own making, driven by a desire to protect himself from the dangers that lurk outside his cabin. However, as the film progresses, it becomes clear that this self-imposed isolation has also led to a deep sense of disconnection from humanity.

The movie delves into the psychological effects of living in a world without rules or social norms, where survival is the only priority. The Survivalist's actions are guided by a strict moral code, which he adheres to with rigid discipline, but this code also serves as a barrier to forming meaningful relationships with others.

One of the most striking aspects of The Survivalist is its exploration of the human condition in the face of catastrophic collapse. The film raises questions about what it means to be human when the very fabric of society has been torn apart. Is survival enough, or do we need more than just physical existence to truly live?

The movie's atmosphere is tense and foreboding, with a sense of unease that permeates every scene. This tension is expertly crafted by Fingleton's direction, which creates a sense of claustrophobia and vulnerability, drawing the viewer into The Survivalist's isolated world.

Ultimately, The Survivalist is a thought-provoking film that challenges its audience to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of our actions in a world without rules.

overview: Washington, D.C. psychologist Carol Bennell and her colleague Dr. Ben Driscoll are the only two people on Earth who are aware of an epidemic running rampant through the city. They discover an alien virus aboard a crashed space shuttle that transforms anyone who comes into contact with it into unfeeling drones while they sleep. Carol realizes her son holds the key to stopping the spread of the plague and she races to find him before it is too late.
tagline: Do not trust anyone. Do not show emotion. Do not fall asleep.
title: The Invasion
plot:
The Invasion is a 2007 American science fiction horror film directed by Oliver Hirschbiegel and starring Nicole Kidman, Daniel Craig, and Kerry Washington.

The main themes of The Invasion include:

1. **Paranoia and Isolation**: The film explores the theme of paranoia and isolation as the protagonist, Sarah Hardesty (Nicole Kidman), becomes increasingly convinced that her husband, Jim (Daniel Craig), is being controlled by an alien entity.
2. **Marital Tension and Trust**: The movie highlights the tension and mistrust between Sarah and Jim, which escalates as Sarah's paranoia grows. This theme is a classic trope in horror movies, where the couple's relationship is put to the test by external forces.
3. **The Dangers of Unchecked Emotions**: As Sarah's anxiety and fear intensify, she becomes increasingly detached from reality, leading her to make irrational decisions that put herself and others at risk. This theme serves as a warning about the dangers of allowing emotions to consume us without rational consideration.
4. **The Blurring of Reality and Fantasy**: The film's use of special effects creates a sense of ambiguity, making it difficult for the audience to distinguish between what is real and what is just Sarah's paranoia. This blurs the lines between reality and fantasy, adding to the overall sense of unease and tension.
5. **The Isolation of Modern Life**: The movie touches on the theme of modern life being isolating, with people increasingly disconnected from each other and themselves. Sarah's growing paranoia serves as a metaphor for the feelings of disconnection and loneliness that can come with urban living.

Overall, The Invasion is a tense, psychological thriller that explores themes of paranoia, isolation, marital tension, and the dangers of unchecked emotions, all set against a backdrop of sci-fi horror elements.

overview: Born free in the American West, Black Beauty is a horse rounded up and brought to Birtwick Stables, where she meets spirited teenager Jo Green. The two forge a bond that carries Beauty through the different chapters, challenges and adventures.
tagline: Find your way home.
title: Black Beauty
plot:
Black Beauty is a 2020 family adventure drama film written, edited and directed by Ashley Avis, the sixth screen adaptation of Anna Sewell's 1877 novel. A co-production between the United States, the United Kingdom, South Africa, France and Germany, it recasts the title horse as a mare. Kate Winslet voices Black Beauty, with Mackenzie Foy as Jo Green, Iain Glen as her uncle John Manly, Calam Lynch as George Winthorp, Fern Deacon as his sister Georgina and Claire Forlani as their mother.

A wild mustang born in Utah's Onaqui Mountains narrates her life, remembering her mother's lesson that horses who die fly up to rest among the stars. Cowboys round up her herd, and she is bought by John Manly, a patient trainer who takes her to Birtwick, a horse sanctuary, where she befriends the horses Ginger and Merrylegs. When John's sister and her husband die in a car accident, he takes in his grieving teenage niece, Jo. Jo shuns her uncle but is drawn to the defiant mustang; recognizing each other's pain, the two bond, and Jo tames her and names her Black Beauty, learning to "partner" rather than "break" a horse. After a stable fire, with Birtwick losing money, Jo works extra hours to save up to buy Beauty. The wealthy Winthorps lease Beauty for their daughter Georgina, who treats her cruelly, while their kind son George, who rides Ginger, takes an interest in Jo. Georgina's reckless riding in a race injures Beauty, and the horse is returned, but Birtwick soon closes and Beauty is sold before Jo can say goodbye. Beauty passes from a ranger, Terry, to a farmer who works her hard and then to a kindly New York carriage driver, Jerry. She briefly reunites with Ginger, who dies soon afterwards. When Jerry falls ill, Beauty is sold to a cruel carriage company involved in illegal horse trading, and after glimpsing Ginger's body being carted away, she sits down in the road in grief, drawing media attention. A stable boy, Manuel, reports the company to the police, and Jo, who has searched for her all along, finds her. Jo has rebuilt Birtwick with John and George, now her husband, to rehabilitate horses, and Beauty spends the rest of her life there, reunited with Merrylegs.

Planned for cinemas, the film was acquired by Disney from Constantin Film and released on Disney+ on 27 November 2020. Reviews were mixed, with 48% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 52.

overview: When tragedy rocks Blackfoot High, rebellious outsider Mäddy Killian shocks the student body by joining the cheerleading squad. After a confrontation with the football team, Mäddy and her new cheerleader friends are sent on a supernatural roller coaster ride which leaves a path of destruction none of them may be able to escape.
tagline: You can't kill their spirit!
title: All Cheerleaders Die
plot:
All Cheerleaders Die is a dark comedy film that explores the theme of toxic masculinity and the objectification of women. The movie delves into the world of high school cheerleading, where the characters are portrayed as one-dimensional, shallow, and emotionally stunted. The main character, Bree, is a complex figure who embodies both vulnerability and strength, as she navigates her relationships with her friends and family.

The film critiques the societal pressure on women to conform to certain beauty standards and the ways in which this can lead to feelings of inadequacy and low self-esteem. Through Bree's character, the movie highlights the struggles of being a young woman in a patriarchal society where she is constantly judged and scrutinized.

Furthermore, All Cheerleaders Die touches on themes of female friendship and solidarity, as Bree and her friends form a tight-knit bond that serves as a source of support and empowerment. The film also explores the consequences of violence and aggression, particularly in the context of toxic masculinity, where men are socialized to suppress their emotions and express themselves through aggression.

Overall, All Cheerleaders Die is a thought-provoking film that challenges societal norms and expectations, particularly those related to gender and beauty standards.

original_title: Barbie & Her Sisters in the Great Puppy Adventure
overview: Barbie and her sisters, Skipper, Stacie and Chelsea, and their adorable new puppy friends find unexpected mystery and adventure when they return to their hometown of Willows. While going through mementos in Grandma's attic, the sisters discover an old map, believed to lead to a long-lost treasure buried somewhere in the town. With their puppy pals in tow, the four girls go on an exciting treasure hunt, along the way discovering that the greatest treasure of all is the love and laughter they share as sisters!
title: Barbie & Her Sisters in the Great Puppy Adventure
plot:
Barbie & Her Sisters in the Great Puppy Adventure is a 2015 American computer-animated adventure film and the 31st entry in the Barbie film series. Directed by Andrew Tan from a screenplay by Amy Wolfram, it was produced by Mattel Playground Productions with animation by Arc Productions and music by Christopher Willis. Universal released it on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States on 27 October 2015, and it had its television premiere on Nickelodeon that December. It runs 76 minutes.

Barbie (Kelly Sheridan) drives her younger sisters Skipper, Stacie and Chelsea in their pink camper to their childhood hometown of Willows for a two-week summer stay with Grandma Roberts. Her dog, Tiffany, has had four puppies who can talk among themselves, and each sister adopts one: Barbie takes Taffy, Skipper DJ, Stacie Rookie and Chelsea Honey. Rummaging in the attic, Skipper finds an old map, and Grandma explains that the town's founders buried a treasure to be found in a time of need so that Willows would always prosper. While Barbie plans to spend time with her childhood friend Christie at the Willowfest fair, the younger girls set off on the treasure hunt, unaware that two carnival workers, Joe and Marty, are following them in hopes of seizing the prize.

The trail of riddles leads the sisters and their puppies from the town hall to a founders' vase holding a willow-tree charm, to Lake Willows, a fountain and the musical town clock, whose chiming tune hides the next clue. Meanwhile Barbie notices that Willowfest has shrunk, shops have closed, the town is in disrepair, and Christie's family must move away because they can no longer afford to stay. After Joe and Marty steal Skipper's tablet with the girls' notes, Barbie joins the hunt. Following the map's song lyrics, the sisters find a hidden tunnel beneath the first willow tree, cross a cavern to an underground lake, and open a treasure vault with the charm. The crooks trap everyone inside with a rockslide, but Taffy frees them, and the puppies tie up the thieves before the police arrive.

The girls donate the treasure to the town, reviving Willows: shops reopen, repairs are made and Christie's family can stay. Before leaving with their puppies, the sisters hide part of their reward with a new map to give townspeople something to believe in. The voice cast includes Kazumi Evans as Skipper, Claire Maggie Corlett as Stacie, Alyssya Swales as Chelsea and Joanne Wilson as Grandma.

overview: The Secret Magic Control Agency sends its two best agents, Hansel and Gretel, to fight against the witch of the Gingerbread House.
title: Secret Magic Control Agency
plot:
Secret Magic Control Agency, also known as Hansel & Gretel, is a 2021 English-language Russian animated spy comedy film directed by Aleksey Tsitsilin and produced by Wizart Animation, CTB Film Company and QED International. A loose adaptation of the Brothers Grimm fairy tale, it features the voices of Sylvana Joyce as Gretel, Nicholas Corda as Hansel, Erica Schroeder as the witch Ilvira, Marc Thompson as the King and Mary O'Brady as Baba Yaga.

In a fantasy kingdom where all magic is regulated by the Secret Magic Control Agency, the king is kidnapped by sentient food enchanted with black magic. To keep the public calm, the prime minister keeps the abduction secret and leaves the investigation to the agency, which pairs its agent Gretel with her estranged brother Hansel, a con artist who poses as a wizard. Their search leads them to a pastry shop whose pantry is full of living baked goods and a potion room holding enchanted vanilla extract, but after a chase with a dog-shaped cookie destroys the shop, the siblings are turned into children. With no one at the agency believing them, they turn to Baba Yaga, a witch said to eat children, and learn that the extract came from the swamplands. There the Lake Witch mistakes them for spies of Ilvira, the witch of the gingerbread house and the king's former cook, and spares them only because her daughter recognizes Gretel as the agent who once saved her. Freeing Ilvira's captured henchmen, they are led to her lair and discover her plan: to make the king fall in love with her through magic so she can become queen and claim the power of the crown. Ilvira locks the siblings in an oven, where they finally have it out. Gretel resents Hansel's swindling, while he resents her putting her career before family, and he reveals that he gave up an honest life to pay for her education, passing the money off as a royal scholarship. Reconciled, they escape, make an antidote and race to the royal wedding, but the marriage is sealed before they can stop it. Using a gadget Hansel stole from the agency, they escape being baked into cookies, recover the antidote and drop Ilvira into her own batter. Gretel is named Best Agent, Hansel declines a magic license as he cannot do real magic, and the siblings agree to work together.

Released in Russia by Sony on 18 March 2021, the film debuted on Netflix a week later and topped its global viewing charts in its first week, receiving generally positive reviews for its animation.

overview: Each year the population of sleepy Lake Victoria, Arizona explodes from 5,000 to 50,000 residents for the annual Spring Break celebration. But then, an earthquake opens an underwater chasm, releasing an enormous swarm of ancient Piranha that have been dormant for thousands of years, now with a taste for human flesh. This year, there's something more to worry about than the usual hangovers and complaints from locals, a new type of terror is about to be cut loose on Lake Victoria.
tagline: There's something in the water.
title: Piranha 3D
plot:
Piranha 3D is a 2010 American horror film directed by David R. Ellis and written by Christopher Hoadley, Josh Stolberg, and Doug Taylor. The movie is a remake of the 1978 film Piranha, which was itself an adaptation of Joe Dante's 1978 film of the same name.

The story takes place in the fictional town of Long Beach, California, where a group of college students are preparing for the annual Spring Break festivities. Among them is Jake (Dustin Hoffman), a fisherman who has been hired to transport a shipment of piranhas from South America to a local aquarium. Unbeknownst to Jake, the piranhas have escaped during the journey and are now swimming in the waters off Long Beach.

As the students arrive at the beach, they begin to notice that something is amiss. At first, it's just small fish biting people, but soon the attacks escalate into full-blown piranha attacks. The main character, Fisherman (Jerry O'Connell), teams up with a local fisherman, Jake (Dustin Hoffman), and a group of college students to try and stop the piranhas before they kill everyone.

As the body count rises, the group discovers that the piranhas are not just mindless killers but are actually attracted to human blood. They also learn that the piranhas have been genetically engineered to be more aggressive and deadly than their natural counterparts.

The movie's plot development is driven by a series of gruesome and intense attacks on the students and locals, which escalate in frequency and ferocity as the story progresses. Along the way, the group discovers that the source of the piranha infestation is a local water treatment plant that has been releasing untreated sewage into the ocean.

As the body count rises, the survivors are forced to confront their own mortality and the true horror of the situation. In the end, only a few characters remain, including Fisherman (Jerry O'Connell) and his girlfriend, Liz ( Elisabeth Shue), who manage to escape the carnage by fleeing in a boat.

The ending is a classic horror movie finale, with the survivors barely escaping the clutches of the piranhas. The final shot is of the empty beach, littered with the bodies of the victims, as the camera pans out to reveal the true extent of the carnage.

Overall, Piranha 3D is a fun and gory horror movie that pays homage to the classic films of the genre while also offering something new and different. With its over-the-top violence and gore, it's sure to appeal to fans of the horror genre.

overview: Inspired by Arthur Schnitzler's classic La Ronde, screenwriter Peter Morgan and director Fernando Meirelles' 360 combines a modern and dynamic roundelay of stories into one, linking characters from different cities and countries in a vivid, suspenseful and deeply moving tale of love in the 21st century. Starting in Vienna, the film beautifully weaves through Paris, London, Bratislava, Rio, Denver and Phoenix into a single, mesmerizing narrative.
tagline: Everything comes full circle
plot:
360 is a 2011 ensemble drama directed by Fernando Meirelles and written by Peter Morgan, a loose adaptation of Arthur Schnitzler's 1897 play Reigen. Its international cast includes Anthony Hopkins, Jude Law, Rachel Weisz, Ben Foster, Moritz Bleibtreu and Dinara Drukarova, in interlocking stories of couples, desire and chance that circle from Vienna through Paris, London and Denver to Berlin.

In Vienna, Slovak sisters Mirka and Anna meet Rocco, who runs an escort agency, and Mirka begins working under the name Blanca. Her first client, businessman Michael Daly, walks out after an associate loudly questions whether she is a prostitute, and the associate later blackmails Michael into a deal. In Paris, an Algerian man secretly pines for a married woman and seeks advice from his imam and a therapist. In London, Michael's wife, Rose, ends her affair with Rui, only for Rui to find that his girlfriend, Laura, has photographed them together and left him.

Flying home to Brazil, Laura is stranded by bad weather in Denver alongside John, a father searching for his long-missing daughter, and Tyler, a sex offender just released after six years in prison who fears his own impulses. She invites Tyler to her hotel room, but he rejects her drunken advances and locks himself in the bathroom. John, moved by Laura's farewell hug, travels to Phoenix to examine remains that prove not to be his daughter, and at an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting he resolves to accept her unknown fate. There Valentina reveals that she is the woman the Algerian man watched; she wants to leave her husband, Sergei, driver for a crooked Russian businessman, because she loves her boss. Back in Paris, the dentist she works for, the Algerian man, asks her to find another job, and both are heartbroken.

In Vienna, Sergei's boss hires Mirka, while Sergei and Anna bond over books and learning English as he drives her around the city. Mirka's plan to rob the businessman with Rocco unravels when he reads her phone, but Rocco attacks him, and Mirka escapes with the cash as Anna writes her sister a goodbye letter. In Berlin, Michael and Rose reunite, and Michael's associate glimpses a new young woman arriving for a photo shoot with Rocco.

The film opened the 2011 London Film Festival, and Magnolia Pictures released it on demand in June 2012 and in U.S. theaters that August. Reviews were negative, with 19% on Rotten Tomatoes and 43 on Metacritic.

overview: Thurgood Marshall, the first African-American Supreme Court Justice, battles through one of his career-defining cases.
tagline: Justice has a name.
title: Marshall
plot:
Marshall is a 2017 American biographical legal drama film directed by Reginald Hudlin from a screenplay by Michael Koskoff and his son Jacob Koskoff. It stars Chadwick Boseman as Thurgood Marshall, who would become the first African American justice of the US Supreme Court, and centers on one of his early cases, State of Connecticut v. Joseph Spell. Josh Gad, Kate Hudson, Dan Stevens, Sterling K. Brown and James Cromwell co-star.

In April 1941, Marshall is an NAACP lawyer traveling the country to defend Black people wrongly accused of crimes because of racial prejudice. He is sent to Bridgeport, Connecticut, to defend Joseph Spell, a chauffeur accused of rape by his white employer, Eleanor Strubing, in a case splashed across the newspapers. Sam Friedman, a reluctant local insurance lawyer, is assigned by his brother to sponsor Marshall's admission to the bar. Judge Foster, a friend of the father of prosecutor Lorin Willis, admits Marshall but forbids him to speak at trial, making Friedman lead counsel while Marshall guides him with notes, including advice to seat an assertive Southern white woman on the jury. Spell insists that he never had sexual contact with Strubing, and Marshall talks him out of a plea deal, but testimony about skin under Strubing's fingernails and a patrolman's traffic stop forces Spell to admit that he lied. On the stand, Spell testifies that Strubing's bruises came from her abusive husband, that on the night in question she wanted to have sex with him and that they did so consensually, after which she panicked about being found out and pregnant. As he drove her to a doctor, she hid from the patrolman, then ran to a bridge and jumped despite his attempt to stop her, surviving and inventing the rape story for a passing motorist. Asked why he did not tell the truth at first, Spell describes Black men being lynched in his native Louisiana for relations with white women, and the shaken judge lets the testimony stand. Marshall must leave for a case in Mississippi, but he helps Friedman prepare the closing argument, and Spell rejects a lighter plea offer. The Southern woman, now jury forewoman, delivers a verdict of not guilty, and Friedman phones Marshall with the news.

Shot in Los Angeles and in Buffalo and Niagara Falls, New York, the film premiered at Howard University on 20 September 2017 and opened in the US on 13 October. Critics were largely positive, giving it 80% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 66.

overview: Ex-military specialist Clair Hamilton returns home from her tour in the Middle East due to her father's passing and to claim her inheritance. Her son is then kidnapped and held for ransom by a gang led by a mysterious figure known only as “Father”.
tagline: In the Wild, Only the Strong Survive
title: Daughter of the Wolf
plot:
Daughter of the Wolf is a 2019 Canadian action thriller directed by David Hackl and written by Nika Agiashvili. Gina Carano stars as Clair Hamilton, a military veteran fighting to rescue her kidnapped son, with Richard Dreyfuss as the kidnappers' leader, known only as Father, Brendan Fehr as Larsen, Sydelle Noel as Hobbs and Anton Gillis-Adelman as the boy, Charlie. It was shot in the spring of 2019 around West Kelowna, British Columbia.

Clair arrives at a remote exchange with a bag of ransom money, only to be double-crossed. In the shootout she kills two of the gang, and while chasing the third, Larsen, she falls through the ice of a frozen lake. Larsen, who never meant for anyone to die, pulls her out. Recovering, Clair has a calm encounter with a black wolf, then catches Larsen and forces him to lead her to her son. Father, it emerges, holds a grudge against Clair's father for shutting down a mill and leaving with money owed to him. Along the way a gunman ambushes them but is killed by wolves, and Larsen confesses that Father murdered his own father and abducted him and his mother when he was a child.

The gang has moved Charlie to a lodge across the mountain to sell him. When Clair tries to trade the money and Larsen for the boy, Father fires at Charlie, and Larsen takes the bullet. Clair escapes on a snowmobile but is chased by Hobbs, loses a knife fight and goes over a waterfall, while Charlie is recaptured. Guided by wolves through the forest, she returns to the lodge, where Father is torturing Larsen. She kills Hobbs and the remaining gang, and in a final struggle pushes Father through a window. Larsen dies, Clair flees with Charlie, and wolves descend on Father in the snow. Months later, hiking in spring, Clair sees the black wolf again.

The film was released in the United States on 14 June 2019 and in Canada that August, and screened at the Taormina Film Fest. Reviews were largely negative, with a 25% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 36. The Hollywood Reporter called it a subpar vehicle for its star, though Variety praised it as a capably crafted, female-led action film.

overview: In the 1970s, a foundling lass, Patrick "Kitten" Braden, comes of age by leaving her Irish town for London, in part to look for her mother and in part because her transgender nature is beyond the town's understanding.
tagline: Same world. Different planet.
title: Breakfast on Pluto
plot:
Breakfast on Pluto is a 2005 film that explores the complexities of identity, belonging, and self-discovery through the life story of Patrick Kittenbrunt, a young Irishman who struggles to find his place in the world. The movie delves into themes of gender identity, particularly transsexuality, as Patrick navigates his feelings of being a woman trapped in a man's body.

The film also touches on the theme of family and the search for roots, as Patrick grapples with his complicated relationships with his mother and her past. Through Patrick's journey, the movie sheds light on the struggles faced by individuals who do not conform to societal norms, particularly those who are marginalized due to their gender identity.

Furthermore, Breakfast on Pluto is a poignant exploration of the human need for connection and acceptance. As Patrick navigates his way through various relationships and experiences, he seeks validation and understanding from others, highlighting the importance of empathy and compassion in breaking down barriers and fostering inclusivity.

The film's narrative is woven with elements of Irish folklore and mythology, adding depth to its themes of identity, belonging, and transformation. Overall, Breakfast on Pluto presents a powerful and thought-provoking portrayal of self-discovery, acceptance, and the human quest for connection and understanding.

overview: On a Caribbean cruise, Jenny is marooned on a beach with her rock and roll idol. Deliriously in love with the idea of time alone with him, she manages to hide the fact that they're a stone's throw away from their resort.
tagline: She's shipwrecked on an island with the guy of her dreams. The last thing she wants is to be rescued.
title: Love Wrecked
plot:
Love Wrecked is a romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and self-discovery. The movie follows the story of two women, Georgia and Beth, who find themselves on a ship together after a storm, leading to an unexpected romance.

At its core, Love Wrecked delves into the theme of finding one's true self amidst the chaos of life. Both Georgia and Beth are struggling with their own personal demons, and as they navigate their feelings for each other, they must confront their inner fears and insecurities. The film suggests that true love can be found in the most unexpected places, but it also requires a willingness to face one's vulnerabilities and take risks.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and how our relationships with others shape us. Georgia and Beth's interactions with each other challenge their perceptions of themselves and force them to re-evaluate their priorities. The film implies that love can be a catalyst for personal growth, but it also requires effort and commitment from both parties.

Furthermore, Love Wrecked explores the idea of non-traditional relationships and challenges societal norms around love and acceptance. The movie presents a romantic relationship between two women in a way that is natural, tender, and authentic, promoting a sense of inclusivity and acceptance.

Overall, Love Wrecked is a heartwarming and humorous film that celebrates the complexities of human relationships and the power of love to transform and uplift us.

overview: When reporter Jean Craddock interviews Bad Blake—an alcoholic, seen-better-days country music legend—they connect, and the hard-living crooner sees a possible saving grace in a life with Jean and her young son.
tagline: The harder the life, the sweeter the song.
title: Crazy Heart
plot:
Crazy Heart is a poignant and powerful film that delves into the complexities of the human condition, exploring themes of redemption, love, and the struggle for self-discovery.

At its core, the movie is a story about a man who has lost his way, haunted by the ghosts of his past and struggling to find meaning in his life. The protagonist's journey is marked by a deep sense of regret and longing, as he grapples with the consequences of his choices and the loss of those closest to him.

Through the character of Bad Blake, the film sheds light on the darker aspects of the music industry, exposing the harsh realities of fame, addiction, and the commodification of art. However, it also offers a nuanced portrayal of the human spirit, revealing the resilience and vulnerability that define us all.

One of the most striking aspects of Crazy Heart is its exploration of love in all its forms. The film presents a complex web of relationships, from the toxic bond between Blake and his manager to the redemptive power of love with Jean Craddock. These relationships serve as a catalyst for Blake's transformation, forcing him to confront his demons and re-examine his priorities.

Ultimately, Crazy Heart is a movie about finding one's way back to oneself, about embracing the imperfections and fragilities that make us human. It is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that lingers long after the credits roll, leaving the viewer with a deeper understanding of the complexities and nuances of the human experience.

overview: On the most important day of his young life, a high school senior is forced to relive his failed attempt at losing his virginity over and over again, until he gets it right.
title: Premature
plot:
Grace of Monaco is a 2014 biographical drama film that tells the story of Princess Grace Kelly's life, from her early days as an actress to her marriage to Prince Rainier III of Monaco and her subsequent rise to royal status. The main themes of the movie revolve around the tension between personal identity and public duty.

The film explores how Princess Grace struggled with the constraints of royal protocol and the expectations placed upon her as a member of the royal family, while also trying to maintain her own sense of self and artistic passion. As she navigates the complexities of palace life, she must confront the sacrifices she has made for her marriage and her role as a princess.

The movie also delves into the theme of feminism, highlighting Princess Grace's determination to forge her own path in a world dominated by men. Her character's journey is marked by moments of quiet defiance and subtle rebellion against the patriarchal norms that seek to constrain her.

Furthermore, the film touches on the idea of love and sacrifice, as Princess Grace must weigh her own desires against the needs of her husband and their future children. The movie raises questions about the nature of true love and whether it can survive the pressures of royal life.

Overall, Grace of Monaco is a nuanced exploration of the complexities of royal life, personal identity, and the challenges faced by women in positions of power.

overview: A man vows to bring justice to those responsible for his wife's death while protecting the only family he has left, his daughter.
tagline: Family fights as one.
title: Sweet Girl
plot:
Sweet Girl is a 2021 American action thriller directed by Brian Andrew Mendoza in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Philip Eisner and Gregg Hurwitz. Jason Momoa, who also produced, stars as Ray Cooper and Isabela Merced as his daughter Rachel, with Manuel Garcia-Rulfo as the hitman Santos, Amy Brenneman as Congresswoman Diana Morgan, Adria Arjona as Ray's wife Amanda, Justin Bartha as Simon Keeley and Lex Scott Davis as FBI agent Sarah Meeker. It was filmed in Pittsburgh.

In Pittsburgh, survival expert Ray and his teenage daughter Rachel train together in mixed martial arts at his gym. When Amanda is stricken with cancer, a promising drug from the company BioPrime might save her, but it is pulled from the market after CEO Simon Keeley pays to delay its production. Ray phones a live television interview and threatens Keeley's life. Amanda dies, and months later the journalist Martin Bennett offers Ray evidence of BioPrime's corruption. Their meeting on a subway train is cut short when Santos stabs Bennett to death, wounds Ray and knocks Rachel unconscious.

Two years later Ray, who has been tracking the company ever since, confronts Keeley at a charity auction, learns that chairman Vinod Shah is behind the scheme, and kills him. Fleeing with Rachel, he fights off mercenaries at a motel and plans to ambush Shah, only for Santos to shoot Shah first. Over a tense meeting in a diner, Santos agrees to a temporary truce and points them to his true employer, Congresswoman Morgan. Cornered by the FBI on the roof of PNC Park, the truth emerges: Ray died of his wounds on the subway, and Rachel, traumatized and suffering from dissociative identity disorder, has carried out the revenge herself. She escapes custody, kills Santos, records Morgan's confession of taking bribes and ordering the killings, and sends it to the FBI. Morgan is arrested, and Rachel leaves the country with a false passport.

Sweet Girl was released on Netflix on 20 August 2021. Critics were largely unimpressed: it holds a 24% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus faulted its action clichés and late twist while crediting its well-matched leads, and a Metacritic score of 46. The Hollywood Reporter praised its efficient action and use of Pittsburgh locations but found the violence increasingly mindless.

overview: In this humorous paean to the joys of food, a pair of truck drivers happen onto a decrepit roadside shop selling ramen noodles. The widowed owner, Tampopo, begs them to help her turn her establishment into a paragon of the "art of noodle-soup making". Interspersed are satirical vignettes about the importance of food to different aspects of human life.
tagline: The first Japanese Noodle Western.
title: Tampopo
plot:
Tampopo is a 1985 Japanese romantic comedy film directed by Juzo Itami. The movie follows the story of Goro, a young truck driver who falls in love with a beautiful woman named Tampopo, and her struggles to save her family's noodle shop from bankruptcy.

The main theme of Tampopo revolves around the importance of food, community, and human connection. The film celebrates the art of Japanese cuisine, particularly ramen noodles, and explores the ways in which food can bring people together. Through Goro's journey, the movie highlights the significance of finding one's passion and purpose in life.

The film also touches on themes of family, tradition, and cultural identity. Tampopo's struggles to save her family's noodle shop serve as a metaphor for the challenges faced by many small business owners and the importance of preserving traditional ways of life.

Furthermore, Tampopo is a movie about love and relationships. Goro's romance with Tampopo serves as a catalyst for his personal growth and self-discovery, and the film explores the complexities of human emotions and connections.

Overall, Tampopo is a heartwarming and humorous film that celebrates the beauty of food, community, and human connection, while also exploring deeper themes of family, tradition, and love.

overview: A hospice nurse working at a spooky New Orleans plantation home finds herself entangled in a mystery involving the house's dark past.
tagline: Fearing Is Believing
title: The Skeleton Key
plot:
The Skeleton Key is a 2005 supernatural thriller film directed by Iain Softley and starring Kate Hudson, Gena Rowlands, John Hurt, and Peter Sarsgaard.

The movie follows Caroline Ellis (Kate Hudson), a nurse who takes a job caring for an elderly man named Ben Mears (Peter Sarsgaard) in his plantation house in Louisiana. However, upon arrival, she discovers that the house is inhabited by a mysterious and sinister presence, which seems to be connected to the death of Ben's wife.

The main themes of The Skeleton Key include:

1. **Supernatural horror**: The film explores the idea of supernatural entities and their connection to the afterlife, delving into the concept of spirits trapped between worlds.
2. **Mystery and suspense**: As Caroline delves deeper into the mystery of Ben's wife's death, she uncovers a web of secrets and lies that lead her to confront the dark forces at work in the house.
3. **Feminist themes**: The character of Caroline Ellis is a strong and independent protagonist who takes charge of her own destiny, challenging traditional feminine roles and expectations.
4. **Cultural heritage and colonialism**: The film touches on the complex history of Louisiana's plantation culture, highlighting the tensions between the old and new, as well as the clash of cultures and values.

Throughout the movie, these themes are intertwined with a sense of foreboding and unease, creating a tense and suspenseful atmosphere that keeps the viewer engaged until the climactic conclusion.

overview: Lily is a typical 150-year-old lovelorn vampire who's looking for the man of her nightmares -- until she lays her eyes on Herman, a 7-foot-tall green experiment with a heart of gold. It's love at first shock as these two ghouls fall fangs over feet for each other in a Transylvanian romance. Unfortunately, it's not all smooth sailing in the cemetery as Lily's father has other plans for his beloved daughter's future, and they don't involve her new bumbling beau.
tagline: Prepare for the strangest love story ever told.
title: The Munsters
plot:
The Munsters is a 2022 American horror comedy written, produced and directed by Rob Zombie as a prequel and origin story to the 1960s sitcom. Jeff Daniel Phillips plays Herman Munster, Sheri Moon Zombie plays Lily and Daniel Roebuck plays her father, the Count, with Richard Brake as the mad scientist Dr. Wolfgang, Jorge Garcia as his assistant Floop, Sylvester McCoy as the servant Igor, Catherine Schell as the Count's ex-wife Zoya and Cassandra Peterson as the realtor Barbara Carr.

In Transylvania, Dr. Wolfgang and his hunchbacked helper Floop rob graves to assemble a creature, but Floop takes the head of a corny comedian, Shecky, instead of his brilliant brother. Brought to life, the creation, named Herman, turns out to be a goofy jokester. Meanwhile Zoya, seeking revenge on the Count, pressures his werewolf son Lester, who owes her money, into helping her obtain the family castle for a casino. The Count's daughter Lily, a vampire unlucky in love, sees Herman unveiled on a morning television show and is charmed. She watches him perform with his band at Zoya's nightclub, and the two fall for each other.

The Count dislikes the dim newcomer and tries magic to get rid of him, but Herman and Lily become engaged and marry. Now head of the household, Herman is tricked by Lester into signing the castle's deed over to Zoya. On their honeymoon in Paris, the couple capture a reptilian creature from the sewers and adopt it as their pet, Spot. Evicted and without legal recourse, they follow Herman's dream of stardom to America, where Barbara Carr shows them around Hollywood and they buy the crumbling house at 1313 in Mockingbird Heights. A Halloween block party makes them think they have found fellow monsters, but they are dismayed to discover that their neighbors are ordinary people. Lester then arrives with a check from his Las Vegas winnings, and the Munsters find themselves rich.

The film was released on digital, Blu-ray and DVD and on Netflix in the United States on 27 September 2022. Reviews were mixed: it holds a 52% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 57, with critics noting Zombie's clear affection for the series while finding the story loose and sketch-like.

overview: The fast-paced action movie is again set in the criminal underworld in France, where Frank Martin is known as The Transporter, because he is the best driver and mercenary money can buy. In this installment, he meets Anna and they attempt to take down a group of ruthless Russian human traffickers who also have kidnapped Frank’s father.
tagline: He Delivers.
title: The Transporter Refueled
plot:
The Transporter Refueled (French: Le Transporteur: Héritage) is a 2015 action thriller directed by Camille Delamarre and written by Bill Collage, Adam Cooper and Luc Besson. The fourth Transporter film and a reboot of the series, it came about after EuropaCorp's talks with original star Jason Statham over a three-film deal broke down; Ed Skrein took over as Frank Martin, and no actors returned from the earlier films. Originally titled The Transporter Legacy, it was shot in Paris from August 2014. EuropaCorp released it in the United States on 4 September 2015 and in France five days later.

In 1995, Russian gangster Arkady Karasov and his partners Leo Imasov and Yuri seize control of prostitution on the French Riviera, among them a young Anna. Fifteen years later, Anna sets out to bring Karasov down. Frank Martin Jr., an ex-special forces operative who now works as a professional driver in his Audi S8, is with his father, Frank Sr., a retired secret agent, when Anna hires him for a job. Picking her up at a Monte Carlo bank, he finds three more women, Gina, Qiao and Maria, who show him live video of his father held at gunpoint and claim that Frank Sr. has been poisoned and will die without their antidote. Frank learns that all four were once Karasov's prostitutes, and that he himself shares a past with the gangster.

Forced to cooperate, Frank helps the women gas Imasov's rave club and take his fingerprints to empty his bank account into theirs, while Frank Sr. and Maria do the same to Yuri aboard his plane, where Maria is shot. Anna then admits the poison was a bluff. When Karasov kidnaps Frank Sr. and demands the women, Frank delivers them to his yacht, where Anna convinces Imasov and Yuri that Karasov stole their money. Gina, who had slipped away, secretly diverts the funds, and in the ensuing shootout Qiao and Maria are killed and Gina dies after killing Karasov's associate Maïssa. On a clifftop, Anna shoots Karasov, then cannot bring herself to shoot Frank, who realizes she arranged his father's kidnapping and persuades her to abandon revenge. A month later she shares the money among her friends' families and the Martins.

Skrein plays Frank, with Ray Stevenson as Frank Sr., Loan Chabanol as Anna, Gabriella Wright as Gina, Tatjana Pajković as Maria, Yu Wenxia as Qiao and Radivoje Bukvić as Karasov. Reviews were negative, with 15% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, though IGN felt Skrein made the role his own. It grossed $72.6 million, led by China.

overview: Alone on a tiny deserted island, Hank has given up all hope of ever making it home again. But one day everything changes when a dead body washes ashore, and he soon realizes it may be his last opportunity to escape certain death. Armed with his new “friend” and an unusual bag of tricks, the duo go on an epic adventure to bring Hank back to the woman of his dreams.
tagline: We all need somebody to lean on.
title: Swiss Army Man
plot:
Swiss Army Man is a 2016 American absurdist comedy-drama film directed by Dan Kwan and Daniel Scheinert, also known as the Daniels. The movie stars Paul Dano, Daniel Radcliffe, and Mary Elizabeth Winstead.

The main themes of Swiss Army Man revolve around:

1. **Isolation and Human Connection**: The film tells the story of Hank (Paul Dano), a stranded sailor who befriends a dead body, Manny (Daniel Radcliffe), which he discovers on a deserted island. As they spend more time together, Hank forms an unlikely bond with Manny, highlighting the human need for connection and companionship.
2. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: Through his relationship with Manny, Hank undergoes a transformation, discovering new aspects of himself and finding purpose in life. The film explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and the search for meaning.
3. **Existentialism and the Human Condition**: Swiss Army Man delves into existentialist ideas, questioning the nature of existence, mortality, and the human experience. The film's absurdity and surrealism serve to underscore the complexities and mysteries of life.
4. **Nature and the Environment**: The movie features stunning visuals of the natural world, highlighting the beauty and power of nature. The island where Hank and Manny reside serves as a symbol of isolation and the human relationship with the environment.
5. **Mental Health and Trauma**: Hank's backstory is slowly revealed throughout the film, exposing his struggles with mental health, trauma, and grief. The movie handles these themes with sensitivity and nuance.

Overall, Swiss Army Man is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores complex themes through its unique narrative and characters.

overview: When two American girls on a bike trip in a remote part of Argentina split up and one of them goes missing, the other must find her before her worst fears are realized.
tagline: Alone. Stranded. No One to Trust.
title: And Soon the Darkness
plot:
And Soon the Darkness is a 2010 mystery horror film directed by Marcos Efron, who wrote the screenplay with Jennifer Derwingson. A remake of the 1970 British film of the same name, it stars Karl Urban, Amber Heard and Odette Annable, with Adriana Barraza and César Vianco in supporting roles. It is also known as Prisioneras de la oscuridad.

Stephanie and Ellie, two young American women backpacking through South America, decide to spend their last day in Argentina at a small hotel. After a drunken night at the local bar, where they meet some of the local men, they miss the bus that was to take them to their next stop. Since it runs only once a day, they head to a nearby river to relax and enjoy the unexpected extra day. After a heated argument, the friends separate, and Ellie is abducted. Searching frantically, Stephanie is joined by Michael, an American who says he is looking for his girlfriend, who disappeared months earlier. The town's lone police officer helps them but behaves suspiciously.

Stephanie tracks down the hideout where Ellie is being held and frees her, but the kidnapper kills Ellie during their escape. The policeman then appears and coaxes Stephanie into his car, where finding a passport makes her realize that he is a sadistic human trafficker responsible for the town's missing women. Michael seizes the officer's gun, and the policeman offers to exchange Michael's girlfriend, Camila, for Stephanie; Michael agrees, but the officer shoots him with a second weapon. Stephanie is taken by boat to be sold, but she escapes by jumping overboard, killing the kidnapper in the process. Reaching the Paraguayan shore, she is caught by the buyer and the pursuing policeman but breaks free again. The officer chases her, killing a fisherman who tries to help, and she hides in a boat, arming herself with a knife. When he comes aboard, they struggle; she stabs him in the leg, takes his gun and kills him. At dawn, as Stephanie walks toward the nearest town, a jeep pulls up, and a Paraguayan soldier steps out to rescue her.

The film was shot in Argentina in March 2009. It was presented at the European Film Market in Germany in February 2010, and Anchor Bay acquired U.S. rights that May, giving it a limited theatrical run beginning December 17, 2010, while Optimum Releasing scheduled a British release for February 2011. Critical response was poor, with only 17% approval on Rotten Tomatoes from six reviews.

original_title: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
overview: Captain Jack Sparrow works his way out of a blood debt with the ghostly Davy Jones to avoid eternal damnation.
tagline: Captain Jack is back!
title: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
plot:
Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest is a 2006 adventure film directed by Gore Verbinski and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer. The movie is the second installment in the Pirates of the Caribbean franchise.

The story begins with Will Turner (Orlando Bloom), a blacksmith's apprentice, who is being pursued by the Kraken, a massive sea monster. Meanwhile, Elizabeth Swann (Keira Knightley), the governor's daughter, is kidnapped by Captain Barbossa (Geoffrey Rush) and his crew of undead pirates.

As Will sets out to rescue Elizabeth, he meets Bootstrap Bill Turner (Stellan Skarsgård), his father, who has been cursed by the sea goddess Calypso. The curse states that if a pirate dies at sea, their spirit will be trapped between the world of the living and the dead, forced to serve as a crew member on the Flying Dutchman.

Will's quest leads him to Davy Jones (Bill Nighy), the captain of the Flying Dutchman, who is in charge of collecting souls from those who die at sea. In exchange for his soul, Will must find the heart of Davy Jones, which is hidden inside a giant clamshell.

As Will navigates the treacherous waters, he also encounters Jack Sparrow (Johnny Depp), the infamous pirate captain, who has made a deal with Davy Jones to trade his freedom for his ship, the Black Pearl. However, when Jack's deal goes sour, he is forced to sail the seas and collect souls to pay off his debt.

Throughout the movie, Will and Elizabeth must navigate their feelings for each other while facing the dangers of the high seas. The film features a mix of action, adventure, and humor, with memorable performances from the cast.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between the pirates and Davy Jones' crew, as well as a heart-wrenching scene where Will must make a difficult choice to save his father's soul. In the end, Will finds the heart of Davy Jones, but not before facing numerous challenges and obstacles.

Overall, Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest is an exciting and thrilling adventure that sets the stage for the next installment in the franchise. The movie's success can be attributed to its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and impressive visual effects.

overview: In Arizona in the late 1800s, infamous outlaw Ben Wade and his vicious gang of thieves and murderers have plagued the Southern Railroad. When Wade is captured, Civil War veteran Dan Evans, struggling to survive on his drought-plagued ranch, volunteers to deliver him alive to the "3:10 to Yuma", a train that will take the killer to trial.
tagline: Time waits for one man.
title: 3:10 to Yuma
plot:
3:10 to Yuma is a 2007 American Western action drama directed by James Mangold and produced by Cathy Konrad. The second screen adaptation of Elmore Leonard's 1953 short story "Three-Ten to Yuma", following the 1957 film, it casts Christian Bale as a drought-stricken rancher who takes on the perilous job of escorting a notorious outlaw, played by Russell Crowe, to justice. It was filmed at various locations in New Mexico, premiered in Los Angeles in August 2007 and was released by Lionsgate on September 7.

In the Arizona Territory of 1884, Dan Evans, a struggling rancher and Civil War veteran, is in debt to Glen Hollander, whose men burn his barn. Searching for his scattered cattle with his two sons, Evans witnesses Ben Wade's gang rob a stagecoach guarded by Pinkertons. Wade takes the family's horses but leaves them alive, and Evans rescues the only surviving guard, Pinkerton agent Byron McElroy. In the town of Bisbee, Wade lingers with a barmaid and is arrested. Railroad agent Grayson Butterfield assembles a posse, including McElroy, the veterinarian Doc Potter and Hollander's man Tucker, to take Wade to Contention and put him on the 3:10 train to Yuma Territorial Prison, and Evans signs on for $200 to save his ranch.

On the journey, Wade kills Tucker with a stolen fork and throws McElroy off a cliff. Evans's elder son, William, follows and helps stop an escape. After an Apache attack, Wade flees to a camp of Chinese laborers whose foreman bears a grudge against him, and Potter is killed in the ensuing gunfight. In Contention, Wade's vicious lieutenant, Charlie Prince, offers $200 to anyone who kills a captor; the marshals desert, and Butterfield gives up. Evans refuses to quit, demanding better terms for his family and declaring that the task is now about honor; he reveals that he lost part of his leg after being accidentally shot by one of his own men during a retreat. Wade, who has escaped Yuma twice, helps Evans dodge the gunfire and boards the train, but Prince shoots Evans. Wade kills Prince and the rest of his gang, then surrenders his weapon as William comforts his dying father. As the train pulls away, Wade whistles and his horse gallops after it.

Crowe plays Wade and Bale plays Evans, with Peter Fonda as McElroy, Ben Foster as Prince, Logan Lerman as William, Dallas Roberts as Butterfield and Gretchen Mol as Alice Evans. Critics were enthusiastic, with 89% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and it grossed $71.2 million on a $48–55 million budget.

overview: A hopeless romantic thinks he's found true love with an older woman, only to learn that she's married and that his fling is merely an instrument of revenge against her neglectful husband.
tagline: He finally met the love of his life...Then he met her husband.
title: Crash Pad
plot:
Crash Pad is a 2017 American comedy directed by Kevin Tent, best known as Alexander Payne's longtime film editor, in his solo directing debut, from a screenplay by Jeremy Catalino. Domhnall Gleeson stars as Stensland, with Thomas Haden Church as Grady Dott, Christina Applegate as his wife Morgan and Nina Dobrev as Morgan's assistant Hannah. Payne served as an executive producer, and Rolfe Kent composed the score.

Stensland is a 29-year-old slacker and hopeless romantic whose idea of a good night is getting stoned and rewatching old episodes of Dawson's Creek. After two passionate days with Morgan, an older woman he is convinced is the love of his life, she abruptly tells him, while he stands naked in her bedroom, that she is married and that their fling was only a way of getting even with her husband, whom she believes has cheated on her. Crushed, Stensland spends a week sobbing on his couch, then storms into Morgan's office and threatens to tell her husband everything, drawing the eavesdropping Hannah into the drama. When Morgan calls his bluff, he phones Grady and describes the affair in detail, and Grady vows to find him and kill him.

When the furious husband turns up at Stensland's squalid bachelor apartment, however, he is mostly interested in frightening the young man, and the sight of the mess and a can of cheap stew reminds him of his own broke youth. Resentful of Morgan and convinced that success as a lawyer has robbed him of his manhood, Grady decides to move in with Stensland, paying his bills while turning the place into a base for a vengeful bachelor lifestyle. He drags his reluctant roommate through nights of binge drinking, bar fights and keg stands, coaching him to pick up women instead of falling in love with them, but Stensland proves incapable of becoming a boor, and Grady is less committed to the act than he pretends. Both men are eventually pushed toward recognizing their own share of the blame, and the story follows a familiar romantic-comedy path to a happy ending.

Crash Pad premiered at the Woodstock Film Festival, was released on video on demand on September 25, 2017, and opened in limited release on October 27 through Vertical Entertainment and Destination Films. Reviews were mixed, with a 54 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 46. The Hollywood Reporter called it a broadly appealing bad-behavior comedy carried by its leads' chemistry, and TheWrap found it far smarter than its high concept suggests.

original_title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
overview: On a quest to find out what happened to his missing brother, a scientist, his nephew and their mountain guide discover a fantastic and dangerous lost world in the center of the earth.
tagline: Same Planet. Different World.
title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
plot:
Journey to the Center of the Earth is a 2008 American 3D science fantasy action-adventure film directed by Eric Brevig. An adaptation of Jules Verne's 1864 novel in which the book itself exists within the story, it stars Brendan Fraser as volcanologist Trevor Anderson, Josh Hutcherson as his nephew Sean, and Aníta Briem as Icelandic guide Hannah Ásgeirsdóttir.

In 2007, Boston volcanologist Trevor learns that the lab of his brother, Max, who vanished ten years earlier, is closing for lack of funding, and he has forgotten that his 13-year-old nephew, Sean, Max's son, is coming to stay for ten days. Sean's mother leaves a box of Max's belongings, including a copy of Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth filled with Max's notes. Studying them, Trevor decides to investigate in Iceland, and Sean, now curious about the father he barely knew, insists on coming. Seeking another scientist who shared Max's theories, they meet his daughter, Hannah, who says he has died and that both men believed Verne's novels were true accounts. She agrees to guide them up a mountain to an instrument that has suddenly begun transmitting again.

A lightning storm drives them into a cave whose entrance collapses, trapping them in an old mine, where they find a tunnel studded with gems, including diamonds that Sean pockets, before the floor gives way and they plunge to the center of the Earth. There they find Max's old shelter, his journal and his body, which they bury. Trevor realizes from Max's notes that the temperature is rising and that they have about 48 hours to reach a geyser that can carry them back to the surface. Crossing an underground sea on a raft, they are attacked by piranhas, and Sean is separated from the others; guided by a small glowing bird, he is rescued by Trevor from an albino Giganotosaurus. Finding the geyser dry, Trevor ignites magnesium in the rock with a flare, and the blast of water and steam shoots them out of Mount Vesuvius in Italy. Sean's diamonds pay for damage to a vineyard, fund Max's lab and buy Trevor and Hannah, who have fallen for each other, a new home. As Sean's visit ends, Trevor hands him a book about Atlantis.

Warner Bros. Pictures released the film on July 11, 2008, and it introduced the 4DX motion-seat format in Seoul. It grossed $245 million worldwide against a $60 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 60% on Rotten Tomatoes, and 57 on Metacritic, while audiences gave it an A− CinemaScore.

overview: An NYPD hostage negotiator teams up with a federal agent to rescue dozens of tourists held hostage during a 10-hour seige at the U.S. Federal Reserve.
title: Inside Man: Most Wanted
plot:
Inside Man: Most Wanted is a 2019 American crime thriller film directed by M. J. Bassett and a sequel to Spike Lee's 2006 film Inside Man, made after plans for a sequel with the original cast were cancelled in 2011. It stars Aml Ameen as NYPD hostage negotiator Remy Darbonne, Rhea Seehorn as FBI hostage negotiator Brynn Stewart and Roxanne McKee as the bank robber Ariella Barash, with Jessica Sutton as her sister Ava, Urs Rechn as the robber Joseph and Akshay Kumar as FBI agent Ansh Ramachandra.

Five years after Dalton Russell's crew robbed the bank of Arthur Case and exposed him as a Nazi collaborator, a gang of robbers led by Ariella Barash seizes the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, taking everyone inside hostage. Their target is a large hoard of Nazi gold kept in the building. A joint task force headed by Stewart and Darbonne is deployed, and as the two negotiate with Ariella, who calls herself "Most Wanted", each begins separately to piece together her real motives. Arthur Case has died under house arrest, and his son Dietrich has taken Dalton, whose real name is David Barash, hostage, forcing his sister Ariella to stage the heist so that Dietrich can recover the fortune his father lost. Unknown to the negotiators and to the rest of her crew, Ariella and her sister Ava have engineered the robbery to look like a failure, leaving subtle clues for the investigators to find. Ava, outside the bank, gets close to Darbonne by claiming that her abusive ex-boyfriend is one of the robbers. Ariella leaves a family photograph in a safety deposit box that reveals the siblings' connection to David, and gives Stewart a mobile phone to guarantee Dietrich's arrest and the recovery of the gold. The FBI arrests Dietrich and recovers the gold, but not before he orders the execution of David, held captive by Nazis in Berlin. In the aftermath, Darbonne and Stewart wonder what has become of Ariella and Ava, and Darbonne predicts that Ariella is alive and that people will die once she learns her brother is dead. In a mid-credits scene, a disguised Ariella walks into a bar in Berlin and guns down Dietrich's men, avenging David.

Ameen was cast in November 2018, and the score was composed by Sonya Belousova and Giona Ostinelli. The film was released direct to video in the United States on 24 September 2019 and also made available on Netflix and other digital platforms.

overview: Set in the changing world of the late 1960s, Susanna Kaysen's prescribed "short rest" from a psychiatrist she had met only once becomes a strange, unknown journey into Alice's Wonderland, where she struggles with the thin line between normal and crazy. Susanna soon realizes how hard it is to get out once she has been committed, and she ultimately has to choose between the world of people who belong inside or the difficult world of reality outside.
tagline: The crazy thing is, you're not crazy.
title: Girl, Interrupted
plot:
Girl, Interrupted is a psychological drama film directed by James Mangold, released in 1999 by Columbia Pictures. The movie is based on the semi-autobiographical novel of the same name by Susanna Kaysen.

The main themes of Girl, Interrupted revolve around:

1. **Mental illness and recovery**: The film explores the experiences of women with mental illnesses, such as borderline personality disorder, in a psychiatric hospital during the 1960s. It delves into the complexities of diagnosis, treatment, and recovery, highlighting the struggles of those who have been institutionalized.

2. **Female empowerment and identity**: The protagonist, Susanna Kaysen (played by Winona Ryder), is a young woman struggling to find her place in the world. As she navigates the hospital's strict rules and societal expectations, she begins to assert her individuality and challenge the patriarchal norms that have shaped her life.

3. **Trauma, abuse, and survival**: The film touches on themes of childhood trauma, emotional abuse, and the resilience of women who have been subjected to these experiences. Susanna's story is intertwined with those of her fellow patients, including Lisa (Angelina Jolie), who has a troubled past and struggles with her own identity.

4. **The complexities of human relationships**: Girl, Interrupted explores the intricate web of relationships between the characters, including friendships, romantic connections, and therapeutic bonds. These relationships serve as a source of support, comfort, and sometimes, conflict.

5. **Social commentary on the 1960s**: The film provides a commentary on the social attitudes and cultural norms of the 1960s, particularly regarding women's roles in society. It critiques the restrictive nature of psychiatric institutions and the limited options available to women during that era.

Throughout the movie, these themes are expertly woven together to create a powerful narrative that explores the complexities of the human experience.

overview: With the 70s behind him, San Diego's top rated newsman, Ron Burgundy, returns to take New York's first 24-hour news channel by storm.
tagline: It's kind of a big deal
title: Anchorman 2: The Legend Continues
plot:
Anchorman 2: The Legend Continues is a comedy film directed by Adam McKay, released in 2013. The movie follows Ron Burgundy (Will Ferrell) and his news team as they navigate the changing media landscape of the 1970s.

The main themes of Anchorman 2: The Legend Continues include:

1. **The Evolution of Media**: The film explores the shift from traditional print journalism to television and cable news, highlighting the challenges faced by news anchors in adapting to new technologies and formats.
2. **Nostalgia and Tradition**: Ron Burgundy's character is a nostalgic representation of the past, clinging to his old-school values and methods despite the changing world around him. This theme serves as a commentary on the importance of tradition and heritage in an increasingly fast-paced and modern society.
3. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As the news team faces new challenges and opportunities, they are forced to re-evaluate their identities and roles within the industry. Ron Burgundy's character, in particular, must confront his own relevance and purpose in a rapidly changing world.
4. **Friendship and Camaraderie**: The movie celebrates the bonds of friendship and camaraderie among the news team, highlighting the importance of teamwork and loyalty in the face of adversity.

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together with humor, satire, and heart, creating a unique and entertaining viewing experience that pays homage to the original Anchorman while also exploring new ideas and perspectives.

original_title: The Little Rascals Save the Day
overview: When the Little Rascals are unable to raise enough money to save their grandma's bakery from shutting down, their only hope is to win a local talent show and use the prize money to save the shop.
tagline: The Little Rascals Are Back
title: The Little Rascals Save the Day
plot:
The Little Rascals Save the Day is a 2014 American comedy film directed by Penelope Spheeris. The movie is based on the classic series of short films featuring the "Little Rascals," a group of young friends who get into various misadventures.

The main themes of The Little Rascals Save the Day include:

1. Friendship and camaraderie: The film highlights the strong bonds between the Little Rascals, showcasing their loyalty, trust, and support for one another as they work together to save the day.
2. Teamwork and collaboration: The movie emphasizes the importance of working together towards a common goal, demonstrating how each character's unique skills and strengths contribute to the team's success.
3. Overcoming adversity: The Little Rascals face various challenges and obstacles, but they persevere and find creative solutions to overcome them, teaching viewers about resilience and determination.
4. Nostalgia and retro charm: The film pays homage to the original series, incorporating many of the classic characters and elements that fans of the franchise love.

The plot follows Spanky (played by Auggie Maturo), Buckwheat (Jordan Warkol), Darla (Mila Brener), and the rest of the Little Rascals as they try to save their neighborhood from a greedy developer who wants to tear it down. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, teamwork, and standing up for what's right.

Overall, The Little Rascals Save the Day is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the spirit of childhood friendships and the power of working together towards a common goal.

overview: A teenage girl and her father travel to a remote alien moon, aiming to strike it rich. They've secured a contract to harvest a large deposit of the elusive gems hidden in the depths of the moon's toxic forest. But there are others roving the wilderness and the job quickly devolves into a fight to survive.
tagline: No one survives alone.
title: Prospect
plot:
Prospect is a 2018 science fiction film directed by Zal Batmanglij and written by Batmanglij and Joe Barton. The movie follows two characters, M: A Humanoid Robot (played by Sophie Thatcher) and her companion, a humanoid robot named C (played by Pedro Pascal), who embark on a perilous journey through space to find a new home after their spaceship is damaged.

The main theme of Prospect revolves around the concept of loneliness and isolation. The film explores how humans and robots can form deep connections with each other in a desolate environment, highlighting the emotional needs that even artificial beings have. As M and C navigate through the vastness of space, they confront existential questions about their own existence, purpose, and what it means to be alive.

The movie also delves into themes of identity, self-discovery, and the blurred lines between human and machine. Through the characters' interactions and relationships, Prospect raises thought-provoking questions about the nature of consciousness, free will, and the consequences of playing god with technology.

Furthermore, the film touches on the idea of hope and resilience in the face of adversity. Despite being stranded in a hostile environment, M and C find ways to adapt, survive, and even thrive, showcasing their capacity for growth, love, and connection.

Overall, Prospect is a poignant and visually stunning exploration of what it means to be human (or not) in a vast, uncaring universe.

overview: Travis Block is a shadowy Government agent who specializes in removing operatives whose covers have been exposed. He then has to uncover a deadly conspiracy within his own ranks that reaches the highest echelons of power.
tagline: They're gonna need more men.
title: Blacklight
plot:
Blacklight is a 2022 action thriller directed and co-written by Mark Williams. Liam Neeson stars as Travis Block, an off-the-books fixer for the FBI who stumbles onto a government conspiracy, with Emmy Raver-Lampman as the journalist Mira Jones, Taylor John Smith as the undercover agent Dusty Crane and Aidan Quinn as FBI Director Gabriel Robinson. It was shot in Melbourne, with a car chase filmed in Canberra, and Mark Isham composed the score.

After a rally in Washington, D.C., the political activist Sofia Flores is killed in a deliberate hit-and-run outside her home. Travis, a Vietnam veteran who quietly handles problems for Robinson, wants to retire and spend time with his daughter Amanda and granddaughter Natalie, but Robinson gives him one more job: bringing in Dusty Crane, an undercover agent who has gone rogue. Dusty has contacted Mira, claiming to know the truth about Sofia's death, and keeps slipping away. When Travis finally reaches him, Dusty says that Robinson ordered the killing, moments before he is shot dead by two FBI agents.

Mira tells Travis that Dusty had spoken of Operation Unity, a secret program run by Robinson that murders innocent civilians. Robinson waves off Travis's questions and warns him to stay away. Mira's editor, Drew, publishes a story about Dusty's death and is killed that night by the same pair of agents, and Amanda and Natalie vanish. Persuaded to help Mira, Travis forces Robinson to open a safe at his house, fights his way past a group of agents, and recovers a hard drive. It reveals that Dusty had fallen in love with Sofia, the woman he was assigned to watch, and that Robinson had her killed because of it. Travis compels Robinson to surrender, Mira publishes the story of the cover-up, and Travis retires and is reunited with his family, who had been placed in witness protection.

Briarcliff Entertainment released the film in the United States on 11 February 2022, where it opened fifth at the box office with $3.5 million. Against a budget of $43 million, it grossed only about $16 million worldwide and was a box-office bomb. Critics were harsh: it holds an 11% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose entire consensus reads "Turn it off," and a Metacritic score of 27.

original_title: 進撃の巨人 ATTACK ON TITAN
overview: 100 years ago, titans suddenly appeared on Earth. Soon, human civilization veered on collapse due to the titans. Humans then built a giant wall to defend themselves. Within the giant walls, humans lived in peace, but, 100 years later, the giant wall is broken.
title: Attack on Titan
plot:
Attack on Titan is a 2015 Japanese post-apocalyptic action film directed by Shinji Higuchi and written by Yūsuke Watanabe and Tomohiro Machiyama, the first of two live-action films based on Hajime Isayama's manga. At Isayama's suggestion, the story moves its setting to an analogue of Japan and adds new characters. Haruma Miura stars as Eren, with Kiko Mizuhara as Mikasa, Kanata Hongō as Armin, Hiroki Hasegawa as Captain Shikishima, Pierre Taki as Souda, Jun Kunimura as Kubal, Satomi Ishihara as Hange and Nanami Sakuraba as Sasha.

A century ago, giant humanoid Titans appeared and wiped out most of humanity, and the survivors walled themselves in to live in peace. In the village of Monzen, Eren tells his friends Armin and Mikasa that he longs to see the world beyond the Outer Wall, and after a failed attempt to approach it, the Garrison captain Souda tells them that the military is forming a scouting regiment to explore outside.
