Suddenly the Colossal Titan breaches the wall, and Titans pour into the village, devouring people and regenerating whenever they are wounded. While trying to save a baby, Mikasa is separated from Eren and presumed dead. Two years later, Eren and Armin join the Scout Regiment along with Sasha, Jean and others, led by Kubal, they set out for a town inside the Outer Wall. Attacked by Titans, they are rescued by Captain Shikishima and by Mikasa, who survived and has joined the Scouts but now treats Eren like a stranger. She tells him that the disaster taught her how cruel the world is, and Eren is crushed to realize that she is probably with Shikishima. When more Titans strike, Kubal retreats and leaves the Scouts to fend for themselves. Lil, who has just lost her lover, sacrifices herself, and Eren, refusing Jean's pleas to flee, loses an arm and is swallowed while saving Armin. A grief-stricken Mikasa fights on until her gear runs low on fuel and she faces the Titan that ate Eren, when a new Titan bursts out of it and begins battling the others. Souda and Mikasa realize that it is Eren, and as it collapses, Mikasa pulls him free from the Titan's body.

After a world premiere at the Egyptian Theatre in Los Angeles on 14 July 2015, the film opened in Japan on 1 August, followed by the second part, End of the World, in September. It topped the Japanese box office on its opening weekend and grossed ¥3.25 billion. Critics were mixed, praising the Titan designs and B-movie style while faulting the script and departures from the manga.

overview: Eric, a highly-gifted golfer but radically-undisciplined college undergrad, finds his world drastically altered after losing a golf bet to a pair of sadistic plastic surgeons. Eric's bad-boy attitude lifestyle comes to a screeching halt as he loses his money, his girlfriend, his dignity and his golf swing. Eric and his best friend Tyler decide to take on the doctors, in a final golf match of "Best-Ball" to get his life back and become the man he should have been all along.
tagline: Big Risk, Big Rewards & Big Attitude!
title: Hole in One
plot:
Hole in One, also released as ParFection: The Golf Movie, is an American sports sex comedy directed by Drew Ann Rosenberg and written by Mike Terrell and Mark Maine. Steve Talley stars as Eric Keller, a talented but undisciplined college golfer, with David Ellison as his friend Tyler Hayden, Sandy Modic as Tyler's sister Mandy, Dean Cameron and Christopher Showerman as a pair of scheming plastic surgeons, K.T. Tatara as Mark, and Dean Cain as a repo man.

Keller skips class to hustle strangers on the golf course, unaware that two men are watching him. At a party he nearly gets close to Mandy, whose protective brother Tyler, struggling to launch his golf apparel business PAHR, disapproves of Keller's lifestyle. When Keller hooks up with another student and Mark secretly films it, the video is shown at Tyler's shop and Mandy is hurt. Keller then accepts a match against the two strangers, who turn out to be surgeons Dr. Carlton and Dr. Hamilton of the company NuBoobs. If he wins he gets $50,000; if he loses, he becomes their test patient. The man who had been helping Keller hustle golfers turns out to be helping the doctors hustle him, and after losing he is tased and wakes up with breast implants.

The surgeons will only reverse the operation for $50,000, and give him two weeks to pay before they mail his photographs to family and friends. With Tyler's encouragement, Keller returns to the course and wins round after round, growing used to golfing with his new figure, while a repo man pursues his overdue Mustang. The pair raise $42,000, still short, so Keller proposes a final match: if they win, the surgery is reversed for free, and if they lose, Tyler gives up PAHR. Keller struggles until Mandy arrives with his father, who has received the photos anyway. Mandy forgives him, his father urges him to pursue golf, and Keller wins by a single stroke. The surgeons refuse to honor the deal but are chased off by a rapper's bodyguards, and the rapper agrees to back PAHR.

Distributed by Universal, the film launched in the United Kingdom on 12 September 2010, with releases in some 65 further territories. Although it was promoted with the tagline "American Pie Plays Golf" and stars Talley, who had appeared in two American Pie spin-offs, it is not part of that series. It drew little critical attention.

overview: When his wealthy grandfather finally dies, Jason Stevens fully expects to benefit when it comes to the reading of the will. But instead of a sizable inheritance, Jason receives a test, a series of tasks he must complete before he can get any money.
tagline: Life is how you live it... not how you spend it.
title: The Ultimate Gift
plot:
The Ultimate Gift is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of family relationships, love, and the true meaning of wealth. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of letting go and embracing the present moment.

The story follows Jason Stevens, a young man who has lost touch with his roots and is struggling to find direction in life. As he navigates through various challenges, he comes to realize that the ultimate gift he can give himself is the ability to appreciate the beauty of simplicity and the love of those around him.

Through Jason's journey, the film highlights the importance of family bonds and the value of cherishing memories with loved ones. The movie also touches on the theme of material wealth versus spiritual wealth, suggesting that true happiness and fulfillment come from within.

One of the most striking aspects of The Ultimate Gift is its exploration of the concept of legacy. The character of Buck Stevens, Jason's grandfather, serves as a symbol of wisdom, love, and selflessness. Through his story, the film shows how our actions and decisions can have a lasting impact on those around us, leaving behind a legacy that transcends time.

Ultimately, The Ultimate Gift is a movie about finding one's way back to what truly matters in life – love, family, and the present moment. It is a poignant reminder to appreciate the beauty of simplicity and to cherish the relationships that bring joy and meaning to our lives.

overview: Two teenage yoga enthusiasts team up with a legendary man-hunter to battle with an ancient evil presence that is threatening their major party plans.
tagline: Do your 'wurst...
title: Yoga Hosers
plot:
Yoga Hosers is a 2016 Canadian horror-comedy film directed by Kevin Smith and written by Smith and Scott Mosier. The movie follows two teenage girls, Colleen Collette and Jeremy "Josh" Collette, who work at a convenience store in the frozen tundra of Canada.

The main themes of Yoga Hosers revolve around the idea of female empowerment, friendship, and the struggle for independence. The film's protagonist, Colleen, is a strong-willed and determined young woman who refuses to be bound by societal expectations. She is fiercely loyal to her best friend Josh and will stop at nothing to protect him.

The movie also explores themes of nostalgia, as it pays homage to classic 80s and 90s pop culture, from music to fashion to movies. The film's use of retro aesthetics and references adds to its lighthearted and humorous tone, which balances out the horror elements.

Furthermore, Yoga Hosers touches on the idea of small-town America and the struggles that come with living in a remote community. The film's setting, a frozen wasteland in Canada, serves as a metaphor for the isolation and confinement that can come with rural life.

Overall, Yoga Hosers is a fun and entertaining film that celebrates female friendship, independence, and the power of pop culture to bring people together.

overview: The story of Elton John's life, from his years as a prodigy at the Royal Academy of Music through his influential and enduring musical partnership with Bernie Taupin.
tagline: Based on a True Fantasy
title: Rocketman
plot:
Rocketman (2019) is a biographical musical drama film directed by Dexter Fletcher, written by Jamie Bell, Lee Hall, and Tom Bennett, and produced by Graham Broadbent, Peter Cavatt, and Tim Bevan.

The main themes of Rocketman (2019) include:

1. **The struggle with fame and identity**: The film explores the highs and lows of Elton John's rise to fame, as he navigates the pressures of stardom while trying to maintain his artistic integrity and individuality.
2. **Mental health and addiction**: Rocketman delves into Elton John's struggles with depression, anxiety, and addiction, showcasing the devastating effects these issues had on his life and relationships.
3. **Love and relationships**: The film highlights Elton John's tumultuous relationships with his manager, songwriter Bernie Taupin, and his husband, David Furnish, as well as his complicated friendships and romantic entanglements.
4. **Creative expression and legacy**: Rocketman celebrates Elton John's remarkable musical talent and the enduring power of his music, while also exploring the challenges he faced in maintaining creative control throughout his career.
5. **Self-discovery and redemption**: The film follows Elton John's journey towards self-acceptance, forgiveness, and personal growth, as he confronts his past mistakes and learns to find peace and happiness.

The movie features a star-studded cast, including Taron Egerton as Elton John, Jamie Bell as Bernie Taupin, and Richard Madden as John Reid. The film's music is an integral part of the story, with many of Elton John's iconic hits featured in the soundtrack.

Overall, Rocketman (2019) is a powerful and poignant biographical drama that explores the complexities of fame, identity, love, and creativity through the remarkable life story of Elton John.

overview: After Air Force One goes down during a storm over the Bermuda Triangle, the United States Navy is dispatched to find the escape pod holding the President. A giant monster beneath the ocean awakens and attacks the fleet.
title: Bermuda Tentacles
plot:
Bermuda Tentacles is a 2014 American made-for-television science fiction action horror film directed by Nick Lyon and produced by The Asylum for the Syfy channel. Linda Hamilton heads a cast that also includes Trevor Donovan, Mýa, John Savage and Jamie Kennedy, in a story about a naval rescue mission in the Bermuda Triangle that runs into gigantic tentacled creatures of alien origin. It premiered on Syfy in April 2014.

While Air Force One is flying through a storm over the Bermuda Triangle, a massive lightning strike knocks out its engines, and President DeSteno is placed in a high-tech escape pod, given a gun and jettisoned moments before the plane explodes. The pod sinks some 7,000 metres to the ocean floor, and with his air supply limited, the Navy dispatches a fleet and an elite special forces team to retrieve him. The team, led by the reckless young Chief Trip Oliver, reports to Admiral Hansen, with whom Oliver shares a history of friction. Before a rescue can be planned, the ships are attacked by enormous translucent tentacles rising from the sea, which snatch and impale sailors and swat helicopters and planes out of the sky, while even larger squid-like limbs join the assault. The ship's scientist, Dr. Zimmer, quickly identifies the creatures as giant tube worms, and only concentrated firepower seems to harm them. Oliver's unit descends in an experimental submersible, following the pod's beacon into a vast undersea chamber filled with ships and aircraft lost in the Triangle over the centuries, and realise they have found the cause of the disappearances. Fighting off more tentacles, they rescue the president, though most of the team is killed. They then discover that the "city" is in fact a colossal alien spacecraft, which rises from the ocean and heads for the Florida coast, destroying naval vessels as it goes, while the president pushes for all-out war. Oliver devises a plan to stop it, and a well-placed rocket fired into the ship's core destroys it before it reaches land.

Hamilton plays Hansen, with Donovan as Oliver, Mýa as Lieutenant Plummer, Savage as DeSteno and Kennedy as Zimmer. Critics panned the film. HorrorNews.Net's Shawn Handling criticised its acting, writing, effects and score, concluding that it deserved to be sunk with the Triangle's missing ships, and Dread Central compared it unfavourably with Deep Rising, The Abyss and Independence Day, describing it as repetitive and short on imagination.

cast: Juan Cruz Márquez de la Serna
overview: In Argentina, between 1982 and 1985, the Puccios, a well-established family of San Isidro, an upper-class suburb of Buenos Aires, kidnap several people and hold them as hostages for a ransom.
tagline: The true story of Argentina's most notorious crime family
title: The Clan
plot:
The Clan is a 2015 Spanish drama film directed by Pablo Trapero and produced by El Deseo. The movie revolves around the true story of the Puccio family, an Italian-Argentine clan involved in organized crime.

At its core, The Clan explores the dark and complex world of organized crime, delving into themes of power, loyalty, and the corrupting influence it can have on individuals and families. The film sheds light on how the pursuit of wealth and status can lead people to compromise their values and morals, ultimately destroying their relationships and sense of self.

The movie also examines the theme of family dynamics and the ways in which crime can be passed down through generations. The Puccio family's history is marked by violence, betrayal, and manipulation, highlighting how these patterns can become ingrained in a family's culture and lead to devastating consequences.

Furthermore, The Clan touches on the idea of identity and how it can be shaped by one's environment and circumstances. The characters are often torn between their loyalty to their family and their own sense of morality, leading to internal conflicts that ultimately define them.

The film also critiques the societal factors that contribute to the rise of organized crime, such as poverty, inequality, and a lack of opportunities. By exploring these themes, The Clan provides a nuanced portrayal of the complexities involved in the world of organized crime, one that is both thought-provoking and deeply unsettling.

overview: The company of three guys and two girls makes their way to the old funicular to have an unforgettable New Year’s Eve celebration at the top of the mountain. A fun adventure turns into a nightmare when the funicular stops over the abyss. Coldness, height and fear of a slow death make them reveal their true essence and get in a fight with each other.
tagline: Trapped at 11,000 feet...
title: Break
plot:
Break (Russian: Otryv) is a 2018 Russian survival thriller directed by Tigran Saakyan from a screenplay by Olga Rud, Saakyan and Denis Kosyakov. Produced by Sergei Selyanov, Artur Astvatsatryan and Oleg Yakovlev for the companies CTB and Attraction, it stars Irina Antonenko, a former Miss Russia, as Katya, Kosyakov as Denis Seleznyov, Ingrid Olerinskaya as Vika, Mikhail Filippov as Roman Mikalovich and Andrey Nazimov as Kirill. Sergei Dyshuk was the cinematographer and Aleksei Chintsov composed the score; the film runs 82 minutes.

On New Year's Eve, a group of five friends, three young men and two women, decide to celebrate at the top of a mountain for an unforgettable experience, and make their way to an old funicular. Things go wrong from the start: Katya's boyfriend Kirill suddenly refuses to board the cable car, while she refuses to get off, so the rest of the group rides up with her. The car stops unexpectedly, then starts moving again when the power returns, so when it halts a second time nobody thinks much of it and they begin celebrating the New Year right there. By the morning of 1 January, however, the car still has not moved, and they realize they are stuck high above an abyss with no way to call for help. At first they expect rescue to come, and they light a fire with whatever rubbish they can find to keep warm, but it soon dies out along with their hope. Cold, height and the fear of a slow death bring out their basest survival instincts. An attempt to climb down the cable ends when one of them falls into a crevice hidden beneath the snow, and as the remaining friends lose hope, a struggle for survival breaks out inside the car, revealing who they really are.

Break premiered at the Oktyabr cinema in Moscow on 12 February 2019 and opened in Russian cinemas two days later, earning about 7.5 million rubles in its first weekend and roughly 200,000 dollars in total. It drew accusations of plagiarism because of its similarity to Adam Green's 2010 American thriller Frozen. Reviewing it for Russo Rosso, Dmitry Sokolov nevertheless considered it a self-sufficient work rather than a pale copy, praising its well-constructed predicaments, its momentum, the performances of Antonenko and Filippov and the camerawork, but criticizing shifts in tone, a melodramatic final third and too many references to other films. Saakyan and Rud received a special prize at the Kaplya awards for their contribution to Russian genre cinema.

keywords.name: based on song, poem or rhyme

overview: An independent, single mother who owns a small hotel on a Greek island is about to marry off the spirited young daughter she's raised alone. But, the daughter has secretly invited three of her mother's ex-lovers in the hopes of finding her biological father.
tagline: Take a trip down the aisle you'll never forget
title: Mamma Mia!
plot:
Mamma Mia! is a 2008 jukebox musical romantic comedy directed by Phyllida Lloyd and written by Catherine Johnson, adapted from her book for the 1999 stage musical. Meryl Streep stars as Donna Sheridan, Amanda Seyfried as her daughter, Sophie, and Pierce Brosnan, Colin Firth and Stellan Skarsgård as Sophie's possible fathers, Sam, Harry and Bill, with Julie Walters, Christine Baranski and Dominic Cooper.

On the Greek island of Kalokairi, 20-year-old bride-to-be Sophie tells her bridesmaids that she has secretly invited three of Donna's old lovers to her wedding: Irish-American architect Sam Carmichael, Swedish travel writer Bill Anderson and British banker Harry Bright. One of them is her father, and she hopes to recognize which after spending time with them, so he can give her away. When the men arrive, believing Donna invited them, Sophie hides them in a goat house, where Donna, stunned, discovers them and orders them to leave, confiding to Rosie and Tanya, her former bandmates in Donna and the Dynamos, that she truly does not know who Sophie's father is. Sophie sails with the men on Bill's boat as they share stories of Donna's carefree youth.

At her bachelorette party, Sophie speaks to each man privately, and Bill, Sam and Harry each come to believe that he is her father and agree to walk her down the aisle in secret. Sam and Donna realize they still have feelings for each other, and Sky reacts angrily when Sophie confesses her scheme. Before the ceremony, Donna reveals that her own mother disowned her when she became pregnant but that she is proud of her daughter, and Sophie asks Donna to give her away. At the altar, Sam explains that he had broken off his engagement years earlier, only to find Donna with another man. The three men agree with Sophie that paternity does not matter and each will be a third of a father. Sophie and Sky postpone their wedding to travel the world, and Sam, now divorced, proposes to Donna, who accepts and marries him on the spot.

Filmed mainly on Skopelos in 2007, with ABBA's Benny Andersson and Björn Ulvaeus composing the score, the film premiered in London on June 30, 2008, and Universal released it in the United States on July 18. Reviews were mixed, with 54% on Rotten Tomatoes, but it grossed $708.2 million on a $52 million budget, becoming the highest-grossing live-action musical at the time.

overview: Recruited by the U.S. government to be a special agent, nerdy teenager Cody Banks must get closer to cute classmate Natalie in order to learn about an evil plan hatched by her father. But despite the agent persona, Cody struggles with teen angst.
tagline: Save the world. Get the girl. Pass math.
title: Agent Cody Banks
plot:
Agent Cody Banks is an action-comedy film that revolves around the story of a young secret agent, Cody Banks, who must navigate his way through high school while working for the Central Intelligence Agency. The movie explores several themes, primarily focusing on identity, loyalty, and self-discovery.

At its core, Agent Cody Banks is a coming-of-age story about a teenager trying to balance his dual life as a spy and a student. As Cody navigates his relationships with his mentor, Agent Ronny Campanella, and his love interest, Natalie Connors, he must confront the challenges of growing up and finding his place in the world.

The film also delves into themes of loyalty and duty, particularly through Cody's relationship with Agent Campanella. As Cody struggles to prove himself as a capable agent, he must also navigate the complexities of loyalty to his mentor and the CIA. This internal conflict serves as a catalyst for Cody's growth and development as a character.

Furthermore, Agent Cody Banks touches on the theme of identity, particularly in the context of Cody's dual life. As he navigates between his spy persona and his everyday life as a high school student, Cody must confront the question of who he truly is and what he wants to achieve in life.

Overall, Agent Cody Banks is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and self-discovery through the lens of a young secret agent's journey.

overview: Shaun lives a supremely uneventful life, which revolves around his girlfriend, his mother, and, above all, his local pub. This gentle routine is threatened when the dead return to life and make strenuous attempts to snack on ordinary Londoners.
tagline: A romantic comedy. With zombies.
title: Shaun of the Dead
plot:
Shaun of the Dead is a 2004 British romantic zombie comedy film directed by Edgar Wright and written by Wright and Simon Pegg. The movie follows the life of Shaun, a 29-year-old slacker who lives with his mother, Barbara, in a small house in London.

At the beginning of the film, Shaun is struggling to find direction in his life. He works as an IT consultant for a large corporation, but he's unhappy and feels unfulfilled. His only friends are his best friend Ed and his on-again, off-again girlfriend Liz. However, their relationship is strained due to Shaun's lack of ambition and commitment.

The story takes a dramatic turn when a zombie outbreak occurs in London, caused by a mysterious virus that reanimates the dead. The zombies are slow-moving but relentless, and they seem to be attracted to noise and human activity. As the situation spirals out of control, Shaun is forced to confront his own shortcomings and take responsibility for his life.

Shaun's mother, Barbara, is initially resistant to the idea of a zombie apocalypse, but eventually she becomes infected after being bitten by one of the zombies. This event sets off a chain reaction of chaos in Shaun's life, as he must navigate the treacherous new world while trying to save his loved ones.

As Shaun navigates the zombie-infested streets of London, he teams up with Ed and Liz to find a safe haven. They eventually discover that their local pub, The Winchester, has been converted into a zombie-free zone by a group of survivors led by a charismatic leader named Fingerman. However, things take a turn for the worse when Shaun's mother is bitten, and he must make an impossible choice between saving her life or sacrificing her to save himself.

In the end, Shaun makes the ultimate sacrifice to save his mother, but not before she bites him as well. This sets off a chain reaction of events that ultimately leads to the destruction of the pub and the death of many of the survivors. However, Shaun emerges victorious, having saved his loved ones and found a new sense of purpose.

Throughout the film, Wright uses humor, satire, and social commentary to critique modern British society. The movie pokes fun at the conventions of zombie movies while also exploring themes of identity, community, and redemption. Pegg's performance as Shaun is particularly noteworthy, capturing the character's awkwardness, vulnerability, and ultimate heroism.

Overall, Shaun of the Dead is a hilarious and heartwarming film that has become a cult classic. Its unique blend of humor, action, and romance makes it a must-see for fans of zombie movies and comedy.

overview: As a young scientist searches for a way to save a dying Earth, she finds a connection with a man who's racing to catch the last shuttle off the planet.
tagline: In the near future we must save Earth or leave it
title: IO
plot:
IO is a 2019 science fiction film that explores the theme of human connection and intimacy in a world where technology has become an integral part of our lives. The movie takes place on a spaceship, the IO, which travels through space to colonize new planets. However, due to a catastrophic event, the ship's systems begin to fail, causing it to drift towards its destination.

The main theme of the film is the importance of human relationships and intimacy in the face of technological failure and isolation. The story revolves around the relationship between two characters, Eve (played by Margaret Qualley) and Max (played by Tom Hiddleston), who are part of a small group of survivors on board the ship.

As the ship's systems fail, Eve and Max find themselves isolated from each other, leading to a deep exploration of their emotional connection. The film delves into the complexities of human intimacy, highlighting the importance of physical touch, emotional vulnerability, and trust in relationships.

Through the characters' experiences, the movie raises questions about what it means to be human in a world where technology is increasingly controlling our lives. It also touches on themes of loneliness, isolation, and the human need for connection and community.

Ultimately, IO is a thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to consider the role of technology in our lives and the importance of nurturing our emotional connections with others.

overview: It has been twenty years since Don Diego de la Vega fought Spanish oppression in Alta California as the legendary romantic hero, Zorro. Having escaped from prison he transforms troubled bandit Alejandro into his successor, in order to foil the plans of the tyrannical Don Rafael Montero who robbed him of his freedom, his wife and his precious daughter.
tagline: No one has seen his face... but everyone ... knows this mark.
title: The Mask of Zorro
plot:
The Mask of Zorro is a 1998 American swashbuckler film directed by Martin Campbell and produced by Amblin Entertainment. The movie is set in 1820s California, during the Mexican-American War.

The story begins with the introduction of Captain Alejandro Murrieta (Antonio Banderas), a Spanish nobleman who has been wrongly accused of being a bandit and sentenced to death. However, before he can be executed, he escapes from prison and flees to the mountains, where he assumes the identity of Zorro, a legendary masked vigilante.

Meanwhile, in the town of San Juan Bautista, Don Diego de la Vega (Antonio Banderas), the son of the wealthy and influential Don Diego, is struggling to find his place in society. He is expected to take over his father's business, but he feels suffocated by the responsibilities and longs for adventure.

One day, a group of bandits led by Captain Murrieta arrive in San Juan Bautista, seeking revenge against the town that wronged him. Don Diego, who has been watching from afar, decides to take matters into his own hands and assumes the identity of Zorro to protect his father's business and the people he cares about.

As Zorro, Don Diego sets out to avenge Captain Murrieta's family and defeat the bandits. Along the way, he meets a beautiful and feisty woman named Elena Monasterio (Catherine Zeta-Jones), who becomes his ally and potential love interest.

Throughout the movie, Don Diego struggles with the dual identity of Zorro and his own sense of self-worth. He must balance his desire for adventure and justice with his responsibilities as a member of society. Meanwhile, Captain Murrieta's true intentions are revealed, and Don Diego must confront him in order to save Elena and the town.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between Zorro and Captain Murrieta, with Don Diego ultimately emerging victorious. In the process, he also finds his own identity and purpose as a hero, rather than just a masked vigilante.

The Mask of Zorro features stunning action sequences, memorable characters, and a sweeping narrative that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption. The movie's blend of humor, adventure, and romance has made it a beloved classic among fans of the swashbuckler genre.

overview: Inspired by the incredible events surrounding a treacherous attempt to reach the summit of the world's highest mountain, "Everest" documents the awe-inspiring journey of two different expeditions challenged beyond their limits by one of the fiercest snowstorms ever encountered by mankind. Their mettle tested by the harshest of elements found on the planet, the climbers will face nearly impossible obstacles as a lifelong obsession becomes a breathtaking struggle for survival.
tagline: The Storm Awaits.
title: Everest
plot:
Everest is a 2015 biographical survival film directed and produced by Baltasar Kormákur from a screenplay by William Nicholson and Simon Beaufoy. It dramatizes the 1996 Mount Everest disaster, in which eight climbers died, following two commercial expeditions: Adventure Consultants, led by Rob Hall, and its rival Mountain Madness, guided by Scott Fischer.

In May 1996 the teams gather at base camp. Hall's clients include the experienced climber Beck Weathers, former mailman Doug Hansen, Yasuko Namba, who is chasing the last of her Seven Summits, and Outside journalist Jon Krakauer, while Helen Wilton runs the camp. Hall has promised his pregnant wife Jan in New Zealand that he will be home for the birth. He persuades Fischer to cooperate to limit crowding. On summit day the climbers lose more than an hour when they find fixed ropes missing on the upper slopes, and Beck, whose vision is failing, is told to wait and turn back if it does not improve. Hall reaches the top on schedule, but on the way down he meets Doug still struggling upward and, against his own 2 p.m. turnaround rule, lets him go on; they summit two hours late. A blizzard then hits. Doug, out of oxygen and hypoxic, wanders off the fixed line and falls to his death, and the ailing Fischer lies down and dies. Lost in the storm, other climbers leave Beck and Yasuko behind to seek help. Guide Andy Harris brings Hall oxygen, but the valve is frozen, and Harris later dies in a hallucinatory state. Stranded and frozen, Hall is put through to Jan, asks her to name their daughter Sarah, and dies. Beck revives, finds Yasuko dead and staggers into camp; his wife Peach arranges a helicopter rescue flown by Nepal Army pilot Madan Khatri Chhetri. Jan later gives birth to Sarah, and closing titles note that Beck lost his hands and nose to frostbite.

Jason Clarke plays Hall and Jake Gyllenhaal plays Fischer, with Josh Brolin as Weathers, John Hawkes as Hansen, Michael Kelly as Krakauer, Robin Wright as Peach, Sam Worthington as guide Guy Cotter and Emily Watson as Helen, alongside Keira Knightley and Martin Henderson. It was shot in Italy, Nepal and Iceland. The film opened the 72nd Venice International Film Festival on 2 September 2015 and was released by Universal, first in IMAX 3D. Critics praised its cinematography more than its storytelling, giving it 73% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Krakauer criticized it as partly fabricated. It grossed $221.3 million on a $55 million budget.

overview: After his wife and daughter are murdered in a home invasion, a widower named John now finds himself up against an army of Universal Soldiers in relentless pursuit, led by a mysterious leader who promises to set UniSols free from their conditioning.
tagline: Under their own command
title: Universal Soldier: Day of Reckoning
plot:
Universal Soldier: Day of Reckoning is an action-packed sci-fi film that delves into the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The movie explores the theme of free will versus determinism, as the main character, Luc Deveraux, struggles to regain his humanity after being subjected to a highly advanced nanotechnology that reprograms him to be a super-soldier.

The film also touches on the idea of identity and what it means to be human. As Deveraux navigates his newfound existence, he begins to question whether his actions are truly his own or if they're just a result of the programming implanted in him. This internal conflict serves as a catalyst for exploring the blurred lines between human and machine.

Furthermore, the movie critiques the notion of technological advancements without moral responsibility. The nanotechnology used on Deveraux is portrayed as a tool that can be exploited for military gain, highlighting the dangers of unchecked technological progress and the need for accountability in scientific research.

Ultimately, Universal Soldier: Day of Reckoning presents a thought-provoking narrative that challenges viewers to consider the implications of emerging technologies on human society.

overview: Follow the adventures of Belle, a bright young woman who finds herself in the castle of a prince who's been turned into a mysterious beast. With the help of the castle's enchanted staff, Belle soon learns the most important lesson of all -- that true beauty comes from within.
tagline: The most beautiful love story ever told.
title: Beauty and the Beast
plot:
Beauty and the Beast is a timeless tale of love, acceptance, and transformation, brought to life by Walt Disney Pictures in 1991.

In a small French village, a prince named Belle lives with her inventor father, Maurice. The villagers are wary of outsiders, and Belle's independent spirit often puts her at odds with the community. When Maurice gets lost in the forest, he seeks shelter in a mysterious castle belonging to the Beast, a prince who has been cursed by an enchantress for his arrogance.

The Beast imprisons Maurice, intending to kill him as punishment. However, Belle sets out to rescue her father and offers to take his place. The Beast agrees, but warns her that she will remain in the castle until he releases her. As Belle navigates the enchanted castle, she discovers a world of magic and wonder.

The Beast is a complex character, struggling with his own darkness and inner demons. He is forced to confront his past mistakes and learn to accept himself for who he truly is. Meanwhile, Belle's kindness and compassion begin to break down the Beast's defenses, and they form an unlikely bond.

As the story unfolds, Belle learns about the curse that afflicts the Beast and the enchantress's plan to break it. She also discovers a hidden library filled with books, which becomes her sanctuary in the castle. The Beast, too, finds solace in the company of Belle, who challenges him to see beyond his physical appearance.

As their relationship deepens, the Beast begins to transform before Belle's eyes. His physical form changes, and he becomes more human-like. However, the curse is not yet broken, and the enchantress demands that the Beast prove his love for Belle by sacrificing himself.

In a dramatic turn of events, the Beast saves Belle from the clutches of Gaston, a vain and arrogant suitor who seeks to marry her. The Beast's selfless act breaks the curse, and he is transformed back into a handsome prince. Belle and the prince fall in love, and they live happily ever after.

The 1991 Disney adaptation of Beauty and the Beast features stunning animation, memorable characters, and a timeless story that has captivated audiences for generations. The film's themes of acceptance, empathy, and the power of love continue to resonate with viewers today.

overview: Joe Toy, on the verge of adolescence, finds himself increasingly frustrated by his single father, Frank's attempts to manage his life. Declaring his freedom once and for all, he escapes to a clearing in the woods with his best friend, Patrick, and a strange kid named Biaggio. He announces that they are going to build a house there, free from responsibility and parents. Once their makeshift abode is finished, the three young men find themselves masters of their own destiny, alone in the woods.
tagline: Why live when you can rule.
title: The Kings of Summer
plot:
The Kings of Summer is a 2013 American coming-of-age comedy-drama film directed by Jordan Vogt-Roberts. The movie follows the story of Joe Toy, a teenager who runs away from home with his best friend Patrick to build a shelter in the woods and live off the land.

At its core, The Kings of Summer explores themes of rebellion, self-discovery, and the struggle for independence. Joe's decision to leave home is motivated by a desire to break free from the constraints of his family life and forge his own path in life. As he navigates the challenges of living in the wilderness, Joe must confront his own vulnerabilities and learn to rely on himself and his friend.

The film also delves into the complexities of male friendship and the ways in which boys navigate their relationships with each other during adolescence. Patrick's character serves as a foil to Joe's, highlighting the tensions and conflicts that can arise when two friends are forced to confront their own desires and needs.

Furthermore, The Kings of Summer touches on themes of identity and belonging. As Joe and Patrick try to create a new life for themselves in the woods, they must also navigate their relationships with the outside world and figure out where they fit into it. This is particularly evident in the character of Joe's father, who represents a more traditional and established way of life that Joe feels stifling.

Throughout the film, Vogt-Roberts uses humor and wit to explore these themes, often using satire and irony to highlight the absurdities and challenges of adolescence. Ultimately, The Kings of Summer is a heartwarming and relatable portrayal of growing up, self-discovery, and the power of male friendship.

overview: Gigli is ordered to kidnap the psychologically challenged younger brother of a powerful federal prosecutor. When plans go awry, Gigli's boss sends in Ricki, a gorgeous free-spirited female gangster who has her own set of orders to assist with the kidnapping. But Gigli begins falling for the decidedly unavailable Ricki, which could be a hazard to his occupation.
tagline: Life doesn't play by the rules.
title: Gigli
plot:
Gigli is a 2003 American romantic comedy crime film written, co-produced and directed by Martin Brest for Revolution Studios. Ben Affleck stars as Larry Gigli, a small-time Los Angeles mobster, and Jennifer Lopez as Ricki, a fellow enforcer sent to keep an eye on him, with Justin Bartha as Brian, Lenny Venito as Louis, Al Pacino as Starkman, Christopher Walken as Detective Stanley Jacobellis and Lainie Kazan in a supporting role.

Larry Gigli is a low-level hoodlum eager to prove that he is tougher and more capable than he really is. His boss, Louis, orders him to kidnap Brian, the intellectually disabled younger brother of a federal prosecutor, so that the prosecutor can be pressured into helping the New York mob boss Starkman stay out of prison. Larry lures Brian away by promising to take him "to the Baywatch", the television series he is obsessed with, but Louis does not trust him to handle the job alone and sends a woman calling herself Ricki to supervise. Larry is instantly attracted to her and resents taking orders from her, and his advances are rebuffed when she tells him that she is a lesbian. Hiding out in Larry's apartment, the trio grows more volatile; Brian keeps demanding to go to "the Baywatch" and runs up huge phone bills calling an Australian operator because he loves the accent. When Louis orders them to cut off Brian's thumb and mail it to the prosecutor, a horrified Larry instead steals a thumb from a corpse in a hospital morgue. As Larry opens up about himself and his frustrations, Ricki softens, and the two sleep together. Summoned before Starkman, they learn that he never approved the kidnapping and is furious, all the more because the thumb does not match Brian's fingerprints and so exposes the bluff. He kills Louis for drawing police attention and is ready to kill them too, until Ricki argues that only they can contain the damage. Spared, the pair decide to leave the mob. Driving along the coast with Brian, they come upon a beach video shoot that looks like Baywatch, and they let him off there, where he is delighted to meet an Australian woman. Larry urges Ricki to drive off without him, but she turns back, and they leave together to start a new life.

Released by Sony on 1 August 2003 amid intense coverage of the stars' off-screen romance, the film was savaged by critics, earning 6% on Rotten Tomatoes and 18 on Metacritic, and grossed $7.3 million on a budget of $75.6 million, one of the costliest flops in history.

overview: Dean and Cindy live a quiet life in a modest neighborhood. They appear to have the world at their feet at the outset of the relationship. However, his lack of ambition and her retreat into self-absorption cause potentially irreversible cracks in their marriage.
tagline: A Love Story.
title: Blue Valentine
plot:
Blue Valentine is a 2010 American romantic drama film directed by Derek Cianfrance and written by Dean Geistfeld. The movie stars Ryan Gosling and Michelle Williams as the lead characters, Cindy and Dean, who are experiencing marital problems.

The main themes of Blue Valentine revolve around the disintegration of a relationship, love, loss, regret, and the passage of time. Here's a brief overview:

Beginning: The film opens with a montage of happy memories from Cindy and Dean's early years together, showcasing their romance and commitment to each other. However, as the story progresses, we see the cracks in their relationship begin to form.

Plot Development: The movie is presented in a non-linear fashion, jumping back and forth between different periods of the couple's relationship. We witness the highs and lows, the arguments, and the moments of tenderness. As the years go by, Cindy and Dean grow apart, and their love becomes increasingly strained. They struggle to connect with each other, and their conversations become stilted.

Ending: The film ultimately ends on a bleak note, with Cindy having left Dean, and he is left alone, reflecting on what went wrong in their relationship. The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the fate of the couple.

Throughout the movie, Cianfrance masterfully captures the complexities of love, relationships, and the human experience. The film's themes are both poignant and thought-provoking, making it a powerful exploration of what happens when love fades away.

It appears that Hunting Lane Films is not associated with Blue Valentine (2010).

overview: A team of special forces head into Afghanistan in the aftermath of the September 11th attacks in an attempt to dismantle the Taliban.
tagline: The declassified true story of the horse soldiers
title: 12 Strong
plot:
12 Strong is a 2018 American war film directed by Nicolai Fuglsig and written by Ted Tally and Peter Craig, based on Doug Stanton's nonfiction book Horse Soldiers about U.S. Army Special Forces sent to Afghanistan after the September 11 attacks. Chris Hemsworth plays Captain Mitch Nelson, with Michael Shannon as Chief Warrant Officer Hal Spencer, Michael Peña as Sergeant First Class Sam Diller, Navid Negahban as Northern Alliance general Abdul Rashid Dostum and William Fichtner as Colonel John Mulholland.

On September 11, 2001, Green Beret captain Nelson is moving into a new home with his family after accepting a staff job when news of the attacks breaks, and he volunteers to lead his former team, Operational Detachment Alpha 595, into Afghanistan. His commander refuses until veteran warrant officer Spencer, who had planned to retire, persuades him and volunteers to go too. After evaluation in Uzbekistan, the team is chosen by Mulholland to fight alongside Dostum and is flown covertly into Afghanistan, landing 40 miles south of Mazar-i-Sharif, a longtime Taliban stronghold. Nelson takes half the team into the mountains with Dostum, while Spencer holds a fortified camp nicknamed "the Alamo".

Dostum aims to take the city and defeat the brutal Taliban commander Mullah Razzan, who murdered his family. After early clashes, and joined by Spencer's half of the team, they win a series of victories using Dostum's horsemen and American air power. When Nelson reveals that another team has been sent to aid Dostum's rival, Atta Muhammad, Dostum's men walk away. Pressing on with only a few Afghan fighters, ODA 595 uses airstrikes against a large Taliban and al-Qaeda force but is discovered; Spencer is badly wounded by a suicide bomber, and the team is nearly overrun when Dostum returns. In the Army's first cavalry charge of the 21st century, the allied forces scatter the enemy and Dostum kills Razzan. Arriving at Mazar-i-Sharif to find Atta already there, Dostum gives Nelson his prized riding crop and calls him a brother. Spencer survives, and all twelve men return home after 23 days of near-constant combat.

Warner Bros. Pictures released the film on January 19, 2018. It grossed $71.1 million worldwide on a $35 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 50% on Rotten Tomatoes and 54 on Metacritic; critics praised the cast and action but faulted its lack of depth.

original_title: The Other Side of the Door
overview: Grieving over the loss of her son, a mother struggles with her feelings for her daughter and her husband. She seeks out a ritual that allows her say goodbye to her dead child, opening the veil between the world of the dead and the living. Her daughter becomes the focus of terror. She must now protect against the evil that was once her beloved son.
tagline: It was never meant to be opened.
title: The Other Side of the Door
plot:
The Other Side of the Door is a supernatural horror film that delves into the complexities of grief, trauma, and the blurred lines between reality and the afterlife. The movie follows a family's struggle to cope with the loss of their young son, who dies in a tragic accident.

As the story unfolds, the family's grief is slowly consumed by an otherworldly presence that seems to be emanating from the spirit world. This malevolent force threatens to destroy their lives and relationships, forcing them to confront the darkest corners of their own emotions.

At its core, The Other Side of the Door explores the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and families. The film masterfully weaves together elements of horror, drama, and supernatural mystery to create a sense of unease and tension that permeates every aspect of the narrative.

Through the characters' experiences, the movie sheds light on the ways in which grief can both consume and transform us. As they navigate the treacherous landscape of their own emotions, the family is forced to confront the possibility that some wounds may never fully heal, and that the line between life and death can be perilously thin.

Ultimately, The Other Side of the Door is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that probes the depths of sorrow, loss, and the unknown.

overview: A fictional account of one year in the life of Empress Elisabeth of Austria. On Christmas Eve 1877, Elisabeth, once idolized for her beauty, turns 40 and is officially deemed an old woman; she starts trying to maintain her public image.
tagline: No pain, no reign.
title: Corsage
plot:
Corsage is a 2022 Austrian drama film directed by Malene Mitsky, not Samsa Film. The movie stars Vicky Krieps as Empress Elisabeth of Austria.

The main themes of Corsage revolve around the complexities of royal life, the constraints placed on women in patriarchal societies, and the struggle for individuality and autonomy. The film explores the personal struggles of Empress Elisabeth, who is portrayed as a strong-willed and independent woman trapped within the confines of her royal duties.

Throughout the movie, the audience witnesses Elisabeth's inner turmoil as she navigates the intricacies of court politics, societal expectations, and her own desires. The film delves into themes such as:

1. The constraints of royal life: The movie highlights the suffocating nature of royal duties and the limited options available to women in positions of power.
2. Female empowerment: Elisabeth's journey is a metaphor for the struggle for female empowerment and autonomy, particularly in patriarchal societies.
3. Identity and self-discovery: As Elisabeth navigates her personal struggles, she begins to question her role as an empress and seeks to redefine herself outside of her royal duties.

The film features stunning cinematography, costumes, and performances, bringing the story of Empress Elisabeth to life in a captivating and thought-provoking way.

overview: Angela is throwing a decadent Halloween party at New Orleans' infamous Broussard Mansion. But after the police break up the festivities, Maddie and a few friends stay behind. Trapped inside the locked mansion gates, the remaining guests uncover a horrifying secret and soon fall victim to seven vicious, blood-thirsty demons.
tagline: All Hell Is Going To Break Loose
title: Night of the Demons
plot:
Night of the Demons is a 2009 supernatural horror film that serves as a remake of the 1988 film of the same name. The movie follows a group of college students who are trapped in a haunted house, where they must face their deepest fears and confront the evil forces that dwell within.

At its core, Night of the Demons explores themes of paranoia, claustrophobia, and the breakdown of social bonds under pressure. As the characters become increasingly isolated and desperate, their relationships with each other begin to fray, revealing underlying tensions and conflicts that were previously masked by their camaraderie.

The film also delves into the idea of the "other," representing the unknown, the supernatural, or the forces of chaos that threaten to disrupt the status quo. The demonic entities in the movie embody this concept, serving as a manifestation of the characters' deepest fears and anxieties.

Furthermore, Night of the Demons touches on the theme of female empowerment, particularly through the character of Tiffany, who becomes a leader among her peers as they navigate the horrors of the haunted house. Her strength and determination serve as a counterpoint to the male-dominated narrative, highlighting the importance of women's voices and agency in the face of adversity.

Overall, Night of the Demons is a tense, unsettling horror film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the fragility of social bonds and the power of fear to break us down.

overview: A wannabe rock star who fronts a Pennsylvania-based tribute band is devastated when his kick him out of the group he founded. Things begin to look up for Izzy when he is asked to join Steel Dragon, the heavy metal rockers he had been imitating for so long. This film is loosely based on the true story of the band Judas Priest.
tagline: The story of a wanna be who got to be.
title: Rock Star
plot:
Rock Star is a 2001 musical drama film that explores the darker side of fame and the excesses of rock 'n' roll. The movie delves into the theme of identity, as the protagonist, Chris Cole, played by Mark Wahlberg, navigates his rise to stardom and struggles with the pressures of maintaining a public image.

The film also examines the destructive nature of addiction and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. As Chris becomes increasingly consumed by his newfound fame, he begins to lose touch with his roots and the people who matter most to him. This leads to a downward spiral of self-destruction, as he struggles to reconcile his public persona with his private demons.

Furthermore, Rock Star touches on the theme of rebellion and nonconformity, as Chris's music becomes a reflection of his own personal struggles and desires. The film suggests that true creativity and authenticity can only be achieved when one is unencumbered by the expectations of others, and that the pursuit of fame and fortune can ultimately lead to a loss of artistic integrity.

Overall, Rock Star presents a cautionary tale about the dangers of excess and the importance of staying true to oneself in the face of overwhelming external pressures.

overview: A weak-willed Italian man becomes a fascist flunky who goes abroad to arrange the assassination of his old teacher, now a political dissident.
tagline: A dazzling movie.
title: The Conformist
plot:
The Conformist (Italian: Il conformista) is a 1970 political drama written and directed by Bernardo Bertolucci, adapted from Alberto Moravia's 1951 novel. An Italian, French and West German co-production set in the Fascist era, it follows a cultivated but emotionally hollow functionary whose overriding desire to be "normal" leads him to betray his former teacher.

In Paris in 1938, Marcello Clerici leaves his bride Giulia at their hotel and is picked up by Manganiello, a secret police agent, for the final stage of an assassination plot. Flashbacks fill in his path there: visits to his morphine-dependent mother and his father in an asylum, talks with his blind friend Italo, and a childhood episode in 1917 in which the chauffeur Lino molested him, after which Marcello shot at Lino and fled, convinced he had killed him. To marry the conventional Giulia, the atheist Marcello goes to confession, where he admits he values her chiefly for the normal life she represents; the priest absolves him once he learns Marcello serves the Fascist police. Ordered to kill Professor Luca Quadri, an anti-Fascist exile in France, Marcello uses his honeymoon as cover. In Paris he becomes infatuated with Quadri's wife Anna, who returns his interest and is also drawn to Giulia, while Manganiello begins to doubt his resolve. Marcello hands back his gun but tells the agent where the Quadris will be travelling. Despite his warning, Anna joins her husband on the drive to Savoy, and on a lonely mountain road agents stab Quadri to death. Seeing Marcello sitting passively in the car behind, Anna flees screaming into the woods and is gunned down, and Manganiello turns away in disgust at his cowardice. In 1943, as Mussolini's regime collapses, Marcello, now a father, encounters the very much alive Lino in the streets of Rome, and in a frenzy denounces him and then Italo to the crowd.

Jean-Louis Trintignant stars as Marcello, with Stefania Sandrelli as Giulia, Dominique Sanda as Anna, Gastone Moschin as Manganiello, Enzo Tarascio as Quadri and Pierre Clémenti as Lino. Shot in Rome, Paris and at Cinecittà for $750,000, it was celebrated for Vittorio Storaro's cinematography and Ferdinando Scarfiotti's evocation of Fascist-era architecture, and for a fractured chronology shaped in the edit. After premiering at the 1970 Berlin festival, it won the David di Donatello for Best Film and earned Oscar and Golden Globe nominations, and it is widely ranked among the greatest films ever made.

overview: When a 12-year-old boy goes missing, lead investigator Greg Harper struggles to balance the pressure of the investigation and troubles with his wife, Jackie. Facing a recent affair, great strain is put on the family that slowly gnaws away at Jackie's grip on reality. But after a malicious presence manifests itself in their home and puts their son, Connor, in mortal danger, the cold, hard truth about evil in the Harper household is finally uncovered.
tagline: Evil Hides In Plain Sight
title: I See You
plot:
I See You is a 2019 American horror thriller directed by Adam Randall from a screenplay by Devon Graye. It stars Helen Hunt, Jon Tenney and Judah Lewis, with Owen Teague and Libe Barer, in a story about a detective's family whose suburban home becomes the scene of increasingly unsettling events.

When ten-year-old Justin Whitter vanishes while riding his bike, detective Greg Harper leads the case with his partner, Spitzky. A green pocket knife left at the scene links the abduction to a series of crimes from fifteen years earlier, committed by a man who is now in prison. At home, Connor resents his mother for a recent affair, and strange things keep happening: objects disappear, a repairman says a daughter the Harpers do not have let him in, and Greg is locked inside a closet. When Jackie's former lover, Todd, shows up, he is struck on the head and later found dead, and Jackie, believing Connor killed him, persuades Greg to help bury the body. Soon afterward the couple find Connor tied up in the bathtub with a green knife beside him.

Flashbacks then reveal that two drifters, Mindy and Alec, have been secretly living in the house. Alec caused the disturbances to torment the family, but Mindy witnessed the true killer of Todd: Greg. Hidden in Greg's car, Mindy finds green knives and Justin's shirt, follows him into the forest and discovers the missing boys locked in a trailer, making a broken 911 call before Greg captures her and kills her at home, staging it as self-defense. Alec confronts Greg, who claims he was once a victim himself, and shoots him dead. Spitzky arrives and wounds Alec, the evidence in Greg's car exposes the truth, and the boys are rescued by tracing Mindy's call.

The film premiered in the Midnighters section of SXSW on March 13, 2019, and Saban Films released it in theaters on December 6, 2019. It grossed about $1.2 million worldwide on a $5 million budget. Reviews were favorable, with 73% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 65; critics found the twisting plot convoluted but praised the cast and its slow-building suspense.

original_title: ワンピース エピソード オブ 空島
overview: One day, a giant ship falls onto the Straw Hats from the sky. After a narrow escape, and while they are still in shock, a map to the “Sky Island” is carried to them by the wind. While researching for the way there, they meet another pirate and learn that he is a descendant of an infamous Sky Island explorer who was even depicted in a picture book “Noland The Liar” four centuries ago. However, Noland was possibly not a liar after all and might actually have gone to the Sky Island.
title: One Piece: Episode of Skypiea
plot:
One Piece: Episode of Skypiea is an animated film that explores the complexities of power, morality, and the consequences of one's actions. The story delves into the character of Gecko Moria, a pirate who seeks to overthrow the World Government and establish a new world order.

At its core, the film grapples with the nature of power and how it can be both a blessing and a curse. Moria's pursuit of power is driven by his desire for revenge against those who wronged him in the past, but as he gains more power, he becomes increasingly consumed by his own ambition. This serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked power and the importance of considering the consequences of one's actions.

The film also explores themes of morality and the gray areas that exist between right and wrong. Moria's character is a prime example of this, as he operates in a world where traditional notions of good and evil are blurred. His actions are motivated by a desire for justice, but his methods are often brutal and violent, leaving the audience to question whether he is truly fighting for what is just or simply seeking revenge.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of redemption and the possibility of personal growth. Moria's character undergoes significant development throughout the story, as he grapples with the consequences of his actions and begins to see the error of his ways. This serves as a powerful reminder that it is never too late to change one's path and seek forgiveness.

Overall, One Piece: Episode of Skypiea is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and characters in a richly detailed world.

overview: In Scooby-Doo’s greatest adventure yet, see the never-before told story of how lifelong friends Scooby and Shaggy first met and how they joined forces with young detectives Fred, Velma, and Daphne to form the famous Mystery Inc. Now, with hundreds of cases solved, Scooby and the gang face their biggest, toughest mystery ever: an evil plot to unleash the ghost dog Cerberus upon the world. As they race to stop this global “dogpocalypse,” the gang discovers that Scooby has a secret legacy and an epic destiny greater than anyone ever imagined.
tagline: Mystery loves company.
title: Scoob!
plot:
Scoob! is a 2020 American mystery-comedy film directed by Joe Wizan and written by Jared Bush, Emily A. Skinner, and Matt Lieberman. The movie is based on the classic Hanna-Barbera cartoon series Scooby-Doo.

The story begins with Shaggy Rogers (voiced by Will Forte) and Scooby-Doo (voiced by Frank Welker), a pair of best friends who travel around in their psychedelic van, the Mystery Machine. They are joined by Velma Dinkley (voiced by Zoe Kravitz), Daphne Blake (voiced by Kiersey Clemons), and Fred Jones (voiced by Jason Isaacs) on various adventures.

The movie takes place during the 1970s, when the gang is still in high school. They are approached by a wealthy businessman named Mr. Jenkins (voiced by Tim Blaney), who hires them to investigate a series of paranormal occurrences at his mansion. The gang soon discovers that they are not alone, as they encounter a group of ghostly apparitions and supernatural creatures.

As the mystery unfolds, the gang learns that the ghostly entities are actually the vengeful spirits of Mr. Jenkins' former business partners, who were wronged by him in the past. The gang must work together to uncover the truth behind the haunting and put an end to it.

Throughout the movie, Shaggy and Scooby-Doo's friendship is put to the test as they face various challenges and obstacles. Velma uses her analytical skills to decipher clues and solve puzzles, while Daphne provides comedic relief with her fashion sense and resourcefulness. Fred, on the other hand, struggles with his leadership role and must learn to trust his friends.

As the mystery deepens, the gang discovers that Mr. Jenkins is not who he claims to be. He is actually a former con artist who has been using his wealth and influence to cover up his past mistakes. The gang must use all their skills and work together to expose Mr. Jenkins' true identity and bring him to justice.

In the end, the gang succeeds in solving the mystery and putting an end to the haunting. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, trust, and believing in themselves. The movie ends with a heartwarming moment of Shaggy and Scooby-Doo sharing a laugh and a Scooby Snack, as the Mystery Machine drives off into the sunset.

Overall, Scoob! is a fun and entertaining movie that pays homage to the classic Scooby-Doo cartoon series while also offering a fresh and modern take on the characters. The movie features plenty of humor, action, and heart, making it a great watch for both old and new fans of the franchise.

original_title: James Corden's Top Gun Training with Tom Cruise
overview: When "Top Gun: Maverick" star Tom Cruise calls you up to hang out for the day, you say yes. And for James Corden, that meant having Tom pilot you in two different fighter planes, pushing the limits of gravity and James's stomach.
title: James Corden's Top Gun Training with Tom Cruise
plot:
"Last Days in the Desert" is a 2016 American Western drama film directed by James Gray. The movie stars Nick Nolte as Henry, a former preacher who has lost his faith and is now a drifter.

The main themes of "Last Days in the Desert" include:

1. **Spiritual Crisis**: The film explores Henry's spiritual crisis, as he grapples with feelings of guilt, shame, and disillusionment with his past life as a preacher. His journey is a metaphor for the search for meaning and purpose in life.

2. **Loneliness and Isolation**: Henry's character is marked by loneliness and isolation, which serves as a backdrop to explore themes of human connection and community. The film highlights the difficulties of forming meaningful relationships in a world that often seems hostile or unforgiving.

3. **Redemption and Forgiveness**: Throughout the movie, Henry seeks redemption for past mistakes and grapples with the idea of forgiveness – both from himself and others. His journey is one of self-discovery and acceptance, as he comes to terms with his own flaws and weaknesses.

4. **The Search for Meaning**: The film's narrative is interwoven with biblical references and allusions, which serve to underscore Henry's spiritual quest. The movie explores the idea that meaning can be found in the simplest moments of life, such as a conversation with a stranger or a moment of introspection.

5. **Human Nature**: Gray's direction and Nolte's performance bring to light the complexities of human nature, revealing both the darkness and the beauty within us all. The film is a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that encourages empathy and understanding.

Overall, "Last Days in the Desert" is a thought-provoking drama that explores themes of spirituality, loneliness, redemption, and the search for meaning in life.

overview: Olivia and Matthew Grey, 18-year-old twins born into a world of privilege and high expectations. There are almost no boundaries between them - even their dreams are connected.
tagline: Control yourself
title: Feed
plot:
Feed is a 2017 American drama film directed by Tommy Bertelsen and written and produced by Troian Bellisario, who also stars. Inspired by Bellisario's own experience of anorexia, which she overcame, it follows a high school senior whose physical and mental health, grades and relationships collapse after the death of her twin brother. Bellisario plays Olivia "Liv" Grey, with Tom Felton as her twin, Matt, Ben Winchell as her crush Julian, James Remar and Paula Malcomson as their parents, Tom and Samantha, and David Warshofsky as Dr. Rothstein.

The twins Olivia and Matt are as close as they are different. Liv, a would-be valedictorian, strives for excellence, which her father seems to demand of her far more than of her fraternity-bound brother, yet easygoing Matt is also the one who looks out for her, sometimes overprotectively. After a Halloween party, Matt argues with Liv over her decision to get drunk and hook up with their friend Julian, and he crashes the car they are riding in and dies. Unable to bear her guilt alone, Liv begins to see Matt, or a hostile version of him, at the moments she most needs him. This phantom tells her what to do, what to say and what to think, and above all when not to eat; Liv imagines that she is saving her food for Matt, who can live on only if she makes the sacrifice. While she tries to keep up a facade of normality, her health deteriorates, and after a suicide attempt during a party hosted by her parents, she is sent to an inpatient treatment center for eating disorders. Even there Matt torments her, pushing her to lie to her therapists and to hide food for him against the center's rules. In a therapy session, Liv finally speaks honestly about how she has been feeling, sending Matt's ghost into a rage in which he screams that he hates her and never loved her. After confronting him, she lets go of this version of her brother and recognizes that the voice urging her to control her eating was never really his.

Bellisario began writing the script at 23, about four years after being hospitalized for anorexia, and developed it over roughly eight years, describing the film as inspired by her illness rather than autobiographical. It marked her debut as a writer and producer, and she worked closely with her former therapist while making it, an experience she called both therapeutic and inflammatory. The film was released on video on demand and digital platforms on 18 July 2017.

overview: Lewis, a brilliant young inventor, is keen on creating a time machine to find his mother, who abandoned him in an orphanage. Things take a turn when he meets Wilbur Robinson and his family.
tagline: Think your family's weird?
title: Meet the Robinsons
plot:
Meet the Robinsons is a 2007 American animated science fiction comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Lewis, an orphan boy who dreams of becoming a great inventor.

The film begins with Lewis, a shy and awkward 12-year-old boy, living in an orphanage. He spends most of his time daydreaming about inventing incredible gadgets and machines that will change the world. However, his life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Wilbur, a mysterious and eccentric old man who claims to be his long-lost father.

Wilbur reveals to Lewis that he is actually the son of a brilliant inventor named Cornelius Robinson, who created a time machine called the "Time Machine 3000." The Time Machine 3000 allows its user to travel through time, but it also has a mind of its own and can be unpredictable. Wilbur warns Lewis that his father's inventions have been stolen by a rival inventor named Bowler Hat Guy, who is using them for evil purposes.

Lewis decides to embark on a journey with Wilbur to find Cornelius Robinson and retrieve the stolen inventions. Along the way, they meet a cast of eccentric characters, including Wilbur's wife, Mrs. Robinson, and their son, Lewis Jr., who becomes Lewis's rival in inventing.

As they travel through time, Lewis and his companions encounter various historical figures, including Leonardo da Vinci, Benjamin Franklin, and Albert Einstein. However, Bowler Hat Guy is always one step ahead, using the stolen inventions to alter historical events for his own gain.

The plot thickens as Lewis and his friends discover that Bowler Hat Guy's ultimate plan is to steal Cornelius Robinson's most prized invention: a machine that can create an army of robotic clones. The movie builds up to a thrilling climax as Lewis and his companions must stop Bowler Hat Guy and his minions from carrying out their evil plan.

In the end, Lewis and his friends succeed in defeating Bowler Hat Guy and restoring the timeline to its original course. Along the way, Lewis learns valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and believing in himself. The movie ends with Lewis returning to the present, where he is reunited with Wilbur and becomes a confident inventor in his own right.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with a unique blend of steampunk and sci-fi elements. The characters are well-developed and quirky, adding to the movie's humor and charm. Meet the Robinsons is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the power of imagination and creativity.

overview: Three young people on a road trip from Colorado to New Jersey talk to a trucker on their CB radio, then must escape when he turns out to be a psychotic killer.
tagline: It started as a joke. Now the joke is on them.
title: Joy Ride
plot:
Joy Ride is a 2001 American road thriller film directed by John Dahl from a screenplay by Clay Tarver and J. J. Abrams, produced by Regency Enterprises, Bad Robot and LivePlanet. It stars Paul Walker as Lewis Thomas, Steve Zahn as his brother Fuller and Leelee Sobieski as Venna, with Jessica Bowman as Charlotte, Jim Beaver as Sheriff Ritter and Ted Levine as the voice of the trucker Rusty Nail.

Lewis is driving from California to Colorado to pick up his childhood friend and crush Venna when he learns that his estranged brother Fuller has been arrested in Salt Lake City. He bails him out, and Fuller comes along, installing a CB radio in the car. Fuller persuades Lewis to prank a trucker known as Rusty Nail by posing as a woman named "Candy Cane" and inviting him to a motel room, room 17, occupied by a rude businessman Fuller had clashed with. From the next room, the brothers hear an argument and a scuffle, and in the morning they learn that the businessman has been found on the highway in a coma, his lower jaw torn off. The sheriff scolds them but lets them go. Near Laramie, Wyoming, Rusty Nail is back on the radio looking for Candy Cane, and when Lewis confesses to the prank, Fuller insults him instead of apologizing. Rusty Nail reveals that he is following them, and after a false alarm involving an ice truck, he slowly crushes their car against a tree before driving off, calling it a joke. The brothers pick up Venna, but Rusty Nail calls their motel room, aware that she has joined them, and leaves spray-painted messages on road signs. He then announces over the radio that he has kidnapped Venna's friend Charlotte and lures the three into a cornfield, where he seizes Venna. At another motel, mirroring the prank, he rigs a shotgun to kill the bound Venna in room 17 if the door is opened. Fuller is wounded trying to enter through a back window, but the brothers free Venna just before Rusty Nail's driverless truck rolls downhill and smashes into the motel. Police find Charlotte alive in the trailer and a dead man in the cab, who turns out to be the kindly ice truck driver who had returned Lewis's lost credit card, and over the ambulance's radio the group hears Rusty Nail's voice.

Shot in Nevada, California and Utah, the film premiered at the 2001 Toronto International Film Festival. It grossed $36.6 million on a $23 million budget, received generally positive reviews (74% on Rotten Tomatoes) and spawned two sequels.

overview: The world’s greatest killing machine is three times as deadly when a mutated shark threatens a cruise ship. As the shark eats its way from one end of the ship to the next, the passengers fight the deadly predator using anything they can find.
tagline: More HEADS! More DEADS!
title: 3-Headed Shark Attack
plot:
3-Headed Shark Attack is a 2015 American direct-to-video creature feature produced by The Asylum and directed by Christopher Ray, a sequel to 2-Headed Shark Attack (2012). Danny Trejo plays fisherman Max Burns, Karrueche Tran plays college graduate Maggie Peterson, and professional wrestler Rob Van Dam plays party-boat passenger Stanley, with Jaason Simmons and Jena Sims as marine biologists Ted Nelson and Laura Thomas.

A great white shark with three heads tears through a party on an atoll, killing every teenager except Mark, who was out on a buoy. It then attacks the Persephone, an underwater research station studying the Pacific Garbage Patch, and the damage makes the facility explode. The only survivors are Ted, Laura and a group of visiting activists: Greg, Ryan Bennett, Omar, Alison and Maggie, who has applied for a job at the station and is Greg's former girlfriend. As the island floods, they swim to the activists' boat, losing Laura and Omar on the way, while Ryan radios Burns, who reluctantly agrees to help. They arrive too late to warn a party boat full of young people; the shark rams it repeatedly and devours passengers who fall overboard. Aboard, Maggie and Ted help passengers Stanley and Rosemarie Grant search for Rosemarie's boyfriend, Howard, who vanished in the chaos, but the shark leaps onto the stern and eats Ted.

With the ship sinking, the survivors escape on the activists' boat, and Ryan dies after trying to kill the creature by riding its back with an axe. Low on fuel, they put in at the atoll. Burns loses his two crewmen but decapitates the middle head, apparently killing the shark, which instead recovers, sprouts three new heads in place of the lost one and swallows Burns. Joined by Mark, the group concludes that the animal is drawn to pollution and that its heads are growing hostile to one another. As they flee in two motorboats, the shark destroys one, killing Alison, Rosemarie, Howard and Mark. Maggie, Stanley and Greg lure it with garbage bags; Stanley, his hand bitten off, sacrifices himself so the heads fight over him, and the shark bleeds to death after three heads are torn off. Maggie and Greg reconcile as a helicopter arrives.

The Asylum continued the series with 5-Headed Shark Attack in 2017 and 6-Headed Shark Attack in 2018.

overview: The story of an impossible love between a woman named Fred and a transgender woman named Laurence who reveals her inner desire to become her true self.
tagline: Will the woman she wants love the woman she wants to be?
title: Laurence Anyways
plot:
Laurence Anyways is a poignant and introspective drama that explores the complexities of love, identity, and acceptance. The film tells the story of two men, François and Laurent, who embark on a transformative journey of self-discovery and love.

At its core, Laurence Anyways is a powerful exploration of the human condition, delving into the intricacies of the human heart and the struggles that come with navigating one's true self. The film masterfully weaves together themes of identity, desire, and acceptance, creating a rich tapestry of emotions that resonates deeply with audiences.

Through François and Laurent's story, the film sheds light on the complexities of love and relationships, highlighting the ways in which societal expectations and norms can both constrain and liberate us. The movie also touches on the theme of self-acceptance, as the two protagonists grapple with their own desires, fears, and insecurities.

One of the most striking aspects of Laurence Anyways is its nuanced portrayal of masculinity and femininity, challenging traditional notions of gender and encouraging viewers to rethink their assumptions about what it means to be male or female. The film's exploration of these themes is both subtle and powerful, inviting audiences to reflect on their own understanding of identity and relationships.

Ultimately, Laurence Anyways is a moving and thought-provoking drama that celebrates the beauty of human connection and the transformative power of love.

overview: A teenage girl with self-esteem issues finds confidence in the most unlikely way, by spending her summer battling vampires that prey on New Orleans' disenfranchised with the help of her best friend, the boy she's always pined for, and a peculiar rich girl.
tagline: Find your own way to slay.
title: Black as Night
plot:
Black as Night is a 2021 American fantasy horror film directed by Marvin Lemus and Sean McNamara. The movie follows a teenage girl named Gela, who discovers she has supernatural abilities after her family is attacked by vampires.

The main themes of Black as Night include:

* Self-discovery: Gela's journey is also one of self-discovery as she learns to control her powers and navigate her new identity.
* Family dynamics: The movie explores the complexities of family relationships, particularly between Gela and her mother, who has been keeping secrets from her daughter.
* Identity and belonging: As a half-human, half-vampire hybrid, Gela struggles to find her place in both human and vampire worlds.
* Coming-of-age: Black as Night can be seen as a coming-of-age story for Gela, as she faces challenges and learns to rely on herself.

The movie also touches on themes of prejudice, fear, and acceptance, particularly in the context of vampire-human relations.
