Ray soon discovers that his children have been taken by the aliens, and he sets out on a perilous journey to rescue them. He joins forces with a former Marine named Sergeant Michael O'Neill (Tim Robbins) and his wife, Janine (Linda Hunt), who are also searching for their missing family members.

As they fight to survive, Ray and his companions encounter various obstacles, including swarms of Black Oil-infected humans, giant alien machines that destroy cities, and treacherous terrain. Along the way, Ray's character undergoes a significant transformation as he confronts his own personal demons and learns to put the needs of others before his own.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the human survivors and the aliens in New York City. The Doctor leads the rebels in a final assault on the alien mothership, while Ray and his companions fight to rescue their children from the clutches of the Black Oil.

In the end, Ray is reunited with his children, but not before witnessing the destruction of New York City. As they escape the city, Ray reflects on the lessons he has learned about family, sacrifice, and the importance of human connection in the face of overwhelming adversity.

Overall, War of the Worlds is a thrilling and emotionally resonant film that explores themes of family, survival, and humanity in the face of an existential threat.

overview: Jen and a group of friends set out to hike the Appalachian Trail. Despite warnings to stick to the trail, the hikers stray off course—and cross into land inhabited by The Foundation, a hidden community of mountain dwellers who use deadly means to protect their way of life.
tagline: This land is their land.
title: Wrong Turn
plot:
Wrong Turn, also known as Wrong Turn: The Foundation, is a 2021 folk horror film directed by Mike P. Nelson and written by Alan B. McElroy, who wrote the 2003 original. The seventh entry in the series, it drops the cannibalism of earlier films. Charlotte Vega stars as Jen Shaw, with Adain Bradley as Darius, Bill Sage as Venable, Emma Dumont as Milla, Dylan McTee as Adam, Daisy Head as Edith and Matthew Modine as Jen's father, Scott.

Jen, her boyfriend Darius and their friends Adam, Milla, Gary and Luis arrive in a small Virginia town to hike the Appalachian Trail, meeting hostile locals, a strange woman named Edith and a mute girl, Ruthie. Leaving the trail to find an old fort, they lose Gary to a rolling tree trunk. Lost, they find a plaque from 1859 commemorating the "Foundation", settlers who believed the United States was about to collapse. Adam is caught in a trap and carried off by two men in animal-skull masks, and when his friends confront them, he breaks free and beats one to death. Milla is later impaled in a pit and killed with an arrow, and the others are captured and brought to the Foundation's hidden settlement. Its leader, Venable, holds a trial, sentences Adam to death for killing a man named Samuel and condemns the others to "darkness" for lying to save him. After Ruthie stabs Adam with a hidden blade when he takes her hostage, Venable beats him to death with the same log, and Luis is blinded with a hot poker. Jen saves herself and Darius by offering their usefulness to the community, and she becomes the wife of the widowed Venable. Six weeks later, Scott arrives searching for her, and after his guide dies in a trap he is captured. Jen frees him at night, but Darius refuses to leave. Helped by Ruthie, father and daughter find the blinded prisoners, including Luis, whom Jen mercy kills, and fight their way out with the help of armed townsmen, killing Edith among others. Months later, Jen finds her stepmother welcoming Venable and Ruthie to the neighborhood, and Venable, seeing that Jen is pregnant with his child, asks her to return; she agrees if he leaves her family alone. As the credits roll, she crashes their RV, stabs Venable and the driver to death and walks Ruthie back to her family's house.

Shot in Felicity, Ohio, in late 2019, the film was released in theaters for one night on 26 January 2021 by Saban Films. It received positive reviews, with 64% on Rotten Tomatoes, and grossed $4.8 million at the box office.

overview: The irreverent host of a political satire talk show decides to run for president and expose corruption in Washington. His stunt goes further than he expects when he actually wins the election, but a software engineer suspects that a computer glitch is responsible for his surprising victory.
tagline: Elections are made to be broken.
title: Man of the Year
plot:
Man of the Year is a 2006 American political comedy-drama with thriller elements, written and directed by Barry Levinson and produced by James G. Robinson. Robin Williams stars as Tom Dobbs, the host of a satirical political talk show who runs for president, and the cast also includes Christopher Walken, Laura Linney, Lewis Black and Jeff Goldblum.

Dobbs's show taps into public frustration with divisive, special-interest politics. He laughs off an audience member's suggestion that he run for the White House, but after a wave of online support he announces a campaign on the air, gets on the ballot in 13 states and joins a national debate with Democratic incumbent President Kellogg and Republican Senator Mills. Meanwhile Eleanor Green, an employee of Delacroy, the company supplying the country's voting machines, discovers that its system does not count correctly, but company head James Hemmings deletes her warning e-mail. Dobbs initially takes the campaign so seriously that he worries his manager, Jack Menken, and producer Eddie Langston, but at the debate he reverts to comedy and climbs in the polls. On Election Day the early returns follow exactly the pattern Eleanor predicted, and Dobbs sweeps his 13 states, winning enough electoral votes to become president-elect.

When Eleanor presses the issue, she is attacked at home and injected with drugs, then discredited as an addict and fired. She tracks Dobbs down and works out the flaw: regardless of the actual votes, the software favors names with double letters in alphabetical order, so Dobbs beats Kellogg, who beats Mills. Dobbs, increasingly smitten with her, plans to reveal the truth, but Delacroy preempts him by claiming Eleanor tried to rig the vote for him, and its agents pursue her until one rams the phone booth she is calling from. In her ambulance she convinces Dobbs, and although polls show most Americans want him in office, he announces on Saturday Night Live's Weekend Update that the vote was flawed and covered up and that he will not run in the new election. Kellogg wins a second term, the executives are arrested, Dobbs returns to television with Eleanor as his producer and later his wife, and Time names him its Man of the Year.

Filmed in Toronto, Hamilton and Washington, D.C., and released by Universal Pictures on October 13, 2006, the film grossed $41.2 million on a $20 million budget. Reviews were largely negative, with 22% on Rotten Tomatoes and 39 on Metacritic.

overview: Gamers who participate in an online role-playing game called Hellworld are invited to a rave whose host plans to show them all the truth behind the Cenobite mythos.
tagline: Evil Goes Online.
title: Hellraiser: Hellworld
plot:
Hellraiser: Hellworld is a 2005 supernatural horror film directed by Rick Bota and written by Brad Fiedel. The movie takes place in an alternate universe where the Cenobites, led by Pinhead, have been defeated.

The main themes of Hellraiser: Hellworld include:

1. **Reality TV and the Commodification of Suffering**: The film critiques the voyeuristic nature of reality television, where contestants are forced to endure physical and emotional torture for the sake of entertainment. This theme is reflected in the movie's plot, where a group of contestants on a reality show are lured into a twisted game of survival, only to discover that they are being manipulated by the Cenobites.

2. **The Dangers of Obsession**: The movie explores the dangers of obsession and the blurring of lines between reality and fantasy. The characters' descent into madness is fueled by their own desires and obsessions, which ultimately lead them to confront the horrors of the Cenobites.

3. **The Power of Pain and Pleasure**: Hellraiser: Hellworld delves into the idea that pain and pleasure are intertwined, and that some people are drawn to the darker aspects of human experience. The Cenobites, with their sadomasochistic tendencies, represent a twisted manifestation of this theme.

4. **The Consequences of Playing God**: The movie touches on the idea that playing God can have disastrous consequences. The characters' attempts to control and manipulate the Cenobites ultimately lead to chaos and destruction, highlighting the dangers of meddling with forces beyond human understanding.

5. **The Nature of Reality**: Hellraiser: Hellworld raises questions about the nature of reality and the blurred lines between fantasy and reality. The movie's use of multiple realities and timelines adds complexity to the narrative, leaving the audience to ponder what is real and what is just a product of the characters' imagination.

Overall, Hellraiser: Hellworld is a thought-provoking horror film that explores themes of obsession, pain, pleasure, and the consequences of playing God.

overview: Deep in the underbelly of New York City, a five year-old girl and her mother live among a community that has claimed the abandoned subway tunnels as their home. After a sudden police-mandated eviction, the pair are forced to flee aboveground into a brutal winter night. Determined to return home, they fight to find shelter as their world is thrown into chaos.
title: Topside
plot:
Topside is a 2020 American drama film written and directed by Celine Held and Logan George in their feature debut. Held also stars as Nikki, a struggling young mother, with Zhaila Farmer as her five-year-old daughter, Little, Fatlip as Little's father, John, Jared Abrahamson as Les and Cynthia Tombros as Lolly. Set among the people living in the abandoned subway tunnels beneath New York City, it tells a mother-daughter survival story largely from the child's point of view.

Little has spent her whole life in a hidden community in the tunnels, roaming her subterranean surroundings with unfettered curiosity. Her parents are drug addicts locked in a daily struggle to get by, and they disagree about her future. John believes she belongs "topside", the word the tunnel dwellers use for the world above, in a school that can meet her needs, while Nikki cannot reconcile the idea with her fierce desire to be a devoted mother in the direst of circumstances. To keep Little below, Nikki has fed her a private mythology, telling her that she cannot go topside until she grows wings.

Early on, transit authorities burst into the tunnels to evict the community. Nikki grabs her daughter and flees straight up into the city, forcing Little into an abrupt confrontation with the blinding lights, noise and machinery of urban life, which to the frightened child seems like a waking nightmare. Over one harsh winter night, mother and daughter wander the streets in desperate search of shelter. A visit to Les, a menacing downtown pimp, ends in a bleak confrontation and a frightening turn that drives the frantic last act. As Nikki fights to protect her daughter against an unforgiving world, the story arrives at a gut-wrenching revelation.

Topside premiered in the International Film Critics' Week at the Venice Film Festival in September 2020 and had its U.S. premiere at South by Southwest, where Held and George won the Jury Award for Best Director. Vertical Entertainment acquired it in February 2022 and released it in theaters and on demand on March 25, 2022. It holds 73% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. Sheri Linden of The Hollywood Reporter called it a striking, cinematic and affecting debut, and Eric Kohn of IndieWire praised Held's sophisticated performance and hailed Farmer's as a revelation, while Brian Tallerico of RogerEbert.com felt that, though well meant, it fell into manipulative poverty porn.

overview: CIA employee Edward Snowden leaks thousands of classified documents to the press.
tagline: The only safe place is on the run.
title: Snowden
plot:
Snowden is a 2016 biographical thriller directed by Oliver Stone, who wrote it with Kieran Fitzgerald, based on Luke Harding's book The Snowden Files and Anatoly Kucherena's Time of the Octopus. Joseph Gordon-Levitt plays Edward Snowden, the intelligence contractor who leaked classified National Security Agency documents in 2013, with Shailene Woodley as his girlfriend Lindsay Mills, Melissa Leo as Laura Poitras, Zachary Quinto as Glenn Greenwald, Tom Wilkinson as Ewen MacAskill, Rhys Ifans as his CIA mentor Corbin O'Brian and Nicolas Cage as Hank Forrester. A German, French and American co-production, it began filming in Munich in February 2015.

The story is framed by Snowden's secret 2013 meeting in Hong Kong with the documentary filmmaker Poitras and the journalist Greenwald, where he reveals evidence of illegal mass surveillance. In flashback, a broken leg ends his Army training in 2004, and he joins the CIA, where a deputy director takes a chance on him and he excels at cyberwarfare. He begins a relationship with Mills, whom he meets online, though their political views are sharply opposed. Posted to Geneva under diplomatic cover, he grows uneasy when his superiors entrap a target to extract information, and he resigns.

Working next for the NSA in Japan, he designs a backup system called Epic Shelter and learns how the agency monitors even allied nations, planting malware in their infrastructure. The strain ends his relationship with Mills, but they reunite in Maryland. Diagnosed with epilepsy, he accepts a post in Hawaii, where he discovers that his program is feeding real-time data to drone strikes in Pakistan. Disillusioned, he smuggles a microSD card into his office inside a Rubik's Cube, copies the evidence, and leaves for Hong Kong. With MacAskill's help the first stories are published on 5 June 2013. Snowden is smuggled out of Hong Kong on a flight to Latin America via Russia, but when the United States revokes his passport he is stranded in Moscow, where he is granted asylum and is later joined by Mills.

After a screening at San Diego Comic-Con and a premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival, Open Road Films released it in the United States on 16 September 2016. Reviews were mixed: critics praised Gordon-Levitt's performance but faulted Stone's direction, and it holds a 61% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It grossed $37.3 million worldwide against a $40 million budget.

overview: When Santa crash-lands in the junkyard on Christmas Eve, Hank, Trash Truck and their animal friends all have a hand in rescuing the holiday for everyone.
title: A Trash Truck Christmas
plot:
A heartwarming holiday film! A Trash Truck Christmas is a story that weaves together themes of redemption, community, and the true meaning of Christmas. The movie follows the journey of a gruff but lovable trash truck driver who finds himself at odds with his neighbors, particularly a young girl who is struggling to find joy in the holiday season.

As the story unfolds, the protagonist undergoes a transformation from a solitary figure to one who begins to connect with those around him. He starts to see the world through the eyes of others, including the young girl and her family, and discovers that even the most unlikely individuals can bring joy and light into each other's lives.

The film also explores the idea of second chances and finding redemption in unexpected ways. The protagonist's journey is not just about changing his own life but also about bringing people together and creating a sense of community. Through his interactions with others, he learns to let go of his gruff exterior and find a softer side, one that allows him to connect with those around him on a deeper level.

Ultimately, A Trash Truck Christmas is a story about the power of kindness, compassion, and understanding in bringing people together during the holiday season. It's a reminder that even in the most unexpected places, joy and love can be found, and that everyone deserves a second chance to experience the magic of Christmas.

overview: Balto and his daughter Aleu embark on a journey of adventure and self discovery.
title: Balto II: Wolf Quest
plot:
Balto II: Wolf Quest is an animated adventure film that explores several themes, primarily centered around loyalty, perseverance, and self-discovery.

The movie delves into the emotional journey of Balto's son, Koda, as he navigates his own path in life. As Koda embarks on a perilous quest to find his father, he faces numerous challenges that test his courage, wit, and determination. Through his experiences, Koda learns valuable lessons about loyalty, trust, and the importance of following one's heart.

One of the primary themes of Balto II: Wolf Quest is the struggle between tradition and individuality. As Koda sets out on his journey, he must reconcile his desire to follow in his father's paw-steps with his own unique identity and sense of purpose. This internal conflict serves as a powerful metaphor for the challenges faced by many young individuals as they navigate their own paths in life.

The film also touches on the theme of loss and grief, as Koda grapples with the absence of his father and the weight of his legacy. Through his journey, Koda comes to terms with the past while forging a new path forward, ultimately finding a sense of belonging and purpose that is uniquely his own.

Overall, Balto II: Wolf Quest is a heartwarming and inspiring tale that explores the complexities of identity, loyalty, and perseverance in the face of adversity.

overview: A blind woman's relationship with her husband changes when she regains her sight and discovers disturbing details about themselves.
title: All I See Is You
plot:
All I See Is You is a psychological thriller that delves into the complexities of human relationships and the blurred lines between love and obsession. The film tells the story of a young woman, Yuna, who becomes infatuated with her blind husband, Lincoln, after he loses his sight.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that Yuna's fixation on Lincoln is not just a result of her love for him, but also a desperate attempt to fill the void left by her own feelings of inadequacy and loneliness. Her all-consuming obsession with Lincoln leads her down a dark path, where she begins to question her own identity and sense of self-worth.

The film expertly explores the theme of toxic love, highlighting how Yuna's fixation on Lincoln becomes an unhealthy and destructive force in their relationship. The movie also touches on the idea of societal expectations and the pressure to conform to traditional norms, as Yuna struggles to navigate her own desires and needs within the confines of a patriarchal society.

Through its thought-provoking narrative, All I See Is You raises important questions about the nature of love, identity, and the human condition. The film's atmospheric tension and suspenseful pacing only add to the sense of unease, making for a deeply unsettling viewing experience that lingers long after the credits roll.

overview: A father living in the forests of the Pacific Northwest with his six young kids tries to assimilate back into society.
tagline: He Prepared Them for Everything Except the Outside World.
title: Captain Fantastic
plot:
Captain Fantastic is a 2016 American drama film directed by Matt Ross and written by Matt Ross. The movie stars Viggo Mortensen, Frank Langella, and Kesten Halpin.

The story revolves around Ben Cash (Viggo Mortensen), a father who has chosen to raise his six children in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest, away from modern society. After their mother's death, Ben became disillusioned with the world and its values, leading him to reject the conventional norms of society. He believes that by living off the grid, he can provide his children with a more authentic and meaningful life.

The movie begins with Ben's eldest son, Jonah (George MacKay), who is now an adult and has become increasingly concerned about his family's lifestyle. He visits his father in their remote cabin, where he finds the family living in a primitive but harmonious community. The children are all skilled in various survival skills, such as hunting, gathering, and building shelters.

As Jonah spends more time with his family, he begins to see the world through their eyes. He witnesses their unique way of life, which is based on self-sufficiency, cooperation, and a deep connection with nature. However, he also starts to question whether this lifestyle is truly beneficial for his siblings, who are struggling to adapt to the harsh realities of living in the wilderness.

Meanwhile, Jonah's younger sister, Raya (Kesten Halpin), has become increasingly dependent on her father's protection and guidance. She struggles with the idea of leaving their isolated community and entering the outside world, where she will have to confront the challenges of modern society.

As the story unfolds, Ben's past is revealed through a series of flashbacks, which show his relationship with his wife, Naomi (Franka Potente), and how he became disillusioned with the world. These flashbacks also reveal that Ben's children are not just innocent bystanders but have been actively involved in their father's decision to live off the grid.

The plot thickens as Jonah becomes increasingly conflicted about his family's lifestyle. He begins to see the benefits of modern society, such as access to education and healthcare, which he believes would be better for his siblings than their isolated community. However, he also struggles with the idea of leaving his father behind, who has become like a surrogate parent to him.

In the end, Jonah makes the difficult decision to leave his family's cabin and enter the outside world. He is met with a mix of emotions from his siblings, who are both excited and scared about this new chapter in their lives. The movie ends on a hopeful note, as Jonah begins his journey into modern society, while Ben remains behind, content in his isolated community.

Throughout the movie, Viggo Mortensen delivers a powerful performance as Ben Cash, bringing depth and nuance to the character. His portrayal of a complex father figure who is both loving and flawed is both captivating and heartbreaking. The supporting cast, including Frank Langella and George MacKay, also deliver strong performances that add depth and complexity to the story.

Overall, Captain Fantastic is a thought-provoking movie that explores themes of family, identity, and community. It challenges viewers to consider alternative ways of living and raises important questions about the value of modern society versus a more primitive way of life.

overview: At the height of the Cold War, a troubled soldier forms a forbidden love triangle with a daring fighter pilot and his female comrade amid the dangerous surroundings of a Soviet Air Force Base.
tagline: Risk everything, trust no one.
title: Firebird
plot:
Firebird is a 2021 romantic war drama film directed by Peeter Rebane in his feature debut and based on Sergey Fetisov's memoir The Story of Roman. Set in the Soviet Air Force during the Cold War, it tells the true story of a forbidden love affair between a private and a fighter pilot. Tom Prior, who co-wrote and co-produced the film with Rebane, stars as Sergey, with Oleg Zagorodnii as Roman and Diana Pozharskaya as Luisa.

Sergey, a young private in the Soviet Air Force, has only a few weeks of military service left. He and his friends chafe under their commanders' strict control, he seems to be drifting into a romance with Luisa, the base commander's secretary, and his hobby of photography is barely tolerated by his superiors. When a new fighter pilot, Roman, arrives at the base, Sergey is assigned to assist him, and an intense attraction grows between them despite the threat of prison that hangs over homosexual relationships under the Soviet regime. They consummate their relationship and are nearly discovered by a KGB agent, and Roman urges Sergey to study acting in Moscow rather than go back to his family's farm. A year after leaving the service and starting a new life in the theater, Sergey is invited to Roman's wedding to Luisa, where he can barely hide his disappointment and his enduring love. Roman and Luisa have a son, but the marriage is a facade, and Roman still longs for Sergey. Leaving his wife and child, ostensibly to study in Moscow, he secretly rents an apartment with Sergey, and the two live together happily and travel together. When Luisa and the boy visit Moscow for Christmas, however, she discovers the truth, and her fury forces the men apart. Roman is later sent to fight in the Soviet–Afghan War and is killed. Sergey visits Luisa, who is still bitter toward him, and returns to his acting life in Moscow; he is last seen watching a performance of Stravinsky's ballet The Firebird, to which Roman had introduced him.

Rebane received Fetisov's memoir in 2014, and he and Prior interviewed the author before his death in 2017. Firebird premiered at the BFI Flare festival in London on 17 March 2021 and won an honorable mention for Best First Feature at San Francisco's Frameline festival. Reviews were mixed, with 57% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 49.

overview: The story of the Tuskegee Airmen, the first African-American pilots to fly in a combat squadron during World War II.
tagline: High-Octane Action and Daring Dogfights!
title: Red Tails
plot:
Red Tails is a 2012 American war drama film directed by Anthony Hemingway and produced by Lucasfilm Ltd., in association with 20th Century Fox, and Jerry Bruckheimer Films.

The film is set during World War II and tells the story of the Tuskegee Airmen, a group of African-American pilots who served in the United States Army Air Forces (USAAF) during the war. The movie begins with the introduction of the main characters: Captain Benjamin O. "B-24" O Malone Jr. (David Oyelowo), Lieutenant Colonel Peter "Pete" Skelly (Nate Parker), and Lieutenant Colonel John "Rip" Robertson (Tristan Wilds).

The story follows the Tuskegee Airmen as they undergo rigorous training at the Tuskegee Army Air Field in Alabama, where they face racism and skepticism from their white counterparts. Despite these challenges, the airmen prove themselves to be skilled pilots, earning the respect of their peers.

As the war intensifies, the Tuskegee Airmen are deployed to Italy, where they participate in several key battles against the German Luftwaffe. The film's climax features an intense dogfight between the Tuskegee Airmen and a group of enemy planes, which ends with the airmen emerging victorious.

Throughout the film, the characters grapple with issues of racism, prejudice, and identity. O Malone struggles to balance his duty as a pilot with his desire to prove himself in a society that doesn't trust him. Skelly faces personal demons, including a troubled relationship with his father. Robertson, meanwhile, finds solace in his faith and his relationships with his fellow pilots.

The film's title, "Red Tails," refers to the distinctive red paint applied to the tails of the Tuskegee Airmen's planes, which made them easily identifiable as friendly aircraft. The term also symbolizes the airmen's pride and identity, as they fly their planes into battle with courage and determination.

One of the most notable aspects of Red Tails is its attention to historical detail. The film features many authentic locations and props, including vintage aircraft and uniforms. The cast, which includes Cuba Gooding Jr., Tom Wilkinson, and Mahershala Ali, delivers strong performances that bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Red Tails is a powerful tribute to the Tuskegee Airmen, who played a crucial role in the Allied victory during World War II. The film's themes of perseverance, courage, and identity are timeless and universal, making it a compelling watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: An adventure-loving couple convince their friends to explore a remote, uncharted cave system in the forests of Northern Australia. With a tropical storm approaching, they abseil into the mouth of the cave, but when the caves start to flood, tensions rise as oxygen levels fall and the friends find themselves trapped. Unknown to them, the storm has also brought in a pack of dangerous and hungry crocodiles.
tagline: Descend into fear
title: Black Water: Abyss
plot:
Black Water: Abyss is a 2020 Australian survival horror film directed by Andrew Traucki and written by John Ridley and Sarah Smith. A standalone sequel to Traucki's Black Water (2007), it traps a group of friends in a flooding cave system deep in the Australian forest with an enormous saltwater crocodile.

After two Japanese tourists stumble into a hidden cave and are killed by an unseen creature, five friends set out to explore the same caverns, which Cash claims to have discovered: Cash, Eric, Jen, Yolanda and Victor. Ignoring a storm warning, they descend to an underground lake, unaware that heavy rain is flooding the entrance behind them. Victor is mauled by the crocodile when he wades in after something in the water, and when Cash and Eric try the submerged entry tunnel they find it blocked; Cash is later killed. Yolanda confides that she is pregnant, and on a scouting trip through a newly found passage she tells Eric that the baby is his rather than Victor's. Jen, finding photographs that betray the affair, tries to retrieve something from the water, slips and knocks herself out, and Victor is dragged under and killed while saving her. Spotting light beneath the surface, Eric realises water is draining toward the outside and the survivors swim for it; he splashes to distract the crocodile and is taken, while Jen and Yolanda escape through the animal's lair to the shore and their car. Fleeing, Jen swerves around a fallen tree into the river, and the crocodile attacks again. Jen, though seized and dragged under, kills the beast, and the two women, their friendship strained, head home together.

Jessica McNamee plays Jen, with Luke Mitchell as Eric, Amali Golden as Yolanda, Benjamin Hoetjes as Victor and Anthony J. Sharpe as Cash. Produced by Neal Kingston, Michael Robertson and Pam Collis for Thrills & Spills, in association with Screen Queensland and Altitude Film Entertainment, it was released in Australian cinemas by R & R Films on 10 July 2020, with Altitude selling it internationally and Screen Media handling the US release. Reviews were mixed to lukewarm; critics found the relationship drama thin but praised its claustrophobic tension and simplicity, with one calling it decently scary.

cast: Prince Eugenio Ruspoli di Poggio Suasa
overview: Journalist and man-about-town Marcello struggles to find his place in the world, torn between the allure of Rome's elite social scene and the stifling domesticity offered by his girlfriend, all the while searching for a way to become a serious writer.
tagline: The world’s most talked about movie today!
title: La Dolce Vita
plot:
La Dolce Vita is a 1960 Italian drama film directed by Federico Fellini, produced by Carlo Ponti for Produzioni Faun, and distributed by Pathé Consortium Cinéma.

The main themes of La Dolce Vita include:

1. **The Decline of the Bourgeoisie**: The film critiques the superficiality and moral decay of Rome's upper class, particularly in the context of post-war Italy. The protagonist, Marcello Rubini (played by Marcello Mastroianni), is a journalist who becomes disillusioned with the empty materialism and hedonism of his social circle.

2. **The Search for Meaning**: As Marcello navigates the city's nightlife, he encounters various characters struggling to find purpose and authenticity in their lives. This theme is reflected in the film's use of surreal and dreamlike sequences, which blur the lines between reality and fantasy.

3. **Moral Ambiguity**: La Dolce Vita explores the gray areas between right and wrong, highlighting the complexities of human relationships and the consequences of one's choices. Marcello's relationships with his friends, colleagues, and romantic interests are all marked by a sense of moral ambiguity.

4. **The Fragmentation of Identity**: The film portrays Marcello as a character in flux, struggling to define himself amidst the chaos of modern life. This theme is reflected in the use of multiple narrative threads and the blurring of boundaries between reality and fantasy.

5. **The Critique of Consumer Culture**: La Dolce Vita critiques the excesses of consumer culture, particularly in the context of post-war Italy. The film's depiction of Rome's nightlife, with its emphasis on luxury, decadence, and superficiality, serves as a commentary on the empty materialism of modern society.

Overall, La Dolce Vita is a complex and nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that continues to resonate with audiences today.

overview: When the renegade crew of Serenity agrees to hide a fugitive on their ship, they find themselves in an action-packed battle between the relentless military might of a totalitarian regime who will destroy anything – or anyone – to get the girl back and the bloodthirsty creatures who roam the uncharted areas of space. But... the greatest danger of all may be on their ship.
tagline: They aim to misbehave.
title: Serenity
plot:
Serenity is a 2005 American space Western written and directed by Joss Whedon in his feature directorial debut. It continues Whedon's Firefly, the Fox series cancelled in 2002, picking up after the final episode with the full main cast returning and Chiwetel Ejiofor joining as a new antagonist. Set in 2517, it follows the crew of a small transport ship whose captain and first mate fought on the losing Independent side against the Alliance.

After an interplanetary war, the central planets' Alliance rules a colonized star system. Prodigy River Tam, conditioned into a psychic assassin by Alliance scientists, was rescued by her brother Simon, a doctor, but in training she glimpsed the minds of senior officials, so a ruthless agent known only as the Operative is sent to recover her. The siblings shelter aboard Serenity with Captain Malcolm "Mal" Reynolds, first mate Zoe, her husband, pilot Wash, mercenary Jayne and mechanic Kaylee. A bank job goes wrong when River warns of approaching Reavers, savage cannibals, and later a subliminal signal hidden in an advertisement triggers her into a violent rampage. The hacker Mr. Universe finds the trigger and hears her whisper "Miranda". Mal escapes a trap the Operative sets through the courtesan Inara, and the crew learns that the Operative is killing everyone who has sheltered them, including their friend Shepherd Book. Disguising the ship as a Reaver vessel, they reach Miranda and find its population dead: a gas meant to calm the colonists made most so passive they simply stopped living, while a fraction became the Reavers. Betrayed by Mr. Universe, whom the Operative kills, the crew lures a Reaver fleet into the waiting Alliance armada. Wash lands the ship but is killed, and the others hold off the Reavers while Mal reaches the transmitter, defeats the Operative and broadcasts the truth. River saves the wounded Simon and kills the attackers. The Operative calls off his troops, helps repair Serenity and warns Mal that the Alliance may still pursue them.

Nathan Fillion plays Mal, with Ejiofor as the Operative, Summer Glau as River, Sean Maher as Simon, Gina Torres as Zoe, Alan Tudyk as Wash, Adam Baldwin as Jayne, Jewel Staite as Kaylee, Morena Baccarin as Inara and Ron Glass as Book. Universal released it on September 30, 2005. Reviews were positive (82% on Rotten Tomatoes), and it won the Hugo Award for Best Dramatic Presentation and the Nebula Award for Best Script, but it grossed only $40.4 million worldwide.

overview: A squad of the Jiaolong Commando Unit - Sea Dragon, a spec ops team of the Chinese Navy, carries out a hostage rescue operation in the nation of Yewaire, on the Arabian Peninsula, and fiercely fights against local rebel groups and Zaka, a terrorist organization.
production_companies: The P.L.A Navy Government TV Art Central of China
title: Operation Red Sea
plot:
Operation Red Sea is a 2018 Chinese war film directed by Guan Hu, produced by Bona Film Group, and starring Donnie Yen, Terry Ma, and Yang Mi. The movie is based on the true story of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy's (PLAN) rescue operation during the 2009 Haiti earthquake.

The film begins with a dramatic sequence showing the devastating effects of the earthquake on Haiti, followed by an introduction to the main characters: Captain Wang (Donnie Yen), a seasoned and respected naval officer; his team, including Lieutenant Liang (Terry Ma) and Lieutenant Zhang (Yang Mi); and their commander, Admiral Shen (Liu Haoran).

The story takes place in 2009, when Haiti is hit by a massive earthquake. The Chinese government receives a distress call from the Haitian government for help, and Captain Wang's team is dispatched to assist in the rescue efforts.

Upon arrival, the Chinese naval team discovers that the situation on the ground is chaotic, with many survivors trapped under the rubble of collapsed buildings. The team quickly gets to work, using their expertise and equipment to locate and extract those in need.

As the operation unfolds, Captain Wang's leadership skills are put to the test as he navigates the treacherous terrain and makes tough decisions to prioritize the rescue efforts. Meanwhile, Lieutenant Liang struggles with his own demons, which threaten to undermine his performance and compromise the mission.

Throughout the film, Guan Hu masterfully weaves together action-packed sequences, heart-wrenching moments of human drama, and poignant reflections on the true meaning of sacrifice and duty. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the intensity of the rescue efforts and the emotional toll on the characters.

As the operation reaches its climax, Captain Wang's team faces numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, limited resources, and personal conflicts. However, through their collective effort and unwavering commitment to their mission, they manage to save countless lives and bring hope to those in need.

The film concludes with a powerful tribute to the bravery and selflessness of the Chinese naval personnel who participated in the rescue operation. The final shot is of Captain Wang, standing alone on the deck of his ship, looking out at the sea, as the sound of sirens and the cries of the rescued fill the air.

Operation Red Sea is a gripping and emotionally charged film that showcases the heroism and sacrifice of the Chinese people during one of the most devastating humanitarian crises of the 21st century. With its stunning action sequences, poignant character development, and powerful themes, this movie is a must-see for fans of war dramas and those interested in exploring the complexities of human nature under extreme circumstances.

overview: Teacher and novelist François Bégaudeau plays a version of himself as he negotiates a year with his racially mixed students from a tough Parisian neighborhood.
tagline: The dynamics of a multicultural class and its teacher will enlighten.
title: The Class
plot:
The Class is a French drama film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the struggles of growing up. The story revolves around a young boy named François, who joins a class at a Parisian public school in the early 1960s. As François navigates his new environment, he faces various challenges, including bullying, social cliques, and family issues.

Through François's experiences, the film delves into themes of identity, belonging, and the search for self. The Class portrays a world where children are struggling to find their place in society, often mirroring the societal tensions and conflicts of the time period. The film also touches on the struggles of the working-class family, highlighting the difficulties faced by parents who are trying to provide for their children.

One of the main themes of The Class is the struggle for social acceptance and belonging. François's desire to fit in with his peers and be accepted as one of them drives much of the plot. However, this quest for acceptance often leads to conflicts and misunderstandings, highlighting the difficulties of navigating complex social dynamics.

The film also explores the theme of childhood innocence and vulnerability. François's experiences are marked by a sense of wonder and curiosity, which is slowly eroded as he faces the harsh realities of growing up. This theme is closely tied to the idea of identity, as François struggles to define himself and find his place in the world.

Overall, The Class is a powerful exploration of the challenges faced by children growing up in a rapidly changing society. Through its portrayal of complex social dynamics, family struggles, and the search for self, the film offers a nuanced and thought-provoking commentary on the human experience.

overview: After a yachting accident, a millionaire and his wife are shipwrecked on a desert island along with their former deckhand, Manuel.
title: Survival Island
plot:

overview: Enjoying college life as a popular student, Laura shares everything with her more than 800 friends on Facebook. But one day, after accepting a friend request from a  social outcast named Marina, Laura’s life is cursed...
tagline: Be careful who you click with.
title: Friend Request
plot:
Friend Request is a 2016 German psychological thriller film that revolves around the dark side of social media and online relationships. The movie follows Laura, a young woman who receives a friend request from an unknown person on Facebook, which sets off a chain of events that exposes her deepest secrets and vulnerabilities.

The main theme of Friend Request is the blurring of reality and online personas, as well as the consequences of sharing intimate details with strangers in the digital age. The film explores how social media can be both a tool for connection and a breeding ground for manipulation and exploitation.

Through Laura's character, the movie delves into the complexities of online relationships, highlighting the ease with which people can curate fake identities and manipulate others through their digital presence. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems, and the lines between reality and fantasy are constantly blurred.

The film also touches on themes of loneliness, isolation, and the human desire for connection in a world where technology often serves as a substitute for meaningful relationships. Ultimately, Friend Request is a cautionary tale about the dangers of getting too close to strangers online and the importance of being mindful of our digital footprint.

overview: Three friends are asked to be bridesmaids at a wedding of a woman they used to ridicule back in high school.
tagline: Old habits party hard.
title: Bachelorette
plot:
Bachelorette is a dark comedy that delves into the complexities of female friendships and the darker aspects of human nature. The film follows the story of Regan, a woman who is about to get married, but her bachelorette party takes an unexpected turn when she gets drunk and passes out, leaving her friends to deal with the aftermath.

As the night progresses, Regan's friends' true personalities are revealed, showcasing their flaws and insecurities. The film explores themes of female empowerment, toxic relationships, and the blurred lines between friendship and codependency. Through Regan's journey, the movie critiques societal expectations placed on women, particularly in regards to marriage and relationships.

The film also touches on the idea of identity and how it can be shaped by external factors, such as social media and peer pressure. The characters' struggles with self-acceptance and self-worth serve as a commentary on the pressures of modern life and the importance of embracing one's true nature.

Ultimately, Bachelorette is a satirical exploration of the human condition, using humor to highlight the complexities and nuances of female relationships and the challenges of growing up.

overview: A harried prehistoric bird mother entrusts her precious, soon-to-hatch egg to Sid. When she recommends him to her neighbours, business booms at his new egg-sitting service. However, dastardly pirate bunny, Squint, who is seeking revenge on the herd, steals, camouflages and hides all the eggs. Once again, with Squint’s twin brother assisting, Manny, Diego and the rest of the gang come to the rescue and take off on a daring mission that turns into the world’s first Easter egg hunt.
tagline: The world’s first Easter egg hunt. It all started right here.
title: Ice Age: The Great Egg-Scapade
plot:
Directed by Ricardo Curtis for Blue Sky Studios, Ice Age: The Great Egg-Scapade is an animated comedy-mystery television special first broadcast in 2016. Set between Ice Age: Continental Drift and Ice Age: Collision Course, it brings back most of the franchise's voice cast, with Ray Romano as Manny, John Leguizamo as Sid, Denis Leary as Diego, Queen Latifah as Ellie, Keke Palmer as Peaches, and Seann William Scott and Josh Peck as the opossum brothers Crash and Eddie. Seth Green replaces Aziz Ansari as the pirate rabbit Squint, and the cast also includes Blake Anderson as his brother Clint, Taraji P. Henson, Gabriel Iglesias, Wendy Williams and Chris Wedge as Scrat.

As spring arrives, the herd prepares for Easter. Ellie struggles to decorate alone while Manny, Diego, Crash and Eddie lounge around watching a fight between animals, and the opossums try in vain to prank Peaches, accidentally inventing April Fools' Day. Peaches only wants to spend the holiday with her friends. Sid, meanwhile, offers to look after other animals' eggs for their parents, to the scorn of Manny and Diego.

Squint, a former member of Captain Gutt's pirate crew, has spent months hiding in his family's burrow with his mother and his lazy brother Clint. Eager for revenge on Manny and his friends for what they did to Gutt and his ship, he demands that they build him a new one, and when they refuse he steals the eggs while Sid sleeps, leaving Sid to take the blame. Clint offers the friends a map, and they recover the eggs, which Squint has painted to blend in with their surroundings, but one is still missing. Squint threatens to scramble it unless he gets his ship by the next day. Clint lures his brother into an ambush, and the last egg turns out to have been painted to look like an acorn and snatched by Scrat. After a struggle and a rescue at the edge of a cliff, Sid defeats Squint with the help of a trap and one of Crash and Eddie's pranks. The family celebrates Easter together, and Sid proposes that Clint become the Easter Bunny, painting and hiding eggs every year.

The special premiered on Fox on 20 March 2016, as a lead-in to the live special The Passion: New Orleans, and was released on DVD in March 2017.

overview: FBI agent Jack Crawford is out for revenge when his partner is killed and all clues point to the mysterious assassin Rogue. But when Rogue turns up years later to take care of some unfinished business, he triggers a violent clash of rival gangs. Will the truth come out before it's too late? And when the dust settles, who will remain standing?
tagline: Vengeance is the ultimate weapon.
title: War
plot:
War, released in many countries as Rogue Assassin, is a 2007 American action thriller directed by Philip G. Atwell in his feature debut, with fight choreography by Corey Yuen. Jason Statham plays FBI agent John Crawford and Jet Li the mysterious assassin Rogue, in the actors' second pairing after The One (2001), with John Lone, Devon Aoki and Luis Guzmán in supporting roles. Its working title, Rogue, was changed to avoid confusion with another film.

During a shootout with the yakuza at a San Francisco dock warehouse, Crawford and his partner, Tom Lone, encounter Rogue, a former CIA assassin working for the Japanese gangsters. Rogue is about to execute Crawford when Lone shoots him in the face and he falls into the water, presumed dead. Soon afterward, Lone, his wife and his daughter are murdered and their house burned. Three years later Rogue resurfaces as an enforcer for Triad boss Li Chang, secretly igniting a war between the Triads and the yakuza of Shiro Yanagawa while recovering a pair of antique gold horses, heirlooms of Chang's family. Crawford, now head of the FBI's Asian organized crime unit, pursues him obsessively, at the cost of his own family, but Rogue always stays a step ahead and wins the trust of both bosses. He kills Chang but spares his wife and child, then turns on the yakuza.

When Rogue delivers the horses to Yanagawa and kills his men, a sword duel reveals that he is not Rogue at all but Tom Lone, who survived and surgically altered his appearance to take the dead assassin's identity and avenge his family. Yanagawa tells him that Crawford was on his payroll and leaked Lone's address, and Lone kills him, sending Chang's widow a gold horse and Yanagawa's daughter her father's head, each with the message "Make a new life". Lone then summons Crawford to the dock warehouse, where, backed by FBI sniper Goi, Crawford fights him and learns his identity. Crawford confesses that he was blackmailed into giving up the address, believing Lone would only be roughed up, and begs forgiveness. Lone refuses; when Crawford steps into Goi's line of fire to protect him, Lone shoots him dead and drives off to start a new life.

Released in the United States on August 24, 2007, the film opened with $9.8 million and grossed $40.7 million worldwide. Critics panned it, giving it 14% on Rotten Tomatoes and 36 on Metacritic.

overview: The beloved Crawleys and their intrepid staff prepare for the most important moment of their lives. A royal visit from the King and Queen of England will unleash scandal, romance and intrigue that will leave the future of Downton hanging in the balance.
tagline: We've been expecting you
title: Downton Abbey
plot:
Downton Abbey is a 2019 film directed by Jake Hanson and written by Julian Fellowes, based on his own television series of the same name.

The main themes of Downton Abbey (2019) include:

1. Family dynamics: The film explores the complexities of the Crawley family's relationships, particularly between the aristocratic Lord Grantham (Hugh Bonneville) and his daughters, as well as the tensions between the old money and the new.
2. Social class and inequality: The movie highlights the rigid social hierarchy of the time period, with the aristocracy at the top and the working class struggling to make ends meet.
3. Tradition vs. modernity: As the Crawleys face various challenges, they must navigate the tension between preserving their traditional way of life and adapting to changing times.
4. Identity and belonging: The film explores the struggles of individual characters to find their place within the family and society, particularly for those who feel like outsiders or are trying to forge their own paths.

The story begins with the Crawleys preparing for a visit from their American cousin, Lady Rose (Lily James), who is returning after her honeymoon. However, their plans are soon disrupted by the arrival of a mysterious stranger, Anna Smith (Michelle Dockery), who claims to be the daughter of the late butler, Mr. Carson.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Anna is actually the long-lost daughter of the late butler's sister, and she has been seeking revenge against the Crawleys for her family's mistreatment. The film builds towards a dramatic confrontation between Anna and the Crawleys, which ultimately leads to a surprising revelation about the true identity of the mysterious stranger.

Throughout the movie, Julian Fellowes weaves together themes of love, loyalty, and social status, creating a rich and engaging narrative that explores the complexities of the human experience.

overview: Alex Belli is a 37 year old advertising executive whose fiancée Elena has just left him, and who is having difficulty at work trying to think of a good advertising campaign for a new Japanese product. Niki is a bubbly 17 year old student. She has three best friends with whom she shares all her problems, and an annoying ex-boyfriend Fabio who is set on getting her back, but Niki's not interested. One day on his way to work, Alex collides with Niki on a city street. They soon begin a romance, despite their 20-year age gap.
title: Sorry if I Love You
plot:
Sorry If I Love You is a 2008 South Korean romantic comedy film directed by Han Suk-joo and produced by Medusa Film. The movie tells the story of two people who meet by chance, but their lives are forever changed when they fall in love.

At its core, Sorry If I Love You explores the complexities of human relationships, love, and identity. It delves into the theme of self-discovery, as the protagonist navigates her way through life, trying to find her place in the world. The film also examines the societal pressures that women face, particularly in terms of marriage and family expectations.

The movie is also a poignant commentary on the fragility of human connections and the impermanence of relationships. It highlights the pain and longing that can come with loving someone who may not be able to reciprocate those feelings or return your love. The film's portrayal of unrequited love is both heart-wrenching and relatable, making it a deeply moving and emotional experience for audiences.

Overall, Sorry If I Love You is a beautifully crafted film that explores the intricacies of human emotions, relationships, and identity with sensitivity, nuance, and depth.

overview: While flying a routine reconnaissance mission over Bosnia, fighter pilot Chris Burnett photographs something he wasn't supposed to see and gets shot down behind enemy lines, where he must outrun an army led by a ruthless Serbian general. With time running out and a deadly tracker on his trail, Burnett's commanding officer decides to risk his career and launch a renegade rescue mission to save his life.
tagline: His only weapon is his will to survive.
title: Behind Enemy Lines
plot:
Behind Enemy Lines is a 2001 American war drama film directed by John Moore. The movie follows the story of Lieutenant A.K. Waters (played by Owen Wilson), an American Navy pilot shot down over Bosnia, and Chief Matt Bissonnette (played by Gabriel Macht), a U.S. Army medic who becomes his rescuer.

The main themes of Behind Enemy Lines include:

1. **Heroism and Sacrifice**: The film highlights the bravery and selflessness of Lieutenant Waters and Chief Bissonnette as they risk their lives to save each other in enemy territory.
2. **War and Its Consequences**: The movie depicts the harsh realities of war, including the loss of life, the destruction of property, and the emotional toll on those involved.
3. **Friendship and Camaraderie**: The bond between Waters and Bissonnette serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of human connection in the face of adversity.
4. **Nationalism and Patriotism**: The film explores the themes of national pride and patriotism, as both characters are driven by a desire to protect their country and its people.

The movie's plot is engaging and suspenseful, with plenty of action-packed sequences and intense emotional moments. Overall, Behind Enemy Lines is a gripping war drama that explores the complexities of human relationships in the midst of conflict.

overview: A man breaks into a tech billionaire's empty vacation home, but things go sideways when the arrogant mogul and his wife arrive for a last-minute getaway.
tagline: Every kidnap is a compromise.
title: Windfall
plot:
Windfall is a 2022 American crime thriller film directed by Charlie McDowell from a screenplay by Andrew Kevin Walker and Justin Lader. Its unnamed characters are played by Jason Segel as Nobody, a burglar, Jesse Plemons as a tech CEO, Lily Collins as his wife and Omar Leyva as a gardener.

A wealthy CEO and his wife arrive at their secluded vacation home and find a burglar inside. The CEO offers him money to leave and promises not to involve the police, and the burglar locks the couple in the sauna. Back at his car, however, he spots a security camera that he suspects has recorded him, and he returns to the house, now demanding $500,000 in cash to disappear for good. The CEO's assistant says the money cannot arrive until the following afternoon, forcing the three to wait together. Their conversations expose the strains in the marriage, although the CEO looks forward to having children. That night the wife confides that she is unhappy, and the burglar tells her to stop casting herself as a victim when she married a man for his money. The next day the CEO guesses that the intruder is a worker laid off because of the algorithm he invented to help companies downsize. When a gardener arrives to discuss planting an oak tree, the CEO secretly writes "Call 911" on his sketch, but the burglar notices and forces the gardener inside, and the wife joins him in condemning her husband for endangering another life. Hours later, the CEO snaps, belittling the burglar and claiming he will never harm them because his life is meaningless. The burglar fires a warning shot, the gardener tries to flee, and he crashes through a glass door, dying when a shard pierces his neck. The money is delivered and the wife collects it, seeing a passing car but choosing not to wave it down. The burglar ties the couple up in separate rooms, admits that he only wanted to know what it is like to live rich and tells the CEO that his wife has been secretly taking birth control pills. Cutting herself free, the wife kills the burglar with a small statue, then shoots her husband dead, plants the gun in the burglar's hand and drives away.

Shot in Ojai, California, in 2021 and then acquired by Netflix for an eight-figure sum, the film was released on 18 March 2022. Reviews were mixed, with 58% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 52, though critics praised its cast.

overview: Three kids hire a low-budget bodyguard to protect them from the playground bully, not realising he is just a homeless beggar and petty thief looking for some easy cash.
tagline: You get what you pay for
title: Drillbit Taylor
plot:
Drillbit Taylor is a 2008 American comedy film directed by Steven Brill. The movie revolves around the story of Matt Allen, a high school student who enlists the help of his eccentric neighbor, Drillbit Taylor, to impress a girl and navigate the challenges of adolescence.

At its core, Drillbit Taylor explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and self-discovery. The film delves into the complexities of male relationships, showcasing the bond between Matt and Drillbit as they navigate the ups and downs of growing up together. Through their adventures, the movie highlights the importance of having a supportive network of friends who can provide guidance and encouragement during difficult times.

The film also touches on themes of identity and belonging. Matt's desire to fit in with his peers and gain acceptance from his crush serves as a catalyst for his journey, which ultimately leads him to discover his own strengths and weaknesses. Drillbit Taylor, too, is on a quest for self-discovery, using his unorthodox methods to find purpose and meaning in his life.

Furthermore, the movie pokes fun at societal expectations and the pressures of conformity. The film's portrayal of suburban life, with its emphasis on material possessions and social status, serves as a commentary on the superficiality of modern society. Through Drillbit Taylor's antics, the movie cleverly subverts these expectations, offering a humorous critique of the norms that govern our lives.

Overall, Drillbit Taylor is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores the complexities of male friendship, self-discovery, and the challenges of growing up in a world that often values superficiality over substance.

overview: Miss Meadows is a school teacher with impeccable manners and grace. However, underneath the candy-sweet exterior hides a ruthless gun-toting vigilante who takes it upon herself to right the wrongs in the world by whatever means necessary. For Miss Meadows, bad behavior is simply unforgivable.
tagline: She doesn't play well with others.
title: Miss Meadows
plot:
Miss Meadows is a dark comedy film that explores the complexities of female relationships and societal expectations. The story revolves around Miss Meadows, a quiet and reserved high school student who appears to be an outsider among her peers. However, beneath her reserved exterior lies a sharp wit and a deep-seated desire for revenge against those who have wronged her.

The main theme of Miss Meadows is the struggle for female empowerment in a patriarchal society. The film critiques the societal norms that restrict women's behavior and expectations, particularly in the context of high school life. Through Miss Meadows' character, the film highlights the difficulties faced by women who are perceived as "different" or "outsiders," and how these individuals often feel forced to conform to societal norms in order to survive.

The movie also explores the theme of revenge and its consequences. Miss Meadows' desire for revenge is a complex and multifaceted one, driven by a sense of injustice and a need for self-preservation. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Miss Meadows' actions are motivated by a deep-seated need to protect herself from those who have hurt her.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of social hierarchy and the ways in which high school life is structured around cliques and social status. The movie critiques the superficiality of this system, highlighting the ways in which it can lead to feelings of isolation and disconnection among students.

Overall, Miss Meadows is a dark comedy that uses humor and satire to explore complex themes related to female empowerment, revenge, and social hierarchy.

overview: A young woman comes to in a roadside diner with no idea where she is or how she got there. Split between two timelines, she gets taken on a violent journey as she seeks out the person responsible for her lover's death.
tagline: There are two sides to every story.
plot:
88 is a 2015 Canadian thriller directed by April Mullen and written by Tim Doiron, starring Katharine Isabelle as Gwen, a woman whose revenge plot unravels when she slips into fugue states and must piece her memories back together. Christopher Lloyd, Kyle Schmid, Jesse McCartney and Michael Ironside also appear.

Gwen snaps out of a daze in a diner, unsure where she is, and finds a pistol in her bag; when police confront her, she accidentally shoots a waitress and flees. A key leads her to a hotel room she does not remember, where she finds the body of her best friend, Winks. A man who arrives to kill her is himself killed by Ty, who insists that the two of them had planned to murder an underworld boss named Cyrus at the diner. Gwen swears she could never kill anyone, but she leaves with him. Flashbacks reveal that she blames Cyrus for the death of her boyfriend, Aster: after she saw Cyrus with a dead woman, later revealed to be Ty's sister, he ordered both Gwen and Aster killed.

Seeking weapons from the illegal arms dealer Lemmy, Gwen and Ty are tracked down by Sheriff Knowles; Lemmy dies in the ensuing shootout, Ty escapes wounded, and the terrified Gwen is arrested. She claims Cyrus framed her, and Knowles, more interested in the gangster, offers her a deal if she can deliver him. Ty storms the station, killing several officers, but dies in a crossfire as he and Gwen escape. More flashbacks show that Gwen herself caused several deaths while in a fugue state, including the killing of Winks, who had given them Cyrus's location but whose concern for Gwen made her suspicious. Still unsure of her own motives, Gwen resumes her hunt, shooting a police officer who pulls her over for speeding. Confronting Cyrus, she blames him for every death, but he denies it, and under his prodding she remembers that she accidentally shot Aster herself while trying to warn him. Telling her to blame him so she might escape prosecution, Cyrus shoots himself in front of her. A final flashback returns to the diner, where Aster's favorite song on the jukebox sends the distraught Gwen into a daze.

The film premiered at the Glasgow Film Festival, and Millennium Entertainment released it on home video in the United States on January 6, 2015. Canadian critics were unenthusiastic: the National Post gave it zero stars, while The Globe and Mail and the Toronto Star rated it 2.5 and 2 out of 4.

overview: A romantic comedy centered on Dexter and Emma, who first meet during their graduation in 1988 and proceed to keep in touch regularly. The film follows what they do on July 15 annually, usually doing something together.
tagline: Twenty years. Two people.
title: One Day
plot:
One Day is a 2011 romantic drama directed by Lone Scherfig, with a screenplay by David Nicholls adapted from his 2009 novel. It stars Anne Hathaway and Jim Sturgess as two friends whose relationship is traced through a single date, St. Swithin's Day, 15 July, over twenty years, with Patricia Clarkson, Ken Stott and Romola Garai in supporting roles.

Emma Morley, from a working-class northern family, and Dexter Mayhew, a privileged Winchester-educated southerner, spend a chaste night together after graduating from Edinburgh University in 1988 and agree to stay friends. Emma moves to London hoping to write but ends up waitressing in a Mexican restaurant, where she meets the would-be comedian Ian, while Dexter drifts abroad, teaching English in Paris. On a 1992 holiday in Dinard, Emma rebuffs him because he will not commit. Dexter becomes a brash late-night television host, arrives drunk to see his terminally ill mother, who tells him he is not yet a nice person, and grows increasingly obnoxious; Emma, now a teacher living unhappily with Ian, breaks with him in 1996 after a coke-fuelled dinner at which he mocks her profession, saying she loves but no longer likes him. By the late 1990s Dexter's career has collapsed and he is with Sylvie, while Emma leaves Ian, who nonetheless urges her to publish her stories. Reconciled at a friend's wedding in 2000, Emma has a book deal and Dexter is engaged to a pregnant Sylvie, who later cheats on him with his old friend Callum. In 2003 Dexter visits Emma, now a successful author in Paris; she chases after him, and they finally become a couple, marry and try for a child while he runs a café. In 2006 Emma is killed by a lorry while cycling. Dexter spirals, but is eventually steadied by his daughter Jasmine, his father, Sylvie and even Ian. In 2011 he climbs Arthur's Seat with Jasmine, and a flashback returns to the day after they first met in 1988.

Hathaway plays Emma and Sturgess plays Dexter, with Clarkson and Stott as his parents, Garai as Sylvie and Rafe Spall as Ian. A Random House Films and Focus Features production co-financed by Film4, it was shot from July 2010 in Edinburgh, London and Brittany. Focus released it in the US on 19 August 2011. Reviews were largely negative, at 36% on Rotten Tomatoes, though Roger Ebert praised its wit; Hathaway's Yorkshire accent drew particular criticism.

overview: The true story of Marine Corporal Megan Leavey, who forms a powerful bond with an aggressive combat dog, Rex. While deployed in Iraq, the two complete more than 100 missions and save countless lives, until an IED explosion puts their faithfulness to the test.
tagline: Based on the true story of a marine's best friend.
title: Megan Leavey
plot:
Megan Leavey is a 2017 American biographical war drama film directed by A.J. Edwards. The movie is based on the true story of U.S. Marine Corps Corporal Megan Leavey, who served in Iraq and was awarded the Purple Heart for her bravery.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. **Loyalty and Sacrifice**: The film highlights the strong bond between Megan and her K9 partner, Rex, a German Shepherd dog that she trained to detect explosives. Their partnership is built on trust, loyalty, and sacrifice, as they work together to protect their fellow soldiers.
2. **War and Its Effects**: The movie portrays the harsh realities of war, including the emotional toll it takes on soldiers and their families. It explores the themes of PTSD, grief, and the struggle to readjust to civilian life after serving in combat.
3. **Female Empowerment**: Megan Leavey is a powerful example of a strong female character who defies traditional stereotypes. She is a Marine Corps corporal, a rare breed in the military, and her story serves as an inspiration to women everywhere.
4. **Grief and Loss**: The film deals with the theme of grief and loss, particularly in the context of war. Megan's experiences in Iraq are marked by tragedy, including the death of Rex, which serves as a catalyst for her emotional journey.
5. **Redemption and Healing**: Through Megan's story, the movie explores the idea of redemption and healing. As she navigates her post-war life, she finds ways to honor Rex's memory and find purpose in her own life.

Overall, Megan Leavey is a powerful and moving film that celebrates the bravery and sacrifice of U.S. Marine Corps Corporal Megan Leavey and her loyal companion, Rex.

overview: A man enters a small town which unwittingly gets obscured as girls, money, bank heists, police, killers and even a loner will strive forward in this crime-thriller.
tagline: Safe is never sex. It’s dangerous.
title: The Hot Spot
plot:
The Hot Spot is a crime drama film that revolves around the story of a young woman named Annie Reed, who becomes embroiled in a complex web of crime and deception. At its core, the movie explores the theme of female empowerment and independence, as Annie navigates a male-dominated world to uncover the truth about her past.

The film also delves into the darker aspects of human nature, particularly the corrupting influence of power and greed. The main antagonist, a ruthless and cunning crime lord, serves as a symbol of the destructive forces that can consume individuals when they prioritize their own interests over others.

Furthermore, The Hot Spot touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery, as Annie struggles to come to terms with her own past and find her place in the world. Through her journey, the movie suggests that true empowerment lies not in conforming to societal expectations, but in embracing one's individuality and taking control of one's own destiny.

Overall, The Hot Spot is a gripping and intense thriller that explores complex themes and moral ambiguities, leaving audiences on the edge of their seats as they follow Annie's perilous quest for truth and redemption.

overview: For centuries, a secret Order of priests has existed within the Church. A renegade priest, Father Alex Bernier, is sent to Rome to investigate the mysterious death of one of the Order's most revered members. Following a series of strangely similar killings, Bernier launches an investigation that forces him to confront unimaginable evil.
production_companies: N1 European Film Produktions GmbH & Co. KG
tagline: Every soul has its price.
title: The Order
plot:
The Order, also released as The Sin Eater, is a 2003 supernatural mystery thriller written and directed by Brian Helgeland. It reunites the director with Heath Ledger, Mark Addy and Shannyn Sossamon, whom he had directed in A Knight's Tale (2001), alongside Benno Fürmann and Peter Weller. The story follows a young priest investigating a suspicious death in Rome who uncovers a sin eater, a figure able to absolve sins outside the Church's authority.

Father Alex Bernier, a disillusioned member of the Carolingians, a fictional order devoted to exorcism and fighting demonic forces, learns that the order's head, Father Dominic, has died mysteriously in Rome. Cardinal Driscoll, an influential Vatican figure and candidate for the papacy, sends him to investigate. Before he leaves, he is visited by Mara Williams, an artist he once tried to exorcise, who had attacked him during the rite and been committed to an asylum; she senses he is in danger, and he lets her come along. Examining Dominic's body, Alex recognises marks left by a sin eater. With his fellow Carolingian Thomas Garrett, he secretly buries Dominic, who was excommunicated and denied consecrated ground. Driscoll gives Alex an ancient dagger and a fragment of parchment bearing an Aramaic incantation, which Alex takes to be a means of destroying the sin eater. Seeking answers, Alex and Thomas are led to the mysterious Black Pope of an underground sect, and a riddle from a dying man brings Alex to the sin eater himself, William Eden, at St. Peter's Basilica, while Thomas is hurt by demons. The weary, centuries-old Eden wants Alex to succeed him, but Alex refuses, intending to leave the priesthood for Mara. Eden then fatally wounds Mara, disguising it as a suicide attempt, and Alex eats her sins so she can reach heaven. Thomas discovers that Driscoll is the Black Pope and that the full text reveals the dagger rite transfers the sin eater's power. Too late to warn him, he arrives after Alex has stabbed Eden and inherited the role. Dominic, Eden and Driscoll had all used him. Alex exposes Driscoll, refuses to absolve him when the ruined cardinal attempts suicide, and resolves to grant salvation only to those he judges worthy.

Ledger plays Alex, with Sossamon as Mara, Fürmann as Eden, Addy as Thomas and Weller as Driscoll. 20th Century Fox released it on September 5, 2003. Critics panned it, giving it 10% on Rotten Tomatoes, with Rolling Stone's Peter Travers dismissing it as "The Exorcist warmed over".

overview: Welcome to Rekall, the company that can turn your dreams into real memories. For a factory worker named Douglas Quaid, even though he's got a beautiful wife who he loves, the mind-trip sounds like the perfect vacation from his frustrating life - real memories of life as a super-spy might be just what he needs. But when the procedure goes horribly wrong, Quaid becomes a hunted man. Finding himself on the run from the police - controlled by Chancellor Cohaagen, the leader of the free world - Quaid teams up with a rebel fighter to find the head of the underground resistance and stop Cohaagen. The line between fantasy and reality gets blurred and the fate of his world hangs in the balance as Quaid discovers his true identity, his true love, and his true fate.
tagline: What Is Real?
title: Total Recall
plot:
Total Recall is a 2012 American science fiction action film directed by Len Wiseman from a screenplay by Kurt Wimmer and Mark Bomback, an adaptation of the 1990 film inspired by Philip K. Dick's 1966 short story "We Can Remember It for You Wholesale". It stars Colin Farrell, Kate Beckinsale and Jessica Biel, with Bryan Cranston, Bokeem Woodbine, John Cho and Bill Nighy, and unlike the original it is set entirely on Earth.

At the end of the 21st century, chemical warfare has left only two habitable regions: the wealthy United Federation of Britain and the Colony in Australia, whose workers commute daily through the planet's core on a gravity elevator called "The Fall". A Resistance branded as terrorists fights for better conditions in the Colony. Factory worker Douglas Quaid, troubled by dreams of being a spy with a mysterious woman, visits Rekall, a company that implants artificial memories, and chooses a secret-agent fantasy, but the technician finds he already holds real spy memories. Police storm the clinic and Quaid instinctively kills the entire squad. At home his wife, Lori, tries to kill him, revealing that she is a UFB agent and that their seven-year marriage is a six-week fiction.

Guided by a message from his former colleague Hammond and a recording he left himself, Quaid flees to the UFB, where he is rescued from Lori by Melina, the woman from his dreams. Another recording reveals that he is Carl Hauser, an agent of Chancellor Cohaagen who defected to the Resistance after learning of a kill code that could stop the robot army Cohaagen plans to use to seize the Colony. When his friend Harry claims Quaid is still dreaming and must kill Melina to wake, Quaid shoots Harry instead. Resistance leader Matthias begins searching Quaid's memories, but Cohaagen, who invented the kill code to locate him, storms the base, kills Matthias and captures Melina. Freed by Hammond, who dies in the attempt, Quaid sneaks aboard the Fall as it carries the robots, plants explosives and rescues Melina; the blast destroys the elevator, Cohaagen and his army. In an ambulance Quaid unmasks a disguised Lori and kills her, then reunites with Melina as the Colony declares independence.

Released by Columbia Pictures on August 3, 2012, it grossed $211.8 million worldwide on a $125 million budget. Reviews were negative, with 30% on Rotten Tomatoes and 43 on Metacritic.

original_title: Behind the Fright: The Making of American Horror Story
overview: In this video-short go behind the scenes with the cast of "American Horror Story" on how the show is made.
title: Behind the Fright: The Making of American Horror Story
plot:
Behind the Fright: The Making of American Horror Story is a 2012 American documentary short directed and written by Jeffrey Lerner. Running about 25 minutes, it is a behind-the-scenes featurette made for the home-video release of American Horror Story: The Complete First Season, the three-disc Blu-ray set released on 25 September 2012. It sits among the set's bonus features alongside two shorter pieces, Overture to Horror: Creating the Title Sequence and Out of the Shadows: Meet the House Ghosts.

The featurette examines the production of the first season of the FX horror anthology series created by Ryan Murphy and Brad Falchuk, later subtitled Murder House, which aired from October to December 2011. That season follows the Harmon family, Vivien (Connie Britton), Ben (Dylan McDermott) and their teenage daughter Violet (Taissa Farmiga), who move from Boston to Los Angeles in an attempt to repair a marriage damaged by a miscarriage and infidelity. They settle in a restored mansion known to locals as the "Murder House", unaware that it is haunted by the ghosts of its former residents and their victims.

Combining behind-the-scenes footage with interviews, the documentary has co-creator and executive producer Falchuk explain the genesis of the project and how its many strange ideas came together into a dramatic horror series. The principal actors, among them Britton, McDermott, Farmiga, Jessica Lange, Evan Peters, Denis O'Hare and Alexandra Breckenridge, discuss the show and their characters, while members of the creative team, including producer Alexis Martin Woodall, set and costume designers, make-up artists and visual effects artists, describe how the distinctive look of the series was achieved. The film covers the show's inspirations, themes, characters, locations, sets, make-up and visual effects.

Reviewers of the Blu-ray gave the featurette a generally favourable mention.
