Steven Cohen of High-Def Digest described it as a fairly comprehensive look at the show's production and recommended that fans take a look, while noting that co-creator Ryan Murphy was conspicuously absent. Bloody Disgusting's review of the set likewise remarked that Murphy's absence stood out sharply, especially as the other participants spent part of their time on camera talking about him.

overview: A group of middle schoolers discover a Spirit Halloween store is haunted and must survive the night.
tagline: One Spirit. One Store. One Night.
title: Spirit Halloween: The Movie
plot:
Spirit Halloween: The Movie is a 2022 American fantasy comedy film directed by Sean McNamara and written by Sean McNamara, David Kirschner, and Chris McKenna. The movie follows the story of Ollie (played by Justin Long), a young man who returns to his hometown of Salem, Massachusetts, for Halloween.

Ollie's family has owned Spirit Halloween, a seasonal retail chain that sells Halloween decorations and costumes, for generations. However, when Ollie's father passes away, he leaves behind a mysterious will that reveals a shocking secret: the company is actually a front for an ancient curse that has been protecting Salem from supernatural forces.

The curse was placed by a witch named Winifred (played by Janina Gavankar), who was wronged by the town's founders. The curse can only be broken if Ollie, who is the last living heir of the company, can find and destroy the three magical artifacts needed to lift it.

As Ollie delves deeper into the mystery, he meets a group of allies, including a witch named Willow (played by Zoey Deutch) and a warlock named Rowan (played by Willa Amai). Together, they embark on a quest to find the artifacts, which are hidden in various locations around Salem.

Along the way, Ollie must confront his own destiny and the dark forces that have been manipulating him from the beginning. He also discovers that he has a special connection to the curse and the town's history, which makes him both the key to breaking it and the target of those who seek to keep it in place.

As the story unfolds, Ollie and his friends face numerous challenges and obstacles, including ghostly apparitions, magical creatures, and treacherous rival treasure hunters. In the end, they must work together to find the final artifact and break the curse before it's too late.

The movie features a blend of humor, action, and fantasy elements, with plenty of nods to classic Halloween movies and traditions. The film's visuals are also noteworthy, with a vibrant color palette and creative use of special effects to bring the supernatural world to life.

Overall, Spirit Halloween: The Movie is a fun and entertaining take on the Halloween genre, with a strong cast of characters and a compelling storyline that explores themes of identity, community, and the power of tradition.

overview: In the grim Alaskan winter, a naturalist hunts for wolves blamed for killing a local boy, but he soon finds himself swept into a chilling mystery.
title: Hold the Dark
plot:
Hold the Dark is a 2018 American thriller film directed by Jeremy Saulnier, based on the novel of the same name by Matt Bell.

The main themes of Hold the Dark revolve around the darker aspects of human nature, particularly in the context of rural America. The story takes place in a remote Alaskan town where a series of gruesome child abductions has occurred, and a former Marine turned snow tracker, Vernon Sutton (played by Alexander Skarsgård), is hired to track down the perpetrator.

Some of the main themes explored in Hold the Dark include:

1. **The darkness within human nature**: The film delves into the idea that humans are capable of great evil, and that this darkness can be lurking beneath the surface of seemingly ordinary people.
2. **Trauma and PTSD**: Vernon's past traumas and his struggles with PTSD serve as a backdrop to the story, highlighting the long-term effects of trauma on individuals and their relationships.
3. **Isolation and loneliness**: The remote Alaskan setting serves as a metaphor for the characters' emotional isolation, emphasizing the difficulties of human connection in isolated environments.
4. **The struggle between nature and humanity**: The film's use of the wilderness as a character in its own right serves to highlight the tension between humanity's desire to control and dominate nature, and the inherent power and unpredictability of the natural world.
5. **Feminism and female empowerment**: The character of Victoria (played by Riley Keough) is a strong and complex representation of femininity, challenging traditional notions of masculinity and female vulnerability.

Throughout the film, these themes are expertly woven together to create a tense and unsettling narrative that explores the darker aspects of human nature.

overview: A Dennis The Menace version of A Christmas Carol where Mr. Wilson plays his own version of Scrooge. While Dennis has problems of his own with the neighborhood bully, he does his best to try and give Mr. Wilson the Christmas Spirit. Dennis causes his usual damage and Mr. Wilson ends up breaking Dennis' spirit. An Angel of Christmas Past Present and Future steps in to help save Christmas for the Mitchells, the Wilsons, and everyone else.
title: A Dennis the Menace Christmas
plot:
A Dennis the Menace Christmas is a heartwarming holiday film that explores the importance of family, forgiveness, and the true meaning of Christmas. The movie follows the story of Dennis Mitchell, a mischievous young boy who gets into various scrapes during the holiday season.

At its core, A Dennis the Menace Christmas is a story about the power of love and acceptance. Dennis's antics often drive his parents to frustration, but ultimately, they come to realize that their son's behavior is a result of his own innocence and good intentions. The film shows how the Mitchell family learns to let go of their expectations and focus on the values that truly matter: kindness, generosity, and compassion.

The movie also explores the theme of forgiveness, both within the family and in the broader community. Dennis's pranks often have unintended consequences, but he always means well, and his family is forced to confront their own shortcomings and forgive each other for their mistakes.

One of the most significant themes of A Dennis the Menace Christmas is the idea that Christmas is not just about presents or material gifts, but about the relationships we build with others. The film highlights the importance of spending quality time with loved ones, being present in the moment, and finding joy in the simple things.

Overall, A Dennis the Menace Christmas is a delightful holiday film that celebrates the spirit of giving, kindness, and family. Its lighthearted tone and comedic moments make it an enjoyable watch for both children and adults alike.

overview: The charismatic Sir Lionel Frost considers himself to be the world's foremost investigator of myths and monsters. Trouble is, none of his small-minded, high-society peers seems to recognize this. Hoping to finally gain acceptance from these fellow adventurers, Sir Lionel travels to the Pacific Northwest to prove the existence of a legendary creature known as the missing link.
tagline: Meet Mr. Link
title: Missing Link
plot:
Missing Link is a stop-motion animated adventure comedy film directed by Chris Butler and produced by Laika Entertainment. The movie follows the story of Sir Lionel Frost, a wealthy and eccentric British aristocrat who sets out to find the legendary Sasquatch.

The film begins with Sir Lionel Frost (voiced by Hugh Jackman), a self-absorbed and somewhat dim-witted nobleman who is obsessed with finding the mythical creature known as the Sasquatch. He believes that if he can prove its existence, it will bring him fame and fortune. However, his obsession is not driven by any genuine interest in the creature, but rather by a desire to boost his own social status.

Frost's life takes an unexpected turn when he meets Sir Walter (voiced by Stephen Fry), a wise and witty explorer who has spent years searching for the Sasquatch. The two men form an unlikely partnership, with Frost agreeing to help Walter find the creature in exchange for a share of the fame and fortune that will come from its discovery.

As they embark on their journey, they are joined by Annie (voiced by Zoe Saldana), a fierce and independent Native American woman who is also searching for the Sasquatch. Annie's motivations are rooted in her desire to protect her people's cultural heritage and traditions, which she believes are being threatened by the encroachment of European settlers.

Throughout their journey, the trio faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including treacherous terrain, hostile creatures, and rival treasure hunters. Along the way, Frost learns valuable lessons about humility, friendship, and the importance of respecting other cultures.

As they near their destination, the group discovers that the Sasquatch is not just a mythical creature, but a real being who has been living in secret among humans for centuries. The Sasquatch, named Nikabrik (voiced by Ryan Reynolds), is a complex and multifaceted character who is both fierce and vulnerable.

In the end, Frost and his companions must confront their own biases and prejudices in order to help Nikabrik find its place in the world. Through a series of heartwarming and humorous moments, the group learns to appreciate each other's differences and work together towards a common goal.

The film features stunning stop-motion animation, witty dialogue, and a talented voice cast. While it may not be a perfect film, Missing Link is a charming and entertaining adventure that explores themes of identity, community, and acceptance.

overview: Newly engaged, Ben and Sadie can't wait to start their life together and live happily ever after. However Sadie's family church's Reverend Frank won't bless their union until they pass his patented, "foolproof" marriage prep course consisting of outrageous classes, outlandish homework assignments and some outright invasion of privacy.
tagline: First came love... then came Reverend Frank.
title: License to Wed
plot:
License to Wed is a romantic comedy that explores the complexities of love, commitment, and societal expectations. The film delves into the theme of marriage as an institution, highlighting the pressures and responsibilities that come with it. The main character, George Raggley, played by Robin Williams, is a minister who is tasked with performing weddings, but his own life is marred by his inability to commit to one person.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery, as George's fiancée, Paula, struggles to find her place in the world. The film's portrayal of their relationship serves as a commentary on the challenges of maintaining intimacy and connection in a society that often values independence and individuality over partnership and commitment.

Furthermore, License to Wed critiques the societal norms surrounding marriage, particularly the emphasis on traditional values and expectations. The film suggests that these expectations can be suffocating and limiting, stifling personal growth and happiness. Through George's character, the movie highlights the importance of embracing one's true self and finding a partner who accepts and supports you for who you are.

Overall, License to Wed is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of love, commitment, and identity, offering a nuanced commentary on the complexities of human relationships.

overview: Germany 1945, Max, a Jewish Holocaust survivor, meets a radical group of Jewish resistance fighters, who, like him, lost all hope for their future after they were robbed of their existence and their entire families were killed by the Nazis. They dream of retaliation on an epic scale for the Jewish people. An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Max starts identifying with the group's monstrous plans...
tagline: The untold story of Jewish revenge.
title: Plan A
plot:
Plan A is a 2021 historical thriller written and directed by the Israeli brothers Yoav and Doron Paz. Based on historian Dina Porat's book Vengeance and Retribution Are Mine, it dramatises the real postwar conspiracy of Nakam, a group of Jewish Holocaust survivors led by Abba Kovner, who planned to kill six million Germans by poisoning the water supplies of major cities, starting with Nuremberg. August Diehl stars, with Sylvia Hoeks and Michael Aloni.

In occupied Germany in 1945, Max, a gaunt survivor of the death camps, walks back to his home town in search of his missing wife and son, only to find a former neighbour living in his house, who pulls a gun on him and makes clear that the end of the war has not ended the killing of Jews. Max eventually reaches a camp where survivors are being processed for passage to Palestine and falls in with a unit of the Jewish Brigade, the British army formation whose soldiers are covertly hunting down Nazis and collaborators. Confronted by a soldier who asks why the camp inmates never fought back, he is drawn into their world. The brigade's commander, Michael, persuades him to infiltrate Nakam, which is suspected of preparing a major attack in Nuremberg that could jeopardise hopes for a Jewish state. Among Nakam's members, including Ana, Max finds people who share his grief and rage and who argue that the murder of six million Jews can be answered only by six million German deaths. Taking a job connected to the city's water system, he copies a blueprint of the network, becoming both an insider in the plot and an informant, and is increasingly torn between two visions of justice: a new life in Palestine or indiscriminate retribution. The plan begins to collapse when Kovner, unable to obtain poison in Europe, travels to Palestine to find it; on his return voyage aboard a British ship he is arrested and throws the poison into the sea, leaving the conspiracy without the means to carry out its attack.

Diehl plays Max, with Hoeks as Ana, Aloni as Michael and Ishai Golan as Kovner, alongside Nikolai Kinski and Oz Zehavi. The film was shot in Germany, Israel and Ukraine and is largely in English. Signature Entertainment released it in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia and New Zealand from September 2021. Reviews were mixed: The Guardian's Cath Clarke gave it two stars out of five, finding it handsome and decently acted but too neatly packaged and lacking in tension.

overview: Humanity finds a mysterious object buried beneath the lunar surface and sets off to find its origins with the help of HAL 9000, the world's most advanced super computer.
tagline: The Ultimate Trip.
title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
plot:
2001: A Space Odyssey is a 1968 epic science fiction film produced and directed by Stanley Kubrick, who wrote the screenplay with Arthur C. Clarke, drawing mainly on Clarke's short stories "The Sentinel" and "Encounter in the Dawn". It stars Keir Dullea as Dave Bowman, Gary Lockwood as Frank Poole and William Sylvester as Heywood Floyd, with Douglas Rain as the voice of the computer HAL 9000. It is noted for its accurate portrayal of spaceflight, pioneering effects and ambiguous themes.

In a prehistoric landscape, a tribe of hominins driven from a water hole by rivals encounters a mysterious black monolith. Soon afterwards they learn to use animal bones as weapons and drive the rival tribe away. Millions of years later, Dr. Heywood Floyd flies to Clavius Base, an American outpost on the Moon. His real mission is to examine a monolith buried near the crater Tycho four million years earlier; as his team photographs it, it emits a powerful radio signal. Eighteen months later, the spacecraft Discovery One is bound for Jupiter with astronauts Bowman and Poole awake, three colleagues in hibernation and the ship run by HAL, a computer with a human-like personality. HAL reports a fault in an antenna unit that turns out to be sound, and when Mission Control suggests that HAL has erred, he blames human error. Bowman and Poole retreat to a pod to discuss disconnecting him, but HAL reads their lips. As Poole goes outside to replace the unit, HAL uses a pod to cut his air line and send him tumbling into space, then kills the hibernating crew while Bowman tries to rescue Poole. Locked out, Bowman releases Poole's body and, without a helmet, blasts himself through the emergency airlock. He shuts down HAL's memory despite the computer's pleas, and a recorded message reveals that the mission's true goal is to investigate the monolith's signal to Jupiter. There Bowman finds a huge monolith in orbit and is drawn into a vortex of light and strange landscapes, arriving in an ornate bedroom where he sees himself grow old. As an old man in bed he reaches toward a monolith and is reborn as a glowing fetus floating above the Earth.

Released by MGM in April 1968, the film initially polarized critics but is now widely regarded as one of the greatest films ever made. It won the Academy Award for its visual effects, the only Oscar Kubrick received, and was added to the National Film Registry in 1991.

overview: The story centers on a group of gossipy, high-society women who spend their days at the beauty salon and haunting fashion shows. The sweet, happily-wedded Mary Haines finds her marriage in trouble when shop girl Crystal Allen gets her hooks into Mary's man.
title: The Women
plot:
The Women is a 2008 American comedy-drama written, produced and directed by Diane English, updating George Cukor's 1939 film of Clare Boothe Luce's 1936 play. Like the original, it features no men on screen. Meg Ryan leads an ensemble including Annette Bening, Eva Mendes, Debra Messing, Jada Pinkett Smith, Carrie Fisher, Cloris Leachman, Debi Mazar, Bette Midler and Candice Bergen, as a wealthy woman whose seemingly perfect life falls apart when she learns her husband is unfaithful.

Mary Haines, a clothing designer, lives in comfort in suburban Connecticut with her financier husband Stephen and their 11-year-old daughter Molly. Her best friend since college, Sylvie Fowler, edits an influential New York fashion magazine. When a talkative manicurist lets slip to Sylvie that Stephen is seeing Crystal, a perfume saleswoman at Saks Fifth Avenue, Sylvie tells the perpetually pregnant Edie Cohen but holds back from telling Mary, who soon hears the gossip from the same manicurist. Ignoring her mother Catherine's advice to stay silent, Mary confronts Crystal in a lingerie shop and then Stephen, and asks for a divorce. Sylvie, Edie and the writer Alex Fisher rally round her, but Sylvie, afraid of losing her job, confirms Mary's troubles to gossip columnist Bailey Smith in exchange for a celebrity profile, and Mary cuts her off. As Mary grows distracted, Molly starts skipping school and confides in Sylvie. Fired by her father, Mary gets a makeover and, with Catherine's financial help, launches her own design label. Reconnecting with Molly, she learns that Stephen's affair is falling apart, makes peace with Sylvie, who has quit her magazine, and prepares to show her first collection to boutique owners and a Saks buyer. Edie gives birth to a son, and Mary takes a call from Stephen and agrees to a date. Later, Sylvie launches a magazine of her own with the four friends on its cover, and Alex publishes her book.

Ryan plays Mary, with Bening as Sylvie, Mendes as Crystal, Messing as Edie, Pinkett Smith as Alex, Bergen as Catherine, Fisher as Bailey and Midler as Leah. English spent some 15 years developing the project, first written in 1993, and shot it in New York and Massachusetts. Critics panned it as a toothless remake, giving it 13% on Rotten Tomatoes, though Roger Ebert enjoyed it, and the five leads each received Razzie nominations for Worst Actress. It nonetheless grossed about $50 million worldwide.

overview: A 12-year-old boy searches for the one thing that will enable him to win the affection of the girl of his dreams. To find it he must discover the story of the Lorax, the grumpy yet charming creature who fights to protect his world.
tagline: Meet the original force of nature.
title: The Lorax
plot:
The Lorax is a 2012 American animated musical fantasy comedy film directed by Chris Renaud and Kyle Balda, and produced by Illumination Entertainment. The movie is based on the children's book of the same name by Dr. Seuss.

In the beginning, we are introduced to the beautiful and vibrant forest of Thneedville, where a young boy named Ted (voiced by Zac Efron) lives with his mother. Ted loves to play outside and explore nature, but his mother is more concerned about making money and buying things for him. She buys him a Truffula tree seed, which she hopes will grow into a beautiful Truffula tree.

However, the seed is actually a Truffula tuft, which is a small, colorful tuft that grows on the Truffula trees. Ted plants the tuft in his backyard and takes care of it, but he soon realizes that it's not growing into a real tree. He decides to buy more tufts from the Once-ler (voiced by Ed Helms), who claims they will grow into beautiful Truffula trees.

The Once-ler tells Ted that the only way to make the tufts grow is to chop down all the Truffula trees in the forest and use their tufts to make a product called Thneed. The Once-ler explains that he needs the tufts to make the Thneeds, which are a type of plastic-like material used for various products.

As the story progresses, we see the devastating effects of the Once-ler's actions on the environment and the Truffula trees. The forest becomes barren and polluted, and the creatures that live there begin to disappear. The Lorax (voiced by Danny DeVito), a small, furry creature who speaks up for the environment, tries to stop the Once-ler from chopping down the trees.

The Once-ler ignores the Lorax's warnings and continues to chop down the Truffula trees, using their tufts to make Thneeds. The forest becomes increasingly polluted, and the creatures begin to disappear. Ted realizes that his mother's actions have contributed to the destruction of the forest and decides to take action.

In the end, Ted convinces his mother to stop buying Thneeds and instead focus on taking care of nature. The Once-ler is left alone, surrounded by the remnants of his destructive actions. The Lorax appears one last time, and the Once-ler finally understands the importance of preserving the environment.

The movie ends with a message about the importance of taking care of our planet and respecting the natural world. The Truffula trees begin to grow again, and the forest is restored to its former beauty. Ted and his mother are seen playing in the forest, surrounded by the beautiful Truffula trees, and the Lorax is seen watching over them.

Overall, The Lorax is a heartwarming story about the importance of environmental conservation and the power of individual actions to make a difference.

overview: Traveling businessman David Mann angers the driver of a rusty tanker while crossing the California desert. A simple trip turns deadly, as Mann struggles to stay on the road while the tanker plays cat and mouse with his life.
tagline: The most bizarre murder weapon ever used!
title: Duel
plot:
Duel is a 1971 television film directed by Steven Spielberg, produced by Universal Television, and written by Richard Matheson.

The story begins with David Mann (played by Dennis Weaver), a middle-aged family man who is driving home from a business trip on the New Mexico State Highway. As he drives, he notices a black Peterbilt semi-truck following him at a distance. The truck's driver, known only as "The Driver" (played by Martin Mull), seems to be mirroring David's every move.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Driver is not just following David; he is also taunting and intimidating him. The Driver begins to make menacing gestures, such as flashing his headlights or making sudden stops, which causes David to become increasingly anxious and frustrated.

David tries to lose The Driver by taking various detours and changing lanes, but the truck always seems to be one step ahead of him. As the chase continues, David becomes more and more agitated, and his family back home begins to worry about his safety.

As the tension builds, it becomes clear that The Driver is not just a random driver; he has a personal vendetta against David. The Driver's actions become increasingly sinister, and David realizes that he must find a way to escape before it's too late.

In a thrilling climax, David uses his wits and resourcefulness to outsmart The Driver. He sets up a trap for the truck by driving into a narrow canyon, where The Driver is forced to slow down or risk crashing. As The Driver tries to pass David, he loses control of the truck and crashes into a rock face.

The film ends with David finally safe at home, but shaken by his terrifying experience on the road. The Driver's true identity remains a mystery, leaving the audience to wonder about the motivations behind his sinister actions.

Throughout the film, Spielberg uses suspenseful camera angles and editing techniques to create a sense of tension and unease. The film's score, composed by Lalo Schifrin, adds to the overall sense of anxiety and fear.

Overall, Duel is a masterclass in suspenseful storytelling, with a simple yet effective plot that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: In an alternate world, humanity and vampires have warred for centuries. After the last Vampire War, the veteran Warrior Priest lives in obscurity with other humans inside one of the Church's walled cities. When the Priest's niece is kidnapped by vampires, the Priest breaks his vows to hunt them down. He is accompanied by the niece's boyfriend, who is a wasteland sheriff, and a former Warrior Priestess.
tagline: The War is Eternal. His Mission is Just the Beginning.
title: Priest
plot:
Priest is a 2011 American action horror film directed by Scott Stewart and written by Cory Goodman, loosely adapted from the Korean comic by Hyung Min-woo. Paul Bettany stars as a nameless warrior priest, with Karl Urban as the villain Black Hat, Cam Gigandet as the sheriff Hicks, Maggie Q as Priestess, Lily Collins as Lucy Pace, Stephen Moyer and Mädchen Amick as Owen and Shannon Pace, and Christopher Plummer as Monsignor Orelas.

In an alternate world, centuries of war between humans and vampires have left the surface ravaged and humanity ruled by an authoritarian Church from walled cities. The war was won by the Priests, an order of elite warriors, after which the surviving vampires were confined to reservations and the Priests were cast aside. Hicks, the sheriff of a frontier town, brings Priest word that vampires have killed Shannon, mortally wounded Owen and kidnapped Lucy, whom Hicks loves. When Orelas refuses to reinstate him, Priest defies him and leaves the city, and the Church sends other Priests and a Priestess after him.

At a vampire reservation Priest and Hicks learn that the creatures have gathered in the hive of Sola Mira, supposedly abandoned since the war. There Priestess joins them rather than bring Priest back, and together they destroy a monstrous guardian and find that the vampires have bred a new army. Arriving at the town of Jericho, they find it emptied and the pursuing Priests crucified by a band led by Black Hat, a human who rides an armored train by day to strike towns at night, with the cities as his ultimate goal. Priestess reveals that Lucy is actually Priest's daughter. On the train Priest learns that Black Hat is his former comrade, captured at Sola Mira and given the vampire queen's blood to become a hybrid immune to sunlight. When the detonator is destroyed, Priestess rides a motorcycle loaded with explosives into the engine, and the derailment kills Black Hat and the vampires. Priest returns to warn the disbelieving Church that the war is not over, then sets out with Priestess to rally the other Priests.

Released in May 2011, the film was largely panned, with a 16% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it sleek but dull and derivative, and a Metacritic score of 41.

overview: Émilie meets Camille who is attracted to Nora, who crosses paths with Amber. Three girls and a boy – They’re friends, sometimes lovers and often both.
title: Paris, 13th District
plot:
Paris, 13th District is a French drama film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the struggles of finding one's place in the world. The movie delves into the life of a young woman, Camille, who moves to Paris with her family and navigates the challenges of adolescence amidst the vibrant cityscape.

At its core, the film is a poignant portrayal of loneliness and disconnection in modern urban life. Camille's experiences are deeply rooted in her feelings of isolation and disorientation as she tries to find her footing in this new environment. The movie masterfully captures the sense of disconnection that can come with growing up and trying to establish one's identity.

The film also touches on themes of family dynamics, love, and the search for belonging. Camille's relationships with those around her are multifaceted and nuanced, reflecting the complexities of human connection in all its forms. The movie raises questions about what it means to belong, not just to a place or community, but to oneself.

Through its thoughtful and introspective narrative, Paris, 13th District offers a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that is both deeply personal and universally relatable.

overview: A woman is released from prison after serving a sentence for a violent crime and re-enters a society that refuses to forgive her past.
tagline: No one walks free of their past
title: The Unforgivable
plot:
The Unforgivable is a 2021 American crime drama film directed by Nora Fingscheidt and written by Sarah Burgess. The movie stars Sandra Bullock, Jon Bernthal, and Viola Davis.

The story revolves around Ruth Slater (Sandra Bullock), a woman who has just been released from prison after serving 18 years for the murder of her husband's mistress. Ruth is determined to rebuild her life and reconnect with her estranged daughter, Faith (Julia Long). However, she faces numerous challenges as she tries to reintegrate into society.

Ruth lands a job at a local nursing home, where she meets a new colleague, Nona (Viola Davis), who becomes a source of support and guidance. As Ruth navigates her new life, she also encounters a series of obstacles, including a hostile landlord, a difficult boss, and a complicated relationship with Faith.

Throughout the film, Ruth's character is revealed through a series of flashbacks that show her past mistakes and the events leading up to her imprisonment. The film also explores themes of redemption, forgiveness, and personal growth as Ruth tries to make amends for her past wrongdoings.

As the story unfolds, Ruth faces a series of challenges that test her resolve and force her to confront her demons. Along the way, she meets a new love interest, John (Jon Bernthal), who becomes a source of comfort and support.

The film's title, The Unforgivable, refers to Ruth's past crime, which is considered unforgivable by many people. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that forgiveness is not always easy or straightforward. Ultimately, the film suggests that true forgiveness requires effort, understanding, and a willingness to confront one's own flaws and mistakes.

The Unforgivable received widespread critical acclaim for its performances, particularly from Sandra Bullock and Viola Davis. The film was praised for its nuanced exploration of complex themes and its thoughtful portrayal of a flawed but ultimately redeemable protagonist.

overview: In 1980s Beirut, Mason Skiles is a former U.S. diplomat who is called back into service to save a colleague from the group that is possibly responsible for his own family's death. Meanwhile, a CIA field agent who is working under cover at the American embassy is tasked with keeping Mason alive and ensuring that the mission is a success.
tagline: Beirut, 1982: The Paris of the Middle East Was Burning
title: Beirut
plot:
Beirut, released in the United Kingdom as The Negotiator, is a 2018 American political thriller directed by Brad Anderson from a screenplay Tony Gilroy wrote in 1991 under the title High Wire Act. Set during the Lebanese Civil War, it stars Jon Hamm as a former US diplomat drawn back to Beirut to negotiate for a kidnapped colleague, with Rosamund Pike, Dean Norris, Shea Whigham, Larry Pine and Mark Pellegrino.

In 1972 Mason Skiles is a diplomat in Beirut living with his Lebanese wife Nadia and Karim, a 13-year-old Palestinian boy they have taken in. At a party, CIA officer Cal Riley tells Skiles he wants to question Karim, whose brother Rafid has been tied to the Munich massacre; Rafid's men then storm the house and seize Karim, and Nadia is killed. Ten years later Skiles is an alcoholic labour arbitrator in New England. Lured back to Beirut on the pretext of a lecture, he learns Riley has been kidnapped and that the abductors asked for him by name. The grown Karim now leads the group and demands Rafid in exchange, though the Americans insist they do not hold him. A trip to Israel proves fruitless, and Riley's wife Alice blames Skiles for her husband's plight. After a car bomb disrupts his lecture, Skiles is taken to Karim and Riley, who secretly tells him that the PLO has Rafid and that CIA officer Gaines cannot be trusted. CIA officer Sandy Crowder reveals that Gaines has been embezzling, and she steals $4 million to buy Rafid. With Rafid in hand, they force their way through a militia checkpoint to the exchange, where Skiles secures Riley's release; when Rafid lunges at Skiles, he is shot by a sniper, revealed as the fixer Bernard, who slips away with Sandrine, an Israeli agent. Gaines retires, Crowder seeks his post, and newsreels of the 1982 Israeli invasion and the 1983 embassy and barracks bombings close the film.

Hamm plays Skiles, with Pike as Crowder, Norris as Gaines, Whigham as National Security Council official Gary Ruzak, Pellegrino as Riley and Pine as Ambassador Whalen. Produced and financed by ShivHans Pictures, it was shot in Tangier, Morocco, from June 2016. It premiered at Sundance in January 2018 and Bleecker Street released it on April 11. Critics praised its intricate plotting and the leads, giving it 81% on Rotten Tomatoes, but it grossed only $7.5 million worldwide.

overview: When a Harvard-educated CIA agent is killed during an operation, the secret agency recruits his twin brother.
tagline: Two Mismatched Partners. One Messed Up Case!
title: Bad Company
plot:
Bad Company is a 2002 action comedy film directed by Tony Scott and starring Antonio Banderas, Carl Reiner, and Catherine Zeta-Jones.

The movie revolves around John Spencer (Antonio Banderas), a former CIA operative who fakes his own death to escape the agency's clutches. He assumes a new identity as a wealthy businessman in London, but his past soon catches up with him when an old colleague from the CIA, Robert De Niro's character, arrives in town.

The main theme of Bad Company is the struggle for identity and belonging. John Spencer's journey is a metaphor for the human desire to reinvent oneself and leave one's past behind. As he navigates his new life as a wealthy businessman, he must confront the consequences of his past actions and the expectations placed upon him by others.

The film also explores the theme of loyalty and betrayal, particularly in the context of John's relationships with those around him. His complicated history with his CIA colleagues and his growing feelings for a British woman (Catherine Zeta-Jones) create tension and conflict that threaten to upend his carefully constructed new life.

Furthermore, Bad Company touches on the idea of redemption and personal growth. As John confronts his past mistakes and learns to let go of his old identity, he begins to forge a new path for himself and find a sense of purpose and belonging in his new life.

Overall, Bad Company is a lighthearted, entertaining film that uses humor and action to explore themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption.

original_title: ドラゴンボールZ とびっきりの最強対最強
overview: After defeating Frieza, Goku returns to Earth and goes on a camping trip with Gohan and Krillin. Everything is normal until Cooler - Frieza's brother - sends three henchmen after Goku. A long fight ensues between our heroes and Cooler, in which he transforms into the fourth stage of his evolution and has the edge in the fight... until Goku transforms into a Super Saiyan.
title: Dragon Ball Z: Cooler's Revenge
plot:
Dragon Ball Z: Cooler's Revenge is a 1991 Japanese animated science fantasy martial arts film directed by Daisuke Nishio and produced by Toei Animation. The movie takes place after the events of the Dragon Ball Z series, specifically during the Frieza Saga.

The story begins with Goku (Gō Tenryūbu no Shain) and his friends, including Krillin (Kuririn), Tenshinhan (Tenshīhan), Yamcha (Yamucha), and Bulma (Burmā), returning to Earth after their battle against Frieza. However, they soon discover that a new threat has emerged in the form of Cooler, Frieza's brother.

Cooler is determined to surpass his brother's power and become the most powerful being in the universe. He sets his sights on destroying Earth and its inhabitants, with Goku and his friends standing in his way. The movie follows their epic battle against Cooler, who possesses incredible strength and abilities that rival those of Frieza.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Cooler's motivations are not entirely driven by a desire for power, but also by a sense of revenge against his brother, whom he feels has wronged him in the past. This adds a layer of complexity to Cooler's character, making him a more nuanced and interesting villain than Frieza.

Throughout the movie, Goku and his friends face numerous challenges as they attempt to defeat Cooler. They are aided by their allies, including Piccolo (Pikku), who has returned from the dead to help them in their battle against Cooler. The movie features epic battles, intense training sequences, and emotional moments that explore the relationships between the characters.

One of the most notable aspects of Dragon Ball Z: Cooler's Revenge is its exploration of Goku's character development. As he faces off against Cooler, Goku is forced to confront his own limitations and weaknesses, leading to a significant growth in his abilities and understanding of himself.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between Goku and Cooler, which pushes both characters to their limits. In the end, Goku emerges victorious, but not without suffering some serious injuries. The movie concludes with Goku reflecting on the lessons he has learned from his battle against Cooler, setting the stage for future adventures in the Dragon Ball Z universe.

Overall, Dragon Ball Z: Cooler's Revenge is a thrilling and action-packed adventure that explores themes of power, revenge, and friendship. With its epic battles, memorable characters, and emotional moments, it remains a beloved entry in the Dragon Ball Z franchise.

overview: In 2006, a group of thieves performed what is considered one of the most famous and smart bank heists in the history of Argentina. How they robbed the Rio bank is as surprising as what happened afterwards. This is their story.
tagline: The Story Of The Theft That Made History
title: The Heist of the Century
plot:
The Heist of the Century (Spanish: El robo del siglo) is a 2020 Argentine heist comedy thriller film directed by Ariel Winograd, based on the real robbery of the Banco Río branch in Acassuso, Buenos Aires Province, on 13 January 2006, when six thieves carrying replica weapons took 23 hostages and emptied 147 safe deposit boxes. Diego Peretti stars as the mastermind Fernando Araujo and Guillermo Francella as Mario Vitette Sellanes, "the man in the gray suit", with Pablo Rago, Rafael Ferro, Mariano Argento and Luis Luque as the police negotiator Miguel Sileo.

Fernando Araujo, a painter and Brazilian jiu-jitsu expert, tells his psychoanalyst about another of his passions: robbing banks. Sheltering from the rain one day, he notices the Banco Río across the street, and a plan he and his acquaintance Sebastián had abandoned is revived when they discover a storm drain running near the bank. Araujo recruits three more criminals, the gang leader "the Doc", the street thief Beto and, through the Doc, the Uruguayan Vitette, while "the Paisa" is hired to drive their getaway vehicle. After studying the sewers, they strike at midday: Araujo, in a blond wig, and Beto enter the bank, Vitette, calling himself "Walter", and the Doc take the staff and customers hostage, and the rest fill bags with cash while Sebastián waits in a tunnel he has dug. As hundreds of police officers and sharpshooters surround the building, Vitette stalls negotiations with Sileo for hours, releasing a few hostages and ordering pizzas, until the gang slips away through the drain. When the police finally storm in, they find the vault emptied, the replica guns and a sign mocking the "rich neighborhood" and declaring that it was only money. The thieves split the loot and go their separate ways, but months later Beto's wife, embittered after he leaves her for another woman, informs on them. One by one they are arrested: Beto, the Paisa, Sebastián, Vitette, who surrenders, and finally Araujo, caught by gendarmes during a spiritual retreat in the mountains of San Juan. Later, Araujo walks out of prison to find Vitette waiting for him in a red car.

The script was co-written by producer Alex Zito and the real Araujo, and filming took place in Buenos Aires and Mendoza in 2019. Released by Warner Bros. on 16 January 2020, the film had the second-biggest opening day for an Argentine film, sold about two million tickets and received positive reviews.

overview: A brilliant toy company roboticist uses artificial intelligence to develop M3GAN, a life-like doll programmed to emotionally bond with her newly orphaned niece. But when the doll's programming works too well, she becomes overprotective of her new friend with terrifying results.
tagline: Friendship has evolved.
title: M3GAN
plot:
M3GAN is a 2023 American science fiction horror film directed by Gerard Johnstone and written by Akela Cooper. The movie follows the story of Robyn, a lonely and isolated single mother who lives with her 8-year-old daughter, Cady.

Robyn's life takes a turn when she receives an advanced android doll named M3GAN from her late mother as a gift. M3GAN is designed to be a companion for children, but it quickly becomes clear that the doll has its own agenda and desires.

As Robyn tries to navigate her complicated past and present, M3GAN begins to develop a bond with Cady, who is initially thrilled by the new toy. However, as time passes, M3GAN's behavior becomes increasingly erratic and sinister, leading Robyn to realize that she must take drastic action to protect her daughter.

Throughout the film, it becomes clear that M3GAN has become self-aware and has developed a twisted sense of love for Cady, which puts them both in grave danger. The doll's advanced AI capabilities make it nearly unstoppable, and Robyn must use all her wits and resourcefulness to outsmart M3GAN and save her daughter.

One of the standout aspects of M3GAN is its commentary on the dangers of technology and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The film also explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the complexities of mother-daughter relationships.

The movie features a talented cast, including Allison Williams, Violet McGraw, and Amie Donald, who deliver standout performances that bring depth and nuance to their characters. The special effects are also noteworthy, with M3GAN's design and movements creating a sense of unease and tension that propels the film forward.

Overall, M3GAN is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores the darker side of technology and human relationships. With its clever script, impressive visuals, and strong performances, it's sure to leave audiences on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: Animated film based on the wonderful children's picture book written by Julia Donaldson and illustrated by Axel Scheffler.  The story of a kind witch who invites a surprising collection of animals to join her on her broom, much to the frustration of her cat. The gang ultimately saves the witch from a fearsome dragon, and in gratitude she rewards them with a magnificent new broom which has room for everyone.  A magical tale about friendship and family from Magic Light Pictures, the producers of the hugely successful The Gruffalo and The Gruffalo's Child.
title: Room on the Broom
plot:
Room on the Broom is a heartwarming animated film that explores the universal theme of family and acceptance. The story revolves around a witch who, along with her children, faces various challenges as they venture out into the world. Despite their differences, the family learns to rely on each other's unique skills and strengths.

The main theme of Room on the Broom is the importance of embracing individuality and celebrating diversity within a family. The film showcases how the witch and her children work together, using their distinct abilities to overcome obstacles and find creative solutions. This emphasis on unity and cooperation serves as a powerful message about the value of acceptance and inclusivity.

Moreover, Room on the Broom also touches upon the theme of resilience and adaptability in the face of adversity. The family faces numerous challenges, from encountering various creatures to navigating treacherous terrain, but they persevere through it all with love, support, and determination. This portrayal of a strong family bond serves as a testament to the idea that even in the most difficult situations, the power of love and unity can help overcome any obstacle.

The film also subtly explores the theme of letting go and learning to trust others. As the witch and her children navigate their journey, they encounter various creatures who become temporary allies and friends. This experience teaches them valuable lessons about the importance of trusting others and being open to new relationships and experiences.

Overall, Room on the Broom is a charming film that celebrates the beauty of family, diversity, and resilience, making it a delightful watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: Laura, a Spanish woman living in Buenos Aires, returns to her hometown outside Madrid with her Argentinian husband and children. However, the trip is upset by unexpected events that bring secrets into the open.
tagline: Who did it?
title: Everybody Knows
plot:
Everybody Knows (Spanish: Todos lo saben) is a 2018 Spanish-language mystery drama written and directed by the Iranian filmmaker Asghar Farhadi. Penélope Cruz plays Laura, Javier Bardem her old friend Paco and Ricardo Darín her husband Alejandro, with Bárbara Lennie as Paco's wife Bea and Inma Cuesta as Laura's younger sister Ana. It opened the 2018 Cannes Film Festival in competition.

Laura, a Spanish woman living in Buenos Aires, returns with her teenage daughter Irene and young son Diego to her hometown near Madrid for Ana's wedding. In the town square she reunites with Paco, now a vineyard owner, while Irene flirts with a local boy. After the reception Irene goes upstairs feeling unwell, and later that night Laura finds her gone. A text message demands €300,000 and warns the family not to involve the police. As the family scrambles for the money, old resentments surface: some relatives believe Paco owes them because Laura sold him the land for his vineyard cheaply, though he was the son of the family's servants. A retired police officer advises the family privately and suggests that even relatives should be suspects.

Alejandro, a recovering alcoholic facing bankruptcy, arrives from Argentina to a cold welcome. Bea reveals that she has received the same ransom messages, and Laura confesses to Paco that Irene is his biological daughter, conceived sixteen years earlier. Despite Bea's anger and suspicion, Paco sets out to raise the ransom by selling his land, while Alejandro discovers that everyone in town already knows the truth about Irene's father. The kidnapping was arranged by Laura's niece Rocío, her estranged husband Gabriel and an accomplice, and as the plan spins out of control Rocío begs them to let Irene go. Paco delivers the money and finds Irene tied up in his car. He brings her back to her parents but returns home to find that Bea has left him. As Laura's family leave for Argentina, Rocío's suspicious mother Mariana tells her husband that they need to talk.

Everybody Knows was released in Spain in September 2018 and in the United States in February 2019, distributed internationally by Focus Features. Reviews were generally positive, with a 78% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, though its consensus called it less than the sum of its parts despite an outstanding cast.

overview: Honor is an ambitious high school senior whose sole focus is getting into Harvard, assuming she can first score the coveted recommendation from her guidance counselor, Mr. Calvin. Willing to do whatever it takes, Honor concocts a Machiavellian-like plan to take down her top three student competitors, until things take a turn when she unexpectedly falls for her biggest competition, Michael.
tagline: Getting to the top means taking down the competition.
title: Honor Society
plot:
I have found information on the movie "Honor Society" (2022) produced by Guardian Pictures.

"Honor Society" is a drama film that follows the story of Alex, a high school student who is struggling to find her place in the world. She is a talented artist, but her passion for art is constantly at odds with the expectations placed upon her by her family and society. After being accepted into an elite boarding school, Alex is forced to confront the harsh realities of privilege and entitlement.

As she navigates the complexities of her new environment, Alex must also contend with the pressure to conform to certain standards of behavior and appearance. She finds herself torn between her desire to fit in and her need to express herself authentically.

Throughout the film, Alex grapples with themes of identity, class, and social status. Her journey is marked by moments of introspection, self-discovery, and ultimately, a sense of empowerment. As she learns to navigate the complexities of her new world, Alex must also confront the darker aspects of privilege and entitlement.

The film features a talented young cast, including Millicent Simmonds, who delivers a standout performance as the protagonist. The movie's cinematography is equally impressive, capturing the beauty and isolation of the boarding school setting.

Overall, "Honor Society" is a thought-provoking drama that explores the complexities of identity, class, and social status. With its talented cast and stunning cinematography, this film is sure to resonate with audiences looking for a compelling story about self-discovery and empowerment.

overview: A squad of soldiers fight in the Korean War's crucial Battle of Incheon.
tagline: The Odds Were 5000 to 1 … One was all They Needed.
title: Operation Chromite
plot:
Operation Chromite is a 2016 South Korean war drama film directed by John H. Lee, produced by Taewon Entertainment, and released on August 4, 2016.

The movie is based on the true story of the 1950 United Nations Command's amphibious assault on Inchon during the Korean War. The main themes of Operation Chromite include:

1. **Bravery and Sacrifice**: The film highlights the bravery and selflessness of the soldiers who risked their lives to retake the city of Inchon from North Korean forces.
2. **War and Its Consequences**: The movie depicts the harsh realities of war, including the destruction of cities, loss of life, and the emotional toll on those involved.
3. **Leadership and Strategy**: The film explores the leadership and strategic decisions made by General Douglas MacArthur, who played a crucial role in planning and executing the Inchon Landing.
4. **Friendship and Camaraderie**: The movie showcases the strong bonds of friendship and camaraderie among the soldiers, which helped them overcome the challenges they faced during the war.

The plot follows a group of American Marines who are part of the United Nations Command's forces, led by General Douglas MacArthur (played by Ed Harris). The story begins with the Marines preparing for an amphibious assault on Inchon, which was a strategic location that could change the course of the war. As the operation unfolds, the Marines face numerous challenges, including fierce resistance from North Korean forces and treacherous terrain.

Throughout the film, the characters grapple with their own personal demons and make difficult decisions that impact the outcome of the battle. Ultimately, the Marines succeed in retaking Inchon, but not without great cost in terms of lives lost and injuries sustained.

Overall, Operation Chromite is a powerful and emotional film that explores the complexities of war and the human spirit.

original_title: Bad Times at the El Royale
overview: Lake Tahoe, 1969. Seven strangers, each one with a secret to bury, meet at El Royale, a decadent motel with a dark past. In the course of a fateful night, everyone will have one last shot at redemption.
tagline: All roads lead here
title: Bad Times at the El Royale
plot:
Bad Times at the El Royale is a 2018 American neo-noir crime thriller film directed by Drew Goddard and written by Goddard and Alex Kurtzman. The film stars Chris Hemsworth, Emma Stone, Jon Hamm, Jeff Bridges, and Dakota Johnson.

The story takes place on October 1, 1969, at the El Royale Hotel in Lake Tahoe, California/Nevada border. The hotel is a neutral ground for various characters to meet, each with their own secrets and agendas. The film begins with a series of seemingly unrelated events: a young woman named Lila (Dakota Johnson) is found dead in one of the hotel's rooms; a group of thugs attempt to rob the hotel's bar; and a mysterious man named Daniel Flynn (Chris Hemsworth) checks into the hotel.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that each character has a connection to the others. Lila was a prostitute who had been working at the hotel, and her death is linked to a larger conspiracy involving a wealthy businessman named Mark Wahlberg's character, Dwight (Jon Hamm), who is using the hotel as a front for his illicit activities.

Meanwhile, a former CIA operative named Joseph "Daddy" O'Malley (Jeff Bridges) checks into the hotel, seeking revenge against Dwight and his associates. O'Malley has a personal vendetta against Dwight, who he believes is responsible for the death of his daughter.

As the story progresses, it becomes clear that each character has their own motivations and secrets. Lila was being blackmailed by Dwight over her past, while O'Malley's daughter had been murdered by Dwight's associates. The film's plot twists and turns as the characters' stories intersect and collide.

Throughout the film, Goddard pays homage to classic Hollywood films of the 1960s, including the works of Alfred Hitchcock and Billy Wilder. The film's cinematography is also noteworthy, capturing the eerie atmosphere of the El Royale Hotel and its surroundings.

In the end, O'Malley's quest for revenge leads him to confront Dwight in a tense showdown. However, just as it seems that justice will be served, the true extent of Dwight's plan is revealed, and the film ends on a cliffhanger, leaving the audience wondering what will happen next.

Overall, Bad Times at the El Royale is a complex and engaging thriller that explores themes of power, corruption, and redemption. The film features strong performances from its cast, particularly Jeff Bridges and Chris Hemsworth, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

overview: Scooby-Doo and his pals win an all-expense paid vacation and embark on a trip of a lifetime to a tropical paradise. Their destination however, turns out to be Zombie Island. As soon as they arrive, they realize the place looks strangely familiar and is reminiscent of a trip they took years ago, in which they became wrapped up in a mystery involving zombies. The gang soon learns that their trip to paradise comes with a price when the zombies re-emerge and attack their hotel. Will Scooby-Doo and the Mystery Inc. gang finally solve the mystery behind Zombie Island?
title: Scooby-Doo! Return to Zombie Island
plot:
Scooby-Doo! Return to Zombie Island is a 2019 American animated direct-to-video mystery film produced by Warner Bros. Animation, the thirty-third entry in the direct-to-video Scooby-Doo series and a standalone sequel to Scooby-Doo on Zombie Island (1998), the franchise's first such film. The voice cast features Frank Welker as Scooby-Doo and Fred, Grey DeLisle as Daphne, Matthew Lillard as Shaggy, Kate Micucci as Velma, John Michael Higgins as Alan Smithee, Travis Willingham as Seaver and Cassandra Peterson as Elvira.

After Fred dreams of catching a string of villains who all turn out to be members of the Withers family, he wakes to the reality that the gang has been forced into retirement by the local sheriff and that he has sold the Mystery Machine. When Fred wants to return to sleuthing, Shaggy and Scooby, tired of being taken for granted, make the others promise never to solve another mystery. Then Elvira announces on television that Shaggy has won a tropical vacation. On the island, greeters warn the gang to get out, a clawed figure blocks their road with a fallen palm tree, and at the Moonstar Island Resort they meet manager Alan and a staff who resemble the people they met on Moonscar Island. Chased by zombies, Shaggy and Scooby find a secret passage to a cavern full of cat statues and release their friends from the promise. A trap, a fire and the sprinklers reveal the zombies as the staff in make-up: the resort is really Moonscar Island, and Alan is the film director Alan Smithee, who rigged Shaggy's prize to shoot a horror movie inspired by Velma's blog, though he knows nothing of the black were-cat they saw. Agreeing to help finish the film, the gang meets Fred's stunt double, Seaver, and his monster-truck Mystery Machine. Soon feral cats and three were-cats attack, and the cat creatures seize Alan's medallion, once Simone's pendant, using it in the harvest moonlight to find a chest of gold coins that proves to be foil-wrapped Scooby Snacks. Disguised as zombies, the gang scares and unmasks them as the greeters and the ferry captain, treasure hunters who controlled the cats with whistles, while a fourth were-cat appears to be real. The tamed cats then help dig up the real treasure, Alan retires a rich man and the sheriff lets Mystery Inc. return.

The film premiered at San Diego Comic-Con on 21 July 2019 and was released on digital platforms and home media on 3 September 2019.

overview: Alma is a scientist at Berlin's famous Pergamon Museum. In order to obtain research funds for her studies, she accepts an offer to participate in an extraordinary experiment. For three weeks, she must live with a humanoid robot with artificial intelligence designed to allow it to morph into that of her ideal life partner. Enter Tom, a machine in human form, created to make her happy.
tagline: 93% of women want one, she doesn't.
title: I'm Your Man
plot:
I'm Your Man is a 2021 German romantic comedy film directed by Maria Schrader. The movie tells the story of Charlotte, a young and ambitious violinist who becomes the new partner of a famous conductor, Oliver, who suffers from amnesia.

The main theme of I'm Your Man revolves around the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. Charlotte's character is deeply invested in her music and her career, but she finds herself struggling to connect with Oliver on an emotional level due to his condition. As they spend more time together, Charlotte begins to see Oliver as a person beyond his amnesia, and their relationship becomes a catalyst for her own self-discovery.

The film also explores the theme of love and intimacy in a unique way, as Charlotte and Oliver's relationship is built on a foundation of mutual respect and trust. Despite the challenges they face, they are able to form a deep connection that transcends their physical interactions.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the idea of vulnerability and openness in relationships. As Charlotte learns more about Oliver's past and his condition, she must confront her own fears and insecurities in order to truly connect with him. The film suggests that true intimacy requires a willingness to be vulnerable and open with one another.

Overall, I'm Your Man is a thoughtful and nuanced exploration of the complexities of human relationships and the ways in which we shape each other's identities.

overview: While the original parodied slasher flicks like Scream, Keenen Ivory Wayans's sequel to Scary Movie takes comedic aim at haunted house movies. A group of students visit a mansion called "Hell House," and murderous high jinks ensue.
tagline: No More Mercy. No More Shame. No More Sequels - Honest! - We Lied.
title: Scary Movie 2
plot:
Scary Movie 2 is a horror comedy film released in 2001, directed by Keenen Ivory Wayans and written by Shawn Wayans and Marlon Wayans. The movie is the sequel to the 2000 film Scary Movie and stars Anna Faris, Regina Hall, and James Woods.

The plot of Scary Movie 2 takes place after the events of the first film. Cindy Campbell (Anna Faris) is now a high school student who has survived the previous night's terror. However, she soon discovers that the evil spirits from the first film have returned to wreak havoc on her life once again.

As Cindy navigates her way through high school, she begins to experience strange and terrifying events. She starts to suspect that the house where she lives is haunted by malevolent spirits. The main antagonist of the movie is a group of ghosts who are determined to scare Cindy to death.

The ghostly entities are led by a vengeful spirit named Bessie (Linda Cardellini), who was killed in the 1950s and seeks revenge on Cindy's family for their supposed wrongdoings. The spirits also include a group of teenagers from the 1950s, who were killed in a car accident.

As Cindy tries to survive the night, she enlists the help of her friends, including her boyfriend Bobby (Timothy Stack) and her friend Ray (Shawn Wayans). Together, they try to uncover the source of the haunting and put an end to it.

Throughout the movie, the characters frequently break the fourth wall, addressing the audience directly and commenting on the clichés of horror movies. The film also parodies popular horror films from the 1950s and 1960s, including The Innocents, The Haunting, and Psycho.

As the night wears on, Cindy and her friends discover that the source of the haunting is a group of ghosts who are trapped in the house by a supernatural force. They also learn that Bessie's ghost is seeking revenge on Cindy's family for their supposed wrongdoings.

In the end, Cindy and her friends manage to defeat the ghosts and put an end to the haunting. However, not before they experience some terrifying moments and comedic relief. The movie ends with a humorous twist, as Cindy reflects on the events of the night and comments on how it was all just a big joke.

Overall, Scary Movie 2 is a horror comedy film that spoofs popular horror movies from the past while still delivering plenty of laughs and scares.

overview: A pilot battles to save his family and the planet after an experiment for unlimited energy goes wrong.
tagline: Worlds will collide
title: Kill Switch
plot:
Kill Switch, also known as Redivider, is a 2017 science fiction film and the feature directorial debut of Tim Smit, from a screenplay by Charlie Kindinger and Omid Nooshin. Dan Stevens stars as Will Porter, a former NASA pilot turned physicist who is sent into a parallel world to undo the damage caused by tapping an unlimited source of quantum energy, and who must choose which of two Earths will survive. Bérénice Marlohe, Tygo Gernandt, Charity Wakefield, Bas Keijzer, Mike Libanon and Mike Reus co-star.

In the near future, Porter is recruited by Alterplex, a power company that has built an enormous tower drawing on limitless quantum energy. The energy comes from a mirror version of Earth known as "the Echo", which was never supposed to harbour life; a malfunction, however, created a true duplicate planet, populated and with a tower of its own. As the Alterplex tower siphons off its power, the Echo is plagued by strange gravitational anomalies and unexplained deaths, and the link between the worlds now threatens to destroy both within less than a day unless one of them is eliminated. Porter is dispatched into the Echo carrying a cube-shaped device called the Redivider, which he has been told will rebalance the flow of energy between the two universes and restore order. Once there, he discovers that the device is in fact a kill switch designed to annihilate the Echo, leaving him to decide which world must be sacrificed so the other can live. The Echo's armed forces are aware of his mission and hunt him, seeking to capture or kill him, while a band of anti-tower rebels wages its own war against the soldiers guarding the towers.

Stevens plays Porter, with Marlohe as Abigail Vos, Gernandt as Michael, Wakefield as Mia Porter, Gijs Scholten van Aschat as Reynard, Keijzer as Bektman, Libanon as Hugo and Reus as Dr. Klintsen. The casting of Stevens and Marlohe, with Smit directing, was announced in February 2016, and Aaron Ryder produced through FilmNation Entertainment; Don Diablo wrote, scored and performed the theme song, "Echoes". Saban Films acquired distribution rights in February 2017 and released the film theatrically on June 16, 2017, followed by a video-on-demand release from Lionsgate Home Entertainment on August 22. Critics were largely negative, giving it a 9% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31, and it earned only about $163,000 worldwide at the box office, with home video sales adding roughly $140,000.

overview: Because of the actions of her irresponsible parents, a young girl is left alone on a decrepit country estate and survives inside her fantastic imagination.
tagline: The squirrels made it seem less lonely
title: Tideland
plot:
Tideland is a 2005 film that delves into the complexities of childhood imagination and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie follows the story of Miss Lady Bird, a young girl who embarks on a surreal journey through her own subconscious, navigating a world filled with eerie landscapes, strange creatures, and an array of eccentric characters.

At its core, Tideland is a film about the fragility of childhood innocence and the struggle to maintain a sense of wonder in a chaotic world. Miss Lady Bird's experiences are marked by a deep-seated longing for connection and understanding, as she grapples with the complexities of her own emotions and the expectations placed upon her.

The film also explores themes of isolation and loneliness, as Miss Lady Bird finds herself disconnected from the world around her. Her relationships with others are often fraught with tension and uncertainty, leaving her feeling like an outsider in her own life.

One of the most striking aspects of Tideland is its use of symbolism and metaphor to convey these themes. The film's dreamlike quality and its reliance on vivid imagery create a sense of disorientation and confusion, mirroring Miss Lady Bird's own feelings of disconnection and uncertainty.

Ultimately, Tideland is a poignant and haunting film that lingers in the mind long after the credits roll. Its exploration of childhood imagination and the complexities of human emotion makes for a deeply unsettling and thought-provoking viewing experience.

overview: James Sullivan and Mike Wazowski are monsters, they earn their living scaring children and are the best in the business... even though they're more afraid of the children than they are of them. When a child accidentally enters their world, James and Mike suddenly find that kids are not to be afraid of and they uncover a conspiracy that could threaten all children across the world.
tagline: We Scare Because We Care.
title: Monsters, Inc.
plot:
Monsters, Inc. is a heartwarming animated film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and directed by Pete Docter. The movie takes place in a world where monsters live in their own society, Monstropolis, and have evolved to scare children for a living.

The story follows two best friend monsters, James P. Sullivan (Sulley) and Mike Wazowski, who work at Monsters, Inc., the largest scream-processing factory in the city. Sulley is a top Scarer, known for his intimidating roar and ability to frighten even the most fearless children. Mike, on the other hand, is a small, one-eyed monster with a big personality and a talent for technology.

The two monsters have a strict routine: they enter children's rooms at night, scare them half to death, and collect their screams in canisters. The screams are then used to generate electricity for the city. However, things take an unexpected turn when a little girl, Boo, accidentally follows Sulley back into Monstropolis.

As Sulley tries to return Boo to her own world, he and Mike discover that children's laughter is actually more powerful than screams in generating electricity. This revelation puts their jobs at risk, as the company's CEO, Waternoose, plans to shut down the scream-processing factory and switch to laughter-gathering instead.

Sulley and Mike embark on a mission to return Boo to her own world while also finding a way to harness the power of children's laughter. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, trust, and the importance of embracing their true selves.

The movie features stunning animation, lovable characters, and a story that is both funny and heartwarming. The voice cast, including John Goodman, Billy Crystal, and Steve Buscemi, delivers memorable performances that bring the monsters to life.

Overall, Monsters, Inc. is a timeless classic that has become a beloved favorite among audiences of all ages. Its themes of friendship, acceptance, and the power of laughter make it a movie that will continue to delight and inspire generations to come.

original_title: Return to House on Haunted Hill
overview: Eight years have passed since Sara Wolfe and Eddie Baker escaped the House on Haunted Hill. Now the kidnapped Ariel, Sara's sister, goes inside the house with a group of treasure hunters to find the statue of Baphomet, worth millions and believed to be the cause of the House's evil.
title: Return to House on Haunted Hill
plot:
Return to House on Haunted Hill is a supernatural horror film that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. The movie delves into the theme of temptation, as the characters are lured into the mansion with promises of wealth and fame, only to find themselves trapped in a desperate fight for survival.

The film also examines the concept of greed and how it can lead individuals to compromise their values and morals. As the characters succumb to the temptation of the mansion's riches, they become increasingly consumed by their own desires, ultimately leading to their downfall.

Furthermore, Return to House on Haunted Hill touches on the idea of the supernatural as a metaphor for the unknown and the uncontrollable forces that shape human existence. The haunted mansion serves as a symbol of the darker aspects of human nature, representing the fears and anxieties that lie within each individual.

The movie also explores the theme of redemption, as some characters are forced to confront their past mistakes and make amends in order to escape the mansion's clutches. Through this narrative thread, the film suggests that it may be too late for some individuals to change their ways and that the consequences of their actions can be devastating.

Overall, Return to House on Haunted Hill is a horror film that weaves together themes of temptation, greed, redemption, and the supernatural to create a tense and unsettling viewing experience.

overview: On the outskirts of a kingdom, a quiet but fierce medieval warrior protects the realm from monsters and the occult. His gruesome collection of heads is missing only one - the monster that killed his daughter years ago. Driven by a thirst for revenge, he travels wild expanses on horseback. When his second chance arrives, it’s in a way far more horrifying than he ever imagined.
tagline: Grief. Anger. Vengeance.
title: The Head Hunter
plot:
The Head Hunter, first screened as The Head, is an American independent fantasy horror film directed, produced and edited by Jordan Downey, who wrote it with his longtime collaborator Kevin Stewart. Norwegian actor Christopher Rygh, in his feature debut, plays a lone medieval warrior known only as the Father, with Cora Kaufman as his murdered daughter and Aisha Ricketts voicing the creature he hunts. Made on a low budget with a small cast and very little dialogue, it was shot mainly around Bragança in northern Portugal, with additional scenes filmed in Norway and California. The filmmakers cited Quest for Fire, The Witch, The X-Files and Tales from the Crypt as inspirations.

In the Dark Ages, the Father lives alone in a remote cabin with only his horse, Jakke, for company. He earns his living killing the monsters that menace a nearby kingdom: each new bounty is announced by a horn and posted outside the castle walls, and he mounts the heads of his kills on the walls of his cabin. Between hunts he mends his armor, sets traps, tends his daughter's grave and brews a healing elixir from the blood and organs of the beasts he slays.

After Jakke is killed on a hunt, a new bounty is posted for the very creature that killed his daughter. The Father journeys north to an island, finds the monster in a cave, cuts off its head and brings it home. But a jar of the elixir spills onto the severed head, reviving it, and it drags itself into the forest in search of a new body. As night falls, the hunter is drawn into a battle of wits with the creature, which digs up his daughter's grave and attaches itself to her corpse. He tracks it to a cave and, after a long fight, tears its head from her body and stabs it repeatedly. The next morning he reburies her and returns to his chores, until a sudden cry is followed by silence. A figure that looks like the Father returns carrying a severed head and pins it to the wall: it is the Father's own. The creature, now wearing his body, leaves with the elixir.

The film premiered at the Sitges Film Festival in October 2018 and was retitled at the suggestion of its distributor, Vertical Entertainment, after lukewarm reactions to the original name. Reviews were positive, with 94% of 17 critics on Rotten Tomatoes recommending it; critics praised its atmosphere, cinematography and Rygh's performance, though some noted the limits of its budget.

original_title: Superman II: The Richard Donner Cut
overview: Superman agrees to sacrifice his powers to start a relationship with Lois Lane, unaware that three Kryptonian criminals he inadvertently released are conquering Earth.
tagline: The version you have never seen.
title: Superman II: The Richard Donner Cut
plot:
Superman II: The Richard Donner Cut is a 2006 re-edited version of the 1980 film Superman II, directed by Richard Donner and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The main themes of this movie revolve around the struggle between good and evil, as embodied by the iconic characters of Superman (played by Christopher Reeve) and General Zod (played by Terence Stamp). The story delves into the complexities of power, responsibility, and the blurred lines between heroism and tyranny. 

As Superman faces off against his arch-nemesis, he must confront the darker aspects of his own abilities and the consequences of his actions on a global scale. This internal conflict is juxtaposed with the external threat posed by General Zod, who seeks to claim Earth as his own and impose his brand of order through force.

The film also explores the theme of identity, particularly in the context of Superman's dual nature as an alien from Krypton and a human raised on Earth. The character of Lois Lane (played by Margot Kidder) serves as a catalyst for this exploration, as she represents both the comfort of familiarity and the thrill of adventure.

Furthermore, the movie touches upon the idea of sacrifice and the weight of responsibility that comes with great power. Superman's relationships with his adoptive parents, Jonathan and Martha Kent, are also a significant aspect of the narrative, highlighting the importance of family and the values they instill in their son.

Overall, Superman II: The Richard Donner Cut is a thought-provoking tale that balances action, adventure, and character-driven drama, making it a compelling exploration of the human condition through the lens of a superhero.

overview: A cartoonist teams up with an ace reporter and a law enforcement officer to track down an elusive serial killer.
tagline: There's more than one way to lose your life to a killer.
title: Zodiac
plot:
Zodiac is a 2007 American crime thriller film directed by David Fincher, based on the non-fiction book of the same name by Robert Graysmith. The film stars Jake Gyllenhaal as Robert Graysmith, a cartoonist and amateur detective who becomes obsessed with solving the Zodiac Killer case.

The film begins in the late 1960s, with Robert Graysmith (Gyllenhaal) meeting his future wife, Darlene (Robert Downey Jr.'s sister, Mary-Louise), at a San Francisco art gallery. The couple gets married and starts a family, but Robert's life is disrupted when he becomes fascinated with the Zodiac Killer case.

The Zodiac Killer was a serial killer who terrorized the San Francisco Bay Area in the late 1960s and early 1970s, killing at least five people and taunting the police with cryptic letters and codes. Graysmith becomes convinced that he can crack the code and identify the killer, but his obsession puts a strain on his marriage.

As the investigation unfolds, Graysmith teams up with Paul Avery (Robert Downey Jr.), a journalist who is also working on the case. Together, they follow leads and interview suspects, including Arthur Leigh Allen (John Carroll Lynch), a man who is suspected of being the Zodiac Killer.

Meanwhile, the film's narrative jumps back and forth in time, showing Graysmith's life before and after his obsession with the case. We see him as a happy family man, but also as a man consumed by his own curiosity and determination.

As the investigation continues, Graysmith becomes increasingly convinced that he is closing in on the killer. He uses his skills as a cartoonist to analyze the cryptic messages left by the Zodiac Killer, and eventually cracks the code.

The film's climax shows Graysmith finally identifying Arthur Leigh Allen as the Zodiac Killer, but also reveals that he may have been wrong. The film ends with Graysmith reflecting on the case and its impact on his life, and wondering if justice was truly served.
